`CONTEXT.md`:

```md
# Obelisk

Obelisk manages games owned through storefront accounts, including their installation and launch.

## Language

**Transfer**:
One account-scoped attempt to install, verify or repair a game's files. Its lifetime includes the remaining disk work after cancellation; verified reusable data can survive for a later attempt.

**Installation receipt**:
A record identifying a game installation whose required files were successfully installed. Partial download data is not an installation receipt.

**Offer**:
What a storefront says Obelisk can install of one game, with Steam's language, before any folder is chosen. The storefront picks its build as the Transfer starts: the Mac build when its game runs natively on Apple silicon, as its program's first bytes tell, else the Windows build. Until a download found that a Mac build's game does not run natively, the game's page shows the Mac build. A Mac build without an arm64 slice, Intel or 32-bit, is never installed, nor launched. A new installation starts from an offer; an installed game launches, updates and uninstalls from its Installation receipt alone.
_Avoid_: download request, install target

**Platform**:
Which of a game's builds a Transfer installs, picked by the storefront as it starts, or an Installation receipt records: the Mac build, which runs natively, or the Windows build, which runs in Wine. Each storefront spells it its own way in its requests, receipts and folder names; Obelisk names it one way everywhere else.
_Avoid_: OS, os list (Steam's declared platforms, Linux included), macos/osx/Mac as values

**Games folder**:
Where Obelisk installs games: its own folder in its library until the player chooses another, such as one on an external disk, inside which Obelisk makes its own. Choosing one moves every installation there, one at a time in the download queue: a game cannot launch while it moves, the others can, and a move the player stops leaves its game where it was. Wine prefixes, launch settings and the Cloud archive stay in the library. An installation whose disk is not connected shows as not installed until the disk comes back.
_Avoid_: library folder (Obelisk's own data), install location

**Account session**:
One storefront account's signed-in connection to its storefront, from sign-in or restoration until sign-out. The account's library, Transfers, launches, friends and chat go through it. Steam's connects again by itself when its CM connection drops: three attempts after growing waits, then only the player's retry or the Mac's wake tries again, and never once Steam asked the account to sign in again. A Transfer whose turn comes meanwhile waits for the new connection, and the download queue waits with it. Each CM connection of a session is numbered, 0 for the first: its transport, in the code.
_Avoid_: login, CM connection (one connection of an account session)

**Library cache**:
The last library each storefront account loaded, with everything the storefront returned for each game and the game's last launch from Obelisk. The library shows from it while the account's session connects; the session keeps it as it loads, and signing the account out forgets it. It is not the catalog of games added by hand.
_Avoid_: library.json (the catalog's file), launch history file

**Account library**:
One storefront account's games as Obelisk shows them, with what orders and narrows each: its name, playtime, last played (on its storefront or from Obelisk, whichever is later), date added, achievements unlocked and size installed. It shows from the Library cache while the account's session connects, becomes live once the session lists the games, and signing the account out forgets it. Every storefront searches, filters and orders it the same six ways, and its featured game, its hero, is the last one played, else the most played, equal ones by name.
_Avoid_: catalog (the games added by hand), filtered games, Library cache (its saved copy)

**Cloud archive**:
Obelisk's own local store of each account's save versions, together with the record of which account currently owns each physical save location. One archive serves every storefront, so two storefront copies of a game that share a save location cannot silently adopt each other's saves.
_Avoid_: vault root, SteamCloud folder

**Last Cloud sync**:
The last moment Obelisk confirmed that an account's local saves for a game and its Cloud saves were identical, by uploading, downloading or finding them equal. Capturing or choosing a version without that confirmation does not count.
_Avoid_: last upload, last played

**Wine prefix**:
The Windows machine one Windows installation runs in, shared by every account that launches it. It holds the game's Windows saves, is readied before each launch of the game, and goes when the installation is uninstalled.
_Avoid_: bottle, Wine folder

**Engine**:
What runs a Windows game's Wine: Rosetta's Wine, Voile's Wine for macOS under Rosetta, for most games, or the Linux engine, Voile's Wine for Linux that voile-lkd runs natively, for games whose anti-cheat supports Linux. Each engine keeps its own Wine prefix of an installation and its own runtime in Voile, offers its own Graphics backends, and starts, quits and stops a game its own way; Prerequisites run only in Rosetta's Wine. Launch settings pick it, and a game moved to the other engine starts in that engine's Wine prefix.
_Avoid_: backend (a Graphics backend renders), runner, bottle, Wine flavour

**Launch settings**:
How one Windows installation runs, for every account that launches it: what Obelisk knows of the game, with the player's choices over it. The player picks the arguments added after the storefront's and the game's own on its command line, its engine, then the graphics backend that renders its Direct3D there and that backend's options, each as the engine allows, and whether Metal's Performance HUD shows over the game. Only the choices that differ from what Obelisk knows of the game are kept. A change applies from the game's next launch, a game moved to the other engine runs in that engine's Wine prefix, and the settings go when the installation is uninstalled.
_Avoid_: bottle, container, game settings, profile (what Obelisk itself knows of a game)

**Graphics backend**:
What renders a Windows game's Direct3D through Metal: D3DMetal, for Direct3D 11 and 12 in 64-bit programs, or DXMT, for Direct3D 10 and 11. A game has one, as Windows has one dxgi per process: on DXMT it has no Direct3D 12. On Rosetta's Wine, a 32-bit program of a game on D3DMetal renders through DXMT.
_Avoid_: renderer, translation layer

**Prerequisite**:
A program a storefront names to run once in a Wine prefix before its game first starts, such as a DirectX or Visual C++ installer. One that fails runs again on the next launch; the game starts anyway.
_Avoid_: redistributable (Steam's name for the package, not the run), dependency

**Runtime**:
What Obelisk downloads beside a game's own files for it to run: Voile for a Windows build, Valve's Steam components for every Steam game. A Transfer gets the missing ones before the game's files, and a launch that still misses one gets it after its Admission, before its game is prepared. A Voile release a newer one replaced goes only once no game of any storefront may still run from it.
_Avoid_: dependency, prerequisite (a Prerequisite runs inside a Wine prefix)

**Reservation**:
The exclusive claim a Game session or Cloud maintenance holds on a game's installation. While it exists, no Transfer, uninstall or other launch of that game can start.
_Avoid_: lock, busy state

**Admission**:
The moment a launch claims its game's Reservation, before any verification, Voile download or authentication can wait. A launch cancelled before its handoff to a supervisor gives the Reservation back; once handed off, only the Game session's end does.
_Avoid_: launch start, pending launch

**Game session**:
One account-scoped launch of a game, holding a Reservation from admission until the game has really exited and its Cloud saves are settled. Obelisk keeps running in the background while it lasts; really quitting Obelisk stops its game first, and if Obelisk dies, its game stops with it.
_Avoid_: launch, supervisor session

**Diagnostics**:
The files Obelisk writes about how a game ran, in its storefront's folder under ~/Library/Logs/Obelisk: the log of the game's last launch, the one before it and its input service's, and a Steam launch's launch or failure report. A bug report attaches them. macOS's crash reports and Obelisk's unified log are not diagnostics.
_Avoid_: logs folder, launch logs

**Cloud maintenance**:
Synchronizing one game's Cloud saves without launching it, at the player's request. It runs inside Obelisk, holds the Reservation of every game of its storefront while it runs, and stops if Obelisk quits or the account signs out.
_Avoid_: Cloud resume, cloud-only session, background sync

**Cloud sync**:
One comparison of an account's local saves for a game with its Cloud saves, before a launch, after the game exits, or as Cloud maintenance. It ends with both sides equal, with the player's choice applied, or with work left pending for a later sync.
_Avoid_: Cloud check, sync cycle

**Cloud record**:
What the Cloud archive keeps of one game for one account besides its saves: the Cloud rules and the configuration that place its saves, the work a Cloud sync left pending, and whether an uninstall may have removed some of them. From an uninstall on, or once a Windows game's engine moves it to another Wine prefix, a save missing locally keeps its archived version and is never sent as deleted, until a Cloud sync finds both sides agreeing. An uninstalled game keeps its record, so its Cloud indicator and Cloud maintenance still find its pending work.
_Avoid_: Cloud context (the storefront's file that holds it), work journal

**Cloud view**:
The complete set of an account's Cloud saves for one game that a Cloud sync compares against: read from the storefront and trusted only while the storefront still lists the same saves afterwards, or what an upload just confirmed. An archived save stands in for a listed one when its size and the storefront's hash for it match, so an unchanged save is not downloaded again.
_Avoid_: remote snapshot, readback, remote listing

**Cloud question**:
A choice a Cloud sync asks the player: which saves to keep after a conflict, or whether to retry, cancel or launch anyway after a failed launch check. It takes one answer and closes with it; it closes unanswered when the sync is cancelled, the account is revoked, or nobody answers in time. An account asks at most one at a time, whichever sync asks it.
_Avoid_: prompt, Cloud decision

**Account revocation**:
Signing a storefront account out while its Game sessions may still run. It stops that account's network work and presence, keeps any exit save locally as pending for that account, and never ends a running game.
_Avoid_: sign-out cancel, logout kill

**Game action**:
What the player can do with one game of an account now, as its button shows it: download, resume or update it, launch it, wait for its queued Transfer, follow its Transfer, wait while it is uninstalled, launched or its session closes, follow a step outside any Transfer (a runtime its launch waits for, or a Cloud sync), or end its running game. A game's page and its library show the same action, except for an installed game whose storefront offers a newer build: the page offers the update alone, while the library launches it and the launch installs the update first. A Game session of another account is not this account's running game.
_Avoid_: primary action, card action

```

`CONTRIBUTING.md`:

```md
# Contributing to Obelisk

This guide covers building Obelisk from source, testing it and finding your way around the code. To install Obelisk as a player, see the [README](README.md).

## Contents

- [Requirements](#requirements)
- [Building and running](#building-and-running)
- [Testing](#testing)
- [Windows games in development](#windows-games-in-development)
- [Project layout](#project-layout)
- [Interface text and translations](#interface-text-and-translations)
- [Editing the Xcode project](#editing-the-xcode-project)
- [Releases](#releases)
- [License](#license)

## Requirements

- A Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 26 or later. Builds target the Mac's own architecture.
- Xcode with its command-line tools.
- Stable Rust with Cargo, through [rustup](https://rustup.rs), with both Mac targets: `rustup target add aarch64-apple-darwin x86_64-apple-darwin`. Part of the Steam host is built for Intel, for the Windows games Wine runs under Rosetta.
- An Apple Development signing identity, with its private key in your Keychain. The build, test and DMG scripts refuse ad hoc signatures.

Obelisk does not use the App Sandbox, so that it can open games and manage Wine processes. It ships no driver, privileged entitlement or system helper.

## Building and running

Signing settings shared by Debug and Release live in `apps/macos/Config/Signing.xcconfig`. To pick your own certificate and team:

```sh
cp apps/macos/Config/Signing.local.xcconfig.example apps/macos/Config/Signing.local.xcconfig
security find-identity -v -p codesigning   # lists your certificates
```

Set the identity and team in `Signing.local.xcconfig`, which git ignores. Use a certificate's fingerprint to avoid an ambiguous match.

Then build and launch Obelisk:

```sh
./scripts/run.sh
```

You can also open `apps/macos/Obelisk.xcodeproj` in Xcode, select the **Obelisk** scheme and choose **Run**. The first build downloads the Cargo dependencies and generates the Swift bindings of the Rust core.

Keep the same signing identity across builds: macOS then keeps trusting it for the Keychain items Obelisk saves sessions in. After a change of identity, macOS asks once for your login Keychain password; choose **Always Allow**.

By default, a build uses the same library as the installed app, in `~/Library/Application Support/com.zagrios.obelisk`. Set `OBELISK_LIBRARY_DIRECTORY` before launching the binary to use another one. The Keychain items stay shared.

## Testing

```sh
./scripts/test.sh
```

This checks the English and French translations, runs `cargo fmt`, Clippy and the Rust tests, runs the Swift ↔ Rust integration tests in Xcode, and verifies the app's signature. Tests use temporary folders and never launch games.

## Windows games in development

Windows games run in [Voile](https://github.com/Zagrios/voile), Obelisk's Wine runtime, in `<library>/Voile/<version>`. Obelisk runs the newest release installed of its contract, the paths, variables and programs it relies on in a runtime, which [docs/CONTRACT.md](docs/CONTRACT.md) lists and `crates/game-runtime/voile-release.json` numbers. As a Windows game launches, Obelisk reads Voile's signed `voile-feed.json`: a newer release of its contract downloads once no game runs, and a game whose profile needs a newer release than the one in place waits for it. The first Windows game gets a release with its download. `voile-release.json` also names the release a build installs before it has read the feed; the Release workflow writes the newest one there with `scripts/pin-voile.sh` before it builds, so it needs no commit.

- **A local Voile build:** run Voile's `./scripts/install-dev.sh`. It installs the runtime in `<library>/Voile/current`, which takes precedence over every release.
- **A local copy of the release in `voile-release.json`:** a Debug build given `OBELISK_VOILE_ARCHIVE=<path to the archive>` installs that file instead of downloading it, after checking its SHA-256.

Steam games also need Valve's Steam components, pinned in `crates/game-runtime/runtime-manifest.json` and downloaded from Valve's CDN into `~/Library/Caches/com.zagrios.obelisk/SteamRuntime`. Obelisk never ships a Valve binary.

What Obelisk knows about particular Windows games is in `crates/game-runtime/profiles.json`. A Release build reads it again from `main` as a Windows game launches and keeps the last one in its library, so a change pushed to `main` reaches players within minutes; a Debug build keeps the file it was built with, as edited. An entry names its game by Steam app ID (`steam`), Epic namespace and app name (`epic`) or GOG product ID (`gog`), and by a file only that game's installation holds (`path`, relative to the installation), which finds it on any storefront. Obelisk looks for the storefront's ID first, then for the file. The entry can then give the `engine` (`Rosetta` or `Linux`) and the `graphics` backend (`D3DMetal` or `Dxmt`) the game runs with, the `executable` started instead of the publisher's, relative to the installation, the `arguments` added after the storefront's, the environment `variables` and `dll_overrides` its Wine needs, and the oldest Voile release it runs in, `minimum_voile`, such as `v26.3.0-16`: the game still runs in the newest release installed, and its launch waits for a download only when an older one is in place. Its `note` says why. Obelisk checks each entry as it reads the file and leaves out one that sets what a profile may not: another key, one of Obelisk's own variables or DLLs, a `DYLD_` or `LD_` variable, a path outside the installation. The file's `format` changes only when an older Obelisk would read it wrong. A player's launch settings apply over it. A Visual C++ runtime installer, which storefronts run as a prerequisite, runs with `CX_HIDE_BUILTIN_VERSION_RESOURCES=1`: otherwise it keeps Wine's own `msvcp140`, `msvcp140_2` and `vcruntime140_1`, whose versions match its own, and a `n,b` override of them would find no Microsoft DLL. `cargo test -p game-runtime profile` checks the file.

Logs are in `~/Library/Logs/Obelisk`, one folder per store. A file named `winedebug` at the root of an installed Voile runtime replaces Obelisk's default Wine debug channels, for example `err+all,+steamclient`.

## Project layout

```text
apps/macos/
  Obelisk.xcodeproj     Xcode project, generated from project.yml
  project.yml           XcodeGen definition
  Config/               Name, version, bundle identifier and signing
  Obelisk/
    App/                Lifecycle, app state, overlay and menu bar
    Bridge/             Swift side of the Rust core; Generated/ is written by the build
    DesignSystem/       Shared visual components
    Features/           Home, store libraries, game pages, settings, overlay
    Models/             Store accounts, downloads, games and Cloud saves
    Resources/          Assets and Localizable.xcstrings
  ObeliskTests/         Swift ↔ Rust integration tests
crates/
  obelisk-core/         Catalog, library cache, verification and the shared download engine
  obelisk-bridge/       UniFFI bridge between Swift and Rust
  game-runtime/         Installations, download queue, launches, Wine, Cloud sync
  cloud-vault/          Local archive of each account's save versions
  steam-native/         Host that runs Valve's Steam components for games
  storefronts/          steam-kit, epic-kit and gog-kit: each store's protocols
packaging/              DMG layout and helper apps
scripts/                Build, run, test and release scripts
```

`CONTEXT.md` defines the words the code uses, such as Transfer, Game session or Reservation. Read it before changing how games install or launch.

The Steam, Epic Games and GOG protocols are implemented in Rust, from a study of public projects such as SteamKit, DepotDownloader, Legendary and Heroic. Obelisk runs none of them, nor SteamCMD. This repository redistributes neither the Steamworks SDK nor Wine.

## Interface text and translations

The interface is in English and French. It follows the system language and falls back to English, unless the player picks a language in **Settings → Language**. That choice is saved as Obelisk's own `AppleLanguages`, as macOS's per-app language setting does, and applies when Obelisk restarts.

- Every text shown to the player lives in `apps/macos/Obelisk/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings` and is read through the `L10n` helper.
- Add the English and the French translation together.
- Text that has to stay in code, such as technical diagnostics, is in English.
- `python3 scripts/verify-localization.py` checks the catalog and every key the code uses.
- The language picker lists every translation the app bundle contains. Each one needs its flag in `Assets.xcassets`, as an image set named `Flag-<code>`, taken from the same [Free Flat Flags](https://github.com/Zagrios/bs-manager/blob/chore/ressources/Img/free_flat_flags_227.zip) set as the others. A language several countries speak shows two flags split across the diagonal, as English shows the United States' and the United Kingdom's: `AppLanguage.countries` names them.

## Editing the Xcode project

After adding, moving or removing Swift files, or changing Xcode settings, install [XcodeGen](https://github.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen) 2.46.0 or later and regenerate the project:

```sh
./scripts/generate-project.sh
```

Never edit the files in `Bridge/Generated`: `scripts/build-rust.sh` regenerates them. `Cargo.lock` pins the Rust dependencies.

The app's display name and version are in `apps/macos/Config/App.xcconfig`. The storage identifier, `com.zagrios.obelisk`, must stay the same when the app is renamed, or come with a migration.

## Releases

```sh
./scripts/build-dmg.sh
```

This builds the Release app, signs it with the Developer ID set as `DISTRIBUTION_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY`, and creates `build/dist/Obelisk-<version>-arm64.dmg` with its SHA-256. It then notarizes and staples the disk image, with the notarytool keychain profile `obelisk-notary` (or `$OBELISK_NOTARY_PROFILE`), or the App Store Connect API key given by `OBELISK_NOTARY_KEY`, `OBELISK_NOTARY_KEY_ID` and `OBELISK_NOTARY_ISSUER`. `--no-notarize` skips that step for a local test.

To publish a version, set `MARKETING_VERSION` in `apps/macos/Config/App.xcconfig`, commit, and push a tag `v<version>`, such as `v0.2.0`. The Release workflow checks the tag against the app version, builds the notarized DMG and drafts the GitHub release with it.

Obelisk updates itself with [Sparkle](https://sparkle-project.org). It reads `appcast.xml` from the latest release, so players get a version only once its release is published. Publishing a release, or editing its notes afterwards, runs the Appcast workflow: it signs the DMG with the EdDSA key in the `SPARKLE_ED_PRIVATE_KEY` secret, turns the release notes into the HTML Sparkle shows, and attaches `appcast.xml`. `scripts/write-appcast.sh` writes the same feed locally, with the key that `generate_keys --account zagrios` keeps in the login Keychain. The key's public half is `SUPublicEDKey` in `apps/macos/Config/Info.plist`. Without the private key, Obelisks already installed accept no new version, so keep a copy of it outside this Mac. Debug builds never update.

## What is Obelisk?

Obelisk is a free game launcher for Macs with Apple silicon. Sign in with your Steam, Epic Games and GOG accounts, and every game you own shows up in one library, ready to download and play.

Windows games play too. Obelisk sets everything up for you: no bottles to create, no Wine to configure, no launcher to install. Click **Download**, then **Play**.

- **One library.** Every store in one place, with search across all of them, your recently played games and what is installed on this Mac.
- **No other launcher needed.** Steam, the Epic Games Launcher and GOG Galaxy do not need to be installed. Obelisk downloads, updates and launches games itself.
- **Windows games without setup.** Windows versions run through [Voile](https://github.com/Zagrios/voile), Obelisk's Windows runtime, which Obelisk installs and keeps up to date on its own.
- **Know how a game runs before you play.** A game's page shows the frame rate other players measured on a Mac with your chip.
- **Your saves follow you.** Steam and Epic Cloud saves sync before you play and after you quit.
- **Your friends are here.** See who is online and what they play, chat with Steam friends, and invite them or join their games.
- **Made for the Mac.** A native macOS app, made with SwiftUI.

## Requirements

- A Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later). Intel Macs are not supported.
- macOS Tahoe 26.4 or later.
- Rosetta, for Windows games. If it is missing, Obelisk asks macOS to install it the first time a game needs it.
- Disk space for your games. The first Windows game also downloads [Voile](https://github.com/Zagrios/voile), a few hundred MB, once.

## Installation

1. Download `Obelisk-<version>-arm64.dmg` from the [latest release](https://github.com/Zagrios/obelisk/releases/latest).
2. Open the disk image and drag **Obelisk** onto **Applications**.
3. Open Obelisk from your Applications folder.

Obelisk is signed and notarized by Apple, so it opens without a security warning.

**Updating Obelisk:** Obelisk looks for a new version by itself. It downloads it in the background and installs it the next time you quit Obelisk. If you rarely do, it offers the new version in a window after a while. **Check for Updates…** in the Obelisk menu looks right away, and **Settings → Updates** lets Obelisk ask before downloading instead. Your games, saves and sign-ins stay where they are.

## Getting started

<img src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/432d27ea-de67-4132-bf00-a3d2810847d8" />

1. Open Obelisk. The **Home** page offers to sign in to each store.
2. Sign in to the stores you use:
   - **Steam:** scan the QR code with the Steam mobile app, or enter your account name and password, then confirm with Steam Guard.
   - **Epic Games** and **GOG:** a window shows the store's own sign-in page. Sign in there, and Obelisk takes over once you are done.
3. Keep **Remember me** on to stay signed in. Obelisk stores the session in your macOS Keychain, never your password.
4. Open a game and choose **Download**. Once it is installed, choose **Play**.

## Features

### Library

<img src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ce35c3c8-c9de-4fb3-ae14-8b4431ba06af" />

- **Home** shows your last game, your recently played games and the games installed on this Mac, and searches all your libraries at once.
- Each store has its own library with cover art, sorted by last played, name or playtime, and filtered to installed games, games compatible with macOS or games you have already played.
- A game's page shows your playtime, when you last played, its size, its achievements, its news on Steam and its details on Epic Games and GOG.
- It also shows the game's **Expected FPS** on your Mac: see [How games run](#how-games-run).

### Downloads and updates

- **Download** picks the Mac version of a game when there is one, otherwise the Windows version.
- Downloads wait in one queue, whatever their store, and run one at a time. The **downloads** button above Settings in the sidebar shows the download speed and lets you pause, resume, reorder or remove each download.
- An interrupted download resumes where it stopped, even after quitting Obelisk.
- Games update automatically when a new version comes out. Updates wait while you play. To update only when you launch a game, turn off **Update games automatically** in **Settings → Games**.
- You can play an installed game while another one downloads.
- **Verify game files**, in the gear menu next to the **Play** button, repairs missing or damaged files. **Uninstall** is in the same menu.

<img src="assets/readme/downloads.jpg">

### Cloud saves

- Steam and Epic Games Cloud saves sync before a game starts and after it quits.
- If your saves on this Mac and in the Cloud differ, Obelisk asks which version to keep. It never overwrites one side silently.
- A game's page shows when its saves last synced, with **Sync now** when something is waiting to be sent.

### Friends, chat and invitations

- The account menu of Steam and Epic Games opens your friends list: who is online, away or playing, and which game.
- Steam friends can chat with you in Obelisk, and you can invite them to the game you are playing.
- When a Steam friend invites you, Obelisk shows a notification. Choose **Join Game** to start the game and join them. You can also right-click a friend who is playing to join their game.
- While Obelisk is open, your Steam friends see you as online.

### In-game overlay

Press **Shift+Tab** during a game to open the overlay without leaving it. It shows your friends, the game's achievements, its store page and the invitations you received. Steam games can also ask you there to authorize an in-game purchase.

<img src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/77b7c3f4-f817-4640-be39-c06bd8f6d4c0" />


### Controllers

Gamepads work in Windows games, which see them as Xbox controllers. Mac games use macOS's own controller support.

Some controllers, such as the Steam Controller, get full support once Obelisk is allowed in **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Input Monitoring**.

## Store support

|                           | Steam | Epic Games | GOG |
| ------------------------- | :---: | :--------: | :-: |
| Mac games                 |  ✅   |     ✅     | ✅  |
| Windows games             |  ✅   |     ✅     | ✅  |
| Automatic updates         |  ✅   |     ✅     | ✅  |
| Cloud saves               |  ✅   |     ✅     | ❌  |
| Achievements              |  ✅   |     ✅     | ✅  |
| Friends list              |  ✅   |     ✅     | ❌  |
| Chat and invitations      |  ✅   |     ❌ (in game)     | ❌ (in game)  |
| In-game overlay           |  ✅   |     ✅     | ✅  |

Support for more stores is planned in the near future.

## Windows games

When a game has no Mac version, Obelisk installs its Windows version and runs it through [Voile](https://github.com/Zagrios/voile), a Windows runtime built on Wine, the same kind of technology as CrossOver and Steam's Proton. You do not need to do anything:

- Obelisk downloads [Voile](https://github.com/Zagrios/voile) with your first Windows game and keeps it up to date.
- Each Windows game gets its own Windows environment. Uninstalling the game deletes it, after its Cloud saves are safe.
- The software a game needs, such as DirectX or Visual C++, installs by itself before its first launch.
- Direct3D 10, 11 and 12 games draw with Metal: 64-bit games through Apple's D3DMetal, 32-bit games through DXMT.
- A Windows game's **Launch Settings**, in the gear menu of its page, add arguments to its command line and choose the engine that runs it and what draws its Direct3D: D3DMetal or DXMT. On D3DMetal, ray tracing can be turned off for a game that renders wrongly with it. Metal's performance HUD can show the frame rate over the game. DLSS is not supported yet.


**Anti-cheat:** We already run games whose anti-cheat supports Linux, such as **Rocket League** and **ELDEN RING**, and more are coming. We are currently working on BattlEye support, and still studying how to run games whose anti-cheat only supports Windows, such as Easy Anti-Cheat on Windows, or works at a lower level of the system. We never modify or bypass an anti-cheat, so every game runs fully legitimately.

We cannot test every game that exists. If a game does not work well, or does not work at all, please [open an issue](#support).

## Performance

Performance and compatibility are our priority. If a tool slows a game down or keeps it from running, we change it. If no tool does the job, we write our own, down to the layers that draw the game. All of it is open source.

We wrote these from scratch:

- [Voile](https://github.com/Zagrios/voile), the Windows runtime Obelisk installs. It builds every piece below from pinned sources and ships them in one release.
- [voile-lkd](https://github.com/Zagrios/voile-lkd), the Linux engine behind games whose anti-cheat supports Linux, such as Rocket League and ELDEN RING. It runs x86-64 Linux programs as native macOS processes, with no virtual machine:
  - LKD implements about 375 Linux system calls on top of macOS.
  - fexdarwin runs the game's x86-64 code, translated to arm64 by FEX.
  - wsd opens the game's windows and shows its frames with Metal, without copying them.
  - obelisk-input serves your gamepads to both of Voile's engines.

We forked and changed these:

- [voile-wine](https://github.com/Zagrios/voile-wine), CrossOver's open-source Wine with fixes from Proton's Wine and our own, for Steam, gamepads, fullscreen windows and audio. It also holds the drivers that connect Wine to the Linux engine.
- [FEX](https://github.com/Zagrios/FEX), FEX-Emu's x86-64 translator, ported to run inside a macOS process.
- [DXMT](https://github.com/Zagrios/dxmt), 3Shain's Direct3D 10 and 11 on Metal. Our fork adds the native backend of UTM's fork and a fix of our own, so the Linux engine can render with it.
- [Neptune](https://github.com/Zagrios/neptune), UTM's Direct3D 11 and 12 driver for virtual machines, adapted to run in Wine on voile-lkd. It hands each Direct3D call to a render server on macOS, which draws it with DXMT or D3DMetal.

If a game runs worse in Obelisk than in another app on the same Mac, [tell us](#support). We treat that as a bug.

## How games run

When a game closes, Obelisk sends its frame rate, how it ended and your Mac's chip to [getobelisk.app](https://getobelisk.app) (see [Privacy](#privacy)). Put together, players' sessions show how each game runs on each Apple chip.

- **In Obelisk**, a game's page shows **Expected FPS**: the median frame rate of the sessions players played on your Mac's chip. When nobody has played the game on your chip yet, it shows the numbers of the nearest weaker chip, and names that chip. Hover over it to see how many sessions it comes from. Click it to open the game on getobelisk.app.
- **On [getobelisk.app](https://getobelisk.app)**, one table lists every game players ran, the most played first. It has a column per chip, from the M1 to the newest. Each cell shows the median frame rate, and its 1% low on hover: the rate the slowest 1% of frames stay under. The last columns show how often the game crashed and when it was last played.
- A session counts toward the frame rate once it lasts a minute. Shorter ones are mostly loading screens and menus, so they only count toward crashes. A crash is a game that ends on an error by itself, never one you stopped from Obelisk.
- Players use different settings and resolutions, so read these numbers as an order of magnitude.

## Privacy

Obelisk has no account of its own and does not track what you do in it. It talks to Steam, Epic Games and GOG to sign you in and get your games, to getobelisk.app for [how games run](#how-games-run) and for the bug reports you send, and to GitHub to look for a new version of Obelisk.

- **What Obelisk sends.** When a game closes, one report goes to getobelisk.app:
  - the game: its store, its ID in that store and its name,
  - how it ran: how long, how many frames it showed, the median frame rate, the 1% low and the hitches (frames shown more than 100 ms after the previous one),
  - how it ended: its exit code or signal, and whether you stopped it from Obelisk,
  - the Mac: its chip, GPU cores, model, memory and macOS version,
  - the versions of Obelisk and [Voile](https://github.com/Zagrios/voile) it ran with.
- **What it never sends.** Nothing in a report names you or ties two reports together: no account, no store ID of yours, no device ID. The site's database keeps each report and the time it arrived, not your IP address.
- **Turning it off.** Turn off **Share game performance** in **Settings → Games**. It is on by default. With it off, Obelisk sends nothing when a game closes, and still shows Expected FPS.
- **Bug reports.** Obelisk sends one only when you send it yourself, from **SOS** on a game's page or **I found a bug** in **Settings → Help**. It holds what you wrote, the contact you gave if any, your Mac's chip, model and macOS version, and the versions of Obelisk and Voile. With **Attach logs** on, it adds the files the sheet lists: the game's logs, Obelisk's log from the last hour and recent crash reports. Obelisk removes your user name from file paths and the device identifiers macOS writes in crash reports. getobelisk.app passes the report to a private channel of Obelisk's Discord server and keeps nothing.

## Known limitations

- Only games you own through Steam, Epic Games or GOG appear. Adding other games by hand is not supported yet.
- Games install in Obelisk's library folder, shown in **Settings → Storage**. Another location cannot be chosen yet.
- Steam: Workshop content and beta branches are not available yet.
- GOG: Cloud saves, friends and GOG Galaxy's online features are not available yet. Games only offered in GOG's older download format cannot be installed yet.
- Games whose anti-cheat does not accept Wine or Linux do not run yet (see [Windows games](#windows-games)).

## FAQ

<details>
<summary><b>Do I need Steam, the Epic Games Launcher or GOG Galaxy installed?</b></summary>
<br>
No. Obelisk talks to the stores directly. It downloads, updates and launches games without them.
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Is my password safe?</b></summary>
<br>
Obelisk never saves your password. Your Steam password goes to Steam to sign in and is then forgotten. Epic Games and GOG passwords are typed on their own websites, which Obelisk never reads. With <b>Remember me</b> on, only the session is kept, in your macOS Keychain.
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Where are my games installed?</b></summary>
<br>
In <code>~/Library/Application Support/com.zagrios.obelisk/Games</code>. <b>Settings → Storage → Show in Finder</b> opens the folder.
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Can I play while something downloads?</b></summary>
<br>
Yes. Any installed game launches while others download. Automatic updates pause while you play and resume afterwards.
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>What happens if I quit Obelisk while playing?</b></summary>
<br>
Closing Obelisk's window keeps the game running, and Obelisk stays in the menu bar. Quitting Obelisk stops the game, after syncing its Cloud saves.
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Will a game run well on my Mac?</b></summary>
<br>
Look at its <b>Expected FPS</b> on its page in Obelisk, or find it in the table on <a href="https://getobelisk.app">getobelisk.app</a>. If nobody has played it yet, play it once: your session fills in the table for the next players.
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Does Obelisk collect data about me?</b></summary>
<br>
Not about you. When a game closes, Obelisk sends how the game ran and which Mac it ran on, with nothing that identifies you, and you can turn that off. See <a href="#privacy">Privacy</a>.
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Is Obelisk free?</b></summary>
<br>
Yes. Obelisk is free, and you only play games you own.
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>How do I remove Obelisk completely?</b></summary>
<br>
Deleting the app alone leaves your games and settings on the Mac. To remove everything:

1. Quit Obelisk and move it from Applications to the Trash.
2. In Finder, choose **Go → Go to Folder…**, enter `~/Library`, and delete:
   - `Application Support/com.zagrios.obelisk`: your games, their Windows environments and [Voile](https://github.com/Zagrios/voile),
   - `Caches/com.zagrios.obelisk`, `HTTPStorages/com.zagrios.obelisk` and `WebKit/com.zagrios.obelisk`,
   - `Preferences/com.zagrios.obelisk.plist`,
   - `Logs/Obelisk`.
3. In the Keychain Access app, delete the items named `com.zagrios.obelisk.steam`, `com.zagrios.obelisk.epic` and `com.zagrios.obelisk.gog`.
</details>

## Support

Found a bug or a game that does not work? The quickest way to tell us is from Obelisk: press **SOS** on the game's page, or **I found a bug** in **Settings → Help** for a problem with Obelisk itself. Say what happened, keep **Attach logs** on and send. Obelisk then shows a code. Mention it on [Discord](https://discord.gg/h5a7F4rZ6f), or press **Open a GitHub issue** to get GitHub's bug form with your report already filled in.

You can also [open an issue](https://github.com/Zagrios/obelisk/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml) yourself. The form asks for your Mac, its macOS version, your Obelisk version (shown in **Settings**) and what happened.

Have an idea? [Request a feature](https://github.com/Zagrios/obelisk/issues/new?template=feature_request.yml), or press **Request a feature** in **Settings → Help**.

Logs help a lot. They are in `~/Library/Logs/Obelisk` (Finder: **Go → Go to Folder…**). Attach the ones of the game you tried, after checking they show nothing you want to keep private. A Windows game's log starts with a line that says how Obelisk ran it: its engine, graphics backend, [Voile](https://github.com/Zagrios/voile) release and the launch arguments you added.

Enjoying Obelisk? Star the repository: it helps other Mac players find it.

// Display identity can change without moving the user's library.
PRODUCT_NAME = Obelisk

```xcconfig
// Release builds are what strangers download: Developer ID, timestamped, no debugger entitlement.
// Signing.local.xcconfig may pin the certificate by its SHA-1 instead of this name.
DISTRIBUTION_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY = Developer ID Application
#include "Signing.xcconfig"
CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY = $(DISTRIBUTION_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY)
CODE_SIGN_INJECT_BASE_ENTITLEMENTS = NO
OTHER_CODE_SIGN_FLAGS = $(inherited) --timestamp

```

`apps/macos/Config/Signing.local.xcconfig.example`:

```example
// Copy to Signing.local.xcconfig, then select existing identities shown by:
// security find-identity -v -p codesigning
// Debug keeps one development certificate so Keychain recognizes every build.
CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY = Apple Development
// Release needs a Developer ID Application certificate for notarization.
DISTRIBUTION_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY = Developer ID Application
DEVELOPMENT_TEAM = YOUR_TEAM_ID

```

`apps/macos/Config/Signing.xcconfig`:

```xcconfig
// Keep the same signing identity across builds so Keychain recognizes Obelisk.
CODE_SIGN_STYLE = Manual
CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY = Apple Development

// Machine-specific certificate selection stays outside version control.
#include? "Signing.local.xcconfig"

```

`apps/macos/Obelisk/App/AppIdentity.swift`:

```swift
import Foundation

enum AppIdentity {
    // Keep the display name independent of storage identifiers for a future rename.
    static let name = Bundle.main.object(forInfoDictionaryKey: "CFBundleDisplayName") as? String ?? "Obelisk"
    static let version = Bundle.main.object(forInfoDictionaryKey: "CFBundleShortVersionString") as? String ?? "0.1.0"
    static let storageIdentifier = "com.zagrios.obelisk"

    static var libraryDirectory: URL {
        // The override is for isolated development and integration tests.
        if let path = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["OBELISK_LIBRARY_DIRECTORY"], !path.isEmpty {
            return URL(fileURLWithPath: path, isDirectory: true)
        }
        return URL.applicationSupportDirectory.appending(path: storageIdentifier, directoryHint: .isDirectory)
    }
}

extension ObeliskLocations {
    /// Every path of an Obelisk whose library lives in `library`. Tests pass their own.
    static func of(library: URL) -> ObeliskLocations {
        obeliskLocations(library: library.path, bundle: Bundle.main.bundleURL.path, home: NSHomeDirectory())
    }

    @MainActor static let live = of(library: AppIdentity.libraryDirectory)
}

`apps/macos/Obelisk/App/AppLifecycle.swift`:

```swift
import AppKit
import SwiftUI

/// Quitting Obelisk, or closing its window, hides it: it keeps running in the
/// menu bar, as Steam does, so its Game sessions and Transfers go on. It really
/// quits from its menu bar item, after stopping a running game, when macOS
/// logs out, restarts or shuts down, or for Sparkle to install a new version.
@MainActor
final class AppLifecycle: NSObject, NSApplicationDelegate {
    /// Asks the menu bar item, which can open windows, to show the library.
    static let showLibrary = Notification.Name("com.zagrios.obelisk.showLibrary")
    /// How long quitting waits for stopped games to settle their Cloud saves.
    private static let settleTimeout: Duration = .seconds(60)

    /// Whether a game runs, and how to stop every one of them.
    var games: (running: @MainActor () -> Bool, stop: @MainActor () async -> Void) = ({ false }, {})
    /// The library cache, whose last changes are still being written.
    var libraryCache: LibraryCache?
    /// Games are being stopped before Obelisk ends.
    private var stopping = false
    /// Obelisk is ending: its termination is let through.
    private var quitting = false
    /// Obelisk opens again once it has exited.
    private var reopens = false
    private var windowClosing: NSObjectProtocol?

    func applicationDidFinishLaunching(_ notification: Notification) {
        // An Obelisk that died took its games' sessions along, but Wine's
        // Windows processes froze on their own. None of them can belong to
        // this Obelisk yet.
        // The test host is no Obelisk of its own: it leaves every game alone.
        if ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["XCTestConfigurationFilePath"] == nil {
            let locations = ObeliskLocations.live
            Task.detached(priority: .utility) { _ = endOrphanedWindowsGames(locations: locations) }
        }
        // Closing the last library window hides Obelisk like quitting does.
        windowClosing = NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
            forName: NSWindow.willCloseNotification, object: nil, queue: .main
        ) { notification in
            let closing = notification.object as? NSWindow
            MainActor.assumeIsolated {
                let others = NSApp.windows.filter { $0 !== closing && $0.isVisible && $0.canBecomeMain }
                if others.isEmpty { NSApp.setActivationPolicy(.accessory) }
            }
        }
    }

    func applicationShouldTerminate(_ sender: NSApplication) -> NSApplication.TerminateReply {
        if quitting { return .terminateNow }
        guard Self.systemQuit else {
            hide()
            return .terminateCancel
        }
        // macOS waits while the games settle, within its own logout deadline.
        quitting = true
        Task {
            await stopGames()
            NSApp.reply(toApplicationShouldTerminate: true)
        }
        return .terminateLater
    }

    func applicationWillTerminate(_ notification: Notification) {
        libraryCache?.flush()
        if reopens { Self.reopenOnceExited() }
    }

    func applicationShouldHandleReopen(_ sender: NSApplication, hasVisibleWindows flag: Bool) -> Bool {
        show()
        return false
    }

    /// Shows the library window and Obelisk's Dock icon.
    func show() {
        NSApp.setActivationPolicy(.regular)
        NotificationCenter.default.post(name: Self.showLibrary, object: nil)
        NSApp.activate()
    }

    /// Closes Obelisk's windows and hides its Dock icon; it keeps running.
    func hide() {
        for window in NSApp.windows where window.canBecomeMain { window.close() }
        NSApp.setActivationPolicy(.accessory)
    }

    /// Really quits: a running game is stopped first, once the player agrees,
    /// and its Cloud saves settle before Obelisk exits.
    func quit() {
        quit(running: L10n.string("app.quit.running.message"), stop: L10n.string("app.quit.stop")) { [self] in
            terminate()
        }
    }

    /// Quits as `quit()` does, then opens Obelisk again once it has exited, so
    /// a new language applies everywhere.
    func restart() {
        quit(running: L10n.string("app.restart.running.message"), stop: L10n.string("app.restart.stop")) { [self] in
            reopens = true
            terminate()
        }
    }

    /// Quits as `quit()` does for Sparkle to install Obelisk's new version:
    /// `install` lets Sparkle end Obelisk, then open the new one.
    func update(_ install: @escaping () -> Void) {
        quit(running: L10n.string("app.update.running.message"), stop: L10n.string("app.update.stop"), then: install)
    }

    private func quit(running message: String, stop: String, then exit: @escaping () -> Void) {
        guard !stopping else { return }
        if games.running(), !Self.confirmsStoppingGames(running: message, stop: stop) { return }
        stopping = true
        Task {
            await stopGames()
            stopping = false
            quitting = true
            exit()
        }
    }

    /// Ends Obelisk. While a sheet is open AppKit refuses with a beep, without
    /// asking the delegate: Obelisk stays as it was, so the player can quit
    /// again once the sheet is closed.
    private func terminate() {
        NSApp.terminate(nil)
        quitting = false
        reopens = false
    }

    /// Asks whether to stop the running game: `message` tells why, `stop`
    /// is the button that agrees.
    static func confirmsStoppingGames(running message: String, stop: String) -> Bool {
        NSApp.activate()
        let alert = NSAlert()
        alert.messageText = L10n.string("app.quit.running.title")
        alert.informativeText = message
        alert.addButton(withTitle: stop)
        alert.addButton(withTitle: L10n.string("ui.common.cancel"))
        return alert.runModal() == .alertFirstButtonReturn
    }

    /// A shell that outlives this Obelisk opens its bundle again once its
    /// process is gone: two Obelisks never run at once.
    private static func reopenOnceExited() {
        let shell = Process()
        shell.executableURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: "/bin/sh")
        shell.arguments = [
            "-c", "while /bin/kill -0 \"$1\" 2>/dev/null; do /bin/sleep 0.2; done; exec /usr/bin/open \"$2\"",
            "obelisk-restart", String(ProcessInfo.processInfo.processIdentifier), Bundle.main.bundlePath,
        ]
        try? shell.run()
    }

    private func stopGames() async {
        guard games.running() else { return }
        await games.stop()
        let deadline = ContinuousClock.now + Self.settleTimeout
        while games.running() && ContinuousClock.now < deadline {
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(250))
        }
    }

    /// Whether macOS itself asks Obelisk to quit, to log out, restart or
    /// shut down, rather than the player.
    private static var systemQuit: Bool {
        // The 'why?' attribute of the quit Apple event names that reason.
        let reason = AEKeyword(0x7768_793F)
        return NSAppleEventManager.shared().currentAppleEvent?.attributeDescriptor(forKeyword: reason) != nil
    }
}

/// Obelisk's menu bar item, which stays while its windows are closed. It
/// tells the lifecycle which games run.
struct AppMenuBarLabel: View {
    let model: AppModel
    let lifecycle: AppLifecycle
    @Environment(\.openWindow) private var openWindow

    var body: some View {
        Image("MenuBarIcon")
            .onAppear {
                lifecycle.libraryCache = model.libraryCache
                model.overlay.showLibrary = { lifecycle.show() }
                model.restart = { lifecycle.restart() }
                model.updates.quitToInstall = { install in lifecycle.update(install) }
                let (steam, epic, gog) = (model.steam.gameSessions, model.epic.gameSessions, model.gog.gameSessions)
                lifecycle.games = (
                    running: { steam.active != nil || epic.active != nil || gog.active != nil },
                    stop: {
                        await steam.stop()
                        await epic.stop()
                        await gog.stop()
                    }
                )
            }
            .onReceive(NotificationCenter.default.publisher(for: AppLifecycle.showLibrary)) { _ in
                openWindow(id: "main")
            }
    }
}

struct AppMenuBarMenu: View {
    let lifecycle: AppLifecycle

    var body: some View {
        Button(L10n.string("app.menu.open")) { lifecycle.show() }
        Divider()
        Button(L10n.string("app.menu.quit")) { lifecycle.quit() }
    }
}

`apps/macos/Obelisk/App/AppModel.swift`:

```swift
import Observation
import SwiftUI

/// A storefront whose account shows its friends: Steam and Epic.
@MainActor
protocol FriendsStorefront: AnyObject {
    var friends: FriendsPresentationState? { get }
    func closeFriends()
    func retryFriends()
    func signOut()
}

extension SteamModel: FriendsStorefront {}
extension WebAccountModel: FriendsStorefront where Store == EpicGames {}

@MainActor
@Observable
final class AppModel {
    var selection: LibrarySection = .home {
        didSet { searchText = "" }
    }
    var searchText = ""
    let libraryDirectory: String
    let steam: SteamModel
    let epic: EpicModel
    let gog: GogModel
    /// The in-game overlay, over whichever storefront's game runs.
    let overlay: GameOverlayController
    /// Every storefront's Transfers, in their one queue.
    let downloads: DownloadsModel
    /// Where Obelisk installs games, which the player may change.
    let gamesFolder: GamesFolderModel
    /// The storefront's store, open over the whole window.
    var presentedStore: StorePresentation?
    /// The bug report being written, open over the whole window.
    var bugReport: BugReportModel?
    private(set) var activeFriendsAccount: FriendsAccountIdentity?
    /// The game whose page Home opened, while its storefront still shows it.
    var homeGame: HomeGame.ID?
    /// The storefronts whose saved session is still restoring since launch,
    /// so Home tells a library on its way from a signed-out one.
    private(set) var restoringStorefronts = Set(LibrarySection.storefronts)
    var appearance: AppAppearance {
        didSet { defaults.set(appearance.rawValue, forKey: "appearance") }
    }
    /// The language Obelisk shows from its next start.
    var language: AppLanguage {
        didSet { language.save(in: defaults) }
    }
    /// Whether Obelisk shows another language than the chosen one until it
    /// restarts.
    var languageNeedsRestart: Bool {
        language.resolved(system: AppLanguage.systemLanguages) != L10n.languageCode
    }
    /// Quits Obelisk and opens it again; its lifecycle provides it.
    @ObservationIgnored var restart: () -> Void = {}
    /// Whether every storefront installs a game's newer build as soon as it
    /// is published, rather than at the game's next launch.
    var updatesGamesAutomatically: Bool {
        didSet {
            defaults.set(updatesGamesAutomatically, forKey: Self.automaticUpdatesKey)
            applyAutomaticUpdates()
        }
    }
    static let automaticUpdatesKey = "obelisk.games.updateAutomatically"
    /// Whether Obelisk reports each game's frame rate and how it ended to
    /// getobelisk.app, which shows how games run on each Mac.
    var sharesGamePerformance: Bool {
        didSet {
            defaults.set(sharesGamePerformance, forKey: Self.sharePerformanceKey)
            performance.isEnabled = sharesGamePerformance
        }
    }
    static let sharePerformanceKey = "obelisk.games.sharePerformance"
    @ObservationIgnored let performance: PerformanceReports
    /// How each game runs on this Mac's chip, as other players measured it.
    let estimates: PerformanceEstimates
    /// Obelisk's own new versions.
    let updates: AppUpdates

    /// The last library of every storefront account.
    @ObservationIgnored let libraryCache: LibraryCache
    @ObservationIgnored private let defaults: UserDefaults

    /// The test host's models register no Shift-Tab, open no overlay and post
    /// no notification.
    init(directory: URL = AppIdentity.libraryDirectory, defaults: UserDefaults = .standard,
         defaultsDomain: String = Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier ?? AppIdentity.storageIdentifier, steam: SteamModel? = nil,
         epic: EpicModel? = nil, gog: GogModel? = nil, downloads: DownloadsModel? = nil,
         gamesFolder: GamesFolderModel? = nil,
         performance: PerformanceReports? = nil, estimates: PerformanceEstimates? = nil, updates: AppUpdates? = nil,
         overlay: GameOverlayEnvironment = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["XCTestConfigurationFilePath"] == nil
            ? .live : .inert) {
        libraryDirectory = directory.path
        self.defaults = defaults
        appearance = AppAppearance(rawValue: defaults.string(forKey: "appearance") ?? "system") ?? .system
        language = AppLanguage(defaults: defaults, domain: defaultsDomain)
        updatesGamesAutomatically = defaults.object(forKey: Self.automaticUpdatesKey) as? Bool ?? true
        let sharesGamePerformance = defaults.object(forKey: Self.sharePerformanceKey) as? Bool ?? true
        self.sharesGamePerformance = sharesGamePerformance
        // Every storefront's library shares one cache, as every cache of the
        // directory does, `LaunchHistory.live`'s included.
        libraryCache = LibraryCache(directory: directory.path)
        self.steam = steam ?? SteamModel(directory: directory, libraryCache: libraryCache)
        self.epic = epic ?? EpicModel(directory: directory, libraryCache: libraryCache)
        self.gog = gog ?? GogModel(directory: directory, libraryCache: libraryCache)
        self.overlay = GameOverlayController(steam: self.steam, epic: self.epic, gog: self.gog, environment: overlay)
        self.steam.overlay = self.overlay
        self.steam.notifier = overlay.notifier
        self.downloads = downloads ?? DownloadsModel()
        self.gamesFolder = gamesFolder ?? GamesFolderModel(library: directory)
        let performance = performance ?? PerformanceReports(isEnabled: sharesGamePerformance)
        performance.isEnabled = sharesGamePerformance
        self.performance = performance
        self.estimates = estimates ?? PerformanceEstimates()
        self.updates = updates ?? AppUpdates()
        self.downloads.progress = { [weak self] item in self?.downloadTransfer(item) }
        applyAutomaticUpdates()
        reportPerformance()
    }

    /// Each storefront's ended games go to the performance reports, with the
    /// title its library knows them by.
    private func reportPerformance() {
        report(steam.gameSessions) { [steam] in steam.gameName(appId: $0) }
        report(epic.gameSessions) { [epic] id in epic.library.game(id)?.title }
        report(gog.gameSessions) { [gog] id in gog.library.game(id)?.title }
    }

    private func report<Store: GameStorefront>(_ sessions: GameSessions<Store>,
                                               title: @escaping (Store.GameID) -> String?) {
        let performance = performance
        sessions.reportPlayed = { game, played in
            guard let id = Store.storeGameID(game) else { return }
            performance.report(played, of: id, titled: title(game), in: Store.storefront)
        }
    }

    /// Opens the bug report sheet on `subject`.
    func reportBug(_ subject: BugReportSubject) {
        bugReport = BugReportModel(subject: subject, sources: .live)
    }

    /// A queued Transfer's progress, from its storefront's installations.
    func downloadTransfer(_ item: DownloadItem) -> GameTransfer? {
        switch item.storefront {
        case .steam: steam.installations.transfer(named: item.game)
        case .epic: epic.installations.transfer(named: item.game)
        case .gog: gog.installations.transfer(named: item.game)
        }
    }

    /// What the download queue shows of a queued Transfer's game.
    func downloadGame(_ item: DownloadItem) -> DownloadGame {
        switch item.storefront {
        case .steam: steam.downloadGame(item, cover: SteamView.cover, artwork: SteamView.heroArtwork)
        case .epic: epic.downloadGame(item, cover: EpicView.cover, artwork: EpicView.heroArtwork)
        case .gog: gog.downloadGame(item, cover: GogView.cover, artwork: GogView.heroArtwork)
        }
    }

    /// Opens a queued Transfer's game page, in its storefront's library.
    func openDownload(_ item: DownloadItem) {
        downloads.isPresented = false
        switch item.storefront {
        case .steam: open(item, in: steam)
        case .epic: open(item, in: epic)
        case .gog: open(item, in: gog)
        }
    }

    private func open<Model: LibraryStorefront>(_ item: DownloadItem, in model: Model) {
        guard let id = Model.Store.game(item.game), let game = model.library.game(id) else { return }
        selection = item.storefront.section
        model.open(game)
    }

    /// The installed games outside the games folder: their move was stopped,
    /// or they were installed meanwhile. Two accounts' installations of one
    /// folder count once.
    var gamesOutsideFolder: Int {
        let directories = steam.installations.receipts.map(\.directory)
            + epic.installations.receipts.map(\.directory)
            + gog.installations.receipts.map(\.directory)
        return Set(directories.filter { !gamesFolder.holds($0) }).count
    }

    /// The games whose move into the games folder waits or runs.
    var gamesMoving: Int {
        downloads.waiting.count(where: { $0.kind == .move }) + (downloads.running?.kind == .move ? 1 : 0)
    }

    private func applyAutomaticUpdates() {
        steam.installations.updatesAutomatically = updatesGamesAutomatically
        epic.installations.updatesAutomatically = updatesGamesAutomatically
        gog.installations.updatesAutomatically = updatesGamesAutomatically
    }

    /// The Cloud or Rosetta question shown over the whole app, whichever tab is
    /// open. One sheet at a time, in a fixed order.
    enum StorefrontPrompt: Equatable {
        case steamRosetta, steamCloud, epicRosetta, epicCloud, gogRosetta
    }

    var presentedPrompt: StorefrontPrompt? {
        if steam.rosetta.prompt != nil { return .steamRosetta }
        if steam.cloud.promptPresented { return .steamCloud }
        if epic.rosetta.prompt != nil { return .epicRosetta }
        if epic.cloud.promptPresented { return .epicCloud }
        if gog.rosetta.prompt != nil { return .gogRosetta }
        return nil
    }

    /// The storefront whose friends `storeID` names; GOG shows none.
    private func friendsModel(storeID: String?) -> (any FriendsStorefront)? {
        switch storeID {
        case "steam": steam
        case "epic": epic
        default: nil
        }
    }

    var presentedFriends: FriendsPresentationState? {
        guard let activeFriendsAccount else { return nil }
        let state = friendsModel(storeID: activeFriendsAccount.storeID)?.friends
        return state?.account == activeFriendsAccount ? state : nil
    }

    func presentFriends(storeID: String) {
        guard let model = friendsModel(storeID: storeID), let state = model.friends else { return }
        activeFriendsAccount = state.account
        for other in [steam, epic] as [any FriendsStorefront] where other !== model { other.closeFriends() }
    }

    func closeFriends(storeID: String? = nil) {
        if let storeID, activeFriendsAccount?.storeID != storeID { return }
        activeFriendsAccount = nil
        steam.closeFriends()
        epic.closeFriends()
    }

    func validateFriendsAccount() {
        if activeFriendsAccount != nil && presentedFriends == nil { closeFriends() }
    }

    func retryPresentedFriends() {
        friendsModel(storeID: activeFriendsAccount?.storeID)?.retryFriends()
    }

    func signInPresentedFriends() {
        friendsModel(storeID: activeFriendsAccount?.storeID)?.signOut()
        closeFriends()
    }

    /// Restores every storefront's saved session, so Home shows each library
    /// from launch. A signed-out store offers its sign-in on its own tab.
    func restoreStorefronts() async {
        let restorations = [
            Task { await steam.start(signIn: false); restoringStorefronts.remove(.steam) },
            Task { await epic.start(); restoringStorefronts.remove(.epic) },
            Task { await gog.start(); restoringStorefronts.remove(.gog) },
        ]
        for restoration in restorations { await restoration.value }
    }

    /// Reloads the open storefront's library; Home's, every storefront's.
    func refresh() {
        switch selection {
        case .home:
            steam.refresh()
            epic.refresh()
            gog.refresh()
        case .steam: steam.refresh()
        case .epic: epic.refresh()
        case .gog: gog.refresh()
        case .settings: break
        }
    }
}

`apps/macos/Obelisk/App/AppUpdates.swift`:

```swift
import Foundation
import Observation
import Sparkle

/// Obelisk's own updates, through Sparkle. Once a day Obelisk reads the latest
/// release's appcast.xml and, by default, downloads a newer version and
/// installs it when Obelisk really quits; otherwise Sparkle offers it in its
/// own window.
@MainActor
@Observable
final class AppUpdates {
    /// Whether a check may start now: not while one runs, nor in a build that
    /// never updates.
    private(set) var canCheck = false
    @ObservationIgnored private let relaunch: UpdateRelaunch
    @ObservationIgnored private let controller: SPUStandardUpdaterController
    @ObservationIgnored private var observation: NSKeyValueObservation?

    /// Debug builds and the test host never start: the latest release would
    /// replace them.
    init(starts: Bool = AppUpdates.startsByDefault) {
        let relaunch = UpdateRelaunch()
        self.relaunch = relaunch
        controller = SPUStandardUpdaterController(startingUpdater: starts, updaterDelegate: relaunch,
                                                  userDriverDelegate: nil)
        // Sparkle changes it on the main thread, as it does everything.
        observation = controller.updater.observe(\.canCheckForUpdates, options: [.initial, .new]) { [weak self] _, change in
            let canCheck = change.newValue ?? false
            MainActor.assumeIsolated { self?.canCheck = canCheck }
        }
    }

    /// Whether Obelisk downloads a new version by itself and installs it when
    /// it quits. Sparkle keeps the choice; its update window can change it too.
    var installsAutomatically: Bool {
        get {
            access(keyPath: \.installsAutomatically)
            return controller.updater.automaticallyDownloadsUpdates
        }
        set {
            withMutation(keyPath: \.installsAutomatically) {
                controller.updater.automaticallyDownloadsUpdates = newValue
            }
        }
    }

    /// How Obelisk quits when the player installs a new version from Sparkle's
    /// window, before Sparkle opens the new one: quitting otherwise only hides
    /// Obelisk. It calls `install` once Obelisk may end.
    var quitToInstall: (_ install: @escaping () -> Void) -> Void {
        get { relaunch.quit }
        set { relaunch.quit = newValue }
    }

    /// Looks for a new version now, in Sparkle's window.
    func check() {
        controller.checkForUpdates(nil)
    }

    private static var startsByDefault: Bool {
        #if DEBUG
        false
        #else
        true
        #endif
    }
}

/// Holds Sparkle's relaunch until the lifecycle lets Obelisk quit.
@MainActor
private final class UpdateRelaunch: NSObject, SPUUpdaterDelegate {
    var quit: (_ install: @escaping () -> Void) -> Void = { $0() }

    func updater(_ updater: SPUUpdater, shouldPostponeRelaunchForUpdate item: SUAppcastItem,
                 untilInvokingBlock installHandler: @escaping () -> Void) -> Bool {
        quit(installHandler)
        return true
    }
}
