`apps/macos/Obelisk/Models/AccountLibrary.swift`:

```swift
import Foundation
import Observation

/// A game of an account's library, from what its own library entry tells.
/// What the entry does not tell loads into the library.
protocol LibraryGame: Identifiable, Equatable where ID: Comparable & Sendable {
    var title: String { get }
    /// How long the account played the game, as its entry tells; nil when it does not.
    var playtime: Duration? { get }
    /// When the account last played the game on its storefront; nil when the entry does not tell.
    var lastPlayedOnStorefront: Date? { get }
    /// What the entry tells that `sort` orders the game by, such as its date
    /// added; nil when it tells nothing.
    func libraryValue(for sort: StorefrontLibrarySort) -> Double?
}

/// A game of the Library cache with what the cache knew apart from its entry.
struct CachedLibraryGame<Game> {
    let game: Game
    var playtime: Duration? = nil
    /// Each order's value, such as Steam's license date or the achievements' share.
    var values: [StorefrontLibrarySort: Double] = [:]
}

/// One storefront account's library (see CONTEXT.md, Account library). Its
/// session pushes what it loads; the library page, Home, the game page, the
/// downloads and the overlay read it. Ordering every game is the costly part:
/// each order is kept until what it reads changes, and a search or a filter
/// only narrows a kept order.
@MainActor
@Observable
final class AccountLibrary<Store: InstallationStorefront, Game: LibraryGame> where Game.ID == Store.GameID {
    /// The games as the storefront lists them.
    private(set) var games: [Game] = [] {
        didSet { changes &+= 1 }
    }
    var searchText = ""
    var filter: StorefrontLibraryFilter = .all
    /// Every storefront opens on its most recently played games.
    var sort: StorefrontLibrarySort = .lastPlayed
    /// The Library cache of an account whose session has not connected yet.
    private(set) var isCached = false

    /// The cached or connected account, whose launches date the games.
    private var account: Store.AccountID? {
        didSet { if account != oldValue { changes &+= 1 } }
    }
    /// Each played game's playtime, once the storefront or the cache told it.
    private var playtimes: [Game.ID: Duration] = [:] {
        didSet { changes &+= 1 }
    }
    /// Each order's values by game, such as Steam's license dates or each
    /// game's achievements: what the Library cache or an earlier load knew
    /// shows until a load replaces it.
    private var values: [StorefrontLibrarySort: [Game.ID: Double]] = [:]
    /// Each order's revision, which changes whenever its values may have.
    private var revisions: [StorefrontLibrarySort: Int] = [:]
    /// Changes with the games, their playtimes and the account whose launches they read.
    private var changes = 0
    private var playtimeLoad = PlaytimeLoad.idle

    private enum PlaytimeLoad { case idle, loading, failed }

    private struct Criteria: Hashable {
        var query: String
        var sort: StorefrontLibrarySort
        var filter: StorefrontLibraryFilter
        /// Each installed game's size, read only by the installed filter and
        /// the order by size.
        var installed: [Game.ID: UInt64]
        /// What the order read apart from the games.
        var inputs: Inputs
    }

    /// What an order reads apart from the games: its values, and for the
    /// order by size, the installed games' sizes.
    private struct Inputs: Hashable {
        var values: Int
        var sizes: [Game.ID: UInt64]
    }

    @ObservationIgnored private let history: LaunchHistory
    @ObservationIgnored private let cache: LibraryCache?
    @ObservationIgnored private let installations: GameInstallations<Store>
    @ObservationIgnored private var keptRevision: Int?
    @ObservationIgnored private var orders: [StorefrontLibrarySort: (inputs: Inputs, games: [Game])] = [:]
    /// A few narrowed results, so Home's and the library page's do not
    /// replace each other on every pass.
    @ObservationIgnored private var narrowed: [Criteria: [Game]] = [:]
    /// The library's featured game, once read: it may have none.
    @ObservationIgnored private var featuredGame: Game??
    @ObservationIgnored private var tasks: [StorefrontLibrarySort: Task<Void, Never>] = [:]
    @ObservationIgnored private var playtimeTask: Task<Void, Never>?

    init(history: LaunchHistory, cache: LibraryCache?, installations: GameInstallations<Store>) {
        self.history = history
        self.cache = cache
        self.installations = installations
    }

    // MARK: Reading

    /// The games the search and the filter keep, in `sort` order.
    var shown: [Game] { games(by: sort, filter: filter, matching: searchText) }

    /// The whole library's featured game: the last played, else the most
    /// played, equal ones by name.
    var featured: Game? {
        keep(revision)
        if let featuredGame { return featuredGame }
        let game: Game?
        if let first = orders[.lastPlayed]?.games.first, lastPlayed(of: first) != nil {
            // The kept last played order already has it first.
            game = first
        } else {
            game = LibraryOrder.featured(games, title: \.title, id: \.id, lastPlayed: lastPlayed(of:),
                                         playtime: playtime(of:))
        }
        featuredGame = .some(game)
        return game
    }

    /// Whether the library shows: once its account connected, or from the
    /// cache while the saved session restores.
    func shows(connected: Bool, restoring: Bool) -> Bool { connected || (isCached && restoring) }

    /// The featured game, unless a search or a filter narrows the library.
    var hero: Game? {
        guard searchText.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).isEmpty, filter == .all else { return nil }
        return featured
    }

    /// The whole library, or what `filter` and `query` keep, in `sort` order,
    /// kept between reads.
    func games(by sort: StorefrontLibrarySort, filter: StorefrontLibraryFilter = .all,
               matching query: String = "") -> [Game] {
        // Read every input even when a result is kept, so the library keeps
        // updating after a search, a filter, an installation or new metadata.
        let games = self.games
        keep(revision)
        let receipts = filter == .installed || sort == .size ? installations.receipts : []
        let installed = Dictionary(receipts.map { ($0.gameID, $0.totalBytes) }, uniquingKeysWith: +)
        // What only one order reads, such as library dates or the sizes an
        // installation changes, changes only that order.
        let inputs = Inputs(values: revisions[sort, default: 0], sizes: sort == .size ? installed : [:])
        let criteria = Criteria(query: query.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines), sort: sort,
                                filter: filter, installed: installed, inputs: inputs)
        if let kept = narrowed[criteria] { return kept }
        let ordered: [Game]
        if let order = orders[sort], order.inputs == inputs {
            ordered = order.games
        } else {
            ordered = LibraryOrder.order(games, title: \.title, id: \.id, rank: rank(sort, sizes: inputs.sizes))
            orders[sort] = (inputs, ordered)
        }
        let kept = criteria.query.isEmpty && filter == .all ? ordered : ordered.filter { game in
            guard criteria.query.isEmpty || game.title.localizedStandardContains(criteria.query) else { return false }
            switch filter {
            case .all: return true
            case .installed: return criteria.installed[game.id] != nil
            case .played: return playtime(of: game) != nil || lastPlayed(of: game) != nil
            }
        }
        if narrowed.count >= 4 { narrowed.removeAll() }
        narrowed[criteria] = kept
        return kept
    }

    func game(_ id: Game.ID) -> Game? { games.first { $0.id == id } }

    /// How long the account played the game; nil until the storefront told
    /// it, or when the game was never played.
    func playtime(of game: Game) -> Duration? {
        (playtimes[game.id] ?? game.playtime).flatMap { $0 > .zero ? $0 : nil }
    }

    /// When the game was last played: on its storefront, or later from
    /// Obelisk by this account.
    func lastPlayed(of game: Game) -> Date? {
        // The cached library's account, while its session connects.
        let launched = account.flatMap { history.lastLaunch(of: game.id, account: $0, in: Store.self) }
        return [game.lastPlayedOnStorefront, launched].compactMap { $0 }.max()
    }

    /// What orders `game` by date added or achievements; nil when nothing
    /// told it. A game the storefront did not answer for has none, as one it
    /// has nothing to tell of.
    func value(of game: Game, for sort: StorefrontLibrarySort) -> Double? {
        values[sort]?[game.id] ?? game.libraryValue(for: sort)
    }

    /// Whether the filter or the order reads the games' playtimes.
    private var usesPlaytime: Bool { filter == .played || sort == .playtime }

    /// What the filter or the order still waits for while it loads.
    var pendingMetadata: String? {
        usesPlaytime && playtimeLoad == .loading ? L10n.string("ui.library.loading_playtime") : nil
    }

    /// What the filter or the order could not load, offered a retry.
    var missingMetadata: String? {
        usesPlaytime && playtimeLoad == .failed ? L10n.string("ui.library.playtime_unavailable") : nil
    }

    // MARK: Loading

    /// Shows the account's Library cache while its session connects, unless
    /// games show. True when shown.
    @discardableResult
    func showCache(of account: Store.AccountID, _ read: (LibraryCache) -> [CachedLibraryGame<Game>]) -> Bool {
        guard games.isEmpty, let cache else { return false }
        let cached = read(cache)
        guard !cached.isEmpty else { return false }
        self.account = account
        isCached = true
        games = cached.map(\.game)
        playtimes = Dictionary(cached.compactMap { entry in entry.playtime.map { (entry.game.id, $0) } },
                               uniquingKeysWith: max)
        for sort in StorefrontLibrarySort.allCases {
            set(Dictionary(cached.compactMap { entry in entry.values[sort].map { (entry.game.id, $0) } },
                           uniquingKeysWith: max), for: sort)
        }
        return true
    }

    /// Hides a cached library whose session did not connect: another account
    /// may sign in next. The cache keeps it. True when one showed.
    @discardableResult
    func dropCache() -> Bool {
        guard isCached else { return false }
        reset()
        account = nil
        isCached = false
        return true
    }

    /// The account's session connected. Keeps the library when it showed this
    /// account's cache, else empties it. True when kept.
    @discardableResult
    func connect(_ account: Store.AccountID) -> Bool {
        let kept = isCached && self.account == account
        if !kept { reset() }
        self.account = account
        isCached = false
        return kept
    }

    /// Shows the games the session listed.
    func show(_ games: [Game]) {
        if self.games != games { self.games = games }
    }

    /// Loads the playtimes through `read`, replacing a load in flight; they
    /// show as loading at once, and a failure keeps what showed and offers
    /// the retry. Playtimes only order and filter the library, so the library
    /// never waits for them. `next` runs once the load ends, unless a newer
    /// load, a connection or the sign-out replaced it.
    func loadPlaytimes(_ read: @escaping @Sendable () async throws -> [Game.ID: Duration],
                       then next: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void) {
        playtimeTask?.cancel()
        playtimeLoad = .loading
        playtimeTask = Task { [weak self] in
            let loaded = try? await read()
            // UniFFI can return after the load was replaced.
            guard !Task.isCancelled, let self else { return }
            self.playtimeTask = nil
            if let loaded {
                if loaded != self.playtimes { self.playtimes = loaded }
                self.playtimeLoad = .idle
            } else {
                self.playtimeLoad = .failed
            }
            next()
        }
    }

    /// Loads `sort`'s values through `read`, unless they are loading.
    func load(_ sort: StorefrontLibrarySort, read: @escaping @Sendable () async throws -> [Game.ID: Double]) {
        guard tasks[sort] == nil else { return }
        tasks[sort] = Task { [weak self] in
            let loaded = try? await read()
            // UniFFI can return after the account was replaced.
            guard !Task.isCancelled, let self else { return }
            self.tasks[sort] = nil
            // A failed load changes nothing: the library's next load asks again.
            if let loaded { self.set(loaded, for: sort) }
        }
    }

    /// Account revocation: forgets the account's Library cache entry and
    /// launches, the games and what is known of them, the search and the
    /// filter. The order stays the player's.
    func forget() {
        if let account {
            cache?.forget(account: Store.account(account))
            history.forget(account: account, in: Store.self)
        }
        reset()
        account = nil
        isCached = false
        searchText = ""
        filter = .all
    }

    // MARK: Implementation

    /// Changes whenever a game, or what every order reads of one, may have.
    private var revision: Int { changes &+ history.revision }

    /// Forgets every kept result once the library's revision changed.
    private func keep(_ revision: Int) {
        guard revision != keptRevision else { return }
        keptRevision = revision
        orders.removeAll()
        narrowed.removeAll()
        featuredGame = nil
    }

    /// What places each game in `sort` order, the greatest first; a game
    /// without one goes after the others. `sizes` are the installed games'.
    private func rank(_ sort: StorefrontLibrarySort, sizes: [Game.ID: UInt64]) -> (Game) -> Double? {
        switch sort {
        case .name: return { _ in nil }
        case .playtime: return { self.playtime(of: $0).map { Double($0.components.seconds) } }
        case .lastPlayed: return { self.lastPlayed(of: $0)?.timeIntervalSince1970 }
        case .size: return { sizes[$0.id].map { Double($0) } }
        case .achievements, .dateAdded: return { self.value(of: $0, for: sort) }
        }
    }

    /// Forgets the games and everything known of them, as another account's
    /// library replaces them.
    private func reset() {
        tasks.values.forEach { $0.cancel() }
        tasks.removeAll()
        playtimeTask?.cancel()
        playtimeTask = nil
        playtimeLoad = .idle
        games = []
        playtimes = [:]
        for sort in values.keys { set([:], for: sort) }
    }

    private func set(_ loaded: [Game.ID: Double], for sort: StorefrontLibrarySort) {
        guard loaded != values[sort, default: [:]] else { return }
        values[sort] = loaded
        revisions[sort, default: 0] &+= 1
    }
}

/// How every library and Home order games: the greatest rank first, a game
/// without one last, equal ones by name, then by ID.
enum LibraryOrder {
    static func order<G, ID: Comparable>(_ games: [G], title: (G) -> String, id: (G) -> ID,
                                         rank: (G) -> Double?) -> [G] {
        keyed(games, title: title, id: id, rank: rank)
            .sorted(by: precedes)
            .map(\.game)
    }

    /// The first of `games` in that order, without ordering the others.
    static func first<G, ID: Comparable>(_ games: [G], title: (G) -> String, id: (G) -> ID,
                                         rank: (G) -> Double?) -> G? {
        keyed(games, title: title, id: id, rank: rank)
            .min(by: precedes)?
            .game
    }

    /// The featured one of `games`: the first by last played when one was
    /// played, else the first by playtime, so every library has one.
    static func featured<G, ID: Comparable>(_ games: [G], title: (G) -> String, id: (G) -> ID,
                                            lastPlayed: (G) -> Date?, playtime: (G) -> Duration?) -> G? {
        if games.contains(where: { lastPlayed($0) != nil }) {
            return first(games, title: title, id: id, rank: { lastPlayed($0)?.timeIntervalSince1970 })
        }
        return first(games, title: title, id: id, rank: { playtime($0).map { Double($0.components.seconds) } })
    }

    /// Merges lists each already in this order; equal games keep the earlier
    /// list's first.
    static func merge<G>(_ orders: [[G]], title: (G) -> String, rank: (G) -> Double?) -> [G] {
        let lists = orders.map { order in order.map { Keyed(game: $0, title: title($0), id: 0, rank: rank($0) ?? -.infinity) } }
        var heads = Array(repeating: 0, count: lists.count)
        var merged: [G] = []
        merged.reserveCapacity(lists.reduce(0) { $0 + $1.count })
        while true {
            var next: Int?
            for list in lists.indices where heads[list] < lists[list].count {
                // Only a game strictly before the earlier lists' heads goes first.
                if let best = next, !precedes(lists[list][heads[list]], lists[best][heads[best]]) { continue }
                next = list
            }
            guard let list = next else { return merged }
            merged.append(lists[list][heads[list]].game)
            heads[list] += 1
        }
    }

    private struct Keyed<G, ID: Comparable> {
        let game: G
        let title: String
        let id: ID
        let rank: Double
    }

    /// Each game's keys, read once rather than at every comparison.
    private static func keyed<G, ID: Comparable>(_ games: [G], title: (G) -> String, id: (G) -> ID,
                                                 rank: (G) -> Double?) -> [Keyed<G, ID>] {
        games.map { Keyed(game: $0, title: title($0), id: id($0), rank: rank($0) ?? -.infinity) }
    }

    private static func precedes<G, ID>(_ left: Keyed<G, ID>, _ right: Keyed<G, ID>) -> Bool {
        if left.rank != right.rank { return left.rank > right.rank }
        let comparison = left.title.localizedStandardCompare(right.title)
        return comparison == .orderedSame ? left.id < right.id : comparison == .orderedAscending
    }
}
```

`apps/macos/Obelisk/Models/BugReports.swift`:

```swift
import AppKit
import Observation
import zlib

/// What a bug report is about: Obelisk itself, from Settings, or one game,
/// from the SOS button on its page.
enum BugReportSubject: Hashable {
    case app
    case game(store: SessionStorefront, id: String, name: String)
}

private extension BugReportSubject {
    /// The subject as Rust finds its diagnostics.
    var diagnostics: DiagnosticsSubject {
        switch self {
        case .app: .app
        case let .game(store, id, _): .game(storefront: store, id: id)
        }
    }
}

/// The `report` part of a bug report. The site's docs/contracts.md describes
/// every field.
struct BugReport: Encodable, Equatable {
    struct Game: Encodable, Equatable {
        let store: String
        let id: String
        let name: String
    }

    /// The site refuses longer descriptions, counted in UTF-16 as JavaScript does.
    static let descriptionLimit = 4000
    static let contactLimit = 200

    let kind: String
    let description: String
    let contact: String?
    let game: Game?
    let obeliskVersion: String
    let voileVersion: String?
    let chip: String
    let macModel: String
    let macOSVersion: String

    enum CodingKeys: String, CodingKey {
        case kind, description, contact, game, chip
        case obeliskVersion = "obelisk_version"
        case voileVersion = "voile_version"
        case macModel = "mac_model"
        case macOSVersion = "macos_version"
    }

    init(subject: BugReportSubject, description: String, contact: String, mac: MacHardware, obeliskVersion: String,
         voileVersion: String?) {
        switch subject {
        case .app:
            kind = "app"
            game = nil
        case let .game(store, id, name):
            kind = "game"
            game = Game(store: store.siteName, id: id, name: name)
        }
        self.description = Self.clamped(description, to: Self.descriptionLimit)
        let contact = Self.clamped(contact, to: Self.contactLimit)
        self.contact = contact.isEmpty ? nil : contact
        self.obeliskVersion = obeliskVersion
        self.voileVersion = voileVersion
        chip = mac.chip
        macModel = mac.model
        macOSVersion = mac.macOSVersion
    }

    private static func clamped(_ text: String, to limit: Int) -> String {
        var text = text.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
        while text.utf16.count > limit { text.removeLast() }
        return text
    }

    /// What is unknown goes as null, as the contract writes it.
    func encode(to encoder: any Encoder) throws {
        var container = encoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)
        try container.encode(kind, forKey: .kind)
        try container.encode(description, forKey: .description)
        try container.encode(contact, forKey: .contact)
        try container.encode(game, forKey: .game)
        try container.encode(obeliskVersion, forKey: .obeliskVersion)
        try container.encode(voileVersion, forKey: .voileVersion)
        try container.encode(chip, forKey: .chip)
        try container.encode(macModel, forKey: .macModel)
        try container.encode(macOSVersion, forKey: .macOSVersion)
    }
}

/// A file a bug report attaches, as its sheet lists it.
struct BugReportFile: Hashable, Identifiable, Sendable {
    /// Its name in the report.
    let name: String
    /// Where it is; nil for Obelisk's log, which macOS keeps.
    let url: URL?

    var id: String { name }
}

/// One file of a report: plain text, then gzip once fitted.
struct BugReportLog: Equatable, Sendable {
    let name: String
    var data: Data
}

/// Where a bug report's files come from.
struct BugReportSources: Sendable {
    /// A game's or Obelisk's diagnostics, as Rust names and finds them, most telling first.
    var diagnostics: @Sendable (BugReportSubject, Date) -> [URL]
    /// Where macOS writes crash reports.
    var crashReports: URL
    /// The process whose crash reports, and its children's, a report attaches.
    var process: String
    /// The player's home folder, which a report never shows.
    var home: String
    /// Obelisk's messages in the unified log over the last hour.
    var unifiedLog: @Sendable () async -> String
    /// The Voile release Windows games run in, once installed.
    var voile: @Sendable () -> String?

    static let unifiedLogName = "obelisk-unified.log"
    /// A Discord message holds at most 10 files.
    static let maxFiles = 10
    private static let maxCrashReports = 4
    private static let maxReadBytes = 16 * 1024 * 1024

    @MainActor static var live: BugReportSources {
        let locations = ObeliskLocations.live
        return BugReportSources(
            diagnostics: { subject, now in
                diagnosticFiles(locations: locations, subject: subject.diagnostics, now: now)
                    .map { URL(fileURLWithPath: $0) }
            },
            crashReports: URL.libraryDirectory.appending(path: "Logs/DiagnosticReports", directoryHint: .isDirectory),
            process: ProcessInfo.processInfo.processName, home: NSHomeDirectory(),
            unifiedLog: { await Self.unifiedLog(process: ProcessInfo.processInfo.processName) },
            voile: { installedVoileRelease(locations: locations) }
        )
    }

    /// What a report on `subject` attaches, most telling first: a game's
    /// diagnostics, Obelisk's log, then crash reports of Obelisk
    /// and what it ran; for Obelisk, its log, its crash reports and the
    /// launch reports of the last day.
    func files(for subject: BugReportSubject, now: Date) -> [BugReportFile] {
        var files: [BugReportFile] = []
        let unified = BugReportFile(name: Self.unifiedLogName, url: nil)
        switch subject {
        case .game:
            files += diagnostics(subject, now).map(Self.file)
            files.append(unified)
            files += crashes(since: now - 24 * 3600).prefix(Self.maxCrashReports).map(Self.file)
        case .app:
            files.append(unified)
            files += crashes(since: now - 7 * 24 * 3600).prefix(Self.maxCrashReports).map(Self.file)
            files += diagnostics(subject, now).map(Self.file)
        }
        return Array(files.prefix(Self.maxFiles))
    }

    /// The files' text, without what a report must not carry.
    func contents(of files: [BugReportFile]) async -> [BugReportLog] {
        var logs: [BugReportLog] = []
        for file in files {
            let text: String?
            if let url = file.url {
                text = Self.tail(of: url)
            } else {
                text = await unifiedLog()
            }
            guard let text else { continue }
            logs.append(BugReportLog(name: file.name, data: Data(BugReportPayload.redacted(text, home: home).utf8)))
        }
        return logs
    }

    /// Crash reports since `date` of this process, or of a process it started
    /// and so answers for, newest first.
    private func crashes(since date: Date) -> [URL] {
        let pattern = #""(procName|responsibleProc)"\s*:\s*"\#(NSRegularExpression.escapedPattern(for: process))""#
        return Self.newest(in: crashReports) { $0.hasSuffix(".ips") }
            .filter { url in
                guard let modified = Self.modified(url), modified >= date,
                      let text = try? String(contentsOf: url, encoding: .utf8) else { return false }
                return text.range(of: pattern, options: .regularExpression) != nil
            }
    }

    private static func file(_ url: URL) -> BugReportFile {
        BugReportFile(name: url.lastPathComponent, url: url)
    }

    private static func modified(_ url: URL) -> Date? {
        try? url.resourceValues(forKeys: [.contentModificationDateKey]).contentModificationDate
    }

    private static func listing(of folder: URL) -> [(url: URL, name: String, modified: Date)] {
        let urls = (try? FileManager.default.contentsOfDirectory(
            at: folder, includingPropertiesForKeys: [.contentModificationDateKey], options: .skipsHiddenFiles
        )) ?? []
        return urls.compactMap { url in modified(url).map { (url, url.lastPathComponent, $0) } }
    }

    /// The files in `folder` whose name `matches`, newest first.
    private static func newest(in folder: URL, where matches: (String) -> Bool) -> [URL] {
        listing(of: folder).filter { matches($0.name) }.sorted { $0.modified > $1.modified }.map(\.url)
    }

    /// The end of the file at `url`: a log can grow without bound, and its
    /// end is where errors are.
    private static func tail(of url: URL) -> String? {
        guard let handle = try? FileHandle(forReadingFrom: url) else { return nil }
        defer { try? handle.close() }
        guard let size = try? handle.seekToEnd() else { return nil }
        try? handle.seek(toOffset: size > UInt64(maxReadBytes) ? size - UInt64(maxReadBytes) : 0)
        return String(decoding: (try? handle.readToEnd()) ?? Data(), as: UTF8.self)
    }

    /// The last hour of the unified log for `process` and Obelisk's own
    /// subsystem, as `log show` prints it; empty when it fails.
    private static func unifiedLog(process: String) async -> String {
        await Task.detached {
            let log = Process()
            log.executableURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: "/usr/bin/log")
            log.arguments = ["show", "--last", "1h", "--style", "compact", "--predicate",
                             #"process == "\#(process)" OR subsystem == "\#(AppIdentity.storageIdentifier)""#]
            let output = Pipe()
            log.standardOutput = output
            log.standardError = FileHandle.nullDevice
            guard (try? log.run()) != nil else { return "" }
            let data = output.fileHandleForReading.readDataToEndOfFile()
            log.waitUntilExit()
            return String(decoding: data, as: UTF8.self)
        }.value
    }
}

/// How a bug report goes out: redacted, gzipped and cut to fit, in one
/// multipart request to getobelisk.app.
enum BugReportPayload {
    static let endpoint = URL(string: "https://getobelisk.app/api/reports")!
    /// Vercel refuses bodies over 4.5 MB.
    static let limit = 4_000_000
    static let cutNote = "[Obelisk cut the start of this file so the report fits.]\n"

    /// `text` without the Metal HUD's frame lines, with the player's home
    /// folder as `~`, as Unix or Wine writes it, and without the identifiers
    /// macOS writes in crash reports.
    static func redacted(_ text: String, home: String) -> String {
        var result = withoutMetalHudFrames(text: text)
        let user = URL(fileURLWithPath: home).lastPathComponent
        let homePattern = home.hasPrefix("/Users/")
            ? #"(?i)[/\\]users[/\\]\#(NSRegularExpression.escapedPattern(for: user))(?![\w.-])"#
            : NSRegularExpression.escapedPattern(for: home)
        let identifiers = #""(crashReporterKey|deviceIdentifierForVendor|bootSessionUUID|sleepWakeUUID)"(\s*:\s*)"[^"]*""#
        for (pattern, template) in [(homePattern, "~"), (identifiers, #""$1"$2"<removed>""#)] {
            guard let expression = try? NSRegularExpression(pattern: pattern) else { continue }
            result = expression.stringByReplacingMatches(in: result, range: NSRange(result.startIndex..., in: result),
                                                         withTemplate: template)
        }
        return result
    }

    static func gzip(_ data: Data) -> Data {
        var stream = z_stream()
        // 31 window bits: 15, plus 16 for a gzip header.
        guard deflateInit2_(&stream, Z_DEFAULT_COMPRESSION, Z_DEFLATED, 31, 8, Z_DEFAULT_STRATEGY, ZLIB_VERSION,
                            Int32(MemoryLayout<z_stream>.size)) == Z_OK else { return Data() }
        defer { deflateEnd(&stream) }
        var output = Data(count: Int(deflateBound(&stream, uLong(data.count))))
        let status: Int32 = data.withUnsafeBytes { input in
            output.withUnsafeMutableBytes { output in
                stream.next_in = UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating: input.bindMemory(to: Bytef.self).baseAddress)
                stream.avail_in = uInt(input.count)
                stream.next_out = output.bindMemory(to: Bytef.self).baseAddress
                stream.avail_out = uInt(output.count)
                return deflate(&stream, Z_FINISH)
            }
        }
        guard status == Z_STREAM_END else { return Data() }
        output.count = Int(stream.total_out)
        return output
    }

    /// `logs` gzipped, `budget` bytes in all: while they go over it, the
    /// largest loses its start, as much as gzip says it must.
    static func fitted(_ logs: [BugReportLog], within budget: Int) -> [BugReportLog] {
        var plain = logs
        var packed = logs.map { BugReportLog(name: $0.name, data: gzip($0.data)) }
        for _ in 0..<32 {
            let total = packed.reduce(0) { $0 + $1.data.count }
            guard total > budget,
                  let largest = packed.indices.max(by: { packed[$0].data.count < packed[$1].data.count }) else { break }
            let size = packed[largest].data.count
            // Text shrinks about evenly, so keep the share that fits, with a margin.
            let share = max(0, Double(size - (total - budget)) / Double(size) * 0.9)
            plain[largest].data = tail(of: plain[largest].data, keeping: Int(Double(plain[largest].data.count) * share))
            packed[largest].data = gzip(plain[largest].data)
        }
        return packed
    }

    /// The last `count` bytes of `data`, from the line they start in, after
    /// the cut note.
    private static func tail(of data: Data, keeping count: Int) -> Data {
        let from = data.index(data.endIndex, offsetBy: -min(count, data.count))
        let start = from == data.startIndex ? from
            : data[from...].firstIndex(of: UInt8(ascii: "\n")).map { $0 + 1 } ?? data.endIndex
        return Data(cutNote.utf8) + data[start...]
    }

    static func body(report: Data, logs: [BugReportLog], boundary: String) -> Data {
        var body = Data()
        func part(_ headers: String, _ content: Data) {
            body += Data("--\(boundary)\r\n\(headers)\r\n\r\n".utf8) + content + Data("\r\n".utf8)
        }
        part("Content-Disposition: form-data; name=\"report\"\r\nContent-Type: application/json", report)
        for log in logs {
            let name = log.name.replacingOccurrences(of: #"["\r\n]"#, with: "_", options: .regularExpression)
            part("Content-Disposition: form-data; name=\"log\"; filename=\"\(name).gz\"\r\n"
                + "Content-Type: application/gzip", log.data)
        }
        body += Data("--\(boundary)--\r\n".utf8)
        return body
    }

    enum Failure: Error {
        /// The site or Discord refused the report, or the network failed.
        case refused
        /// The site's firewall turned away more reports from this network.
        case tooMany
    }

    /// Sends `report` with `logs`, returning the code the site gave it.
    static func send(_ report: BugReport, logs: [BugReportLog],
                     post: @Sendable (URLRequest) async throws -> (Data, URLResponse)) async throws -> String {
        let json = try JSONEncoder().encode(report)
        // Each part's headers and boundary take well under 256 bytes.
        let logs = fitted(logs, within: limit - json.count - 256 * (logs.count + 2))
        let boundary = "obelisk-\(UUID().uuidString)"
        var request = URLRequest(url: endpoint, timeoutInterval: 120)
        request.httpMethod = "POST"
        request.setValue("multipart/form-data; boundary=\(boundary)", forHTTPHeaderField: "Content-Type")
        request.httpBody = body(report: json, logs: logs, boundary: boundary)
        let (data, response) = try await post(request)
        struct Answer: Decodable { let code: String }
        let status = (response as? HTTPURLResponse)?.statusCode
        if status == 429 { throw Failure.tooMany }
        guard status == 201, let answer = try? JSONDecoder().decode(Answer.self, from: data) else {
            throw Failure.refused
        }
        return answer.code
    }

    private static let session = URLSession(configuration: .ephemeral)

    static func post(_ request: URLRequest) async throws -> (Data, URLResponse) {
        try await session.data(for: request)
    }
}

/// The bug report sheet's state: what the player writes, the files that go
/// with it, and how sending went.
@MainActor
@Observable
final class BugReportModel: Identifiable {
    enum Phase: Equatable {
        case editing
        case sending
        case sent(code: String)
        /// Sending failed; `tooMany` when the site turned away more reports
        /// from this network for a while.
        case failed(tooMany: Bool)
    }

    let subject: BugReportSubject
    var description = ""
    var contact = ""
    var attachesLogs = true
    private(set) var files: [BugReportFile] = []
    private(set) var phase = Phase.editing
    /// GitHub's bug form with the sent report filled in.
    private(set) var issue: URL?

    @ObservationIgnored private let sources: BugReportSources
    @ObservationIgnored private let mac: MacHardware
    @ObservationIgnored private let post: @Sendable (URLRequest) async throws -> (Data, URLResponse)

    init(subject: BugReportSubject, sources: BugReportSources, mac: MacHardware = .current,
         post: @escaping @Sendable (URLRequest) async throws -> (Data, URLResponse) = BugReportPayload.post) {
        self.subject = subject
        self.sources = sources
        self.mac = mac
        self.post = post
    }

    var canSend: Bool {
        switch phase {
        case .editing, .failed: !description.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).isEmpty
        case .sending, .sent: false
        }
    }

    /// Lists the files the report attaches.
    func load() async {
        let sources = self.sources, subject = self.subject
        files = await Task.detached { sources.files(for: subject, now: .now) }.value
    }

    func send() async {
        guard canSend else { return }
        phase = .sending
        let sources = self.sources, post = self.post, files = attachesLogs ? self.files : []
        let subject = self.subject, description = self.description, contact = self.contact, mac = self.mac
        do {
            let (report, code) = try await Task.detached {
                let report = BugReport(subject: subject, description: description, contact: contact, mac: mac,
                                       obeliskVersion: AppIdentity.version, voileVersion: sources.voile())
                let code = try await BugReportPayload.send(report, logs: await sources.contents(of: files), post: post)
                return (report, code)
            }.value
            issue = GitHubIssues.bug(report, code: code)
            phase = .sent(code: code)
        } catch BugReportPayload.Failure.tooMany {
            phase = .failed(tooMany: true)
        } catch {
            phase = .failed(tooMany: false)
        }
    }

    func openIssue() {
        if let issue { NSWorkspace.shared.open(issue) }
    }

    /// Shows the attached files that are on disk in Finder.
    func revealFiles() {
        NSWorkspace.shared.activateFileViewerSelecting(files.compactMap(\.url))
    }
}
```

```swift
import Foundation
import Observation

/// The account's Cloud sync running now, as Rust shows it: a launch's, an
/// exit's or a maintenance's, with the one Cloud question the account asks.
struct GameCloudSync<Game: Hashable>: Equatable {
    let game: Game
    let kind: CloudSyncKind
    /// Binds a cancellation to the sync as it shows now.
    let decisionId: UInt64
    /// It compares or transfers saves now.
    let working: Bool
    /// Its Game session's control connection was lost: nothing reaches it.
    let reconnecting: Bool
    /// The player may cancel it: a launch check still in progress.
    let cancellable: Bool
    let question: CloudQuestion?
}

typealias SteamCloudModel = CloudModel<SteamGames>
typealias EpicCloudModel = CloudModel<EpicGames>

/// Presents one account's Cloud: indicators, and the Cloud sync and question
/// Rust shows for it. Rust runs every sync, asks every question and routes
/// each answer; this owns no save comparison or transfer.
@MainActor @Observable
final class CloudModel<Store: InstallationStorefront> {
    private let sessions: GameSessions<Store>
    private(set) var account: Store.AccountID?
    @ObservationIgnored private var backend: (any InstallationsBackend<Store>)?
    private var generation = 0
    private(set) var indicators: [Store.GameID: CloudIndicator] = [:]
    /// The account's Cloud sync, as its installations mirror it. Once a
    /// maintenance ends, its game's indicator is read again and the failure of
    /// an answer goes.
    var sync: GameCloudSync<Store.GameID>? {
        didSet {
            guard let ended = oldValue, ended.kind == .maintenance,
                  sync?.kind != .maintenance || sync?.game != ended.game else { return }
            if question == nil { promptError = nil }
            refreshIndicators(for: [ended.game])
        }
    }
    private(set) var promptBusy = false
    private var promptError: String?

    init(sessions: GameSessions<Store>) {
        self.sessions = sessions
    }

    /// `backend` holds the account's installations, which run its Cloud.
    func connect(account: Store.AccountID, backend: any InstallationsBackend<Store>) {
        reset()
        self.account = account
        self.backend = backend
    }

    func signedOut() {
        let old = account
        reset()
        if let old { sessions.signedOut(account: old) }
    }

    /// Everything presented belongs to one account; a change invalidates it all.
    private func reset() {
        generation += 1
        backend = nil
        sync = nil
        indicators = [:]
        account = nil
        promptError = nil
        promptBusy = false
    }

    func indicator(for game: Store.GameID) -> CloudIndicator? { indicators[game] }

    /// Reads the journals off the main thread. Never polls: callers refresh
    /// when a game page opens, the account changes, or a sync ends.
    func refreshIndicators(for games: [Store.GameID]) {
        guard account != nil, let backend else { return }
        let current = generation
        Task {
            guard let values = try? await backend.cloudIndicators(games), current == generation else { return }
            for (game, indicator) in values { indicators[game] = indicator }
        }
    }

    var isMaintaining: Bool { sync?.kind == .maintenance }

    /// The one Cloud question the account asks, until it has its answer.
    var question: CloudQuestion? { account == nil ? nil : sync?.question }

    var promptPresented: Bool { question?.kind == .conflict }
    var promptGame: Store.GameID? { question == nil ? nil : sync?.game }
    /// Only a launch check asks after a failure; a failed maintenance shows in
    /// the game's Cloud indicator instead.
    var failurePresented: Bool { question?.kind == .failed }
    var promptMessage: String { promptError ?? question?.error ?? L10n.string("ui.cloud.working") }
    var promptWorking: Bool { promptBusy || sync?.reconnecting == true || sync?.working == true }
    var canLaunchAnyway: Bool { question?.kind == .failed && question?.choices.contains(.launchAnyway) == true }

    func isSynchronizing(for game: Store.GameID) -> Bool {
        guard account != nil, let sync, sync.game == game else { return false }
        return sync.working || promptBusy
    }

    func canCancelSynchronization(for game: Store.GameID) -> Bool {
        guard account != nil, let sync, sync.game == game else { return false }
        return sync.cancellable && !promptBusy
    }

    /// Answers the question shown. Rust gives it to the sync that asked.
    func respond(_ choice: CloudChoice) {
        guard let game = sync?.game, let question else { return }
        answer(game, decision: question.decisionId, choice: choice)
    }

    /// Cancels `game`'s launch check still in progress.
    func cancelSynchronization(for game: Store.GameID) {
        guard canCancelSynchronization(for: game), let sync else { return }
        answer(game, decision: sync.decisionId, choice: .cancel)
    }

    private func answer(_ game: Store.GameID, decision: UInt64, choice: CloudChoice) {
        guard account != nil, let backend, !promptBusy else { return }
        let current = generation
        promptBusy = true
        promptError = nil
        Task {
            defer { if current == generation { promptBusy = false } }
            do {
                try await backend.answerCloud(game, decisionId: decision, choice: choice)
            } catch {
                guard current == generation else { return }
                promptError = Store.describe(error)
            }
        }
    }
}
```

`apps/macos/Obelisk/Models/DownloadsModel.swift`:

```swift
import Foundation
import Observation

/// The process's download queue, as Rust keeps it. Each action returns at
/// once; the next state tells how it went.
@MainActor
protocol DownloadsBackend: AnyObject {
    func state() -> DownloadQueueState
    /// Waits for a revision newer than `after`.
    func changed(after: UInt64) async -> DownloadQueueState
    func remove(_ id: UInt64)
    func pause(_ id: UInt64)
    func resume(_ id: UInt64)
    func moveToTop(_ id: UInt64)
}

/// The queue every account's installations share in Rust.
final class RustDownloads: DownloadsBackend {
    private let core = Downloads()

    func state() -> DownloadQueueState { core.state() }
    func changed(after: UInt64) async -> DownloadQueueState { await core.changed(after: after) }
    func remove(_ id: UInt64) { core.remove(id: id) }
    func pause(_ id: UInt64) { core.pause(id: id) }
    func resume(_ id: UInt64) { core.resume(id: id) }
    func moveToTop(_ id: UInt64) { core.moveToTop(id: id) }
}

/// The running Transfer's download speed at one moment.
struct DownloadSpeedSample: Identifiable, Equatable {
    let id: Int
    let time: Date
    let bytesPerSecond: Double
}

/// Every storefront's Transfers, waiting in one queue and running one at a
/// time: the player's downloads, updates and repairs, and Obelisk's
/// automatic updates. It also keeps the running Transfer's speed.
@MainActor @Observable
final class DownloadsModel {
    private(set) var running: DownloadItem?
    private(set) var waiting: [DownloadItem] = []
    /// A game runs: automatic updates wait.
    private(set) var held = false
    /// The running Transfer's download speed, one sample a period, for the
    /// last two minutes.
    private(set) var samples: [DownloadSpeedSample] = []
    var isPresented = false

    /// The running Transfer's progress, as its storefront's installations show it.
    @ObservationIgnored var progress: @MainActor (DownloadItem) -> GameTransfer? = { _ in nil }

    /// How many samples the speed graph keeps.
    static let sampleLimit = 120

    @ObservationIgnored private let backend: any DownloadsBackend
    @ObservationIgnored private let period: Duration
    @ObservationIgnored private var revision: UInt64?
    @ObservationIgnored private var observation: Task<Void, Never>?
    @ObservationIgnored private var sampling: Task<Void, Never>?
    /// The running Transfer's bytes when last sampled.
    @ObservationIgnored private var lastSample: (time: Date, bytes: UInt64)?
    @ObservationIgnored private var nextSample = 0

    init(backend: any DownloadsBackend = RustDownloads(), period: Duration = .seconds(1)) {
        self.backend = backend
        self.period = period
        apply(backend.state())
        observation = Task { [weak self, backend] in
            var after = self?.revision ?? 0
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                let state = await backend.changed(after: after)
                guard let self else { return }
                after = state.revision
                apply(state)
            }
        }
    }

    /// Whether anything runs or waits: the sidebar shows the queue then.
    var isVisible: Bool { running != nil || !waiting.isEmpty }

    var count: Int { waiting.count + (running == nil ? 0 : 1) }

    var currentTransfer: GameTransfer? { running.flatMap(progress) }

    /// The latest speed, once two samples are known.
    var currentSpeed: Double? { samples.last?.bytesPerSecond }

    var peakSpeed: Double { samples.map(\.bytesPerSecond).max() ?? 0 }

    /// Only automatic updates wait, for the game that runs.
    var waitsForGame: Bool { held && running == nil && !waiting.isEmpty && waiting.allSatisfy(\.automatic) }

    func remove(_ item: DownloadItem) { backend.remove(item.id) }
    func pause(_ item: DownloadItem) { backend.pause(item.id) }
    func resume(_ item: DownloadItem) { backend.resume(item.id) }
    func moveToTop(_ item: DownloadItem) { backend.moveToTop(item.id) }

    private func apply(_ state: DownloadQueueState) {
        if let revision, state.revision <= revision { return }
        revision = state.revision
        if running?.id != state.running?.id {
            samples = []
            lastSample = nil
        }
        if running != state.running { running = state.running }
        if waiting != state.waiting { waiting = state.waiting }
        if held != state.held { held = state.held }
        if running == nil {
            sampling?.cancel()
            sampling = nil
        } else if sampling == nil {
            sampling = Task { [weak self, period] in
                // Ends with the model, or once nothing runs.
                repeat {
                    try? await Task.sleep(for: period)
                } while !Task.isCancelled && self?.sampleRunning() == true
            }
        }
    }

    private func sampleRunning() -> Bool {
        sample()
        return running != nil
    }

    /// Adds the speed since the last sample of the running Transfer.
    func sample(at now: Date = Date()) {
        guard let running, let transfer = progress(running) else { return }
        defer { lastSample = (now, transfer.networkBytes) }
        guard let last = lastSample else { return }
        let elapsed = now.timeIntervalSince(last.time)
        guard elapsed > 0 else { return }
        let bytes = transfer.networkBytes >= last.bytes ? transfer.networkBytes - last.bytes : 0
        nextSample += 1
        samples.append(DownloadSpeedSample(id: nextSample, time: now, bytesPerSecond: Double(bytes) / elapsed))
        if samples.count > Self.sampleLimit { samples.removeFirst(samples.count - Self.sampleLimit) }
    }
}
```

```swift
import Foundation

/// Epic library entries are unique per namespace and app name across platforms.
func epicLibraryID(namespace: String, appName: String) -> String { "\(namespace):\(appName)" }
/// The game a library ID names: an Epic namespace has no colon.
func epicGameID(_ libraryID: String) -> (namespace: String, appName: String)? {
    guard let colon = libraryID.firstIndex(of: ":") else { return nil }
    return (String(libraryID[..<colon]), String(libraryID[libraryID.index(after: colon)...]))
}

typealias EpicModel = WebAccountModel<EpicGames>

extension EpicGames: WebStorefront {
    typealias Session = any EpicSessionProtocol
    typealias Credentials = EpicCredentials
    typealias Game = EpicGame
    typealias Details = EpicGameDetails
    typealias Presence = EpicFriends

    static let storeID = "epic"
    static let storeURL = URL(string: "https://store.epicgames.com/")!
    static let webSignIn = WebSignIn.epic
    static func keychain() -> any CredentialStore<EpicCredentials> { EpicKeychain() }

    static func signIn(code: String, library: LibraryCache?) async throws -> Session {
        try await EpicSession.signIn(authorizationCode: code, library: library)
    }
    static func restore(_ credentials: EpicCredentials, library: LibraryCache?) async throws -> Session {
        try await EpicSession.restore(credentials: credentials, library: library)
    }
    static func accountID(_ credentials: EpicCredentials) -> String { credentials.accountId }
    static func accountName(_ credentials: EpicCredentials) -> String { credentials.displayName }
    static func rotating(_ session: Session) -> RotatingSession<EpicCredentials> {
        RotatingSession(
            identity: ObjectIdentifier(session),
            credentials: { try await session.credentials() },
            persist: { (saver: any CredentialSave) in await session.persist(credentials: saver) },
            shutdownObservers: { session.shutdownObservers() }
        )
    }
    static func disconnect(_ session: Session) async throws { try await session.disconnect() }
    /// Each address spends a new exchange code of the session.
    static func webSignInURL(session: Session) async throws -> URL? {
        URL(string: try await session.webSignInUrl(redirectUrl: storeURL.absoluteString))
    }

    static func games(of session: Session) async throws -> [EpicGame] { try await session.games() }
    /// Epic answers every game's playtime in one request, by app name.
    static func playtimes(of session: Session, games: [EpicGame]) async throws -> [String: Duration] {
        let seconds = Dictionary(try await session.playtimes().map { ($0.appName, $0.seconds) }, uniquingKeysWith: max)
        return Dictionary(games.compactMap { game in seconds[game.appName].map { (game.id, Duration.seconds(Int64(clamping: $0))) } },
                          uniquingKeysWith: max)
    }
    /// Epic tells achievements by sandbox, which several games may share.
    static func achievementShares(of games: [EpicGame], session: Session, language: String) async throws -> [String: Double] {
        let shares = try await session.achievementShares(namespaces: Array(Set(games.map(\.namespace))).sorted(),
                                                         locale: achievementLocale(language))
        return Dictionary(games.compactMap { game in shares[game.namespace].map { (game.id, $0) } },
                          uniquingKeysWith: { first, _ in first })
    }
    static func cachedLibrary(in cache: LibraryCache, account: String)
        -> [(game: EpicGame, playtime: Duration?, achievements: Double?)] {
        cache.epicLibrary(accountId: account).map {
            ($0.game, $0.playtimeSeconds.map { .seconds(Int64(clamping: $0)) }, $0.achievementShare)
        }
    }
    static func details(of game: EpicGame, session: Session, language: String) async throws -> EpicGameDetails {
        try await session.gameDetails(namespace: game.namespace, catalogItemId: game.catalogItemId,
                                      appName: game.appName)
    }
    static func achievements(of game: EpicGame, session: Session, language: String,
                             fresh: Bool) async throws -> [GameAchievement] {
        try await session.achievements(namespace: game.namespace, locale: achievementLocale(language), fresh: fresh)
            .map(GameAchievement.init)
    }
    /// Epic's achievements take a bare language code, such as "fr".
    private static func achievementLocale(_ language: String) -> String {
        Locale(identifier: language).language.languageCode?.identifier ?? "en"
    }
    @MainActor static func installations(of session: Session, account: String, language: String,
                                          sessions: any StorefrontSessionsProtocol, receipts: URL,
                                          locations: ObeliskLocations) -> any InstallationsBackend<EpicGames> {
        guard let session = session as? EpicSession, let sessions = sessions as? StorefrontSessions else {
            return NoInstallations<EpicGames>()
        }
        return RustInstallations<EpicGames>(try! AccountInstallations.epic(
            session: session, accountId: account, language: language, sessions: sessions,
            receipts: receipts.path, locations: locations
        ))
    }
    static func isUnauthorized(_ error: Error) -> Bool {
        if case EpicError.Unauthorized = error { true } else { false }
    }
    @MainActor static func describe(_ error: Error) -> String {
        switch error {
        case EpicError.Network: L10n.string("model.epic.network")
        case EpicError.Unauthorized: L10n.string("model.epic.unauthorized")
        case EpicError.InvalidCode: L10n.string("model.epic.invalidCode")
        case EpicError.InvalidResponse: L10n.string("model.epic.invalidResponse")
        case let EpicError.Service(message): L10n.message(message)
        case let browserError as WebAuthenticationError: browserError.localizedDescription
        case let failure as GameInstallationFailure: failure.localizedDescription
        default: L10n.string("model.epic.failure")
        }
    }

    static var sessionNotSaved: String { L10n.string("model.epic.sessionNotSaved") }
    static var revocationUnconfirmed: String { L10n.string("model.epic.revocationUnconfirmed") }
    static var otherGameRunning: String { L10n.string("model.epic.otherGameRunning") }
    static var cloudTitle: String { L10n.string("ui.epic.cloud.title") }
}

/// Epic's friends: the connected account's social socket. Waking the Mac retries it.
@MainActor
@Observable
final class EpicFriends: AccountPresence {
    private(set) var state: FriendsPresentationState?
    private(set) var isPresented = false
    @ObservationIgnored private var session: (any EpicSessionProtocol)?
    @ObservationIgnored private var account: String?
    /// Cancelled when the observation is revoked or replaced, which rejects its later snapshots.
    @ObservationIgnored private var task: Task<Void, Never>?
    @ObservationIgnored private var wakeObserver: SystemWakeObservation?

    init() {
        wakeObserver = SystemWakeObservation { [weak self] in
            Task { @MainActor [weak self] in self?.retry() }
        }
    }

    deinit {
        task?.cancel()
    }

    func connect(_ session: any EpicSessionProtocol, account: String) {
        self.session = session
        self.account = account
        state = .epic(accountID: account)
        observe(reconnect: false)
    }

    func revoke() {
        task?.cancel()
        task = nil
        session = nil
        account = nil
        state = nil
        isPresented = false
    }

    func open() {
        guard state != nil else { return }
        isPresented = true
    }

    func close() { isPresented = false }

    /// Replaces only the social socket. The OAuth session and downloads stay
    /// alive. Does nothing once the account is revoked.
    func retry() {
        guard session != nil, state?.connection != .authenticationRequired else { return }
        observe(reconnect: true)
    }

    private func observe(reconnect: Bool) {
        guard let session, let account else { return }
        task?.cancel()
        task = Task { [weak self] in
            guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
            await withTaskCancellationHandler {
                if reconnect { await session.reconnectFriends() }
                else { await session.startFriends() }
                var revision: UInt64 = 0
                while !Task.isCancelled {
                    let snapshot = await session.nextFriends(afterRevision: revision)
                    guard let self, !Task.isCancelled, snapshot.accountId == account else { return }
                    revision = snapshot.revision
                    if snapshot.connection == .stopped { return }
                    var state = self.state
                    state?.apply(snapshot)
                    // Repeated snapshots do not invalidate unchanged presentation.
                    if state != self.state { self.state = state }
                }
            } onCancel: { session.stopFriends() }
        }
    }
}

/// Epic's friends, in SteamModel's words, so AppModel treats both stores alike.
extension WebAccountModel where Store == EpicGames {
    var friends: FriendsPresentationState? { presence.state }
    var isFriendsPresented: Bool { presence.isPresented }

    func openFriends() { presence.open() }
    func closeFriends() { presence.close() }
    /// Replaces only the social socket. The OAuth session and downloads stay alive.
    func retryFriends() { presence.retry() }
}
```

```swift
    let friendID: String

        case .lookingToTrade: L10n.string("ui.friends.presence.lookingToTrade")
        case .lookingToPlay: L10n.string("ui.friends.presence.lookingToPlay")
        case .unknown: L10n.string("ui.friends.presence.unknown")
        }
    }

struct FriendGameActivity: Equatable, Sendable {
    let id: String
    let name: String?

    var title: String {
        let value = name?.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) ?? ""
        return value.isEmpty ? L10n.string("ui.friends.inGameUnknown") : L10n.string("ui.friends.inGame", value)
    }
}

struct FriendPresentation: Identifiable, Equatable, Sendable {
    let id: FriendIdentity
    let name: String?
    let avatarURL: URL?
    let presence: FriendPresence
    let activity: FriendGameActivity?
    /// A Steam friend's game and how Steam's "Join Game" joins it, while it can.
    var steamJoin: SteamJoinTarget? = nil

    var displayName: String {
        let value = name?.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) ?? ""
        return value.isEmpty ? L10n.string("ui.friends.unknownName") : value
    }

    var initials: String { name?.initials ?? "" }

    var status: String {
        [presence.title, activity?.title].compactMap { $0 }.joined(separator: " · ")
    }
}

enum FriendsConnectionState: Equatable, Sendable {
    case loading, connected, interrupted, failed(String), authenticationRequired
}

struct FriendsPresentationState: Equatable, Sendable {
    let store: FriendsStoreIdentity
    let account: FriendsAccountIdentity
    var friends: [FriendPresentation]
    var connection: FriendsConnectionState
    var lastKnownOnlineCount: Int? = nil

    var title: String { L10n.string("ui.friends.title", store.name) }
    var onlineCount: Int { friends.lazy.filter { $0.presence.isOnline }.count }
    var onlineSummary: String {
        let count = onlineCount
        return count > 0
            ? L10n.string("ui.friends.onlineCount", Int64(count))
            : L10n.string("ui.friends.totalCount", Int64(friends.count))
    }

    var menuTitle: String {
        switch connection {
        case .connected: onlineCount > 0 ? L10n.string("ui.friends.menu", onlineSummary) : onlineSummary
        case .loading: L10n.string("ui.friends.menuLoading")
        case .interrupted: L10n.string("ui.friends.menuInterrupted")
        case .failed: L10n.string("ui.friends.menuUnavailable")
        case .authenticationRequired: L10n.string("ui.friends.menuAuthenticationRequired")
        }
    }

    var headerSummary: String {
        if connection == .connected { return onlineSummary }
        if connection == .loading { return L10n.string("ui.friends.loading") }
        guard let lastKnownOnlineCount else { return summary }
        return L10n.string("ui.friends.lastKnownCount", L10n.string("ui.friends.onlineCount", Int64(lastKnownOnlineCount)))
    }

    var summary: String {
        switch connection {
        case .connected: onlineSummary
        case .loading: L10n.string("ui.friends.loading")
        case .interrupted: L10n.string("ui.friends.stale")
        case .failed(let message): L10n.message(message)
        case .authenticationRequired: L10n.string("model.friends.authenticationRequired")
        }
    }

    /// Unknown presence is kept separate from offline. Search always includes both.
    func sections(matching search: String) -> FriendsSections {
        let query = search.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
        let matches = friends.filter { query.isEmpty || $0.displayName.localizedStandardContains(query) }
        func ordered(_ values: [FriendPresentation]) -> [FriendPresentation] {
            values.sorted {
                let order = $0.displayName.localizedStandardCompare($1.displayName)
                return order == .orderedSame ? $0.id.friendID < $1.id.friendID : order == .orderedAscending
            }
        }
        return FriendsSections(
            playing: ordered(matches.filter { $0.presence.isOnline && $0.activity != nil }),
            online: ordered(matches.filter { $0.presence.isOnline && $0.activity == nil }),
            unknown: ordered(matches.filter { $0.presence == .unknown }),
            offline: ordered(matches.filter { $0.presence == .offline || $0.presence == .invisible }),
            isSearching: !query.isEmpty
        )
    }
}

extension StringProtocol {
    /// Up to two uppercase initials from the leading words, for avatar placeholders.
    var initials: String {
        String(split(whereSeparator: \.isWhitespace).prefix(2).compactMap(\.first).map(String.init).joined().uppercased().prefix(2))
    }
}

struct FriendsSections: Equatable {
    let playing: [FriendPresentation]
    let online: [FriendPresentation]
    let unknown: [FriendPresentation]
    let offline: [FriendPresentation]
    let isSearching: Bool
    var isEmpty: Bool { playing.isEmpty && online.isEmpty && unknown.isEmpty && offline.isEmpty }
    var hasOnline: Bool { !playing.isEmpty || !online.isEmpty }
    func showsOffline(isExpanded: Bool) -> Bool { isSearching || isExpanded }
}
```

`apps/macos/Obelisk/Models/GameAchievementsModel.swift`:

```swift
import Foundation
import Observation

@MainActor
@Observable
final class GameAchievementsModel {
    let storeID: String
    /// Each storefront maps its own backend failures, as it does for details
    /// and news, so this model stays free of store-specific error types.
    @ObservationIgnored private let describe: @MainActor (Error) -> String

    init(storeID: String, describe: @escaping @MainActor (Error) -> String) {
        self.storeID = storeID
        self.describe = describe
    }

    private(set) var items: [GameAchievement]?
    private(set) var isLoading = false
    private(set) var error: String?
    var isPresented = false
    @ObservationIgnored private var task: Task<Void, Never>?
    // Counters invalidate late responses, as in the storefront models. The
    // request task is cancelled too, which frees its work rather than gating it.
    @ObservationIgnored private var generation = 0

    private var unlocked: Int { items?.count(where: \.unlocked) ?? 0 }
    var fraction: Double? {
        guard let items, !items.isEmpty else { return nil }
        return Double(unlocked) / Double(items.count)
    }
    var countText: String {
        guard let items else { return "—" }
        return "\(unlocked)/\(items.count)"
    }
    /// A game with no achievements has nothing to show, and neither has one whose
    /// list has not been requested; a load in flight or a failure both do.
    var hasContent: Bool { isLoading || error != nil || items?.isEmpty == false }

    func reset() {
        generation += 1
        task?.cancel()
        task = nil
        items = nil
        error = nil
        isLoading = false
        isPresented = false
    }

    func load(_ fetch: @escaping @MainActor @Sendable () async throws -> [GameAchievement]) {
        generation += 1
        let request = generation
        task?.cancel()
        items = nil
        error = nil
        isLoading = true
        task = Task { [weak self] in
            do {
                let items = try await fetch()
                guard let self, self.generation == request else { return }
                self.items = items
                self.isLoading = false
            } catch {
                guard let self, self.generation == request else { return }
                self.error = self.describe(error)
                self.isLoading = false
            }
        }
    }
    deinit { task?.cancel() }
}


struct GameAchievement: Sendable {
    let id: String
    let name: String
    let description: String
    let iconUrl: String
    let hidden: Bool
    let unlocked: Bool
    let unlockDate: Date?
}

extension GameAchievement {
    init(_ value: LibraryAchievement) {
        self.init(id: value.id, name: value.name, description: value.description, iconUrl: value.iconUrl,
                  hidden: value.hidden, unlocked: value.unlocked,
                  unlockDate: value.unlockedAt.map { Date(timeIntervalSince1970: TimeInterval($0)) })
    }
}
```
