```swift
import AppKit
import SwiftUI
import XCTest
@testable import Obelisk

final class StorefrontSortPopoverTests: XCTestCase {
    @MainActor
    func testClickAppliesSortBeforeDismissingInTheSameEvent() async throws {
        var selected = "recent"
        var events: [String] = []
        let option = StorefrontSortOption(id: "name", title: StorefrontLibrarySort.name.title, isSelected: false) {
            selected = "name"
            events.append("selected")
        }
        let fixture = SortPopoverFixture(options: [option]) {
            events.append("dismissed:\(selected)")
        }
        defer { fixture.close() }
        try await fixture.prepare()

        // With one row, the fitted content's center is inside the actual button.
        // Send input to the mounted view instead of calling the supplied action.
        fixture.clickCenter()

        XCTAssertEqual(selected, "name")
        XCTAssertEqual(events, ["selected", "dismissed:name"], "Selection and dismissal must finish in the input handler, in that order")
    }

    @MainActor
    func testEscapeDismissesWithoutChangingTheSort() async throws {
        var selected = "recent"
        var events: [String] = []
        let options = ["recent", "name", "playtime"].map { id in
            StorefrontSortOption(id: id, title: id, isSelected: id == selected) {
                selected = id
                events.append("selected:\(id)")
            }
        }
        let fixture = SortPopoverFixture(options: options) { events.append("dismissed") }
        defer { fixture.close() }
        try await fixture.prepare()

        fixture.press(keyCode: 53, characters: "\u{1b}")

        XCTAssertEqual(selected, "recent")
        XCTAssertEqual(events, ["dismissed"])
    }

    @MainActor
    func testArrowKeysThenReturnApplyTheFocusedOption() async throws {
        var selected = "recent"
        var events: [String] = []
        let options = ["recent", "name", "playtime"].map { id in
            StorefrontSortOption(id: id, title: id, isSelected: id == selected) {
                selected = id
                events.append("selected:\(id)")
            }
        }
        let fixture = SortPopoverFixture(options: options) { events.append("dismissed:\(selected)") }
        defer { fixture.close() }
        try await fixture.prepare()

        fixture.press(keyCode: 125, characters: "\u{f701}")
        await fixture.settleUI()
        fixture.press(keyCode: 125, characters: "\u{f701}")
        await fixture.settleUI()
        fixture.press(keyCode: 126, characters: "\u{f700}")
        await fixture.settleUI()
        XCTAssertEqual(selected, "recent", "Moving focus must not apply a sort")
        XCTAssertTrue(events.isEmpty)
        fixture.press(keyCode: 36, characters: "\r")

        XCTAssertEqual(selected, "name")
        XCTAssertEqual(events, ["selected:name", "dismissed:name"])
    }
}

@MainActor
private final class SortPopoverFixture {
    let host: NSView
    let window: SortPopoverWindow
    private let mountState: SortPopoverMountState

    init(options: [StorefrontSortOption], dismiss: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void) {
        let mountState = SortPopoverMountState()
        self.mountState = mountState
        host = NSHostingView(rootView: StorefrontSortPopover(options: options, dismiss: dismiss)
            .onAppear { mountState.appeared = true })
        window = SortPopoverWindow(contentRect: NSRect(x: -20_000, y: -20_000, width: 260, height: 180), styleMask: .borderless, backing: .buffered, defer: false)
        window.isReleasedWhenClosed = false
        window.sharingType = .none
        window.contentView = host
        window.makeKeyAndOrderFront(nil)
    }

    func prepare() async throws {
        // Let onAppear establish the selected row's real SwiftUI focus target.
        // No sleep or deadline is used to judge input latency.
        let deadline = ContinuousClock.now + .seconds(3)
        repeat {
            host.layoutSubtreeIfNeeded()
            let size = host.fittingSize
            if size.width > 0 && size.height > 0 { window.setContentSize(size) }
            await settleUI()
            if mountState.appeared && window.firstResponder is NSView { return }
            try await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(5))
        } while ContinuousClock.now < deadline
        throw SortPopoverFixtureError.missingFocus
    }

    func settleUI() async {
        // Real key events arrive on separate AppKit turns. Give FocusState its
        // deferred update before delivering the next key in the fixture.
        for _ in 0..<2 {
            await withCheckedContinuation { continuation in
                DispatchQueue.main.async { continuation.resume() }
            }
            host.layoutSubtreeIfNeeded()
            window.displayIfNeeded()
        }
    }

    func clickCenter() {
        let location = host.convert(NSPoint(x: host.bounds.midX, y: host.bounds.midY), to: nil)
        let timestamp = ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime
        let mouseDown = NSEvent.mouseEvent(with: .leftMouseDown, location: location, modifierFlags: [], timestamp: timestamp, windowNumber: window.windowNumber, context: nil, eventNumber: 9_123, clickCount: 1, pressure: 1)!
        let mouseUp = NSEvent.mouseEvent(with: .leftMouseUp, location: location, modifierFlags: [], timestamp: timestamp + 0.001, windowNumber: window.windowNumber, context: nil, eventNumber: 9_124, clickCount: 1, pressure: 0)!
        // A native control may track the mouse synchronously inside mouseDown.
        // Queue its release first, and deliver it ourselves if no tracking loop
        // consumed it. Both events stay inside this test application's queue.
        NSApp.postEvent(mouseUp, atStart: true)
        window.sendEvent(mouseDown)
        if let release = NSApp.nextEvent(matching: .leftMouseUp, until: Date(), inMode: .default, dequeue: true) {
            window.sendEvent(release)
        }
    }

    func press(keyCode: UInt16, characters: String) {
        for type in [NSEvent.EventType.keyDown, .keyUp] {
            let event = NSEvent.keyEvent(with: type, location: .zero, modifierFlags: [], timestamp: ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime, windowNumber: window.windowNumber, context: nil, characters: characters, charactersIgnoringModifiers: characters, isARepeat: false, keyCode: keyCode)!
            window.sendEvent(event)
        }
    }

    func close() { window.close() }
}

private final class SortPopoverWindow: NSWindow {
    override var canBecomeKey: Bool { true }
}

@MainActor
private final class SortPopoverMountState {
    var appeared = false
}

private enum SortPopoverFixtureError: Error { case missingFocus }
```

```swift
import Foundation
import XCTest
@testable import Obelisk

/// A web storefront as the shared account tests drive it: how its fixtures
/// are named, and what its session answers and throws.
protocol WebStoreFixture: WebStorefront where Credentials: Equatable {
    associatedtype Playtime: Sendable
    associatedtype DetailsRequest: Equatable & Sendable

    /// The account a test signs in unless it names another.
    static var fixtureAccount: String { get }
    static var fixtureName: String { get }
    /// The fixture account carries `fixtureName`; any other is named
    /// "Name of" its id, so a test tells two accounts, and a name from an id, apart.
    static func credentials(_ token: String, account: String) -> Credentials
    /// A Windows game. The `title:` label keeps it apart from `InstallationStorefront.game(_:)`.
    static func game(_ key: String, title: String) -> Game
    static func playtime(_ key: String, minutes: UInt64) -> Playtime
    static func details(bytes: UInt64?) -> Details
    /// The Library cache of `directory` once it holds `entries` for `account`.
    static func cache(_ entries: [(game: Game, minutes: UInt64?)], account: String, in directory: URL) throws -> LibraryCache
    static var unauthorized: Error { get }
    static var network: Error { get }
    static var expectedAvatar: URL? { get }
    /// What the store shows once it refuses the account, spelled out here
    /// rather than asked of the adapter, so a wrong mapping fails.
    static var unauthorizedMessage: String { get }
    /// The warning after a sign-out the store may not have revoked, spelled
    /// out for the same reason.
    static var revocationMessage: String { get }
    static func session(_ fake: WebTestSession<Self>) -> Session
}

extension WebStoreFixture {
    static func credentials(_ token: String) -> Credentials { credentials(token, account: fixtureAccount) }
}

/// The store's account model, with test Game sessions. A sign-in or
/// restoration the test does not inject fails rather than reach the storefront.
@MainActor
func webModel<S: WebStoreFixture>(
    _: S.Type,
    _ keychain: MemoryStore<S.Credentials>,
    authorize: @escaping @MainActor () async throws -> String = { "test-code" },
    signIn: @escaping @Sendable (String) async throws -> S.Session = { _ in throw S.network },
    restore: @escaping @Sendable (S.Credentials) async throws -> S.Session = { _ in throw S.network },
    language: String = "en-US",
    gameSessions: GameSessions<S>? = nil,
    libraryCache: LibraryCache? = nil
) -> WebAccountModel<S> {
    WebAccountModel(keychain: keychain, authorize: authorize, signIn: signIn, restore: restore, language: language,
                    gameSessions: gameSessions ?? GameSessions(), libraryCache: libraryCache)
}

/// A model whose saved session restores as `session`, once its library loaded.
@MainActor
func connectedModel<S: WebStoreFixture>(_ session: WebTestSession<S>, language: String = "en-US") async -> WebAccountModel<S> {
    let model = webModel(S.self, MemoryStore(S.credentials("current")), restore: { _ in S.session(session) },
                         language: language)
    await model.start()
    XCTAssertTrue(model.isConnected)
    return model
}

extension EpicGames: WebStoreFixture {
    typealias Playtime = EpicPlaytime
    typealias DetailsRequest = EpicDetailsRequest

    static let fixtureAccount = "fixture-id"
    static let fixtureName = "Fixture"
    static func credentials(_ token: String, account: String) -> EpicCredentials {
        EpicCredentials(accountId: account, displayName: account == fixtureAccount ? fixtureName : "Name of \(account)",
                        refreshToken: token)
    }
    /// The app name and catalog item are the key, in the "fixture" namespace.
    static func game(_ key: String, title: String) -> EpicGame {
        EpicGame(appName: key, namespace: "fixture", catalogItemId: key, title: title, description: "", imageUrl: nil,
                 headerImageUrl: nil, developer: "", windows: true, macos: false)
    }
    static func playtime(_ key: String, minutes: UInt64) -> EpicPlaytime { EpicPlaytime(appName: key, seconds: minutes * 60) }
    static func details(bytes: UInt64?) -> EpicGameDetails { EpicGameDetails(platform: nil, installationBytes: bytes) }
    static func cache(_ entries: [(game: EpicGame, minutes: UInt64?)], account: String, in directory: URL) throws -> LibraryCache {
        let games = entries.map { CachedEpicGame(game: $0.game, playtimeSeconds: $0.minutes.map { $0 * 60 }) }
        return try LibraryCache.holding(epic: [account: games], in: directory)
    }
    static var unauthorized: Error { EpicError.Unauthorized }
    static var network: Error { EpicError.Network }
    static let expectedAvatar: URL? = nil
    static var unauthorizedMessage: String { L10n.string("model.epic.unauthorized") }
    static var revocationMessage: String { L10n.string("model.epic.revocationUnconfirmed") }
    static func session(_ fake: WebTestSession<EpicGames>) -> any EpicSessionProtocol { fake }

typealias EpicTestSession = WebTestSession<EpicGames>
typealias GogTestSession = WebTestSession<GogGames>

/// A storefront's Rust session as the model tests drive it: the test holds,
/// fails or rotates each answer, and the session records every call.
actor WebTestSession<Store: WebStoreFixture> {
    nonisolated let credentialRevisions = EpicCredentialRevisionFeed()

    private var currentCredentials: Store.Credentials {
        didSet { credentialRevisions.publish() }
    }
    private let ownedGames: [Store.Game]
    private let ownedPlaytimes: [Store.Playtime]
    private var rotated: Store.Credentials?
    private var prepared: Store.Credentials?
    private var failNext = false
    private var expireNext = false
    private var holdNext = false
    private var gameContinuation: CheckedContinuation<[Store.Game], Never>?
    private(set) var waitingForGames = false
    private(set) var gameCalls = 0
    private var failNextPlaytimeRequest = false
    private(set) var playtimeCalls = 0
    /// The product ids of each of GOG's playtime requests.
    private(set) var playtimeRequests: [[String]] = []
    private var shouldHoldDetails = false
    private var detailsFailureCredentials: Store.Credentials?
    private var detailsContinuations: [Int: CheckedContinuation<Store.Details, Never>] = [:]
    private(set) var detailsCalls: [Store.DetailsRequest] = []
    private(set) var returnedDetails = 0
    private var shouldHoldCredentials = false
    private var credentialsContinuation: CheckedContinuation<Bool, Never>?
    private(set) var waitingForCredentials = false
    private var shouldHoldDisconnect = false
    private var shouldFailDisconnect = false
    private var disconnectContinuation: CheckedContinuation<Bool, Never>?
    private(set) var waitingForDisconnect = false
    private(set) var disconnections = 0
    /// Each achievements request, as the storefront received it.
    private(set) var achievementReads: [AchievementRead] = []
    /// Each game's achievements, unlocked or not, by the name requests give
    /// it; a game not named has one unlocked of two.
    private var achievementStates: [String: [Bool]] = [:]
    /// The games whose achievements request fails.
    private var failingAchievements: Set<String> = []

    init(credentials: Store.Credentials, games: [Store.Game], rotated: Store.Credentials? = nil,
         playtimes: [Store.Playtime] = []) {
        currentCredentials = credentials
        ownedGames = games
        self.rotated = rotated
        ownedPlaytimes = playtimes
    }

    /// Ignores cancellation, as the generated bindings do: a cancelled sign-in
    /// still gets its credentials back, and the model must drop them itself.
    func credentials() async throws -> Store.Credentials {
        if shouldHoldCredentials {
            shouldHoldCredentials = false
            waitingForCredentials = true
            let failing = await withCheckedContinuation { credentialsContinuation = $0 }
            waitingForCredentials = false
            if failing { throw Store.network }
        }
        return currentCredentials
    }
    func holdNextCredentials() { shouldHoldCredentials = true }
    func completeCredentials(failing: Bool) {
        credentialsContinuation?.resume(returning: failing)
        credentialsContinuation = nil
    }
    func rotate(_ credentials: Store.Credentials) { currentCredentials = credentials }
    func rotateOnPrepare(_ credentials: Store.Credentials) { prepared = credentials }

    func games() async throws -> [Store.Game] {
        gameCalls += 1
        if let rotated { currentCredentials = rotated; self.rotated = nil }
        if expireNext { expireNext = false; throw Store.unauthorized }
        if failNext { failNext = false; throw Store.network }
        if holdNext {
            holdNext = false
            waitingForGames = true
            let result = await withCheckedContinuation { gameContinuation = $0 }
            waitingForGames = false
            return result
        }
        return ownedGames
    }
    func holdNextGames() { holdNext = true }
    func completeGames(_ games: [Store.Game]) { gameContinuation?.resume(returning: games); gameContinuation = nil }
    func expireNextGames() { expireNext = true }
    func failNextGames(rotated: Store.Credentials) { failNext = true; self.rotated = rotated }

    func failNextPlaytimes() { failNextPlaytimeRequest = true }

    func holdNextDetails() { shouldHoldDetails = true }
    func completeDetails(_ invocation: Int, with details: Store.Details, rotated: Store.Credentials? = nil) {
        if let rotated { currentCredentials = rotated }
        detailsContinuations.removeValue(forKey: invocation)?.resume(returning: details)
    }
    func failNextDetails(rotated: Store.Credentials) { detailsFailureCredentials = rotated }

    func disconnect() async throws {
        disconnections += 1
        if shouldHoldDisconnect {
            shouldHoldDisconnect = false
            waitingForDisconnect = true
            let failing = await withCheckedContinuation { disconnectContinuation = $0 }
            waitingForDisconnect = false
            if failing { throw Store.network }
        }
        if shouldFailDisconnect { shouldFailDisconnect = false; throw Store.network }
    }
    func holdNextDisconnect() { shouldHoldDisconnect = true }
    func completeDisconnect(failing: Bool) { disconnectContinuation?.resume(returning: failing); disconnectContinuation = nil }
    func failNextDisconnect() { shouldFailDisconnect = true }

    func nextCredentialsRevision(afterRevision: UInt64) async -> UInt64? {
        await credentialRevisions.next(after: afterRevision)
    }
    nonisolated func shutdownObservers() { credentialRevisions.stop() }

    /// Rotates as Rust's client does when it renews its token before a call.
    private func preparing() {
        if let prepared { currentCredentials = prepared; self.prepared = nil }
    }

    private func answerPlaytimes() async throws -> [Store.Playtime] {
        playtimeCalls += 1
        if failNextPlaytimeRequest { failNextPlaytimeRequest = false; throw Store.network }
        return ownedPlaytimes
    }

    private func answerDetails(_ request: Store.DetailsRequest) async throws -> Store.Details {
        preparing()
        detailsCalls.append(request)
        defer { returnedDetails += 1 }
        if let rotated = detailsFailureCredentials {
            currentCredentials = rotated
            detailsFailureCredentials = nil
            throw Store.network
        }
        if shouldHoldDetails {
            shouldHoldDetails = false
            let invocation = detailsCalls.count
            return await withCheckedContinuation { detailsContinuations[invocation] = $0 }
        }
        return Store.details(bytes: nil)
    }

    func setAchievements(_ states: [String: [Bool]], failing: Set<String> = []) {
        achievementStates = states
        failingAchievements = failing
    }

    /// Records the request, then tells which of each game's achievements
    /// are unlocked, but the `failing` games'; it throws when it could tell
    /// none.
    private func readAchievements(_ ids: [String], locale: String, fresh: Bool) throws -> [String: [Bool]] {
        achievementReads.append(AchievementRead(ids: ids, locale: locale, fresh: fresh))
        let told = ids.filter { !failingAchievements.contains($0) }.map { ($0, achievementStates[$0] ?? [true, false]) }
        if told.isEmpty && !ids.isEmpty { throw Store.network }
        return Dictionary(told, uniquingKeysWith: { first, _ in first })
    }

    fileprivate func readAchievements(of id: String, locale: String, fresh: Bool) throws -> [LibraryAchievement] {
        let states = try readAchievements([id], locale: locale, fresh: fresh)[id] ?? []
        return states.enumerated().map { index, unlocked in
            LibraryAchievement(id: "\(index)", name: "Achievement \(index)", description: "", iconUrl: "",
                               hidden: false, unlocked: unlocked, unlockedAt: unlocked ? 1_790_000_000 : nil)
        }
    }

    fileprivate func readAchievementShares(_ ids: [String], locale: String) throws -> [String: Double] {
        try readAchievements(ids, locale: locale, fresh: false).compactMapValues { states in
            states.isEmpty ? nil : Double(states.count { $0 }) / Double(states.count)
        }
    }
}

/// One achievements request: the games it names (Epic's namespaces, GOG's
/// products), its locale, and whether it skips the Library cache.
struct AchievementRead: Equatable, Sendable {
    let ids: [String]
    let locale: String
    let fresh: Bool
}

extension WebTestSession: EpicSessionProtocol where Store == EpicGames {
    func gameDetails(namespace: String, catalogItemId: String, appName: String) async throws -> EpicGameDetails {
        try await answerDetails(EpicDetailsRequest(namespace: namespace, catalogItemId: catalogItemId, appName: appName))
    }
    func playtimes() async throws -> [EpicPlaytime] { try await answerPlaytimes() }
    func achievements(namespace: String, locale: String, fresh: Bool) async throws -> [LibraryAchievement] {
        try readAchievements(of: namespace, locale: locale, fresh: fresh)
    }
    func achievementShares(namespaces: [String], locale: String) async throws -> [String: Double] {
        try readAchievementShares(namespaces, locale: locale)
    }

    func startFriends() async {}
    func reconnectFriends() async {}
    nonisolated func stopFriends() {}
    nonisolated func friends() -> EpicFriendsSnapshot {
        EpicFriendsSnapshot(accountId: "unused", revision: 1, connection: .stopped, friends: [], message: nil)
    }
    func nextFriends(afterRevision: UInt64) async -> EpicFriendsSnapshot { friends() }
}

extension WebTestSession: GogSessionProtocol where Store == GogGames {
    func gameDetails(productId: String, language: String) async throws -> GogGameDetails {
        try await answerDetails(GogDetailsRequest(productId: productId, language: language))
    }
    func playtimes(productIds: [String]) async throws -> [GogPlaytime] {
        playtimeRequests.append(productIds)
        return try await answerPlaytimes()
    }
    func achievements(productId: String, locale: String, fresh: Bool) async throws -> [LibraryAchievement] {
        try readAchievements(of: productId, locale: locale, fresh: fresh)
    }
    func achievementShares(productIds: [String], locale: String) async throws -> [String: Double] {
        try readAchievementShares(productIds, locale: locale)
    }
    nonisolated func avatarUrl() -> String? { GogGames.expectedAvatar?.absoluteString }
}

typealias EpicMemoryStore = MemoryStore<EpicCredentials>

/// The Keychain as the model tests drive it: it records every write, and the
/// test holds or rejects saves.
actor MemoryStore<Credentials: Sendable>: CredentialStore {
    private(set) var value: Credentials?
    private(set) var loads = 0
    private(set) var writes: [Credentials?] = []
    private(set) var waitingForSave = false
    private var shouldHoldSave = false
    private var shouldRejectSaves = false
    private var saveContinuation: CheckedContinuation<Void, Never>?

    init(_ value: Credentials?) { self.value = value }
    func load() async throws -> Credentials? { loads += 1; return value }
    func save(_ credentials: Credentials) async throws {
        if shouldRejectSaves { throw CocoaError(.fileWriteUnknown) }
        if shouldHoldSave {
            shouldHoldSave = false
            waitingForSave = true
            await withCheckedContinuation { saveContinuation = $0 }
            waitingForSave = false
        }
        value = credentials
        writes.append(credentials)
    }
    func remove() async throws { value = nil; writes.append(nil) }
    func holdNextSave() { shouldHoldSave = true }
    func completeSave() { saveContinuation?.resume(); saveContinuation = nil }
    func rejectSaves(_ reject: Bool = true) { shouldRejectSaves = reject }
}

/// A sign-in that records each code it exchanges.
actor SignInCounter<Session: Sendable> {
    let session: Session
    private(set) var calls = 0
    private(set) var codes: [String] = []
    init(session: Session) { self.session = session }
    func signIn(code: String? = nil) -> Session {
        calls += 1
        if let code { codes.append(code) }
        return session
    }
}

/// A restoration whose first attempt fails with `failure`.
actor RestoreAttempt<Session: Sendable> {
    let session: Session
    private let failure: Error
    private var attempts = 0
    init(session: Session, failure: Error) {
        self.session = session
        self.failure = failure
    }
    func restore() throws -> Session {
        attempts += 1
        if attempts == 1 { throw failure }
        return session
    }
}

/// The storefront's page, answering each authorization when the test completes it.
@MainActor
final class AuthorizationGate {
    private var continuations: [Int: CheckedContinuation<String, Error>] = [:]
    private(set) var calls = 0
    private(set) var returnedCalls = 0

    func wait() async throws -> String {
        calls += 1
        let invocation = calls
        let code = try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { continuations[invocation] = $0 }
        returnedCalls += 1
        return code
    }

    func complete(_ invocation: Int, code: String) {
        continuations.removeValue(forKey: invocation)?.resume(returning: code)
    }
}
```

```swift
/// The account lifecycle, library and game page every web storefront shares.

    func testPlaytimesLoadFromOneRequestAndOrderTheLibrary() async throws {

    private func playtimeOrder<S: WebStoreFixture>(_: S.Type) async throws {
        let games = [S.game("a", title: "Alpha"), S.game("b", title: "Beta"), S.game("c", title: "Gamma"),
                     S.game("d", title: "Delta")]
        let stored = S.credentials("current")
        let session = WebTestSession<S>(credentials: stored, games: games, playtimes: [
            S.playtime("c", minutes: 600), S.playtime("b", minutes: 10), S.playtime("a", minutes: 0),

        await model.start()
        defer { model.signOut() }
        try await eventually { model.library.playtime(of: games[2]) == .seconds(36_000) }

        XCTAssertNil(model.library.pendingMetadata)
        XCTAssertNil(model.library.missingMetadata)

        model.signOut()

    }

    // MARK: Account

    func testRestoreRunsOnceAndSavesRotatedRefreshToken() async throws {

    private func restoreOnce<S: WebStoreFixture>(_: S.Type) async throws {
        let original = S.credentials("original")
        let rotated = S.credentials("rotated")
        let store = MemoryStore(original)
        let session = WebTestSession<S>(credentials: original, games: [S.game("1", title: "One")], rotated: rotated)

    func testCancelledAuthorizationCannotExchangeLateCodeOrReplaceNewLogin() async throws {
        try await cancelledAuthorization(Self.store!)
    }
    private func cancelledAuthorization<S: WebStoreFixture>(_: S.Type) async throws {
        let store = MemoryStore<S.Credentials>(nil)
        let current = S.credentials("current")
        let session = WebTestSession<S>(credentials: current, games: [S.game("1", title: "One")])
        let browser = AuthorizationGate()
        let login = SignInCounter(session: S.session(session))
        let model = webModel(S.self, store, authorize: { try await browser.wait() }, signIn: { await login.signIn(code: $0) })

        model.signIn()
        try await eventually { browser.calls == 1 }
        model.cancelSignIn()
        model.signIn()
        try await eventually { browser.calls == 2 }
        browser.complete(1, code: "late-code")
        try await eventually { browser.returnedCalls == 1 }
        let codesWhileWaiting = await login.codes
        XCTAssertTrue(codesWhileWaiting.isEmpty)
        XCTAssertTrue(model.isConnecting)
        XCTAssertFalse(model.isConnected)

        browser.complete(2, code: "current-code")
        try await eventually { model.isConnected && !model.isLoadingGames }
        try await eventually { browser.returnedCalls == 2 }
        let codes = await login.codes
        let saved = await store.value
        XCTAssertEqual(codes, ["current-code"])
        XCTAssertEqual(saved, current)
        XCTAssertTrue(model.isConnected)
        XCTAssertFalse(model.isConnecting)
        XCTAssertNil(model.errorMessage)
    }

    func testALateRevocationFailureDoesNotWarnTheNextSignIn() async throws {
        try await lateRevocationFailure(Self.store!)
    }
    private func lateRevocationFailure<S: WebStoreFixture>(_: S.Type) async throws {
        let stored = S.credentials("current")
        let session = WebTestSession<S>(credentials: stored, games: [S.game("1", title: "One")])
        let browser = AuthorizationGate()
        let model = webModel(S.self, MemoryStore(stored), authorize: { try await browser.wait() },
                             restore: { _ in S.session(session) })
        await model.start()
        XCTAssertTrue(model.isConnected)
        await session.holdNextDisconnect()

        model.signOut()
        try await eventually { await session.waitingForDisconnect }
        XCTAssertFalse(model.isSigningOut)
        model.signIn()
        try await eventually { browser.calls == 1 }
        await session.completeDisconnect(failing: true)
        // The failed revocation's continuation runs on the main actor next.
        await drainMainQueue(times: 2)
        XCTAssertNil(model.storageWarning, "A sign-in that started since owns the warning")
        XCTAssertTrue(model.isConnecting)

        model.cancelSignIn()
        browser.complete(1, code: "late-code")
        try await eventually { browser.returnedCalls == 1 }
        XCTAssertFalse(model.isConnecting)
    }

    func testPlaytimesAreAskedOnceTheGamesLoaded() async throws {
        try await playtimesAfterGames(Self.store!)
    }
    private func playtimesAfterGames<S: WebStoreFixture>(_: S.Type) async throws {

                                        playtimes: [S.playtime("1", minutes: 5)])

    func testLateDetailsCannotReplaceAnotherGamesDetails() async throws {
        try await lateDetails(Self.store!)
    }
    private func lateDetails<S: WebStoreFixture>(_: S.Type) async throws {
        let first = S.game("1", title: "One")
        let second = S.game("2", title: "Two")
        let session = WebTestSession<S>(credentials: S.credentials("current"), games: [first, second])
        let model = webModel(S.self, MemoryStore(S.credentials("current")), restore: { _ in S.session(session) })
        await model.start()
        await session.holdNextDetails()
        model.open(first)
        try await eventually { await session.detailsCalls.count == 1 }

        model.open(second)
        try await eventually { !model.isLoadingGameDetails }
        let secondDetails = model.selectedGameDetails
        await session.completeDetails(1, with: S.details(bytes: 999))
        try await eventually { await session.returnedDetails == 2 }
        await Task.yield()

        XCTAssertEqual(model.selectedGame?.id, second.id)
        XCTAssertEqual(model.selectedGameDetails, secondDetails)
        XCTAssertFalse(model.isLoadingGameDetails)
    }

    func testReopeningSameGameDiscardsItsPreviousDetailsRequest() async throws {
        try await reopenedDetails(Self.store!)
    }
    private func reopenedDetails<S: WebStoreFixture>(_: S.Type) async throws {

    }

    func testSigningOutDiscardsLateDetailsAndClearsSelection() async throws {

    }
    private func signOutDetails<S: WebStoreFixture>(_: S.Type) async throws {

        await session.completeDetails(1, with: S.details(bytes: 999))
        try await eventually {
            let returned = await session.returnedDetails
            return returned == 1 && !model.isSigningOut
        }
        await Task.yield()
        XCTAssertNil(model.selectedGame)
        XCTAssertNil(model.selectedGameDetails)
        XCTAssertFalse(model.isLoadingGameDetails)
        XCTAssertFalse(model.isConnected)
        let saved = await store.value
        XCTAssertNil(saved)
    }

    func testClosingGameStillSavesTokenRotatedByItsLateDetailsResponse() async throws {
        try await closedGameRotation(Self.store!)
    }
    private func closedGameRotation<S: WebStoreFixture>(_: S.Type) async throws {
        let owned = S.game("1", title: "One")
        let store = MemoryStore(S.credentials("current"))
        let session = WebTestSession<S>(credentials: S.credentials("current"), games: [owned])
        let model = webModel(S.self, store, restore: { _ in S.session(session) })
        await model.start()
        await session.holdNextDetails()
        model.open(owned)
        try await eventually { await session.detailsCalls.count == 1 }

        model.closeGame()
        let rotation = S.credentials("late-rotation")
        await session.completeDetails(1, with: S.details(bytes: 999), rotated: rotation)
        try await eventually { await store.value == rotation }
        XCTAssertNil(model.selectedGame)
        XCTAssertNil(model.selectedGameDetails)
        XCTAssertFalse(model.isLoadingGameDetails)
        XCTAssertTrue(model.isConnected)
    }

    func testDetailsFailureIsNonblockingAndCanRetryByReopeningOrRefreshing() async throws {
        try await detailsFailure(Self.store!)
    }
    private func detailsFailure<S: WebStoreFixture>(_: S.Type) async throws {
        let owned = S.game("1", title: "One")

        XCTAssertNil(model.errorMessage)
        XCTAssertTrue(model.isConnected)

        let calls = await session.detailsCalls
        XCTAssertEqual(calls.count, 3)

    /// Each store's tests check how its request names the game and the player's language.
    func testOpeningAGameLoadsItsAchievements() async throws {
```

```rs
//! Obelisk-owned Cloud decisions and durable save storage. No Valve ABI or network
//! calls belong here. An adapter must supply complete, verified remote views.
mod model;
mod reconcile;
mod retry;
mod vault;

pub use model::*;
pub use reconcile::*;
pub use retry::*;
pub use vault::*;

/// Exclusive locks that tolerate a child briefly sharing them while it spawns.
pub mod lock {
    pub use crate::vault::disk::try_lock;
}
/// Durable JSON journal primitives shared with adapters that keep their own
/// small state files beside the archive.
pub mod journal {
    pub use crate::vault::disk::{read, regular, write};
}

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum Error {
    #[error("Invalid Cloud state")]
    Invalid,
    #[error("Cloud storage is already in use")]
    Busy,
    /// A save path belongs to the other storefront, whose Cloud storage is in
    /// use, for example by its running game.
    #[error("Cloud saves are in use by another storefront")]
    OtherStoreBusy,
    #[error("Cloud content failed verification")]
    Integrity,
    #[error("Cloud state changed since the decision")]
    Stale,
    #[error("Cloud work requires authentication by its original account")]
    Authentication,
    #[error("Cloud preferences are disabled or unavailable")]
    Preferences,
    #[error("Cloud operation requires recovery")]
    Recovery,
    #[error("Cloud storage I/O failed")]
    Io(#[from] std::io::Error),
    #[error("Invalid Cloud journal")]
    Journal(#[from] serde_json::Error),
}

pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, Error>;
```

`crates/cloud-vault/src/model.rs`:

```rs
use crate::{Error, Result};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
use std::{
    collections::BTreeMap,
    path::{Path, PathBuf},
};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Ord, PartialOrd, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Scope {
    pub steam_id: u64,
    pub app_id: u32,
    pub cloud_app_id: u32,
}

impl Scope {
    pub fn validate(self) -> Result<()> {
        // Public-universe individual desktop account with a nonzero AccountID.
        if self.steam_id >> 32 != 0x0110_0001
            || self.steam_id as u32 == 0
            || self.app_id == 0
            || self.cloud_app_id == 0
        {
            return Err(Error::Invalid);
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Epic's account and game identity remains distinct from Steam's numeric IDs.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Ord, PartialOrd, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct EpicScope {
    pub account_id: String,
    pub namespace: String,
    pub app_name: String,
}

/// The directory under a vault root holding every Epic account.
const EPIC_STORE_DIRECTORY: &str = "epic";

/// Epic account IDs are 32 lowercase hex digits. Exposed on its own so callers
/// that know only an account never have to invent a scope to reach the rule.
pub fn epic_account_id(value: &str) -> Result<()> {
    if value.len() != 32
        || !value
            .bytes()
            .all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit() || (b'a'..=b'f').contains(&c))
    {
        return Err(Error::Invalid);
    }
    Ok(())
}

impl EpicScope {
    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<()> {
        epic_account_id(&self.account_id)?;
        if [&self.namespace, &self.app_name].into_iter().any(|value| {
            value.is_empty()
                || value.len() > 256
                || !value
                    .bytes()
                    .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(c, b'-' | b'_' | b'.'))
                || matches!(value.as_str(), "." | "..")
        }) {
            return Err(Error::Invalid);
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Untagged Steam serialization preserves existing schema-2 journals exactly.
/// Epic uses disjoint named fields, including its unmodified external identity.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Ord, PartialOrd, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(untagged)]
pub enum StoreScope {
    Steam(Scope),
    Epic(EpicScope),
}

impl From<Scope> for StoreScope {
    fn from(scope: Scope) -> Self {
        Self::Steam(scope)
    }
}

impl From<EpicScope> for StoreScope {
    fn from(scope: EpicScope) -> Self {
        Self::Epic(scope)
    }
}

impl StoreScope {
    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<()> {
        match self {
            Self::Steam(scope) => scope.validate(),
            Self::Epic(scope) => scope.validate(),
        }
    }

    /// Location for adapter journals beside the vault's state and blobs.
    /// This only derives a path; opening a Vault validates and locks its storage.
    pub fn directory(&self, root: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf> {
        self.validate()?;
        if !root.is_absolute() {
            return Err(Error::Invalid);
        }
        let account = self.account_directory(root);
        Ok(match self {
            Self::Steam(scope) => account.join(scope.cloud_app_id.to_string()),
            Self::Epic(scope) => {
                // Hash only the filesystem component, never the game identity.
                // Length-delimited JSON preserves tuple boundaries and case.
                let key = serde_json::to_vec(&(&scope.namespace, &scope.app_name))?;
                account.join(ContentHash::of(&key).as_str())
            }
        })
    }

    /// Every directory from `root` down to this scope's account directory, in
    /// creation order. Epic namespaces its accounts one level below Steam's.
    pub(crate) fn account_directories(&self, root: &Path) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
        match self {
            Self::Steam(_) => vec![self.account_directory(root)],
            Self::Epic(_) => vec![
                root.join(EPIC_STORE_DIRECTORY),
                self.account_directory(root),
            ],
        }
    }

    /// Where this storefront's archive lock lives.
    pub(crate) fn store_directory(&self, root: &Path) -> PathBuf {
        match self {
            Self::Steam(_) => root.to_path_buf(),
            Self::Epic(_) => root.join(EPIC_STORE_DIRECTORY),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn same_storefront(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            (self, other),
            (Self::Steam(_), Self::Steam(_)) | (Self::Epic(_), Self::Epic(_))
        )
    }

    pub(crate) fn account_directory(&self, root: &Path) -> PathBuf {
        self.account().layout(root)
    }

    pub(crate) fn account(&self) -> AccountIdentity {
        match self {
            Self::Steam(scope) => AccountIdentity::Steam(scope.steam_id),
            Self::Epic(scope) => AccountIdentity::Epic(scope.account_id.clone()),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn store_key(&self) -> Self {
        match self {
            Self::Steam(scope) => Self::Steam(Scope {
                app_id: scope.cloud_app_id,
                ..*scope
            }),
            Self::Epic(_) => self.clone(),
        }
    }
}

/// The adapter must supply the identity of its actual authenticated account.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum AccountIdentity {
    Steam(u64),
    Epic(String),
}

impl From<u64> for AccountIdentity {
    fn from(account: u64) -> Self {
        Self::Steam(account)
    }
}

impl From<&str> for AccountIdentity {
    fn from(account: &str) -> Self {
        Self::Epic(account.into())
    }
}

impl AccountIdentity {
    /// Where this account's game journals live. The layout has a single owner;
    /// callers derive it from here rather than re-spelling it.
    pub fn directory(&self, root: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf> {
        if let Self::Epic(account) = self {
            epic_account_id(account)?;
        }
        Ok(self.layout(root))
    }

    /// The account's directory, for an identity already validated.
    fn layout(&self, root: &Path) -> PathBuf {
        match self {
            Self::Steam(account) => root.join(account.to_string()),
            Self::Epic(account) => root.join(EPIC_STORE_DIRECTORY).join(account),
        }
    }

    // A private permit fingerprint keeps Authorization Copy. It is never an
    // external account identifier or a persisted store identity.
    pub(crate) fn permit_key(&self) -> [u8; 32] {
        let mut hash = Sha256::new();
        match self {
            Self::Steam(account) => {
                hash.update(b"steam\0");
                hash.update(account.to_le_bytes());
            }
            Self::Epic(account) => {
                hash.update(b"epic\0");
                hash.update(account.as_bytes());
            }
        }
        hash.finalize().into()
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Ord, PartialOrd, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(try_from = "String", into = "String")]
pub struct ContentHash(String);

impl ContentHash {
    pub fn of(bytes: &[u8]) -> Self {
        Self::of_hasher(Sha256::new_with_prefix(bytes))
    }

    pub(crate) fn of_hasher(hasher: Sha256) -> Self {
        Self(format!("{:x}", hasher.finalize()))
    }

    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &str {
        &self.0
    }
}

impl TryFrom<String> for ContentHash {
    type Error = Error;
    fn try_from(value: String) -> Result<Self> {
        if value.len() != 64
            || !value
                .bytes()
                .all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit() || (b'a'..=b'f').contains(&c))
        {
            return Err(Error::Invalid);
        }
        Ok(Self(value))
    }
}

impl From<ContentHash> for String {
    fn from(hash: ContentHash) -> Self {
        hash.0
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct FileVersion {
    pub hash: ContentHash,
    pub size: u64,
    pub platforms: u32,
}

/// A complete set. Absence means deletion. A CM delta must never be passed here
/// without first applying it to its known complete base. Names are remote keys,
/// not filesystem paths; only a separately validated resolver may map them.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, Eq, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(transparent)]
pub struct Manifest(pub BTreeMap<String, FileVersion>);

impl Manifest {
    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<()> {
        Self::validate_names(self.0.keys().map(String::as_str))
    }

    /// The remote-name rules shared by manifests and the bindings that map them.
    pub fn validate_names<'a>(names: impl ExactSizeIterator<Item = &'a str>) -> Result<()> {
        if names.len() > 100_000 {
            return Err(Error::Invalid);
        }
        for name in names {
            if name.is_empty() || name.len() > 4096 || name.chars().any(char::is_control) {
                return Err(Error::Invalid);
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn id(&self) -> ContentHash {
        // BTreeMap ordering and fixed field order make the persisted identity
        // independent of enumeration order and timestamps.
        ContentHash::of(&serde_json::to_vec(self).expect("manifest serialization"))
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct RemoteView {
    /// Opaque adapter cursor. Content is also compared when fencing decisions.
    pub revision: String,
    pub files: Manifest,
}

impl RemoteView {
    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<()> {
        if self.revision.is_empty() || self.revision.len() > 1024 {
            return Err(Error::Invalid);
        }
        self.files.validate()
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct LocalIntent {
    /// Remote view observed when the user chose local during a conflict. This
    /// does not claim that those local bytes have ever reached Steam.
    pub against: RemoteView,
}

/// Unknown preferences never grant permission to transfer. An authenticated
/// adapter refreshes both settings when it opens a coordinator.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]
pub struct Preferences {
    pub account_enabled: Option<bool>,
    pub game_enabled: Option<bool>,
}

impl Preferences {
    pub fn enabled(self) -> bool {
        self.account_enabled == Some(true) && self.game_enabled == Some(true)
    }
}
```

`crates/cloud-vault/src/reconcile.rs`:

```rs
use crate::{LocalIntent, Manifest, RemoteView};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Decision {
    Converged,
    KeepLocal,
    Download,
    Conflict,
}

/// Pure three-way comparison of complete content, including deletions. The
/// caller cannot represent an unavailable remote as a successful empty view.
pub fn reconcile(
    baseline: Option<&RemoteView>,
    local: &Manifest,
    remote: &RemoteView,
    intent: Option<&LocalIntent>,
) -> Decision {
    if local == &remote.files {
        return Decision::Converged;
    }
    if let Some(intent) = intent {
        return if &intent.against == remote {
            Decision::KeepLocal
        } else {
            // A stale local choice never authorizes replacing a newer remote.
            Decision::Conflict
        };
    }
    match baseline {
        Some(base) => match (local != &base.files, remote.files != base.files) {
            (false, true) => Decision::Download,
            (true, false) => Decision::KeepLocal,
            _ => Decision::Conflict,
        },
        None if local.0.is_empty() => Decision::Download,
        None if remote.files.0.is_empty() => Decision::KeepLocal,
        None => Decision::Conflict,
    }
}
```

`crates/cloud-vault/src/retry.rs`:

```rs
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

const DELAYS: [u64; 2] = [1, 2];

#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum Retry {
    Wait(Duration),
    Attempt { remaining: Duration },
    Defer,
}

/// One monotonic budget includes requests and confirmation. Reopening a worker
/// creates a new budget; transient failures and wake do not reset this one.
pub struct RetryBudget {
    deadline: Instant,
    retry_at: Option<Instant>,
    attempts: usize,
    active: bool,
    action_required: bool,
}

impl RetryBudget {
    pub fn new(start: Instant) -> Self {
        Self {
            deadline: start + Duration::from_secs(120),
            retry_at: None,
            attempts: 0,
            active: false,
            action_required: false,
        }
    }

    pub fn poll(&mut self, now: Instant) -> Retry {
        if self.action_required || now >= self.deadline {
            return Retry::Defer;
        }
        if self.active {
            return Retry::Wait(self.deadline - now);
        }
        if self.attempts > 0 {
            let Some(due) = self.retry_at else {
                return Retry::Defer;
            };
            if due >= self.deadline {
                return Retry::Defer;
            }
            if now < due {
                return Retry::Wait(due - now);
            }
        }
        self.active = true;
        self.attempts += 1;
        self.retry_at = None;
        Retry::Attempt {
            remaining: self.deadline - now,
        }
    }

    pub fn failed(&mut self, now: Instant, requires_action: bool) {
        if self.active {
            self.active = false;
            self.retry_at = DELAYS
                .get(self.attempts - 1)
                .map(|delay| now + Duration::from_secs(*delay));
            self.action_required |= requires_action;
        }
    }
}
```
