```rs
use std::{
    path::PathBuf,
    sync::{
        Arc, Mutex,
        atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering},
    },
    time::{Duration, Instant},
};

/// Every supervisor entry point drives its async work from one blocking thread.
pub(crate) fn executor() -> std::io::Result<Executor> {
    tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread()
        .enable_all()
        .build()
        .map(|runtime| Executor(Some(runtime)))
}

/// Dropping waits at most a second for blocking work, so a pending DNS lookup
/// cannot hold a caller whose async work has already completed.
pub(crate) struct Executor(Option<tokio::runtime::Runtime>);
impl Executor {
    pub(crate) fn block_on<F: std::future::Future>(&self, future: F) -> F::Output {
        self.0
            .as_ref()
            .expect("executor runs until dropped")
            .block_on(future)
    }
}
impl Drop for Executor {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if let Some(runtime) = self.0.take() {
            runtime.shutdown_timeout(Duration::from_secs(1));
        }
    }
}

/// Seconds since the Unix epoch.
pub(crate) fn unix_now() -> u64 {
    std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .unwrap_or_default()
        .as_secs()
}

/// The pinned engine hash lives only in the runtime manifest; this reads it back.
pub fn client_sha256() -> &'static str {
    &package::entry("steamclient.dylib").sha256
}
pub fn native_cache_checkpoint(directory: PathBuf, app_id: u32, platforms: u32) -> bool {
    native_cache_files(directory, app_id, platforms).is_ok()
}
/// A published projection always carries its index, so a missing `remotecache.vdf`
/// is an incomplete projection rather than an empty one. `SdkCloudPaths::records`
/// cannot tell the two apart, so the distinction is enforced here for every caller.
pub fn native_cache_files(
    directory: PathBuf,
    app_id: u32,
    platforms: u32,
) -> Result<Vec<steam_kit::cloud::LocalCloudFile>, Error> {
    if !directory.join("remotecache.vdf").is_file() {
        return Err(Error::Storage);
    }
    steam_kit::cloud::SdkCloudPaths::new(directory, app_id, platforms)
        .and_then(|paths| paths.local_files(&[]))
        .map_err(|_| Error::Storage)
}
pub fn sha(path: &std::path::Path) -> std::io::Result<String> {
    use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
    let mut digest = Sha256::new();
    let mut file = std::io::BufReader::with_capacity(64 * 1024, std::fs::File::open(path)?);
    std::io::copy(&mut file, &mut digest)?;
    Ok(format!("{:x}", digest.finalize()))
}

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum Error {
    #[error("{0}")]
    Cloud(steam::cloud::Failure),
    #[error("backend.steam.runtime.sessionBusy")]
    SessionBusy,
    #[error("backend.steam.runtime.cancelled")]
    Cancelled,
    #[error("backend.steam.runtime.invalidSession")]
    InvalidSession,
    #[error("backend.steam.runtime.unavailable")]
    Unavailable,
    #[error("backend.steam.runtime.versionMismatch")]
    VersionMismatch,
    #[error("backend.steam.runtime.startFailed")]
    StartFailed,
    #[error("backend.steam.runtime.authenticationFailed")]
    Authentication,
    #[error("backend.steam.runtime.ownershipFailed")]
    Ownership,
    #[error("backend.steam.runtime.timeout")]
    Timeout,
    #[error("backend.steam.runtime.storageFailed")]
    Storage,
    /// A Mac build without an arm64 slice, installed before Obelisk
    /// installed such a game's Windows build instead.
    #[error("backend.runtime.macBuildNotNative")]
    IncompatibleArchitecture,
    #[error("backend.runtime.rosettaUnavailable")]
    RosettaUnavailable,
    #[error("backend.runtime.invalidApplication")]
    InvalidApplication,
    #[error("backend.runtime.notExecutable")]
    NotExecutable,
    #[error("backend.steam.runtime.apiMissing")]
    ApiMissing,
    #[error("backend.runtime.wineUnavailable")]
    WineUnavailable,
}
impl From<std::io::Error> for Error {
    fn from(_: std::io::Error) -> Self {
        Self::Storage
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Config {
    pub helpers: PathBuf,
    pub package: PathBuf,
    pub cache: PathBuf,
    pub diagnostics: PathBuf,
    /// A Mac game's Steam API library, whose slices choose the game's. A
    /// Windows game names none: Wine loads whatever Steam API the game
    /// ships, if any.
    pub steam_api: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub home: PathBuf,
    pub app_id: u32,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub cloud_save_roots: Vec<PathBuf>,
    /// Set for a Windows game, which runs in Obelisk's Wine runtime.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub wine: Option<wine::Config>,
}

pub struct Launch {
    credentials: Mutex<Option<Credentials>>,
    cancelled: Arc<AtomicBool>,
}
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct NativeStorage {
    pub home: PathBuf,
    pub account_id: u64,
    pub app_id: u32,
    /// The game's platform, as a Cloud platform mask. A Windows game's SDK
    /// files live in the macOS Steam engine's storage too.
    pub platforms: u32,
}
impl NativeStorage {
    pub fn steam_directory(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.home.join("Library/Application Support/Steam")
    }
    /// The account- and app-specific SDK cloud cache the coordinator projects into.
    pub fn cache_directory(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.steam_directory().join(format!(
            "userdata/{}/{}",
            self.account_id as u32, self.app_id
        ))
    }
}
impl Launch {
    pub fn new(credentials: Credentials) -> Self {
        Self {
            credentials: Mutex::new(Some(credentials)),
            cancelled: Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false)),
        }
    }
    pub fn cancel(&self) {
        self.cancelled.store(true, Ordering::Release);
    }
    /// Starts the native host. `storage` is the Steam Cloud cache the game's
    /// SDK reads, when Cloud runs for this launch.
    pub fn prepare(
        &self,
        config: Config,
        storage: Option<NativeStorage>,
    ) -> Result<Runtime, Error> {
        let mut events = Vec::new();
        let result = self.prepare_inner(&config, storage, &mut events);
        if let Err(error) = &result {
            let _ = files::failure_report(&config, error, &events);
        }
        result
    }
    fn prepare_inner(
        &self,
        config: &Config,
        storage: Option<NativeStorage>,
        events: &mut Vec<Event>,
    ) -> Result<Runtime, Error> {
        self.check_cancelled()?;
        let credentials = self
            .credentials
            .lock()
            .map_err(|_| Error::InvalidSession)?
            .take()
            .ok_or(Error::InvalidSession)?;
        if !credentials.valid() || config.app_id == 0 {
            return Err(Error::InvalidSession);
        }
        let prepared = files::prepare(config, &self.cancelled)?;
        self.prepare_runtime(
            config,
            storage,
            events,
            credentials,
            prepared,
            process::Child::host,
        )
    }
    fn prepare_runtime(
        &self,
        config: &Config,
        storage: Option<NativeStorage>,
        events: &mut Vec<Event>,
        credentials: Credentials,
        mut prepared: files::Prepared,
        start_host: impl FnOnce(&files::Prepared, &Config, &str) -> Result<process::Child, Error>,
    ) -> Result<Runtime, Error> {
        let id = credentials.steam_id;
        if let Some(storage) = &storage {
            if storage.account_id != id || storage.app_id != config.app_id {
                return Err(Error::InvalidSession);
            }
            prepared.enable_storage(storage)?;
        }
        self.check_cancelled()?;
        let service = format!(
            "com.zagrios.obelisk.discovery.{}",
            uuid::Uuid::new_v4().simple()
        );
        let mut host = start_host(&prepared, config, &service)?;
        credentials
            .write(host.input.as_mut().ok_or(Error::StartFailed)?)
            .map_err(|_| Error::StartFailed)?;
        drop(credentials);
        let ticket_bytes = self.wait_for_host(&mut host, config.app_id, events)?;
        self.check_cancelled()?;
        if !host.alive()? {
            return Err(Error::StartFailed);
        }
        // The pinned host has verified its account, subscription and ticket.
        // Let the game attach using its own SDK and interface versions. The
        // host does not initialize the game's SDK.
        let proof = Proof {
            app_id: config.app_id,
            host_pid: host.id(),
            authenticated: true,
            ticket_bytes,
            host_account_verified: true,
            host_license_verified: true,
            sdk_checked: false,
            game_pid: None,
            game_exit: None,
            discovery_paths: 0,
            host_state: HostState::Online,
            state: "ready".into(),
        };
        let wakeup = host.wakeup.clone();
        let runtime = Runtime {
            inner: Mutex::new(Inner {
                host,
                proof,
                requests: GameRequests::default(),
                sequence: 0,
                stopped: false,
            }),
            wakeup,
            service,
            prepared,
        };
        runtime.write_report()?;
        Ok(runtime)
    }
    fn wait_for_host(
        &self,
        host: &mut process::Child,
        expected_app: u32,
        events: &mut Vec<Event>,
    ) -> Result<u32, Error> {
        let start = Instant::now();
        let mut authenticated = false;
        loop {
            self.check_cancelled()?;
            if start.elapsed() > Duration::from_secs(50) {
                return Err(Error::Timeout);
            }
            let event = host.next(Duration::from_millis(50))?;
            if let Some(event) = &event {
                events.push(event.clone());
            }
            match event {
                Some(Event::Authenticated {}) if !authenticated => authenticated = true,
                Some(Event::Ready {
                    app_id,
                    host_pid,
                    ticket_bytes,
                }) if authenticated
                    && app_id == expected_app
                    && host_pid == host.id()
                    && ticket_bytes > 0 =>
                {
                    return Ok(ticket_bytes);
                }
                Some(Event::Failed { reason }) => return Err(failure(reason)),
                Some(_) => return Err(Error::StartFailed),
                None => {}
            }
        }
    }
    fn check_cancelled(&self) -> Result<(), Error> {
        package::check(&self.cancelled)
    }
}
fn failure(reason: protocol::Failure) -> Error {
    match reason {
        protocol::Failure::Authentication => Error::Authentication,
        protocol::Failure::Ownership => Error::Ownership,
        protocol::Failure::Cancelled => Error::Cancelled,
        _ => Error::StartFailed,
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, serde::Serialize)]
pub struct Proof {
    pub app_id: u32,
    pub host_pid: u32,
    pub authenticated: bool,
    pub ticket_bytes: u32,
    pub host_account_verified: bool,
    pub host_license_verified: bool,
    pub sdk_checked: bool,
    pub game_pid: Option<u32>,
    pub game_exit: Option<i32>,
    pub discovery_paths: u32,
    pub host_state: HostState,
    pub state: String,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum HostState {
    Online,
    Disconnected,
    Lost,
    Stopped,
}
/// The latest invite dialog the game asked for. `sequence` grows with every
/// request of the session, so a repeated request still reads as new.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct InviteRequest {
    pub sequence: u64,
    pub target: protocol::InviteTarget,
}

/// The latest overlay the game asked Steam for. `sequence` grows with every
/// request of the session, so a repeated request still reads as new.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct OverlayRequest {
    pub sequence: u64,
    pub dialog: protocol::OverlayDialog,
}
impl OverlayRequest {
    /// The same request, when it asks for an invite dialog.
    pub fn invite(&self) -> Option<InviteRequest> {
        Some(InviteRequest {
            sequence: self.sequence,
            target: self.dialog.invite()?,
        })
    }
}

/// An invitation a friend sent into the running game.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct ReceivedInvite {
    pub friend: u64,
    pub target: protocol::InviteTarget,
    /// When the host last told of it, in seconds since the Unix epoch.
    pub received_at: u64,
}

/// A purchase the running game asks the player to confirm.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct MicroTxn {
    pub order_id: u64,
    pub app_id: u32,
}

/// The most invitations a session keeps; the oldest goes first.
pub const MAX_RECEIVED_INVITES: usize = 16;

/// What the running game asks of the player's Steam session, as its host
/// tells it. A record from before any of it has none.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct GameRequests {
    /// The latest overlay the game asked Steam for, invite dialogs included.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub overlay: Option<OverlayRequest>,
    /// The Steam lobby the game is in now, as the account's engine shows it.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub lobby: Option<u64>,
    /// Invitations friends sent into the game, newest first.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    pub invites: Vec<ReceivedInvite>,
    /// The purchase the game waits on the player to confirm.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub microtxn: Option<MicroTxn>,
}
impl GameRequests {
    /// The overlay's invite request, while it asks for an invite dialog.
    pub fn invite(&self) -> Option<InviteRequest> {
        self.overlay.as_ref().and_then(OverlayRequest::invite)
    }
}

/// What the native host tells of the game's Steam session. The requests
/// only hold while the host is online: a host that lost Steam, or the game,
/// is in no lobby anyone can join, and can answer nothing.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct HostUpdate {
    pub state: HostState,
    pub requests: GameRequests,
}
impl HostUpdate {
    pub fn new(state: HostState) -> Self {
        Self {
            state,
            requests: GameRequests::default(),
        }
    }
}

struct Inner {
    host: process::Child,
    proof: Proof,
    /// Its invitations are kept across a disconnection: Steam still holds
    /// them.
    requests: GameRequests,
    /// Overlay requests of the session so far, the last one's sequence.
    sequence: u64,
    stopped: bool,
}
impl Inner {
    fn update(&self) -> HostUpdate {
        let state = self.proof.host_state;
        if state != HostState::Online {
            return HostUpdate::new(state);
        }
        HostUpdate {
            state,
            requests: self.requests.clone(),
        }
    }
    /// Keeps `target` from `friend` first, once.
    fn received(&mut self, friend: u64, target: protocol::InviteTarget) {
        if !protocol::individual(friend) || !target.valid() {
            return;
        }
        let invites = &mut self.requests.invites;
        invites.retain(|invite| invite.friend != friend || invite.target != target);
        invites.insert(
            0,
            ReceivedInvite {
                friend,
                target,
                received_at: unix_now(),
            },
        );
        invites.truncate(MAX_RECEIVED_INVITES);
    }
}
pub struct Runtime {
    inner: Mutex<Inner>,
    wakeup: Arc<process::Wake>,
    service: String,
    prepared: files::Prepared,
}
impl Runtime {
    pub fn environment(&self) -> std::collections::HashMap<String, String> {
        self.prepared.consumer_environment(&self.service)
    }
    pub(crate) fn set_presence(&self, online: bool) -> Result<(), Error> {
        let mut inner = self.inner.lock().map_err(|_| Error::StartFailed)?;
        if inner.stopped {
            return Ok(());
        }
        Self::send(&mut inner, &protocol::HostCommand::SetPresence { online })
            .map_err(|_| Error::StartFailed)
    }
    fn send(inner: &mut Inner, command: &protocol::HostCommand) -> Result<(), Error> {
        command
            .write(inner.host.input.as_mut().ok_or(Error::Unavailable)?)
            .map_err(|_| Error::Unavailable)
    }
    /// Sends the player's `command` to the host while it serves the game
    /// online; `change` first checks it against what the host told and
    /// records its effect. An observer sees that effect at once.
    fn control(
        &self,
        command: &protocol::HostCommand,
        change: impl FnOnce(&mut Inner) -> Result<(), Error>,
    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
        if !command.valid() {
            return Err(Error::InvalidSession);
        }
        let mut inner = self.inner.lock().map_err(|_| Error::Unavailable)?;
        if inner.stopped || inner.proof.host_state != HostState::Online {
            return Err(Error::Unavailable);
        }
        change(&mut inner)?;
        let sent = Self::send(&mut inner, command);
        drop(inner);
        self.wakeup.notify();
        sent
    }
    /// Tells the game Obelisk's overlay opened or closed over it.
    pub fn overlay_state(&self, active: bool, user_initiated: bool) -> Result<(), Error> {
        self.control(
            &protocol::HostCommand::OverlayState {
                active,
                user_initiated,
            },
            |_| Ok(()),
        )
    }
    /// Hands the running game the invitation `friend` sent into it, which
    /// the player accepted, from the host or from Steam's chat alike.
    pub fn accept_invite(&self, friend: u64, target: protocol::InviteTarget) -> Result<(), Error> {
        let command = match &target {
            protocol::InviteTarget::Lobby { lobby_id } => {
                protocol::HostCommand::AcceptLobbyInvite {
                    lobby_id: *lobby_id,
                    friend,
                }
            }
            protocol::InviteTarget::Connect { connect } => {
                protocol::HostCommand::AcceptRichInvite {
                    friend,
                    connect: connect.clone(),
                }
            }
        };
        self.control(&command, |inner| {
            inner
                .requests
                .invites
                .retain(|invite| invite.friend != friend || invite.target != target);
            Ok(())
        })
    }
    /// The player's answer to the purchase the game waits on: only that one.
    pub fn authorize_microtxn(&self, order_id: u64, approve: bool) -> Result<(), Error> {
        self.control(
            &protocol::HostCommand::AuthorizeMicroTxn { order_id, approve },
            |inner| match &inner.requests.microtxn {
                Some(pending) if pending.order_id == order_id => {
                    inner.requests.microtxn = None;
                    Ok(())
                }
                _ => Err(Error::InvalidSession),
            },
        )
    }
    pub fn started(&self, pid: u32) -> Result<(), Error> {
        let mut inner = self.inner.lock().map_err(|_| Error::StartFailed)?;
        if inner.stopped {
            return Ok(());
        }
        // The game already exists. Record it even if its host has just died;
        // losing Steam must never turn into permission to terminate the game.
        Self::drain(&mut inner);
        inner.proof.game_pid = Some(pid);
        inner.proof.state = "game_started".into();
        files::report(&self.prepared.report, &inner.proof)
    }
    /// Wait on the private event pipe, independently of the UI, until the
    /// host's state, the game's invite request or its lobby differs from
    /// `previous`.
    /// `stopped` wakes this wait; Swift task cancellation must not abandon a
    /// live game.
    pub fn next_update(&self, previous: &HostUpdate) -> HostUpdate {
        loop {
            let generation = self.wakeup.generation();
            let Ok(mut inner) = self.inner.lock() else {
                return HostUpdate::new(HostState::Lost);
            };
            if inner.stopped {
                return HostUpdate::new(HostState::Stopped);
            }
            let before = (inner.proof.host_state, inner.proof.discovery_paths);
            // Sweep without blocking: `next` reports host death as an error, and
            // only returns `Ok(None)` once it has confirmed the host is alive.
            loop {
                match inner.host.next(Duration::ZERO) {
                    Ok(Some(event)) => Self::accept(&mut inner, event),
                    Ok(None) => break,
                    Err(_) => {
                        inner.proof.host_state = HostState::Lost;
                        break;
                    }
                }
            }
            if before != (inner.proof.host_state, inner.proof.discovery_paths) {
                let _ = files::report(&self.prepared.report, &inner.proof);
            }
            let update = inner.update();
            if update != *previous {
                return update;
            }
            // Never hold the runtime mutex while waiting for pipe input.
            drop(inner);
            self.wakeup.wait(generation);
        }
    }
    pub fn stopped(&self, exit: Option<i32>) {
        if let Ok(mut inner) = self.inner.lock() {
            if inner.stopped {
                return;
            }
            inner.stopped = true;
            Self::drain(&mut inner);
            inner.host.stop();
            inner.proof.game_exit = exit;
            inner.proof.state = if inner.proof.game_pid.is_some() {
                "game_exited"
            } else {
                "stopped"
            }
            .into();
            let _ = files::report(&self.prepared.report, &inner.proof);
            self.wakeup.notify();
        }
    }
    fn drain(inner: &mut Inner) {
        while let Some(event) = inner.host.try_event() {
            Self::accept(inner, event);
        }
    }
    fn accept(inner: &mut Inner, event: Event) {
        let app = inner.proof.app_id;
        match event {
            Event::Discovery { paths } => inner.proof.discovery_paths = paths,
            // Off Steam, the game's lobby, the dialog that named it and the
            // purchase it asked about are gone; a reconnected engine reports
            // its lobby again.
            Event::Disconnected {} if inner.proof.host_state != HostState::Lost => {
                inner.proof.host_state = HostState::Disconnected;
                inner.requests.overlay = None;
                inner.requests.lobby = None;
                inner.requests.microtxn = None;
            }
            Event::Reconnected {} if inner.proof.host_state != HostState::Lost => {
                inner.proof.host_state = HostState::Online;
            }
            // Only the game this host serves, and only what Steam accepts.
            Event::OverlayRequested { app_id, request } if app_id == app && request.valid() => {
                inner.sequence += 1;
                inner.requests.overlay = Some(OverlayRequest {
                    sequence: inner.sequence,
                    dialog: request,
                });
            }
            Event::GameLobby { app_id, lobby_id } if app_id == app => {
                inner.requests.lobby = lobby_id.filter(|lobby| protocol::lobby(*lobby));
            }
            Event::LobbyInviteReceived {
                inviter,
                lobby_id,
                app_id,
            } if app_id == app => {
                inner.received(inviter, protocol::InviteTarget::Lobby { lobby_id });
            }
            Event::RichInviteReceived {
                friend,
                app_id,
                connect,
            } if app_id == app => {
                inner.received(friend, protocol::InviteTarget::Connect { connect });
            }
            Event::MicroTxnRequested { order_id, app_id } if app_id == app && order_id != 0 => {
                inner.requests.microtxn = Some(MicroTxn { order_id, app_id });
            }
            Event::MicroTxnDismissed { order_id }
                if inner
                    .requests
                    .microtxn
                    .as_ref()
                    .is_some_and(|pending| pending.order_id == order_id) =>
            {
                inner.requests.microtxn = None;
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    fn write_report(&self) -> Result<(), Error> {
        files::report(
            &self.prepared.report,
            &self.inner.lock().map_err(|_| Error::StartFailed)?.proof,
        )
    }
}
impl Drop for Runtime {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.stopped(None);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod launch_tests;

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    fn launch() -> Launch {
        Launch::new(Credentials {
            steam_id: 1,
            account_name: "fixture".into(),
            refresh_token: "fixture-token".into(),
        })
    }
    pub(crate) fn child(script: &str) -> process::Child {
        let mut command = std::process::Command::new("/bin/sh");
        command.arg("-c").arg(script);
        process::Child::spawn(command).unwrap()
    }
    /// Parallel fixture processes may retain a dropped flock until exec. Bound
    /// the wait and unlock the probe before the caller reopens the lock file.
    pub(crate) fn wait_for_lock_release(path: &std::path::Path) {
        let lock = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()
            .read(true)
            .write(true)
            .open(path)
            .unwrap();
        if lock.try_lock().is_ok() {
            lock.unlock().unwrap();
            return;
        }
        let (send, receive) = std::sync::mpsc::sync_channel(1);
        std::thread::spawn(move || {
            let result = lock.lock().and_then(|()| lock.unlock());
            let _ = send.send(result);
        });
        receive
            .recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(2))
            .expect("dropped fixture lock remained held")
            .expect("probing the released fixture lock failed");
    }
    pub(crate) fn prepared(root: &std::path::Path) -> files::Prepared {
        files::Prepared {
            storage: None,
            directory: root.into(),
            run_directory: root.join("scratch"),
            profile: root.join("profile"),
            report: root.join("report.json"),
            endpoints: [
                ("Steam3Master".into(), "127.0.0.1:1".into()),
                ("SteamClientService".into(), "127.0.0.1:2".into()),
            ],
        }
    }
    pub(crate) fn runtime(script: &str, root: &std::path::Path) -> Runtime {
        let host = child(script);
        let wakeup = host.wakeup.clone();
        Runtime {
            inner: Mutex::new(Inner {
                proof: Proof {
                    app_id: 42,
                    host_pid: host.id(),
                    authenticated: true,
                    ticket_bytes: 178,
                    host_account_verified: true,
                    host_license_verified: true,
                    sdk_checked: false,
                    game_pid: None,
                    game_exit: None,
                    discovery_paths: 0,
                    host_state: HostState::Online,
                    state: "ready".into(),
                },
                host,
                requests: GameRequests::default(),
                sequence: 0,
                stopped: false,
            }),
            wakeup,
            service: "fixture".into(),
            prepared: prepared(root),
        }
    }
    fn signal(runtime: &Runtime) {
        use std::io::Write;
        runtime
            .inner
            .lock()
            .unwrap()
            .host
            .input
            .as_mut()
            .unwrap()
            .write_all(b"go\n")
            .unwrap();
    }
    fn state(state: HostState) -> HostUpdate {
        HostUpdate::new(state)
    }
    fn changed(runtime: &Arc<Runtime>, previous: HostState) -> HostState {
        updated(runtime, &state(previous)).state
    }
    fn updated(runtime: &Arc<Runtime>, previous: &HostUpdate) -> HostUpdate {
        let (send, receive) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();
        let observer = runtime.clone();
        let previous = previous.clone();
        let worker = std::thread::spawn(move || {
            let _ = send.send(observer.next_update(&previous));
        });
        let result = receive.recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(3));
        if result.is_err() {
            runtime.stopped(None);
        }
        worker.join().unwrap();
        result.expect("host state did not change")
    }
    #[test]
    fn session_distinguishes_connection_recovery_and_host_loss_until_game_exit() {
        let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let runtime = Arc::new(runtime(
            r#"read line; printf '%s\n' '{"event":"disconnected"}'; read line; printf '%s\n' '{"event":"reconnected"}'; read line; exit 0"#,
            root.path(),
        ));
        runtime.started(1234).unwrap();
        signal(&runtime);
        assert_eq!(
            changed(&runtime, HostState::Online),
            HostState::Disconnected
        );
        signal(&runtime);
        assert_eq!(
            changed(&runtime, HostState::Disconnected),
            HostState::Online
        );
        signal(&runtime);
        assert_eq!(changed(&runtime, HostState::Online), HostState::Lost);
        {
            let inner = runtime.inner.lock().unwrap();
            assert!(!inner.stopped);
            assert_eq!(inner.proof.game_pid, Some(1234));
            assert_eq!(inner.proof.state, "game_started");
        }
        runtime.stopped(Some(0));
        assert_eq!(
            runtime.next_update(&state(HostState::Lost)).state,
            HostState::Stopped
        );
        let proof: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_slice(&std::fs::read(root.path().join("report.json")).unwrap())
                .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(proof["state"], "game_exited");
        assert_eq!(proof["host_state"], "lost");
        assert_eq!(proof["game_exit"], 0);
    }
    #[test]
    fn overlay_requests_of_the_game_wake_the_observer_with_a_new_sequence() {
        let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let lobby = r#"'{"event":"overlay_requested","app_id":42,"request":{"lobby_invite":{"lobby_id":109775244421126053}}}'"#;
        let script = [
            // Another game's request and an individual account as a lobby
            // are ignored; the same lobby asked twice is two requests.
            r#"read line; printf '%s\n' '{"event":"overlay_requested","app_id":7,"request":{"lobby_invite":{"lobby_id":109775244421126053}}}' '{"event":"overlay_requested","app_id":42,"request":{"lobby_invite":{"lobby_id":76561197960265729}}}' LOBBY"#,
            "read line; printf '%s\\n' LOBBY",
            r#"read line; printf '%s\n' '{"event":"overlay_requested","app_id":42,"request":{"connect_invite":{"connect":"+connect 10.0.0.1"}}}'"#,
            r#"read line; printf '%s\n' '{"event":"overlay_requested","app_id":42,"request":{"web_page":{"url":"file:///etc/passwd","modal":false}}}' '{"event":"overlay_requested","app_id":42,"request":{"store":{"app_id":42,"flag":1}}}'"#,
            r#"read line; printf '%s\n' '{"event":"disconnected"}'"#,
            r#"read line; printf '%s\n' '{"event":"reconnected"}'"#,
            "read line; printf '%s\\n' LOBBY",
            "read line",
        ]
        .join("; ")
        .replace("LOBBY", lobby);
        let runtime = Arc::new(runtime(&script, root.path()));
        runtime.started(1234).unwrap();
        let request = |sequence, dialog: &protocol::OverlayDialog| OverlayRequest {
            sequence,
            dialog: dialog.clone(),
        };
        let invite = |sequence, target: &protocol::InviteTarget| InviteRequest {
            sequence,
            target: target.clone(),
        };
        let dialog = protocol::OverlayDialog::LobbyInvite {
            lobby_id: 109_775_244_421_126_053,
        };
        let target = protocol::InviteTarget::Lobby {
            lobby_id: 109_775_244_421_126_053,
        };
        signal(&runtime);
        let first = updated(&runtime, &state(HostState::Online));
        assert_eq!(first.state, HostState::Online);
        assert_eq!(first.requests.overlay, Some(request(1, &dialog)));
        assert_eq!(first.requests.invite(), Some(invite(1, &target)));
        signal(&runtime);
        let second = updated(&runtime, &first);
        assert_eq!(second.requests.invite(), Some(invite(2, &target)));
        signal(&runtime);
        let third = updated(&runtime, &second);
        let connect = protocol::InviteTarget::Connect {
            connect: "+connect 10.0.0.1".into(),
        };
        assert_eq!(third.requests.invite(), Some(invite(3, &connect)));
        signal(&runtime);
        let store = updated(&runtime, &third);
        assert_eq!(
            store.requests.overlay,
            Some(request(
                4,
                &protocol::OverlayDialog::Store {
                    app_id: 42,
                    flag: 1
                }
            )),
            "a file URL is no web page"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            store.requests.invite(),
            None,
            "the store is no invite dialog"
        );
        signal(&runtime);
        let disconnected = updated(&runtime, &store);
        assert_eq!(
            disconnected,
            state(HostState::Disconnected),
            "off Steam, the dialog's target is gone"
        );
        signal(&runtime);
        let reconnected = updated(&runtime, &disconnected);
        assert_eq!(reconnected, state(HostState::Online), "and it stays gone");
        signal(&runtime);
        let again = updated(&runtime, &reconnected);
        assert_eq!(
            again.requests.invite(),
            Some(invite(5, &target)),
            "the session's sequence keeps growing"
        );
        runtime.stopped(Some(0));
        assert_eq!(
            runtime.next_update(&again),
            state(HostState::Stopped),
            "nothing outlives the game"
        );
    }
    const FRIEND: u64 = 76_561_197_960_265_729;
    const OTHER: u64 = 76_561_197_960_265_730;
    const LOBBY: u64 = 109_775_244_421_126_053;
    /// A host that tells `events`, one batch per signal, then records every
    /// command it gets into `input`.
    fn recording(root: &std::path::Path, events: &[&str]) -> Arc<Runtime> {
        let mut script: Vec<String> = events
            .iter()
            .map(|batch| format!("read line; printf '%s\\n' {batch}"))
            .collect();
        script.push(format!("cat > '{}'", root.join("input").display()));
        let runtime = Arc::new(runtime(&script.join("; "), root));
        runtime.started(1234).unwrap();
        runtime
    }
    fn commands(root: &std::path::Path) -> Vec<protocol::HostCommand> {
        let wire = std::fs::read(root.join("input")).unwrap();
        let mut input = wire.as_slice();
        let mut commands = Vec::new();
        while let Some(command) = protocol::HostCommand::read(&mut input).unwrap() {
            commands.push(command);
        }
        commands
    }
    /// The first update after `previous` that is `done`: a batch of events
    /// may wake the observer more than once.
    fn until(
        runtime: &Arc<Runtime>,
        previous: &HostUpdate,
        done: impl Fn(&HostUpdate) -> bool,
    ) -> HostUpdate {
        let mut update = updated(runtime, previous);
        while !done(&update) {
            update = updated(runtime, &update);
        }
        update
    }
    fn received(friend: u64, target: protocol::InviteTarget) -> (u64, protocol::InviteTarget) {
        (friend, target)
    }
    fn invites(update: &HostUpdate) -> Vec<(u64, protocol::InviteTarget)> {
        update
            .requests
            .invites
            .iter()
            .map(|invite| received(invite.friend, invite.target.clone()))
            .collect()
    }
    #[test]
    fn received_invites_of_the_game_come_newest_first_once_each() {
        let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let lobby = format!(
            r#"'{{"event":"lobby_invite_received","inviter":{FRIEND},"lobby_id":{LOBBY},"app_id":42}}'"#
        );
        let rich = format!(
            r#"'{{"event":"rich_invite_received","friend":{OTHER},"app_id":42,"connect":"+connect 10.0.0.1"}}'"#
        );
        let ignored = [
            format!(r#"'{{"event":"lobby_invite_received","inviter":{FRIEND},"lobby_id":{LOBBY},"app_id":7}}'"#),
            format!(r#"'{{"event":"lobby_invite_received","inviter":{LOBBY},"lobby_id":{LOBBY},"app_id":42}}'"#),
            format!(r#"'{{"event":"lobby_invite_received","inviter":{FRIEND},"lobby_id":{FRIEND},"app_id":42}}'"#),
            format!(r#"'{{"event":"rich_invite_received","friend":{OTHER},"app_id":42,"connect":""}}'"#),
        ]
        .join(" ");
        let many: String = (1..=20)
            .map(|account| {
                format!(
                    r#"'{{"event":"rich_invite_received","friend":{},"app_id":42,"connect":"+connect 10.0.0.{account}"}}'"#,
                    FRIEND + account
                )
            })
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join(" ");
        let batches = [
            format!("{lobby} {ignored} {rich}"),
            lobby.clone(),
            r#"'{"event":"disconnected"}'"#.to_owned(),
            r#"'{"event":"reconnected"}'"#.to_owned(),
            many,
        ];
        let runtime = recording(
            root.path(),
            &batches.iter().map(String::as_str).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        );
        let lobby = || received(FRIEND, protocol::InviteTarget::Lobby { lobby_id: LOBBY });
        let rich = || {
            received(
                OTHER,
                protocol::InviteTarget::Connect {
                    connect: "+connect 10.0.0.1".into(),
                },
            )
        };
        signal(&runtime);
        let first = until(&runtime, &state(HostState::Online), |update| {
            update.requests.invites.len() == 2
        });
        assert_eq!(invites(&first), [rich(), lobby()]);
        signal(&runtime);
        let second = updated(&runtime, &first);
        assert_eq!(invites(&second), [lobby(), rich()], "again, first and once");
        signal(&runtime);
        let away = updated(&runtime, &second);
        assert_eq!(
            away,
            state(HostState::Disconnected),
            "off Steam, none shows"
        );
        signal(&runtime);
        let back = updated(&runtime, &away);
        assert_eq!(invites(&back), [lobby(), rich()], "Steam still holds them");
        signal(&runtime);
        let many = until(&runtime, &back, |update| {
            update.requests.invites.first().map(|invite| invite.friend) == Some(FRIEND + 20)
        });
        assert_eq!(many.requests.invites.len(), MAX_RECEIVED_INVITES);
        assert_eq!(many.requests.invites[0].friend, FRIEND + 20);
        assert_eq!(
            many.requests.invites[15].friend,
            FRIEND + 5,
            "the oldest go"
        );
        // Accepting one hands it to the game and takes it off the list.
        runtime
            .accept_invite(
                FRIEND + 20,
                protocol::InviteTarget::Connect {
                    connect: "+connect 10.0.0.20".into(),
                },
            )
            .unwrap();
        let accepted = updated(&runtime, &many);
        assert_eq!(accepted.requests.invites.len(), MAX_RECEIVED_INVITES - 1);
        assert_eq!(accepted.requests.invites[0].friend, FRIEND + 19);
        // An invitation from Steam's chat, never told by the host.
        runtime
            .accept_invite(FRIEND, protocol::InviteTarget::Lobby { lobby_id: LOBBY })
            .unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            runtime.accept_invite(LOBBY, protocol::InviteTarget::Lobby { lobby_id: LOBBY }),
            Err(Error::InvalidSession)
        ));
        runtime.stopped(Some(0));
        assert_eq!(runtime.next_update(&accepted), state(HostState::Stopped));
        assert_eq!(
            commands(root.path()),
            [
                protocol::HostCommand::AcceptRichInvite {
                    friend: FRIEND + 20,
                    connect: "+connect 10.0.0.20".into(),
                },
                protocol::HostCommand::AcceptLobbyInvite {
                    lobby_id: LOBBY,
                    friend: FRIEND,
                },
            ]
        );
        assert!(matches!(
            runtime.overlay_state(true, true),
            Err(Error::Unavailable)
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn cancellation_interrupts_waiting_for_a_live_helper() {
        let launch = Arc::new(launch());
        let mut host = child("read line");
        let cancel = launch.clone();
        let cancellation = std::thread::spawn(move || {
            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
            cancel.cancel();
        });
        let started = Instant::now();
        assert!(matches!(
            launch.wait_for_host(&mut host, 1030300, &mut Vec::new()),
            Err(Error::Cancelled)
        ));
        host.stop();
        cancellation.join().unwrap();
        assert!(!host.alive().unwrap());
        assert!(started.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(2));
    }
```

```rs
//! Every path Obelisk uses, named once.
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

/// Where Obelisk keeps everything, derived from its library directory, its
/// application bundle and the user's home.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Locations {
    pub library: PathBuf,
    pub home: PathBuf,
    /// The Cloud archive every storefront shares. The folder keeps its first
    /// name so existing save versions and running Game sessions stay valid.
    pub cloud_archive: PathBuf,
    pub steam_sessions: PathBuf,
    pub epic_sessions: PathBuf,
    pub gog_sessions: PathBuf,
    /// The bundled native host every supervisor runs as.
    pub helper: PathBuf,
    pub helpers: PathBuf,
    /// Valve's Steam components the Steam host loads, which a Steam game's
    /// download, or a launch that misses them, gets from Valve's CDN.
    pub steam_runtime_package: PathBuf,
    pub steam_runtime_cache: PathBuf,
    /// The Voile runtimes that run Windows games: the pinned release and a
    /// development runtime.
    pub voile: PathBuf,
    /// One Wine prefix per Windows installation, named after its folder.
    pub wine_prefixes: PathBuf,
}

impl Locations {
    pub fn new(library: &Path, bundle: &Path, home: &Path) -> Self {
        let helpers = bundle.join("Contents/Helpers/SteamNative");
        let steam_runtime_cache = home.join("Library/Caches/com.zagrios.obelisk/SteamRuntime");
        Self {
            cloud_archive: library.join("SteamCloud"),
            steam_sessions: library.join("SteamSessions"),
            epic_sessions: library.join("EpicSessions"),
            gog_sessions: library.join("GOGSessions"),
            helper: helpers.join(crate::package::HOST),
            helpers,
            steam_runtime_package: crate::valve::payload(&steam_runtime_cache),
            steam_runtime_cache,
            voile: library.join("Voile"),
            wine_prefixes: library.join("Prefixes"),
            library: library.to_owned(),
            home: home.to_owned(),
        }
    }
}
```

`crates/game-runtime/src/metal_hud.rs`:

```rs
//! The frames a game presented, as Metal's Performance HUD reports them. Every
//! game starts with the HUD on, invisible unless its player shows it; once per
//! second Metal then writes a `metal-HUD:` line to the presenting process's
//! standard error, which the game's log keeps. Read once the game has exited,
//! those lines give its frame rate whatever runs it: Rosetta's Wine, the Linux
//! engine's wsd or a native build.
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::{
    collections::HashMap,
    fs::File,
    io::{self, BufRead, BufReader},
    path::Path,
};

/// Turns the HUD on.
pub(crate) const ENABLED: &str = "MTL_HUD_ENABLED";
/// Has Metal write the HUD's `metal-HUD:` lines.
pub(crate) const LOG_ENABLED: &str = "MTL_HUD_LOG_ENABLED";
/// How visible the HUD is over the game.
pub(crate) const OPACITY: &str = "MTL_HUD_OPACITY";
/// Leaves the HUD's menu out.
pub(crate) const DISABLE_MENU_BAR: &str = "MTL_HUD_DISABLE_MENU_BAR";

/// What turns the HUD on for a process, without its menu: over the game when
/// `shown`, else invisible.
pub(crate) fn environment(shown: bool) -> [(&'static str, &'static str); 4] {
    [
        (ENABLED, "1"),
        (LOG_ENABLED, "1"),
        (OPACITY, if shown { "1" } else { "0" }),
        (DISABLE_MENU_BAR, "1"),
    ]
}

const MARKER: &[u8] = b"metal-HUD: ";
/// A frame shown this long after the previous one is a hitch the player sees.
const HITCH_MS: f32 = 100.0;
/// Rates above this, such as an uncapped menu's, are reported as this.
const MAX_FPS: f64 = 1000.0;

/// The frames of the process that presented the most of them.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Frames {
    pub count: u64,
    /// The median present interval, in microseconds.
    pub median_us: Option<u32>,
    /// The 99th percentile present interval, in microseconds: the slowest
    /// 1 % of frames took at least this long.
    pub slowest_percent_us: Option<u32>,
    /// Frames shown more than 100 ms after the previous one.
    pub hitches: u64,
}
impl Frames {
    /// Frames per second at the median interval, to a tenth.
    pub fn median_fps(&self) -> Option<f64> {
        self.median_us.map(rate)
    }
    /// Frames per second the slowest 1 % of frames stay under, to a tenth.
    pub fn low_1pct_fps(&self) -> Option<f64> {
        self.slowest_percent_us.map(rate)
    }
}

/// The frames `log` reports. A log that cannot be read reports none.
pub fn read(log: &Path) -> Frames {
    File::open(log)
        .and_then(|file| parse(BufReader::new(file)))
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

/// `text` without the lines Metal writes the frames in: a bug report
/// carries the game's messages, not a line per second of frame times.
pub fn without_frame_lines(text: &str) -> String {
    // Reports have always dropped the marker without its trailing space too.
    let marker = MARKER.trim_ascii_end();
    text.split('\n')
        .filter(|line| !line.as_bytes().windows(marker.len()).any(|w| w == marker))
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join("\n")
}

fn parse(log: impl BufRead) -> io::Result<Frames> {
    // Present intervals in ms, per process: a game's launcher may present too.
    let mut intervals: HashMap<u32, Vec<f32>> = HashMap::new();
    for line in log.split(b'\n') {
        let line = line?;
        let Some(at) = line.windows(MARKER.len()).position(|w| w == MARKER) else {
            continue;
        };
        let values = String::from_utf8_lossy(&line[at + MARKER.len()..]);
        // <first frame>,<GPU MB>,<process MB>, then <interval>,<GPU time> per frame.
        let process = intervals.entry(pid(&line[..at])).or_default();
        process.extend(
            values
                .trim_end()
                .split(',')
                .skip(3)
                .step_by(2)
                .filter_map(|value| value.parse::<f32>().ok())
                .filter(|interval| interval.is_finite() && *interval > 0.0),
        );
    }
    let mut intervals = intervals
        .into_values()
        .max_by_key(Vec::len)
        .unwrap_or_default();
    Ok(frames(&mut intervals))
}

/// The process ID in the `name[pid:thread]` that precedes the marker; 0 when
/// the line has none.
fn pid(prefix: &[u8]) -> u32 {
    let prefix = String::from_utf8_lossy(prefix);
    prefix
        .rfind('[')
        .and_then(|open| prefix[open + 1..].split(':').next()?.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(0)
}

fn frames(intervals: &mut [f32]) -> Frames {
    if intervals.is_empty() {
        return Frames::default();
    }
    intervals.sort_by(f32::total_cmp);
    let count = intervals.len();
    let middle = count / 2;
    let median = if count.is_multiple_of(2) {
        (intervals[middle - 1] + intervals[middle]) / 2.0
    } else {
        intervals[middle]
    };
    // Nearest rank: the smallest interval at least 99 % of frames don't exceed.
    let p99 = intervals[(count * 99).div_ceil(100) - 1];
    Frames {
        count: count as u64,
        median_us: Some(microseconds(median)),
        slowest_percent_us: Some(microseconds(p99)),
        hitches: intervals.iter().filter(|&&i| i > HITCH_MS).count() as u64,
    }
}

fn microseconds(interval_ms: f32) -> u32 {
    (f64::from(interval_ms) * 1000.0).round() as u32
}

/// Frames per second for a present interval, to a tenth.
fn rate(interval_us: u32) -> f64 {
    ((1_000_000.0 / f64::from(interval_us.max(1))).min(MAX_FPS) * 10.0).round() / 10.0
}

mod tests;
```

```rs
use super::*;

fn line(process: &str, pid: u32, first: u64, intervals: &[f32]) -> String {
    let frames: Vec<String> = intervals.iter().map(|i| format!("{i:.2},0.02")).collect();
    format!(
        "2026-10-14 09:04:41.290 {process}[{pid}:38256263] metal-HUD: {first},3.08,277.88,{}\n",
        frames.join(",")
    )
}

fn parsed(log: &str) -> Frames {
    parse(log.as_bytes()).unwrap()
}

#[test]
fn a_real_capture_reads_as_60_fps() {
    // Six seconds of a Metal test app presenting at 60 fps on a 120 Hz screen.
    let frames = parsed(include_str!("probe-60fps.log"));
    assert_eq!(frames.count, 363);
    assert_eq!(frames.median_us, Some(16_670));
    assert_eq!(frames.median_fps(), Some(60.0));
    assert_eq!(frames.low_1pct_fps(), Some(40.0));
    assert_eq!(frames.hitches, 0);
}

#[test]
fn the_process_with_the_most_frames_is_the_game() {
    let log = [
        line("Launcher.exe", 11, 1, &[16.67; 30]),
        "wine: some diagnostic\n".to_owned(),
        line("Game.exe", 12, 1, &[8.33; 120]),
        line("Game.exe", 12, 121, &[8.33; 120]),
    ]
    .concat();
    let frames = parsed(&log);
    assert_eq!(frames.count, 240);
    assert_eq!(frames.median_fps(), Some(120.0));
}

#[test]
fn the_slowest_percent_and_hitches_come_from_the_long_intervals() {
    let mut intervals = vec![10.0; 98];
    intervals.extend([50.0, 250.0]);
    let frames = parsed(&line("Game", 7, 1, &intervals));
    assert_eq!(frames.median_fps(), Some(100.0));
    assert_eq!(frames.low_1pct_fps(), Some(20.0));
    assert_eq!(frames.hitches, 1);
}

#[test]
fn an_uncapped_menu_reports_at_most_1000_fps() {
    let frames = parsed(&line("Game", 7, 1, &[0.25; 10]));
    assert_eq!(frames.median_fps(), Some(MAX_FPS));
    assert_eq!(frames.low_1pct_fps(), Some(MAX_FPS));
}

#[test]
fn a_log_without_hud_lines_reports_no_frames() {
    assert_eq!(Frames::default().median_fps(), None);
    assert_eq!(
        parsed("wine: starting\nerr:module:import_dll\n"),
        Frames::default()
    );
    assert_eq!(parsed(""), Frames::default());
    assert_eq!(read(Path::new("/nonexistent/game.log")), Frames::default());
}

#[test]
fn malformed_values_and_invalid_utf8_are_skipped() {
    let mut log = line("Game", 7, 1, &[16.67; 4]).into_bytes();
    log.extend(b"\xff\xfe Game[7:1] metal-HUD: 5,1,1,abc,0.02,-3,0.02,16.67\n");
    let frames = parse(log.as_slice()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(frames.count, 5);
}

#[test]
fn a_line_without_a_process_counts_as_process_zero() {
    assert_eq!(pid(b"metal"), 0);
    assert_eq!(pid(b"2026-10-14 09:04:41.290 Game[38516:38256263] "), 38516);
    assert_eq!(pid(b"Df probe[38314:2479811] (libMTLHud.dylib) "), 38314);
}

#[test]
fn the_hud_shows_over_the_game_only_when_asked() {
    let opacity = |shown| {
        environment(shown)
            .into_iter()
            .find(|(name, _)| *name == "MTL_HUD_OPACITY")
            .map(|(_, value)| value)
    };
    assert_eq!(opacity(false), Some("0"));
    assert_eq!(opacity(true), Some("1"));
    assert!(environment(true).contains(&("MTL_HUD_LOG_ENABLED", "1")));
}

#[test]
fn a_report_drops_every_line_the_frames_come_from() {
    let probe = include_str!("probe-60fps.log");

    assert_eq!(
        without_frame_lines("a\n\nmetal-HUD:x\nb\r\nmetal-HUD: 1\n"),
        "a\n\nb\r\n"
    );
}
```

`crates/game-runtime/src/native.rs`:

```rs
//! A native game's executable inside its installation, and the environment
//! every game starts with, whatever its storefront.
use crate::{
    Error,
    supervisor::{Target, architecture::Architecture},
};
use obelisk_core::launch::LaunchTarget;
use std::{
    collections::HashMap,
    os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt,
    path::{Path, PathBuf},
    process::Command,
};

/// The executable `target` names inside `root`: an application bundle's
/// declared executable, or the file itself. It must be a Mach-O Obelisk can run.
/// Installers may drop its execute permission; only then is it repaired.
pub fn executable(root: &Path, target: &LaunchTarget) -> Result<(PathBuf, Architecture), Error> {
    let root = root.canonicalize()?;
    let named = Path::new(&target.executable)
        .canonicalize()
        .map_err(|_| Error::NotExecutable)?;
    let executable = if target.is_application_bundle {
        bundle_executable(&named)?
    } else {
        named
    };
    if !executable.starts_with(&root) || !executable.is_file() {
        return Err(Error::NotExecutable);
    }
    let architecture = Architecture::preferred(&executable)?;
    let mode = std::fs::metadata(&executable)?.permissions().mode();
    if mode & 0o100 == 0 {
        std::fs::set_permissions(&executable, std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(mode | 0o100))?;
    }
    Ok((executable, architecture))
}

/// The executable an application bundle declares, which must stay inside it.
fn bundle_executable(bundle: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, Error> {
    let output = Command::new("/usr/bin/plutil")
        .args(["-extract", "CFBundleExecutable", "raw", "-o", "-"])
        .arg(bundle.join("Contents/Info.plist"))
        .env_clear()
        .output()?;
    let name = std::str::from_utf8(&output.stdout)
        .map_err(|_| Error::InvalidApplication)?
        .trim();
    if !output.status.success()
        || name.is_empty()
        || name.len() > 255
        || name.contains('/')
        || name == "."
        || name == ".."
    {
        return Err(Error::InvalidApplication);
    }
    let executable = bundle
        .join("Contents/MacOS")
        .join(name)
        .canonicalize()
        .map_err(|_| Error::InvalidApplication)?;
    if !executable.starts_with(bundle) {
        return Err(Error::InvalidApplication);
    }
    Ok(executable)
}

/// The Mac game `launched` names inside `install`, started with `arguments`
/// and `environment`, and the architecture it runs as. Its standard error
/// goes to `log`.
pub fn target(
    install: &Path,
    launched: &LaunchTarget,
    arguments: Vec<String>,
    environment: HashMap<String, String>,
    log: PathBuf,
) -> Result<(Target, Architecture), Error> {
    let (executable, architecture) = executable(install, launched)?;
    Ok((
        Target {
            executable,
            arguments,
            working_directory: launched.working_directory.clone().into(),
            environment,
            log: Some(log),
            installation: Some(install.to_owned()),
            program: None,
        },
        architecture,
    ))
}

/// The environment every game starts with: the player's home, account and
/// language, and nothing else of Obelisk's. A supervisor starts without any
/// environment, so Obelisk builds this before handing the game over.
pub fn environment(home: &Path) -> HashMap<String, String> {
    environment_from(home, |key| std::env::var(key).ok())
}

fn environment_from(home: &Path, read: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<String>) -> HashMap<String, String> {
    let mut environment = HashMap::from([
        ("HOME".to_owned(), home.to_string_lossy().into_owned()),
        (
            "PATH".to_owned(),
            "/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin".to_owned(),
        ),
        (
            "TMPDIR".to_owned(),
            read("TMPDIR").unwrap_or_else(|| std::env::temp_dir().to_string_lossy().into_owned()),
        ),
    ]);
    if let Some(user) = read("USER").or_else(|| read("LOGNAME")) {
        environment.insert("USER".into(), user.clone());
        environment.insert("LOGNAME".into(), user);
    }
    for key in ["LANG", "LC_ALL", "LC_CTYPE"] {
        if let Some(value) = read(key).filter(|value| !value.is_empty()) {
            environment.insert(key.into(), value);
        }
    }
    // Without any language, many games misread their own text files.
    if !["LANG", "LC_ALL", "LC_CTYPE"]
        .iter()
        .any(|key| environment.contains_key(*key))
    {
        environment.insert("LANG".into(), "en_US.UTF-8".into());
    }
    environment
}
```

```rs
use super::*;
use crate::supervisor::architecture::tests::{ARM64, thin};
use std::fs;

fn target(executable: &Path, bundle: bool) -> LaunchTarget {
    LaunchTarget {
        executable: executable.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
        arguments: vec![],
        working_directory: String::new(),
        is_application_bundle: bundle,
    }
}

fn installation() -> (tempfile::TempDir, PathBuf) {
    let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let root = directory.path().canonicalize().unwrap();
    (directory, root)
}

fn mode(path: &Path) -> u32 {
    fs::metadata(path).unwrap().permissions().mode() & 0o777
}

fn application(root: &Path, declared: &str) -> PathBuf {
    let bundle = root.join("Game.app");
    fs::create_dir_all(bundle.join("Contents/MacOS")).unwrap();
    fs::create_dir_all(bundle.join("Contents/Resources")).unwrap();
    fs::write(
        bundle.join("Contents/Info.plist"),
        format!(
            r#"<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0"><dict><key>CFBundleExecutable</key><string>{declared}</string></dict></plist>"#
        ),
    )
    .unwrap();
    bundle
}

#[test]
fn a_standalone_macho_gets_only_its_owner_execute_permission_back() {
    let (_directory, root) = installation();
    let game = root.join("game");
    fs::write(&game, thin(ARM64, true)).unwrap();
    fs::set_permissions(&game, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o640)).unwrap();

    let (executable, architecture) = executable(&root, &target(&game, false)).unwrap();

    assert_eq!(executable, game);
    assert_eq!(architecture, Architecture::Arm64);
    assert_eq!(mode(&game), 0o740);
}

#[test]
fn a_file_that_is_not_a_macho_is_never_made_executable() {
    let (_directory, root) = installation();
    let script = root.join("game.sh");
    fs::write(&script, b"#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n").unwrap();
    fs::set_permissions(&script, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o644)).unwrap();

    assert!(executable(&root, &target(&script, false)).is_err());
    assert_eq!(mode(&script), 0o644);
}

#[test]
fn a_bundle_launches_its_declared_executable_without_touching_resources() {
    let (_directory, root) = installation();
    let bundle = application(&root, "Game");
    let binary = bundle.join("Contents/MacOS/Game");
    let resource = bundle.join("Contents/Resources/data.bin");
    fs::write(&binary, thin(ARM64, true)).unwrap();
    fs::write(&resource, thin(ARM64, true)).unwrap();
    fs::set_permissions(&binary, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o644)).unwrap();
    fs::set_permissions(&resource, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o644)).unwrap();

    let (executable, _) = executable(&root, &target(&bundle, true)).unwrap();

    assert_eq!(executable, binary);
    assert_eq!(mode(&binary), 0o744);
    assert_eq!(mode(&resource), 0o644);
}

#[test]
fn a_bundle_cannot_declare_an_executable_outside_itself_or_missing() {
    let (_directory, root) = installation();
    for declared in ["", "../../outside", "Missing"] {
        let bundle = application(&root, declared);
        assert!(
            matches!(
                executable(&root, &target(&bundle, true)),
                Err(Error::InvalidApplication)
            ),
            "{declared:?}"
        );
        fs::remove_dir_all(&bundle).unwrap();
    }
}

#[test]
fn nothing_outside_the_installation_is_a_target() {
    let (_directory, root) = installation();
    let outside = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let game = outside.path().join("game");
    fs::write(&game, thin(ARM64, true)).unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(
        executable(&root, &target(&game, false)),
        Err(Error::NotExecutable)
    ));
    let link = root.join("game");
    std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&game, &link).unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(
        executable(&root, &target(&link, false)),
        Err(Error::NotExecutable)
    ));
}

#[test]
fn a_game_inherits_the_players_language_and_account_only() {
    let obelisk = HashMap::from([
        ("USER", "player"),
        ("LANG", "fr_FR.UTF-8"),
        ("LC_ALL", ""),
        ("TMPDIR", "/private/var/folders/obelisk/T/"),
        ("DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES", "/tmp/inject.dylib"),
        ("OBELISK_LIBRARY_DIRECTORY", "/tmp/library"),
    ]);
    let environment = environment_from(Path::new("/Users/player"), |key| {
        obelisk.get(key).map(|value| (*value).to_owned())
    });
    assert_eq!(
        environment,
        HashMap::from([
            ("HOME".into(), "/Users/player".into()),
            ("PATH".into(), "/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin".into()),
            ("TMPDIR".into(), "/private/var/folders/obelisk/T/".into()),
            ("USER".into(), "player".into()),
            ("LOGNAME".into(), "player".into()),
            ("LANG".into(), "fr_FR.UTF-8".into()),
        ])
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_game_without_any_language_gets_utf8_english() {
    let environment = environment_from(Path::new("/Users/player"), |_| None);
    assert_eq!(
        environment.get("LANG").map(String::as_str),
        Some("en_US.UTF-8")
    );
    assert!(!environment.contains_key("USER"));
}
```

`crates/game-runtime/src/package.rs`:

```rs
//! Hash-pinned Valve payload. Runtime preparation is local-only: it reads the
//! payload `crate::valve` downloaded from Valve's CDN, with a Steam game's
//! Transfer or, when it is still missing, its launch.
use crate::{Config, Error};
use serde::Deserialize;
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
use std::{
    collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet},
    fs::{self, File},
    io::{Read, Write},
    path::{Path, PathBuf},
    sync::{
        OnceLock,
        atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering},
    },
};

const MANIFEST: &str = include_str!("../runtime-manifest.json");
pub const HOST: &str = "obelisk-steam-host";
pub(crate) const ADAPTER: &str = "libobelisk_steam_discovery_adapter.dylib";
pub(crate) const SDK_INTEL: &str = "obelisk-steam-sdk-x86_64";
pub(crate) const HELPERS: [&str; 3] = [HOST, ADAPTER, SDK_INTEL];
/// What Steam launches leave in the runtime cache: the generations `prepare`
/// extracts, their unfinished staging, and each launch's own folder.
const GENERATION: &str = "runtime-v1-";
const STAGING: &str = ".staging-";
pub(crate) const LAUNCH: &str = "launch-";

fn executable_helper(name: &str) -> bool {
    matches!(name, HOST | SDK_INTEL)
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub struct Manifest {
    pub version: String,
    pub packages: Vec<SourcePackage>,
    pub files: Vec<PayloadFile>,
}
#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub struct SourcePackage {
    pub name: String,
    pub url: String,
    pub size: u64,
    pub sha256: String,
}
#[derive(Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct PayloadFile {
    pub path: String,
    pub package: String,
    pub size: u64,
    pub sha256: String,
}
pub fn manifest() -> &'static Manifest {
    static VALUE: OnceLock<Manifest> = OnceLock::new();
    VALUE.get_or_init(|| serde_json::from_str(MANIFEST).expect("checked-in runtime manifest"))
}
pub fn entry(path: &str) -> &'static PayloadFile {
    manifest()
        .files
        .iter()
        .find(|file| file.path == path)
        .expect("checked-in runtime manifest")
}
pub(crate) fn check(cancelled: &AtomicBool) -> Result<(), Error> {
    if cancelled.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
        Err(Error::Cancelled)
    } else {
        Ok(())
    }
}
fn regular(path: &Path) -> Result<fs::Metadata, Error> {
    let metadata = fs::symlink_metadata(path).map_err(|_| Error::Unavailable)?;
    if !metadata.file_type().is_file() {
        return Err(Error::VersionMismatch);
    }
    Ok(metadata)
}
fn is_directory(path: &Path) -> Result<(), Error> {
    if fs::symlink_metadata(path)?.file_type().is_dir() {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(Error::VersionMismatch)
    }
}
fn verify_file(root: &Path, entry: &PayloadFile, cancelled: &AtomicBool) -> Result<(), Error> {
    check(cancelled)?;
    let path = root.join(&entry.path);
    let metadata = regular(&path)?;
    if metadata.len() != entry.size || crate::sha(&path)? != entry.sha256 {
        return Err(Error::VersionMismatch);
    }
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
        if executable_helper(&entry.path) && metadata.permissions().mode() & 0o100 == 0 {
            return Err(Error::VersionMismatch);
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}
fn verify_tree(root: &Path, entries: &[PayloadFile], cancelled: &AtomicBool) -> Result<(), Error> {
    is_directory(root)?;
    let mut files = BTreeMap::new();
    let mut directories = BTreeSet::new();
    for entry in entries {
        let path = Path::new(&entry.path);
        if path.as_os_str().is_empty()
            || path
                .components()
                .any(|c| !matches!(c, std::path::Component::Normal(_)))
            || files.insert(path.to_path_buf(), entry).is_some()
        {
            return Err(Error::VersionMismatch);
        }
        let mut parent = path.parent();
        while let Some(path) = parent.filter(|p| !p.as_os_str().is_empty()) {
            directories.insert(path.to_path_buf());
            parent = path.parent();
        }
    }
    // Validate each ancestor before descending, and each regular file before
    // hashing. No unvalidated path is opened, including symlinked parents.
    let mut pending = vec![root.to_path_buf()];
    while let Some(directory) = pending.pop() {
        is_directory(&directory)?;
        for entry in fs::read_dir(directory)? {
            check(cancelled)?;
            let entry = entry?;
            let path = entry.path();
            let relative = path
                .strip_prefix(root)
                .map_err(|_| Error::VersionMismatch)?;
            let kind = entry.file_type()?;
            if kind.is_dir() && directories.contains(relative) {
                pending.push(path);
            } else if kind.is_file() {
                let expected = files.remove(relative).ok_or(Error::VersionMismatch)?;
                verify_file(root, expected, cancelled)?;
            } else {
                return Err(Error::VersionMismatch);
            }
        }
    }
    if !files.is_empty() {
        return Err(Error::VersionMismatch);
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Inspect every archive entry before writing. Only exact manifest paths and
/// ordinary files are accepted; ZIP paths are never used as arbitrary targets.
/// It reads the central directory only: no entry is inflated.
pub(crate) fn archive(
    path: &Path,
    entries: &[PayloadFile],
) -> Result<zip::ZipArchive<File>, Error> {
    if regular(path)?.len() > 128 * 1024 * 1024 {
        return Err(Error::VersionMismatch);
    }
    let mut archive =
        zip::ZipArchive::new(File::open(path)?).map_err(|_| Error::VersionMismatch)?;
    if archive.len() != entries.len() {
        return Err(Error::VersionMismatch);
    }
    let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
    for index in 0..archive.len() {
        let file = archive
            .by_index(index)
            .map_err(|_| Error::VersionMismatch)?;
        let expected = entries
            .iter()
            .find(|entry| entry.path == file.name())
            .ok_or(Error::VersionMismatch)?;
        if !seen.insert(file.name().to_owned())
            || file.size() != expected.size
            || !file.is_file()
            || file
                .unix_mode()
                .is_some_and(|mode| ![0, 0o100000].contains(&(mode & 0o170000)))
        {
            return Err(Error::VersionMismatch);
        }
    }
    Ok(archive)
}
pub(crate) fn copy_verified(
    mut input: impl Read,
    mut output: impl Write,
    entry: &PayloadFile,
    cancelled: &AtomicBool,
) -> Result<(), Error> {
    let mut digest = Sha256::new();
    let mut size = 0_u64;
    let mut buffer = [0_u8; 64 * 1024];
    loop {
        check(cancelled)?;
        let length = input
            .read(&mut buffer)
            .map_err(|_| Error::VersionMismatch)?;
        if length == 0 {
            break;
        }
        size += length as u64;
        if size > entry.size {
            return Err(Error::VersionMismatch);
        }
        digest.update(&buffer[..length]);
        output.write_all(&buffer[..length])?;
    }
    if size != entry.size || format!("{:x}", digest.finalize()) != entry.sha256 {
        return Err(Error::VersionMismatch);
    }
    Ok(())
}
pub(crate) fn verify(
    path: &Path,
    entries: &[PayloadFile],
    cancelled: &AtomicBool,
) -> Result<(), Error> {
    let mut archive = archive(path, entries)?;
    for entry in entries {
        let file = archive
            .by_name(&entry.path)
            .map_err(|_| Error::VersionMismatch)?;
        copy_verified(file, std::io::sink(), entry, cancelled)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub(crate) fn prepare(config: &Config, cancelled: &AtomicBool) -> Result<PathBuf, Error> {
    prepare_with(config, &manifest().files, cancelled)
}
fn prepare_with(
    config: &Config,
    payload: &[PayloadFile],
    cancelled: &AtomicBool,
) -> Result<PathBuf, Error> {
    check(cancelled)?;
    let mut entries = payload.to_vec();
    for name in HELPERS {
        let path = config.helpers.join(name);
        let metadata = regular(&path)?;
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
            if executable_helper(name) && metadata.permissions().mode() & 0o100 == 0 {
                return Err(Error::Unavailable);
            }
        }
        entries.push(PayloadFile {
            path: name.into(),
            package: String::new(),
            size: metadata.len(),
            sha256: crate::sha(&path)?,
        });
    }
    let mut digest = Sha256::new();
    // Hashes are fixed-width; paths are delimited, so different inventories cannot alias.
    for entry in &entries {
        digest.update(entry.path.as_bytes());
        digest.update([0]);
        digest.update(entry.sha256.as_bytes());
    }
    let prefix = format!("{GENERATION}{:x}-", digest.finalize());
    super::files::private_directory(&config.cache)?;
    // Sandbox literal rules use canonical paths (not macOS /var aliases).
    let cache = config.cache.canonicalize()?;
    let mut candidates = fs::read_dir(&cache)?.collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
    candidates.sort_by_key(|entry| entry.file_name());
    for candidate in candidates {
        check(cancelled)?;
        if candidate.file_name().to_string_lossy().starts_with(&prefix)
            && candidate.file_type()?.is_dir()
        {
            match verify_tree(&candidate.path(), &entries, cancelled) {
                Ok(()) => return Ok(candidate.path()),
                Err(Error::Cancelled) => return Err(Error::Cancelled),
                Err(_) => {} // Repair into a new directory; never alter a running runtime.
            }
        }
    }
    let mut archive = archive(&config.package, payload)?;
    let staging = tempfile::Builder::new()
        .prefix(STAGING)
        .tempdir_in(&cache)?;
    for entry in payload {
        check(cancelled)?;
        let target = staging.path().join(&entry.path);
        fs::create_dir_all(target.parent().ok_or(Error::Storage)?)?;
        let mut output = File::create(&target)?;
        let input = archive
            .by_name(&entry.path)
            .map_err(|_| Error::VersionMismatch)?;
        if let Err(error) = copy_verified(input, &mut output, entry, cancelled) {
            // The payload lists the right files but holds other bytes: removed,
            // the next Transfer or launch downloads it again.
            if matches!(error, Error::VersionMismatch) {
                let _ = fs::remove_file(&config.package);
            }
            return Err(error);
        }
        output.sync_all()?;
    }
    for name in HELPERS {
        check(cancelled)?;
        let target = staging.path().join(name);
        fs::copy(config.helpers.join(name), &target)?;
        File::open(target)?.sync_all()?;
    }
    verify_tree(staging.path(), &entries, cancelled)?;
    check(cancelled)?;
    let directory = cache.join(format!("{prefix}{}", uuid::Uuid::new_v4()));
    // Unique immutable generations also make concurrent preparations safe.
    fs::rename(staging.path(), &directory)?;
    File::open(&cache)?.sync_all()?;
    Ok(directory)
}

/// Removes from `cache` every generation, staging folder and launch folder
/// but `generation` and `launch`, the current launch's, and nothing else: the
/// payloads stay. Whatever cannot be removed goes with a later launch. Only
/// the Steam supervisor calls it, after `prepare`: it holds the Steam
/// sessions' owner lock, and starts no game while an earlier one still runs,
/// so no other launch uses what goes. The lock lives in the library while the
/// cache does not: two Obelisks with libraries of their own, as
/// `OBELISK_LIBRARY_DIRECTORY` gives in development, must not both run Steam
/// games.
pub(crate) fn remove_stale(cache: &Path, generation: &Path, launch: &Path) {
    let kept: Vec<_> = [generation, launch]
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|path| path.file_name())
        .collect();
    crate::voile::remove_entries(cache, |name| {
        [GENERATION, STAGING, LAUNCH]
            .iter()
            .any(|prefix| name.starts_with(prefix))
            && !kept.iter().any(|kept| **kept == *name)
    });
}
```

```rs
fn executable(path: &Path) {
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
        fs::set_permissions(path, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o700)).unwrap();
    }

fn write_zip(path: &Path, entries: Vec<(&str, &[u8])>) {
    let mut writer = zip::ZipWriter::new(File::create(path).unwrap());
    for (name, bytes) in entries {
        writer
            .start_file(name, zip::write::SimpleFileOptions::default())
            .unwrap();
        writer.write_all(bytes).unwrap();
    }
    writer.finish().unwrap();
}

#[test]
fn cancellation_before_and_during_copy_is_observed() {
    let fixture = Fixture::new();
    let cancelled = AtomicBool::new(true);
    assert!(matches!(
        prepare_with(&fixture.config, &fixture.files, &cancelled),
        Err(Error::Cancelled)
    ));
    assert!(!fixture.config.cache.exists());
    struct CancelReader<'a>(&'a AtomicBool);
    impl Read for CancelReader<'_> {
        fn read(&mut self, bytes: &mut [u8]) -> std::io::Result<usize> {
            self.0.store(true, Ordering::Release);
            bytes[0] = 1;
            Ok(1)
        }
    }
    cancelled.store(false, Ordering::Release);
    assert!(matches!(
        copy_verified(
            CancelReader(&cancelled),
            std::io::sink(),
            &fixture.files[0],
            &cancelled
        ),
        Err(Error::Cancelled)
    ));
}

fn downloaded_runtime_loads_without_steam_installation_access() {

        wine: None,
        app_id: 0,
    };
    let directory = prepare(&config, &AtomicBool::new(false)).unwrap();
    let executable = directory.join(HELPERS[0]);
    let actual_home = std::env::var_os("HOME").unwrap();
    let steam = PathBuf::from(actual_home).join("Library/Application Support/Steam");
    let profile = format!(
        "(version 1)(allow default)(deny network*)(deny file-write*)(allow file-write* (literal \"/dev/null\"))(deny file-read* (subpath {}))(deny process-exec)(allow process-exec (literal {}))",
        serde_json::to_string(steam.to_str().unwrap()).unwrap(),
        serde_json::to_string(executable.to_str().unwrap()).unwrap()
    );
    let status = std::process::Command::new("/usr/bin/sandbox-exec")
        .args(["-p", &profile])
        .arg(executable)
        .arg("verify-runtime")
        .arg(directory.join("steamclient.dylib"))
        .env_clear()
        .env("HOME", &config.home)
        .env("TMPDIR", root.path())
        .status()
        .unwrap();
    assert!(
        status.success(),
        "minimal packaged runtime must load without Steam, network or writes"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        prepare(&config, &AtomicBool::new(false)).unwrap(),
        directory
    );
}

#[test]
fn equal_size_and_timestamp_tampering_is_still_detected() {
    let fixture = Fixture::new();
    let old = fixture.prepare().unwrap();
    let path = old.join("steamclient.dylib");
    let before = fs::metadata(&path).unwrap();
    let file = fs::OpenOptions::new().write(true).open(&path).unwrap();
    (&file)
        .write_all(&vec![b'x'; before.len() as usize])
        .unwrap();
    file.set_times(fs::FileTimes::new().set_modified(before.modified().unwrap()))
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(fs::metadata(&path).unwrap().len(), before.len());
    assert_eq!(
        fs::metadata(&path).unwrap().modified().unwrap(),
        before.modified().unwrap()
    );
    assert_ne!(fixture.prepare().unwrap(), old);
}

#[test]
fn a_launch_removes_what_earlier_launches_left_but_keeps_its_own_and_the_payloads() {
    let fixture = Fixture::new();
    let current = fixture.prepare().unwrap();
    let cache = &fixture.config.cache;
    let launch = cache.join(format!("{LAUNCH}current"));
    for stale in [
        "runtime-v1-0000-old",
        "runtime-v1-ffff-other",
        ".staging-interrupted",
        "launch-crashed",
    ] {
        fs::create_dir_all(cache.join(stale).join("nested")).unwrap();
        fs::write(cache.join(stale).join("nested/file"), b"stale").unwrap();
    }
    fs::create_dir_all(&launch).unwrap();
    fs::write(cache.join("valve-41.zip"), b"older payload").unwrap();
    fs::write(cache.join("valve-42.zip"), b"payload").unwrap();

    remove_stale(cache, &current, &launch);

    let mut contents = fixture.contents();
    contents.sort();
    let mut expected = vec![
        current.file_name().unwrap().to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
        "launch-current".to_owned(),
        "valve-41.zip".to_owned(),
        "valve-42.zip".to_owned(),
    ];
    expected.sort();
    assert_eq!(contents, expected);
    // The kept generation is still the one a launch reuses.
    assert_eq!(fixture.prepare().unwrap(), current);
}
```
