`crates/game-runtime/src/process.rs`:

```rs
use crate::{Config, Error, files::Prepared, protocol::Event};
use std::{
    io::{BufRead, BufReader, Read},
    process::{ChildStdin, Command, Stdio},
    sync::{
        Arc, Condvar, Mutex,
        mpsc::{self, Receiver, RecvTimeoutError},
    },
    thread::JoinHandle,
    time::{Duration, Instant},
};

/// Generation-based notifications avoid losing an event between drain and wait.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct Wake {
    generation: Mutex<u64>,
    changed: Condvar,
}
impl Wake {
    pub fn generation(&self) -> u64 {
        *self.generation.lock().unwrap()
    }
    pub fn notify(&self) {
        *self.generation.lock().unwrap() += 1;
        self.changed.notify_all();
    }
    pub fn wait(&self, previous: u64) {
        drop(
            self.changed
                .wait_while(self.generation.lock().unwrap(), |g| *g == previous)
                .unwrap(),
        );
    }
}

pub(crate) struct Child {
    child: std::process::Child,
    pub input: Option<ChildStdin>,
    events: Receiver<Event>,
    reader: Option<JoinHandle<()>>,
    reaped: bool,
    pub wakeup: Arc<Wake>,
}
impl Child {
    pub fn host(prepared: &Prepared, config: &Config, service: &str) -> Result<Self, Error> {
        Self::spawn(Self::host_command(prepared, config, service))
    }
    pub(crate) fn host_command(prepared: &Prepared, config: &Config, service: &str) -> Command {
        let mut command = Command::new("/usr/bin/sandbox-exec");
        command
            .arg("-f")
            .arg(&prepared.profile)
            .arg(prepared.directory.join(crate::package::HOST))
            .arg("engine")
            .arg(prepared.directory.join("steamclient.dylib"))
            .arg(config.app_id.to_string())
            .arg(service)
            // This host has no Steam friends UI to apply persona changes.
            .arg("-nofriendsui")
            .current_dir(&prepared.directory)
            .env_clear()
            .env("PATH", "/usr/bin:/bin")
            .env("HOME", prepared.home())
            .env("TMPDIR", prepared.run_directory.join("tmp"));
        // Host and game must connect to the same private IPC.
        command.envs(prepared.endpoints.iter().map(|(key, value)| (key, value)));
        // The host checks the SDK projection under the game's platform.
        if let Some(storage) = &prepared.storage {
            command.env("OBELISK_STORAGE_METADATA", storage.platforms.to_string());
        }
        command
    }
    pub(crate) fn spawn(mut command: Command) -> Result<Self, Error> {
        let mut child = command
            .stdin(Stdio::piped())
            .stdout(Stdio::piped())
            .stderr(Stdio::null())
            .spawn()
            .map_err(|_| Error::StartFailed)?;
        let input = child.stdin.take();
        let output = child.stdout.take().ok_or(Error::StartFailed)?;
        let (sender, events) = mpsc::sync_channel(64);
        let wakeup = Arc::new(Wake::default());
        let changed = wakeup.clone();
        let reader = std::thread::spawn(move || {
            let mut reader = BufReader::new(output);
            loop {
                let mut bytes = Vec::new();
                match (&mut reader).take(4097).read_until(b'\n', &mut bytes) {
                    Ok(0) | Err(_) => break,
                    Ok(length) if length > 4096 => break,
                    Ok(_) => {}
                }
                let Ok(event) = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes) else {
                    break;
                };
                // Do not block process teardown when the game sends many lookups.
                if sender.try_send(event).is_err() {
                    break;
                }
                changed.notify();
            }
            // Disconnect first, then notify: observers must see EOF on wakeup.
            drop(sender);
            changed.notify();
        });
        Ok(Self {
            child,
            input,
            events,
            reader: Some(reader),
            reaped: false,
            wakeup,
        })
    }
    pub fn id(&self) -> u32 {
        self.child.id()
    }
    pub fn alive(&mut self) -> Result<bool, Error> {
        if self.reaped {
            return Ok(false);
        }
        if self
            .child
            .try_wait()
            .map_err(|_| Error::StartFailed)?
            .is_some()
        {
            self.reaped = true;
            return Ok(false);
        }
        Ok(true)
    }
    pub fn next(&mut self, timeout: Duration) -> Result<Option<Event>, Error> {
        match self.events.recv_timeout(timeout) {
            Ok(event) => Ok(Some(event)),
            Err(RecvTimeoutError::Timeout) if self.alive()? => Ok(None),
            Err(_) => Err(Error::StartFailed),
        }
    }
    pub fn try_event(&self) -> Option<Event> {
        self.events.try_recv().ok()
    }
    pub fn stop(&mut self) {
        self.input.take();
        let start = Instant::now();
        while !self.reaped && start.elapsed() < Duration::from_millis(700) {
            if !self.alive().unwrap_or(false) {
                break;
            }
            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20));
        }
        if !self.reaped {
            let _ = self.child.kill();
            let _ = self.child.wait();
            self.reaped = true;
        }
        if let Some(reader) = self.reader.take() {
            let _ = reader.join();
        }
    }
}
impl Drop for Child {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.stop();
    }
}
```

`crates/game-runtime/src/profile.rs`:

```rs
//! What Obelisk knows about particular Windows games, whatever their
//! storefront: the engine that runs one, the graphics backend its Direct3D
//! goes through there, the program started instead of its publisher's, what
//! that program needs besides (arguments, environment variables and DLL
//! overrides), and the oldest Voile release it runs in. The table is
//! `profiles.json`. Obelisk is built with it, and a release build reads it
//! again from Obelisk's `main` as a Windows game launches, keeping the last
//! one beside its library; a development build keeps the one it was built
//! with. Each entry is checked as it is read, and one that sets what a
//! profile may not is left out. It names a game by its storefronts' ids, or
//! by a file of its installation, which finds the game whatever the
//! storefront. Every game it does not name runs with the defaults, in
//! Rosetta's Wine with D3DMetal. The player's launch settings apply over it.
use crate::wine::{Engine, Graphics, GraphicsOptions};
use serde::Deserialize;
use std::{
    collections::BTreeMap,
    fs,
    path::Path,
    sync::{LazyLock, Mutex},
};

const TABLE: &str = include_str!("../profiles.json");
/// Where the table is on Obelisk's `main`.
const URL: &str =
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Zagrios/Obelisk/main/crates/game-runtime/profiles.json";
/// The table's format this Obelisk reads. Another one is a table it ignores.
const FORMAT: u32 = 1;
/// The last table read, in Obelisk's library.
const KEPT: &str = "profiles.json";
/// How `WINEDLLOVERRIDES` loads a DLL: nothing for never.
const MODES: [&str; 6] = ["", "n", "b", "n,b", "b,n", "d"];
/// Variables that load code into the programs Wine starts, on macOS or in
/// the Linux engine: no profile sets them.
const LOADERS: [&str; 2] = ["DYLD_", "LD_"];

/// A game as its storefront names it.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Game<'a> {
    Steam {
        app_id: u32,
    },
    Epic {
        namespace: &'a str,
        app_name: &'a str,
    },
    Gog {
        product_id: &'a str,
    },
}

/// How Obelisk runs one Windows game.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct Profile {
    pub engine: Engine,
    /// What renders its Direct3D on that engine.
    pub graphics: Graphics,
    /// What it asks of that backend.
    pub options: GraphicsOptions,
    /// The program the game starts with instead of its publisher's, relative
    /// to the installation, when that one cannot run there.
    pub executable: Option<&'static str>,
    /// What it adds to the storefront's arguments, before the player's.
    pub arguments: &'static [String],
    /// The environment variables every Wine command of its prefix runs
    /// with, over Obelisk's own.
    pub variables: &'static BTreeMap<String, String>,
    /// How Wine loads some of its DLLs, by DLL, as `WINEDLLOVERRIDES` spells
    /// it: `n,b` for the game's own copy first, nothing to never load it.
    pub dll_overrides: &'static BTreeMap<String, String>,
    /// The oldest Voile release it runs in, such as `v26.3.0-16`: its launch
    /// waits for the newest when an older one is in place, and runs in the
    /// newest installed otherwise, as every game does.
    pub minimum_voile: Option<&'static str>,
}

static NONE: BTreeMap<String, String> = BTreeMap::new();

impl Default for Profile {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            engine: Engine::Rosetta,
            graphics: Graphics::default_on(Engine::Rosetta),
            options: GraphicsOptions::default(),
            executable: None,
            arguments: &[],
            variables: &NONE,
            dll_overrides: &NONE,
            minimum_voile: None,
        }
    }
}

/// The table, as `profiles.json` holds it: each game as written there, which
/// `checked` reads.
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
struct Table {
    format: u32,
    games: Vec<serde_json::Value>,
}

/// One game of the table: its name and why it runs so, for the table's
/// readers, the storefronts' names for it, a file only its installation
/// holds, and what its profile changes from the defaults. Nothing else.
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct Known {
    name: String,
    note: String,
    steam: Option<u32>,
    epic: Option<EpicGame>,
    gog: Option<String>,
    /// Relative to the installation.
    path: Option<String>,
    engine: Option<Engine>,
    graphics: Option<Graphics>,
    executable: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    arguments: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    variables: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    dll_overrides: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    minimum_voile: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct EpicGame {
    namespace: String,
    app_name: String,
}

/// The table launches read now.
struct Current {
    games: &'static [Known],
    /// The table read last, as it came: none until one is read, which
    /// leaves the one Obelisk was built with. A read that brings the same
    /// leaves `games` in place.
    read: Option<Vec<u8>>,
}

static CURRENT: LazyLock<Mutex<Current>> = LazyLock::new(|| {
    Mutex::new(Current {
        games: Vec::leak(parsed(TABLE.as_bytes()).expect("checked-in profiles")),
        read: None,
    })
});

fn table() -> &'static [Known] {
    CURRENT.lock().unwrap().games
}

/// The entries of `table` that `checked` keeps, when it is a table of the
/// format Obelisk reads.
fn parsed(table: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<Known>> {
    let table: Table = serde_json::from_slice(table).ok()?;
    (table.format == FORMAT).then(|| table.games.into_iter().filter_map(checked).collect())
}

/// `entry` as Obelisk reads it, when it holds only what Obelisk reads and
/// sets nothing a profile may not: a name and a note, a storefront's id or a
/// file, a known engine and backend, variables and DLL overrides Obelisk
/// leaves to profiles, paths inside the installation and a release's version.
fn checked(entry: serde_json::Value) -> Option<Known> {
    // An entry is an object: serde would also read an array, field by field.
    if !entry.is_object() {
        return None;
    }
    let known: Known = serde_json::from_value(entry).ok()?;
    known.allowed().then_some(known)
}

/// The names Obelisk sets in the Wine of each engine.
fn reserved() -> impl Iterator<Item = &'static crate::wine::Reserved> {
    crate::launch_settings::ENGINES
        .iter()
        .map(|offer| offer.engine.reserved())
}

fn variable_allowed(name: &str) -> bool {
    let mut characters = name.chars();
    characters
        .next()
        .is_some_and(|first| first.is_ascii_alphabetic() || first == '_')
        && characters.all(|next| next.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || next == '_')
        && !LOADERS.iter().any(|loader| name.starts_with(loader))
        && reserved().all(|own| !own.variables.contains(&name))
}

fn dll_allowed(dll: &str, mode: &str) -> bool {
    let name = dll.to_ascii_lowercase();
    !dll.is_empty()
        && !dll.contains([',', '=', ';'])
        && MODES.contains(&mode)
        && reserved().all(|own| !own.dlls.contains(&name.as_str()))
}

/// Whether `path` stays inside the installation it is relative to.
fn inside(path: &str) -> bool {
    obelisk_core::install::safe_relative_path(path).is_ok()
}

impl Known {
    fn allowed(&self) -> bool {
        !self.name.is_empty()
            && !self.note.is_empty()
            && (self.steam.is_some()
                || self.epic.is_some()
                || self.gog.is_some()
                || self.path.is_some())
            && self.variables.keys().all(|name| variable_allowed(name))
            && self
                .dll_overrides
                .iter()
                .all(|(dll, mode)| dll_allowed(dll, mode))
            && self.executable.as_deref().is_none_or(inside)
            && self.path.as_deref().is_none_or(inside)
            && self
                .minimum_voile
                .as_deref()
                .is_none_or(crate::voile::is_version)
    }

    /// Whether this entry names `game` by its storefront's id.
    fn names(&self, game: Game<'_>) -> bool {
        match game {
            Game::Steam { app_id } => self.steam == Some(app_id),
            Game::Epic {
                namespace,
                app_name,
            } => self
                .epic
                .as_ref()
                .is_some_and(|epic| epic.namespace == namespace && epic.app_name == app_name),
            Game::Gog { product_id } => self.gog.as_deref() == Some(product_id),
        }
    }

    fn profile(&'static self) -> Profile {
        let engine = self.engine.unwrap_or_default();
        Profile {
            engine,
            graphics: self.graphics.unwrap_or(Graphics::default_on(engine)),
            options: GraphicsOptions::default(),
            executable: self.executable.as_deref(),
            arguments: &self.arguments,
            variables: &self.variables,
            dll_overrides: &self.dll_overrides,
            minimum_voile: self.minimum_voile.as_deref(),
        }
    }

    /// Whether the installation in `install` holds this entry's file.
    fn found_in(&self, install: &Path) -> bool {
        self.path
            .as_ref()
            .is_some_and(|path| install.join(path).is_file())
    }
}

/// The profile of `game`, installed in `install`: the one the table gives
/// its storefront's id, else the one whose file the installation holds, else
/// the defaults.
pub(crate) fn of(game: Game<'_>, install: &Path) -> Profile {
    let table = table();
    table
        .iter()
        .find(|known| known.names(game))
        .or_else(|| table.iter().find(|known| known.found_in(install)))
        .map(Known::profile)
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

/// Reads the table again from Obelisk's `main` and keeps it in `library`.
/// Without the network, launches read the last one kept, else the one
/// Obelisk was built with. A development build keeps the one it was built
/// with, as edited.
pub(crate) async fn refresh(library: &Path) {
    if cfg!(debug_assertions) {
        return;
    }
    let kept = library.join(KEPT);
    match crate::remote::fetched(URL).await {
        Some(table) if read(&table) => {
            let _ = crate::remote::keep(&kept, &table);
        }
        _ => {
            let unread = CURRENT.lock().unwrap().read.is_none();
            if unread && let Ok(table) = fs::read(&kept) {
                read(&table);
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Makes `table` the one launches read, when it is a table Obelisk reads
/// with at least one game. Whether it is.
fn read(table: &[u8]) -> bool {
    let mut current = CURRENT.lock().unwrap();
    if current.read.as_deref().unwrap_or(TABLE.as_bytes()) != table {
        let Some(games) = parsed(table).filter(|games| !games.is_empty()) else {
            return false;
        };
        current.games = Vec::leak(games);
    }
    current.read = Some(table.to_vec());
    true
}
```

```rs
use super::*;
use std::collections::HashSet;

/// The profile of `game` found by its id, in an installation that holds no
/// file of the table.
fn by_id(game: Game<'_>) -> Profile {
    of(game, Path::new("/nowhere"))
}

const ROCKET_LEAGUE: Game<'static> = Game::Epic {
    namespace: "9773aa1aa54f4f7b80e44bef04986cea",
    app_name: "Sugar",
};

const FALL_GUYS: Game<'static> = Game::Epic {
    namespace: "50118b7f954e450f8823df1614b24e80",
    app_name: "0a2d9f6403244d12969e11da6713137b",
};

#[test]
fn rocket_league_fall_guys_and_elden_ring_run_on_the_linux_engine_and_nothing_else_does() {
    assert_eq!(by_id(ROCKET_LEAGUE).engine, Engine::Linux);
    assert_eq!(
        by_id(ROCKET_LEAGUE).executable,
        Some("Binaries/Win64/RocketLeague_EAC.exe")
    );
    assert_eq!(by_id(FALL_GUYS).engine, Engine::Linux);
    assert_eq!(by_id(FALL_GUYS).graphics, Graphics::Dxmt);
    assert_eq!(
        by_id(FALL_GUYS).executable,
        Some("start_protected_game.exe")
    );
    assert_eq!(by_id(FALL_GUYS).minimum_voile, Some("v26.3.0-16"));
    assert_eq!(by_id(Game::Steam { app_id: 1245620 }).engine, Engine::Linux);
    for other in [
        Game::Epic {
            namespace: "9773aa1aa54f4f7b80e44bef04986cea",
            app_name: "Other",
        },
        Game::Epic {
            namespace: "5a6d34ba28bc45d081d9311c3885feef",
            app_name: "Sugar",
        },
        Game::Steam { app_id: 252950 },
        Game::Gog {
            product_id: "1245620",
        },

}

/// A table entry Obelisk keeps, with `key` set to `value`, or removed
/// without one.
fn entry_with(key: &str, value: Option<serde_json::Value>) -> Option<Known> {
    let mut entry = serde_json::json!({
        "name": "A game",
        "note": "Why it runs so.",
        "steam": 42,
        "engine": "Linux",
        "graphics": "Dxmt",
        "executable": "Binaries/Win64/Game.exe",
        "variables": {"SteamDeck": "1"},
        "dll_overrides": {"xaudio2_7": "n,b"},
        "minimum_voile": "v26.3.0-16"
    });
    let fields = entry.as_object_mut().unwrap();
    match value {
        Some(value) => fields.insert(key.into(), value),
        None => fields.remove(key),
    };
    checked(entry)
}

#[test]
fn an_entry_that_sets_what_a_profile_may_not_is_left_out() {
    use serde_json::json;
    let kept = entry_with("gog", Some(json!("1207658924"))).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(kept.minimum_voile.as_deref(), Some("v26.3.0-16"));

    for (what, key, value) in [
        ("a key Obelisk does not read", "launcher", Some(json!("x"))),
        ("no note", "note", None),
        ("no id nor file", "steam", None),
```

`crates/game-runtime/src/protocol.rs`:

```rs
//! The only input containing secrets is the inherited, private stdin pipe.
use std::io::{Read, Write};
use zeroize::{Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop, Zeroizing};

#[derive(Clone, Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop)]
pub struct Credentials {
    pub steam_id: u64,
    pub account_name: String,
    pub refresh_token: String,
}
impl Credentials {
    pub fn valid(&self) -> bool {
        self.steam_id != 0
            && (1..=64).contains(&self.account_name.len())
            && (1..=32768).contains(&self.refresh_token.len())
            && !self.account_name.contains('\0')
            && !self.refresh_token.contains('\0')
    }
    pub fn write(&self, mut output: impl Write) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        if !self.valid() {
            return Err(invalid());
        }
        output.write_all(&self.steam_id.to_le_bytes())?;
        output.write_all(&(self.refresh_token.len() as u32).to_le_bytes())?;
        output.write_all(&(self.account_name.len() as u32).to_le_bytes())?;
        output.write_all(self.refresh_token.as_bytes())?;
        output.write_all(self.account_name.as_bytes())
    }
    pub fn read(mut input: impl Read) -> std::io::Result<Self> {
        let mut header = [0; 16];
        input.read_exact(&mut header)?;
        let steam_id = u64::from_le_bytes(header[..8].try_into().map_err(|_| invalid())?);
        let token_length =
            u32::from_le_bytes(header[8..12].try_into().map_err(|_| invalid())?) as usize;
        let account_length =
            u32::from_le_bytes(header[12..].try_into().map_err(|_| invalid())?) as usize;
        if steam_id == 0
            || !(1..=32768).contains(&token_length)
            || !(1..=64).contains(&account_length)
        {
            return Err(invalid());
        }
        let mut token = Zeroizing::new(vec![0; token_length]);
        let mut account = Zeroizing::new(vec![0; account_length]);
        input.read_exact(&mut token)?;
        input.read_exact(&mut account)?;
        let credentials = Self {
            steam_id,
            refresh_token: std::str::from_utf8(&token).map_err(|_| invalid())?.into(),
            account_name: std::str::from_utf8(&account).map_err(|_| invalid())?.into(),
        };
        if !credentials.valid() {
            return Err(invalid());
        }
        Ok(credentials)
    }
}
fn invalid() -> std::io::Error {
    std::io::Error::new(
        std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,
        "Invalid Steam session handoff",
    )
}

/// Commands after the credential handoff, one frame each: the protocol
/// version, a tag, the payload's little-endian `u16` length, then the payload.
/// A frame of another version, or longer than `MAX_PAYLOAD`, ends the stream;
/// a well-framed command the host does not know, or whose payload it refuses,
/// is skipped. EOF between frames still releases the native host.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum HostCommand {
    SetPresence {
        online: bool,
    },
    /// Tells the game Steam's overlay opened or closed
    /// (`GameOverlayActivated_t`), as Obelisk's own overlay does.
    OverlayState {
        active: bool,
        user_initiated: bool,
    },
    /// Hands the running game a lobby invitation the player accepted
    /// (`GameLobbyJoinRequested_t`).
    AcceptLobbyInvite {
        lobby_id: u64,
        friend: u64,
    },
    /// Hands the running game a connect-string invitation the player
    /// accepted (`GameRichPresenceJoinRequested_t`).
    AcceptRichInvite {
        friend: u64,
        connect: String,
    },
    /// The player's answer to the purchase the game asked Steam to confirm.
    AuthorizeMicroTxn {
        order_id: u64,
        approve: bool,
    },
}
impl HostCommand {
    pub const VERSION: u8 = 1;
    /// Bounds every frame: the largest command is a connect string.
    pub const MAX_PAYLOAD: usize = 512;
    const SET_PRESENCE: u8 = 1;
    const OVERLAY_STATE: u8 = 2;
    const ACCEPT_LOBBY_INVITE: u8 = 3;
    const ACCEPT_RICH_INVITE: u8 = 4;
    const AUTHORIZE_MICRO_TXN: u8 = 5;

    /// The next command, `None` at EOF between frames.
    pub fn read(mut input: impl Read) -> std::io::Result<Option<Self>> {
        loop {
            let mut header = [0; 4];
            match input.read_exact(&mut header[..1]) {
                Ok(()) => {}
                Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof => {
                    return Ok(None);
                }
                Err(error) => return Err(error),
            }
            input.read_exact(&mut header[1..])?;
            let length = usize::from(u16::from_le_bytes([header[2], header[3]]));
            if header[0] != Self::VERSION || length > Self::MAX_PAYLOAD {
                return Err(invalid());
            }
            let mut payload = vec![0; length];
            input.read_exact(&mut payload)?;
            if let Some(command) = Self::decode(header[1], &payload) {
                return Ok(Some(command));
            }
        }
    }
    pub fn write(&self, mut output: impl Write) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        let (tag, payload) = self.encode().ok_or_else(invalid)?;
        let length = u16::try_from(payload.len()).map_err(|_| invalid())?;
        let mut frame = vec![Self::VERSION, tag];
        frame.extend_from_slice(&length.to_le_bytes());
        frame.extend_from_slice(&payload);
        output.write_all(&frame)
    }
    /// Whether the host may carry this command out as it stands.
    pub fn valid(&self) -> bool {
        match self {
            Self::SetPresence { .. } | Self::OverlayState { .. } => true,
            Self::AcceptLobbyInvite { lobby_id, friend } => lobby(*lobby_id) && individual(*friend),
            Self::AcceptRichInvite { friend, connect } => {
                individual(*friend) && self::connect(connect)
            }
            Self::AuthorizeMicroTxn { order_id, .. } => *order_id != 0,
        }
    }
    fn encode(&self) -> Option<(u8, Vec<u8>)> {
        if !self.valid() {
            return None;
        }
        Some(match self {
            Self::SetPresence { online } => (Self::SET_PRESENCE, vec![u8::from(*online)]),
            Self::OverlayState {
                active,
                user_initiated,
            } => (
                Self::OVERLAY_STATE,
                vec![u8::from(*active), u8::from(*user_initiated)],
            ),
            Self::AcceptLobbyInvite { lobby_id, friend } => (
                Self::ACCEPT_LOBBY_INVITE,
                [lobby_id.to_le_bytes(), friend.to_le_bytes()].concat(),
            ),
            Self::AcceptRichInvite { friend, connect } => (
                Self::ACCEPT_RICH_INVITE,
                [&friend.to_le_bytes()[..], connect.as_bytes()].concat(),
            ),
            Self::AuthorizeMicroTxn { order_id, approve } => (
                Self::AUTHORIZE_MICRO_TXN,
                [&order_id.to_le_bytes()[..], &[u8::from(*approve)]].concat(),
            ),
        })
    }
    fn decode(tag: u8, payload: &[u8]) -> Option<Self> {
        let flag = |byte: u8| match byte {
            0 => Some(false),
            1 => Some(true),
            _ => None,
        };
        let id = |at: usize| {
            Some(u64::from_le_bytes(
                payload.get(at..at + 8)?.try_into().ok()?,
            ))
        };
        let command = match (tag, payload.len()) {
            (Self::SET_PRESENCE, 1) => Self::SetPresence {
                online: flag(payload[0])?,
            },
            (Self::OVERLAY_STATE, 2) => Self::OverlayState {
                active: flag(payload[0])?,
                user_initiated: flag(payload[1])?,
            },
            (Self::ACCEPT_LOBBY_INVITE, 16) => Self::AcceptLobbyInvite {
                lobby_id: id(0)?,
                friend: id(8)?,
            },
            (Self::ACCEPT_RICH_INVITE, 9..) => Self::AcceptRichInvite {
                friend: id(0)?,
                connect: std::str::from_utf8(&payload[8..]).ok()?.to_owned(),
            },
            (Self::AUTHORIZE_MICRO_TXN, 9) => Self::AuthorizeMicroTxn {
                order_id: id(0)?,
                approve: flag(payload[8])?,
            },
            _ => return None,
        };
        command.valid().then_some(command)
    }
}

/// Reply of an exec helper whose preparation or exec failed. A helper that
/// replaced itself with the game instead closes its confirmation pipe silently.
pub const EXEC_FAILED: &[u8] = b"exec-failed\n";

/// Runs an exec helper's preparation and exec. The supervisor treats EOF as a
/// successful exec, which never returns here; every other outcome sends
/// `EXEC_FAILED` before the confirmation pipe closes.
pub fn exec_or_report<E: From<std::io::Error>>(
    exec: impl FnOnce() -> Result<(), E>,
) -> Result<(), E> {
    exec_or_report_to(exec_confirmation()?, exec)
}

/// `confirmation` must close on exec.
fn exec_or_report_to<E>(
    mut confirmation: std::fs::File,
    exec: impl FnOnce() -> Result<(), E>,
) -> Result<(), E> {
    let result = exec();
    let _ = confirmation.write_all(EXEC_FAILED);
    result
}

/// A CLOEXEC duplicate of stdout that closes atomically on a successful exec.
/// When even that fails, the marker still reaches the supervisor through stdout.
fn exec_confirmation() -> std::io::Result<std::fs::File> {
    use std::os::fd::AsFd;
    let stdout = std::io::stdout();
    stdout
        .as_fd()
        .try_clone_to_owned()
        .map(std::fs::File::from)
        .inspect_err(|_| {
            let _ = stdout.lock().write_all(EXEC_FAILED);
        })
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[serde(tag = "event", rename_all = "snake_case", deny_unknown_fields)]
pub enum Event {
    Authenticated {},
    Ready {
        app_id: u32,
        host_pid: u32,
        ticket_bytes: u32,
    },
    Discovery {
        paths: u32,
    },
    Disconnected {},
    Reconnected {},
    Failed {
        reason: Failure,
    },
    /// The game asked Steam's overlay for `request`, which this host cannot
    /// show: Obelisk shows its own instead.
    OverlayRequested {
        app_id: u32,
        request: OverlayDialog,
    },
    /// A friend invited the account into a lobby of game `app_id`
    /// (`LobbyInvite_t`).
    LobbyInviteReceived {
        inviter: u64,
        lobby_id: u64,
        app_id: u32,
    },
    /// A friend invited the account to join them with a connect string
    /// (`RichInviteReceived_t`, internal).
    RichInviteReceived {
        friend: u64,
        app_id: u32,
        connect: String,
    },
    /// Game `app_id` asks the player to confirm purchase `order_id`
    /// (`MicroTxnAuthRequestCallback_t`, internal).
    MicroTxnRequested {
        order_id: u64,
        app_id: u32,
    },
    /// Steam no longer waits for an answer to purchase `order_id`.
    MicroTxnDismissed {
        order_id: u64,
    },
    /// The lobby the account's Steam engine shows it in while playing
    /// `app_id`, as the host last read it; `None` once it is in none.
    GameLobby {
        app_id: u32,
        lobby_id: Option<u64>,
    },
}

/// What a game asked to invite friends into: its Steam lobby, or the
/// command line a friend's game starts with.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case", deny_unknown_fields)]
pub enum InviteTarget {
    Lobby { lobby_id: u64 },
    Connect { connect: String },
}
impl InviteTarget {
    /// Steam's own limit on a connect string, without its terminating NUL.
    pub const MAX_CONNECT: usize = 255;

    /// A lobby is a Chat SteamID; a connect string fits Steam's buffer.
    pub fn valid(&self) -> bool {
        match self {
            Self::Lobby { lobby_id } => lobby(*lobby_id),
            Self::Connect { connect } => self::connect(connect),
        }
    }
}

/// What a game asked Steam's overlay to show (`GameOverlayActivateRequested_t`,
/// 1010001), one variant per `ISteamFriends::ActivateGameOverlay*` call.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case", deny_unknown_fields)]
pub enum OverlayDialog {
    /// `ActivateGameOverlay(dialog)`: "friends", "community", "players",
    /// "settings", "officialgamegroup", "stats", "achievements",
    /// "chatroomgroup/<id>", …
    Dialog { dialog: String },
    /// `ActivateGameOverlayToUser(dialog, steam_id)`: "steamid", "chat",
    /// "jointrade", "stats", "achievements", "friendadd", …
    User { dialog: String, steam_id: u64 },
    /// `ActivateGameOverlayToWebPage(url, mode)`; `modal` is
    /// `k_EActivateGameOverlayToWebPageMode_Modal`.
    WebPage { url: String, modal: bool },
    /// `ActivateGameOverlayToStore(app_id, flag)`; `flag` is
    /// `EOverlayToStoreFlag`: 0 none, 1 add to cart, 2 add to cart and show.
    Store { app_id: u32, flag: u32 },
    /// `ActivateGameOverlayInviteDialog(lobby)`.
    LobbyInvite { lobby_id: u64 },
    /// `ActivateGameOverlayRemotePlayTogetherInviteDialog(lobby)`.
    RemotePlayTogetherInvite { lobby_id: Option<u64> },
    /// `ActivateGameOverlayInviteDialogConnectString(connect)`.
    ConnectInvite { connect: String },
    /// Steam's own Remote Play Together dialog.
    RemotePlayTogether {},
}
impl OverlayDialog {
    /// Longest dialog name Obelisk accepts, such as "chatroomgroup/<id>".
    pub const MAX_DIALOG: usize = 128;
    /// Longest web page URL Obelisk accepts: the event stays far below the
    /// host's line limit.
    pub const MAX_URL: usize = 2048;
    /// The highest `EOverlayToStoreFlag`.
    pub const MAX_STORE_FLAG: u32 = 2;

    /// Each field within Steam's own limits and Obelisk's.
    pub fn valid(&self) -> bool {
        let dialog = |dialog: &str| {
            (1..=Self::MAX_DIALOG).contains(&dialog.len())
                && dialog
                    .bytes()
                    .all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b"_-./".contains(&byte))
        };
        match self {
            Self::Dialog { dialog: name } => dialog(name),
            Self::User {
                dialog: name,
                steam_id,
            } => dialog(name) && *steam_id != 0,
            Self::WebPage { url, .. } => {
                url.len() <= Self::MAX_URL
                    && (url.starts_with("https://") || url.starts_with("http://"))
                    && url
                        .bytes()
                        .all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_graphic() && byte != b'"' && byte != b'\\')
            }
            Self::Store { flag, .. } => *flag <= Self::MAX_STORE_FLAG,
            Self::LobbyInvite { lobby_id } => lobby(*lobby_id),
            Self::RemotePlayTogetherInvite { lobby_id } => lobby_id.is_none_or(lobby),
            Self::ConnectInvite { connect } => self::connect(connect),
            Self::RemotePlayTogether {} => true,
        }
    }
    /// The invitation an invite dialog asks for; every other dialog has none.
    pub fn invite(&self) -> Option<InviteTarget> {
        match self {
            Self::LobbyInvite { lobby_id } => Some(InviteTarget::Lobby {
                lobby_id: *lobby_id,
            }),
            Self::ConnectInvite { connect } => Some(InviteTarget::Connect {
                connect: connect.clone(),
            }),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// A Steam lobby's SteamID: account type Chat (8), in a real universe, with
/// an account number.
pub fn lobby(steam_id: u64) -> bool {
    (steam_id >> 52) & 0xf == 8 && steam_id >> 56 != 0 && steam_id as u32 != 0
}

/// A person's SteamID: account type Individual (1), in a real universe, with
/// an account number.
pub fn individual(steam_id: u64) -> bool {
    (steam_id >> 52) & 0xf == 1 && steam_id >> 56 != 0 && steam_id as u32 != 0
}

/// A rich presence connect string that fits Steam's buffer.
pub fn connect(connect: &str) -> bool {
    !connect.is_empty() && connect.len() <= InviteTarget::MAX_CONNECT && !connect.contains('\0')
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Failure {
    Engine,
    Authentication,
    Ownership,
    Discovery,
    Cancelled,
}

mod tests {
    use super::*;
    const LOBBY: u64 = 109_775_244_421_126_053;
    const FRIEND: u64 = 76_561_197_960_265_729;

    fn commands() -> Vec<HostCommand> {
        vec![
            HostCommand::SetPresence { online: true },
            HostCommand::SetPresence { online: false },
            HostCommand::OverlayState {
                active: true,
                user_initiated: false,
            },
            HostCommand::AcceptLobbyInvite {
                lobby_id: LOBBY,
                friend: FRIEND,
            },
            HostCommand::AcceptRichInvite {
                friend: FRIEND,
                connect: "+connect_lobby 109775244421126053".into(),
            },
            HostCommand::AuthorizeMicroTxn {
                order_id: 4_242,
                approve: false,
            },
        ]
    }

    #[test]
    fn host_commands_round_trip_framed_until_eof() {
        let mut wire = Vec::new();
        for command in commands() {
            command.write(&mut wire).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(&wire[..5], [1, 1, 1, 0, 1], "version, tag, length, online");
        assert_eq!(&wire[5..10], [1, 1, 1, 0, 0]);
        assert_eq!(&wire[10..16], [1, 2, 2, 0, 1, 0]);
        let mut input = wire.as_slice();
        for command in commands() {
            assert_eq!(HostCommand::read(&mut input).unwrap(), Some(command));
        }
        assert_eq!(HostCommand::read(&mut input).unwrap(), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn host_commands_skip_what_they_refuse_and_stop_on_a_broken_frame() {
        let frame = |tag: u8, payload: &[u8]| {
            let mut frame = vec![HostCommand::VERSION, tag];
            frame.extend_from_slice(&(payload.len() as u16).to_le_bytes());
            frame.extend_from_slice(payload);
            frame
        };
        let mut wire = Vec::new();
        for skipped in [
            frame(9, b"future"),
            frame(1, &[2]),
            frame(1, &[1, 0]),
            frame(2, &[1, 7]),
            // An account is no lobby, a lobby is no friend.
            frame(3, &[FRIEND.to_le_bytes(), FRIEND.to_le_bytes()].concat()),
            frame(3, &[LOBBY.to_le_bytes(), LOBBY.to_le_bytes()].concat()),
            frame(4, &FRIEND.to_le_bytes()),
            frame(4, &[&FRIEND.to_le_bytes()[..], &[0xff]].concat()),
            frame(4, &[&FRIEND.to_le_bytes()[..], b"a\0b"].concat()),
            frame(4, &[&FRIEND.to_le_bytes()[..], &[b'a'; 256]].concat()),
            frame(5, &[0; 9]),
            frame(5, &[&1_u64.to_le_bytes()[..], &[2]].concat()),
        ] {
            wire.extend_from_slice(&skipped);
        }
        HostCommand::SetPresence { online: true }
            .write(&mut wire)
            .unwrap();
        let mut input = wire.as_slice();
        assert_eq!(
            HostCommand::read(&mut input).unwrap(),
            Some(HostCommand::SetPresence { online: true })
        );
        assert_eq!(HostCommand::read(&mut input).unwrap(), None);

        assert!(
            HostCommand::read(&frame(1, &[1])[..3]).is_err(),
            "truncated"
        );
        let mut version = frame(1, &[1]);
        version[0] = 2;
        assert!(HostCommand::read(version.as_slice()).is_err());
        let mut long = vec![HostCommand::VERSION, 4];
        long.extend_from_slice(&513_u16.to_le_bytes());
        long.resize(4 + 513, b'a');
        assert!(HostCommand::read(long.as_slice()).is_err());
        assert!(
            HostCommand::AcceptRichInvite {
                friend: FRIEND,
                connect: "a".repeat(256),
            }
            .write(Vec::new())
            .is_err(),
            "nothing invalid is written"
        );
        assert!(
            HostCommand::AcceptRichInvite {
                friend: FRIEND,
                connect: "a".repeat(255),
            }
            .write(Vec::new())
            .is_ok()
        );
    }

    #[test]

        assert!(individual(FRIEND));
        assert!(!individual(LOBBY) && !individual(0) && !individual(FRIEND & !0xffff_ffff));
        assert!(!individual(FRIEND & ((1 << 56) - 1)), "no universe");
        for valid in [

    #[test]

```

`crates/game-runtime/src/queue.rs`:

```rs
//! The process's one download queue. Every storefront account's Transfers
//! wait in it and run one at a time, in its order: the player's downloads,
//! updates and repairs, Obelisk's automatic updates, and a launch's own
//! Transfer, which goes first and pauses the one under way. While a game
//! runs, whatever its storefront, automatic updates wait.
//!
//! The queue only orders: each Transfer's owner, an account's
//! installations, says when it may start, starts it and reports its end. The
//! queue never calls an owner while it holds its own lock, and owners never
//! call the queue while they hold theirs.
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex, Weak};
use tokio::sync::{oneshot, watch};

/// The storefront a queued Transfer, or a game's diagnostics, belong to.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Storefront {
    Steam,
    Epic,
    Gog,
}

/// What a queued Transfer does to its game.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Kind {
    /// The game has no installation of that build yet.
    Install,
    /// The storefront offers a newer build.
    Update,
    /// The installed build's files are checked and repaired.
    Repair,
    /// The installation moves into the games folder.
    Move,
}

/// One Transfer in the queue, as the player sees it.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Item {
    pub id: u64,
    pub storefront: Storefront,
    pub account: String,
    /// The game, as its storefront's installations name it.
    pub game: String,
    pub name: String,
    pub kind: Kind,
    /// Obelisk queued it for a newer build, not the player.
    pub automatic: bool,
    /// A launch waits for it: it goes first and cannot be paused.
    pub launching: bool,
    /// The player paused it: it waits until resumed.
    pub paused: bool,
}

/// Everything the queue presents. `revision` grows with every change.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct View {
    pub revision: u64,
    /// The Transfer under way.
    pub running: Option<Item>,
    /// The Transfers waiting, in the order they will run.
    pub waiting: Vec<Item>,
    /// A game runs: automatic updates wait.
    pub held: bool,
}

/// What an account's installations do for the Transfers they queued.
pub(crate) trait Owner: Send + Sync {
    /// Whether the Transfer `id` may start now.
    fn ready(&self, id: u64) -> bool;
    /// Starts the Transfer `id`; the owner reports `finished` once it ends.
    fn start(self: Arc<Self>, id: u64);
    /// Stops the running Transfer `id`; `finished` then reports its end.
    fn stop(&self, id: u64);
    /// The Transfer `id` left the queue without running.
    fn removed(&self, id: u64);
}

/// A Transfer an owner adds to the queue.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub(crate) struct Request {
    pub storefront: Storefront,
    pub account: String,
    pub game: String,
    pub name: String,
    pub kind: Kind,
    pub automatic: bool,
}

/// What becomes of a running Transfer the queue stopped, once it ends.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Stop {
    /// It waits first again, paused or not.
    Requeue { paused: bool },
    /// It leaves the queue.
    Remove,
}

struct Entry {
    item: Item,
    owner: Weak<dyn Owner>,
    /// A launch waits for its turn here instead of the owner starting it.
    turn: Option<oneshot::Sender<()>>,
}

struct Running {
    entry: Entry,
    stop: Option<Stop>,
}

#[derive(Default)]
struct State {
    revision: u64,
    next_id: u64,
    running: Option<Running>,
    waiting: Vec<Entry>,
    /// The owners whose storefront runs a game.
    holders: Vec<Weak<dyn Owner>>,
}

impl State {
    fn view(&self) -> View {
        View {
            revision: self.revision,
            running: self
                .running
                .as_ref()
                .map(|running| running.entry.item.clone()),
            waiting: self
                .waiting
                .iter()
                .map(|entry| entry.item.clone())
                .collect(),
            held: self.held(),
        }
    }

    fn held(&self) -> bool {
        !self.holders.is_empty()
    }

    /// Where a Transfer that goes first lands: behind the launches waiting.
    fn head(&self) -> usize {
        self.waiting
            .iter()
            .take_while(|entry| entry.item.launching)
            .count()
    }

    fn eligible(&self, item: &Item) -> bool {
        !item.paused && !(item.automatic && self.held())
    }

    /// Marks the running Transfer stopped, unless a launch waits for it,
    /// and returns what its owner must stop.
    fn stop_running(&mut self, how: Stop, which: impl Fn(&Item) -> bool) -> Stopping {
        let running = self.running.as_mut()?;
        let item = &running.entry.item;
        if running.stop.is_some() || item.launching || !which(item) {
            return None;
        }
        running.stop = Some(how);
        Some((item.id, running.entry.owner.clone()))
    }
}

/// A running Transfer's id and owner, which the queue asked to stop.
type Stopping = Option<(u64, Weak<dyn Owner>)>;

/// The process's one download queue.
pub struct DownloadQueue {
    state: Mutex<State>,
    published: watch::Sender<View>,
}

impl DownloadQueue {
    pub fn new() -> Arc<Self> {
        let state = State::default();
        let (published, _) = watch::channel(state.view());
        Arc::new(Self {
            state: Mutex::new(state),
            published,
        })
    }

    pub fn view(&self) -> View {
        self.published.borrow().clone()
    }

    /// Waits for a revision newer than `after`, or returns at once.
    pub async fn changed(&self, after: u64) -> View {
        let mut receiver = self.published.subscribe();
        let _ = receiver.wait_for(|view| view.revision > after).await;
        receiver.borrow().clone()
    }

    /// Changes the state and publishes it; `change` returns what to do once
    /// the lock is released.
    fn update<T>(&self, change: impl FnOnce(&mut State) -> T) -> T {
        let mut state = self.state.lock().unwrap();
        let before = state.view();
        let result = change(&mut state);
        let mut after = state.view();
        after.revision = before.revision;
        if after != before {
            state.revision += 1;
            after.revision = state.revision;
            self.published.send_replace(after);
        }
        result
    }

    fn entry(
        state: &mut State,
        owner: &Arc<dyn Owner>,
        request: Request,
        launching: bool,
    ) -> Entry {
        state.next_id += 1;
        Entry {
            item: Item {
                id: state.next_id,
                storefront: request.storefront,
                account: request.account,
                game: request.game,
                name: request.name,
                kind: request.kind,
                automatic: request.automatic,
                launching,
                paused: false,
            },
            owner: Arc::downgrade(owner),
            turn: None,
        }
    }

    /// Adds a Transfer behind the others and returns its id. It may start at
    /// the next `advance`, once its owner recorded it.
    pub(crate) fn push(&self, owner: &Arc<dyn Owner>, request: Request) -> u64 {
        self.update(|state| {
            let entry = Self::entry(state, owner, request, false);
            let id = entry.item.id;
            state.waiting.push(entry);
            id
        })
    }

    /// Puts a launch's Transfer first, pausing the one under way, and returns
    /// its id with the turn it waits for. Once its turn came, it runs until
    /// `finished`; removed before, its turn is dropped.
    pub(crate) fn push_first(
        &self,
        owner: &Arc<dyn Owner>,
        request: Request,
    ) -> (u64, oneshot::Receiver<()>) {
        let (sender, turn) = oneshot::channel();
        let (id, stopping) = self.update(|state| {
            let mut entry = Self::entry(state, owner, request, true);
            entry.turn = Some(sender);
            let id = entry.item.id;
            let head = state.head();
            state.waiting.insert(head, entry);
            let stopping = state.stop_running(Stop::Requeue { paused: false }, |_| true);
            (id, stopping)
        });
        stop(stopping);
        self.advance();
        (id, turn)
    }

    /// Ends the running Transfer `id`. When the queue stopped it to pause
    /// it, it waits first again: `true` then.
    pub(crate) fn finished(&self, id: u64) -> bool {
        let requeued = self.update(|state| {
            let running = state
                .running
                .take_if(|running| running.entry.item.id == id)?;
            let Some(Stop::Requeue { paused }) = running.stop else {
                return Some(false);
            };
            let mut entry = running.entry;
            entry.item.paused = paused;
            let head = state.head();
            state.waiting.insert(head, entry);
            Some(true)
        });
        self.advance();
        requeued.unwrap_or(false)
    }

    /// Takes the Transfer `id` out of the queue: a waiting one at once, the
    /// running one once its owner stopped it.
    pub fn remove(&self, id: u64) {
        let (removed, stopping) = self.update(|state| {
            if let Some(index) = state.waiting.iter().position(|entry| entry.item.id == id) {
                return (Some(state.waiting.remove(index).owner), None);
            }
            let stopping = state.running.as_mut().and_then(|running| {
                (running.entry.item.id == id && running.stop != Some(Stop::Remove)).then(|| {
                    running.stop = Some(Stop::Remove);
                    (id, running.entry.owner.clone())
                })
            });
            (None, stopping)
        });
        if let Some(owner) = removed.and_then(|owner| owner.upgrade()) {
            owner.removed(id);
        }
        stop(stopping);
        self.advance();
    }

    /// Takes every Transfer of `owner` out of the queue, and its hold, as
    /// its account signs out.
    pub(crate) fn withdraw(&self, owner: &Arc<dyn Owner>) {
        let ids: Vec<u64> = self.update(|state| {
            state.holders.retain(|holder| !owns(holder, owner));
            state
                .running
                .iter()
                .map(|running| &running.entry)
                .chain(state.waiting.iter())
                .filter(|entry| owns(&entry.owner, owner))
                .map(|entry| entry.item.id)
                .collect()
        });
        self.advance();
        for id in ids {
            self.remove(id);
        }
    }

    /// Pauses the Transfer `id`: a waiting one stays where it is, the running
    /// one stops and waits first. A launch's goes on.
    pub fn pause(&self, id: u64) {
        let stopping = self.update(|state| {
            if let Some(entry) = state.waiting.iter_mut().find(|entry| entry.item.id == id) {
                entry.item.paused = !entry.item.launching;
                return None;
            }
            state.stop_running(Stop::Requeue { paused: true }, |item| item.id == id)
        });
        stop(stopping);
        self.advance();
    }

    pub fn resume(&self, id: u64) {
        self.update(|state| {
            if let Some(entry) = state.waiting.iter_mut().find(|entry| entry.item.id == id) {
                entry.item.paused = false;
            }
        });
        self.advance();
    }

    /// Moves the waiting Transfer `id` first, behind any launch's. The one
    /// under way goes on.
    pub fn move_to_top(&self, id: u64) {
        self.update(|state| {
            let head = state.head();
            if let Some(index) = state.waiting.iter().position(|entry| entry.item.id == id)
                && index > head
            {
                let entry = state.waiting.remove(index);
                state.waiting.insert(head, entry);
            }
        });
    }

    /// Whether `owner`'s storefront runs a game. While one does, whatever its
    /// storefront, automatic updates wait, and one under way stops and waits
    /// first.
    pub(crate) fn hold(&self, owner: &Arc<dyn Owner>, holding: bool) {
        let stopping = self.update(|state| {
            state.holders.retain(|holder| !owns(holder, owner));
            if !holding {
                return None;
            }
            state.holders.push(Arc::downgrade(owner));
            state.stop_running(Stop::Requeue { paused: false }, |item| item.automatic)
        });
        stop(stopping);
        self.advance();
    }

    /// Starts the first waiting Transfer that may start, when none runs.
    /// Owners call it whenever what they let start may have changed.
    pub(crate) fn advance(&self) {
        loop {
            let candidates: Vec<(u64, Weak<dyn Owner>, bool)> = {
                let state = self.state.lock().unwrap();
                if state.running.is_some() {
                    return;
                }
                state
                    .waiting
                    .iter()
                    .filter(|entry| state.eligible(&entry.item))
                    .map(|entry| (entry.item.id, entry.owner.clone(), entry.item.launching))
                    .collect()
            };
            let mut chosen = None;
            let mut gone = Vec::new();
            for (id, owner, launching) in candidates {
                match owner.upgrade() {
                    None => gone.push(id),
                    Some(owner) if launching || owner.ready(id) => {
                        chosen = Some((id, owner));
                        break;
                    }
                    Some(_) => {}
                }
            }
            let claimed = self.update(|state| {
                state.waiting.retain(|entry| !gone.contains(&entry.item.id));
                let (id, _) = chosen.as_ref()?;
                if state.running.is_some() {
                    return None;
                }
                let index = state
                    .waiting
                    .iter()
                    .position(|entry| entry.item.id == *id)?;
                let mut entry = state.waiting.remove(index);
                let turn = entry.turn.take();
                state.running = Some(Running { entry, stop: None });
                Some(turn)
            });
            let Some((id, owner)) = chosen else { return };
            // Another caller started one, or the chosen one left: look again.
            let Some(turn) = claimed else { continue };
            match turn {
                // A launch that stopped waiting gives its turn back.
                Some(turn) => {
                    if turn.send(()).is_err() {
                        self.finished(id);
                    }
                }
                None => owner.start(id),
            }
            return;
        }
    }
}

fn owns(entry: &Weak<dyn Owner>, owner: &Arc<dyn Owner>) -> bool {
    std::ptr::addr_eq(entry.as_ptr(), Arc::as_ptr(owner))
}

/// Asks the owner of a running Transfer the queue stopped to stop it.
fn stop(stopping: Stopping) {
    if let Some((id, owner)) = stopping
        && let Some(owner) = owner.upgrade()
    {
        owner.stop(id);
    }
}
```

```rs
/// An owner whose Transfers the test ends, and what the queue asked of it.
#[derive(Default)]
struct Fake {
    /// Transfers that may not start yet.
    blocked: Mutex<Vec<u64>>,
    log: Mutex<Vec<String>>,
}

impl Fake {
    fn log(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        self.log.lock().unwrap().clone()
    }
    fn note(&self, entry: String) {
        self.log.lock().unwrap().push(entry);
    }
}

impl Owner for Fake {
    fn ready(&self, id: u64) -> bool {
        !self.blocked.lock().unwrap().contains(&id)
    }
    fn start(self: Arc<Self>, id: u64) {
        self.note(format!("start:{id}"));
    }
    fn stop(&self, id: u64) {
        self.note(format!("stop:{id}"));
    }
    fn removed(&self, id: u64) {
        self.note(format!("removed:{id}"));
    }
}

    }

        .view()

    queue.advance();

    assert_eq!(running(&queue), Some(second));
```

`crates/game-runtime/src/remote.rs`:

```rs
//! What a Windows game's launch reads anew from GitHub, Voile's feed and the
//! game profiles: fetched within a few seconds, and kept for the launches
//! that find no network.
use std::{fs, io, path::Path, sync::OnceLock, time::Duration};

/// How long a launch waits for what it reads anew before going on with the
/// last one kept.
const WAIT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(3);

/// The body at `url`, over HTTPS, unless it takes longer than `WAIT`. One
/// client serves every read, so a launch reuses the connections of the last.
pub(crate) async fn fetched(url: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    static CLIENT: OnceLock<reqwest::Client> = OnceLock::new();
    let client = match CLIENT.get() {
        Some(client) => client,
        None => {
            let client = reqwest::Client::builder().https_only(true).build().ok()?;
            CLIENT.get_or_init(|| client)
        }
    };
    let response = client
        .get(url)
        .timeout(WAIT)
        .send()
        .await
        .ok()?
        .error_for_status()
        .ok()?;
    Some(response.bytes().await.ok()?.to_vec())
}

/// Writes `bytes` at `path` in one step, unless they are there already.
pub(crate) fn keep(path: &Path, bytes: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()> {
    if fs::read(path).is_ok_and(|kept| kept == bytes) {
        return Ok(());
    }
    if let Some(folder) = path.parent() {
        fs::create_dir_all(folder)?;
    }
    obelisk_core::write_atomic(path, bytes)
}
```

`crates/game-runtime/src/runtimes.rs`:

```rs
//! The runtimes a game needs beside its own files: Voile for a build that
//! runs in Wine, Valve's Steam components for every Steam game. A Transfer
//! gets the missing ones before the game's files. A launch that still misses
//! one gets it after its Admission, before its game is prepared. Each shows
//! the download its own way. A newer Voile release than the one in place
//! downloads once no game runs, unless the game's profile needs it. A Voile
//! release a newer one replaced goes only when a launch finds no Game
//! session, of any storefront, that may run a game from it.
use crate::{
    installations::blocking,
    sessions::{self, BoxFuture, Failure, failed},
};
use obelisk_core::{Platform, transfer::CancelToken};
use std::{
    path::PathBuf,
    sync::{
        Arc, Mutex,
        atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering},
    },
    time::Duration,
};

/// How often a download under way shows its progress.
const PACE: Duration = Duration::from_millis(250);
/// How often a newer release waiting to download looks for a running game.
const PREFETCH_PACE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
/// How long a newer release waits for the launch that found it to run its
/// game, before it downloads anyway once no game runs.
const PREFETCH_DELAY: Duration = Duration::from_secs(600);

/// A runtime a build needs to launch, beside its own files.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Runtime {
    /// Voile, the Wine runtime Windows games run in.
    Voile,
    /// Valve's Steam components, which Obelisk's Steam host loads.
    SteamComponents,
}

/// What a launch makes of a runtime in place.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum Standing {
    /// In place, and nothing newer is offered.
    Current,
    /// In place and enough for the game, while a newer release is offered:
    /// it downloads once no game runs.
    Outdated,
    /// Not in place, or not enough for the game while a release that is
    /// enough is offered: the launch waits for it.
    Missing,
}

/// How much of a runtime has downloaded: the bytes received, and the total.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Progress {
    pub runtime: Runtime,
    pub received: u64,
    pub total: u64,
}

/// One runtime's download, which the one waiting for it runs, cancels and
/// watches.
pub(crate) trait RuntimeDownload: Send + Sync {
    /// The bytes received so far, and the total.
    fn progress(&self) -> (u64, u64);
    fn cancel(&self);
    /// A failure is the runtime's own localization key.
    fn run(&self) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<(), Failure>>;
}

/// Where the runtimes are: where one stands, its download, what decides
/// which release a launch wants, and the Voile releases a newer one
/// replaced. Tests stand in for it.
pub(crate) trait RuntimeSource: Send + Sync {
    /// Where `runtime` stands for a game whose profile needs `voile` or a
    /// newer Voile release. It reads a few files, never a whole runtime.
    fn standing(&self, runtime: Runtime, voile: Option<&str>) -> Standing;
    /// The download of the release a launch wants: for Voile, the newest its
    /// feed offers once read again.
    fn download(&self, runtime: Runtime) -> Arc<dyn RuntimeDownload>;
    /// Reads anew what launches decide on: Voile's feed and the game
    /// profiles. Without the network, it soon gives up and keeps the last.
    fn refresh(&self) -> BoxFuture<'_, ()>;
    /// Removes the Voile releases a newer one replaced. What cannot go now
    /// goes with a later launch.
    fn remove_replaced(&self);
}

/// The process's runtimes, which every storefront's Transfers and launches
/// share.
pub struct Runtimes {
    source: Arc<dyn RuntimeSource>,
    /// Whether each storefront's Game sessions may run a game now.
    sessions: Mutex<Vec<Box<dyn Fn() -> bool + Send + Sync>>>,
    /// A newer release downloads, or waits for no game to run.
    prefetching: AtomicBool,
}

impl Runtimes {
    /// Gets the runtimes into the places `locations` names, where launches
    /// read them.
    pub fn new(locations: &crate::Locations) -> Arc<Self> {
        Self::from_source(Arc::new(Downloads(locations.clone())))
    }

    pub(crate) fn from_source(source: Arc<dyn RuntimeSource>) -> Arc<Self> {
        Arc::new(Self {
            source,
            sessions: Mutex::new(Vec::new()),
            prefetching: AtomicBool::new(false),
        })
    }

    /// Counts a storefront's Game sessions, which `may_run` tells about,
    /// before a launch removes a replaced release.
    pub(crate) fn watch_sessions(&self, may_run: impl Fn() -> bool + Send + Sync + 'static) {
        self.sessions.lock().unwrap().push(Box::new(may_run));
    }

    /// Reads anew what a launch decides on, before its game's profile is
    /// read: Voile's feed and the game profiles.
    pub(crate) async fn refresh_before_launch(&self) {
        self.source.refresh().await;
    }

    /// Gets each runtime a build of `platform` from P needs that is missing,
    /// in order, the newest Voile release offered when Voile is. `shown` gets
    /// each download's progress when it starts and every `PACE`. Cancelling
    /// `cancel` stops the download under way and any after it. Never removes
    /// a release.
    pub(crate) async fn get<P: sessions::Storefront>(
        &self,
        platform: Platform,
        cancel: &CancelToken,
        shown: impl Fn(Progress) + Send,
    ) -> Result<(), Failure> {
        for runtime in needed::<P>(platform) {
            if self.standing(runtime, None).await? == Standing::Missing {
                self.download(runtime, cancel, &shown).await?;
            }
        }
        match cancel.is_cancelled() {
            true => Err(Failure::Cancelled),
            false => Ok(()),
        }
    }

    /// Gets the runtimes as `get` does, for a game whose profile needs
    /// `voile` or a newer Voile release; a newer release than the one in
    /// place and enough downloads once no game runs. Then, for a build that
    /// needs Voile, removes the releases a newer one replaced, unless the
    /// Game sessions of a storefront may run a game. A failed or cancelled
    /// launch removes nothing.
    pub(crate) async fn get_for_launch<P: sessions::Storefront>(
        self: &Arc<Self>,
        platform: Platform,
        voile: Option<&'static str>,
        cancel: &CancelToken,
        shown: impl Fn(Progress) + Send,
    ) -> Result<(), Failure> {
        for runtime in needed::<P>(platform) {
            match self.standing(runtime, voile).await? {
                Standing::Current => {}
                Standing::Outdated => self.prefetch(runtime),
                Standing::Missing => self.download(runtime, cancel, &shown).await?,
            }
        }
        if cancel.is_cancelled() {
            return Err(Failure::Cancelled);
        }
        if needed::<P>(platform).contains(&Runtime::Voile) && !self.may_run() {
            let source = self.source.clone();
            let _ = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || source.remove_replaced()).await;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    async fn standing(
        &self,
        runtime: Runtime,
        voile: Option<&'static str>,
    ) -> Result<Standing, Failure> {
        let source = self.source.clone();
        blocking(storage_failed(runtime), move || {
            source.standing(runtime, voile)
        })
        .await
    }

    /// Downloads `runtime`, showing its progress through `shown`, until it
    /// ends or `cancel` stops it.
    async fn download(
        &self,
        runtime: Runtime,
        cancel: &CancelToken,
        shown: &(impl Fn(Progress) + Send),
    ) -> Result<(), Failure> {
        if cancel.is_cancelled() {
            return Err(Failure::Cancelled);
        }
        let download = self.source.download(runtime);
        let mut run = download.run();
        let outcome = loop {
            let (received, total) = download.progress();
            shown(Progress {
                runtime,
                received,
                total,
            });
            tokio::select! {
                outcome = &mut run => break outcome,
                () = cancel.cancelled() => {
                    download.cancel();
                    // The install cleans up before the wait ends.
                    break (&mut run).await;
                }
                () = tokio::time::sleep(PACE) => {}
            }
        };
        match outcome {
            Err(_) if cancel.is_cancelled() => Err(Failure::Cancelled),
            outcome => outcome,
        }
    }

    /// Downloads the newer release of `runtime` once no game runs, as
    /// automatic updates wait for one: the launch that found it goes on with
    /// the release in place, and a later launch runs the new one.
    fn prefetch(self: &Arc<Self>, runtime: Runtime) {
        if self.prefetching.swap(true, Ordering::AcqRel) {
            return;
        }
        let runtimes = self.clone();
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            runtimes.until_no_game_runs().await;
            let _ = runtimes.source.download(runtime).run().await;
            runtimes.prefetching.store(false, Ordering::Release);
        });
    }

    /// Waits until no Game session may run a game, once a game has run, or
    /// after `PREFETCH_DELAY` when none did.
    async fn until_no_game_runs(&self) {
        let since = tokio::time::Instant::now();
        let mut ran = false;
        loop {
            tokio::time::sleep(PREFETCH_PACE).await;
            let running = self.may_run();
            ran |= running;
            if !running && (ran || since.elapsed() >= PREFETCH_DELAY) {
                return;
            }
        }
    }

    /// Whether the Game sessions of a storefront may run a game now.
    fn may_run(&self) -> bool {
        self.sessions
            .lock()
            .unwrap()
            .iter()
            .any(|may_run| may_run())
    }
}

/// The runtimes a build of `platform` from P needs, in the order they are
/// got: the storefront's own, then Voile for a build that runs in Wine.
fn needed<P: sessions::Storefront>(platform: Platform) -> Vec<Runtime> {
    let mut needed = P::RUNTIMES.to_vec();
    if platform == Platform::Windows {
        needed.push(Runtime::Voile);
    }
    needed
}

fn storage_failed(runtime: Runtime) -> String {
    match runtime {
        Runtime::Voile => crate::voile::Failure::Storage.to_string(),
        Runtime::SteamComponents => crate::valve::Failure::Storage.to_string(),
    }
}

/// The runtimes Obelisk downloads, in the places its launches read them.
struct Downloads(crate::Locations);

impl RuntimeSource for Downloads {
    fn standing(&self, runtime: Runtime, voile: Option<&str>) -> Standing {
        match runtime {
            Runtime::Voile => crate::voile::standing(&self.0.voile, voile),
            Runtime::SteamComponents => {
                match crate::valve::installed(&self.0.steam_runtime_package) {
                    true => Standing::Current,
                    false => Standing::Missing,
                }
            }
        }
    }
    fn download(&self, runtime: Runtime) -> Arc<dyn RuntimeDownload> {
        match runtime {
            Runtime::Voile => Arc::new(Download {
                install: crate::voile::Install::new(),
                path: self.0.voile.clone(),
            }),
            Runtime::SteamComponents => Arc::new(Download {
                install: crate::valve::Install::new(),
                path: self.0.steam_runtime_package.clone(),
            }),
        }
    }
    fn refresh(&self) -> BoxFuture<'_, ()> {
        Box::pin(async move {
            tokio::join!(
                crate::voile::refresh(&self.0.voile),
                crate::profile::refresh(&self.0.library),
            );
        })
    }
    fn remove_replaced(&self) {
        crate::voile::remove_replaced(&self.0.voile);
    }
}

/// One runtime's install into `path`.
struct Download<I> {
    install: I,
    path: PathBuf,
}

impl RuntimeDownload for Download<crate::voile::Install> {
    fn progress(&self) -> (u64, u64) {
        self.install.progress()
    }
    fn cancel(&self) {
        self.install.cancel();
    }
    fn run(&self) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<(), Failure>> {
        Box::pin(async move {
            let archive = development_archive();
            self.install
                .run(&self.path, archive.as_deref())
                .await
                .map(drop)
                .map_err(Into::into)
        })
    }
}

impl RuntimeDownload for Download<crate::valve::Install> {
    fn progress(&self) -> (u64, u64) {
        self.install.progress()
    }
    fn cancel(&self) {
        self.install.cancel();
    }
    fn run(&self) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<(), Failure>> {
        Box::pin(async move { self.install.run(&self.path).await.map_err(Into::into) })
    }
}

/// A local copy of the Voile release Obelisk was built with, which replaces
/// its download in development builds.
fn development_archive() -> Option<PathBuf> {
    if !cfg!(debug_assertions) {
        return None;
    }
    std::env::var_os("OBELISK_VOILE_ARCHIVE")
        .filter(|archive| !archive.is_empty())
        .map(Into::into)
}

impl From<crate::voile::Failure> for Failure {
    fn from(failure: crate::voile::Failure) -> Self {
        match failure {
            crate::voile::Failure::Cancelled => Self::Cancelled,
            failure => failed(failure),
        }
    }
}

impl From<crate::valve::Failure> for Failure {
    fn from(failure: crate::valve::Failure) -> Self {
        match failure {
            crate::valve::Failure::Cancelled => Self::Cancelled,
            failure => failed(failure),
        }
    }
}
```

`crates/game-runtime/src/runtimes/tests.rs`:

```rs
//! Runtimes through their interface, against runtimes the test stands in
//! for.
use super::*;
use crate::{epic::Epic, gog::Gog, installations::tests::eventually, steam::Steam};
use std::sync::{
    Mutex,
    atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering},
};

/// What `FakeRuntimes` does, shared with each of its downloads.
struct FakeRuntime {
    present: Vec<Runtime>,
    /// In place, while a newer release is offered.
    outdated: Vec<Runtime>,
    /// The next download's failure.
    failure: Option<Failure>,
    /// Downloads wait until they are cancelled, or until the test releases
    /// them.
    held: Option<CancelToken>,
    record: Arc<dyn Fn(String) + Send + Sync>,
}

/// Runtimes a test stands in for. Those `present` are in place, and those
/// `outdate` names are in place while a newer release is offered, which a
/// game that needs a newer release cannot run in. A download of another
/// records its name through `record`, then waits once `hold` is called until
/// it is cancelled or `release` lets it go on, then fails as `fail` says, or
/// else puts the newest release of its runtime in place. Reading the feed
/// and the profiles again records "refresh", and removing the replaced
/// releases "remove replaced".
pub(crate) struct FakeRuntimes(Arc<Mutex<FakeRuntime>>);

impl FakeRuntimes {
    pub(crate) fn new(
        present: &[Runtime],
        record: impl Fn(String) + Send + Sync + 'static,
    ) -> Arc<Self> {
        Arc::new(Self(Arc::new(Mutex::new(FakeRuntime {
            present: present.to_vec(),
            outdated: Vec::new(),
            failure: None,
            held: None,
            record: Arc::new(record),
        }))))
    }
    /// `runtime` is in place, and a newer release of it is offered.
    fn outdate(&self, runtime: Runtime) {
        self.0.lock().unwrap().outdated.push(runtime);
    }
    pub(crate) fn fail(&self, failure: Failure) {
        self.0.lock().unwrap().failure = Some(failure);
    }
    pub(crate) fn hold(&self) {
        self.0.lock().unwrap().held = Some(CancelToken::new());
    }
    /// The downloads held go on, and the next ones no longer wait.
    pub(crate) fn release(&self) {
        if let Some(released) = self.0.lock().unwrap().held.take() {
            released.cancel();
        }
    }
    /// The runtimes in place now, in the order they came.
    pub(crate) fn in_place(&self) -> Vec<Runtime> {
        self.0.lock().unwrap().present.clone()
    }
}

/// Runtimes whose every runtime is in place.
pub(crate) fn ready() -> Arc<Runtimes> {
    Runtimes::from_source(FakeRuntimes::new(
        &[Runtime::SteamComponents, Runtime::Voile],
        |_| {},
    ))
}

pub(crate) fn runtime_name(runtime: Runtime) -> String {
    match runtime {
        Runtime::Voile => "voile".into(),
        Runtime::SteamComponents => "steam components".into(),
    }
}

impl RuntimeSource for FakeRuntimes {
    fn standing(&self, runtime: Runtime, voile: Option<&str>) -> Standing {
        let state = self.0.lock().unwrap();
        match (state.outdated.contains(&runtime), voile) {
            (true, Some(_)) => Standing::Missing,
            (true, None) => Standing::Outdated,
            _ if state.present.contains(&runtime) => Standing::Current,
            _ => Standing::Missing,
        }
    }
    fn download(&self, runtime: Runtime) -> Arc<dyn RuntimeDownload> {
        Arc::new(FakeDownload {
            runtime,
            state: self.0.clone(),
            cancel: CancelToken::new(),
        })
    }
    fn refresh(&self) -> BoxFuture<'_, ()> {
        let record = self.0.lock().unwrap().record.clone();
        Box::pin(async move { record("refresh".into()) })
    }
    fn remove_replaced(&self) {
        let record = self.0.lock().unwrap().record.clone();
        record("remove replaced".into());
    }
}

struct FakeDownload {
    runtime: Runtime,
    state: Arc<Mutex<FakeRuntime>>,
    cancel: CancelToken,
}

impl RuntimeDownload for FakeDownload {
    fn progress(&self) -> (u64, u64) {
        (5, 10)
    }
    fn cancel(&self) {
        self.cancel.cancel();
    }
    fn run(&self) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<(), Failure>> {
        Box::pin(async move {
            let (record, held) = {
                let state = self.state.lock().unwrap();
                (state.record.clone(), state.held.clone())
            };
            record(runtime_name(self.runtime));
            if let Some(released) = held {
                tokio::select! {
                    biased;
                    () = self.cancel.cancelled() => return Err(Failure::Cancelled),
                    () = released.cancelled() => {}
                }
            }
            let mut state = self.state.lock().unwrap();
            if let Some(failure) = state.failure.take() {
                return Err(failure);
            }
            state.outdated.retain(|outdated| *outdated != self.runtime);
            state.present.push(self.runtime);
            Ok(())
        })
    }
}

pub(crate) fn recorded() -> (
    Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>>,
    impl Fn(String) + Send + Sync + 'static,
) {
    let events = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
    let recording = events.clone();
    (events, move |event| recording.lock().unwrap().push(event))
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_build_gets_the_runtimes_its_storefront_and_platform_need_in_order() {
    /// What a build of `platform` from P downloads with nothing in place.
    async fn downloads<P: sessions::Storefront>(platform: Platform) -> Vec<String> {
        let (events, record) = recorded();
        let runtimes = Runtimes::from_source(FakeRuntimes::new(&[], record));
        runtimes
            .get::<P>(platform, &CancelToken::new(), |_| {})
            .await
            .unwrap();
        events.lock().unwrap().clone()
    }

    assert_eq!(
        downloads::<Steam>(Platform::Windows).await,
        ["steam components", "voile"]
    );
    assert_eq!(
        downloads::<Steam>(Platform::Mac).await,
        ["steam components"]
    );
    assert_eq!(downloads::<Epic>(Platform::Windows).await, ["voile"]);
    assert_eq!(downloads::<Epic>(Platform::Mac).await, Vec::<String>::new());
    assert_eq!(downloads::<Gog>(Platform::Windows).await, ["voile"]);
    assert_eq!(downloads::<Gog>(Platform::Mac).await, Vec::<String>::new());
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn runtimes_in_place_are_not_downloaded_again() {
    let (events, record) = recorded();
    let fake = FakeRuntimes::new(&[Runtime::Voile], record);
    let runtimes = Runtimes::from_source(fake.clone());
    let cancel = CancelToken::new();

    runtimes
        .get::<Steam>(Platform::Windows, &cancel, |_| {})
        .await
        .unwrap();
    runtimes
        .get::<Steam>(Platform::Windows, &cancel, |_| {})
        .await
        .unwrap();

    assert_eq!(*events.lock().unwrap(), ["steam components"]);
    assert_eq!(fake.in_place(), [Runtime::Voile, Runtime::SteamComponents]);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_download_shows_its_runtime_and_bytes_and_cancelling_stops_it() {
    let (events, record) = recorded();
    let fake = FakeRuntimes::new(&[], record);
    fake.hold();
    let runtimes = Runtimes::from_source(fake.clone());
    let cancel = CancelToken::new();
    let shown = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
    let getting = {
        let (runtimes, cancel, shown) = (runtimes.clone(), cancel.clone(), shown.clone());
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            runtimes
                .get::<Epic>(Platform::Windows, &cancel, |progress| {
                    shown.lock().unwrap().push(progress)
                })
                .await
        })
    };
    eventually(|| !shown.lock().unwrap().is_empty()).await;
    assert_eq!(
        shown.lock().unwrap()[0],
        Progress {
            runtime: Runtime::Voile,
            received: 5,
            total: 10
        }
    );

    cancel.cancel();

    assert_eq!(getting.await.unwrap(), Err(Failure::Cancelled));
    assert!(fake.in_place().is_empty());
    // The same token gets nothing more; a fresh one downloads again.
    assert_eq!(
        runtimes
            .get::<Epic>(Platform::Windows, &cancel, |_| {})
            .await,
        Err(Failure::Cancelled)
    );
    assert_eq!(*events.lock().unwrap(), ["voile"]);
    fake.release();
    runtimes
        .get::<Epic>(Platform::Windows, &CancelToken::new(), |_| {})
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(*events.lock().unwrap(), ["voile", "voile"]);
    assert_eq!(fake.in_place(), [Runtime::Voile]);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_failed_download_ends_the_wait_with_its_own_failure_before_the_next_runtime() {
    let (events, record) = recorded();

}
```
