```rs
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_launch_gets_steam_components_for_every_build_and_voile_for_a_windows_one() {
    let fixture = Fixture::new();
    let (events, record) = recorded();
    let runtimes = FakeRuntimes::new(&[], record);
    let sessions = Sessions::<Steam>::new(
        Box::new(|| Ok(None)),
        Runtimes::from_source(runtimes.clone()),
    );
    eventually(|| !sessions.state().recovering).await;

    // The Mac build has no Steam API library once prepared.
    let admission = sessions.admit(620, 42).unwrap();
    let launched = fixture
        .content
        .launch(&fixture.installed(Platform::Mac), admission, None)
        .await;
    assert_eq!(
        launched,
        Err(Failure::Failed(crate::Error::ApiMissing.to_string()))
    );
    assert_eq!(*events.lock().unwrap(), ["steam components"]);

    runtimes.hold();
    let admission = sessions.admit(620, 42).unwrap();
    let canceller = admission.canceller();
    let windows = fixture.installed(Platform::Windows);
    let (launched, ()) = tokio::join!(fixture.content.launch(&windows, admission, None), async {
        eventually(|| events.lock().unwrap().len() == 2).await;
        canceller.cancel();
    });

    assert_eq!(launched, Err(Failure::Cancelled), "nothing is prepared");
    assert_eq!(*events.lock().unwrap(), ["steam components", "voile"]);
}
```

`crates/game-runtime/src/steam/launch.rs`:

```rs
//! A Steam launch: the native host that owns the game's Steam session, Steam
//! Cloud, and the game slice chosen against the pinned Steam API library.
use super::*;
use crate::{
    HostUpdate, NativeStorage, Runtime, package,
    supervisor::{
        Error as Core,
        architecture::Architecture,
        session::{self, LaunchCloud, Opening, Prepared, Session},
        storage,
    },
};
use std::{io::Read, marker::PhantomData, sync::Arc};

/// Makes `ISteamUtils::IsOverlayEnabled` true for a game in Wine, so it asks
/// Steam for its overlay (callback 1010001) and Obelisk shows its own: many
/// games hide their invite or store buttons otherwise. The game's own
/// steamclient answers it, never the host. In the pinned steamclient.dylib,
/// that answer is `getenv("SteamOS") != NULL`, and only without it the
/// `IsOverlayEnabled` export of a loaded overlay renderer, through `dlsym`:
/// arm64 0xa060b8 (string 0x15a3dd0), x86_64 0x9c6586 (string 0x16af134),
/// the slice lsteamclient loads. Neither checks the value.
pub(crate) const OVERLAY_ENABLED: (&str, &str) = ("SteamOS", "1");

/// What a Steam launch asks of the machine. Tests replace it.
pub(crate) trait Machine: Send + Sync + 'static {
    /// The game slice to launch against the pinned Steam API library.
    fn select(target: &Target, config: &Config) -> Result<Option<Architecture>, Error>;
    /// Starts the native host for this account and game.
    fn prepare(
        launch: &crate::Launch,
        config: Config,
        storage: Option<NativeStorage>,
    ) -> Result<Runtime, Error>;
    fn publish(runtime: &Runtime, active: bool);
    fn cloud(
        config: cloud::Config,
        credentials: Credentials,
        id: String,
        control: Arc<crate::cloud::Control>,
    ) -> Result<Box<dyn SteamCloud>, Error>;
    fn rosetta(helper: &Path) -> Result<bool, Core>;
}

/// The machine Obelisk runs on.
pub(crate) struct Mac;
impl Machine for Mac {
    fn select(target: &Target, config: &Config) -> Result<Option<Architecture>, Error> {
        if let Some(wine) = &config.wine {
            return Ok(Some(wine.architecture()));
        }
        let library = config.steam_api.as_deref().ok_or(Error::ApiMissing)?;
        Architecture::select(&target.executable, library).map(Some)
    }
    fn prepare(
        launch: &crate::Launch,
        config: Config,
        storage: Option<NativeStorage>,
    ) -> Result<Runtime, Error> {
        launch.prepare(config, storage)
    }
    fn publish(runtime: &Runtime, active: bool) {
        let _ = runtime.set_presence(active);
    }
    fn cloud(
        config: cloud::Config,
        credentials: Credentials,
        id: String,
        control: Arc<crate::cloud::Control>,
    ) -> Result<Box<dyn SteamCloud>, Error> {
        Ok(Box::new(cloud::open(config, credentials, id, control)?))
    }
    fn rosetta(helper: &Path) -> Result<bool, Core> {
        crate::supervisor::architecture::rosetta_available(helper)
    }
}

/// Steam Cloud as a launch uses it: its prepared sync also names the SDK
/// Cloud storage the native host serves.
pub(crate) trait SteamCloud: LaunchCloud<Error> {
    fn native_storage(&self) -> Result<Option<NativeStorage>, Error>;
}
impl SteamCloud for cloud::Session {
    fn native_storage(&self) -> Result<Option<NativeStorage>, Error> {
        self.store().native_storage()
    }
}

pub(crate) struct Launch<M: Machine = Mac> {
    request: Request,
    /// Zeroized on drop. Only the host and Steam Cloud receive them.
    credentials: Credentials,
    launch: Arc<crate::Launch>,
    machine: PhantomData<M>,
}

impl<M: Machine> session::Launch for Launch<M> {
    type P = Steam;
    type Host = Runtime;
    type Cloud = Box<dyn SteamCloud>;

    fn open(input: &mut dyn Read) -> Result<(Opening<Steam>, Self), Error> {
        let credentials = Credentials::read(&mut *input)?;
        let request: Request = storage::packet(input)?;
        if uuid::Uuid::parse_str(&request.id).is_err()
            || request.config.app_id == 0
            || request.cloud.as_ref().is_some_and(|cloud| {
                cloud.app_id != request.config.app_id
                    || cloud.prefix.as_ref()
                        != request.config.wine.as_ref().map(|wine| &wine.prefix)
            })
        {
            return Err(Error::InvalidSession);
        }
        let helpers = crate::supervisor::rosetta::helpers(&request.config.helpers)
            .unwrap_or(&request.config.helpers);
        let opening = Opening {
            root: request.root.clone(),
            id: request.id.clone(),
            account_id: credentials.steam_id,
            store: Store::new(request.config.app_id),
            helpers: helpers.into(),
        };
        let launch = Self {
            launch: Arc::new(crate::Launch::new(credentials.clone())),
            credentials,
            request,
            machine: PhantomData,
        };
        Ok((opening, launch))
    }

    fn interrupt(&self) -> Box<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync> {
        let launch = self.launch.clone();
        Box::new(move || launch.cancel())
    }

    fn wine(&self) -> Option<crate::wine::Config> {
        self.request.config.wine.clone()
    }

    async fn cloud(
        &mut self,
        session: &Arc<Session<Steam>>,
    ) -> Result<Option<Box<dyn SteamCloud>>, Error> {
        let Some(config) = self.request.cloud.clone() else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        Ok(Some(M::cloud(
            config,
            self.credentials.clone(),
            self.request.id.clone(),
            session.cloud().clone(),
        )?))
    }

    async fn target(
        &mut self,
        _: &Arc<Session<Steam>>,
    ) -> Result<(Target, Option<Architecture>), Error> {
        let architecture = M::select(&self.request.target, &self.request.config)?;
        Ok((self.request.target.clone(), architecture))
    }

    async fn prepare_host(
        &mut self,
        _: &Arc<Session<Steam>>,
        target: &Target,
        architecture: Option<Architecture>,
        cloud: Option<&Box<dyn SteamCloud>>,
    ) -> Result<Prepared<Runtime>, Error> {
        let storage = match cloud {
            Some(cloud) => cloud.native_storage()?,
            None => None,
        };
        let (launch, config) = (self.launch.clone(), self.request.config.clone());
        let runtime = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || M::prepare(&launch, config, storage))
            .await
            .map_err(|_| Error::StartFailed)??;
        // The Intel helper comes from the prepared runtime; arm64 games use
        // the bundled host's gated exec.
        let (helper, subcommand) = if architecture == Some(Architecture::Intel) {
            (
                runtime.prepared.directory.join(package::SDK_INTEL),
                "exec-game",
            )
        } else {
            (self.request.config.helpers.join(package::HOST), "game-exec")
        };
        let mut environment = target.environment.clone();
        environment.extend(runtime.environment());
        game_environment(
            &mut environment,
            self.request.config.app_id,
            self.request.config.wine.is_some(),
            &runtime.prepared.directory,
        );
        Ok(Prepared {
            host: runtime,
            helper,
            subcommand,
            environment,
        })
    }

    fn running(&self, host: &Arc<Runtime>, pid: u32) -> Box<dyn Fn(bool) + Send + Sync> {
        let _ = host.started(pid);
        let host = host.clone();
        Box::new(move |active| M::publish(&host, active))
    }

    fn control(&self, host: &Arc<Runtime>) -> Option<session::Control<Steam>> {
        let host = host.clone();
        Some(Box::new(move |control| {
            match control {
                Control::Overlay {
                    active,
                    user_initiated,
                } => host.overlay_state(active, user_initiated),
                Control::AcceptInvite { friend, target } => host.accept_invite(friend, target),
                Control::AuthorizeMicroTxn { order_id, approve } => {
                    host.authorize_microtxn(order_id, approve)
                }
            }
            .map_err(|error| match error {
                Error::InvalidSession => Core::InvalidSession,
                _ => Core::Unavailable,
            })
        }))
    }

    fn watch(
        &self,
        host: &Arc<Runtime>,
        session: &Arc<Session<Steam>>,
    ) -> Option<std::thread::JoinHandle<()>> {
        let (host, session) = (host.clone(), session.clone());
        Some(std::thread::spawn(move || {
            let mut previous = HostUpdate::new(HostState::Online);
            loop {
                let next = host.next_update(&previous);
                let _ = session.update(|record| record.store.apply(&next));
                if matches!(next.state, HostState::Stopped | HostState::Lost) {
                    break;
                }
                previous = next;
            }
        }))
    }

    fn stopped(&self, host: &Runtime, exit: Option<i32>) {
        host.stopped(exit);
    }

    fn terminal(record: &mut Snapshot) {
        record.store.apply(&HostUpdate::new(HostState::Stopped));
    }

    fn rosetta(helper: &Path) -> Result<bool, Core> {
        M::rosetta(helper)
    }
}

/// What the game's own Steam API reads, over the host's environment: its
/// AppID, and in Wine, the host's engine and an enabled overlay.
fn game_environment(
    environment: &mut std::collections::HashMap<String, String>,
    app_id: u32,
    wine: bool,
    runtime: &Path,
) {
    let app_id = app_id.to_string();
    environment.insert("SteamAppId".into(), app_id.clone());
    environment.insert("SteamGameId".into(), app_id);
    if wine {
        let (name, value) = OVERLAY_ENABLED;
        environment.insert(name.into(), value.into());
        // lsteamclient loads the Intel slice of the host's steamclient.dylib.
        environment.insert(
            "STEAM_COMPAT_CLIENT_INSTALL_PATH".into(),
            runtime.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
        );
    }
}

/// Games ship the Steam API library beside their executable or inside their
/// bundle. Links are never followed, and the search stays bounded.
pub(crate) fn steam_api(target: &obelisk_core::launch::LaunchTarget) -> Result<PathBuf, Error> {
    library(target, &["libsteam_api.dylib"])
}

/// The first file under the game's directory, its bundle or its executable's
/// folder, named like one of `names`.
fn library(target: &obelisk_core::launch::LaunchTarget, names: &[&str]) -> Result<PathBuf, Error> {
    let executable = Path::new(&target.executable)
        .canonicalize()
        .map_err(|_| Error::ApiMissing)?;
    if target.is_application_bundle {
        return library_in(&executable, names);
    }
    library_in(executable.parent().ok_or(Error::ApiMissing)?, names)
}

/// The first file under `directory` named like one of `names`, ignoring case.
fn library_in(directory: &Path, names: &[&str]) -> Result<PathBuf, Error> {
    const MAX_ENTRIES: usize = 20_000;
    let directory = directory.canonicalize().map_err(|_| Error::ApiMissing)?;
    let mut pending = vec![directory.clone()];
    let mut inspected = 0;
    while let Some(folder) = pending.pop() {
        let mut entries: Vec<_> = std::fs::read_dir(&folder)
            .map_err(|_| Error::ApiMissing)?
            .filter_map(std::result::Result::ok)
            .collect();
        entries.sort_by_key(std::fs::DirEntry::file_name);
        for entry in entries {
            inspected += 1;
            if inspected > MAX_ENTRIES {
                return Err(Error::ApiMissing);
            }
            let name = entry.file_name();
            if name.to_string_lossy().starts_with('.') {
                continue;
            }
            let Ok(kind) = entry.file_type() else {
                continue;
            };
            if kind.is_dir() {
                pending.push(entry.path());
            } else if kind.is_file()
                && names
                    .iter()
                    .any(|library| name.to_string_lossy().eq_ignore_ascii_case(library))
                && let Ok(library) = entry.path().canonicalize()
                && library.starts_with(&directory)
            {
                return Ok(library);
            }
        }
    }
    Err(Error::ApiMissing)
}
```

```rs
struct FakeCloud {
    directory: PathBuf,
    script: Script,
    control: Arc<crate::cloud::Control>,
}
impl SteamCloud for FakeCloud {
    fn native_storage(&self) -> Result<Option<NativeStorage>, Error> {
        Ok(None)
    }
}
impl LaunchCloud<Error> for FakeCloud {
    fn prepare<'a>(&'a mut self, _: &'a SessionAlive<'a>) -> Operation<'a, Result<(), Error>> {
        Box::pin(async move {
            record(&self.directory, "cloud.prepare");
            let check = || {
                self.control
                    .check()
                    .map_err(|stop| Error::from(cloud::Failure::from(stop)))
            };
            if self.script.hold_cloud {
                fs::write(self.directory.join("cloud-ready"), b"").unwrap();
                hold(&self.directory, "release-cloud", check).await?;
            }
            if self.script.ask {
                let choice = self
                    .control
                    .ask(crate::cloud::Question::Conflict, None)
                    .await
                    .map_err(cloud::Failure::from)?;
                record(&self.directory, &format!("answered:{choice:?}"));
                self.control.show(crate::cloud::Phase::Ready, None);
            }
            Ok(())
        })
    }
    fn started(&mut self) -> Result<(), Error> {
        record(&self.directory, "cloud.started");
        Ok(())
    }
    fn finished(&mut self, confirmed: bool) -> Operation<'_, ()> {
        Box::pin(async move {
            if self.script.hold_finish {
                fs::write(self.directory.join("finish-ready"), b"").unwrap();
                let _ = hold(&self.directory, "release-finish", || Ok::<_, Error>(())).await;
            }
            self.control.show(crate::cloud::Phase::Syncing, None);
            record(&self.directory, &format!("cloud.finished:{confirmed}"));
        })
    }
    fn aborted(&mut self) {
        record(&self.directory, "cloud.aborted");
    }
}

#[test]
fn a_lost_steam_host_keeps_the_game_reserved() {
    let run = launch::<SteamHarness>(script(HELD));
    run.until(|r| r.phase == Phase::Running);
    let host = fs::read_to_string(run.directory.join("host-pid")).unwrap();
    assert!(
        std::process::Command::new("/bin/kill")

            .status()
            .unwrap()
            .success()
    );

    assert_eq!(
        lost.phase,
        Phase::Running,

    assert!(!lost.finished());
    run.release("release-game");
    let finished = run.until(Snapshot::finished);
    assert_eq!(finished.exit_code, Some(3));
    assert_eq!(finished.store.host, HostState::Stopped);
}

    let library = bundle.join("Contents/Frameworks/libsteam_api.dylib");

    );

    fs::write(

        b"library",
    )
    .unwrap();
    std::os::unix::fs::symlink(outside.path(), bundle.join("Contents/Linked")).unwrap();
    std::os::unix::fs::symlink(
        outside.path().join("libsteam_api.dylib"),
        bundle.join("Contents/libsteam_api.dylib"),
    )
    .unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(
        steam_api(&launch_target(&bundle, true)),
        Err(Error::ApiMissing)
    ));
}

#[test]
fn a_steam_store_keeps_what_the_host_told_and_reads_records_without_it() {

    };

    assert_eq!(serde_json::from_value::<Store>(value).unwrap(), store);
    let mut terminal = store.clone();
    terminal.apply(&crate::HostUpdate::new(HostState::Stopped));
    assert_eq!(
        terminal,
        Store {
            host: HostState::Stopped,
            ..Store::new(42)
        }
    );

            },

                lobby_id: 109_775_244_421_126_053,

            },
        ]
    );
```

`crates/game-runtime/src/steam/windows.rs`:

```rs
//! A Windows Steam game: Wine starts it behind Proton's steam.exe helper,
//! which stands in for Steam, once its prefix ran the steps of the install
//! scripts the installation lists.
use crate::{Error, supervisor::Target, wine};
use obelisk_core::launch::LaunchTarget;
use std::{fs, io::Read, path::Path};

/// The helper every Windows game starts behind. Wine installs it in each prefix.
const HELPER: &str = r"C:\windows\system32\steam.exe";
/// Valve's Windows libraries that steam_api loads through the ActiveProcess
/// registry keys. The runtime's ntdll redirects their exports to lsteamclient.
const CLIENTS: [&str; 2] = ["steamclient.dll", "steamclient64.dll"];
/// What the game's steam_api and lsteamclient read, which its session sets
/// as it starts the game (see `launch::game_environment` and the host's
/// ports). The Linux engine's guest receives them from its launcher.
const GAME_ENVIRONMENT: &[&str] = &[
    "SteamAppId",
    "SteamGameId",
    "SteamOS",
    "Steam3Master",
    "SteamClientService",
];
/// The largest install script read.
const MAX_SCRIPT_BYTES: usize = 1024 * 1024;
/// How much of each library is compared at a time.
const BLOCK: u64 = 64 * 1024;

/// What Steam adds to the prefix of the installation in `install`.
pub(super) struct Prefix<'a> {
    pub install: &'a Path,
}

impl wine::Storefront for Prefix<'_> {
    const HELPER: Option<&'static str> = Some(HELPER);
    const PASSED: &'static [&'static str] = GAME_ENVIRONMENT;
    const STEAM_CLIENT: bool = true;

    /// The steps of the install scripts the installation lists, which Steam
    /// runs before a game first starts. A script that cannot be read is left
    /// out.
    fn prerequisites(&self) -> Result<Vec<wine::Prerequisite>, Error> {
        let read = |relative: &Path| {
            obelisk_core::install::read_cached_file(self.install, relative, MAX_SCRIPT_BYTES)
                .map_err(|_| Error::Storage)
        };
        let Some(list) = read(Path::new(steam_kit::install_script::LIST))? else {
            return Ok(Vec::new());
        };
        let windows_install = wine::windows_path(self.install);
        let mut prerequisites = Vec::new();
        for script in String::from_utf8_lossy(&list).lines() {
            let Ok(Some(bytes)) = read(Path::new(script)) else {
                continue;
            };
            let Ok(steps) =
                steam_kit::install_script::steps(&bytes, self.install, &windows_install)
            else {
                continue;
            };
            prerequisites.extend(steps.into_iter().map(|step| {
                wine::Prerequisite {
                    id: step.id,
                    programs: step
                        .programs
                        .into_iter()
                        .map(|program| (program.path, program.arguments))
                        .collect(),
                }
            }));
        }
        Ok(prerequisites)
    }

    /// Places Valve's steamclient libraries where the prefix's registry
    /// points steam_api.
    fn furnish(&self, config: &wine::Config) -> Result<(), Error> {
        let steam = config.prefix.join("drive_c/Program Files (x86)/Steam");
        fs::create_dir_all(&steam)?;
        for name in CLIENTS {
            let source = config.runtime.join("steam").join(name);
            let destination = steam.join(name);
            if !destination.is_file() || !same_contents(&destination, &source)? {
                fs::copy(&source, &destination)?;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Whether the files at `a` and `b` hold the same bytes. Reading stops at
/// their first difference.
fn same_contents(a: &Path, b: &Path) -> std::io::Result<bool> {
    let (mut a, mut b) = (fs::File::open(a)?, fs::File::open(b)?);
    if a.metadata()?.len() != b.metadata()?.len() {
        return Ok(false);
    }
    let (mut left, mut right) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
    loop {
        left.clear();
        right.clear();
        let read = (&mut a).take(BLOCK).read_to_end(&mut left)?;
        (&mut b).take(BLOCK).read_to_end(&mut right)?;
        if left != right {
            return Ok(false);
        }
        if read == 0 {
            return Ok(true);
        }
    }
}

/// The Windows game `target` names, started by steam.exe. A game that ships
/// no Steam API starts all the same, and its Game session keeps the host,
/// Cloud and quitting.
pub(super) fn target(
    config: &wine::Config,
    game: &wine::Game<'_>,
    target: &LaunchTarget,
    home: &Path,
) -> Result<Target, Error> {
    wine::target::<Prefix<'_>>(config, game, target, crate::native::environment(home))
}
```

```rs
use super::*;
use crate::installations::Receipt;
use crate::wine::tests::{
    config, engine_runtime, installation, locations, pe, record_calls, target,
};
use std::path::PathBuf;

/// The receipt of Steam's `app_id`, named `name`, as a Windows build in
/// `install`.
fn receipt(install: &Path, app_id: u32, name: &str) -> Receipt<crate::steam::Steam> {
    Receipt {
        product: crate::steam::Product {
            app_id,
            language: "english".into(),
        },
        name: name.into(),
        directory: install.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
        platform: obelisk_core::Platform::Windows,
        total_bytes: 1,
        needs_verification: false,
    }
}

/// A game installed in `install`, without a store title.
fn game(install: &Path) -> wine::Game<'_> {
    wine::Game { install, title: "" }
}

/// A Windows game in `root/game` whose Steam API sits beside Unity's plugins.
fn steam_game(root: &Path) -> PathBuf {
    let install = root.join("game");
    fs::create_dir_all(install.join("Game_Data/Plugins/x86_64")).unwrap();
    fs::write(install.join("Game.exe"), pe()).unwrap();
    fs::write(
        install.join("Game_Data/Plugins/x86_64/steam_api64.dll"),
        pe(),
    )
    .unwrap();
    install
}

fn libraries_compare_by_their_bytes_across_blocks() {

        let path = directory.path().join(name);
        fs::write(&path, bytes).unwrap();
        path
    };
    let library = vec![7_u8; BLOCK as usize * 2 + 5];
    let mut changed = library.clone();
    *changed.last_mut().unwrap() = 8;
    let original = write("original", &library);

    assert!(same_contents(&original, &write("copy", &library)).unwrap());
    assert!(!same_contents(&original, &write("changed", &changed)).unwrap());
    assert!(!same_contents(&original, &write("shorter", &library[1..])).unwrap());
}
```

`crates/game-runtime/src/supervisor/architecture.rs`:

```rs
//! Select supported Mach-O slices before launching native games or Steam SDK code.
use crate::Error;
use std::{
    fs::File,
    io::{Read, Seek, SeekFrom},
    path::Path,
    process::{Command, Stdio},
    time::{Duration, Instant},
};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum Architecture {
    Arm64,
    Intel,
}
impl Architecture {
    pub fn select(executable: &Path, library: &Path) -> Result<Self, Error> {
        Self::from_slices(slices(executable)? & slices(library)?)
    }
    /// The preferred supported slice of an executable or library on its own.
    pub fn preferred(binary: &Path) -> Result<Self, Error> {
        Self::from_slices(slices(binary)?)
    }
    /// A Mac game runs only natively: Obelisk installs the Windows build of a
    /// game whose Mac build has no arm64 slice, and Rosetta runs Wine alone.
    fn from_slices(mask: u8) -> Result<Self, Error> {
        if mask & 1 != 0 {
            Ok(Self::Arm64)
        } else {
            Err(Error::IncompatibleArchitecture)
        }
    }
}

fn cpu_mask(cpu: u32) -> u8 {
    match cpu {
        0x0100_000c => 1,
        0x0100_0007 => 2,
        _ => 0,
    }
}
fn number(bytes: &[u8], little: bool) -> u32 {
    let bytes = bytes.try_into().expect("four-byte Mach-O field");
    if little {
        u32::from_le_bytes(bytes)
    } else {
        u32::from_be_bytes(bytes)
    }
}
fn wide(bytes: &[u8], little: bool) -> u64 {
    let bytes = bytes.try_into().expect("eight-byte Mach-O field");
    if little {
        u64::from_le_bytes(bytes)
    } else {
        u64::from_be_bytes(bytes)
    }
}
fn header(file: &mut File, offset: u64) -> Result<(u32, bool), Error> {
    file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(offset))?;
    let mut bytes = [0; 8];
    file.read_exact(&mut bytes)
        .map_err(|_| Error::IncompatibleArchitecture)?;
    let little = match bytes[..4] {
        [0xcf, 0xfa, 0xed, 0xfe] | [0xce, 0xfa, 0xed, 0xfe] => true,
        [0xfe, 0xed, 0xfa, 0xcf] | [0xfe, 0xed, 0xfa, 0xce] => false,
        _ => return Err(Error::IncompatibleArchitecture),
    };
    Ok((
        number(&bytes[4..], little),
        bytes[0] == 0xcf || bytes[3] == 0xcf,
    ))
}
fn slices(path: &Path) -> Result<u8, Error> {
    let mut file = File::open(path).map_err(|_| Error::Unavailable)?;
    let length = file.metadata()?.len();
    let mut prefix = [0; 8];
    file.read_exact(&mut prefix)
        .map_err(|_| Error::IncompatibleArchitecture)?;
    let fat = match prefix[..4] {
        [0xca, 0xfe, 0xba, 0xbe] => Some((false, false)),
        [0xbe, 0xba, 0xfe, 0xca] => Some((true, false)),
        [0xca, 0xfe, 0xba, 0xbf] => Some((false, true)),
        [0xbf, 0xba, 0xfe, 0xca] => Some((true, true)),
        _ => None,
    };
    let Some((little, is_wide)) = fat else {
        let (cpu, is_64) = header(&mut file, 0)?;
        return if is_64 && length >= 32 && cpu_mask(cpu) != 0 {
            Ok(cpu_mask(cpu))
        } else {
            Err(Error::IncompatibleArchitecture)
        };
    };
    let count = number(&prefix[4..], little) as usize;
    if !(1..=32).contains(&count) {
        return Err(Error::IncompatibleArchitecture);
    }
    let entry_size = if is_wide { 32 } else { 20 };
    let table_end = 8 + count * entry_size;
    let mut entries = vec![0; count * entry_size];
    file.read_exact(&mut entries)
        .map_err(|_| Error::IncompatibleArchitecture)?;
    let mut result = 0;
    let mut intervals = Vec::new();
    for entry in entries.chunks_exact(entry_size) {
        let cpu = number(&entry[..4], little);
        let (offset, size) = if is_wide {
            (wide(&entry[8..16], little), wide(&entry[16..24], little))
        } else {
            (
                number(&entry[8..12], little) as u64,
                number(&entry[12..16], little) as u64,
            )
        };
        let end = offset
            .checked_add(size)
            .ok_or(Error::IncompatibleArchitecture)?;
        if offset < table_end as u64
            || size < 28
            || end > length
            || intervals
                .iter()
                .any(|&(start, stop)| offset < stop && end > start)
        {
            return Err(Error::IncompatibleArchitecture);
        }
        intervals.push((offset, end));
        let (actual, is_64) = header(&mut file, offset)?;
        if actual != cpu || cpu_mask(cpu) != 0 && (!is_64 || size < 32) {
            return Err(Error::IncompatibleArchitecture);
        }
        result |= cpu_mask(cpu);
    }
    if result == 0 {
        Err(Error::IncompatibleArchitecture)
    } else {
        Ok(result)
    }
}

/// A bounded execution of our signed Intel helper proves availability. It does
/// not open an app through LaunchServices or request a system installation.
pub(crate) fn rosetta_available(helper: &Path) -> Result<bool, crate::supervisor::Error> {
    use crate::supervisor::Error;
    let mut child = match Command::new(helper)
        .arg("--probe")
        .env_clear()
        .stdin(Stdio::null())
        .stdout(Stdio::null())
        .stderr(Stdio::null())
        .spawn()
    {
        Ok(child) => child,
        Err(error) if error.raw_os_error() == Some(86) => return Ok(false),
        Err(_) => return Err(Error::Unavailable),
    };
    let start = Instant::now();
    loop {
        match child.try_wait() {
            Ok(Some(status)) if status.success() => return Ok(true),
            Ok(Some(_)) => return Err(Error::RosettaUnavailable),
            Ok(None) if start.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(3) => {
                std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20));
            }
            _ => {
                let _ = child.kill();
                let _ = child.wait();
                return Err(Error::RosettaUnavailable);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

`crates/game-runtime/src/supervisor/architecture/tests.rs`:

```rs
use super::*;

pub(crate) const ARM64: u32 = 0x0100_000c;
pub(crate) const INTEL: u32 = 0x0100_0007;

fn word(value: u32, little: bool) -> [u8; 4] {
    if little {
        value.to_le_bytes()
    } else {
        value.to_be_bytes()
    }
}

fn long_word(value: u64, little: bool) -> [u8; 8] {
    if little {
        value.to_le_bytes()
    } else {
        value.to_be_bytes()
    }
}

pub(crate) fn thin(cpu: u32, little: bool) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut bytes = vec![0; 32];
    bytes[..4].copy_from_slice(&word(0xfeedfacf, little));
    bytes[4..8].copy_from_slice(&word(cpu, little));
    bytes
}

fn universal(cpus: &[u32], little: bool, wide: bool) -> Vec<u8> {
    let entry_size = if wide { 32 } else { 20 };
    let mut bytes = vec![0; 8 + cpus.len() * entry_size];
    let magic = if wide { 0xcafebabf } else { 0xcafebabe };
    bytes[..4].copy_from_slice(&word(magic, little));
    bytes[4..8].copy_from_slice(&word(cpus.len() as u32, little));
    for (index, cpu) in cpus.iter().enumerate() {
        let start = 8 + index * entry_size;
        let offset = bytes.len();
        bytes[start..start + 4].copy_from_slice(&word(*cpu, little));
        if wide {
            bytes[start + 8..start + 16].copy_from_slice(&long_word(offset as u64, little));
            bytes[start + 16..start + 24].copy_from_slice(&long_word(32, little));
        } else {
            bytes[start + 8..start + 12].copy_from_slice(&word(offset as u32, little));
            bytes[start + 12..start + 16].copy_from_slice(&word(32, little));
        }
        // The slice's byte order is independent of its enclosing fat header.
        bytes.extend(thin(*cpu, !little));
    }
    bytes
}

fn parse(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<u8, Error> {
    let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let path = root.path().join("executable");
    std::fs::write(&path, bytes).unwrap();
    slices(&path)
}

#[test]
fn selects_the_shared_arm64_slice_only() {
    let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let game = root.path().join("game");
    let sdk = root.path().join("sdk");
    for (game_bytes, sdk_bytes, expected) in [
        (
            thin(ARM64, true),
            thin(ARM64, true),
            Some(Architecture::Arm64),
        ),
        // An Intel game never runs natively, whatever its library holds.
        (
            thin(INTEL, true),
            universal(&[INTEL, ARM64], false, false),
            None,
        ),
        (
            universal(&[INTEL, ARM64], false, false),
            universal(&[INTEL, ARM64], false, true),
            Some(Architecture::Arm64),
        ),
        (
            universal(&[INTEL, ARM64], true, true),
            thin(INTEL, true),
            None,
        ),
        (thin(ARM64, true), thin(INTEL, true), None),
        (thin(7, true), thin(7, true), None),
    ] {
        std::fs::write(&game, game_bytes).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(&sdk, sdk_bytes).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(Architecture::select(&game, &sdk).ok(), expected);
    }
}

#[test]
fn standalone_executable_runs_its_arm64_slice_without_an_sdk_dependency() {
    let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let game = root.path().join("game");
    for (bytes, expected) in [
        (thin(ARM64, true), Architecture::Arm64),
        (
            universal(&[INTEL, ARM64], false, false),
            Architecture::Arm64,
        ),
        (universal(&[INTEL, ARM64], true, true), Architecture::Arm64),
    ] {
        std::fs::write(&game, bytes).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(Architecture::preferred(&game).unwrap(), expected);
    }
    for bytes in [thin(INTEL, true), b"\xcf\xfa\xed\xfe".to_vec()] {
        std::fs::write(&game, bytes).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            Architecture::preferred(&game),
            Err(Error::IncompatibleArchitecture)
        ));
    }
}

#[test]
fn reads_thin_and_both_fat_entry_widths_in_either_byte_order() {
    for little in [false, true] {
        assert_eq!(parse(&thin(ARM64, little)).unwrap(), 1);
        assert_eq!(parse(&thin(INTEL, little)).unwrap(), 2);
        for wide in [false, true] {
            assert_eq!(parse(&universal(&[ARM64], little, wide)).unwrap(), 1);
            assert_eq!(parse(&universal(&[INTEL], little, wide)).unwrap(), 2);
            assert_eq!(parse(&universal(&[INTEL, ARM64], little, wide)).unwrap(), 3);
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn accepts_cpu_variants_with_different_subtypes() {
    let mut bytes = universal(&[INTEL, INTEL], false, false);
    // CPU_SUBTYPE_X86_64_ALL and CPU_SUBTYPE_X86_64_H share a CPU type.
    for (index, subtype) in [3_u32, 8].into_iter().enumerate() {
        let entry = 8 + index * 20;
        let slice = 48 + index * 32;
        bytes[entry + 4..entry + 8].copy_from_slice(&subtype.to_be_bytes());
        bytes[slice + 8..slice + 12].copy_from_slice(&subtype.to_le_bytes());
    }
    assert_eq!(parse(&bytes).unwrap(), 2);
}

#[test]
fn rejects_scripts_unsupported_cpu_and_truncated_headers() {
    let valid = universal(&[INTEL, ARM64], false, false);
    let mut thin32 = thin(INTEL, true);
    thin32[..4].copy_from_slice(&0xfeedface_u32.to_le_bytes());
    for bytes in [
        Vec::new(),
        b"#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n".to_vec(),
        thin(7, true),
        thin32,
        thin(INTEL, true)[..31].to_vec(),
        valid[..20].to_vec(),
        valid[..valid.len() - 1].to_vec(),
    ] {
        assert!(matches!(
            parse(&bytes),
            Err(Error::IncompatibleArchitecture)
        ));
    }
    for count in [0_u32, 33] {
        let mut bytes = valid.clone();
        bytes[4..8].copy_from_slice(&count.to_be_bytes());
        assert!(matches!(
            parse(&bytes),
            Err(Error::IncompatibleArchitecture)
        ));
    }
}

#[test]
fn rejects_overlapping_table_and_slices_and_mislabeled_cpu() {
    for little in [false, true] {
        let valid = universal(&[INTEL, ARM64], little, false);
        let mut table_overlap = valid.clone();
        table_overlap[16..20].copy_from_slice(&word(8, little));
        let mut slice_overlap = valid.clone();
        slice_overlap[36..40].copy_from_slice(&word(48, little));
        let mut wrong_cpu = valid.clone();
        wrong_cpu[8..12].copy_from_slice(&word(ARM64, little));
        let mut small_slice = valid.clone();
        small_slice[20..24].copy_from_slice(&word(31, little));
        let mut outside_file = valid.clone();
        outside_file[16..20].copy_from_slice(&word(valid.len() as u32 + 1, little));
        for bytes in [
            table_overlap,
            slice_overlap,
            wrong_cpu,
            small_slice,
            outside_file,
        ] {
            assert!(matches!(
                parse(&bytes),
                Err(Error::IncompatibleArchitecture)
            ));
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn rejects_fat64_offset_overflow_and_truncated_entry_in_both_byte_orders() {
    for little in [false, true] {
        let valid = universal(&[INTEL], little, true);
        let mut overflow = valid.clone();
        overflow[16..24].copy_from_slice(&long_word(u64::MAX - 15, little));
        let mut table_overlap = valid.clone();
        table_overlap[16..24].copy_from_slice(&long_word(8, little));
        for bytes in [overflow, table_overlap, valid[..39].to_vec()] {
            assert!(matches!(
                parse(&bytes),
                Err(Error::IncompatibleArchitecture)
            ));
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(unix)]
fn probe_script(root: &Path, body: &str) -> std::path::PathBuf {
    use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
    let path = root.join("probe");
    std::fs::write(&path, format!("#!/bin/sh\n{body}\n")).unwrap();
    std::fs::set_permissions(&path, std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o700)).unwrap();
    path
}
```

`crates/game-runtime/src/supervisor/child.rs`:

```rs
//! Process ownership shared by Steam and Epic supervisors.
//!
//! A helper's confirmed exec starts the game; only reaping that child ends it.
//! Inspection supplies durable identities, never permission to abandon a child.
use crate::supervisor::Identity;
use std::{io, path::Path, time::Duration};
use tokio::{io::AsyncReadExt, process::Child, time::Instant};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum Execution {
    Started,
    Failed,
    ExitedUnconfirmed,
}

/// How the child ended: its exit code, or the signal that ended it.
pub(crate) async fn wait_for_exit(child: &mut Child) -> std::process::ExitStatus {
    loop {
        match child.wait().await {
            Ok(status) => return status,
            // Losing an observation never releases ownership of a live game.
            Err(_) => tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100)).await,
        }
    }
}

/// The signed helper owns a CLOEXEC pipe: EOF confirms replacement by the game,
/// while ordinary preparation/exec failures send an explicit bounded marker.
pub(crate) async fn confirm_execution(
    child: &mut Child,
    executable: &Path,
    inspect: impl Fn(u32) -> Option<Identity>,
) -> Execution {
    let pid = child.id();
    let expected = executable.canonicalize().ok();
    let observing = Instant::now();
    let output = child.stdout.take();
    let read = async move {
        let Some(output) = output else {
            return std::future::pending::<io::Result<Vec<u8>>>().await;
        };
        let mut bytes = Vec::new();
        output.take(64).read_to_end(&mut bytes).await?;
        Ok(bytes)
    };
    tokio::pin!(read);
    let mut received = false;
    loop {
        tokio::select! {
            biased;
            result = &mut read, if !received => {
                received = true;
                if let Some(execution) = execution_reply(result) {
                    return execution;
                }
            }
            result = child.wait() => {
                if result.is_ok() {
                    // Reaping and pipe EOF can become ready together. Consume
                    // the final reply before rejecting a very short game.
                    if !received
                        && let Ok(result) = tokio::time::timeout(
                            Duration::from_millis(100), &mut read,
                        ).await
                        && let Some(execution) = execution_reply(result)
                    {
                        return execution;
                    }
                    return Execution::ExitedUnconfirmed;
                }
                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100)).await;
            }
            _ = tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(25)) => {
                if observing.elapsed() >= Duration::from_secs(3)
                    && pid.and_then(&inspect).is_some_and(|identity| {
                        Some(Path::new(&identity.executable)) == expected.as_deref()
                    })
                {
                    return Execution::Started;
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

fn execution_reply(result: io::Result<Vec<u8>>) -> Option<Execution> {
    match result {
        Ok(bytes) if bytes.is_empty() => Some(Execution::Started),
        Ok(bytes) if bytes == crate::protocol::EXEC_FAILED => Some(Execution::Failed),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Never persist an architecture helper as the running game's identity.
pub(crate) async fn wait_identity(
    child: &mut Child,
    executable: &Path,
    inspect: impl Fn(u32) -> Option<Identity>,
) -> Option<Identity> {
    let pid = child.id()?;
    let expected = executable.canonicalize().ok()?;
    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(1);
    loop {
        if let Some(identity) = inspect(pid)
            && Path::new(&identity.executable) == expected
        {
            return Some(identity);
        }
        tokio::select! {
            result = child.wait() => {
                if result.is_ok() {
                    return None;
                }
            }
            _ = tokio::time::sleep_until(deadline) => return None,
            _ = tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(5)) => (),
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::{
        process::Stdio,
        sync::{
            Arc,
            atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering},
        },
    };

    fn child(script: &str, output: bool) -> Child {
        tokio::process::Command::new("/bin/sh")
            .args(["-c", script])
            .stdin(Stdio::null())
            .stdout(if output {
                Stdio::piped()
            } else {
                Stdio::null()
            })
            .stderr(Stdio::null())
            .kill_on_drop(false)
            .spawn()
            .unwrap()
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn pipe_confirmation_precedes_actual_exit_and_keeps_runtime_available() {
        let mut game = child("exec 1>/dev/null; sleep 0.1; exit 7", true);
        assert_eq!(
            confirm_execution(&mut game, Path::new("/bin/sh"), |_| None).await,
            Execution::Started
        );
        assert!(game.try_wait().unwrap().is_none());
        let progressed = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
        let progress = progressed.clone();
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
            progress.store(true, Ordering::Release);
        });
        assert_eq!(wait_for_exit(&mut game).await.code(), Some(7));
        assert!(progressed.load(Ordering::Acquire));
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn explicit_exec_failure_and_missing_confirmation_remain_distinct() {
        let mut failed = child("printf 'exec-failed\\n'; exit 126", true);
        assert_eq!(
            confirm_execution(&mut failed, Path::new("/bin/sh"), |_| None).await,
            Execution::Failed
        );
        assert_eq!(wait_for_exit(&mut failed).await.code(), Some(126));
        let mut unknown = child("exit 0", false);
        assert_eq!(
            confirm_execution(&mut unknown, Path::new("/bin/sh"), |_| None).await,
            Execution::ExitedUnconfirmed
        );
        assert_eq!(wait_for_exit(&mut unknown).await.code(), Some(0));
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn unknown_reply_does_not_release_a_live_child() {
        let mut game = child("printf unknown; exec 1>/dev/null; sleep 0.1; exit 4", true);
        let start = Instant::now();
        assert_eq!(
            confirm_execution(&mut game, Path::new("/bin/sh"), |_| None).await,
            Execution::ExitedUnconfirmed
        );
        assert!(start.elapsed() >= Duration::from_millis(80));
        assert_eq!(wait_for_exit(&mut game).await.code(), Some(4));
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn helper_identity_is_never_published_as_the_game() {
        let mut game = child("sleep 0.1", false);
        let identity = wait_identity(&mut game, Path::new("/bin/sh"), |pid| {
            Some(Identity {
                pid,
                uid: 0,
                birth_seconds: 1,
                birth_microseconds: 0,
                executable: "/not-the-game".into(),
            })
        })
        .await;
        assert!(identity.is_none());
        assert_eq!(wait_for_exit(&mut game).await.code(), Some(0));
    }
}
```

`crates/game-runtime/src/supervisor/client.rs`:

```rs
//! The UI's side of a Game session: starting or recovering its supervisor,
//! observing it and sending it commands. Dropping a client only detaches; it
//! never owns or stops a game.
use super::*;
use std::{
    fs,
    marker::PhantomData,
    os::fd::OwnedFd,
    os::unix::{
        fs::{MetadataExt, PermissionsExt},
        net::UnixStream,
    },
    path::Path,
    process::{Command as Process, Stdio},
    sync::Mutex,
    time::{Duration, Instant},
};

pub(crate) type Probe = fn(&Path, u32) -> Result<Option<Identity>, Error>;

/// Every native failure and uncertain observation is paced here, including
/// failures before a valid record exists. The UI owns presentation, not
/// transport retry policy.
const PACE: Duration = Duration::from_millis(500);

pub struct Client<P: Provider> {
    root: PathBuf,
    helper: PathBuf,
    id: String,
    probe: Probe,
    last: Mutex<Option<Record<P>>>,
}

/// Answers whether the Game session with this ID still owns a process.
pub(crate) type SessionAlive<'a> = dyn Fn(&str) -> Result<bool, Error> + Sync + 'a;

/// No other Game session holds the saves.
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) fn no_other_session(_: &str) -> Result<bool, Error> {
    Ok(false)
}

/// A storefront's `owner.lock`, held: no other supervisor of that storefront
/// is alive.
pub struct OwnerLock<P> {
    _file: fs::File,
    root: PathBuf,
    provider: PhantomData<P>,
}
impl<P: Provider> OwnerLock<P> {
    pub(crate) fn take(root: &Path) -> Result<Self, Error> {
        Ok(Self {
            _file: storage::lock(root, "owner.lock")?,
            root: root.into(),
            provider: PhantomData,
        })
    }

    /// With no other supervisor alive, a session without a record is dead: it
    /// was never accepted, or a previous build launched it.
    pub(crate) fn session_alive(
        &self,
        id: &str,
        inspect: impl Fn(u32) -> Result<Option<Identity>, Error>,
    ) -> Result<bool, Error> {
        match journal::by_id::<Record<P>>(&self.root, id)? {
            Some(record) if !record.finished() => {
                Ok(record.liveness(inspect)? != ownership::Liveness::Dead)
            }
            _ => Ok(false),
        }
    }
}

/// Excludes a storefront's launch admission while Cloud maintenance runs in
/// Obelisk, including stores left by a dead supervisor. Construction checks the
/// kernel identities of the recorded supervisor and game.
pub struct IdleGuard<P> {
    _starting: fs::File,
    owner: OwnerLock<P>,
    helper: PathBuf,
    probe: Probe,
}
impl<P: Provider> IdleGuard<P> {
    pub(crate) fn session_alive(&self, id: &str) -> Result<bool, Error> {
        self.owner
            .session_alive(id, |pid| (self.probe)(&self.helper, pid))
    }
}

impl<P: Provider> Client<P> {
    pub fn id(&self) -> &str {
        &self.id
    }

    pub fn idle_guard(root: &Path, helper: &Path) -> Result<IdleGuard<P>, P::Error> {
        Ok(Self::idle_guard_with(root, helper, inspect)?)
    }

    pub(crate) fn idle_guard_with(
        root: &Path,
        helper: &Path,
        probe: Probe,
    ) -> Result<IdleGuard<P>, Error> {
        let starting = storage::lock(root, "start.lock")?;
        let owner = OwnerLock::take(root)?;
        if let Some(saved) = journal::current::<Record<P>>(root)?
            && !saved.finished()
            && (ownership::alive(&saved.supervisor, |pid| probe(helper, pid))?
                || saved.liveness(|pid| probe(helper, pid))? != ownership::Liveness::Dead)
        {
            return Err(Error::Busy);
        }
        Ok(IdleGuard {
            _starting: starting,
            owner,
            helper: helper.into(),
            probe,
        })
    }

    pub fn recover(root: &Path, helper: &Path) -> Result<Option<Self>, P::Error> {
        Ok(paced(Self::recover_with(root, helper, inspect))?)
    }

    pub(crate) fn recover_with(
        root: &Path,
        helper: &Path,
        probe: Probe,
    ) -> Result<Option<Self>, Error> {
        let _starting = storage::lock(root, "start.lock")?;
        let Some(record) = journal::current::<Record<P>>(root)? else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let client = Self::new(root, helper, record.id, probe);
        let first = client.observe(None)?;
        if first.finished() {
            Ok(None)
        } else {
            *client.last.lock().unwrap() = Some(first);
            Ok(Some(client))
        }
    }

    fn new(root: &Path, helper: &Path, id: String, probe: Probe) -> Self {
        Self {
            root: root.into(),
            helper: helper.into(),
            id,
            probe,
            last: Mutex::new(None),
        }
    }

    pub fn snapshot(&self, after: Option<u64>) -> Result<Record<P>, P::Error> {
        let result = paced(self.observe(after));
        if let Ok(record) = &result {
            self.remember(record);
        }
        Ok(result?)
    }

    fn remember(&self, record: &Record<P>) {
        let mut last = self.last.lock().unwrap();
        if last
            .as_ref()
            .is_none_or(|old| old.revision <= record.revision)
        {
            *last = Some(record.clone());
        }
    }

    fn observe(&self, after: Option<u64>) -> Result<Record<P>, Error> {
        let disk = journal::by_id::<Record<P>>(&self.root, &self.id);
        let cached = self.last.lock().unwrap().clone();
        let saved = match (disk, cached) {
            (Ok(Some(saved)), Some(last)) if last.revision > saved.revision => last,
            (Ok(Some(saved)), _) => saved,
            (_, Some(last)) => last,
            (Err(error), None) => return Err(error),
            (Ok(None), None) => return Err(Error::Unavailable),
        };
        if saved.finished() {
            return Ok(saved);
        }
        // A failed inspection or RPC is uncertainty, not proof of the
        // supervisor's death. Keep the record and every guard while reconnecting.
        match self.observe_saved(saved.clone(), after) {
            Ok(record) => Ok(record),
            Err(_) => {
                std::thread::sleep(PACE);
                Ok(Record {
                    reconnecting: true,
                    ..saved
                })
            }
        }
    }

    fn observe_saved(&self, saved: Record<P>, after: Option<u64>) -> Result<Record<P>, Error> {
        // Socket permissions and the session UUID bind the connection to this
        // supervisor instance once its kernel identity matches.
        if ownership::alive(&saved.supervisor, |pid| (self.probe)(&self.helper, pid))? {
            let response = exchange(
                &saved,
                &Command::<P>::Observe {
                    id: self.id.clone(),
                    after,
                },
            );
            if response.is_err()
                && let Some(last) = journal::by_id::<Record<P>>(&self.root, &self.id)?
                && last.finished()
            {
                return Ok(last);
            }
            return response;
        }
        // Only the supervisor writes the journal. A lost supervisor's record
        // is retired in memory, and only while no other supervisor can start.
        let _owner = storage::lock(&self.root, "owner.lock")?;
        let mut orphan = saved;
        orphan.reconnecting = false;
        orphan.revision += 1;
        match orphan.liveness(|pid| (self.probe)(&self.helper, pid))? {
            ownership::Liveness::Dead => {
                orphan.phase = Phase::Finished;
                orphan.exit_code = None;
                orphan.game = None;
                orphan.starting = None;
                orphan.rosetta = None;
                P::orphaned(&mut orphan, false);
            }
            ownership::Liveness::Owned => {
                // Supervisor loss preserves even a helper that has not replaced
                // itself yet. Never restart or cancel its accepted launch.
                P::orphaned(&mut orphan, true);
                if after.is_some() {
                    std::thread::sleep(PACE);
                }
            }
            ownership::Liveness::Unknown => return Err(Error::Busy),
        }
        Ok(orphan)
    }

    /// Best effort: a supervisor ignores Cancel once the game was spawned.
    pub fn cancel(&self) {
        if let Ok(Some(saved)) = journal::by_id::<Record<P>>(&self.root, &self.id)
            && !saved.finished()
            && ownership::alive(&saved.supervisor, |pid| (self.probe)(&self.helper, pid))
                .unwrap_or(false)
        {
            let _ = exchange(
                &saved,
                &Command::<P>::Cancel {
                    id: self.id.clone(),
                },
            );
        }
    }

    /// Ends the game, which gets a few seconds to quit before it is killed;
    /// its exit Cloud sync still runs. Before spawn it cancels preparation.
    pub fn stop(&self) -> Result<(), P::Error> {
        self.end(Command::<P>::Stop {
            id: self.id.clone(),
        })
    }

    /// The player's Quit: the game is asked to close its windows, and nothing
    /// is killed. Before spawn it cancels preparation.
    pub fn quit(&self) -> Result<(), P::Error> {
        self.end(Command::<P>::Quit {
            id: self.id.clone(),
        })
    }

    /// The player's Force Quit: the game ends now, with whatever still runs
    /// for its installation; its exit Cloud sync still runs. Before spawn it
    /// cancels preparation.
    pub fn force_quit(&self) -> Result<(), P::Error> {
        self.end(Command::<P>::ForceQuit {
            id: self.id.clone(),
        })
    }

    fn end(&self, command: Command<P>) -> Result<(), P::Error> {
        self.command(None, command, false)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// The player's `control` of the running game. Refused before the game
    /// runs, once it exited, and for another account.
    pub fn control(&self, account_id: &P::Account, control: P::Control) -> Result<(), P::Error> {
        let command = Command::<P>::Control {
            id: self.id.clone(),
            account_id: account_id.clone(),
            control,
        };
        self.command(Some(account_id), command, true)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Opens a supervisor's start gate. Begin is idempotent, so a lost request
    /// is retried while the supervisor lives, instead of silently expiring.
    pub fn begin(&self) -> Result<(), P::Error> {
        // As long as the supervisor itself waits for it.
        let deadline = Instant::now() + super::session::BEGIN_DEADLINE;
        loop {
            let saved =
                journal::by_id::<Record<P>>(&self.root, &self.id)?.ok_or(Error::Unavailable)?;
            let command = Command::<P>::Begin {
                id: self.id.clone(),
                account_id: saved.account_id.clone(),
            };
            match self.command(None, command, false) {
                Ok(_) => return Ok(()),
                Err(Error::InvalidSession) => return Err(Error::InvalidSession.into()),
                Err(error) if Instant::now() >= deadline => return Err(error.into()),
                Err(_) => std::thread::sleep(PACE),
            }
        }
    }

    pub fn choose(
        &self,
        account_id: &P::Account,
        decision_id: u64,
        choice: crate::cloud::Choice,
    ) -> Result<(), P::Error> {
        let command = Command::<P>::CloudChoice {
            id: self.id.clone(),
            account_id: account_id.clone(),
            decision_id,
            choice,
        };
        self.command(Some(account_id), command, true)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn revoke(&self, account_id: &P::Account) -> Result<(), P::Error> {
        let command = Command::<P>::Revoke {
            id: self.id.clone(),
            account_id: account_id.clone(),
        };
        self.command(Some(account_id), command, false)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn resume_after_rosetta(
        &self,
        account_id: &P::Account,
        decision_id: u64,
    ) -> Result<(), P::Error> {
        let command = Command::<P>::ResumeAfterRosetta {
            id: self.id.clone(),
            account_id: account_id.clone(),
            decision_id,
        };
        let response = self.command(Some(account_id), command, true)?;
        if response.rosetta.is_some() {
            return Err(Error::RosettaUnavailable.into());
        }
        if response.finished() && response.phase != Phase::Finished {
            return Err(Error::InvalidSession.into());
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// An answer to a terminal session is refused, so a stale answer never
    /// reads as accepted. Other commands to it have nothing left to do.
    pub(super) fn command(
        &self,
        account_id: Option<&P::Account>,
        command: Command<P>,
        answer: bool,
    ) -> Result<Record<P>, Error> {
        let saved = journal::by_id::<Record<P>>(&self.root, &self.id)?.ok_or(Error::Unavailable)?;
        if account_id.is_some_and(|account_id| *account_id != saved.account_id) {
            return Err(Error::InvalidSession);
        }
        if saved.finished() {
            return if answer {
                Err(Error::InvalidSession)
            } else {
                Ok(saved)
            };
        }
        if !ownership::alive(&saved.supervisor, |pid| (self.probe)(&self.helper, pid))? {
            return Err(Error::InvalidSession);
        }
        let response = exchange(&saved, &command)?;
        self.remember(&response);
        Ok(response)
    }

    /// The default supervisor command: the storefront's helper subcommand
    /// with an empty environment.
    pub(crate) fn supervisor_command(helper: &Path) -> Process {
        let mut command = Process::new(helper);
        command
            .arg(P::SUPERVISE)
            .env_clear()
            .env("PATH", "/usr/bin:/bin");
        command
    }

    /// Spawns a supervisor and hands it the launch. `handoff` writes the
    /// storefront's request, including any credentials, to the private pipe;
    /// `acknowledges` checks that the reply describes that launch.
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub(crate) fn start_with(
        root: &Path,
        helper: &Path,
        id: String,
        mut command: Process,
        probe: Probe,
        handoff: impl FnOnce(&mut UnixStream) -> Result<(), Error>,
        acknowledges: impl Fn(&Record<P>) -> bool,
        cancelled: impl Fn() -> bool,
    ) -> Result<Self, Error> {
        let starting = storage::lock(root, "start.lock")?;
        if let Some(saved) = journal::current::<Record<P>>(root)? {
            let old = Self::new(root, helper, saved.id, probe);
            if !paced(old.observe(None))?.finished() {
                return Err(Error::Busy);
            }
        }
        // Even an absent record must not permit racing an owner that is
        // publishing its first state. A supervisor holds owner.lock for life.
        let _starting = storage::owner_released(root, starting)?;
        if cancelled() {
            return Err(Error::Cancelled);
        }
        // A private duplex pipe carries the request on stdin and one
        // acknowledgement on stderr. Neither reaches a log file.
        let (mut pipe, child_pipe) = UnixStream::pair()?;
        pipe.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(15)))?;
        pipe.set_write_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(3)))?;
        let mut child = command
            .stdin(Stdio::from(OwnedFd::from(child_pipe.try_clone()?)))
            .stdout(Stdio::null())
            .stderr(Stdio::from(OwnedFd::from(child_pipe)))
            .spawn()
            .map_err(|_| Error::StartFailed)?;
        drop(command);
        let client = Self::new(root, helper, id, probe);
        let result = handoff(&mut pipe).and_then(|()| {
            let acknowledged = storage::packet::<Record<P>>(&pipe).and_then(|ack| {
                if ack.id != client.id
                    || ack.supervisor.pid != child.id()
                    || !acknowledges(&ack)
                    || !ownership::alive(&ack.supervisor, |pid| probe(helper, pid))?
                {
                    return Err(Error::InvalidSession);
                }
                Ok(())
            });
            // An accepted launch survives a lost reply, including a UI crash:
            // its durable record and authenticated socket stay recoverable.
            if let Err(error) = acknowledged {
                match journal::by_id::<Record<P>>(root, &client.id)? {
                    Some(_) => drop(paced(client.observe(None))?),
                    None => return Err(error),
                }
            }
            if cancelled() {
                client.cancel();
            }
            Ok(())
        });
        // Reap while this UI exists. Parent exit reparents the supervisor;
        // none of its stdio stays attached to Obelisk after the handoff.
        std::thread::spawn(move || {
            let _ = child.wait();
        });
        result.map(|()| client)
    }
}

fn exchange<P: Provider>(saved: &Record<P>, command: &Command<P>) -> Result<Record<P>, Error> {
    let parent = saved.socket.parent().ok_or(Error::InvalidSession)?;
    let metadata = fs::symlink_metadata(parent)?;
    if !metadata.file_type().is_dir()
        || metadata.uid() != saved.supervisor.uid
        || metadata.permissions().mode() & 0o077 != 0
    {
        return Err(Error::InvalidSession);
    }
    let mut stream = UnixStream::connect(&saved.socket)?;
    stream.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(20)))?;
    stream.set_write_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(3)))?;
    storage::send_command(&mut stream, command)?;
    let response: Record<P> = storage::packet(stream)?;
    if response.id != saved.id
        || response.account_id != saved.account_id
        || !P::same_game(&response.store, &saved.store)
        || !ownership::same_process(&saved.supervisor, &response.supervisor)
    {
        return Err(Error::InvalidSession);
    }
    Ok(response)
}

pub(crate) fn inspect(helper: &Path, pid: u32) -> Result<Option<Identity>, Error> {
    let output = Process::new(helper)
        .arg("process-identity")
        .arg(pid.to_string())
        .env_clear()
        .stdin(Stdio::null())
        .stderr(Stdio::null())
        .output()?;
    if !output.status.success() || output.stdout.len() > 8192 {
        return Err(Error::Unavailable);
    }
    serde_json::from_slice(&output.stdout).map_err(|_| Error::InvalidSession)
}

fn paced<T>(result: Result<T, Error>) -> Result<T, Error> {
    if result.is_err() {
        std::thread::sleep(PACE);
    }
    result
}
```

```rs
    let table: Vec<Identity> =

struct Fixture<P: Provider> {
    _root: tempfile::TempDir,
    sessions: PathBuf,
    helper: PathBuf,
    record: Record<P>,
}
impl<P: Sample> Fixture<P> {
    fn new(phase: Phase, game: Option<Identity>, live: &[Identity]) -> Self {
        let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let sessions = root.path().join("sessions");
        crate::files::private_directory(&sessions).unwrap();
        let record = Record::<P> {
            version: journal::VERSION,
            id: uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
            account_id: P::account(),
            store: P::store(),
            phase,
            cloud: Default::default(),
            exit_code: None,
            played: None,
            error: None,
            failure_reason: None,
            revision: 1,
            rosetta: None,
            reconnecting: false,
            supervisor: process(SUPERVISOR),
            game,
            starting: None,
            socket: root.path().join("unused-socket"),
        };
        journal::write(&sessions, &record).unwrap();
        let helper = root.path().join("process-table.json");
        let fixture = Self {
            _root: root,
            sessions,
            helper,
            record,
        };
        fixture.live(live);
        fixture
    }

    fn starting(live: &[Identity]) -> Self {
        let mut fixture = Self::new(Phase::Preparing, None, live);
        fixture.record.starting = Some(starting_process());
        journal::write(&fixture.sessions, &fixture.record).unwrap();
        fixture
    }

    fn live(&self, live: &[Identity]) {
        fs::write(&self.helper, serde_json::to_vec(live).unwrap()).unwrap();
    }

    fn guard(&self) -> Result<IdleGuard<P>, Error> {
        Client::<P>::idle_guard_with(&self.sessions, &self.helper, inspect_table)
    }

    fn recover(&self) -> Result<Option<Client<P>>, Error> {
        Client::<P>::recover_with(&self.sessions, &self.helper, inspect_table)
    }

    fn client(&self, probe: Probe) -> Client<P> {
        Client::new(&self.sessions, &self.helper, self.record.id.clone(), probe)
    }

    /// A launch that must be refused before any supervisor is spawned.
    fn start(&self) -> Result<Client<P>, Error> {
        Client::<P>::start_with(
            &self.sessions,
            &self.helper,
            uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
            Process::new("/obelisk-no-supervisor-fixture"),
            inspect_table,
            |_| panic!("a refused launch never hands anything over"),
            |_| false,
            || false,
        )
    }

    /// A concurrently spawned test process can briefly hold an inherited
    /// lock descriptor; wait for it rather than racing it.
    fn settled(&self) -> &Self {
        crate::tests::wait_for_lock_release(&self.sessions.join("start.lock"));
        crate::tests::wait_for_lock_release(&self.sessions.join("owner.lock"));
        self
    }
}

    StartingGame::Process {
        identity: process(GAME),
        executable: "/disposable/intended-game".into(),
    }

fn replaced(mut identity: Identity) -> Identity {
    identity.executable = "/disposable/another-binary".into();

fn a_live_supervisor_or_game_reserves_the_session<P: Sample>() {
    for (phase, game, live) in [
        (Phase::Finalizing, None, vec![process(SUPERVISOR)]),
        (Phase::Running, Some(process(GAME)), vec![process(GAME)]),
    ] {
        let fixture = Fixture::<P>::new(phase, game, &live);
        assert!(matches!(fixture.guard(), Err(Error::Busy)));
        // A refused guard releases both locks it took.
        fixture.settled();
    }
}

fn a_starting_helper_or_its_replacement_outlives_its_supervisor<P: Sample>() {
    for live in [process(GAME), replaced(process(GAME))] {
        let fixture = Fixture::<P>::starting(&[live]);
        assert!(matches!(fixture.guard(), Err(Error::Busy)));
        let client = fixture
            .settled()
            .recover()
            .unwrap()
            .expect("an accepted helper stays recoverable without its supervisor");
        let orphan = client.snapshot(None).unwrap();
        assert!(!orphan.finished());
        assert_eq!(orphan.starting, Some(starting_process()));
        assert!(matches!(fixture.settled().start(), Err(Error::Busy)));

        // Only a fresh negative inspection releases the orphan, in memory:
        // nothing but a supervisor writes the journal.
        let before = fs::read(
            fixture
                .sessions
                .join(format!("{}.v2.json", fixture.record.id)),
        );
        fixture.live(&[]);
        let finished = client.snapshot(Some(orphan.revision)).unwrap();
        assert!(finished.finished());
        assert!(finished.starting.is_none());
        let after = fs::read(
            fixture
                .sessions
                .join(format!("{}.v2.json", fixture.record.id)),
        );
        assert_eq!(before.unwrap(), after.unwrap());
        drop(fixture.settled().guard().unwrap());
    }
}

fn a_reused_pid_releases_the_old_game_but_an_exec_replacement_does_not<P: Sample>() {
    for change in 0..3 {
        let mut live = vec![process(SUPERVISOR), process(GAME)];
        for identity in &mut live {
            match change {
                0 => identity.birth_seconds += 1,
                1 => identity.birth_microseconds += 1,
                _ => identity.uid += 1,
            }
        }
        let fixture = Fixture::<P>::new(Phase::Running, Some(process(GAME)), &live);
        assert!(fixture.recover().unwrap().is_none(), "change {change}");
        drop(fixture.settled().guard().unwrap());
    }
    let fixture = Fixture::<P>::new(
        Phase::Running,
        Some(process(GAME)),
        &[replaced(process(GAME))],
    );
    assert!(matches!(fixture.guard(), Err(Error::Busy)));
    assert!(fixture.settled().recover().unwrap().is_some());
}

fn a_failed_inspection_keeps_the_reservation<P: Sample>() {
    fn failed_child(helper: &Path, pid: u32) -> Result<Option<Identity>, Error> {
        if pid == GAME {
            Err(Error::Unavailable)
        } else {
            inspect_table(helper, pid)
        }
    }
    let fixture = Fixture::<P>::starting(&[]);
    assert!(matches!(
        Client::<P>::idle_guard_with(&fixture.sessions, &fixture.helper, failed_child),
        Err(Error::Unavailable)
    ));
    let client =
        Client::<P>::recover_with(&fixture.settled().sessions, &fixture.helper, failed_child)
            .unwrap()
            .unwrap();
    let snapshot = client.snapshot(None).unwrap();
    assert!(!snapshot.finished());
    assert!(snapshot.reconnecting);
    assert_eq!(snapshot.starting, Some(starting_process()));
}

fn the_maintenance_guard_excludes_maintenance_and_launch_until_dropped<P: Sample>() {

            storage::lock(&fixture.sessions, name),
            Err(Error::Busy)

fn commands_check_the_account_and_the_supervisor_before_sending<P: Sample>() {
    let fixture = Fixture::<P>::new(Phase::Preparing, None, &[]);
    let client = fixture.client(must_not_probe);
    assert!(matches!(
        client.command(
            Some(&P::other_account()),
            Command::Revoke {
                id: fixture.record.id.clone(),
                account_id: P::other_account(),
            },
            false,
        ),
        Err(Error::InvalidSession)
    ));

    let mut replacement = fixture.record.clone();
    replacement.id = uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string();
    journal::write(&fixture.sessions, &replacement).unwrap();
    fs::copy(
        fixture.sessions.join(format!("{}.v2.json", replacement.id)),
        fixture
            .sessions
            .join(format!("{}.v2.json", fixture.record.id)),
    )
    .unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(
        client.command(
            Some(&P::account()),
            Command::Revoke {
                id: fixture.record.id.clone(),
                account_id: P::account(),
            },
            false,
        ),
        Err(Error::InvalidSession)
    ));

    // A recycled supervisor PID is never sent a command.
    let fixture = Fixture::<P>::new(Phase::Preparing, None, &[replaced_birth()]);
    let client = fixture.client(inspect_table);
    for answer in [false, true] {
        let command = if answer {
            Command::CloudChoice {
                id: fixture.record.id.clone(),
                account_id: P::account(),
                decision_id: 7,
                choice: crate::cloud::Choice::Local,
            }
        } else {
            Command::Revoke {
                id: fixture.record.id.clone(),
                account_id: P::account(),
            }
        };
        assert!(matches!(
            client.command(Some(&P::account()), command, answer),
            Err(Error::InvalidSession)
        ));
    }
}

fn replaced_birth() -> Identity {
    let mut supervisor = process(SUPERVISOR);
    supervisor.birth_seconds += 1;
    supervisor
}

fn a_game_guard_session_is_alive_only_while_it_owns_a_process<P: Sample>() {
    let fixture = Fixture::<P>::new(Phase::Running, Some(process(GAME)), &[process(GAME)]);
    let guard = fixture.guard_after_supervisor_loss();
    assert!(guard.session_alive(&fixture.record.id).unwrap());
    fixture.live(&[]);
    assert!(!guard.session_alive(&fixture.record.id).unwrap());
    // A session that never produced a current record, such as one launched by
    // a previous build, is dead once no supervisor of this storefront runs.
    assert!(
        !guard
            .session_alive(&uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string())
            .unwrap()
    );
    drop(guard);

    let unknown = Fixture::<P>::new(Phase::Running, None, &[]);
    let owner = OwnerLock::<P>::take(&unknown.sessions).unwrap();
    assert!(
        owner
            .session_alive(&unknown.record.id, |_| Ok(None))
            .unwrap(),
        "a running record without a process cannot be proven dead"
    );
}

impl<P: Sample> Fixture<P> {
    /// The guard refuses a live game, so model a session whose supervisor and
    /// game were both inspected dead when the guard was taken, then check the
    /// question maintenance asks about the vault's recorded session.
    fn guard_after_supervisor_loss(&self) -> IdleGuard<P> {
        let live = fs::read(&self.helper).unwrap();
        self.live(&[]);
        let guard = self.guard().unwrap();
        fs::write(&self.helper, live).unwrap();
        guard
    }
}

#[test]
fn an_owner_wait_that_times_out_keeps_other_starters_out() {
    let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let owner = storage::lock(root.path(), "owner.lock").unwrap();
    let starting = storage::lock(root.path(), "start.lock").unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(
        storage::owner_released(root.path(), starting),
        Err(Error::Busy)
    ));
    assert!(matches!(
        storage::lock(root.path(), "start.lock"),
        Err(Error::Busy)
    ));
    drop(owner);
    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(2);
    while storage::lock(root.path(), "start.lock").is_err() {
        assert!(Instant::now() < deadline);
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10));
    }
}
```

`crates/game-runtime/src/supervisor/exec.rs`:

```rs
//! Exec admission. The supervisor spawns an exec helper, records that process
//! as the Game session's durable `starting` ownership, then admits it with one
//! message on its stdin. The helper becomes the game only after a complete
//! message: losing the supervisor first closes the pipe and prevents exec.
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::{
    io::{self, BufRead, Read, Write},
    os::unix::process::CommandExt,
    path::PathBuf,
    process::{Command, Stdio},
};

/// The game to become. Its environment is the helper's own, set when the
/// supervisor spawned it, so exec passes it on verbatim.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Admission {
    pub executable: PathBuf,
    pub arguments: Vec<String>,
    pub working_directory: PathBuf,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub log: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// What the log starts with, before the game writes to it.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub log_header: Option<String>,
}

/// Game arguments are bounded like the kernel's ARG_MAX, not like a record.
const MAX: u64 = 1024 * 1024;

pub fn send(output: &mut impl Write, admission: &Admission) -> io::Result<()> {
    let mut bytes = serde_json::to_vec(admission).map_err(io::Error::other)?;
    bytes.push(b'\n');
    if bytes.len() as u64 > MAX {
        return Err(io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput.into());
    }
    output.write_all(&bytes)?;
    output.flush()
}

/// Reads one complete admission. A truncated or unbounded message, or a
/// relative path, is refused.
pub fn receive(input: impl Read) -> io::Result<Admission> {
    let mut bytes = Vec::new();
    io::BufReader::new(input.take(MAX + 1)).read_until(b'\n', &mut bytes)?;
    if bytes.len() as u64 > MAX || bytes.last() != Some(&b'\n') {
        return Err(io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput.into());
    }
    let admission: Admission =
        serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).map_err(|_| io::Error::from(io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput))?;
    if !admission.executable.is_absolute()
        || !admission.working_directory.is_absolute()
        || admission.log.as_ref().is_some_and(|log| !log.is_absolute())
    {
        return Err(io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput.into());
    }
    Ok(admission)
}

/// The game's standard error: its log, emptied for this launch and started
/// with its header, or nothing.
pub fn standard_error(admission: &Admission) -> io::Result<Stdio> {
    let Some(log) = &admission.log else {
        return Ok(Stdio::null());
    };
    let mut log = crate::diagnostics::open_log(log)?;
    if let Some(header) = &admission.log_header {
        log.write_all(header.as_bytes())?;
    }
    Ok(log.into())
}

/// The arm64 helper. `std` exec restores the default SIGPIPE disposition
/// that the Rust runtime ignores, and leaves the environment untouched.
pub fn game_exec(input: impl Read) -> io::Result<()> {
    crate::protocol::exec_or_report(|| exec(input))
}

fn exec(input: impl Read) -> io::Result<()> {
    let admission = receive(input)?;
    Err(Command::new(&admission.executable)
        .args(&admission.arguments)
        .current_dir(&admission.working_directory)
        .stdin(Stdio::null())
        .stdout(Stdio::null())
        .stderr(standard_error(&admission)?)
        .exec())
}
```
