`crates/game-runtime/src/supervisor/journal.rs`:

```rs
//! Durable Game session records, one private directory per storefront.
//!
//! `session.v2.json` only names the current session; `<id>.v2.json` holds its
//! record. A launch writes the name first and its record last, so a record
//! exists only once the whole initial write succeeded. Older builds' files use
//! other names and are never opened.
use super::Error;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize, de::DeserializeOwned};
use std::{
    fs::{self, File},
    io::Read,
    os::unix::fs::{MetadataExt, PermissionsExt},
    path::Path,
};

/// The record and command protocol this build writes and understands.
pub(crate) const VERSION: u32 = 2;
const CURRENT: &str = "session.v2.json";
const MAX: u64 = 64 * 1024;

pub(crate) trait Entry: Serialize + DeserializeOwned {
    fn id(&self) -> &str;
    /// Storefront-specific checks beyond the shared identity checks.
    fn valid(&self) -> bool;
}

#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct Current {
    version: u32,
    id: String,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct Header {
    version: u32,
}

fn record_name(id: &str) -> Result<String, Error> {
    uuid::Uuid::parse_str(id).map_err(|_| Error::InvalidSession)?;
    Ok(format!("{id}.v2.json"))
}

/// The current session's record, or `None` when no launch was accepted.
pub(crate) fn current<T: Entry>(root: &Path) -> Result<Option<T>, Error> {
    match read::<Current>(&root.join(CURRENT))? {
        Some(current) => by_id(root, &current.id),
        None => Ok(None),
    }
}

pub(crate) fn by_id<T: Entry>(root: &Path, id: &str) -> Result<Option<T>, Error> {
    let Some(entry) = read::<T>(&root.join(record_name(id)?))? else {
        return Ok(None);
    };
    if entry.id() != id {
        return Err(Error::InvalidSession);
    }
    if !entry.valid() {
        return Err(Error::Storage);
    }
    Ok(Some(entry))
}

/// Names the session current first, then writes its record.
pub(crate) fn write<T: Entry>(root: &Path, entry: &T) -> Result<(), Error> {
    let name = record_name(entry.id())?;
    let path = root.join(CURRENT);
    if read::<Current>(&path)
        .ok()
        .flatten()
        .is_none_or(|current| current.id != entry.id())
    {
        replace(
            &path,
            &Current {
                version: VERSION,
                id: entry.id().into(),
            },
        )?;
    }
    replace(&root.join(name), entry)
}

fn read<T: DeserializeOwned>(path: &Path) -> Result<Option<T>, Error> {
    let before = match fs::symlink_metadata(path) {
        Ok(metadata) if metadata.file_type().is_file() => metadata,
        Ok(_) => return Err(Error::Storage),
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(None),
        Err(_) => return Err(Error::Storage),
    };
    let file = File::open(path).map_err(|_| Error::Storage)?;
    // Check the opened file: an atomic writer may have replaced the path.
    let opened = file.metadata().map_err(|_| Error::Storage)?;
    let directory =
        fs::metadata(path.parent().ok_or(Error::Storage)?).map_err(|_| Error::Storage)?;
    if !opened.is_file()
        || (opened.dev(), opened.ino()) != (before.dev(), before.ino())
        || opened.uid() != directory.uid()
        || opened.permissions().mode() & 0o077 != 0
        || opened.len() > MAX
    {
        return Err(Error::Storage);
    }
    let mut bytes = Vec::new();
    file.take(MAX + 1)
        .read_to_end(&mut bytes)
        .map_err(|_| Error::Storage)?;
    if bytes.len() as u64 > MAX {
        return Err(Error::Storage);
    }
    let header: Header = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).map_err(|_| Error::Storage)?;
    if header.version > VERSION {
        return Err(Error::NewerSession);
    }
    if header.version != VERSION {
        return Err(Error::Storage);
    }
    serde_json::from_slice(&bytes)
        .map(Some)
        .map_err(|_| Error::Storage)
}

fn replace(path: &Path, value: &impl Serialize) -> Result<(), Error> {
    let bytes = serde_json::to_vec(value).map_err(|_| Error::Storage)?;
    if bytes.len() as u64 > MAX
        || fs::symlink_metadata(path).is_ok_and(|metadata| !metadata.file_type().is_file())
    {
        return Err(Error::Storage);
    }
    let directory = path.parent().ok_or(Error::Storage)?;
    obelisk_core::write_atomic(path, &bytes).map_err(|_| Error::Storage)?;
    // Unlike write_atomic, recovery needs the rename itself durable.
    File::open(directory)
        .and_then(|directory| directory.sync_all())
        .map_err(|_| Error::Storage)
}
```

```rs
use super::*;
use std::os::unix::fs::symlink;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq)]
struct Record {
    version: u32,
    id: String,
    value: u32,
}
impl Entry for Record {
    fn id(&self) -> &str {
        &self.id
    }
    fn valid(&self) -> bool {
        self.value != 0
    }
}

fn record(value: u32) -> Record {
    Record {
        version: VERSION,
        id: uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
        value,
    }
}

fn directory() -> tempfile::TempDir {
    let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    fs::set_permissions(root.path(), fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o700)).unwrap();
    root
}

fn private(path: &Path, bytes: impl AsRef<[u8]>) {
    fs::write(path, bytes).unwrap();
    fs::set_permissions(path, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o600)).unwrap();
}

#[test]
fn a_written_session_is_current_and_readable_by_id() {
    let root = directory();
    assert!(current::<Record>(root.path()).unwrap().is_none());
    let first = record(1);
    write(root.path(), &first).unwrap();
    let second = record(2);
    write(root.path(), &second).unwrap();

    assert_eq!(
        current::<Record>(root.path()).unwrap(),
        Some(second.clone())
    );
    assert_eq!(
        by_id::<Record>(root.path(), &first.id).unwrap(),
        Some(first.clone())
    );
    for name in ["session.v2.json", &format!("{}.v2.json", second.id)] {
        let mode = fs::metadata(root.path().join(name))
            .unwrap()
            .permissions()
            .mode();
        assert_eq!(mode & 0o077, 0, "{name} is private");
    }
}

    let root = directory();
    let entry = record(1);
    write(root.path(), &entry).unwrap();
    let path = root.path().join(format!("{}.v2.json", entry.id));
    let saved = fs::read(&path).unwrap();

    assert!(matches!(
        by_id::<Record>(root.path(), &entry.id),
        Err(Error::Storage)
    ));

    let elsewhere = root.path().join("elsewhere");

    fs::remove_file(&path).unwrap();
    symlink(&elsewhere, &path).unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(
        by_id::<Record>(root.path(), &entry.id),
        Err(Error::Storage)

        Err(Error::Storage)
    ));

    private(&path, "not json");
    assert!(matches!(
        current::<Record>(root.path()),
        Err(Error::Storage)
    ));

    private(&path, serde_json::to_vec(&other).unwrap());
    assert!(matches!(
        by_id::<Record>(root.path(), &entry.id),

            value: 0,

        by_id::<Record>(root.path(), &entry.id),
        Err(Error::Storage)

#[test]
fn a_newer_record_is_an_unknown_live_session_and_unknown_fields_are_tolerated() {
    let root = directory();
    let entry = record(1);
    write(root.path(), &entry).unwrap();
    let path = root.path().join(format!("{}.v2.json", entry.id));

    let mut extended = serde_json::to_value(&entry).unwrap();
    extended["added_later"] = serde_json::json!({"any": ["shape"]});
    private(&path, serde_json::to_vec(&extended).unwrap());
    assert_eq!(current::<Record>(root.path()).unwrap(), Some(entry));

    extended["version"] = (VERSION + 1).into();
    extended["value"] = "changed type".into();
    private(&path, serde_json::to_vec(&extended).unwrap());
    assert!(matches!(
        current::<Record>(root.path()),
        Err(Error::NewerSession)
    ));

    extended["version"] = (VERSION - 1).into();
    private(&path, serde_json::to_vec(&extended).unwrap());
    assert!(matches!(
        current::<Record>(root.path()),
        Err(Error::Storage)
    ));
}

#[test]
fn a_refused_write_keeps_the_previous_record_and_leaves_no_temporary_file() {
    let root = directory();
    let mut entry = record(1);
    write(root.path(), &entry).unwrap();
    let names = || {
        let mut names: Vec<_> = fs::read_dir(root.path())
            .unwrap()
            .map(|entry| entry.unwrap().file_name())
            .collect();
        names.sort();
        names
    };
    let before = names();

    entry.value = 2;
    let path = root.path().join(format!("{}.v2.json", entry.id));
    let saved = fs::read(&path).unwrap();
    fs::remove_file(&path).unwrap();
    symlink(root.path().join("elsewhere"), &path).unwrap();
    assert!(
        write(root.path(), &entry).is_err(),
        "a link is never replaced"
    );
    fs::remove_file(&path).unwrap();
    private(&path, &saved);

    struct Huge(Record);
    impl Serialize for Huge {
        fn serialize<S: serde::Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
            let mut value = serde_json::to_value(&self.0).unwrap();
            value["padding"] = "x".repeat(MAX as usize).into();
            value.serialize(serializer)
        }
    }
    assert!(replace(&path, &Huge(entry.clone())).is_err());

    assert_eq!(names(), before);
    assert_eq!(
        by_id::<Record>(root.path(), &entry.id)
            .unwrap()
            .unwrap()
            .value,
        1
    );
}
```

```rs
/// Whether `path` is absolute and never climbs with `..`.
pub(crate) fn plain_absolute(path: &Path) -> bool {
    path.is_absolute() && !path.components().any(|c| c == Component::ParentDir)

/// The conversions a storefront's session `Error` makes from the
/// supervisor's and the runtime's errors, alike for Epic and GOG: its
/// `Session`, `Busy`, `Cancelled`, `Storage`, `Unsupported`, `NotNative`,
/// `RosettaUnavailable` and `WineUnavailable` stand for them.
macro_rules! session_error_conversions {
    ($error:ty) => {
        impl From<$crate::supervisor::Error> for $error {
            fn from(error: $crate::supervisor::Error) -> Self {
                use $crate::supervisor::Error as E;
                match error {
                    E::Storage => Self::Storage,
                    E::NewerSession | E::Busy => Self::Busy,
                    E::Cancelled => Self::Cancelled,
                    E::RosettaUnavailable => Self::RosettaUnavailable,
                    E::InvalidSession | E::Unavailable | E::StartFailed => Self::Session,
                }
            }
        }
        impl From<$crate::Error> for $error {
            fn from(error: $crate::Error) -> Self {
                match error {
                    $crate::Error::RosettaUnavailable => Self::RosettaUnavailable,
                    $crate::Error::WineUnavailable => Self::WineUnavailable,
                    $crate::Error::IncompatibleArchitecture => Self::NotNative,
                    $crate::Error::InvalidApplication | $crate::Error::NotExecutable => {
                        Self::Unsupported
                    }
                    _ => Self::Session,
                }
            }
        }
    };
}

/// What a storefront adds to the storefront-neutral supervisor.
pub trait Provider: Clone + std::fmt::Debug + PartialEq + Eq + Send + Sync + 'static {
    type Account: Clone
        + std::fmt::Debug
        + PartialEq
        + Eq
        + Serialize
        + DeserializeOwned
        + Send
        + Sync;
    /// What the session records about the storefront's game.
    type Store: Clone
        + std::fmt::Debug
        + PartialEq
        + Eq
        + Serialize
        + DeserializeOwned
        + Send
        + Sync;
    /// What the player may ask of the storefront's running game, such as
    /// accepting an invitation; `NoControl` when nothing.
    type Control: std::fmt::Debug + Serialize + DeserializeOwned + Send;
    /// The errors the storefront's callers expect. Core failures map into
    /// it; its display is a localization key.
    type Error: From<Error> + std::fmt::Debug + std::fmt::Display + Send;
    /// The helper subcommand that becomes this storefront's supervisor.
    const SUPERVISE: &'static str;
    /// Failure keys older helpers used for a cancellation.
    const CANCELLED: &'static [&'static str];

    fn valid(record: &Record<Self>) -> bool;
    /// Whether a failure is a cancellation, which ends a session silently.
    fn cancelled(error: &Self::Error) -> bool;
    /// Whether two records describe the same game; live facts may differ.
    fn same_game(a: &Self::Store, b: &Self::Store) -> bool;
    /// How a record whose supervisor is gone presents. `owned` means its game
    /// still runs; otherwise the record is already terminal.
    fn orphaned(record: &mut Record<Self>, owned: bool);
}

/// What a session's game did once it ran: for how long, how smoothly, how it
/// ended and what ran it. Obelisk reports it when the player shares game
/// performance.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Played {
    pub seconds: u64,
    pub frames: crate::metal_hud::Frames,
    /// Absent when a signal ended the game.
    pub exit_code: Option<i32>,
    pub exit_signal: Option<i32>,
    /// The player quit or stopped the game from Obelisk.
    pub ended_by_obelisk: bool,
    /// What ran a Windows game; absent for a Mac one.
    pub engine: Option<crate::wine::Engine>,
    /// The graphics backend a Windows game ran with, as its launch settings
    /// picked it; absent for a Mac one.
    pub graphics: Option<crate::wine::Graphics>,
    /// The Voile release a Windows game ran in.
    pub voile: Option<String>,
}

/// A Game session as its supervisor journals it. Ownership (the supervisor,
/// game, starting helper and socket) decides the Reservation.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[serde(bound = "")]
pub struct Record<P: Provider> {
    pub version: u32,
    pub id: String,
    pub account_id: P::Account,
    pub store: P::Store,
    pub phase: Phase,
    pub cloud: crate::cloud::Status,
    pub exit_code: Option<i32>,
    /// Set once the game ran and exited.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub played: Option<Played>,
    pub error: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub failure_reason: Option<FailureReason>,
    pub revision: u64,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub rosetta: Option<RosettaRequest>,
    /// Client-side confidence in the control connection, never persisted.
    #[serde(skip)]
    pub reconnecting: bool,
    pub supervisor: Identity,
    pub game: Option<Identity>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub starting: Option<StartingGame>,
    pub socket: PathBuf,
}
impl<P: Provider> Record<P> {
    /// Whether the game or starting process this record owns still lives.
    pub(crate) fn liveness(
        &self,
        inspect: impl Fn(u32) -> Result<Option<Identity>, Error>,
    ) -> Result<ownership::Liveness, Error> {
        ownership::owns_process(
            self.phase == Phase::Running,
            self.game.as_ref(),
            self.starting.as_ref(),
            inspect,
        )
    }
    /// Terminal only once its phase is final and it owns no process.
    pub fn finished(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self.phase, Phase::Finished | Phase::Failed)
            && self.game.is_none()
            && self.starting.is_none()
    }

    pub fn failure_reason(&self) -> Option<FailureReason> {
        if !self.finished() || self.phase != Phase::Failed {
            return None;
        }
        if let Some(reason) = self.failure_reason {
            return Some(reason);
        }
        // Records without a typed reason classify only the cancellation key.
        Some(match self.error.as_deref() {
            Some(error) if P::CANCELLED.contains(&error) => FailureReason::Cancelled,
            _ => FailureReason::Failed,
        })
    }
}
impl<P: Provider> journal::Entry for Record<P> {
    fn id(&self) -> &str {
        &self.id
    }
    fn valid(&self) -> bool {
        P::valid(self)
    }
}

/// The controls of a storefront that has none to offer.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]

/// Storefront-neutral supervisor failures. Each storefront maps them to its
/// own localization keys.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum Error {
    #[error("session storage failed")]
    Storage,
    #[error("invalid session")]
    InvalidSession,
    /// Written by a newer build: its process may be alive, so it stays reserved.
    #[error("session written by a newer build")]
    NewerSession,
    #[error("session busy")]
    Busy,
    #[error("supervisor unavailable")]
    Unavailable,
    #[error("cancelled")]
    Cancelled,
    #[error("supervisor start failed")]
    StartFailed,
    #[error("Rosetta unavailable")]
    RosettaUnavailable,
}
impl From<std::io::Error> for Error {
    fn from(_: std::io::Error) -> Self {
        Self::Storage
    }
}
impl From<Error> for crate::Error {
    fn from(error: Error) -> Self {
        match error {
            Error::Storage => Self::Storage,
            Error::InvalidSession => Self::InvalidSession,
            Error::NewerSession | Error::Busy => Self::SessionBusy,
            Error::Unavailable => Self::Unavailable,
            Error::Cancelled => Self::Cancelled,
            Error::StartFailed => Self::StartFailed,
            Error::RosettaUnavailable => Self::RosettaUnavailable,
        }
    }
}
```

`crates/game-runtime/src/supervisor/ownership.rs`:

```rs
//! Whether a Game session still owns a process. The recorded process is the
//! one whose PID, UID and kernel birth time still match: exec can replace a
//! game's executable without ending it, so the executable never decides.
use super::{Identity, StartingGame};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum Liveness {
    Dead,
    Owned,
    /// The record claims a running game it cannot name; keep its Reservation.
    Unknown,
}

pub(crate) fn same_process(recorded: &Identity, now: &Identity) -> bool {
    now.pid == recorded.pid
        && now.uid == recorded.uid
        && now.birth_seconds == recorded.birth_seconds
        && now.birth_microseconds == recorded.birth_microseconds
}

/// `inspect` proves absence with `Ok(None)`; a failed inspection is an error,
/// and uncertainty never releases anything.
pub(crate) fn alive<E>(
    recorded: &Identity,
    inspect: impl Fn(u32) -> Result<Option<Identity>, E>,
) -> Result<bool, E> {
    Ok(inspect(recorded.pid)?.is_some_and(|now| same_process(recorded, &now)))
}

/// The game, or the helper that becomes it, is still alive. `running` is the
/// recorded phase, before any terminal state.
pub(crate) fn owns_process<E>(
    running: bool,
    game: Option<&Identity>,
    starting: Option<&StartingGame>,
    inspect: impl Fn(u32) -> Result<Option<Identity>, E>,
) -> Result<Liveness, E> {
    if let Some(game) = game
        && alive(game, &inspect)?
    {
        return Ok(Liveness::Owned);
    }
    match starting {
        Some(StartingGame::Process { identity, .. }) if alive(identity, &inspect)? => {
            Ok(Liveness::Owned)
        }
        None if running && game.is_none() => Ok(Liveness::Unknown),
        _ => Ok(Liveness::Dead),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn process(pid: u32) -> Identity {
        Identity {
            pid,
            uid: 501,
            birth_seconds: 1_700_000_000,
            birth_microseconds: 250,
            executable: "/fixture/launcher".into(),
        }
    }

    fn table(live: Vec<Identity>) -> impl Fn(u32) -> Result<Option<Identity>, ()> {
        move |pid| Ok(live.iter().find(|identity| identity.pid == pid).cloned())
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_exec_replacement_is_still_the_recorded_process_but_a_reused_pid_is_not() {
        let recorded = process(42);
        let mut replaced = recorded.clone();
        replaced.executable = "/fixture/second-binary".into();
        assert!(alive(&recorded, table(vec![replaced])).unwrap());

        for change in 0..3 {
            let mut reused = recorded.clone();
            match change {
                0 => reused.birth_seconds += 1,
                1 => reused.birth_microseconds += 1,
                _ => reused.uid += 1,
            }
            assert!(
                !alive(&recorded, table(vec![reused])).unwrap(),
                "change {change}"
            );
        }
        assert!(!alive(&recorded, table(vec![])).unwrap());
        assert!(alive(&recorded, |_| Err::<Option<Identity>, _>("uncertain")).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_game_or_its_starting_helper_keeps_the_session_owned() {
        let game = process(42);
        let starting = StartingGame::Process {
            identity: process(43),
            executable: "/fixture/game".into(),
        };
        let owned = |game, starting, live| owns_process(true, game, starting, table(live));

        assert_eq!(
            owned(Some(&game), None, vec![game.clone()]),
            Ok(Liveness::Owned)
        );
        let mut exec = process(43);
        exec.executable = "/fixture/any-binary".into();
        assert_eq!(
            owned(None, Some(&starting), vec![exec]),
            Ok(Liveness::Owned)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            owned(Some(&game), Some(&starting), vec![]),
            Ok(Liveness::Dead)
        );
        assert_eq!(owned(None, None, vec![]), Ok(Liveness::Unknown));
        assert_eq!(
            owns_process(false, None, None, table(vec![])),
            Ok(Liveness::Dead)
        );
        assert!(
            owns_process(true, Some(&game), None, |_| Err::<Option<Identity>, _>(
                "uncertain"
            ))
            .is_err()
        );
    }
}
```

```rs
//! Force quitting a game for its player: the game, what it started, and what
//! still runs for its installation or its Wine prefix. A process ends only
//! when it runs this game's or Voile's files and uses this game's files, so
//! another game and Obelisk itself never end with it.
use crate::wine;
use std::{
    collections::HashMap,
    io::Read,
    path::{Path, PathBuf},
    process::{Command, Stdio},
    time::Duration,
};

/// A process listing still running after this long is abandoned.
const LISTING_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10);

/// What ending the spawned game needs to know of its launch.
pub(crate) struct Game {
    /// The environment the launch gave the game, before its host's own.
    pub environment: HashMap<String, String>,
    pub installation: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub program: Option<PathBuf>,
}

/// The processes a game may leave behind: they run files from one of `runs`,
/// use files under one of `uses`, and run nothing from `spared`.
#[derive(Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub(crate) struct Scope {
    runs: Vec<PathBuf>,
    uses: Vec<PathBuf>,
    spared: Vec<PathBuf>,
}

impl Scope {
    /// The scope of `game`, whose launch helper is `pid`, for a supervisor
    /// running `own`.
    pub(crate) fn of(
        game: &Game,
        wine: Option<&wine::Config>,
        pid: Option<u32>,
        own: &Path,
    ) -> Self {
        let mut scope = Self::default();
        if let Some(installation) = &game.installation {
            scope.runs.push(installation.clone());
            scope.uses.push(installation.clone());
        }
        if let Some(wine) = wine {
            scope.runs.push(wine.runtime.clone());
            scope
                .uses
                .extend(wine::private_folders(wine, &game.environment, pid));
        }
        scope.spared.push(bundle(own));
        // lsof names files by their real path, such as /private/tmp for /tmp.
        for paths in [&mut scope.runs, &mut scope.uses, &mut scope.spared] {
            let real: Vec<_> = paths
                .iter()
                .filter_map(|path| path.canonicalize().ok())
                .filter(|path| !paths.contains(path))
                .collect();
            paths.extend(real);
        }
        scope
    }
}

/// The application bundle `executable` belongs to, else its folder.
fn bundle(executable: &Path) -> PathBuf {
    executable
        .ancestors()
        .filter(|folder| {
            folder
                .extension()
                .is_some_and(|extension| extension == "app")
        })
        .last()
        .or(executable.parent())
        .unwrap_or(executable)
        .to_owned()
}

/// The processes of an `lsof -Fpfn` listing inside `scope`, except `own`.
pub(crate) fn matching(listing: &str, scope: &Scope, own: u32) -> Vec<u32> {
    #[derive(Default)]
    struct Seen {
        runs: bool,
        uses: bool,
        spared: bool,
    }
    fn settle(current: Option<(u32, Seen)>, own: u32, found: &mut Vec<u32>) {
        if let Some((pid, seen)) = current
            && seen.runs
            && seen.uses
            && !seen.spared
            && pid != own
            && !found.contains(&pid)
        {
            found.push(pid);
        }
    }
    let under = |path: &Path, roots: &[PathBuf]| roots.iter().any(|root| path.starts_with(root));
    let mut found = Vec::new();
    let mut current = None;
    // lsof lists what a process runs, its executable and libraries, as txt.
    let mut runs = false;
    for line in listing.lines() {
        if let Some(pid) = line.strip_prefix('p') {
            settle(current.take(), own, &mut found);
            current = pid.parse().ok().map(|pid| (pid, Seen::default()));
        } else if let Some(descriptor) = line.strip_prefix('f') {
            runs = descriptor == "txt";
        } else if let Some(name) = line.strip_prefix('n')
            && let Some((_, seen)) = &mut current
        {
            let path = Path::new(name);
            if runs {
                seen.runs |= under(path, &scope.runs);
                seen.spared |= under(path, &scope.spared);
            }
            seen.uses |= under(path, &scope.uses);
        }
    }
    settle(current, own, &mut found);
    found
}

/// Every descendant of `root` in a `ps -o pid=,ppid=` listing.
pub(crate) fn descendants(listing: &str, root: u32) -> Vec<u32> {
    let parents: Vec<(u32, u32)> = listing
        .lines()
        .filter_map(|line| {
            let mut fields = line.split_whitespace();
            Some((fields.next()?.parse().ok()?, fields.next()?.parse().ok()?))
        })
        .collect();
    let mut found = Vec::new();
    let mut pending = vec![root];
    while let Some(parent) = pending.pop() {
        for &(pid, ppid) in &parents {
            if ppid == parent && pid != root && !found.contains(&pid) {
                found.push(pid);
                pending.push(pid);
            }
        }
    }
    found
}

/// Everything the game's helper `pid` started, listed while it lives: once
/// it dies, they belong to launchd.
pub(crate) fn started_by(pid: u32) -> Vec<u32> {
    let mut command = Command::new("/bin/ps");
    command.args(["-axo", "pid=,ppid="]);
    listing(command)
        .map(|listing| descendants(&listing, pid))
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

/// Kills whatever still runs inside `scope`.
pub(crate) fn sweep(scope: &Scope) {
    let mut command = Command::new("/usr/sbin/lsof");
    command.args(["-n", "-P", "-w", "-Fpfn"]);
    if let Some(listing) = listing(command) {
        kill(&matching(&listing, scope, std::process::id()));
    }
}

pub(crate) fn kill(pids: &[u32]) {
    if pids.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    let _ = Command::new("/bin/kill")
        .arg("-KILL")
        .args(pids.iter().map(u32::to_string))
        .stdin(Stdio::null())
        .stdout(Stdio::null())
        .stderr(Stdio::null())
        .status();
}

/// What `command` prints, unless it fails or outlasts `LISTING_TIMEOUT`.
pub(crate) fn listing(mut command: Command) -> Option<String> {
    let mut child = command
        .env_clear()
        .env("LC_ALL", "C")
        .stdin(Stdio::null())
        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
        .stderr(Stdio::null())
        .spawn()
        .ok()?;
    let mut output = child.stdout.take()?;
    // Read apart: a full pipe would otherwise keep the command from exiting.
    let reading = std::thread::spawn(move || {
        let mut bytes = Vec::new();
        output.read_to_end(&mut bytes).map(|_| bytes)
    });
    let code = wine::wait(child, LISTING_TIMEOUT).ok().flatten();
    let bytes = reading.join().ok()?.ok()?;
    code.map(|_| String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes).into_owned())
}
```

```rs
    let listing = [
        // The game in Wine, and a Wine service of its prefix.
        "p10\nfcwd\nn/Games/Peak\nftxt\nn/lib/Voile/v1/bin/wine-preloader",
        "p11\nfcwd\nn/lib/Prefixes/Peak/drive_c/windows/system32\nftxt\nn/lib/Voile/v1/lib/wine/ntdll.so",

        "p13\nftxt\nn/Games/Peak/Peak.app/Contents/MacOS/CrashHandler\nf4\nn/Games/Peak/log.txt",
        // Another game in Wine.

        engine.uses,
        [
            Path::new("/Games/Peak"),
            Path::new("/lib/Prefixes/Peak-linux"),
            Path::new("/var/folders/T/obelisk-engine-7"),

    );
}
```

`crates/game-runtime/src/supervisor/rosetta.rs`:

```rs
//! Rosetta translation gate shared by the Steam and Epic supervisors.
use crate::supervisor::Error;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use tokio::sync::Notify;

/// The Rosetta helper app bundled beside the storefront helpers.
pub(crate) fn helper(helpers: &Path) -> PathBuf {
    helpers.join("Obelisk Rosetta.app/Contents/MacOS/ObeliskRosetta")
}

/// The directory that bundles the Rosetta helper app, which sits beside the
/// storefront helpers directory `storefront` (`Helpers/SteamNative`).
pub(crate) fn helpers(storefront: &Path) -> Option<&Path> {
    storefront.parent()
}

/// The directory that bundles the Rosetta helper app, for the storefront
/// helper `host` (`Helpers/SteamNative/obelisk-steam-host`).
pub(crate) fn helpers_of_host(host: &Path) -> Option<&Path> {
    host.parent().and_then(helpers)
}

pub(crate) struct Gate {
    pub(crate) helper: PathBuf,
    pub(crate) check: fn(&Path) -> Result<bool, Error>,
    changed: Notify,
}

impl Gate {
    pub(crate) fn new(helper: PathBuf, check: fn(&Path) -> Result<bool, Error>) -> Self {
        Self {
            helper,
            check,
            changed: Notify::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Wake `wait` after the published request or cancellation state changed.
    pub(crate) fn wake(&self) {
        self.changed.notify_waiters();
    }

    /// Synchronous check for command handlers running off the executor.
    pub(crate) fn available(&self) -> Result<bool, Error> {
        (self.check)(&self.helper)
    }

    pub(crate) async fn probe(&self) -> Result<bool, Error> {
        let helper = self.helper.clone();
        let check = self.check;
        tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || check(&helper))
            .await
            .map_err(|_| Error::StartFailed)?
    }

    /// Returns true if installation interrupted preparation and short-lived
    /// launch credentials may need refreshing. `pending` also checks session
    /// cancellation; callers must `wake` when resuming or cancelling the session.
    pub(crate) async fn wait<E: From<Error>>(
        &self,
        request: impl FnOnce() -> Result<(), E>,
        pending: impl Fn() -> Result<bool, E>,
    ) -> Result<bool, E> {
        pending()?;
        if self.probe().await? {
            pending()?;
            return Ok(false);
        }
        request()?;
        loop {
            let notified = self.changed.notified();
            tokio::pin!(notified);
            // Register before reading state, including when resume/cancel races
            // with publication of the installation request.
            notified.as_mut().enable();
            if !pending()? {
                break;
            }
            notified.await;
        }
        // Acknowledgement alone cannot authorize launch: verify translation again.
        let available = self.probe().await?;
        pending()?;
        if !available {
            return Err(Error::RosettaUnavailable.into());
        }
        Ok(true)
    }
}
```

```rs
use super::*;
use std::{cell::Cell, io::Read, time::Duration};
use tokio::io::AsyncWriteExt;

#[tokio::test]
async fn resume_between_state_read_and_await_is_not_lost() {
    let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let helper = root.path().join("available");
    let gate = Gate::new(helper.clone(), |path| Ok(path.exists()));
    let requested = Cell::new(false);
    let pending = Cell::new(false);
    let waited = tokio::time::timeout(
        Duration::from_secs(2),
        gate.wait(
            || {
                requested.set(true);
                pending.set(true);
                Ok::<_, Error>(())
            },
            || {
                let observed = pending.get();
                if observed {
                    // Resume after reading the old state but before awaiting.
                    std::fs::write(&helper, b"available").unwrap();
                    pending.set(false);
                    gate.wake();
                }
                Ok(observed)
            },
        ),
    )
    .await
    .expect("resume notification was lost")
    .unwrap();
    assert!(waited && requested.get());
    assert!(!pending.get());
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn cancellation_during_the_initial_probe_preserves_the_provider_error() {
    let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let helper = root.path().join("probe.sock");
    let listener = tokio::net::UnixListener::bind(&helper).unwrap();
    let gate = Gate::new(helper, |path| {
        let mut connection = std::os::unix::net::UnixStream::connect(path)?;
        connection.read_exact(&mut [0])?;
        Ok(true)
    });
    let cancelled = Cell::new(false);
    let waiting = gate.wait(
        || panic!("cancelled preparation published an installation request"),
        || {
            if cancelled.get() {
                Err(crate::epic::Error::Cancelled)
            } else {
                Ok(false)
            }
        },
    );
    let cancel = async {
        let (mut connection, _) = listener.accept().await.unwrap();
        cancelled.set(true);
        gate.wake();
        connection.write_all(&[1]).await.unwrap();
    };
    let (result, ()) = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(2), async {
        tokio::join!(waiting, cancel)
    })
    .await
    .expect("cancelled probe did not complete");
    assert!(matches!(result, Err(crate::epic::Error::Cancelled)));
}
```

`crates/game-runtime/src/supervisor/session.rs`:

```rs
//! The supervisor side of a Game session, shared by every storefront. A
//! supervisor process hosts exactly one Game session, from the client's
//! handoff until the game has really exited and its Cloud saves are settled.
//! A storefront supplies its `Launch`; the order of the steps is the core's.
use super::*;
use crate::supervisor::architecture::Architecture;
use obelisk_core::transfer::CancelToken;
use std::{
    io::{Read, Write},
    os::fd::OwnedFd,
    os::unix::{
        fs::PermissionsExt,
        net::{UnixListener, UnixStream},
    },
    path::Path,
    process::{Command as Process, Stdio},
    sync::{
        Arc, Condvar, Mutex, OnceLock,
        atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU64, AtomicUsize, Ordering},
    },
    time::{Duration, Instant},
};

/// The supervisor's own process inspection. `Ok(None)` proves absence; an
/// error is uncertainty.
pub type Inspect = fn(u32) -> Result<Option<Identity>, Error>;

type Failure<L> = <<L as Launch>::P as Provider>::Error;
/// How the player's controls reach a running game.
pub(crate) type Control<P> =
    Box<dyn Fn(<P as Provider>::Control) -> Result<(), Error> + Send + Sync>;
/// A storefront's own async step, boxed so its traits stay object safe.
pub(crate) type Operation<'a, T> = std::pin::Pin<Box<dyn std::future::Future<Output = T> + 'a>>;

/// A Cloud question is abandoned this long after it was published.
const QUESTION_DEADLINE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(600);
/// A Cloud question is abandoned once no observer has asked for this long.
const OBSERVER_DEADLINE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(120);
/// A supervisor abandons a launch that its UI never begins.
pub(crate) const BEGIN_DEADLINE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(120);
/// Concurrent control connections; more are dropped unanswered.
const WORKERS: usize = 16;
/// How long a game asked to stop gets to quit before it is killed.
const STOP_GRACE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5);

/// What the client handed over, as the core needs it.
pub(crate) struct Opening<P: Provider> {
    pub root: PathBuf,
    pub id: String,
    pub account_id: P::Account,
    pub store: P::Store,
    /// The directory that bundles the Obelisk Rosetta helper app.
    pub helpers: PathBuf,
}

/// A prepared game, ready for exec admission.
pub(crate) struct Prepared<H> {
    pub host: H,
    /// The exec helper and its subcommand.
    pub helper: PathBuf,
    pub subcommand: &'static str,
    /// The game's environment. It is set on the helper and inherited through
    /// exec, so it reaches the game verbatim.
    pub environment: std::collections::HashMap<String, String>,
}

/// A launch's Cloud sync, which the core drives around the game: prepared
/// before it, started inside the admission lock, finished once the game
/// exits, or abandoned when it never starts.
pub(crate) trait LaunchCloud<E>: Send {
    /// `alive` answers for a previous session whose Cloud game guard remains.
    fn prepare<'a>(&'a mut self, alive: &'a SessionAlive<'a>) -> Operation<'a, Result<(), E>>;
    fn started(&mut self) -> Result<(), E>;
    /// Settles the exit save. Never fails the session: its result lives in
    /// the Cloud status. `confirmed` is false when exec was never confirmed;
    /// the exit save is then only captured and kept pending.
    fn finished(&mut self, confirmed: bool) -> Operation<'_, ()>;
    /// Releases the Cloud work of a launch abandoned before spawn.
    fn aborted(&mut self);
}
impl<E, C: LaunchCloud<E> + ?Sized> LaunchCloud<E> for Box<C> {
    fn prepare<'a>(&'a mut self, alive: &'a SessionAlive<'a>) -> Operation<'a, Result<(), E>> {
        (**self).prepare(alive)
    }
    fn started(&mut self) -> Result<(), E> {
        (**self).started()
    }
    fn finished(&mut self, confirmed: bool) -> Operation<'_, ()> {
        (**self).finished(confirmed)
    }
    fn aborted(&mut self) {
        (**self).aborted();
    }
}
impl<S, E> LaunchCloud<E> for crate::cloud::sync::CloudSync<S>
where
    S: crate::cloud::sync::Storefront + Send,
    E: From<S::Failure>,
    Self: Send,
{
    fn prepare<'a>(&'a mut self, alive: &'a SessionAlive<'a>) -> Operation<'a, Result<(), E>> {
        Box::pin(async move { Ok(crate::cloud::sync::CloudSync::prepare(self, alive).await?) })
    }
    fn started(&mut self) -> Result<(), E> {
        Ok(crate::cloud::sync::CloudSync::started(self)?)
    }
    fn finished(&mut self, confirmed: bool) -> Operation<'_, ()> {
        Box::pin(crate::cloud::sync::CloudSync::finished(self, confirmed))
    }
    fn aborted(&mut self) {
        crate::cloud::sync::CloudSync::aborted(self);
    }
}

/// A storefront's launch. The core calls it in this order: authentication,
/// the Cloud sync it opens and prepares, target and architecture, the Rosetta
/// gate (then the target again, once Rosetta was just installed), host
/// preparation, then exec admission, where the Cloud sync starts.
#[allow(async_fn_in_trait)]
pub(crate) trait Launch: Sized + 'static {
    type P: Provider;
    /// What preparation leaves running until the game exits, such as
    /// Steam's native host.
    type Host: Send + Sync + 'static;
    /// The launch's Cloud sync.
    type Cloud: LaunchCloud<Failure<Self>>;
    /// Only a launch that waits for its UI's Begin sets this.
    const BEGIN: bool = false;

    fn open(input: &mut dyn Read) -> Result<(Opening<Self::P>, Self), Failure<Self>>;
    /// Stops the storefront's own preparation outside Cloud, such as Steam's
    /// native host, when the launch is cancelled or revoked before spawn.
    fn interrupt(&self) -> Box<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync> {
        Box::new(|| {})
    }
    /// How a Windows game runs, whose prefix stopping the game empties too.
    fn wine(&self) -> Option<crate::wine::Config> {
        None
    }
    async fn authenticate(
        &mut self,
        _session: &Arc<Session<Self::P>>,
    ) -> Result<(), Failure<Self>> {
        Ok(())
    }
    /// Opens the launch's Cloud sync, if its game has one.
    async fn cloud(
        &mut self,
        session: &Arc<Session<Self::P>>,
    ) -> Result<Option<Self::Cloud>, Failure<Self>>;
    /// Called again after Rosetta was just installed: short-lived launch
    /// credentials may need refreshing.
    async fn target(
        &mut self,
        session: &Arc<Session<Self::P>>,
    ) -> Result<(Target, Option<Architecture>), Failure<Self>>;
    /// `cloud` is the prepared Cloud sync.
    async fn prepare_host(
        &mut self,
        session: &Arc<Session<Self::P>>,
        target: &Target,
        architecture: Option<Architecture>,
        cloud: Option<&Self::Cloud>,
    ) -> Result<Prepared<Self::Host>, Failure<Self>>;
    /// The game runs. Returns how its presence is published.
    fn running(&self, host: &Arc<Self::Host>, pid: u32) -> Box<dyn Fn(bool) + Send + Sync>;
    /// The game runs: how the player's controls reach it, if the storefront
    /// offers any. They stop once the game exits.
    fn control(&self, _host: &Arc<Self::Host>) -> Option<Control<Self::P>> {
        None
    }
    /// Reports host changes while the game runs, until the host stops.
    fn watch(
        &self,
        _host: &Arc<Self::Host>,
        _session: &Arc<Session<Self::P>>,
    ) -> Option<std::thread::JoinHandle<()>> {
        None
    }
    fn stopped(&self, host: &Self::Host, exit: Option<i32>);
    /// Ends the launch's own network session, whatever the outcome.
    async fn close(&mut self) {}
    /// Storefront facts of a terminal record.
    fn terminal(_record: &mut Record<Self::P>) {}
    /// Whether Rosetta translates Intel games, asked of the bundled helper.
    fn rosetta(helper: &Path) -> Result<bool, Error> {
        crate::supervisor::architecture::rosetta_available(helper)
    }
}

/// The session's decisions: one counter for Cloud questions and the Rosetta
/// requirement, and the deadlines after which a Cloud question is abandoned.
pub struct Questions {
    next: AtomicU64,
    /// When an observer last asked. Only a supervised session has one.
    observed: Option<Mutex<Instant>>,
}
impl Questions {
    /// Cloud maintenance in Obelisk: the UI itself waits for the answer.
    pub fn in_app() -> Self {
        Self {
            next: AtomicU64::new(0),
            observed: None,
        }
    }
    fn supervised() -> Self {
        Self {
            next: AtomicU64::new(0),
            observed: Some(Mutex::new(Instant::now())),
        }
    }
    pub fn next(&self) -> u64 {
        self.next.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel) + 1
    }
    fn observe(&self) {
        if let Some(observed) = &self.observed {
            *observed.lock().unwrap() = Instant::now();
        }
    }
    /// A question published at `published` has nobody left to answer it.
    pub fn abandoned(&self, published: Instant) -> bool {
        published.elapsed() >= QUESTION_DEADLINE
            || self
                .observed
                .as_ref()
                .is_some_and(|observed| observed.lock().unwrap().elapsed() >= OBSERVER_DEADLINE)
    }
}

/// Presence goes Active once, after exec is confirmed, and stops for good:
/// a revocation before exec prevents any later publication.
struct Presence(Mutex<PresenceState>);
enum PresenceState {
    Pending,
    Active(Box<dyn Fn(bool) + Send + Sync>),
    Stopped,
}
impl Presence {
    fn start(&self, publish: Box<dyn Fn(bool) + Send + Sync>) {
        let mut state = self.0.lock().unwrap();
        if matches!(*state, PresenceState::Pending) {
            publish(true);
            *state = PresenceState::Active(publish);
        }
    }
    fn stop(&self) {
        let mut state = self.0.lock().unwrap();
        if let PresenceState::Active(publish) = &*state {
            publish(false);
        }
        *state = PresenceState::Stopped;
    }
}

struct State<P: Provider> {
    record: Record<P>,
    spawned: bool,
    /// The spawned helper that becomes the game, until it is reaped.
    game: Option<u32>,
    begun: bool,
    revoked: bool,
    /// A journal write failed before spawn: the launch fails closed.
    unsaved: bool,
}

pub(crate) struct Session<P: Provider> {
    state: Mutex<State<P>>,
    changed: Condvar,
    /// Spawn, cancellation, revocation, Rosetta publication and the Running
    /// publication linearize here. Take it before `state`, never after.
    admission: Mutex<()>,
    cancel: CancelToken,
    root: PathBuf,
    questions: Arc<Questions>,
    presence: Presence,
    rosetta: crate::supervisor::rosetta::Gate,
    /// The session's Cloud sync publishes into the record through it.
    cloud: Arc<crate::cloud::Control>,
    interrupt: OnceLock<Box<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>>,
    wine: OnceLock<Option<crate::wine::Config>>,
    /// Set before spawn, for the player's Quit and Force Quit.
    launched: OnceLock<super::quit::Game>,
    /// A Quit, or a Force Quit, is underway: the same request again adds
    /// nothing to it.
    quitting: AtomicBool,
    forcing: AtomicBool,
    /// The player quit or stopped the game from Obelisk, which its exit
    /// then reports.
    ended_by_obelisk: AtomicBool,
    /// The running game's controls, from its start until its exit.
    control: Mutex<Option<Control<P>>>,
    /// The Force Quit underway, which the session waits for before it ends:
    /// it kills what outlives the game, after the game.
    forced: Mutex<Option<std::thread::JoinHandle<()>>>,
}
impl<P: Provider> Session<P> {
    /// Obelisk is ending: macOS asks every process it started to quit, the
    /// Wine server of a Windows game included. The game stops as on a quit,
    /// and the Windows processes left frozen without their server go too; the
    /// session then settles its Cloud saves.
    fn terminated(&self) {
        if !self.state.lock().unwrap().spawned {
            self.stop_preparation();
            self.notify();
            return;
        }
        self.stop_game();
        if let Some(wine) = self.wine.get().cloned().flatten() {
            crate::wine::end_orphans(&wine.runtime);
        }
    }

    /// Ends the running game: it gets `STOP_GRACE` to quit before it is
    /// killed. A Windows game's prefix is emptied, which also ends the
    /// processes Wine started apart from it.
    fn stop_game(&self) {
        let Some(pid) = self.state.lock().unwrap().game else {
            return;
        };
        self.ended_by_obelisk.store(true, Ordering::Release);
        let wine = self.wine.get().cloned().flatten();
        self.signal(pid, "-TERM");
        if let Some(wine) = &wine {
            crate::wine::stop(wine);
        }
        self.wait_reaped(pid, STOP_GRACE);
        self.signal(pid, "-KILL");
    }

    /// The player's Quit: the game is asked to close as its player closing
    /// its windows would, and nothing is killed. A Windows game is asked
    /// through Wine; a Mac game gets SIGTERM, which it may handle to quit
    /// cleanly, the closest the supervisor has to the app's own Quit.
    fn quit_game(&self) {
        let Some(pid) = self.state.lock().unwrap().game else {
            return;
        };
        self.ended_by_obelisk.store(true, Ordering::Release);
        match (self.wine.get().cloned().flatten(), self.launched.get()) {
            (Some(wine), Some(game)) => {
                crate::wine::quit(&wine, &game.environment, game.program.as_deref(), pid)
            }
            _ => self.signal(pid, "-TERM"),
        }
    }

    /// The player's Force Quit: the game and what it started are killed at
    /// once, then whatever still runs for its installation or its prefix.
    /// The session then ends as after any exit, Cloud saves included.
    fn force_quit_game(&self) {
        let wine = self.wine.get().cloned().flatten();
        let pid = self.state.lock().unwrap().game;
        self.ended_by_obelisk.store(true, Ordering::Release);
        if let Some(pid) = pid {
            // An engine's launcher stops its window, render and input servers
            // itself: they are not frozen with the game, and SIGTERM lets the
            // input server give each gamepad back its own behaviour.
            if let Some(grace) = wine.as_ref().and_then(crate::wine::Config::launcher_grace) {
                self.signal(pid, "-TERM");
                self.wait_reaped(pid, grace);
            }
            let started = super::quit::started_by(pid);
            self.signal(pid, "-KILL");
            super::quit::kill(&started);
        }
        if let Some(wine) = &wine {
            crate::wine::kill(wine);
        }
        if let (Some(game), Ok(own)) = (self.launched.get(), std::env::current_exe()) {
            super::quit::sweep(&super::quit::Scope::of(game, wine.as_ref(), pid, &own));
        }
    }

    /// Waits at most `grace` for the game's helper `pid` to be reaped.
    fn wait_reaped(&self, pid: u32, grace: Duration) {
        let deadline = Instant::now() + grace;
        while self.state.lock().unwrap().game == Some(pid) && Instant::now() < deadline {
            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));
        }
    }

    /// Waits for the Force Quit underway, if any: the supervisor would
    /// otherwise exit before it killed what the game left running.
    async fn forced(&self) {
        let Some(forcing) = self.forced.lock().unwrap().take() else {
            return;
        };
        while !forcing.is_finished() {
            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
        }
        let _ = forcing.join();
    }

    /// Whether a Force Quit, or else a Quit, is underway.
    fn underway(&self, force: bool) -> &AtomicBool {
        if force { &self.forcing } else { &self.quitting }
    }

    /// Signals the game's helper while the supervisor has not reaped it.
    fn signal(&self, pid: u32, signal: &str) {
        // The helper stays unreaped until the supervisor waits for it, so its
        // pid cannot name another process meanwhile.
        if self.state.lock().unwrap().game == Some(pid) {
            let _ = std::process::Command::new("/bin/kill")
                .args([signal, &pid.to_string()])
                .stdin(Stdio::null())
                .stdout(Stdio::null())
                .stderr(Stdio::null())
                .status();
        }
    }
    pub(crate) fn record(&self) -> Record<P> {
        self.state.lock().unwrap().record.clone()
    }
    pub(crate) fn cloud(&self) -> &Arc<crate::cloud::Control> {
        &self.cloud
    }
    /// Wakes blocking observers and the Rosetta wait.
    pub(crate) fn notify(&self) {
        self.changed.notify_all();
        self.rosetta.wake();
    }
    /// Changes the record and journals it. Observers always see the change;
    /// a failed write before spawn makes the launch fail closed.
    pub(crate) fn update(&self, change: impl FnOnce(&mut Record<P>)) -> Result<(), Error> {
        let mut state = self.state.lock().unwrap();
        change(&mut state.record);
        state.record.revision += 1;
        let written = journal::write(&self.root, &state.record);
        if written.is_err() && !state.spawned {
            state.unsaved = true;
        }
        drop(state);
        self.notify();
        written
    }
    /// Whether preparation may go on.
    pub(crate) fn check(&self) -> Result<(), Error> {
        let state = self.state.lock().unwrap();
        if self.cancel.is_cancelled() || state.revoked {
            Err(Error::Cancelled)
        } else if state.unsaved {
            Err(Error::Storage)
        } else {
            Ok(())
        }
    }
    async fn begun(&self) -> Result<(), Error> {
        let deadline = Instant::now() + BEGIN_DEADLINE;
        loop {
            self.check()?;
            if self.state.lock().unwrap().begun {
                return Ok(());
            }
            if Instant::now() >= deadline {
                return Err(Error::Cancelled);
            }
            tokio::select! {
                _ = tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(25)) => (),
                _ = self.cancel.cancelled() => return Err(Error::Cancelled),
            }
        }
    }

    /// Returns true when Rosetta was just installed.
    async fn wait_for_rosetta(&self) -> Result<bool, Error> {
        self.rosetta
            .wait(
                || {
                    let _admission = self.admission.lock().unwrap();
                    self.check()?;
                    let decision_id = self.questions.next();
                    self.update(|r| r.rosetta = Some(RosettaRequest { decision_id }))
                },
                || {
                    self.check()?;
                    Ok(self.state.lock().unwrap().record.rosetta.is_some())
                },
            )
            .await
    }

    /// Stops preparation before spawn: the core, the storefront and Cloud.
    fn stop_preparation(&self) {
        self.cancel.cancel();
        if let Some(interrupt) = self.interrupt.get() {
            interrupt();
        }
        self.cloud.cancel();
    }
}

/// Runs one supervisor. It returns an error, and the process exits non-zero,
/// only when the session ends Failed for a reason other than cancellation.
pub(crate) fn serve<L: Launch>(
    mut input: impl Read,
    mut output: impl Write,
    inspect: Inspect,
) -> Result<(), Failure<L>> {
    // The executor exists before any durable write.
    let executor = crate::executor().map_err(Error::from)?;
    let (opening, mut launch) = L::open(&mut input)?;
    let owner = OwnerLock::<L::P>::take(&opening.root)?;
    // No other supervisor of this storefront lives, but its game may.
    if let Some(previous) = journal::current::<Record<L::P>>(&opening.root)?
        && !previous.finished()
        && previous.liveness(inspect)? != ownership::Liveness::Dead
    {
        return Err(Error::Busy.into());
    }
    // A short socket path avoids macOS's 104-byte sockaddr_un limit, including
    // when the account home is long. tempfile creates an unpredictable 0700 dir.
    let socket_directory = tempfile::Builder::new()
        .prefix("obelisk-session-")
        .permissions(std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o700))
        .tempdir_in("/tmp")
        .map_err(Error::from)?;
    let socket = socket_directory.path().join("control");
    let listener = UnixListener::bind(&socket).map_err(Error::from)?;
    let record = Record::<L::P> {
        version: journal::VERSION,
        id: opening.id,
        account_id: opening.account_id,
        store: opening.store,
        phase: Phase::Preparing,
        cloud: Default::default(),
        exit_code: None,
        played: None,
        error: None,
        failure_reason: None,
        revision: 1,
        rosetta: None,
        reconnecting: false,
        supervisor: inspect(std::process::id())?.ok_or(Error::StartFailed)?,
        game: None,
        starting: None,
        socket: socket.clone(),
    };
    journal::write(&opening.root, &record)?;
    let questions = Arc::new(Questions::supervised());
    let session = Arc::new_cyclic(|session: &std::sync::Weak<Session<L::P>>| Session {
        state: Mutex::new(State {
            record,
            spawned: false,
            game: None,
            begun: !L::BEGIN,
            revoked: false,
            unsaved: false,
        }),
        changed: Condvar::new(),
        admission: Mutex::new(()),
        cancel: CancelToken::new(),
        root: opening.root,
        questions: questions.clone(),
        presence: Presence(Mutex::new(PresenceState::Pending)),
        rosetta: crate::supervisor::rosetta::Gate::new(
            crate::supervisor::rosetta::helper(&opening.helpers),
            L::rosetta,
        ),
        cloud: Arc::new(crate::cloud::Control::with_questions(questions, {
            let session = session.clone();
            // Observers read the session itself, so a failed journal write
            // hides nothing: the core fails closed before spawn.
            move |status| {
                if let Some(session) = session.upgrade() {
                    let _ = session.update(|record| record.cloud = status);
                }
            }
        })),
        interrupt: OnceLock::new(),
        wine: OnceLock::new(),
        launched: OnceLock::new(),
        quitting: AtomicBool::new(false),
        forcing: AtomicBool::new(false),
        ended_by_obelisk: AtomicBool::new(false),
        control: Mutex::new(None),
        forced: Mutex::new(None),
    });
    let _ = session.interrupt.set(launch.interrupt());
    let _ = session.wine.set(launch.wine());
    let finished = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
    let listening = {
        let session = session.clone();
        let finished = finished.clone();
        std::thread::spawn(move || listen::<L>(listener, session, finished))
    };
    // Journal, then listener, then acknowledgement. Losing the parent here
    // never revokes an accepted launch or ownership of its game.
    let _ = storage::send(&mut output, &session.record());
    drop(output);
    let alive = |id: &str| owner.session_alive(id, inspect);
    let outcome = executor.block_on(async {
        // Catching SIGTERM keeps this supervisor alive when Obelisk ends,
        // long enough to stop its game and settle its Cloud saves.
        let terminated = tokio::signal::unix::signal(tokio::signal::unix::SignalKind::terminate())
            .ok()
            .map(|mut terminate| {
                let session = session.clone();
                tokio::spawn(async move {
                    if terminate.recv().await.is_some() {
                        std::thread::spawn(move || session.terminated());
                    }
                })
            });
        // Kept even if preparation fails, so an abandoned launch still
        // releases its Cloud work.
        let mut cloud = None;
        let outcome = run(&mut launch, &mut cloud, &session, inspect, &alive).await;
        if let Some(terminated) = terminated {
            terminated.abort();
        }
        if outcome.is_err()
            && !session.state.lock().unwrap().spawned
            && let Some(cloud) = &mut cloud
        {
            cloud.aborted();
        }
        // A Force Quit asked once the game was gone still ends what it
        // left running.
        session.forced().await;
        launch.close().await;
        outcome
    });
    session.presence.stop();
    let result = match outcome {
        // An exec that never became the game is a failed launch.
        Ok(()) if session.record().phase == Phase::Failed => Err(Error::StartFailed.into()),
        Ok(()) => Ok(()),
        Err(failure) => {
            let cancelled = <L::P as Provider>::cancelled(&failure);
            let _ = session.update(|r| {
                r.phase = Phase::Failed;
                r.failure_reason = Some(if cancelled {
                    FailureReason::Cancelled
                } else {
                    FailureReason::Failed
                });
                r.error = Some(failure.to_string());
                r.rosetta = None;
                r.game = None;
                r.starting = None;
                L::terminal(r);
            });
            if cancelled { Ok(()) } else { Err(failure) }
        }
    };
    finished.store(true, Ordering::Release);
    // Wake the blocking accept even when no UI is connected. If the socket
    // was removed, this dedicated process exits next and closes its listener.
    if UnixStream::connect(&socket).is_ok() || listening.is_finished() {
        let _ = listening.join();
    }
    // The socket directory and owner lock go only after game and host
    // teardown, and after the executor's bounded shutdown.
    drop(executor);
    drop(socket_directory);
    drop(owner);
    result
}

async fn run<L: Launch>(
    launch: &mut L,
    cloud: &mut Option<L::Cloud>,
    session: &Arc<Session<L::P>>,
    inspect: Inspect,
    alive: &SessionAlive<'_>,
) -> Result<(), Failure<L>> {
    use super::child::{Execution, confirm_execution, wait_for_exit, wait_identity};

    if L::BEGIN {
        session.begun().await?;
    }
    launch.authenticate(session).await?;
    if let Some(opened) = launch.cloud(session).await? {
        cloud.insert(opened).prepare(alive).await?;
    }
    session.check()?;
    let mut refreshed = false;
    let (target, architecture) = loop {
        let (target, architecture) = launch.target(session).await?;
        session.check()?;
        if architecture == Some(Architecture::Intel) && cfg!(target_arch = "aarch64") {
            if refreshed {
                // A second interruption cannot loop over fresh launch
                // credentials indefinitely. Fail if availability changed.
                if !session.rosetta.probe().await? {
                    return Err(Error::RosettaUnavailable.into());
                }
            } else if session.wait_for_rosetta().await? {
                refreshed = true;
                continue;
            }
        }
        break (target, architecture);
    };
    session.check()?;
    let mut prepared = launch
        .prepare_host(session, &target, architecture, cloud.as_ref())
        .await?;
    let wine = launch.wine();
    // A game in Wine for macOS reads the Mac's gamepads through the input
    // service while it runs.
    let input = wine
        .as_ref()
        .and_then(crate::input::Service::start)
        .map(|(service, socket)| {
            prepared.environment.insert(
                crate::input::SOCKET.to_owned(),
                socket.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
            );
            service
        });
    // Metal reports the game's frames to its log, and shows them over the
    // game only to a player who asked in its launch settings.
    let shown = wine.is_some_and(|wine| wine.settings.performance_hud);
    prepared.environment.extend(
        crate::metal_hud::environment(shown)
            .map(|(name, value)| (name.to_owned(), value.to_owned())),
    );
    let _ = session.launched.set(super::quit::Game {
        environment: target.environment.clone(),
        installation: target.installation.clone(),
        program: target.program.clone(),
    });
    let host = Arc::new(prepared.host);
    let mut command = Process::new(&prepared.helper);
    let (mut pipe, child_pipe) = UnixStream::pair().map_err(Error::from)?;
    pipe.set_write_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(5)))
        .map_err(Error::from)?;
    command
        .arg(prepared.subcommand)
        .env_clear()
        .envs(&prepared.environment)
        .stdin(Stdio::from(OwnedFd::from(child_pipe)))
        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
        .stderr(Stdio::null());
    let expected = target
        .executable
        .canonicalize()
        .map_err(|_| Error::StartFailed)?;
    let (mut game, admitted) = {
        // Cancellation and spawn have one linearization point. Cancellation
        // after it never ends a game, including sign-out and UI loss.
        let _admission = session.admission.lock().unwrap();
        session.check()?;
        if let Some(cloud) = cloud.as_mut() {
            cloud.started()?;
        }
        let game = tokio::process::Command::from(command)
            .kill_on_drop(false)
            .spawn()
            .map_err(|_| Error::StartFailed)?;
        {
            let mut state = session.state.lock().unwrap();
            state.spawned = true;
            state.game = game.id();
        }
        let admitted = (|| {
            // Read now: a game reaped during confirmation no longer has one.
            let pid = game.id().ok_or(Error::StartFailed)?;
            let identity = inspect(pid)?.ok_or(Error::StartFailed)?;
            // The helper cannot exec before its identity and destination are
            // durable: this write must succeed.
            session.update(|r| {
                r.starting = Some(StartingGame::Process {
                    identity,
                    executable: expected.clone(),
                })
            })?;
            exec::send(
                &mut pipe,
                &exec::Admission {
                    executable: target.executable.clone(),
                    arguments: target.arguments.clone(),
                    working_directory: target.working_directory.clone(),
                    log: target.log.clone(),
                    log_header: session
                        .wine
                        .get()
                        .and_then(Option::as_ref)
                        .map(crate::wine::Config::log_header),
                },
            )
            .map_err(|_| Error::StartFailed)?;
            Ok(pid)
        })();
        (game, admitted)
    };
    drop(pipe);
    // A helper that never became the game keeps its ownership until it is
    // reaped, outside the admission lock.
    let reap = async |mut game: tokio::process::Child, error: Error| {
        let exit = wait_for_exit(&mut game).await.code().unwrap_or(-1);
        session.state.lock().unwrap().game = None;
        launch.stopped(&host, Some(exit));
        session.state.lock().unwrap().spawned = false;
        let _ = session.update(|r| r.starting = None);
        Err(error.into())
    };
    // Without a complete admission the helper exits without exec.
    let pid = match admitted {
        Ok(pid) => pid,
        Err(error) => return reap(game, error).await,
    };
    let inspect_game = |pid| inspect(pid).ok().flatten();
    let execution = confirm_execution(&mut game, &target.executable, inspect_game).await;
    if execution == Execution::Failed {
        return reap(game, Error::StartFailed).await;
    }
    let started = execution == Execution::Started;
    if started {
        let identity = wait_identity(&mut game, &target.executable, inspect_game).await;
        // Revocation takes this same lock: its permanent stop fences a late exec.
        let _admission = session.admission.lock().unwrap();
        session.presence.start(launch.running(&host, pid));
        *session.control.lock().unwrap() = launch.control(&host);
        let _ = session.update(|r| {
            // A path the helper could not confirm keeps its starting identity,
            // which the birth-time rule still owns.
            let starting = r
                .starting
                .take()
                .map(|StartingGame::Process { identity, .. }| identity);
            r.game = identity.or(starting);
            r.phase = Phase::Running;
        });
    }
    let watching = launch.watch(&host, session);
    let began = Instant::now();
    let status = wait_for_exit(&mut game).await;
    let seconds = began.elapsed().as_secs();
    let exit = status.code().unwrap_or(-1);
    drop(input);
    session.control.lock().unwrap().take();
    session.state.lock().unwrap().game = None;
    session.presence.stop();
    launch.stopped(&host, Some(exit));
    if let Some(watching) = watching {
        let _ = watching.join();
    }
    // What a Force Quit kills after the game is gone before its saves are
    // read.
    session.forced().await;
    let played = if started {
        let log = target.log.clone();
        let frames = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
            log.map(|log| crate::metal_hud::read(&log))
                .unwrap_or_default()
        })
        .await
        .unwrap_or_default();
        let wine = session.wine.get().cloned().flatten();
        Some(Played {
            seconds,
            frames,
            exit_code: status.code(),
            exit_signal: std::os::unix::process::ExitStatusExt::signal(&status),
            ended_by_obelisk: session.ended_by_obelisk.load(Ordering::Acquire),
            graphics: wine.as_ref().map(|wine| wine.settings.graphics),
            voile: wine
                .as_ref()
                .and_then(|wine| crate::voile::release_of(&wine.runtime)),
            engine: wine.map(|wine| wine.settings.engine),
        })
    } else {
        None
    };
    // After exit every write is best effort: finalization always runs, and a
    // success never turns into a failure.
    let _ = session.update(|r| {
        r.phase = Phase::Finalizing;
        r.exit_code = Some(exit);
        r.played = played;
        r.game = None;
        r.starting = None;
    });
    if let Some(cloud) = cloud.as_mut() {
        cloud.finished(started).await;
    }
    let _ = session.update(|r| {
        r.phase = if started {
            Phase::Finished
        } else {
            Phase::Failed
        };
        r.exit_code = Some(exit);
        if !started {
            r.failure_reason = Some(FailureReason::Failed);
            r.error = Some(<L::P as Provider>::Error::from(Error::StartFailed).to_string());
        }
        L::terminal(r);
    });
    Ok(())
}

fn listen<L: Launch>(
    listener: UnixListener,
    session: Arc<Session<L::P>>,
    finished: Arc<AtomicBool>,
) {
    let workers = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
    while !finished.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
        match listener.accept() {
            Ok((stream, _)) => {
                if finished.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
                    break;
                }
                if workers.load(Ordering::Acquire) >= WORKERS {
                    continue;
                }
                workers.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
                let workers = workers.clone();
                let session = session.clone();
                std::thread::spawn(move || {
                    let _ = respond::<L>(stream, &session);
                    workers.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
                });
            }
            Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::Interrupted => continue,
            Err(_) => break,
        }
    }
}

fn respond<L: Launch>(mut stream: UnixStream, session: &Arc<Session<L::P>>) -> Result<(), Error> {
    stream.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(2)))?;
    stream.set_write_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(2)))?;
    let command: Command<L::P> = storage::command(&stream)?;
    let same = |state: &State<L::P>, id: &str, account_id: Option<&<L::P as Provider>::Account>| {
        state.record.id == id
            && account_id.is_none_or(|account_id| *account_id == state.record.account_id)
    };
    match command {
        Command::Observe { id, after } => {
            let state = session.state.lock().unwrap();
            if !same(&state, &id, None) {
                return Err(Error::InvalidSession);
            }
            session.questions.observe();
            let waiting = |state: &mut State<L::P>| {
                after == Some(state.record.revision) && !state.record.finished()
            };
            let (state, _) = session
                .changed
                .wait_timeout_while(state, Duration::from_secs(15), waiting)
                .unwrap();
            let record = state.record.clone();
            drop(state);
            return storage::send(&mut stream, &record);
        }
        Command::Begin { id, account_id } => {
            if !L::BEGIN || !same(&session.state.lock().unwrap(), &id, Some(&account_id)) {
                return Err(Error::InvalidSession);
            }
            session.check()?;
            session.state.lock().unwrap().begun = true;
            session.notify();
        }
        Command::Cancel { id } => {
            let _admission = session.admission.lock().unwrap();
            let state = session.state.lock().unwrap();
            if !same(&state, &id, None) {
                return Err(Error::InvalidSession);
            }
            let preparing = !state.spawned;
            drop(state);
            if preparing {
                session.stop_preparation();
                session.notify();
            }
        }
        Command::Stop { id } => {
            let _admission = session.admission.lock().unwrap();
            let state = session.state.lock().unwrap();
            if !same(&state, &id, None) {
                return Err(Error::InvalidSession);
            }
            let spawned = state.spawned;
            drop(state);
            if spawned {
                // The reply does not wait for the game to go.
                let session = session.clone();
                std::thread::spawn(move || session.stop_game());
            } else {
                session.stop_preparation();
                session.notify();
            }
        }
        Command::Quit { id } => end(session, &id, false)?,
        Command::ForceQuit { id } => end(session, &id, true)?,
        Command::Control {
            id,
            account_id,
            control,
        } => {
            if !same(&session.state.lock().unwrap(), &id, Some(&account_id)) {
                return Err(Error::InvalidSession);
            }
            let controls = session.control.lock().unwrap();
            controls.as_ref().ok_or(Error::InvalidSession)?(control)?;
        }
        Command::CloudChoice {
            id,
            account_id,
            decision_id,
            choice,
        } => {
            if !same(&session.state.lock().unwrap(), &id, Some(&account_id)) {
                return Err(Error::InvalidSession);
            }
            session
                .cloud
                .answer(decision_id, choice)
                .map_err(|_| Error::InvalidSession)?;
            session.notify();
        }
        Command::Revoke { id, account_id } => {
            // Serialized with spawn: an acknowledged revocation cannot precede
            // a later launch, and presence goes offline before the reply.
            let _admission = session.admission.lock().unwrap();
            let mut state = session.state.lock().unwrap();
            if !same(&state, &id, Some(&account_id)) {
                return Err(Error::InvalidSession);
            }
            let preparing = !state.spawned;
            if preparing {
                state.revoked = true;
            }
            drop(state);
            if preparing {
                session.stop_preparation();
            }
            session.presence.stop();
            // Cloud network work stops; the exit save stays local and pending.
            session.cloud.revoke();
            session.notify();
        }
        Command::ResumeAfterRosetta {
            id,
            account_id,
            decision_id,
        } => {
            let requested = |state: &State<L::P>| {
                state.record.rosetta == Some(RosettaRequest { decision_id })
                    && !state.spawned
                    && !state.revoked
                    && !session.cancel.is_cancelled()
            };
            {
                let state = session.state.lock().unwrap();
                if !same(&state, &id, Some(&account_id)) || !requested(&state) {
                    return Err(Error::InvalidSession);
                }
            }
            let available = session.rosetta.available()?;
            let _admission = session.admission.lock().unwrap();
            if !requested(&session.state.lock().unwrap()) {
                return Err(Error::InvalidSession);
            }
            if available {
                let _ = session.update(|r| r.rosetta = None);
            }
        }
    }
    let record = session.record();
    storage::send(&mut stream, &record)
}

/// The player's Quit, or Force Quit. Before spawn either one cancels
/// preparation. After it, the work runs apart: the reply never waits for the
/// game, and a repeated request joins the one underway.
fn end<P: Provider>(session: &Arc<Session<P>>, id: &str, force: bool) -> Result<(), Error> {
    let _admission = session.admission.lock().unwrap();
    let state = session.state.lock().unwrap();
    if state.record.id != id {
        return Err(Error::InvalidSession);
    }
    let spawned = state.spawned;
    drop(state);
    if !spawned {
        session.stop_preparation();
        session.notify();
        return Ok(());
    }
    if !session.underway(force).swap(true, Ordering::AcqRel) {
        // Held from spawn on: the session waits for a Force Quit only once
        // it can find it.
        let mut forced = session.forced.lock().unwrap();
        let ending = session.clone();
        let thread = std::thread::spawn(move || {
            if force {
                ending.force_quit_game();
            } else {
                ending.quit_game();
            }
            ending.underway(force).store(false, Ordering::Release);
        });
        if force && let Some(previous) = forced.replace(thread) {
            // A previous Force Quit is over, or about to be.
            let _ = previous.join();
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

```rs
//! The Game session lifecycle through the supervisor's interface: a real
//! supervisor process, its control socket and an exec helper process. Each
//! storefront's harness runs every scenario; its fakes follow one script and
//! record one vocabulary of events. Only process inspection is replaced.
use super::*;
use crate::supervisor::client::Client;
use std::{fs, path::Path};

mod recording;

/// What the storefront's fakes do at each step.
#[derive(Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub(crate) struct Script {
    /// The game's shell body, run in the test directory.
    pub game: String,
    /// Cloud preparation waits until `release-cloud` exists.
    pub hold_cloud: bool,
    /// Cloud preparation asks a question and waits for its answer.
    pub ask: bool,
    /// Cloud finalization waits until `release-finish` exists.
    pub hold_finish: bool,
    /// The game is an Intel executable.
    pub intel: bool,
    pub helper: Helper,
    /// The admission names an executable that does not exist.
    pub missing: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub(crate) enum Helper {
    #[default]
    Exec,
    /// Holds before exec until `release-exec` exists.
    Hold,
    /// Exits without confirming its exec.
    Unconfirmed,
    /// Confirms its exec only after the game has already been reaped.
    Late,
}

/// A storefront under test.
pub(crate) trait Harness: 'static {
    type P: Provider;
    /// Selects this harness in the re-entered supervisor process.
    const NAME: &'static str;
    fn account() -> <Self::P as Provider>::Account;
    fn other_account() -> <Self::P as Provider>::Account;
    /// Writes this storefront's handoff for a launch.
    fn handoff(
        directory: &Path,
        sessions: &Path,
        id: &str,
        pipe: &mut std::os::unix::net::UnixStream,
    ) -> Result<(), Error>;
    /// Runs this storefront's supervisor with its fakes.
    fn serve(
        input: std::io::StdinLock<'static>,
        output: std::io::StderrLock<'static>,
    ) -> Result<(), String>;
    /// Its UI sends Begin after each start, as Obelisk does for Epic.
    fn begins() -> bool {
        false
    }
    /// A running record in the format and under the names the previous
    /// build used.
    fn previous_build_record(id: &str, live: &Identity, socket: &Path) -> serde_json::Value;
```
