`crates/game-runtime/src/voile/feed.rs`:

```rs
//! The releases Voile offers, as `voile-feed.json` on Voile's `main` lists
//! them: each one's archive, the contract it keeps with Obelisk, and whether
//! players should leave it. Voile's Feed workflow writes it when a release is
//! published and signs it. Obelisk reads it as a Windows game launches, and
//! keeps the last one whose signature it checked beside the runtimes.
use super::Release;
use aws_lc_rs::signature::{ED25519, UnparsedPublicKey};
use base64::Engine as _;
use serde::Deserialize;
use std::{fs, path::Path};

/// The feed, and its signature beside it with `.sig` added.
const URL: &str = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Zagrios/Voile/main/voile-feed.json";
/// The public key the feed is signed with, made by Voile's
/// scripts/feed-key.sh: the base64 of its 32 bytes.
const KEY: &str = "ZUQNaLpt7otj1aDIN1adX8VxRSGoidNqCUbILs431oE=";
/// The feed's format this Obelisk reads. Another one is a feed it ignores.
const FORMAT: u32 = 1;
/// The last feed Obelisk checked, in the runtimes' folder.
pub(super) const KEPT: &str = "feed.json";

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
struct Feed {
    format: u32,
    releases: Vec<Offered>,
}

/// A release the feed offers.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) struct Offered {
    /// What it keeps of what Obelisk relies on: Obelisk runs only a release
    /// of its own contract.
    pub contract: u32,
    #[serde(flatten)]
    pub release: Release,
    /// Why players should leave it, once it is withdrawn.
    pub withdrawn: Option<String>,
}

/// The releases the last checked feed in `root` offers, or none.
pub(super) fn offered(root: &Path) -> Vec<Offered> {
    fs::read(root.join(KEPT))
        .ok()
        .and_then(|feed| releases(&feed))
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

/// Reads the feed again and keeps it in `root` once its signature holds.
/// Without the network, or with a feed it cannot check, the last one stays.
pub(crate) async fn refresh(root: &Path) {
    let signature = format!("{URL}.sig");
    let (feed, signature) = tokio::join!(
        crate::remote::fetched(URL),
        crate::remote::fetched(&signature)
    );
    if let (Some(feed), Some(signature)) = (feed, signature)
        && signed(&feed, &signature, KEY)
        && releases(&feed).is_some()
    {
        let _ = crate::remote::keep(&root.join(KEPT), &feed);
    }
}

/// Whether `signature`, the base64 of an Ed25519 signature, signs `feed`
/// with `key`.
fn signed(feed: &[u8], signature: &[u8], key: &str) -> bool {
    let base64 = base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD;
    let (Ok(key), Ok(signature)) = (base64.decode(key), base64.decode(signature.trim_ascii()))
    else {
        return false;
    };
    UnparsedPublicKey::new(&ED25519, key)
        .verify(feed, &signature)
        .is_ok()
}

/// The releases `feed` offers, when it is a feed of the format Obelisk
/// reads.
fn releases(feed: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<Offered>> {
    let feed: Feed = serde_json::from_slice(feed).ok()?;
    (feed.format == FORMAT).then_some(feed.releases)
}
```

```rs
use super::*;

/// A feed signed as Voile's Feed workflow signs one, with OpenSSL, by a key
/// made for these tests and thrown away.
const SIGNED: &[u8] = include_bytes!("signed-feed.json");
const SIGNATURE: &[u8] = include_bytes!("signed-feed.json.sig");
const SIGNER: &str = "auwHg9+CBTsKq3oTfRLk54XE1fcAUz5XLuEgFifqx6s=";

#[test]
fn obelisk_checks_the_feed_with_an_ed25519_key() {
    let key = base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD
        .decode(KEY)
        .expect("Voile's feed key, from scripts/feed-key.sh");
    assert_eq!(key.len(), 32);
}

#[test]
fn a_feed_holds_only_with_the_signature_its_signer_made() {
    assert!(signed(SIGNED, SIGNATURE, SIGNER));
    // The workflow writes no newline after it; one is no matter.
    assert!(signed(SIGNED, &[SIGNATURE, b"\n"].concat(), SIGNER));

    let mut changed = SIGNED.to_vec();
    let at = changed.iter().position(|&byte| byte == b'6').unwrap();
    changed[at] = b'7';
    assert!(!signed(&changed, SIGNATURE, SIGNER));
    assert!(!signed(SIGNED, SIGNATURE, KEY));
    assert!(!signed(SIGNED, b"not base64", SIGNER));
    assert!(!signed(SIGNED, SIGNATURE, "not a key"));
}

#[test]
fn obelisk_reads_the_releases_of_a_feed_of_its_format() {
    assert_eq!(
        releases(SIGNED).unwrap(),
        [Offered {
            contract: 1,
            release: Release {
                version: "v26.3.0-16".into(),
                url: "https://example.invalid/voile-v26.3.0-16.tar.xz".into(),
                size: 3,
                sha256: "a3c2e7b9b0f2f5e8c4d1e6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8091a2b3c4d5e6f7081".into(),
            },
            withdrawn: None,
        }]
    );
    assert_eq!(releases(br#"{"format": 2, "releases": []}"#), None);
    assert_eq!(releases(b"<html>"), None);
}

#[test]
fn the_feed_kept_is_the_one_launches_read() {
    let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let root = directory.path().join("Voile");
    assert_eq!(offered(&root), Vec::<Offered>::new());
    crate::remote::keep(&root.join(KEPT), SIGNED).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(offered(&root), releases(SIGNED).unwrap());
    assert_eq!(fs::read(root.join(KEPT)).unwrap(), SIGNED);
}
```

```rs
use super::*;

/// A release archive laid out as voile's package.sh makes it, with the Linux
/// engine's runtime in its `linux` folder, and the release that pins it.
/// `manifest_version` is what its runtime.json claims.
fn release_archive(directory: &Path, version: &str, manifest_version: &str) -> (PathBuf, Release) {
    let package = directory.join("package");
    lay(
        &package,
        &format!("voile-{version}"),
        &format!(r#"{{"version": "{manifest_version}"}}"#),
    );
    let archive = directory.join(format!("voile-{version}.tar.xz"));
    let status = std::process::Command::new("/usr/bin/tar")
        .arg("-cJf")
        .arg(&archive)
        .arg("-C")
        .arg(&package)
        .arg(format!("voile-{version}"))
        .status()
        .unwrap();
    assert!(status.success());
    let release = Release {
        version: version.into(),
        url: "https://example.invalid/voile.tar.xz".into(),
        size: fs::metadata(&archive).unwrap().len(),
        sha256: crate::sha(&archive).unwrap(),
    };
    (archive, release)
}

fn names(root: &Path) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut names: Vec<_> = fs::read_dir(root)
        .unwrap()
        .map(|entry| entry.unwrap().file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned())
        .collect();
    names.sort();
    names
}

/// A release's runtime in `root`, in `folder`, as its archive and an install
/// lay it, whose runtime.json holds `manifest`.
fn lay(root: &Path, folder: &str, manifest: &str) {
    let runtime = root.join(folder);
    fs::create_dir_all(runtime.join("bin")).unwrap();
    fs::write(runtime.join("bin/wine"), "wine").unwrap();
    fs::create_dir_all(runtime.join("linux/engine")).unwrap();
    fs::create_dir_all(runtime.join("linux/wine/bin")).unwrap();
    fs::write(runtime.join("linux/engine/fexdarwin-run"), "engine").unwrap();
    fs::write(runtime.join("linux/wine/bin/wine"), "wine").unwrap();
    fs::write(runtime.join(MANIFEST), manifest).unwrap();
}

/// The feed Obelisk read last, in `root`, offering `releases`.
fn feed(root: &Path, releases: &str) {
    fs::create_dir_all(root).unwrap();
    fs::write(
        root.join(feed::KEPT),
        format!(r#"{{"format": 1, "releases": [{releases}]}}"#),
    )
    .unwrap();
}

/// A release a feed offers, of `contract`.
fn offered(version: &str, contract: u32, withdrawn: Option<&str>) -> String {
    let withdrawn = withdrawn
        .map(|reason| format!(r#", "withdrawn": "{reason}""#))
        .unwrap_or_default();
    format!(
        r#"{{"version": "{version}", "contract": {contract}, "url": "https://example.invalid/voile-{version}.tar.xz", "size": 3, "sha256": "{}"{withdrawn}}}"#,
        "a".repeat(64)
    )
}

#[test]
fn the_checked_in_release_names_its_archive_and_obelisk_s_contract() {
    let release = release();
    assert!(release.url.ends_with(&format!(
        "/releases/download/{0}/voile-{0}.tar.xz",
        release.version
    )));
    assert_eq!(release.sha256.len(), 64);
    assert!(is_version(&release.version));
    assert!(contract() >= 1);
}

#[test]
fn versions_order_by_their_numbers() {
    assert_eq!(numbers("v26.3.0-16"), Some(vec![26, 3, 0, 16]));
    assert!(numbers("v26.3.0-10") > numbers("v26.3.0-9"));
    assert!(numbers("v26.4.0-1") > numbers("v26.3.0-16"));
    assert_eq!(numbers("current"), None);
    assert_eq!(numbers("v26.3.0-x"), None);
    assert!(is_version("v26.3.0-16"));
    assert!(!is_version("v26.3"));
    assert!(!is_version("26.3.0-16"));
}

#[test]
fn games_run_in_the_newest_release_of_obelisk_s_contract() {
    let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let root = directory.path();
    assert_eq!(runtime(root), None);
    // A release before CONTRACT kept the first contract.
    lay(root, "v1.0.0-9", r#"{"version": "v1.0.0-9"}"#);
    lay(
        root,
        "v1.0.0-10",
        r#"{"version": "v1.0.0-10", "contract": 1}"#,
    );
    lay(
        root,
        "v1.0.0-11",
        r#"{"version": "v1.0.0-11", "contract": 2}"#,
    );
    lay(
        root,
        "v1.0.0-12",
        r#"{"version": "v1.0.0-1", "contract": 1}"#,
    );
    assert_eq!(runtime(root), Some(root.join("v1.0.0-10")));
    assert_eq!(linux_runtime(root), Some(root.join("v1.0.0-10/linux")));
    assert_eq!(installed_release(root), Some("v1.0.0-10".into()));
}

#[test]
fn a_withdrawn_release_runs_no_game_and_goes_with_the_others_replaced() {
    let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let root = directory.path();
    lay(root, "v1.0.0-1", r#"{"version": "v1.0.0-1"}"#);
    lay(root, "v1.0.0-2", r#"{"version": "v1.0.0-2"}"#);

#[test]
fn a_launch_waits_for_a_missing_release_and_lets_an_outdated_one_run() {
    let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let root = directory.path();
    feed(root, &offered("v1.0.0-3", 1, None));
    assert_eq!(standing(root, None), Standing::Missing);

    lay(root, "v1.0.0-2", r#"{"version": "v1.0.0-2"}"#);
    assert_eq!(standing(root, None), Standing::Outdated);
    assert_eq!(
        standing(root, Some("v1.0.0-3")),
        Standing::Missing,
        "the game needs the release offered"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        standing(root, Some("v1.0.0-9")),
        Standing::Outdated,
        "no release offered is enough: the game runs in the newest it can"
    );
    assert_eq!(standing(root, Some("v1.0.0-2")), Standing::Outdated);

    lay(root, "v1.0.0-3", r#"{"version": "v1.0.0-3"}"#);
    assert_eq!(standing(root, Some("v1.0.0-3")), Standing::Current);

    fs::create_dir_all(root.join("current/bin")).unwrap();
    fs::write(root.join("current/bin/wine"), "wine").unwrap();
    feed(root, &offered("v1.0.0-4", 1, None));
    assert_eq!(standing(root, Some("v1.0.0-4")), Standing::Current);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_release_keeps_the_ones_before_it_until_they_are_removed() {
    let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let root = directory.path().join("Voile");
    let (archive, release) = release_archive(directory.path(), "v1.0.0-2", "v1.0.0-2");
    fs::create_dir_all(root.join("v1.0.0-1/bin")).unwrap();
    fs::create_dir_all(root.join(".interrupted")).unwrap();

    let runtime = Install::new()
        .install(&root, &release, Some(&archive))
        .await
        .unwrap();

    assert_eq!(runtime, root.join("v1.0.0-2"));
    assert_eq!(self::runtime(&root), Some(runtime));
    assert_eq!(names(&root), ["v1.0.0-1", "v1.0.0-2"]);

    // Once no game may run from them, the ones before it go.
    fs::create_dir_all(root.join("current/bin")).unwrap();
    fs::create_dir_all(root.join(".unfinished")).unwrap();
    remove_replaced(&root);
    assert_eq!(names(&root), [".unfinished", "current", "v1.0.0-2"]);

    // The same release again is in place already.
    assert_eq!(
        Install::new()
            .install(&root, &release, Some(&root.join("no archive")))
            .await,
        Ok(root.join("v1.0.0-2"))
    );
}

```

`crates/game-runtime/src/wine.rs`:

```rs
//! A Windows game runs in Obelisk's Wine runtime, inside the prefix of its
//! installation. What a storefront adds, such as Steam's steam.exe helper or
//! the prerequisites it names, comes from that storefront's side, and is
//! translated here for the engine its Launch settings name, by that engine's
//! adapter.
use crate::{
    Error,
    supervisor::{Target, architecture::Architecture},
};
use obelisk_core::{Platform, launch::LaunchTarget};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::{
    collections::HashMap,
    fs,
    io::Read,
    path::{Path, PathBuf},
    process::{Child, Command, Stdio},
    thread,
    time::{Duration, Instant},
};

pub(crate) mod linux_engine;
mod rosetta;

/// The user every prefix of CrossOver's Wine names its profile after.
const USER: &str = "crossover";
/// A command that ends a game is stopped after this long: the Wine server it
/// talks to may be frozen with the game.
const QUIT_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10);

/// The Windows user profile inside `prefix`, where Auto-Cloud roots such as
/// AppData and Documents live.
pub fn profile(prefix: &Path) -> PathBuf {
    prefix.join("drive_c/users").join(USER)
}

/// How one Windows installation runs: the Wine runtime, the installation's
/// prefix, the log Wine writes while its game runs, and the launch settings
/// it runs with.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Config {
    pub runtime: PathBuf,
    pub prefix: PathBuf,
    pub log: PathBuf,
    pub settings: crate::launch_settings::Settings,
}

/// What runs a Windows game's Wine.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Engine {
    /// Voile's Wine for macOS, under Rosetta.
    #[default]
    Rosetta,
    /// Voile's Wine for Linux, which voile-lkd's engine runs natively; for the
    /// games whose Launch settings name it.
    Linux,
}

/// The graphics backend that renders a Windows game's Direct3D 10 to 12
/// through Metal. dxgi is one per process, so a game has one: on DXMT, it has
/// no Direct3D 12.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Graphics {
    /// DXMT: Direct3D 10 and 11. On the Linux engine, in Neptune's arm64
    /// render server.
    Dxmt,
    /// D3DMetal: Direct3D 11 and 12, for 64-bit programs only, so 32-bit
    /// games on Rosetta's Wine render through DXMT. On the Linux engine, in
    /// Neptune's Intel render server under Rosetta.
    D3DMetal,
}

impl Graphics {
    /// What renders on `engine` when neither the game's profile nor its
    /// player picks another backend.
    pub fn default_on(engine: Engine) -> Self {
        engine.adapter().facts().graphics
    }

    /// The name Wine, Neptune and Obelisk's reports know it by.
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::D3DMetal => "d3dmetal",
            Self::Dxmt => "dxmt",
        }
    }
}

/// What a game asks of D3DMetal on Rosetta's Wine. The Linux engine's render
/// servers take none of these.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct GraphicsOptions {
    /// Direct3D 12 offers DirectX Raytracing, as D3DMetal does by default.
    pub ray_tracing: bool,
}

impl Default for GraphicsOptions {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self { ray_tracing: true }
    }
}

/// The Wine prefix of the Windows installation in `install`, named after the
/// installation's folder.
pub fn prefix(prefixes: &Path, install: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, Error> {
    let name = install.file_name().ok_or(Error::NotExecutable)?;
    Ok(prefixes.join(name))
}

impl Config {
    /// The adapter of the engine its Launch settings name. It is derived on
    /// each call, never kept: a configuration crosses to its Game session as
    /// JSON.
    fn adapter(&self) -> &'static dyn Adapter {
        self.settings.engine.adapter()
    }

    /// How the game starts.
    pub(crate) fn architecture(&self) -> Architecture {
        self.adapter().facts().architecture
    }

    /// How long the engine's launcher gets on a Force Quit to stop its own
    /// servers before it is killed; none when it has none.
    pub(crate) fn launcher_grace(&self) -> Option<Duration> {
        self.adapter().facts().launcher_grace
    }

    /// The gamepad service the game's supervisor runs while the game does;
    /// none when the engine's launcher starts its own.
    pub(crate) fn input_service(&self) -> Option<PathBuf> {
        self.adapter()
            .facts()
            .input_service
            .map(|path| self.runtime.join(path))
    }

    /// Wine's `own` DLL overrides, then the profile's.
    fn with_profile_overrides(&self, own: &str) -> String {
        std::iter::once(own.to_owned())
            .chain(self.profile_overrides())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join(";")
    }

    /// The profile's DLL overrides, each as `WINEDLLOVERRIDES` spells it.
    fn profile_overrides(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = String> + '_ {
        self.settings
            .dll_overrides
            .iter()
            .map(|(dll, mode)| format!("{dll}={mode}"))
    }

    /// Wine's errors, unless a development runtime's `winedebug` file names
    /// other channels, such as `+steamclient`.
    fn debug_channels(&self) -> String {
        fs::read_to_string(self.runtime.join("winedebug"))
            .ok()
            .and_then(|channels| channels.lines().next().map(str::to_owned))
            .filter(|channels| !channels.is_empty())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "err+all,fixme-all".into())
    }

    /// The line the game's log starts with: how Obelisk runs it, for whoever
    /// reads the log, such as a bug report's reader. Of the arguments, only
    /// those its player adds: a storefront's may carry credentials.
    pub(crate) fn log_header(&self) -> String {
        let mut header = format!(
            "obelisk: engine={} graphics={}",
            self.adapter().facts().name,
            self.settings.graphics.name()
        );
        let ray_tracing = crate::launch_settings::offer(self.settings.engine)
            .graphics(self.settings.graphics)
            .is_some_and(|offer| {
                offer
                    .options
                    .contains(&crate::launch_settings::GraphicsOption::RayTracing)
            });
        if ray_tracing {
            let state = if self.settings.options.ray_tracing {
                "on"
            } else {
                "off"
            };
            header.push_str(&format!(" ray_tracing={state}"));
        }
        // Only a development runtime has no manifest.
        let voile = crate::voile::release_of(&self.runtime);
        header.push_str(&format!(
            " voile={}",
            voile.as_deref().unwrap_or("development")
        ));
        if !self.settings.variables.is_empty() {
            let variables: Vec<_> = self
                .settings
                .variables
                .iter()
                .map(|(name, value)| format!("{name}={value}"))
                .collect();
            header.push_str(&format!(" variables={}", typed(&variables)));
        }
        if !self.settings.dll_overrides.is_empty() {
            let overrides: Vec<_> = self.profile_overrides().collect();
            header.push_str(&format!(" dll_overrides={}", overrides.join(";")));
        }
        if !self.settings.arguments.is_empty() {
            header.push_str(&format!(" arguments={}", typed(&self.settings.arguments)));
        }
        header.push('\n');
        header
    }
}

/// One engine's side of a Windows game: where it keeps an installation's
/// prefix and its runtime, how it readies the prefix and starts the game
/// there, and how what runs there ends. Rosetta's Wine and the Linux engine
/// are its two adapters; `Engine::adapter` picks one.
trait Adapter {
    /// What the engine is, whatever the game.
    fn facts(&self) -> &'static Facts;
    /// Its runtime among Voile's in `voile`, once installed.
    fn runtime(&self, voile: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf>;
    /// Its prefix of the installation whose Rosetta prefix is `rosetta`.
    fn prefix(&self, rosetta: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, Error>;
    /// Readies config's prefix for a game whose program is already checked:
    /// creates or updates it, has `storefront` furnish it, then makes the
    /// log's folder. Fails with WineUnavailable before the prefix is created.
    fn ready(
        &self,
        config: &Config,
        locations: &crate::Locations,
        storefront: &dyn Furnisher,
    ) -> Result<(), Error>;
    /// How `program`, checked inside `game.install`, starts with
    /// `launched`'s arguments and working directory, behind the storefront's
    /// helper, with `environment`, the Game session's own.
    fn target(
        &self,
        config: &Config,
        game: &Game<'_>,
        launched: &LaunchTarget,
        program: PathBuf,
        additions: Additions,
        environment: HashMap<String, String>,
    ) -> Result<Target, Error>;
    /// A file the game reads, in a private folder that lives as long as the
    /// returned TempDir, and its Windows path.
    fn private_file(
        &self,
        config: &Config,
        name: &str,
        bytes: &[u8],
    ) -> Result<(tempfile::TempDir, String), Error>;
    /// The command asking the game to close its windows, if it can be asked.
    /// `environment` is the game's own, `pid` its launch helper's.
    fn quit_command(
        &self,
        config: &Config,
        environment: &HashMap<String, String>,
        program: Option<&Path>,
        pid: u32,
    ) -> Option<Command>;
    /// The command ending every process of the prefix at once; none when
    /// they follow the engine's launcher, which the session ends.
    fn end_command(&self, config: &Config) -> Option<Command>;
    /// The folders whose files only this game's processes use, given its
    /// environment and, once spawned, its launch helper's `pid`.
    fn private_folders(
        &self,
        config: &Config,
        environment: &HashMap<String, String>,
        pid: Option<u32>,
    ) -> Vec<PathBuf>;
    /// Deletes `prefix`, its prefix of an uninstalled installation. A missing
    /// one is already gone; a link in its place is never followed.
    fn remove(
        &self,
        locations: &crate::Locations,
        prefix: &Path,
    ) -> Result<(), obelisk_core::installation::RemovalFailure>;
}

/// What an engine is, whatever the game it runs.
struct Facts {
    /// How the game's log names it.
    name: &'static str,
    /// How its games start.
    architecture: Architecture,
    /// The gamepad service its supervisor runs while the game does, inside
    /// its runtime; none when the engine's launcher starts its own.
    input_service: Option<&'static str>,
    /// What renders its games when neither the game's profile nor its player
    /// picks another backend.
    graphics: Graphics,
    /// How long its launcher gets on a Force Quit to stop its own servers
    /// before it is killed; none when it has none.
    launcher_grace: Option<Duration>,
    /// The variables and DLL overrides its Wine gets from Obelisk.
    reserved: Reserved,
}

/// Names Obelisk sets in an engine's Wine. A profile could still replace one
/// for its game; the profiles table sets none, and a table that does loses
/// that game.
pub(crate) struct Reserved {
    pub variables: &'static [&'static str],
    pub dlls: &'static [&'static str],
}

/// What a storefront adds to its games' launches, as an engine reads it.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Additions {
    /// `Storefront::HELPER`.
    helper: Option<&'static str>,
    /// `Storefront::PASSED`.
    passed: &'static [&'static str],
    /// `Storefront::STEAM_CLIENT`.
    steam_client: bool,
}

impl Additions {
    fn of<S: Storefront>() -> Self {
        Self {
            helper: S::HELPER,
            passed: S::PASSED,
            steam_client: S::STEAM_CLIENT,
        }
    }
}

/// A storefront as an engine readies a prefix for it, whatever its type.
/// Its methods are named apart from `Storefront`'s: with both traits in
/// scope, a call on a concrete storefront would be ambiguous.
trait Furnisher {
    /// What it adds to its games' launches.
    fn additions(&self) -> Additions;
    /// `Storefront::furnish`.
    fn furnish_prefix(&self, config: &Config) -> Result<(), Error>;
    /// `Storefront::prerequisites`.
    fn prerequisites_to_run(&self) -> Result<Vec<Prerequisite>, Error>;
}

impl<S: Storefront> Furnisher for S {
    fn additions(&self) -> Additions {
        Additions::of::<S>()
    }
    fn furnish_prefix(&self, config: &Config) -> Result<(), Error> {
        Storefront::furnish(self, config)
    }
    fn prerequisites_to_run(&self) -> Result<Vec<Prerequisite>, Error> {
        Storefront::prerequisites(self)
    }
}

impl Engine {
    /// The adapter that runs this engine's games.
    fn adapter(self) -> &'static dyn Adapter {
        match self {
            Self::Rosetta => &rosetta::RosettaWine,
            Self::Linux => &linux_engine::LinuxEngine,
        }
    }

    /// The names Obelisk sets in this engine's Wine.
    pub(crate) fn reserved(self) -> &'static Reserved {
        &self.adapter().facts().reserved
    }
}

/// What one storefront adds to the prefix of its Windows installations, and
/// to the games that start there.
pub trait Storefront {
    /// The Windows program its games start behind, given the game's program
    /// and arguments, such as Steam's steam.exe.
    const HELPER: Option<&'static str> = None;
    /// Variables its games read that exist only once their Game session
    /// starts them, such as the Steam host's ports.
    const PASSED: &'static [&'static str] = &[];
    /// Whether its games reach Valve's steamclient through lsteamclient.
    const STEAM_CLIENT: bool = false;
    /// The programs it names to run once in a prefix before a game first
    /// starts, in order.
    fn prerequisites(&self) -> Result<Vec<Prerequisite>, Error>;
    /// Places its own files in the prefix, before any prerequisite runs.
    fn furnish(&self, _config: &Config) -> Result<(), Error> {
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// A storefront's Windows game as Wine starts it: its installation's folder
/// and its name in the store.
pub(crate) struct Game<'a> {
    pub install: &'a Path,
    pub title: &'a str,
}

/// Readies the prefix of the Windows installation in `install` to start
/// `target`: the game must be a Windows program inside the installation; then
/// its engine readies the prefix. Nothing touches the prefix for a game that
/// cannot start.
fn prepare<S: Storefront>(
    config: &Config,
    locations: &crate::Locations,
    install: &Path,
    target: &LaunchTarget,
    storefront: &S,
) -> Result<(), Error> {
    program(install, target)?;
    config.adapter().ready(config, locations, storefront)
}

/// The game `target` names, or the program its launch settings start
/// instead, that Wine starts in the prefix with `environment` and Wine's own
/// settings, as S completes it, logging to the installation's log.
pub(crate) fn target<S: Storefront>(
    config: &Config,
    game: &Game<'_>,
    target: &LaunchTarget,
    environment: HashMap<String, String>,
) -> Result<Target, Error> {
    let launched = config.settings.started(game.install, target);
    let program = program(game.install, &launched)?;
    config.adapter().target(
        config,
        game,
        &launched,
        program,
        Additions::of::<S>(),
        environment,
    )
}

/// A file the game reads, in a private folder that lives as long as the
/// returned TempDir, and its Windows path. Rosetta's Wine reads it on the
/// Mac's disk, through its Z: drive; the engine's guest, which cannot see
/// that disk, in the prefix's C: drive.
pub(crate) fn private_file(
    config: &Config,
    name: &str,
    bytes: &[u8],
) -> Result<(tempfile::TempDir, String), Error> {
    config.adapter().private_file(config, name, bytes)
}

/// The Windows program `target` names, when it is one inside `install`.
fn program(install: &Path, target: &LaunchTarget) -> Result<PathBuf, Error> {
    let root = install.canonicalize()?;
    let executable = Path::new(&target.executable)
        .canonicalize()
        .map_err(|_| Error::NotExecutable)?;
    if !executable.starts_with(&root) || !portable_executable(&executable)? {
        return Err(Error::NotExecutable);
    }
    Ok(executable)
}

/// A program run once in a prefix before its game starts, such as a DirectX
/// installer. Storefronts name them: Steam in install scripts, Epic in its
/// manifests.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Prerequisite {
    /// A prefix runs each id once.
    pub id: String,
    /// Run in order, each with its Windows command line.
    pub programs: Vec<(PathBuf, String)>,
}

/// Where `path` is inside a prefix of Rosetta's Wine, whose Z: drive is the
/// Mac's root.
pub(crate) fn windows_path(path: &Path) -> String {
    format!("Z:{}", path.to_string_lossy().replace('/', "\\"))
}

/// One Windows installation: its game runs in Wine, in the installation's own
/// prefix, where its saves live too. The prefix is readied before each launch
/// and goes when the installation is uninstalled.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Installation {
    install: PathBuf,
    prefix: PathBuf,
    /// Where Wine logs while its game runs.
    log: PathBuf,
    settings: crate::launch_settings::Settings,
}

impl Installation {
    /// The installation of `game` in `install`, when `platform` is the
    /// Windows build, run as the game's profile and its player's launch
    /// settings say.
    pub fn of(
        locations: &crate::Locations,
        game: crate::profile::Game<'_>,
        platform: Platform,
        install: &Path,
    ) -> Result<Option<Self>, Error> {
        if platform != Platform::Windows {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let settings = crate::launch_settings::of(&locations.library, game, install).settings;
        let rosetta = prefix(&locations.wine_prefixes, install)?;
        let prefix = settings.engine.adapter().prefix(&rosetta)?;
        Ok(Some(Self {
            install: install.to_owned(),
            prefix,
            log: log(locations, game),
            settings,
        }))
    }

    /// The Windows machine the installation runs in.
    pub fn prefix(&self) -> &Path {
        &self.prefix
    }

    /// Readies the prefix, with `storefront`'s additions, to start `target`
    /// or the program the game's profile names instead, and returns how its
    /// game runs. D3DMetal is translated before a game that renders with it
    /// starts.
    pub fn ready<S: Storefront>(
        &self,
        locations: &crate::Locations,
        target: &LaunchTarget,
        storefront: &S,
    ) -> Result<Config, Error> {
        let config = self.runtime(locations)?;
        let target = self.settings.started(&self.install, target);
        prepare(&config, locations, &self.install, &target, storefront)?;
        Ok(config)
    }

    /// How its game runs, once Voile is installed.
    fn runtime(&self, locations: &crate::Locations) -> Result<Config, Error> {
        let runtime = self.settings.engine.adapter().runtime(&locations.voile);
        Ok(Config {
            runtime: runtime.ok_or(Error::WineUnavailable)?,
            prefix: self.prefix.clone(),
            log: self.log.clone(),
            settings: self.settings.clone(),
        })
    }

    /// Forgets the prerequisites `forget` picks among those its Rosetta
    /// prefix ran: they run again at the next launch. Only Rosetta's Wine runs
    /// prerequisites.
    pub(crate) fn forget_prerequisites(
        &self,
        locations: &crate::Locations,
        forget: impl Fn(&str) -> bool,
    ) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        let rosetta = prefix(&locations.wine_prefixes, &self.install)
            .map_err(|error| std::io::Error::other(error.to_string()))?;
        rosetta::forget_prerequisites(&rosetta, forget)
    }

    /// Deletes the prefixes of the uninstalled installation, as Steam deletes
    /// a Proton prefix, and its launch settings. Both engines' go, whichever
    /// runs the game now: an earlier launch may have made the other's before
    /// the game moved. A missing prefix is already gone; a link in its place
    /// is never followed.
    pub fn remove(
        &self,
        locations: &crate::Locations,
    ) -> Result<(), obelisk_core::installation::RemovalFailure> {
        use obelisk_core::installation::RemovalFailure;
        let unsafe_prefix = |_| RemovalFailure::Unsafe(self.prefix.clone());
        let rosetta = prefix(&locations.wine_prefixes, &self.install).map_err(unsafe_prefix)?;
        for engine in [Engine::Linux, Engine::Rosetta] {
            let adapter = engine.adapter();
            adapter.remove(locations, &adapter.prefix(&rosetta).map_err(unsafe_prefix)?)?;
        }
        crate::launch_settings::remove(&locations.library, &self.install)?;
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Where Wine logs `game`: in its storefront's diagnostics folder.
fn log(locations: &crate::Locations, game: crate::profile::Game<'_>) -> PathBuf {
    crate::diagnostics::game_log(&locations.home, game.into(), Platform::Windows)
}

/// Deletes `folder`. A missing one is already gone; a link in its place is
/// never followed.
fn remove_folder(folder: &Path) -> Result<(), obelisk_core::installation::RemovalFailure> {
    use obelisk_core::installation::RemovalFailure;
    match fs::symlink_metadata(folder) {
        Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(()),
        Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
        Ok(metadata) if !metadata.is_dir() => {
            return Err(RemovalFailure::Unsafe(folder.to_owned()));
        }
        Ok(_) => {}
    }
    Ok(fs::remove_dir_all(folder)?)
}

/// The exit code of `child`, or `None` once it ran for `timeout` and was killed.
pub(crate) fn wait(mut child: Child, timeout: Duration) -> Result<Option<i32>, Error> {
    let deadline = Instant::now() + timeout;
    loop {
        if let Some(status) = child.try_wait()? {
            return Ok(Some(status.code().unwrap_or(-1)));
        }
        if Instant::now() >= deadline {
            child.kill()?;
            child.wait()?;
            return Ok(None);
        }
        thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
    }
}

/// Ends every process of the prefix: Wine asks them to quit, then kills
/// those that remain, including the ones it started apart from the game.
pub(crate) fn stop(config: &Config) {
    if let Some(mut command) = config.adapter().end_command(config) {
        let _ = command
            .stdin(Stdio::null())
            .stdout(Stdio::null())
            .stderr(Stdio::null())
            .status();
    }
}

/// Asks the Windows game to quit as its player closing its windows would, and
/// kills nothing. `environment` is the game's own, `pid` its launch helper's.
pub(crate) fn quit(
    config: &Config,
    environment: &HashMap<String, String>,
    program: Option<&Path>,
    pid: u32,
) {
    if let Some(command) = config
        .adapter()
        .quit_command(config, environment, program, pid)
    {
        let _ = run(command, QUIT_TIMEOUT);
    }
}

/// Kills every process of the prefix at once. Unlike `stop`, it never waits
/// on a Wine server frozen with its game for longer than `QUIT_TIMEOUT`.
pub(crate) fn kill(config: &Config) {
    if let Some(command) = config.adapter().end_command(config) {
        let _ = run(command, QUIT_TIMEOUT);
    }
}

/// The folders whose files only the game's processes use, given its
/// `environment` and, once spawned, its launch helper's `pid`.
pub(crate) fn private_folders(
    config: &Config,
    environment: &HashMap<String, String>,
    pid: Option<u32>,
) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
    config.adapter().private_folders(config, environment, pid)
}

/// Runs `command` without input or output for at most `timeout`.
fn run(mut command: Command, timeout: Duration) -> Result<Option<i32>, Error> {
    let child = command
        .stdin(Stdio::null())
        .stdout(Stdio::null())
        .stderr(Stdio::null())
        .spawn()?;
    wait(child, timeout)
}

/// Ends the Wine processes an Obelisk that died left behind, and returns how
/// many. macOS ends every process of an Obelisk that dies, its sessions'
/// supervisors and Steam hosts included, but not the Windows processes Wine
/// starts apart: those froze without their session, and nothing else runs
/// from `voile`.
pub fn end_orphans(voile: &Path) -> usize {
    let mut command = Command::new("/usr/sbin/lsof");
    command.args(["-n", "-P", "-d", "txt", "-Fpn"]);
    let Some(listing) = crate::supervisor::quit::listing(command) else {
        return 0;
    };
    let voile = voile.canonicalize().unwrap_or_else(|_| voile.to_owned());
    let orphans = running_from(&listing, &voile, std::process::id());
    crate::supervisor::quit::kill(&orphans);
    orphans.len()
}

/// The processes of an `lsof -Fpn` listing that run files from `root`.
fn running_from(listing: &str, root: &Path, own: u32) -> Vec<u32> {
    let mut found = Vec::new();
    let mut pid = None;
    for line in listing.lines() {
        if let Some(value) = line.strip_prefix('p') {
            pid = value.parse::<u32>().ok().filter(|pid| *pid != own);
        } else if let Some(path) = line.strip_prefix('n')
            && let Some(current) = pid
            && Path::new(path).starts_with(root)
            && !found.contains(&current)
        {
            found.push(current);
        }
    }
    found
}

/// Splits a Windows command line on the spaces outside double quotes.
pub(crate) fn command_line(line: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut arguments = Vec::new();
    let mut current = String::new();
    let mut quoted = false;
    let mut started = false;
    for character in line.chars() {
        match character {
            '"' => {
                quoted = !quoted;
                started = true;
            }
            ' ' | '\t' if !quoted => {
                if started {
                    arguments.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
                    started = false;
                }
            }
            _ => {
                current.push(character);
                started = true;
            }
        }
    }
    if started {
        arguments.push(current);
    }
    arguments
}

/// `arguments` as a command line `command_line` splits back into them.
fn typed(arguments: &[String]) -> String {
    arguments
        .iter()
        .map(|argument| {
            if argument.is_empty() || argument.contains([' ', '\t']) {
                format!("\"{argument}\"")
            } else {
                argument.clone()
            }
        })
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join(" ")
}

/// Whether `path` starts like a Windows program: a DOS header naming a PE header.
fn portable_executable(path: &Path) -> Result<bool, Error> {
    let mut file = fs::File::open(path)?;
    let mut dos = [0u8; 64];
    if file.read_exact(&mut dos).is_err() || &dos[..2] != b"MZ" {
        return Ok(false);
    }
    let offset = u32::from_le_bytes(dos[60..64].try_into().expect("four bytes")) as u64;
    let mut signature = [0u8; 4];
    use std::io::{Seek, SeekFrom};
    file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(offset))?;
    Ok(file.read_exact(&mut signature).is_ok() && &signature == b"PE\0\0")
}

#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) mod tests;

```

`crates/game-runtime/src/wine/linux_engine.rs`:

```rs
//! Voile's Linux engine. A Windows game whose anti-cheat supports Linux, such
//! as Rocket League's Easy Anti-Cheat, runs in voile-wine built for x86-64
//! Linux, which voile-lkd's engine executes in native macOS processes: the
//! anti-cheat then loads its Linux module. Only the games whose Launch settings
//! name the engine run there, by their profile's choice or their player's;
//! every other Windows game keeps Rosetta's Wine.
use super::{Adapter, Additions, Config, Facts, Furnisher, Game, Graphics};
use crate::{
    Error,
    supervisor::{Target, architecture::Architecture},
};
use obelisk_core::launch::LaunchTarget;
use std::{
    collections::HashMap,
    fs,
    path::{Path, PathBuf},
    process::{Command, Stdio},
    time::Duration,
};

/// Starts the window server and Neptune's render server, then the game, and
/// ends them with it (see the script).
const LAUNCHER: &str = include_str!("linux_engine/launch.sh");
/// The private folder of the window server and the render server that the
/// launcher with `pid` started, in the temporary folder of its `environment`.
fn sockets(environment: &HashMap<String, String>, pid: u32) -> PathBuf {
    let root = environment
        .get("TMPDIR")
        .filter(|root| !root.is_empty())
        .map_or("/tmp", String::as_str);
    Path::new(root).join(format!("obelisk-engine-{pid}"))
}

/// The window server socket of the launcher with `pid`.
fn window_server(environment: &HashMap<String, String>, pid: u32) -> PathBuf {
    sockets(environment, pid).join("wsd.sock")
}

/// The launcher's variable that names the game in the menu bar, the Dock and
/// Cmd-Tab: its name in the store, or its program's file name without one.
pub(crate) const APP_NAME: &str = "OBELISK_APP_NAME";
/// A store title as an application name: without the trademark signs stores
/// add ("Rocket League®"), which Mac apps leave out.
fn app_name(title: &str) -> String {
    title
        .chars()
        .filter(|c| !matches!(c, '®' | '™' | '©'))
        .collect::<String>()
        .trim()
        .to_owned()
}

/// The guest sees the installation here, and the prefix in its home. Every
/// folder above a mount must exist in the engine's root: Wine's CreateProcess
/// lists each folder of the program's path, and a folder the engine makes up
/// for a mount, such as /games for /games/game, cannot be handed to the Wine
/// server, which then ends the game.
const GAME: &str = "/opt/game";
const HOME: &str = "/home/user";
/// The runtime's Steam folder, where linux64 holds Valve's Linux steamclient.
const STEAM: &str = "/opt/steam";
/// The runtime's guest libraries.
const LIBRARIES: &str = "/opt/obelisk";
/// The library that gives Valve's steamclient the macOS pid of its process.
const HOST_PID: &str = "steam-hostpid.so";
/// The prefix's folder in the guest's home.
const PREFIX: &str = "prefix";
/// Neptune's Direct3D, which replaces Wine's in the prefix.
const DIRECT3D: [&str; 3] = ["d3d11.dll", "dxgi.dll", "d3d12.dll"];
/// Creating a prefix through the engine takes about a minute.
const BOOT_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10 * 60);
/// Records, in a runtime, the macOS build Rosetta translated its D3DMetal for.
const TRANSLATED: &str = ".obelisk-d3dmetal-translated";
/// Translating D3DMetal takes about 8 seconds; one still running after this
/// long is abandoned, and the game pays for the rest.
const TRANSLATION_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2 * 60);
/// How long the launcher gets to stop its own servers on a Force Quit; it
/// gives them a second.
const LAUNCHER_GRACE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2);

/// Voile's Linux engine.
pub(super) struct LinuxEngine;

static FACTS: Facts = Facts {
    name: "wine-linux",
    // The launcher is a native program.
    architecture: Architecture::Arm64,
    input_service: None,
    graphics: Graphics::Dxmt,
    launcher_grace: Some(LAUNCHER_GRACE),
    reserved: super::Reserved {
        variables: &[
            "HOME",
            "USER",
            "LOGNAME",
            "PATH",
            "LANG",
            "WINEPREFIX",
            "WINEARCH",
            "WINEDEBUG",
            "WINEDLLOVERRIDES",
            "VTEST_SOCKET_NAME",
            "NPT_DEBUG",
            "LD_PRELOAD",
        ],
        dlls: &[
            "mscoree",
            "mshtml",
            "winemenubuilder.exe",
            "d3d11",
            "dxgi",
            "d3d12",
        ],
    },
};

impl Adapter for LinuxEngine {
    fn facts(&self) -> &'static Facts {
        &FACTS
    }

    fn runtime(&self, voile: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf> {
        crate::voile::linux_runtime(voile)
    }

    fn prefix(&self, rosetta: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, Error> {
        prefix(rosetta)
    }

    /// The prefix is created through the engine on first use, lsteamclient
    /// is led to Valve's Linux steamclient for a storefront whose games reach
    /// it, the storefront furnishes the prefix, and Neptune's Direct3D goes
    /// into it before each launch. Storefront prerequisites do not run there.
    /// D3DMetal is translated before a game that renders with it starts.
    fn ready(
        &self,
        config: &Config,
        locations: &crate::Locations,
        storefront: &dyn Furnisher,
    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
        if !installed(config) {
            return Err(Error::WineUnavailable);
        }
        crate::files::private_directory(home(&config.prefix)?)?;
        if !config.prefix.join("system.reg").is_file() {
            boot(config)?;
        }
        if storefront.additions().steam_client {
            link_steam_client(config)?;
        }
        storefront.furnish_prefix(config)?;
        let system32 = config.prefix.join("drive_c/windows/system32");
        for library in DIRECT3D {
            fs::copy(
                config.runtime.join("windows").join(library),
                system32.join(library),
            )?;
        }
        match config.log.parent() {
            Some(logs) => crate::files::private_directory(logs)?,
            None => return Err(Error::Storage),
        }
        translate_d3dmetal(config, &locations.helpers);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// The game starts through the engine's launcher, in a guest the
    /// storefront completes. The menu bar, the Dock and Cmd-Tab show its
    /// title, or the program's file name without one.
    fn target(
        &self,
        config: &Config,
        game: &Game<'_>,
        launched: &LaunchTarget,
        program: PathBuf,
        additions: Additions,
        environment: HashMap<String, String>,
    ) -> Result<Target, Error> {
        let guest = Guest::of(config, additions.steam_client);
        let executable = guest_path(game.install, &program).ok_or(Error::NotExecutable)?;
        let name = match (
            app_name(game.title),
            Path::new(&launched.executable).file_stem(),
        ) {
            (name, Some(stem)) if name.is_empty() => stem.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
            (name, _) => name,
        };
        let mut environment = environment;
        environment.insert(APP_NAME.to_owned(), name);
        let install = game.install.canonicalize()?;
        let working_directory = guest_path(&install, Path::new(&launched.working_directory))
            .unwrap_or_else(|| GAME.to_owned());
        let mut arguments = vec![
            "-c".to_owned(),
            LAUNCHER.to_owned(),
            "obelisk-linux-engine".to_owned(),
            config.runtime.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
            home(&config.prefix)?.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
            install.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
            working_directory,
            "--graphics".to_owned(),
            config.settings.graphics.name().to_owned(),
        ];
        for (path, folder) in &guest.binds {
            arguments.push("--bind".to_owned());
            arguments.push(format!("{path}={}:ro", folder.display()));
        }
        let variables = guest_environment(config).into_iter().chain(
            guest
                .environment
                .iter()
                .map(|(name, value)| ((*name).to_owned(), value.clone())),
        );
        for (name, value) in variables {
            arguments.push("--env".to_owned());
            arguments.push(format!("{name}={value}"));
        }
        // The launcher hands the guest the variables the storefront's games
        // get from their session, which exist only once the game starts.
        for name in additions.passed {
            arguments.push("--pass".to_owned());
            arguments.push((*name).to_owned());
        }
        arguments.push("--".to_owned());
        arguments.extend(additions.helper.map(str::to_owned));
        arguments.push(executable);
        arguments.extend(launched.arguments.iter().cloned());
        Ok(Target {
            executable: "/bin/bash".into(),
            arguments,
            working_directory: install.clone(),
            environment,
            log: Some(config.log.clone()),
            installation: Some(install),
            program: Some(program),
        })
    }

    /// The guest cannot see the Mac's disk, so the file goes into the
    /// prefix's C: drive.
    fn private_file(
        &self,
        config: &Config,
        name: &str,
        bytes: &[u8],
    ) -> Result<(tempfile::TempDir, String), Error> {
        let drive = config.prefix.join("drive_c");
        let (directory, _) = crate::files::private_temp_file(&drive, ".obelisk-", name, bytes)?;
        let folder = directory
            .path()
            .file_name()
            .ok_or(Error::Storage)?
            .to_string_lossy()
            .into_owned();
        Ok((directory, format!("C:\\{folder}\\{name}")))
    }

    /// The window server asks every window of the game to close, as its own
    /// Quit menu does; a game that shows no window yet is asked nothing.
    fn quit_command(
        &self,
        config: &Config,
        environment: &HashMap<String, String>,
        _program: Option<&Path>,
        pid: u32,
    ) -> Option<Command> {
        let mut command = Command::new(config.runtime.join("engine/wsdctl"));
        command
            .arg(window_server(environment, pid))
            .args(["window", "quit"])
            .env_clear();
        Some(command)
    }

    fn end_command(&self, _config: &Config) -> Option<Command> {
        // The engine's processes follow its launcher, which the session stops
        // or kills.
        None
    }

    /// The guest's home, and once the launcher runs, its servers' folder.
    fn private_folders(
        &self,
        config: &Config,
        environment: &HashMap<String, String>,
        pid: Option<u32>,
    ) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
        let mut folders = home(&config.prefix)
            .map(|home| vec![home.to_owned()])
            .unwrap_or_default();
        if let Some(pid) = pid {
            folders.push(sockets(environment, pid));
        }
        folders
    }

    fn remove(
        &self,
        _locations: &crate::Locations,
        prefix: &Path,
    ) -> Result<(), obelisk_core::installation::RemovalFailure> {
        use obelisk_core::installation::RemovalFailure;
        super::remove_folder(home(prefix).map_err(|_| RemovalFailure::Unsafe(prefix.to_owned()))?)
    }
}

/// The engine's prefix of the installation whose Rosetta prefix is
/// `rosetta`: its own folder beside it, the prefix inside, since the guest
/// sees that folder as its home.
fn prefix(rosetta: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, Error> {
    let name = rosetta.file_name().ok_or(Error::Storage)?;
    let mut home = name.to_owned();
    home.push("-linux");
    Ok(rosetta.with_file_name(home).join(PREFIX))
}

/// The guest's home of an engine prefix.
fn home(prefix: &Path) -> Result<&Path, Error> {
    prefix.parent().ok_or(Error::Storage)
}

/// Whether the runtime is in place.
fn installed(config: &Config) -> bool {
    config.runtime.join("engine/fexdarwin-run").is_file()
}

/// What every Wine command of the engine runs with in the guest, then the
/// variables the game's profile adds.
fn guest_environment(config: &Config) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
    let own = [
        ("HOME", HOME.into()),
        ("USER", "user".into()),
        ("LOGNAME", "user".into()),
        ("PATH", "/opt/wine/bin:/usr/bin:/bin".into()),
        ("LANG", "en_US.UTF-8".into()),
        ("WINEPREFIX", format!("{HOME}/{PREFIX}")),
        ("WINEARCH", "win64".into()),
        ("WINEDEBUG", config.debug_channels()),
        (
            "WINEDLLOVERRIDES",
            config
                .with_profile_overrides("mscoree,mshtml=;winemenubuilder.exe=d;d3d11,dxgi,d3d12=n"),
        ),
        ("VTEST_SOCKET_NAME", "/run/obelisk/vtest.sock".into()),
        ("NPT_DEBUG", "force_vtest".into()),
    ];
    own.into_iter()
        .map(|(name, value)| (name.to_owned(), value))
        .chain(config.settings.variables.clone())
        .collect()
}

/// Where the guest sees `path`, a file or folder inside `install`.
fn guest_path(install: &Path, path: &Path) -> Option<String> {
    let root = install.canonicalize().ok()?;
    let path = path.canonicalize().ok()?;
    let relative = path.strip_prefix(&root).ok()?;
    Some(match relative.as_os_str().is_empty() {
        true => GAME.to_owned(),
        false => format!("{GAME}/{}", relative.to_string_lossy()),
    })
}

/// Creates the prefix through the engine, under its timeout wrapper, which
/// ends every process of the engine it started.
fn boot(config: &Config) -> Result<(), Error> {
    let engine = config.runtime.join("engine");
    let mut command = Command::new(engine.join("run-with-timeout.sh"));
    command
        .arg(BOOT_TIMEOUT.as_secs().to_string())
        .arg(engine.join("fexdarwin-run"))
        .args(["--cwd", HOME]);
    for (name, value) in guest_environment(config) {
        command.arg("--env").arg(format!("{name}={value}"));
    }
    let status = command
        .args([
            "/bin/sh",
            "-c",
            "/opt/wine/bin/wine wineboot --init; /opt/wine/bin/wineserver -w",
        ])
        .env_clear()
        .env("FEXDARWIN_LKD", "1")
        .env("FEXDARWIN_ROOT", config.runtime.join("root"))
        .env("FEXDARWIN_ROOT_RO", "1")
        .env("FEXDARWIN_BIND", binds(config, None)?)
        .stdin(Stdio::null())
        .stdout(Stdio::null())
        .stderr(Stdio::null())
        .status()?;
    if !status.success() || !config.prefix.join("system.reg").is_file() {
        return Err(Error::StartFailed);
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// The engine's folders as the guest sees them; a launch adds the game.
fn binds(config: &Config, install: Option<&Path>) -> Result<String, Error> {
    let mut binds = vec![
        format!("/opt/wine={}:ro", config.runtime.join("wine").display()),
        format!("{HOME}={}", home(&config.prefix)?.display()),
    ];
    if let Some(install) = install {
        binds.push(format!("{GAME}={}", install.display()));
    }
    Ok(binds.join(";"))
}

/// Has Rosetta translate D3DMetal and the Intel render server before the
/// first game of `config` that renders with D3DMetal. The render server
/// loads D3DMetal when its game first asks for Direct3D, and translating it
/// then holds the game about 7 seconds, long enough for Easy Anti-Cheat to
/// give up. Rosetta keeps a translation per file until macOS updates, so it
/// runs once per runtime and macOS build, through Obelisk's Intel helper in
/// `helpers`. A failure only leaves the cost to the game.
fn translate_d3dmetal(config: &Config, helpers: &Path) {
    if config.settings.graphics != Graphics::D3DMetal {
        return;
    }
    let (Some(system), Some(release)) = (macos_build(), config.runtime.parent()) else {
        return;
    };
    let record = config.runtime.join(TRANSLATED);
    if fs::read_to_string(&record).is_ok_and(|translated| translated == system) {
        return;
    }
    let server = config.runtime.join("graphics/x86_64");
    // Each server is translated as it starts, and stops at an unknown option.
    for program in ["bin/virgl_test_server", "libexec/virgl_render_server"] {
        let mut command = Command::new(server.join(program));
        command.arg("--obelisk-translate");
        quietly(command);
    }
    let mut command = Command::new(helpers.join(crate::package::SDK_INTEL));
    command
        .arg("warm-d3dmetal")
        .arg(server.join("lib/libd3dmetal-native.dylib"))
        .arg(release.join("lib/external/D3DMetal.framework"));
    if quietly(command) == Some(0) {
        let _ = obelisk_core::write_atomic(&record, system.as_bytes());
    }
}

/// The exit code of `command`, run without input or output, or `None` when
/// it could not start or outlasted `TRANSLATION_TIMEOUT`.
fn quietly(mut command: Command) -> Option<i32> {
    let child = command
        .stdin(Stdio::null())
        .stdout(Stdio::null())
        .stderr(Stdio::null())
        .spawn()
        .ok()?;
    super::wait(child, TRANSLATION_TIMEOUT).ok().flatten()
}

/// The running macOS build, such as `25A354`.
fn macos_build() -> Option<String> {
    let output = Command::new("/usr/sbin/sysctl")
        .args(["-n", "kern.osversion"])
        .stdin(Stdio::null())
        .stderr(Stdio::null())
        .output()
        .ok()?;
    let build = String::from_utf8(output.stdout).ok()?.trim().to_owned();
    (output.status.success() && !build.is_empty()).then_some(build)
}

/// Leads lsteamclient to Valve's Linux steamclient: it loads the library the
/// guest home's .steam/sdk64 leads to, here the runtime's, which the guest
/// sees in /opt/steam.
fn link_steam_client(config: &Config) -> Result<(), Error> {
    let steam = home(&config.prefix)?.join(".steam");
    crate::files::private_directory(&steam)?;
    let link = steam.join("sdk64");
    let client = Path::new(STEAM).join("linux64");
    match fs::read_link(&link) {
        Ok(current) if current == client => return Ok(()),
        Ok(_) => fs::remove_file(&link)?,
        Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {}
        // Something that is not a link stands there.
        Err(_) => return Err(Error::Storage),
    }
    std::os::unix::fs::symlink(client, link)?;
    Ok(())
}

/// What a storefront's games need in the guest beyond Wine's own.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
struct Guest {
    /// Runtime folders the guest sees, read-only, by their guest path.
    binds: Vec<(&'static str, PathBuf)>,
    environment: Vec<(&'static str, String)>,
}

impl Guest {
    /// The guest of a storefront's games. When they reach Valve's steamclient,
    /// lsteamclient finds Valve's Linux steamclient in the runtime. Steam's
    /// engine drops a client whose pid is not a live macOS process: a runtime
    /// that carries steam-hostpid.so has it preloaded in every guest process,
    /// where it gives that pid to Valve's steamclient alone.
    fn of(config: &Config, steam_client: bool) -> Self {
        let mut guest = Self::default();
        if !steam_client {
            return guest;
        }
        guest.binds.push((STEAM, config.runtime.join("steam")));
        let libraries = config.runtime.join("guest");
        if libraries.join(HOST_PID).is_file() {
            guest.binds.push((LIBRARIES, libraries));
            guest
                .environment
                .push(("LD_PRELOAD", format!("{LIBRARIES}/{HOST_PID}")));
        }
        guest
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
pub(super) mod tests;

```

`crates/game-runtime/src/wine/linux_engine/launch.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Runs a Windows game through Voile's Linux engine (voile-lkd): voile-wine built for x86-64 Linux, which
# fexdarwin-run executes in native macOS processes. Starts the window server, Neptune's render server and the input
# service, then the game, and ends them when the game ends or this script is stopped. Every guest process follows
# this script (FEXDARWIN_SUPERVISOR_PID) and ends within half a second once it is gone.
#
# Usage: launch.sh RUNTIME HOME INSTALL CWD [OPTION]... -- EXECUTABLE [ARGUMENT]...
#   RUNTIME     the Linux engine runtime (engine/, graphics/, wine/, root/)
#   HOME        the guest's /home/user; the prefix is its prefix folder
#   INSTALL     the game's installation, seen as /opt/game
#   CWD         the guest working directory
#   EXECUTABLE  the guest path of the Windows program, which Wine starts with its arguments
# Options:
#   --graphics dxmt|d3dmetal  what renders the game's Direct3D (default dxmt)
#   --bind GUEST=HOST[:ro]    a folder the guest also sees, at GUEST, whose parent exists in the root
#   --env NAME=VALUE          a variable of the guest
#   --pass NAME               this script's variable NAME, when set, as a variable of the guest
# OBELISK_APP_NAME names the game in the menu bar, the Dock and Cmd-Tab.
set -u
runtime=$1 home=$2 install=$3 cwd=$4
shift 4
graphics=dxmt binds= guest_env=()
while [ $# -gt 0 ] && [ "$1" != "--" ]; do
    [ $# -ge 2 ] || exit 2
    case $1 in
    --graphics) graphics=$2 ;;
    --bind) binds="$binds;$2" ;;
    --env) guest_env+=(--env "$2") ;;
    --pass)
        [[ $2 =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]] || exit 2
        [ -n "${!2+set}" ] && guest_env+=(--env "$2=${!2}")
        ;;
    *) exit 2 ;;
    esac
    shift 2
done
shift

# The guest root has no time zone file: every program ran in UTC, and glibc looked for /etc/localtime again at each
# localtime() (about 80 times a second in ELDEN RING, 1.9 us each instead of 0.04). The rule that ends the Mac's zone
# file gives the guest the Mac's zone, unless the caller passed one.
case " ${guest_env[*]-} " in
*" TZ="*) ;;
*)
    tz=$(tail -n 1 /etc/localtime 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C tr -cd '[:print:]')
    [ -n "$tz" ] && guest_env+=(--env "TZ=$tz")
    ;;
esac

# Wine, the render server and D3DMetal keep a file open for each mapped resource. An app the Finder starts gets 256,
# which Wine outgrows: take up to 65536, as far as the hard limit and macOS allow.
files=$(ulimit -H -n)
{ [ "$files" = unlimited ] || [ "$files" -gt 65536 ]; } && files=65536
ulimit -S -n "$files" 2>/dev/null || ulimit -S -n 10240 2>/dev/null

# wsd and the render server bind UNIX sockets in a private folder; a relative path keeps them inside sun_path.
sockets_root=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}
sockets=obelisk-engine-$$
cd "$sockets_root" || exit 1
mkdir -m 700 "$sockets" || exit 1

helpers=()
game=
finish() {
    [ -n "$game" ] && kill -TERM "$game" 2>/dev/null
    for helper in ${helpers[@]+"${helpers[@]}"}; do kill -TERM "$helper" 2>/dev/null; done
    # They end within a few milliseconds of SIGTERM; a helper still there after a second is killed.
    for _ in $(seq 1 20); do
        alive=
        for helper in ${helpers[@]+"${helpers[@]}"}; do kill -0 "$helper" 2>/dev/null && alive=1; done
        [ -z "$alive" ] && break
        sleep 0.05
    done
    for helper in ${helpers[@]+"${helpers[@]}"}; do kill -KILL "$helper" 2>/dev/null; done
    rm -rf "${sockets_root:?}/$sockets"
}
trap 'finish; trap - EXIT; exit 143' TERM INT HUP
trap finish EXIT

# wsd runs from an application bundle named after the game: macOS takes the name in the menu bar, the Dock and
# Cmd-Tab from it (the game gives the icon). The bundle keeps one place per game, so Launch Services sees one app.
app_name=${OBELISK_APP_NAME:-Game}
app_name=${app_name//\//-}
app_id=$(printf '%s' "$app_name" | LC_ALL=C tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9' '-')
app="$sockets_root/obelisk-apps/$app_id/$app_name.app"
mkdir -p "$app/Contents/MacOS" || exit 1
rm -f "$app/Contents/MacOS/wsd"
cp -c "$runtime/engine/wsd" "$app/Contents/MacOS/wsd" 2>/dev/null || cp "$runtime/engine/wsd" "$app/Contents/MacOS/wsd" || exit 1
xml_name=$(printf '%s' "$app_name" | sed -e 's/&/\&amp;/g' -e 's/</\&lt;/g' -e 's/>/\&gt;/g')
cat > "$app/Contents/Info.plist" <<PLIST
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
  <key>CFBundleExecutable</key><string>wsd</string>
  <key>CFBundleIdentifier</key><string>com.zagrios.obelisk.game.$app_id</string>
  <key>CFBundleName</key><string>$xml_name</string>
  <key>CFBundleDisplayName</key><string>$xml_name</string>
  <key>CFBundlePackageType</key><string>APPL</string>
  <key>LSApplicationCategoryType</key><string>public.app-category.games</string>
  <key>NSHighResolutionCapable</key><true/>
</dict>
</plist>
PLIST

# The render server runs from a helper bundle inside the game's, one per graphics backend: Metal keeps its compiled
# shaders per bundle identifier. Outside a bundle every render server shared one cache, and each start of DXMT's arm64
# server emptied what D3DMetal's Intel server had compiled there: ELDEN RING compiled its 7,500 Metal functions again,
# about 4 minutes, after every Rocket League start. The helper is in place before wsd starts: for a moment after an
# executable of the bundle starts, macOS refuses any new file in it (EPERM). Prints the path to run.
render_server() {
    local helper="$app/Contents/Helpers/$2.app"
    local server="$helper/Contents/MacOS/virgl_render_server"
    mkdir -p "$helper/Contents/MacOS" || return 1
    # A copy kept from one launch to the next keeps its Rosetta translation.
    if ! cmp -s "$1" "$server"; then
        rm -f "$server"
        cp -c "$1" "$server" 2>/dev/null || cp "$1" "$server" || return 1
    fi
    cat > "$helper/Contents/Info.plist" <<PLIST
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
  <key>CFBundleExecutable</key><string>virgl_render_server</string>
  <key>CFBundleIdentifier</key><string>com.zagrios.obelisk.game.$app_id.$2</string>
  <key>CFBundleName</key><string>$xml_name</string>
  <key>CFBundlePackageType</key><string>APPL</string>
  <key>LSBackgroundOnly</key><true/>
</dict>
</plist>
PLIST
    # The Intel server starts at the game's first Direct3D call, inside Easy Anti-Cheat's window, and Rosetta
    # translates a new copy then: half a second. Have it translated now; it stops at the unknown option (9 ms once
    # translated).
    if [ "$2" = d3dmetal ]; then
        "$server" --obelisk-translate </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$server"
}
if [ "$graphics" = d3dmetal ]; then
    render=$(render_server "$runtime/graphics/x86_64/libexec/virgl_render_server" d3dmetal) || exit 1
else
    render=$(render_server "$runtime/graphics/libexec/virgl_render_server" dxmt) || exit 1
fi

"$app/Contents/MacOS/wsd" --dir "$sockets" &
helpers+=($!)
if [ "$graphics" = d3dmetal ]; then
    # D3DMetal is an Intel library: the Intel render server runs it under Rosetta. d3dmetal-native loads the
    # runtime's D3DMetal, unmodified, from its absolute path. DMN_RESIDENCY_SET=0: the game's buffers are made
    # resident by each command buffer that uses them instead of being pinned for good in a residency set. ELDEN
    # RING's three 4 GiB upload buffers then no longer count as GPU memory (14.6 GB instead of 26.3 on average), the
    # pinned memory no longer peaks at 24 GB while it loads, and the frame rate and hitches stay the same.
    server="$runtime/graphics/x86_64"
    d3dmetal="$server/lib/libd3dmetal-native.dylib"
    RENDER_SERVER_EXEC_PATH="$render" NPT_BACKEND=d3dmetal DMN_RESIDENCY_SET=0 \
        NPT_D3D11_LIBRARY_PATH="$d3dmetal" NPT_DXGI_LIBRARY_PATH="$d3dmetal" NPT_D3D12_LIBRARY_PATH="$d3dmetal" \
        D3DMETAL_FRAMEWORK_PATH="$runtime/../lib/external/D3DMetal.framework" \
        "$server/bin/virgl_test_server" --no-virgl --no-fork --socket-path "$sockets/vtest.sock" &
else
    dxmt="$runtime/graphics/dxmt-native.framework/Versions/A/dxmt-native"
    RENDER_SERVER_EXEC_PATH="$render" NPT_BACKEND=dxmt \
        NPT_D3D11_LIBRARY_PATH="$dxmt" NPT_DXGI_LIBRARY_PATH="$dxmt" NPT_D3D12_LIBRARY_PATH="$dxmt" \
        "$runtime/graphics/bin/virgl_test_server" --no-virgl --no-fork --socket-path "$sockets/vtest.sock" &
fi
helpers+=($!)
# The input service gives the Mac's gamepads to Wine's Obelisk bus. A runtime without it starts the game without
# gamepads.
input=
if [ -x "$runtime/engine/obelisk-input" ]; then
    "$runtime/engine/obelisk-input" --dir "$sockets" &
    helpers+=($!)
    input=1
fi
for _ in $(seq 1 100); do
    [ -S "$sockets/wsd.sock" ] && [ -S "$sockets/vtest.sock" ] && { [ -z "$input" ] || [ -S "$sockets/input.sock" ]; } &&
        break
    sleep 0.05
done

export FEXDARWIN_LKD=1 FEXDARWIN_ROOT="$runtime/root" FEXDARWIN_ROOT_RO=1 FEXDARWIN_SUPERVISOR_PID=$$
export FEXDARWIN_BIND="/opt/wine=$runtime/wine:ro;/home/user=$home;/opt/game=$install;/run/obelisk=$sockets_root/$sockets$binds"
# wineserver writes the registry only when it exits: wait for it inside the guest before the game ends. Started
# with -p0, it stops Wine's own processes as soon as the game's last process ends, instead of 3 seconds later.
"$runtime/engine/fexdarwin-run" --cwd "$cwd" ${guest_env[@]+"${guest_env[@]}"} \
    /bin/sh -c '/opt/wine/bin/wineserver -p0; /opt/wine/bin/wine "$@"; status=$?; /opt/wine/bin/wineserver -w; exit $status' sh "$@" &
game=$!
wait "$game"
status=$?
game=
exit "$status"
```

```rs
use super::*;
use crate::launch_settings::Settings;
use crate::wine;
use crate::wine::tests::{installation, pe, target as launch_target};

fn linux_config(root: &Path) -> wine::Config {
    wine::Config {
        runtime: root.join("runtime"),
        prefix: root.join("Prefixes/game-linux/prefix"),
        log: root.join("logs/wine-game.log"),
        settings: Settings {
            engine: wine::Engine::Linux,
            graphics: wine::Graphics::Dxmt,
            ..Settings::default()
        },
    }
}

/// A game installed in `install`, without a store title.
fn game(install: &Path) -> wine::Game<'_> {
    wine::Game { install, title: "" }
}

/// A storefront that adds nothing.
struct Plain;
impl wine::Storefront for Plain {
    fn prerequisites(&self) -> Result<Vec<wine::Prerequisite>, Error> {
        Ok(Vec::new())
    }
}

/// A storefront whose games start behind steam.exe and reach Valve's
/// steamclient, as Steam's do.
struct SteamClient;
impl wine::Storefront for SteamClient {
    const HELPER: Option<&'static str> = Some(r"C:\windows\system32\steam.exe");
    const PASSED: &'static [&'static str] = &["SteamAppId", "Steam3Master"];
    const STEAM_CLIENT: bool = true;
    fn prerequisites(&self) -> Result<Vec<wine::Prerequisite>, Error> {
        Ok(Vec::new())
    }
}

/// The values of every `option` pair in the launcher's arguments.
pub(crate) fn options<'a>(target: &'a Target, option: &str) -> Vec<&'a str> {
    let separator = target
        .arguments
        .iter()
        .position(|argument| argument == "--")
        .unwrap();
    target.arguments[7..separator]
        .chunks(2)
        .filter(|pair| pair[0] == option)
        .map(|pair| pair[1].as_str())
        .collect()
}

/// What the launcher starts in the guest: the program and its arguments.
pub(crate) fn guest_command(target: &Target) -> &[String] {
    let separator = target
        .arguments
        .iter()
        .position(|argument| argument == "--")
        .unwrap();
    &target.arguments[separator + 1..]
}

#[test]
fn the_engine_keeps_its_prefix_in_its_own_folder_beside_rosetta_s() {
    let rosetta = Path::new("/library/Prefixes/epic-game-Windows");
    let prefix = prefix(rosetta).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        prefix,
        Path::new("/library/Prefixes/epic-game-Windows-linux/prefix")
    );
    assert_eq!(
        home(&prefix).unwrap(),
        Path::new("/library/Prefixes/epic-game-Windows-linux")
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_game_starts_through_the_native_launcher_with_guest_paths() {
    let (_directory, root) = installation();
    let install = root.join("install");
    fs::create_dir_all(install.join("Binaries/Win64")).unwrap();
    let executable = install.join("Binaries/Win64/Game.exe");
    fs::write(&executable, pe()).unwrap();
    let config = linux_config(&root);
    let mut environment = HashMap::new();
    environment.insert("HOME".to_owned(), "/Users/player".to_owned());

    let target = wine::target::<Plain>(
        &config,
        &game(&install),
        &launch_target(&executable, &["-AUTH_TYPE=exchangecode"]),
        environment,
    )
    .unwrap();

    assert_eq!(target.executable, Path::new("/bin/bash"));
    assert_eq!(target.arguments[0], "-c");
    assert_eq!(target.arguments[1], LAUNCHER);
    assert_eq!(
        target.arguments[3..7],
        [
            root.join("runtime").to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
            root.join("Prefixes/game-linux")
                .to_string_lossy()
                .into_owned(),
            install.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
            "/opt/game/Binaries/Win64".to_owned(),
        ]
    );
    assert_eq!(
        guest_command(&target),
        [
            "/opt/game/Binaries/Win64/Game.exe",
            "-AUTH_TYPE=exchangecode"
        ]
    );
    assert!(options(&target, "--env").contains(&"WINEPREFIX=/home/user/prefix"));
    assert_eq!(options(&target, "--graphics"), ["dxmt"]);
    // Only a storefront's guest sees more of the runtime.
    assert!(options(&target, "--bind").is_empty());
    assert!(options(&target, "--pass").is_empty());
    assert_eq!(target.environment["HOME"], "/Users/player");
    // Without a title, the Dock names the game after its program.
    assert_eq!(target.environment[APP_NAME], "Game");
    assert_eq!(target.log, Some(config.log.clone()));
}

/// A Steam game whose program is `Game/start_protected_game.exe`, in a
/// runtime that carries steam-hostpid.so when `host_pid`.
fn steam_target(root: &Path, host_pid: bool) -> (wine::Config, Target) {
    let install = root.join("install");
    fs::create_dir_all(install.join("Game")).unwrap();
    let program = install.join("Game/start_protected_game.exe");
    fs::write(&program, pe()).unwrap();
    let config = linux_config(root);
    if host_pid {
        fs::create_dir_all(config.runtime.join("guest")).unwrap();
        fs::write(config.runtime.join("guest").join(HOST_PID), b"elf").unwrap();
    }
    let target = wine::target::<SteamClient>(
        &config,
        &game(&install),
        &launch_target(&program, &["-eac"]),
        HashMap::new(),
    )
    .unwrap();
    (config, target)
}

#[test]
fn a_steam_game_starts_behind_steam_exe_with_valve_s_linux_client_and_its_session_s_values() {
    let (_directory, root) = installation();
    let (config, target) = steam_target(&root, true);

    assert_eq!(
        guest_command(&target),
        [
            r"C:\windows\system32\steam.exe",
            "/opt/game/Game/start_protected_game.exe",
            "-eac"
        ]
    );
    assert_eq!(target.arguments[6], "/opt/game/Game");
    let runtime = config.runtime.display();
    assert_eq!(
        options(&target, "--bind"),
        [
            format!("/opt/steam={runtime}/steam:ro"),
            format!("/opt/obelisk={runtime}/guest:ro"),
        ]
    );
    assert!(options(&target, "--env").contains(&"LD_PRELOAD=/opt/obelisk/steam-hostpid.so"));
    // The host's ports exist only once the session starts the game.
    assert_eq!(options(&target, "--pass"), ["SteamAppId", "Steam3Master"]);
}
```
