```rs
        match kind {
            auth::GuardType::None => Self::None,
            auth::GuardType::EmailCode => Self::EmailCode,
            auth::GuardType::DeviceCode => Self::DeviceCode,
            auth::GuardType::DeviceConfirmation => Self::DeviceConfirmation,
            auth::GuardType::EmailConfirmation => Self::EmailConfirmation,
            auth::GuardType::MachineToken => Self::MachineToken,
            auth::GuardType::Unknown => Self::Unknown,
        }
    }

impl From<SteamGuardKind> for auth::GuardType {

            SteamGuardKind::None => Self::None,
            SteamGuardKind::EmailCode => Self::EmailCode,
            SteamGuardKind::DeviceCode => Self::DeviceCode,
            SteamGuardKind::DeviceConfirmation => Self::DeviceConfirmation,

            SteamGuardKind::MachineToken => Self::MachineToken,

#[derive(Clone, Debug, uniffi::Record)]

    pub message: String,

// A QR challenge can approve an account session: deliberately no Debug.
#[derive(Clone, uniffi::Record)]
pub struct SteamChallenge {
    pub qr_url: Option<String>,
    pub confirmations: Vec<SteamGuardMethod>,
    pub poll_interval_ms: u32,
    pub remote_interaction: bool,
}

#[derive(uniffi::Object)]
pub struct SteamLogin {
    client: auth::AuthClient,
    session: Mutex<auth::AuthSession>,
}

#[uniffi::export(async_runtime = "tokio")]
impl SteamLogin {
    #[uniffi::constructor]
    pub async fn begin_qr() -> Result<Arc<Self>, SteamError> {
        let client = auth::AuthClient::new(client::http_client()?);
        let session = client.begin_qr().await?;
        Ok(Arc::new(Self {
            client,
            session: Mutex::new(session),
        }))
    }
    #[uniffi::constructor]
    pub async fn begin_credentials(
        account_name: String,
        password: String,
    ) -> Result<Arc<Self>, SteamError> {
        let client = auth::AuthClient::new(client::http_client()?);
        let session = client.begin_credentials(&account_name, &password).await?;
        Ok(Arc::new(Self {
            client,
            session: Mutex::new(session),
        }))
    }
    pub async fn challenge(&self) -> SteamChallenge {
        let session = self.session.lock().await;
        SteamChallenge {
            qr_url: session.challenge_url().map(str::to_owned),
            confirmations: session
                .allowed_confirmations()
                .iter()
                .map(|confirmation| SteamGuardMethod {
                    kind: confirmation.kind.into(),
                    message: confirmation.message.clone(),
                })
                .collect(),
            poll_interval_ms: session.polling_interval().as_millis().min(u32::MAX as u128) as u32,
            remote_interaction: session.had_remote_interaction(),
        }
    }
    pub async fn poll(&self) -> Result<Option<SteamCredentials>, SteamError> {
        let mut session = self.session.lock().await;
        Ok(self
            .client
            .poll(&mut session)
            .await?
            .map(|tokens| SteamCredentials {
                account_name: tokens.account_name,
                steam_id: tokens.steam_id,
                refresh_token: tokens.refresh_token,
            }))
    }
    pub async fn submit_guard(&self, code: String, kind: SteamGuardKind) -> Result<(), SteamError> {
        let session = self.session.lock().await;
        self.client
            .submit_guard(&session, &code, kind.into())
            .await
            .map_err(Into::into)
    }
}

#[derive(uniffi::Object)]
pub struct SteamSession {
    /// Shared with the account's installations for the whole sign-in.
    pub(crate) account: Arc<AccountSession>,
    /// Where the account's library is kept as it loads.
    library: Option<SteamLibrary>,
}

impl SteamSession {
    /// The account's CM connection of the moment.
    pub(crate) fn client(&self) -> Arc<client::Client> {
        self.account.current()
    }

    /// `app_ids`' achievements in `language`: the library's for a game not
    /// played since they were read, unless `fresh`, else Steam's, a few
    /// games at a time, which the library then keeps. A game Steam did not
    /// answer for is left out; when none could be told, the first failure.
    async fn read_achievements(
        &self,
        app_ids: Vec<u32>,
        language: &str,
        fresh: bool,
    ) -> Result<Vec<GameAchievements>, SteamError> {
        let client = &self.client();
        library_cache::achievements(
            self.library.as_ref().map(SteamLibrary::achievements),
            app_ids,
            language,
            fresh,
            ACHIEVEMENT_READS,
            |app_id| async move {
                client
                    .achievements(app_id, language)
                    .await
                    .map_err(SteamError::from)
            },
        )
        .await
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, uniffi::Record)]
pub struct SteamProfile {
    pub display_name: Option<String>,
    pub avatar_url: Option<String>,
}

#[uniffi::export(async_runtime = "tokio")]
impl SteamSession {
    /// Keeps every library it loads in `library`.
    #[uniffi::constructor]
    pub async fn connect(
        credentials: SteamCredentials,
        library: Option<Arc<LibraryCache>>,
    ) -> Result<Arc<Self>, SteamError> {
        // Decode the routing identity before sending the token, then let Steam
        // validate its signature, expiry, revocation and account ownership.
        let token = auth::AuthTokens::restore(credentials.account_name, credentials.refresh_token)?;
        if token.steam_id != credentials.steam_id {
            return Err(auth::AuthError::Protocol.into());
        }
        let library = library.map(|library| library.steam(token.steam_id));
        let account = AccountSession::connect(Credentials {
            steam_id: token.steam_id,
            account_name: token.account_name,
            refresh_token: token.refresh_token,
        })
        .await?;
        Ok(Arc::new(Self { account, library }))
    }
    pub async fn games(&self) -> Result<Vec<SteamGame>, SteamError> {
        let games = self.client().games().await?;
        Ok(match &self.library {
            Some(library) => library.games(games),
            None => games.into_iter().map(Into::into).collect(),
        })
    }
    /// The game's achievements in `language`, such as the game page's: the
    /// library's while the game was not played since they were read, unless
    /// `fresh`, else Steam's, which the library then keeps.
    pub async fn achievements(
        &self,
        app_id: u32,
        language: String,
        fresh: bool,
    ) -> Result<Vec<LibraryAchievement>, SteamError> {
        let read = self
            .read_achievements(vec![app_id], &language, fresh)
            .await?;
        Ok(read
            .into_iter()
            .next()
            .map(|game| game.achievements)
            .unwrap_or_default())
    }
    /// The share of each of `app_ids`' achievements the account unlocked, by
    /// app ID, as `achievements` reads them: none for a game without
    /// achievements or that Steam did not answer for. It fails only when no
    /// game could be told.
    pub async fn achievement_shares(
        &self,
        app_ids: Vec<u32>,
        language: String,
    ) -> Result<HashMap<u32, f64>, SteamError> {
        let read = self.read_achievements(app_ids, &language, false).await?;
        Ok(library_cache::unlocked_shares(read)
            .filter_map(|(id, share)| Some((<steam::Steam as Named>::named(&id)?, share)))
            .collect())
    }
    /// When the account got each game its licenses grant, in seconds since
    /// the Unix epoch, by app ID. It expands every license through PICS.
    pub async fn acquisitions(&self) -> Result<HashMap<u32, u64>, SteamError> {
        let acquired = self.client().acquisitions().await?;
        if let Some(library) = &self.library {
            library.acquisitions(&acquired);
        }
        Ok(acquired
            .into_iter()
            .map(|(app_id, at)| (app_id, u64::from(at)))
            .collect())
    }
    /// The session's state after `after_revision`: its friends and how it
    /// stands with Steam, across its CM connections. No content-query mutex
    /// is held.
    pub async fn next_friends(&self, after_revision: u64) -> crate::SteamFriendsSnapshot {
        self.account.next(after_revision).await.into()
    }

    /// Cookies that sign Steam's sites in as this session's account.
    pub async fn web_cookies(&self) -> Result<Vec<SteamWebCookie>, SteamError> {
        Ok(self
            .client()
            .web_cookies()
            .await?
            .into_iter()
            .map(|cookie| SteamWebCookie {
                domain: cookie.domain.into(),
                name: cookie.name.into(),
                value: cookie.value,
                http_only: cookie.http_only,
            })
            .collect())
    }

    /// Stops reconnecting and ends the CM connection. Also wakes UniFFI
    /// futures, whose Swift wrappers do not cancel Rust awaits.
    pub fn shutdown(&self) {
        self.account.close();
    }
    /// Replaces the CM connection, live or not, and connects again, as on the
    /// player's retry or the Mac's wake. Nothing once Steam asked the account
    /// to sign in again.
    pub fn reconnect(&self) {
        self.account.reconnect();
    }
    pub async fn profile(&self) -> Result<SteamProfile, SteamError> {
        let profile = self.client().profile().await?;
        Ok(SteamProfile {
            display_name: profile.display_name,
            avatar_url: profile.avatar_url,
        })
    }
    /// Explicit diagnostic operation using this already-authenticated session.
    /// It downloads a verified backup; no Cloud mutation or game launch occurs.
    pub async fn cloud_backup(&self, app_id: u32, directory: String) -> Result<String, SteamError> {
        Ok(self
            .client()
            .cloud_backup(app_id, Path::new(&directory))
            .await?)
    }
    /// Returns only Cloud preferences and source revision, never roaming data.
    pub async fn cloud_preferences(&self, app_id: u32) -> Result<String, SteamError> {
        let preferences = self.client().cloud_preferences(app_id).await?;
        serde_json::to_string(&preferences).map_err(|_| SteamError::Failure {
            reason: "Invalid Cloud preference report".into(),
        })
    }
    /// Declared application platforms in batches; an empty platform list means
    /// unknown. Each game's library artwork comes with them, in `language`.
    pub async fn platforms(
        &self,
        app_ids: Vec<u32>,
        language: String,
    ) -> Result<Vec<SteamGamePlatforms>, SteamError> {
        let games = self.client().platforms(&app_ids).await?;
        let platforms = games
            .iter()
            .map(|game| SteamGamePlatforms {
                app_id: game.app_id,
                platforms: game.platforms.clone(),
                artwork: game
                    .pics
                    .as_ref()
                    .map(|pics| artwork::library_artwork(pics, &language).into()),
            })
            .collect();
        if let Some(library) = &self.library {
            library.platforms(games);
        }
        Ok(platforms)
    }
    pub async fn details(
        &self,
        app_id: u32,
        language: String,
    ) -> Result<SteamGameDetails, SteamError> {
        let details = self.client().details(app_id, &language).await?;
        Ok(SteamGameDetails {
            app_id: details.app_id,
            name: details.name,
            platform: details.platform.map(Into::into),
            windows_bytes: details.windows_bytes,
            macos_bytes: details.macos_bytes,
        })
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn verification_with_metadata_network_bytes_stays_verification_across_bridge() {
        let mut progress = client::TransferProgress::new("1");
        progress.state = client::TransferState::Verifying;
        progress.completed_bytes = 522_734_781;
        progress.total_bytes = 522_734_781;
        progress.network_bytes = 253;
        progress.current_file = "game.exe".into();
        let mapped = crate::GameTransfer::from(progress);
        assert!(matches!(mapped.state, crate::TransferState::Verifying));
        assert_eq!(mapped.game, "1");
        assert_eq!(mapped.completed_bytes, 522_734_781);
        assert_eq!(mapped.network_bytes, 253);
        assert_eq!(mapped.content_bytes, 0);
    }
}
```

```rs
//! Friends chat, Online presence and game invitations of the account's UI
//! session. Chat arrives as sequenced events rather than snapshots; a `gap`
//! tells Swift it fell behind and must reload the history it shows.
use std::sync::Arc;

use steam_kit::{chat, invites, own_game};

use crate::{SteamError, SteamSession, game_session::SteamReceivedInvite};

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, uniffi::Record)]
pub struct SteamChatMessage {
    pub friend_steam_id: u64,
    /// Sent by this account, from Obelisk or another of its sessions.
    pub from_me: bool,
    pub entry_type: i32,
    /// BBCode, as Steam stores it.
    pub message: String,
    pub plain_message: String,
    pub timestamp: u32,
    pub ordinal: u32,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, uniffi::Enum)]
pub enum SteamChatEvent {
    Message {
        message: SteamChatMessage,
    },
    Typing {
        friend_steam_id: u64,
    },
    /// The account read the conversation up to `timestamp` in another session.
    Read {
        friend_steam_id: u64,
        timestamp: u32,
    },
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, uniffi::Record)]
pub struct SteamChatEventEntry {
    pub sequence: u64,
    pub event: SteamChatEvent,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, uniffi::Record)]
pub struct SteamChatEvents {
    pub events: Vec<SteamChatEventEntry>,
    /// The cursor to pass to the next call.
    pub last_sequence: u64,
    pub gap: bool,
    pub connected: bool,
}

impl From<chat::ChatEvents> for SteamChatEvents {
    fn from(events: chat::ChatEvents) -> Self {
        Self {
            events: events
                .events
                .into_iter()
                .map(|entry| SteamChatEventEntry {
                    sequence: entry.sequence,
                    event: match entry.event {
                        chat::ChatEvent::Message(message) => SteamChatEvent::Message {
                            message: SteamChatMessage {
                                friend_steam_id: message.friend,
                                from_me: message.from_me,
                                entry_type: message.entry_type,
                                message: message.message,
                                plain_message: message.plain,
                                timestamp: message.timestamp,
                                ordinal: message.ordinal,
                            },
                        },
                        chat::ChatEvent::Typing { friend } => SteamChatEvent::Typing {
                            friend_steam_id: friend,
                        },
                        chat::ChatEvent::Read { friend, timestamp } => SteamChatEvent::Read {
                            friend_steam_id: friend,
                            timestamp,
                        },
                    },
                })
                .collect(),
            last_sequence: events.last_sequence,
            gap: events.gap,
            connected: events.connected,
        }
    }
}

/// A game and how to join it: a friend's lobby or rich presence `connect`
/// string, as an invitation or Steam's "Join Game" names it.

/// The invitations friends sent the account's session, newest first, at most
/// one per friend.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, uniffi::Record)]
pub struct SteamReceivedInvites {
    pub revision: u64,
    pub connected: bool,
    pub invites: Vec<SteamReceivedInvite>,
}

impl From<invites::ReceivedInvites> for SteamReceivedInvites {
    fn from(received: invites::ReceivedInvites) -> Self {
        Self {
            revision: received.revision,
            connected: received.connected,
            invites: received
                .invites
                .into_iter()
                .map(|invite| SteamReceivedInvite {
                    friend_steam_id: invite.friend,
                    app_id: invite.app_id,
                    invite: invite.invite.into(),
                    received_at: invite.received_at,
                })
                .collect(),
        }
    }
}

/// The invitation a friends chat message carries, read as Steam's chat reads
/// its `[lobbyinvite]` and `[gameinvite]` tags; none for Remote Play.
#[uniffi::export]
pub fn steam_chat_invite(bbcode: String) -> Option<SteamJoinTarget> {
    invites::chat_invite(&bbcode).map(|(app_id, invite)| SteamJoinTarget {
        app_id,
        invite: invite.into(),
    })

#[uniffi::export(async_runtime = "tokio")]
impl SteamSession {
    /// Shows the account Online again, for instance after a game ended.
    pub async fn set_online(&self) -> Result<(), SteamError> {
        Ok(self.client().set_online().await?)
    }

    /// Suspends until chat events follow `after_sequence` or the session ends.
    pub async fn next_chat(&self, after_sequence: u64) -> SteamChatEvents {
        self.client().next_chat(after_sequence).await.into()
    }

    pub async fn send_message(
        &self,
        friend_steam_id: u64,
        text: String,
    ) -> Result<SteamSentMessage, SteamError> {
        let sent = self.client().send_message(friend_steam_id, &text).await?;
        Ok(SteamSentMessage {
            timestamp: sent.timestamp,
            ordinal: sent.ordinal,
            message: sent.message,
            plain_message: sent.plain,
        })
    }

    /// Throttled per friend in Rust; calling on every keystroke is fine.
    pub async fn send_typing(&self, friend_steam_id: u64) -> Result<(), SteamError> {
        Ok(self.client().send_typing(friend_steam_id).await?)
    }

    /// Up to `count` (at most 50) messages before `before`, or the latest ones.
    pub async fn recent_messages(
        &self,
        friend_steam_id: u64,
        before: Option<SteamChatPosition>,
        count: u32,
    ) -> Result<SteamChatHistory, SteamError> {
        let history = self
            .client()
            .recent_messages(
                friend_steam_id,
                before.map(|position| (position.timestamp, position.ordinal)),
                count,
            )
            .await?;
        Ok(SteamChatHistory {
            messages: history
                .messages
                .into_iter()
                .map(|message| SteamChatHistoryMessage {
                    from_me: message.from_me,
                    timestamp: message.timestamp,
                    ordinal: message.ordinal,
                    message: message.message,
                })
                .collect(),
            more_available: history.more_available,
        })
    }

    pub async fn active_sessions(&self) -> Result<Vec<SteamChatSession>, SteamError> {
        Ok(self
            .client()
            .active_sessions()
            .await?
            .into_iter()
            .map(|session| SteamChatSession {
                friend_steam_id: session.friend,
                last_message: session.last_message,
                last_view: session.last_view,
                unread_message_count: session.unread_message_count,
            })
            .collect())
    }

    /// Marks the conversation read up to `timestamp` in every session.
    pub async fn ack(&self, friend_steam_id: u64, timestamp: u32) -> Result<(), SteamError> {
        Ok(self.client().ack(friend_steam_id, timestamp).await?)
    }

    /// Suspends until the own game's revision differs or the session ends.
    pub async fn next_own_game(&self, after_revision: u64) -> SteamOwnGame {
        self.client().next_own_game(after_revision).await.into()
    }

    /// Suspends until the invitations friends sent change or the session ends.
    pub async fn next_invites(&self, after_revision: u64) -> SteamReceivedInvites {
        self.client().next_invites(after_revision).await.into()
    }

    /// Fails with `backend.steam.invite.unavailable` unless the account plays
    /// `app_id` and that game can take an invitation now.
    pub async fn invite_to_game(
        &self,
        friend_steam_id: u64,
        app_id: u32,
    ) -> Result<(), SteamError> {
        self.client()
            .invite_to_game(friend_steam_id, app_id)
            .await?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Invites into `invite`, which the account's running game of `app_id`
    /// reported itself. Fails with `backend.steam.invite.unavailable` for an
    /// invitation Steam cannot carry or while the account plays another game.
    pub async fn invite_into_game(
        &self,
        friend_steam_id: u64,
        app_id: u32,
        invite: SteamGameInvite,
    ) -> Result<(), SteamError> {
        self.client()
            .invite_into_game(friend_steam_id, app_id, &invite.into())
            .await?;
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl SteamChatFixture {
    #[uniffi::constructor]

    /// A friend's chat message, as Steam writes it for an invitation too.
    pub fn incoming_invitation(
        &self,
        friend_steam_id: u64,
        message: String,
        timestamp: u32,
        ordinal: u32,
    ) {

            chat::CHAT_MESSAGE,
            &message,
            timestamp,
            ordinal,
            false,
        );

        self.invites
            .receive_notification(chat::INCOMING_MESSAGE, &body);
    }

    /// A lobby invitation, as Steam sends it apart from the chat.

        self.invites.receive_packet(
            invites::CHAT_INVITE,
            None,
            &invites::fixture::lobby_invite(friend_steam_id, lobby_id, app_id),
        );
    }

    /// A connect invitation into `app_id`, its header's routing AppID.
    pub fn connect_invite(&self, friend_steam_id: u64, app_id: u32, connect: String) {
        self.invites.receive_packet(
            invites::INVITE_TO_GAME,
            Some(app_id),
            &invites::fixture::connect_invite(friend_steam_id, &connect),
        );
    }

    pub fn incoming_message(
        &self,
        friend_steam_id: u64,
        message: String,
        timestamp: u32,
        ordinal: u32,
        from_me: bool,
    ) {
        self.chat.receive(
            chat::INCOMING_MESSAGE,
            &chat::fixture::incoming_message(
                friend_steam_id,
                chat::CHAT_MESSAGE,
                &message,
                timestamp,
                ordinal,
                from_me,
            ),
        );
    }

    pub fn typing(&self, friend_steam_id: u64) {
        self.chat.receive(
            chat::INCOMING_MESSAGE,
            &chat::fixture::incoming_message(friend_steam_id, chat::TYPING, "", 0, 0, false),
        );
    }

    pub fn read_elsewhere(&self, friend_steam_id: u64, timestamp: u32) {
        self.chat.receive(
            chat::ACK_ECHO,
            &chat::fixture::ack_echo(friend_steam_id, timestamp),
        );
    }

    /// The account playing `app_id` (0 for none), with an optional lobby and
    /// rich presence `connect` string.

        self.own_game.receive(
            self.account_id,
            &own_game::fixture::persona(self.account_id, app_id, lobby_id, connect.as_deref()),
        );
    }

    pub fn disconnect(&self) {
        self.chat.disconnect();
        self.own_game.disconnect();
        self.invites.disconnect();
    }

    pub async fn next_invites(&self, after_revision: u64) -> SteamReceivedInvites {
        self.invites.next(after_revision).await.into()
    }

    pub async fn next_chat(&self, after_sequence: u64) -> SteamChatEvents {
        self.chat.next(after_sequence).await.into()
    }

    pub async fn next_own_game(&self, after_revision: u64) -> SteamOwnGame {
        self.own_game.next(after_revision).await.into()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    const ACCOUNT: u64 = 76_561_197_960_265_730;
    const FRIEND: u64 = ACCOUNT - 1;

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn fixture_drives_chat_and_own_game_across_the_bridge() {
        let fixture = SteamChatFixture::new(ACCOUNT);
        fixture.incoming_message(FRIEND, "hi".into(), 10, 1, false);
        fixture.typing(FRIEND);
        fixture.read_elsewhere(FRIEND, 10);
        let events = fixture.next_chat(0).await;
        assert_eq!(events.last_sequence, 3);
        assert!(!events.gap && events.connected);
        assert_eq!(
            events.events[0].event,
            SteamChatEvent::Message {
                message: SteamChatMessage {
                    friend_steam_id: FRIEND,
                    from_me: false,
                    entry_type: 1,
                    message: "hi".into(),
                    plain_message: "hi".into(),
                    timestamp: 10,
                    ordinal: 1,
                }
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(
            events.events[2].event,
            SteamChatEvent::Read {
                friend_steam_id: FRIEND,
                timestamp: 10
            }
        );

        fixture.own_game(620, 0, Some("+join".into()));
        let game = fixture.next_own_game(1).await;
        assert_eq!(game.app_id, 620);
        assert_eq!(
            game.invite,
            SteamGameInvite::Connect {
                connect: "+join".into()
            }
        );
        fixture.disconnect();
        assert!(!fixture.next_chat(3).await.connected);
        assert!(!fixture.next_own_game(game.revision).await.connected);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn invitations_cross_the_bridge_once_whatever_their_channel() {
        const LOBBY: u64 = 109_775_244_421_126_053;
        let tag = format!("[lobbyinvite appid=\"3527290\" lobbyid=\"{LOBBY}\"][/lobbyinvite]");
        let target = SteamJoinTarget {
            app_id: 3_527_290,
            invite: SteamGameInvite::Lobby { lobby_id: LOBBY },
        };
        assert_eq!(steam_chat_invite(tag.clone()), Some(target.clone()));
        assert_eq!(steam_chat_invite("hi".into()), None);

        let fixture = SteamChatFixture::new(ACCOUNT);
        fixture.incoming_invitation(FRIEND, tag, 10, 1);
        fixture.lobby_invite(FRIEND, LOBBY, 3_527_290);
        let invites = fixture.next_invites(1).await;
        assert_eq!(invites.revision, 2);
        assert_eq!(invites.invites.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(invites.invites[0].friend_steam_id, FRIEND);
        assert_eq!(invites.invites[0].app_id, target.app_id);
        assert_eq!(invites.invites[0].invite, target.invite);

        fixture.connect_invite(ACCOUNT + 1, 620, "+connect 1".into());
        let invites = fixture.next_invites(2).await;
        assert_eq!(invites.invites[0].app_id, 620);
        fixture.disconnect();
        assert!(!fixture.next_invites(invites.revision).await.connected);
    }
}
```

`crates/obelisk-bridge/src/steam_friends.rs`:

```rs
//! Social records contain no credentials or protobuf types. Revisioned full
//! snapshots coalesce bursts without dropping the final state.
use std::sync::Arc;

use game_runtime::steam::account_session::{Phase, State};
use obelisk_core::transfer::CancelToken;
use steam_kit::friends;

use crate::{
    LibraryCache, SteamCredentials, SteamError, SteamSession, steam_chat::SteamJoinTarget,
};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, uniffi::Enum)]
pub enum SteamFriendPresence {
    Unknown,
    Offline,
    Online,
    Busy,
    Away,
    Snooze,
    LookingToTrade,
    LookingToPlay,
    Invisible,
}

impl From<friends::FriendPresence> for SteamFriendPresence {
    fn from(value: friends::FriendPresence) -> Self {
        match value {
            friends::FriendPresence::Unknown => Self::Unknown,
            friends::FriendPresence::Offline => Self::Offline,
            friends::FriendPresence::Online => Self::Online,
            friends::FriendPresence::Busy => Self::Busy,
            friends::FriendPresence::Away => Self::Away,
            friends::FriendPresence::Snooze => Self::Snooze,
            friends::FriendPresence::LookingToTrade => Self::LookingToTrade,
            friends::FriendPresence::LookingToPlay => Self::LookingToPlay,
            friends::FriendPresence::Invisible => Self::Invisible,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, uniffi::Enum)]
pub enum SteamFriendsConnection {
    Loading,
    Ready,
    /// The CM connection dropped, and the session connects again.
    Disconnected,
    AuthenticationRequired,
    Error,
    /// Every attempt to connect again failed; a retry or the Mac's wake
    /// tries again.
    Unreachable,
    /// The session was shut down.
    Stopped,
}

impl From<friends::FriendsConnection> for SteamFriendsConnection {
    fn from(value: friends::FriendsConnection) -> Self {
        match value {
            friends::FriendsConnection::Loading => Self::Loading,
            friends::FriendsConnection::Ready => Self::Ready,
            friends::FriendsConnection::Disconnected => Self::Disconnected,
            friends::FriendsConnection::AuthenticationRequired => Self::AuthenticationRequired,
            friends::FriendsConnection::Error => Self::Error,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, uniffi::Record)]
pub struct SteamFriendGame {
    pub app_id: Option<u32>,
    pub name: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, uniffi::Record)]
pub struct SteamFriend {
    pub steam_id: u64,
    pub display_name: Option<String>,
    pub avatar_url: Option<String>,
    pub presence: SteamFriendPresence,
    pub game: Option<SteamFriendGame>,
    /// The friend's game and how Steam's "Join Game" joins it, while it can.
    #[uniffi(default = None)]
    pub join: Option<SteamJoinTarget>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, uniffi::Record)]
pub struct SteamFriendsSnapshot {
    /// The session's revision, which grows across its CM connections.
    pub revision: u64,
    pub account_id: u64,
    pub connection: SteamFriendsConnection,
    /// The session's CM connection: 0 for the first, one more for each that
    /// replaced a dropped one.
    pub transport: u64,
    pub friends: Vec<SteamFriend>,
}

/// The session's state, as the friends list shows it: the connection its
/// friends tell while it is up, else where the session stands.
impl From<State> for SteamFriendsSnapshot {
    fn from(state: State) -> Self {
        let snapshot = state.friends;
        let connection = match state.phase {
            Phase::Connected => snapshot.connection.into(),
            Phase::Reconnecting => SteamFriendsConnection::Disconnected,
            Phase::Unreachable => SteamFriendsConnection::Unreachable,
            Phase::AuthenticationRequired => SteamFriendsConnection::AuthenticationRequired,
            Phase::Closed => SteamFriendsConnection::Stopped,
        };
        Self {
            revision: state.revision,
            account_id: snapshot.account_id,
            connection,
            transport: state.transport,
            friends: snapshot
                .friends
                .into_iter()
                .map(|friend| SteamFriend {
                    steam_id: friend.steam_id,
                    display_name: friend.display_name,
                    avatar_url: friend.avatar_url,
                    presence: friend.presence.into(),
                    join: friend.game.as_ref().and_then(|game| {
                        let invite = game.invite();
                        let app_id = game.app_id?;
                        invite.sendable().then(|| SteamJoinTarget {
                            app_id,
                            invite: invite.into(),
                        })
                    }),
                    game: friend.game.map(|game| SteamFriendGame {
                        app_id: game.app_id,
                        name: game.name,
                    }),
                })
                .collect(),
        }
    }
}

/// A single-use connection attempt with explicit cancellation across UniFFI.
#[derive(uniffi::Object)]
pub struct SteamConnectionAttempt {
    cancel: CancelToken,
}

#[uniffi::export(async_runtime = "tokio")]
impl SteamConnectionAttempt {
    #[uniffi::constructor]
    pub fn new() -> Arc<Self> {
        Arc::new(Self {
            cancel: CancelToken::new(),
        })
    }

    pub fn cancel(&self) {
        self.cancel.cancel();
    }

    pub async fn connect(
        &self,
        credentials: SteamCredentials,
        library: Option<Arc<LibraryCache>>,
    ) -> Result<Arc<SteamSession>, SteamError> {
        tokio::select! {
            biased;
            () = self.cancel.cancelled() => Err(SteamError::Cancelled),
            result = SteamSession::connect(credentials, library) => result,
        }
    }
}

/// Debug-only controlled Account session. Its friends go through the
/// production reducer and its states through the production conversion,
/// letting macOS tests exercise raw packets and reconnections across UniFFI.
#[cfg(debug_assertions)]
#[derive(uniffi::Object)]
pub struct SteamFriendsFixture {
    account_id: u64,
    /// The friends of the CM connection of the moment.
    source: std::sync::Mutex<friends::FriendsEventSource>,
    state: tokio::sync::watch::Sender<State>,
}

#[cfg(debug_assertions)]
impl SteamFriendsFixture {
    /// Publishes the source's friends, the session standing as `phase` with
    /// `transport`, when anything changed.
    fn publish(&self, source: &friends::FriendsEventSource, phase: Phase, transport: u64) {
        let friends = source.snapshot();
        self.state.send_if_modified(|state| {
            if (state.phase, state.transport, &state.friends) == (phase, transport, &friends) {
                return false;
            }
            *state = State {
                revision: state.revision + 1,
                phase,
                transport,
                friends,
            };
            true
        });
    }

    fn source(&self) -> std::sync::MutexGuard<'_, friends::FriendsEventSource> {
        self.source
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner)
    }

    /// Publishes the same friends, the session standing as `phase`.
    fn stand(&self, phase: Phase) {
        let transport = self.state.borrow().transport;
        self.publish(&self.source(), phase, transport);
    }
}

#[cfg(debug_assertions)]
#[uniffi::export(async_runtime = "tokio")]
impl SteamFriendsFixture {
    #[uniffi::constructor]
    pub fn new(account_id: u64) -> Arc<Self> {
        let source = friends::FriendsEventSource::new(account_id);
        let (state, _) = tokio::sync::watch::channel(State {
            revision: 1,
            phase: Phase::Connected,
            transport: 0,
            friends: source.snapshot(),
        });
        Arc::new(Self {
            account_id,
            source: std::sync::Mutex::new(source),
            state,
        })
    }

    /// The CM connection of the moment receives a packet.
    pub fn receive(&self, kind: u32, body: Vec<u8>) {
        let source = self.source();
        source.apply_packet(kind, &body);
        let (phase, transport) = {
            let state = self.state.borrow();
            (state.phase, state.transport)
        };
        self.publish(&source, phase, transport);
    }

    /// Steam pushes `friend_steam_id` playing `app_id` (0 for none), in a
    /// lobby and with a rich presence `connect` string when given.
    pub fn friend_playing(
        &self,
        friend_steam_id: u64,
        app_id: u32,
        lobby_id: u64,
        connect: Option<String>,
    ) {
        // ClientPersonaState.
        self.receive(
            766,
            steam_kit::own_game::fixture::persona(
                friend_steam_id,
                app_id,
                lobby_id,
                connect.as_deref(),
            ),
        );
    }

    /// The CM connection drops and the session connects again, or Steam
    /// asks the account to sign in again.
    pub fn disconnect(&self, authentication_required: bool) {
        let source = self.source();
        source.disconnect(authentication_required);
        let transport = self.state.borrow().transport;
        let phase = if authentication_required {
            Phase::AuthenticationRequired
        } else {
            Phase::Reconnecting
        };
        self.publish(&source, phase, transport);
    }

    /// A new CM connection replaces the one that dropped, its friends still
    /// loading.
    pub fn reconnect(&self) {
        let mut source = self.source();
        *source = friends::FriendsEventSource::new(self.account_id);
        let transport = self.state.borrow().transport + 1;
        self.publish(&source, Phase::Connected, transport);
    }

    /// Every attempt to connect again failed.
    pub fn unreachable(&self) {
        self.stand(Phase::Unreachable);
    }

    /// The player's retry, or the Mac's wake: the session connects again,
    /// unless its account must sign in again or it closed.
    pub fn retry(&self) {
        if self.state.borrow().retries() {
            self.stand(Phase::Reconnecting);
        }
    }

    /// The session is shut down.
    pub fn close(&self) {
        self.stand(Phase::Closed);
    }

    pub async fn next_friends(&self, after_revision: u64) -> SteamFriendsSnapshot {
        let ready = obelisk_core::watch::next_matching(self.state.subscribe(), |state| {
            state.follows(after_revision)
        })
        .await;
        match ready {
            Ok(state) | Err(state) => state.into(),
        }
    }
}

                ..Default::default()
            })),
            friend(Some(friends::FriendGame {
                app_id: Some(620),
                ..Default::default()
            })),
            friend(None),
        ];
        let crossed = SteamFriendsSnapshot::from(state);
        assert_eq!(
            crossed.friends[0].join,
            Some(SteamJoinTarget {
                app_id: 620,
                invite: crate::SteamGameInvite::Lobby { lobby_id: LOBBY }
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(crossed.friends[1].join, None, "no lobby or connect string");
        assert_eq!(crossed.friends[2].join, None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn each_session_phase_crosses_as_the_friends_connection_swift_shows() {
        use friends::FriendsConnection as Friends;
        let crossed =
            |phase, connection| SteamFriendsSnapshot::from(state(phase, connection)).connection;

        assert_eq!(
            crossed(Phase::Connected, Friends::Loading),
            SteamFriendsConnection::Loading
        );
        assert_eq!(
            crossed(Phase::Connected, Friends::Ready),
            SteamFriendsConnection::Ready
        );
        assert_eq!(
            crossed(Phase::Connected, Friends::Error),
            SteamFriendsConnection::Error
        );
        assert_eq!(
            crossed(Phase::Reconnecting, Friends::Disconnected),
            SteamFriendsConnection::Disconnected
        );
        assert_eq!(
            crossed(Phase::Unreachable, Friends::Disconnected),
            SteamFriendsConnection::Unreachable
        );
        assert_eq!(
            crossed(Phase::AuthenticationRequired, Friends::Ready),
            SteamFriendsConnection::AuthenticationRequired
        );
        assert_eq!(
            crossed(Phase::Closed, Friends::Ready),
            SteamFriendsConnection::Stopped
        );

        let snapshot = SteamFriendsSnapshot::from(state(Phase::Connected, Friends::Ready));
        assert_eq!(
            (snapshot.revision, snapshot.account_id, snapshot.transport),
            (12, 7, 2),
            "the session's revision and connection, the friends' account"
        );
    }
}
```

`crates/obelisk-core/src/atomic_file.rs`:

```rs
//! Crash-safe file replacement shared by every catalogue, receipt and cache writer.
use std::fs::File;
use std::io::{self, Write};
use std::path::Path;

use tempfile::NamedTempFile;

/// Writes `bytes` to a temporary file beside `path`, fsyncs it, then atomically
/// replaces `path`. The directory sync afterwards is best effort: a failure
/// there cannot truthfully mean the replacement was rolled back.
pub fn write_atomic(path: &Path, bytes: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()> {
    write_atomic_with(path, bytes, || Ok(()))
}

/// [`write_atomic`] with a hook that runs after the temporary file is durable
/// and immediately before the rename, so a link substituted at `path` while
/// the bytes were being written can still be rejected.
pub fn write_atomic_with<E: From<io::Error>>(
    path: &Path,
    bytes: &[u8],
    before_replace: impl FnOnce() -> Result<(), E>,
) -> Result<(), E> {
    let directory = path.parent().unwrap_or_else(|| Path::new("."));
    // The temporary file lives beside the destination, on the same volume.
    let mut temporary = NamedTempFile::new_in(directory)?;
    temporary.write_all(bytes)?;
    temporary.as_file().sync_all()?;
    before_replace()?;
    temporary.persist(path).map_err(|error| error.error)?;
    if let Ok(directory) = File::open(directory) {
        let _ = directory.sync_all();
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

`crates/obelisk-core/src/build_choice.rs`:

```rs
//! Which of a game's builds a download installs, and which one its page
//! shows before any download. Only a download reads a Mac build's files, as
//! its Transfer starts, once per build; the page shows the Mac build until
//! one found that its game does not run natively. Each storefront answers
//! for its builds through a [`GameBuilds`] adapter.
use std::{
    collections::HashMap,
    future::Future,
    hash::Hash,
    sync::{Mutex, MutexGuard, PoisonError},
};

use crate::{
    Platform,
    transfer::{CancelToken, Cancelled},
};

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;

/// The message key of a Mac-only game that does not run natively, the same
/// on every storefront.
pub const NOT_NATIVE: &str = "backend.install.macBuildNotNative";

/// The builds a storefront offers the account of one game, as it lists them.
pub struct Offered<B> {
    pub mac: Option<B>,
    pub windows: Option<B>,
}

/// What reading a Mac build's files told.
pub enum Inspection<V> {
    /// Its game runs natively; `V` is what the build's download starts from.
    Native(V),
    /// Its game does not, or Obelisk cannot install the build.
    NotNative,
}

/// Why a game has no build a download can install. Storefront errors
/// convert it, as they convert `Cancelled`.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Unavailable {
    /// The storefront offers the account neither build.
    NoBuild,
    /// Only a Mac build, whose game does not run natively.
    NotNative,
}

/// One game's builds at one storefront, as the build choice asks for them.
pub trait GameBuilds: Sync {
    /// What the storefront lists of a build.
    type Build: Send + Sync;
    /// Names one immutable Mac build; its verdict is kept by it.
    type Key: Clone + Eq + Hash + Send;
    /// What the download of a native Mac build starts from.
    type Kept: Send;
    type Error: From<Unavailable> + Send;

    /// The builds the account can install. Reads no build's files.
    fn builds(&self) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Offered<Self::Build>, Self::Error>> + Send;

    /// The key of the Mac build `mac`; none when the storefront names no
    /// immutable build, which keeps no verdict.
    fn key(
        &self,
        mac: &Self::Build,
    ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Option<Self::Key>, Self::Error>> + Send;

    /// Reads the few files of `mac` that tell whether its game runs
    /// natively, through `mac_build::runs_natively`.
    fn inspect(
        &self,
        mac: &Self::Build,
        cancel: &CancelToken,
    ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Inspection<Self::Kept>, Self::Error>> + Send;
}

/// One storefront client's build choice for the session: each Mac build's
/// verdict, what the last pick read of a native build, and the pick a
/// cancellation stops.
pub struct BuildChoice<K, V> {
    verdicts: Mutex<HashMap<K, bool>>,
    kept: Mutex<Option<(K, V)>>,
    picking: Mutex<Option<CancelToken>>,
}

impl<K, V> Default for BuildChoice<K, V> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            verdicts: Mutex::new(HashMap::new()),
            kept: Mutex::new(None),
            picking: Mutex::new(None),
        }
    }
}

impl<K: Clone + Eq + Hash, V> BuildChoice<K, V> {
    /// The build a download installs. `work` runs the choice with
    /// [`Pick::of`], inside whatever the storefront wraps around its calls,
    /// such as its token funnel; [`cancel`](Self::cancel) stops all of it.
    pub async fn pick<E: From<Cancelled>>(
        &self,
        work: impl for<'a> AsyncFnOnce(Pick<'a, K, V>) -> Result<Platform, E>,
    ) -> Result<Platform, E> {
        let token = CancelToken::new();
        *self.lock_picking() = Some(token.clone());
        let picked = token
            .race(work(Pick {
                choice: self,
                cancel: token.clone(),
            }))
            .await;
        self.lock_picking().take();
        picked?
    }

    /// The build a game's page shows, of those `offered`, with what the
    /// storefront listed of it: the Mac build, unless a pick found that its
    /// game does not run natively and there is a Windows build. Reads no
    /// build's files; a key the storefront cannot tell shows the Mac build.
    pub async fn shown<G: GameBuilds<Key = K>>(
        &self,
        game: &G,
        offered: Offered<G::Build>,
    ) -> Option<(Platform, G::Build)> {
        // Only with both builds can a verdict change the answer, and a key
        // may cost the storefront a request.
        let not_native = match (&offered.mac, &offered.windows) {
            (Some(mac), Some(_)) => {
                matches!(game.key(mac).await, Ok(Some(key)) if self.verdict(&key) == Some(false))
            }
            _ => false,
        };
        match (offered.mac, offered.windows) {
            (Some(_), Some(windows)) if not_native => Some((Platform::Windows, windows)),
            (Some(mac), _) => Some((Platform::Mac, mac)),
            (None, Some(windows)) => Some((Platform::Windows, windows)),
            (None, None) => None,
        }
    }

    /// What the last pick read of `build`, once.
    pub fn take(&self, build: &K) -> Option<V> {
        let mut kept = self.lock_kept();
        match kept.as_ref() {
            Some((key, _)) if key == build => kept.take().map(|(_, value)| value),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// Stops a pick in flight and forgets what the last one read.
    pub fn cancel(&self) {
        if let Some(token) = self.lock_picking().as_ref() {
            token.cancel();
        }
        self.lock_kept().take();
    }

    fn verdict(&self, build: &K) -> Option<bool> {
        self.lock_verdicts().get(build).copied()
    }

    fn lock_verdicts(&self) -> MutexGuard<'_, HashMap<K, bool>> {
        self.verdicts.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
    }

    fn lock_kept(&self) -> MutexGuard<'_, Option<(K, V)>> {
        self.kept.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
    }

    fn lock_picking(&self) -> MutexGuard<'_, Option<CancelToken>> {
        self.picking.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
    }
}

/// A pick in flight, which its cancellation stops.
pub struct Pick<'a, K, V> {
    choice: &'a BuildChoice<K, V>,
    cancel: CancelToken,
}

impl<K: Clone + Eq + Hash, V> Pick<'_, K, V> {
    /// The Mac build when its game runs natively, else the Windows build.
    /// A Mac build is read once per key.
    pub async fn of<G: GameBuilds<Key = K, Kept = V>>(
        &self,
        game: &G,
    ) -> Result<Platform, G::Error> {
        let offered = game.builds().await?;
        if let Some(mac) = &offered.mac
            && self.runs_natively(game, mac).await?
        {
            return Ok(Platform::Mac);
        }
        match (offered.mac, offered.windows) {
            (_, Some(_)) => Ok(Platform::Windows),
            (Some(_), None) => Err(Unavailable::NotNative.into()),
            (None, None) => Err(Unavailable::NoBuild.into()),
        }
    }

    /// Whether the game of `mac` runs natively, from its verdict when one is
    /// kept, else from its files. What a native build's read is kept for its
    /// download, in place of any other build's.
    async fn runs_natively<G: GameBuilds<Key = K, Kept = V>>(
        &self,
        game: &G,
        mac: &G::Build,
    ) -> Result<bool, G::Error> {
        let key = game.key(mac).await?;
        if let Some(native) = key.as_ref().and_then(|key| self.choice.verdict(key)) {
            return Ok(native);
        }
        let inspection = game.inspect(mac, &self.cancel).await?;
        let native = matches!(inspection, Inspection::Native(_));
        if let Some(key) = key {
            self.choice.lock_verdicts().insert(key.clone(), native);
            *self.choice.lock_kept() = match inspection {
                Inspection::Native(kept) => Some((key, kept)),
                Inspection::NotNative => None,
            };
        }
        Ok(native)
    }
}
```

`crates/obelisk-core/src/build_choice/tests.rs`:

```rs
use super::*;
use std::sync::Arc;

use tokio::sync::Notify;

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
enum FakeError {
    Cancelled,
    Unavailable(Unavailable),
    Failed,
}

impl From<Cancelled> for FakeError {
    fn from(_: Cancelled) -> Self {
        Self::Cancelled
    }
}

impl From<Unavailable> for FakeError {
    fn from(unavailable: Unavailable) -> Self {
        Self::Unavailable(unavailable)
    }
}

/// A game whose storefront answers as scripted, and logs what it was asked.
struct FakeGame {
    offered: (Option<&'static str>, Option<&'static str>),
    key: Result<Option<u8>, ()>,
    /// What reading the Mac build tells: what it keeps when native, `None`
    /// when not.
    inspection: Result<Option<&'static str>, ()>,
    /// Holds `inspect` until notified.
    gate: Option<Arc<Notify>>,
    log: Mutex<Vec<&'static str>>,
}

impl FakeGame {
    fn new(mac: Option<&'static str>, windows: Option<&'static str>) -> Self {
        Self {
            offered: (mac, windows),
            key: Ok(Some(1)),
            inspection: Ok(Some("read")),
            gate: None,
            log: Mutex::new(Vec::new()),
        }
    }

    fn native(key: u8, kept: &'static str) -> Self {
        Self {
            key: Ok(Some(key)),
            inspection: Ok(Some(kept)),
            ..Self::new(Some("mac"), Some("windows"))
        }
    }

    fn not_native(key: u8) -> Self {
        Self {
            key: Ok(Some(key)),
            inspection: Ok(None),
            ..Self::new(Some("mac"), Some("windows"))
        }
    }

    fn asked(&self, call: &str) -> usize {
        self.log
            .lock()
            .unwrap()
            .iter()
            .filter(|asked| **asked == call)
            .count()
    }

    fn note(&self, call: &'static str) {
        self.log.lock().unwrap().push(call);
    }
}

impl GameBuilds for FakeGame {
    type Build = &'static str;
    type Key = u8;
    type Kept = &'static str;
    type Error = FakeError;

    async fn builds(&self) -> Result<Offered<&'static str>, FakeError> {
        self.note("builds");
        Ok(Offered {
            mac: self.offered.0,
            windows: self.offered.1,
        })
    }

    async fn key(&self, mac: &&'static str) -> Result<Option<u8>, FakeError> {
        assert_eq!(*mac, self.offered.0.unwrap());
        self.note("key");
        self.key.map_err(|()| FakeError::Failed)
    }

    async fn inspect(
        &self,
        mac: &&'static str,
        _cancel: &CancelToken,
    ) -> Result<Inspection<&'static str>, FakeError> {
        assert_eq!(*mac, self.offered.0.unwrap());
        self.note("inspect");
        if let Some(gate) = &self.gate {
            gate.notified().await;
        }
        match self.inspection.map_err(|()| FakeError::Failed)? {
            Some(kept) => Ok(Inspection::Native(kept)),
            None => Ok(Inspection::NotNative),
        }
    }
}

type Choice = BuildChoice<u8, &'static str>;

async fn pick(choice: &Choice, game: &FakeGame) -> Result<Platform, FakeError> {
    choice.pick(async |pick| pick.of(game).await).await
}

async fn shown(choice: &Choice, game: &FakeGame) -> Option<(Platform, &'static str)> {
    let offered = game.builds().await.unwrap();
    choice.shown(game, offered).await
}

/// Keeps the verdict `native` for key 1, as a pick of its build finds it.
async fn judge(choice: &Choice, native: bool) {
    let game = match native {
        true => FakeGame::native(1, "one"),
        false => FakeGame::not_native(1),
    };
    pick(choice, &game).await.unwrap();
}

/// Whether a pick of a build keyed `key` reads it, which leaves its
/// verdict as `native` when it does.
async fn reads(choice: &Choice, key: u8, native: bool) -> bool {
    let game = match native {
        true => FakeGame::native(key, "again"),
        false => FakeGame::not_native(key),
    };
    pick(choice, &game).await.unwrap();
    game.asked("inspect") == 1
}

const MAC: Option<&str> = Some("mac");
const WINDOWS: Option<&str> = Some("windows");
/// What reading a native Mac build keeps.
const NATIVE: Option<&str> = Some("read");
const NOT_NATIVE: Option<&str> = None;

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_download_installs_the_mac_build_when_its_game_runs_natively_else_the_windows_build() {
    use Platform::{Mac, Windows};
    let no_build = Err(FakeError::Unavailable(Unavailable::NoBuild));
    let not_native = Err(FakeError::Unavailable(Unavailable::NotNative));
    // (mac, windows, what reading the Mac build tells, picked, whether it was read)
    let cases = [
        (None, None, NATIVE, no_build, false),
        (None, WINDOWS, NATIVE, Ok(Windows), false),
        (MAC, None, NATIVE, Ok(Mac), true),
        (MAC, WINDOWS, NATIVE, Ok(Mac), true),
        (MAC, WINDOWS, NOT_NATIVE, Ok(Windows), true),
        (MAC, None, NOT_NATIVE, not_native, true),
    ];
    for (mac, windows, inspection, expected, inspected) in cases {
        let game = FakeGame {
            inspection: Ok(inspection),
            ..FakeGame::new(mac, windows)
        };
        let choice = Choice::default();
        let case = (mac, windows, inspection);
        assert_eq!(pick(&choice, &game).await, expected, "{case:?}");
        assert_eq!(game.asked("inspect"), usize::from(inspected), "{case:?}");
        if mac.is_none() {
            assert_eq!(game.asked("key"), 0, "{case:?}: no Mac build, no key");
        }
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_page_shows_the_mac_build_until_a_pick_found_its_game_is_not_native() {
    use Platform::{Mac, Windows};
    let (shows_mac, shows_windows) = (Some((Mac, "mac")), Some((Windows, "windows")));
    // (mac, windows, the verdict kept for key 1, the key the page gets, shown)
    let cases = [
        (None, None, Some(false), Ok(Some(1)), None),
        (None, WINDOWS, Some(false), Ok(Some(1)), shows_windows),
        (MAC, None, Some(false), Ok(Some(1)), shows_mac),
        (MAC, None, None, Ok(Some(1)), shows_mac),
        (MAC, WINDOWS, None, Ok(Some(1)), shows_mac),
        (MAC, WINDOWS, Some(true), Ok(Some(1)), shows_mac),
        (MAC, WINDOWS, Some(false), Ok(Some(1)), shows_windows),
        (MAC, WINDOWS, Some(false), Ok(Some(2)), shows_mac),
        (MAC, WINDOWS, Some(false), Ok(None), shows_mac),
        (MAC, WINDOWS, Some(false), Err(()), shows_mac),
        (MAC, WINDOWS, Some(true), Err(()), shows_mac),
    ];
    for (mac, windows, verdict, key, expected) in cases {
        let choice = Choice::default();
        if let Some(native) = verdict {
            judge(&choice, native).await;
        }
        let game = FakeGame {
            key,
            ..FakeGame::new(mac, windows)
        };
        let case = (mac, windows, verdict, key);
        assert_eq!(shown(&choice, &game).await, expected, "{case:?}");
        assert_eq!(game.asked("inspect"), 0, "{case:?}: a page reads no file");
        let both = mac.is_some() && windows.is_some();
        assert_eq!(game.asked("key"), usize::from(both), "{case:?}");
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_mac_build_is_read_once_per_key() {
    let choice = Choice::default();
    let first = FakeGame::not_native(1);
    assert_eq!(pick(&choice, &first).await, Ok(Platform::Windows));
    assert_eq!(pick(&choice, &first).await, Ok(Platform::Windows));
    assert_eq!(first.asked("inspect"), 1, "the verdict of key 1 is kept");
    assert_eq!(first.asked("key"), 2);

    let other = FakeGame::native(2, "two");
    assert_eq!(pick(&choice, &other).await, Ok(Platform::Mac));
    assert_eq!(other.asked("inspect"), 1, "another key reads its build");

    // A build without a key is read each time and changes nothing kept.
    let unkeyed = FakeGame {
        key: Ok(None),
        ..FakeGame::not_native(0)
    };
    assert_eq!(pick(&choice, &unkeyed).await, Ok(Platform::Windows));
    assert_eq!(pick(&choice, &unkeyed).await, Ok(Platform::Windows));
    assert_eq!(unkeyed.asked("inspect"), 2);
    assert_eq!(shown(&choice, &unkeyed).await, Some((Platform::Mac, "mac")));
    assert_eq!(choice.take(&2), Some("two"));

    // A failed key or read remembers nothing.
    let failing_key = FakeGame {
        key: Err(()),
        ..FakeGame::not_native(3)
    };
    assert_eq!(pick(&choice, &failing_key).await, Err(FakeError::Failed));
    assert_eq!(failing_key.asked("inspect"), 0);
    let failing_read = FakeGame {
        inspection: Err(()),
        ..FakeGame::not_native(3)
    };
    assert_eq!(pick(&choice, &failing_read).await, Err(FakeError::Failed));
    let read_again = FakeGame::not_native(3);
    assert_eq!(pick(&choice, &read_again).await, Ok(Platform::Windows));
    assert_eq!(
        read_again.asked("inspect"),
        1,
        "the next pick reads it again"
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_native_pick_hands_what_it_read_to_that_build_s_download_once() {
    let choice = Choice::default();
    let one = FakeGame::native(1, "one");
    assert_eq!(pick(&choice, &one).await, Ok(Platform::Mac));
    assert_eq!(
        choice.take(&2),
        None,
        "another build's download reads its own"
    );
    assert_eq!(choice.take(&1), Some("one"));
    assert_eq!(choice.take(&1), None, "a manifest starts one download");

    // A cache hit leaves what is kept alone.
    let two = FakeGame::native(2, "two");
    assert_eq!(pick(&choice, &two).await, Ok(Platform::Mac));
    assert_eq!(pick(&choice, &one).await, Ok(Platform::Mac));
    assert_eq!(one.asked("inspect"), 1);
    // So does a build without a key.
    let unkeyed = FakeGame {
        key: Ok(None),
        ..FakeGame::native(0, "unkeyed")
    };
    assert_eq!(pick(&choice, &unkeyed).await, Ok(Platform::Mac));
    assert_eq!(choice.take(&2), Some("two"));

    // A native pick of another build replaces it.
    assert_eq!(
        pick(&choice, &FakeGame::native(3, "three")).await,
        Ok(Platform::Mac)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        pick(&choice, &FakeGame::native(4, "four")).await,
        Ok(Platform::Mac)
    );
    assert_eq!(choice.take(&3), None);
    assert_eq!(choice.take(&4), Some("four"));

    // A keyed pick found not native clears it.
    assert_eq!(
        pick(&choice, &FakeGame::native(5, "five")).await,
        Ok(Platform::Mac)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        pick(&choice, &FakeGame::not_native(6)).await,
        Ok(Platform::Windows)
    );
    assert_eq!(choice.take(&5), None);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn cancel_stops_a_pick_and_forgets_what_it_read() {
    let choice = Choice::default();
    // Harmless with nothing in flight.
    choice.cancel();

    assert_eq!(
        pick(&choice, &FakeGame::not_native(1)).await,
        Ok(Platform::Windows)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        pick(&choice, &FakeGame::native(2, "two")).await,
        Ok(Platform::Mac)
    );

    let gated = FakeGame {
        gate: Some(Arc::new(Notify::new())),
        ..FakeGame::native(3, "three")
    };
    let cancelling = async {
        while gated.asked("inspect") == 0 {
            tokio::task::yield_now().await;
        }
        choice.cancel();
    };
    let (picked, ()) = tokio::join!(pick(&choice, &gated), cancelling);
    assert_eq!(picked, Err(FakeError::Cancelled));
    assert_eq!(choice.take(&2), None, "a cancel forgets what was read");
    assert!(!reads(&choice, 1, false).await, "verdicts survive a cancel");
    assert!(!reads(&choice, 2, true).await);

    // The next pick runs on a fresh token, and reads the stopped build again.
    let again = FakeGame::native(3, "three");
    assert_eq!(pick(&choice, &again).await, Ok(Platform::Mac));
    assert_eq!(again.asked("inspect"), 1, "a stopped read keeps no verdict");
    assert_eq!(choice.take(&3), Some("three"));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_pick_runs_inside_what_the_storefront_wraps_around_it() {
    let choice = Choice::default();
    let failing = FakeGame {
        inspection: Err(()),
        ..FakeGame::native(1, "one")
    };
    let gated = FakeGame {
        gate: Some(Arc::new(Notify::new())),
        ..FakeGame::native(1, "one")
    };
    // As a token funnel retries its call: the second attempt runs under the
    // same pick, which a cancel still stops.
    let attempts = choice.pick(async |pick| {
        assert_eq!(pick.of(&failing).await, Err(FakeError::Failed));
        pick.of(&gated).await
    });
    let cancelling = async {
        while gated.asked("inspect") == 0 {
            tokio::task::yield_now().await;
        }
        choice.cancel();
    };
    let (picked, ()) = tokio::join!(attempts, cancelling);
    assert_eq!(picked, Err(FakeError::Cancelled));
    assert_eq!(failing.asked("inspect"), 1);
    assert_eq!(gated.asked("inspect"), 1);
    assert!(
        reads(&choice, 1, true).await,
        "neither attempt kept a verdict"
    );
}
```

`crates/obelisk-core/src/date.rs`:

```rs
//! Proleptic Gregorian dates as days from 1970-01-01, by Howard Hinnant's
//! `days_from_civil` and `civil_from_days`.

/// The days from 1970-01-01 to a date, negative before it. `month` is 1 to
/// 12; a `day` past its month's end runs on into the next month.
pub fn days_from_civil(year: i64, month: i64, day: i64) -> i64 {
    let year = if month <= 2 { year - 1 } else { year };
    let era = year.div_euclid(400);
    let year_of_era = year - era * 400;
    let of_year = (153 * ((month + 9) % 12) + 2) / 5 + day - 1;
    let of_era = year_of_era * 365 + year_of_era / 4 - year_of_era / 100 + of_year;
    era * 146_097 + of_era - 719_468
}

/// The `(year, month, day)` that is `days` after 1970-01-01.
pub fn civil_from_days(days: i64) -> (i64, i64, i64) {
    let days = days + 719_468;
    let era = days.div_euclid(146_097);
    let of_era = days - era * 146_097;
    let year_of_era = (of_era - of_era / 1460 + of_era / 36_524 - of_era / 146_096) / 365;
    let of_year = of_era - (365 * year_of_era + year_of_era / 4 - year_of_era / 100);
    let shifted_month = (5 * of_year + 2) / 153;
    let day = of_year - (153 * shifted_month + 2) / 5 + 1;
    let month = if shifted_month < 10 {
        shifted_month + 3
    } else {
        shifted_month - 9
    };
    let year = year_of_era + era * 400 + i64::from(month <= 2);
    (year, month, day)
}

/// The moment an ISO 8601 date names, such as GOG's
/// `2014-10-13T00:00:00+0000` or Epic's `2021-05-27T17:33:54.987Z`, in
/// seconds since the Unix epoch; a bare date is its midnight in UTC.
pub fn unix_seconds(text: &str) -> Option<u64> {
    let number = |range: std::ops::Range<usize>| -> Option<i64> {
        let part = text.get(range)?;
        part.bytes()
            .all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_digit())
            .then(|| part.parse().ok())?
    };
    if text.get(4..5) != Some("-") || text.get(7..8) != Some("-") {
        return None;
    }
    let (year, month, day) = (number(0..4)?, number(5..7)?, number(8..10)?);
    if !(1..=12).contains(&month) || !(1..=31).contains(&day) {
        return None;
    }
    let (mut seconds, rest) = match text.get(10..11) {
        None => (0, ""),
        Some("T" | " ") if text.get(13..14) == Some(":") && text.get(16..17) == Some(":") => (
            number(11..13)? * 3600 + number(14..16)? * 60 + number(17..19)?,
            &text[19..],
        ),
        _ => return None,
    };
    // A fraction of a second, then the offset from UTC.
    let rest = rest.trim_start_matches(|c: char| c == '.' || c.is_ascii_digit());
    match rest {
        "" | "Z" => {}
        offset => {
            let sign = match offset.get(..1)? {
                "+" => 1,
                "-" => -1,
                _ => return None,
            };
            let digits = offset[1..].replace(':', "");
            if digits.len() != 4 || !digits.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_digit()) {
                return None;
            }
            let minutes: i64 =
                digits[..2].parse::<i64>().ok()? * 60 + digits[2..].parse::<i64>().ok()?;
            seconds -= sign * minutes * 60;
        }
    }
    u64::try_from(days_from_civil(year, month, day) * 86_400 + seconds).ok()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn iso_dates_read_as_unix_seconds() {
        assert_eq!(
            unix_seconds("2014-10-13T00:00:00+0000"),
            Some(1_413_158_400)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            unix_seconds("2011-05-09T23:00:00+0200"),
            Some(1_304_974_800)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            unix_seconds("2024-11-05T10:31:15+00:00"),
            Some(1_730_802_675)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            unix_seconds("2020-02-29T12:00:00.250Z"),
            Some(1_582_977_600)
        );
        assert_eq!(unix_seconds("1970-01-01"), Some(0));
        for text in [
            "",
            "2014-13-01",
            "2014/10/13",
            "2014-10-13T00:00",
            "2014-10-13T00:00:00+00",
            "x",
        ] {
            assert_eq!(unix_seconds(text), None, "{text}");
        }
    }
}
```
