`crates/obelisk-core/src/install.rs`:

```rs
//! Filesystem primitives shared by storefront installers: paths confined to an
//! installation root, the per-installation advisory lock, bounded cache files,
//! SHA-1 and MD5 file checks and permission bits. Storefronts keep their manifest
//! formats and error vocabularies; these helpers never follow a symlink.
use std::{
    fs::{self, File, OpenOptions},
    io::{self, Read},
    path::{Component, Path, PathBuf},
};

use md5::Md5;
use sha1::{Digest, Sha1};
use thiserror::Error;

use crate::{
    atomic_file::write_atomic_with,
    transfer::{CancelToken, Cancelled},
};

/// Partial files, chunk caches, manifest caches and the engine lock live here,
/// inside the installation directory, so manifests may never name it.
pub const PARTIAL_DIRECTORY: &str = ".obelisk-content";
/// Receipt written only after every file of an installation succeeded.
pub const RECEIPT_FILE: &str = ".obelisk-install.json";
/// Advisory lock held from preparation until the receipt is published.
pub const LOCK_FILE: &str = ".obelisk-install.lock";
/// The engine lock, inside the installation's own partial directory. Distinct
/// from [`LOCK_FILE`]: this one guards the detached disk worker, which outlives
/// a dropped transfer future, while [`LOCK_FILE`] spans a whole transfer.
pub const ENGINE_LOCK_FILE: &str = "install.lock";

#[derive(Debug, Error)]
pub enum InstallError {
    #[error("cancelled")]
    Cancelled,
    #[error("unsafe path: {0}")]
    UnsafePath(String),
    #[error(transparent)]
    Io(#[from] io::Error),
}

impl From<Cancelled> for InstallError {
    fn from(_: Cancelled) -> Self {
        Self::Cancelled
    }
}

/// Lowercase hex without an allocation per byte.
pub fn hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    const DIGITS: &[u8; 16] = b"0123456789abcdef";
    let mut output = String::with_capacity(bytes.len() * 2);
    for &byte in bytes {
        output.push(DIGITS[usize::from(byte >> 4)] as char);
        output.push(DIGITS[usize::from(byte & 15)] as char);
    }
    output
}

/// The `N` bytes `value` spells in hex, either case; `None` for any other
/// length or a character that is not a hex digit.
pub fn unhex<const N: usize>(value: &str) -> Option<[u8; N]> {
    if value.len() != N * 2 || !value.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {
        return None;
    }
    let mut bytes = [0; N];
    for (index, byte) in bytes.iter_mut().enumerate() {
        *byte = u8::from_str_radix(&value[index * 2..index * 2 + 2], 16).ok()?;
    }
    Some(bytes)
}

/// Normalizes a manifest file name into a relative path made only of plain
/// components. Absolute paths, drive letters, `.`/`..`, empty segments, NUL and
/// Obelisk's own reserved names are rejected before touching the filesystem.
pub fn safe_relative_path(name: &str) -> Result<PathBuf, InstallError> {
    let normalized = name.replace('\\', "/");
    if normalized.is_empty()
        || normalized.starts_with('/')
        || normalized.contains(['\0', ':'])
        || normalized
            .split('/')
            .any(|part| matches!(part, "" | "." | ".."))
        || normalized.split('/').next().is_some_and(|part| {
            part.eq_ignore_ascii_case(PARTIAL_DIRECTORY)
                || part.eq_ignore_ascii_case(RECEIPT_FILE)
                || part.eq_ignore_ascii_case(LOCK_FILE)
        })
    {
        return Err(InstallError::UnsafePath(name.into()));
    }
    let path = PathBuf::from(normalized);
    if !path
        .components()
        .all(|component| matches!(component, Component::Normal(_)))
    {
        return Err(InstallError::UnsafePath(name.into()));
    }
    Ok(path)
}

/// Creates every missing directory of `relative` under `root`, refusing to
/// traverse or replace anything that is not a real directory.
pub fn ensure_directory(root: &Path, relative: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, InstallError> {
    let mut path = root.to_path_buf();
    for component in relative.components() {
        let Component::Normal(name) = component else {
            return Err(InstallError::UnsafePath(relative.display().to_string()));
        };
        path.push(name);
        match fs::symlink_metadata(&path) {
            Ok(metadata) if metadata.is_dir() && !metadata.file_type().is_symlink() => {}
            Ok(_) => return Err(InstallError::UnsafePath(path.display().to_string())),
            Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => fs::create_dir(&path)?,
            Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
        }
    }
    Ok(path)
}

/// Resolves `relative` under `root` for a file that may or may not exist yet.
/// Every existing intermediate must be a real directory and an existing leaf
/// must be a regular file with a single link, so a write can never escape root.
pub fn checked_file_path(root: &Path, relative: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, InstallError> {
    let mut path = root.to_path_buf();
    let count = relative.components().count();
    for (index, component) in relative.components().enumerate() {
        let Component::Normal(name) = component else {
            return Err(InstallError::UnsafePath(relative.display().to_string()));
        };
        path.push(name);
        let last = index + 1 == count;
        match fs::symlink_metadata(&path) {
            Ok(metadata) => {
                if metadata.file_type().is_symlink()
                    || !last && !metadata.is_dir()
                    || last && !metadata.is_file()
                    || last && has_extra_links(&metadata)
                {
                    return Err(InstallError::UnsafePath(path.display().to_string()));
                }
            }
            Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {}
            Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
        }
    }
    Ok(path)
}

/// Places a symbolic link at `relative` under `root`, pointing at `target` as
/// given, replacing whatever an earlier build left there. Its parents must be
/// real directories; confining `target` is the caller's part.
#[cfg(unix)]
pub fn place_link(root: &Path, relative: &Path, target: &Path) -> Result<(), InstallError> {
    let name = relative
        .file_name()
        .ok_or_else(|| InstallError::UnsafePath(relative.display().to_string()))?;
    let location = ensure_directory(root, relative.parent().unwrap_or(Path::new("")))?.join(name);
    match fs::symlink_metadata(&location) {
        Ok(metadata) if metadata.file_type().is_symlink() => {
            if fs::read_link(&location)? == target {
                return Ok(());
            }
            fs::remove_file(&location)?;
        }
        Ok(metadata) if metadata.is_dir() => fs::remove_dir_all(&location)?,
        Ok(_) => fs::remove_file(&location)?,
        Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {}
        Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
    }
    std::os::unix::fs::symlink(target, &location)?;
    Ok(())
}

/// Accepts a missing path or a regular, unlinked file; rejects everything else.
pub fn reject_link_or_special_file(path: &Path) -> Result<(), InstallError> {
    match fs::symlink_metadata(path) {
        Ok(metadata)
            if !metadata.is_file()
                || metadata.file_type().is_symlink()
                || has_extra_links(&metadata) =>
        {
            Err(InstallError::UnsafePath(path.display().to_string()))
        }
        Ok(_) => Ok(()),
        Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(()),
        Err(error) => Err(error.into()),
    }
}

fn has_extra_links(metadata: &fs::Metadata) -> bool {
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;
        metadata.nlink() > 1
    }
    #[cfg(not(unix))]
    {
        let _ = metadata;
        false
    }
}

/// `Ok(true)` for an existing real directory, `Ok(false)` when nothing exists
/// there, and an error for a symlink or a file in its place.
pub fn existing_plain_directory(path: &Path) -> Result<bool, InstallError> {
    match fs::symlink_metadata(path) {
        Ok(metadata) if metadata.is_dir() && !metadata.file_type().is_symlink() => Ok(true),
        Ok(_) => Err(InstallError::UnsafePath(path.display().to_string())),
        Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(false),
        Err(error) => Err(error.into()),
    }
}

/// Opens (creating if needed) `path` and takes an exclusive advisory lock.
/// `Ok(None)` means another process or session already holds it.
pub fn try_lock_file(path: &Path) -> io::Result<Option<File>> {
    let file = OpenOptions::new()
        .create(true)
        .truncate(false)
        .read(true)
        .write(true)
        .open(path)?;
    Ok(file.try_lock().is_ok().then_some(file))
}

/// Creates the partial directory under an installation root and takes the
/// engine lock inside it. `Ok(None)` means another disk worker, in this process
/// or another, still holds it. The lock is released when the returned file is
/// dropped, so a caller holds it by keeping the handle alive.
pub fn lock_engine(root: &Path) -> Result<Option<File>, InstallError> {
    let cache = ensure_directory(root, Path::new(PARTIAL_DIRECTORY))?;
    let path = checked_file_path(&cache, Path::new(ENGINE_LOCK_FILE))?;
    try_lock_file(&path).map_err(Into::into)
}

/// Reads a whole file of at most `limit` bytes. `None` when the file is missing
/// or larger than the limit, which callers treat alike: as absent.
pub fn read_file_bounded(path: &Path, limit: usize) -> io::Result<Option<Vec<u8>>> {
    let file = match File::open(path) {
        Ok(file) => file,
        Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(None),
        Err(error) => return Err(error),
    };
    if file.metadata()?.len() > limit as u64 {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    let mut bytes = Vec::new();
    file.take(limit as u64 + 1).read_to_end(&mut bytes)?;
    Ok((bytes.len() <= limit).then_some(bytes))
}

/// Reads a bounded cache file confined under an existing installation root.
/// A missing root or file is a miss; a redirected path is an error.
pub fn read_cached_file(
    root: &Path,
    relative: &Path,
    limit: usize,
) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, InstallError> {
    if !existing_plain_directory(root)? {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    let path = checked_file_path(root, relative)?;
    Ok(read_file_bounded(&path, limit)?)
}

/// Atomically stores a cache file confined under an existing installation
/// root, creating parent directories and re-checking the path right before the
/// replacement so a link substituted meanwhile is rejected too.
pub fn write_cached_file(root: &Path, relative: &Path, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), InstallError> {
    if !existing_plain_directory(root)? {
        return Err(io::Error::from(io::ErrorKind::NotFound).into());
    }
    ensure_directory(root, relative.parent().unwrap_or(Path::new("")))?;
    let path = checked_file_path(root, relative)?;
    write_atomic_with(&path, bytes, || checked_file_path(root, relative).map(drop))
}

/// What a whole installed file must hash to.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub enum FileDigest<'a> {
    /// The SHA-1 of the whole file, as Steam and Epic record it.
    Sha1(&'a [u8]),
    /// The MD5 of each consecutive part of the file, as GOG records its
    /// chunks.
    Md5Parts(&'a [Md5Part]),
}

/// One consecutive part of a file and its MD5.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Md5Part {
    pub size: u64,
    pub md5: [u8; 16],
}

/// How much of a file on disk matched its digest.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Matched {
    pub whole: bool,
    /// The leading parts that hashed as expected, before the first that did
    /// not; none when the file is missing or its size differs.
    pub parts: usize,
}

/// Reads a file through its digest in 64 KiB reads, reporting bytes read in
/// bounded batches without treating them as validated content. A missing file
/// or a size mismatch simply does not match; cancellation is checked before
/// every read.
pub(crate) fn verify_file_with_progress(
    path: &Path,
    size: u64,
    digest: FileDigest<'_>,
    cancel: &CancelToken,
    progress: impl FnMut(u64),
) -> Result<Matched, InstallError> {
    match digest {
        FileDigest::Sha1(expected) => {
            verify_parts::<Sha1>(path, size, [(size, expected)], cancel, progress)
        }
        FileDigest::Md5Parts(parts) => {
            let parts = parts.iter().map(|part| (part.size, &part.md5[..]));
            verify_parts::<Md5>(path, size, parts, cancel, progress)
        }
    }
}

/// Streams a file through SHA-1 in 64 KiB reads. A missing file or a size
/// mismatch is simply `false`; cancellation is checked between reads.
pub fn verify_sha1_file(
    path: &Path,
    size: u64,
    expected: &[u8],
    cancel: &CancelToken,
) -> Result<bool, InstallError> {
    verify_file_with_progress(path, size, FileDigest::Sha1(expected), cancel, |_| {})
        .map(|matched| matched.whole)
}

/// Hashes each consecutive part of the file on its own, stopping at the first
/// part that differs.
fn verify_parts<'a, D: Digest>(
    path: &Path,
    size: u64,
    parts: impl IntoIterator<Item = (u64, &'a [u8])> + Clone,
    cancel: &CancelToken,
    mut progress: impl FnMut(u64),
) -> Result<Matched, InstallError> {
    let mut file = match File::open(path) {
        Ok(file) => file,
        Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(Matched::default()),
        Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
    };
    let parts_size: u64 = parts.clone().into_iter().map(|(size, _)| size).sum();
    if file.metadata()?.len() != size || parts_size != size {
        return Ok(Matched::default());
    }
    let mut buffer = [0_u8; 64 * 1024];
    let mut pending = 0_u64;
    let mut matched = Matched {
        whole: true,
        parts: 0,
    };
    for (part_size, expected) in parts {
        let mut hasher = D::new();
        let mut remaining = part_size;
        while remaining > 0 {
            cancel.check()?;
            let count = buffer
                .len()
                .min(usize::try_from(remaining).unwrap_or(usize::MAX));
            file.read_exact(&mut buffer[..count])?;
            hasher.update(&buffer[..count]);
            remaining -= count as u64;
            pending += count as u64;
            if pending >= 1024 * 1024 {
                progress(pending);
                pending = 0;
            }
        }
        if hasher.finalize()[..] != *expected {
            matched.whole = false;
            break;
        }
        matched.parts += 1;
    }
    if pending != 0 {
        progress(pending);
    }
    Ok(matched)
}

/// Whether the file starts as a program does: a Mach-O binary or a script.
/// Some manifests flag only a build's launch executable, not the helpers it
/// starts.
pub fn starts_as_program(path: &Path) -> io::Result<bool> {
    const PROGRAMS: [&[u8]; 5] = [
        &[0xcf, 0xfa, 0xed, 0xfe], // 64-bit Mach-O
        &[0xce, 0xfa, 0xed, 0xfe], // 32-bit Mach-O
        &[0xca, 0xfe, 0xba, 0xbe], // universal binary
        &[0xca, 0xfe, 0xba, 0xbf], // 64-bit universal binary
        b"#!",
    ];
    let mut header = Vec::with_capacity(4);
    File::open(path)?.take(4).read_to_end(&mut header)?;
    Ok(PROGRAMS.iter().any(|magic| header.starts_with(magic)))
}

/// Installed files are user-readable; only manifest-declared executables get
/// the execute bit. No other mode information crosses a storefront manifest.
pub fn apply_permissions(path: &Path, executable: bool) -> io::Result<()> {
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
        let mode = if executable { 0o755 } else { 0o644 };
        fs::set_permissions(path, fs::Permissions::from_mode(mode))?;
    }
    #[cfg(not(unix))]
    {
        let _ = (path, executable);
    }
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn relative_paths_reject_escapes_and_reserved_names() {
        for name in [
            "",
            "/absolute",
            "C:\\outside",
            "../outside",
            "safe/../outside",
            "safe/./file",
            "safe//file",
            "nul\0byte",
            ".obelisk-content/lock",
            ".OBELISK-INSTALL.json",
            ".obelisk-install.lock",
        ] {
            assert!(
                matches!(safe_relative_path(name), Err(InstallError::UnsafePath(_))),
                "{name:?}"
            );
        }
        assert_eq!(
            safe_relative_path("Game.app\\Contents/MacOS\\Game").unwrap(),
            Path::new("Game.app/Contents/MacOS/Game")
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn bounded_reads_treat_missing_and_oversized_files_as_absent() {
        let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let path = directory.path().join("cache");
        assert!(read_file_bounded(&path, 4).unwrap().is_none());
        fs::write(&path, b"12345").unwrap();
        assert!(read_file_bounded(&path, 4).unwrap().is_none());
        assert_eq!(read_file_bounded(&path, 5).unwrap().unwrap(), b"12345");
    }

    #[test]
    fn cached_files_round_trip_under_an_existing_root_only() {
        let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let relative = Path::new(PARTIAL_DIRECTORY).join("manifests/1.bin");
        let missing_root = directory.path().join("missing");
        assert!(
            read_cached_file(&missing_root, &relative, 16)
                .unwrap()
                .is_none()
        );
        assert!(matches!(
            write_cached_file(&missing_root, &relative, b"x"),
            Err(InstallError::Io(_))
        ));
        write_cached_file(directory.path(), &relative, b"payload").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            read_cached_file(directory.path(), &relative, 16)
                .unwrap()
                .unwrap(),
            b"payload"
        );
    }

    #[cfg(unix)]
    #[test]
    fn confined_paths_refuse_links_and_special_files() {
        let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let outside = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(outside.path(), root.path().join("link")).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            checked_file_path(root.path(), Path::new("link/game")),
            Err(InstallError::UnsafePath(_))
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            ensure_directory(root.path(), Path::new("link")),
            Err(InstallError::UnsafePath(_))
        ));
        fs::write(outside.path().join("original"), b"unchanged").unwrap();
        fs::hard_link(
            outside.path().join("original"),
            root.path().join("hardlink"),
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            checked_file_path(root.path(), Path::new("hardlink")),
            Err(InstallError::UnsafePath(_))
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            reject_link_or_special_file(&root.path().join("hardlink")),
            Err(InstallError::UnsafePath(_))
        ));
        fs::write(root.path().join("plain"), b"file").unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            checked_file_path(root.path(), Path::new("plain/child")),
            Err(InstallError::UnsafePath(_))
        ));
        assert!(checked_file_path(root.path(), Path::new("new/file")).is_ok());
        assert!(reject_link_or_special_file(&root.path().join("plain")).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_engine_lock_is_exclusive_and_released_with_its_handle() {
        let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let held = lock_engine(root.path())
            .unwrap()
            .expect("first worker takes it");
        assert!(
            root.path()
                .join(PARTIAL_DIRECTORY)
                .join(ENGINE_LOCK_FILE)
                .is_file(),
            "the lock lives inside the installation's own partial directory"
        );
        assert!(
            lock_engine(root.path()).unwrap().is_none(),
            "a second worker is refused while the first holds it"
        );
        drop(held);
        assert!(lock_engine(root.path()).unwrap().is_some());
    }

    #[cfg(unix)]
    #[test]
    fn the_engine_lock_refuses_a_redirected_partial_directory() {
        let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let outside = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(outside.path(), root.path().join(PARTIAL_DIRECTORY)).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            lock_engine(root.path()),
            Err(InstallError::UnsafePath(_))
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn sha1_verification_handles_missing_and_mismatched_files() {
        let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let path = directory.path().join("file");
        let cancel = CancelToken::new();
        let digest: [u8; 20] = Sha1::digest(b"content").into();
        assert!(!verify_sha1_file(&path, 7, &digest, &cancel).unwrap());
        fs::write(&path, b"content").unwrap();
        assert!(verify_sha1_file(&path, 7, &digest, &cancel).unwrap());
        assert!(!verify_sha1_file(&path, 8, &digest, &cancel).unwrap());
        assert!(!verify_sha1_file(&path, 7, &[0; 20], &cancel).unwrap());
        cancel.cancel();
        assert!(matches!(
            verify_sha1_file(&path, 7, &digest, &cancel),
            Err(InstallError::Cancelled)
        ));
    }
}

```

`crates/obelisk-core/src/installation.rs`:

```rs
//! One installation Transfer, in the order every storefront follows around its
//! content engine. Obelisk confines the destination, lets the storefront prepare
//! before any file exists, holds the installation lock from the first file to
//! the receipt, withdraws the old Installation receipt before files change and
//! publishes the new one only after every file succeeded. Storefronts supply
//! only preparation and file installation.
use std::{
    fmt::Display,
    fs::{self, File, FileTimes},
    future::Future,
    io::{self, Read, Write},
    path::{Component, Path, PathBuf},
};

use serde::{Serialize, de::DeserializeOwned};
use thiserror::Error;

use crate::{
    install::{
        InstallError, LOCK_FILE, PARTIAL_DIRECTORY, RECEIPT_FILE, checked_file_path,
        read_file_bounded, try_lock_file,
    },
    transfer::{
        CancelToken, Cancelled, DownloadProgress, TransferBusy, TransferContext, TransferState,
        TransferStatus, Transfers,
    },
};

/// Receipts are small JSON documents; anything larger is not one of ours.
const MAX_RECEIPT_BYTES: usize = 1024 * 1024;
/// How much of a file a move copies between two looks at its cancellation.
const COPY_CHUNK: usize = 4 * 1024 * 1024;
/// Ends the name of the hidden folder a move to another disk copies into.
const STAGING_SUFFIX: &str = ".obelisk-moving";

/// A Transfer's progress, as every storefront presents it.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct TransferProgress {
    /// The storefront's own identity for the game.
    pub game: String,
    pub state: TransferState,
    pub completed_bytes: u64,
    pub total_bytes: u64,
    /// Compressed bytes received, including manifests.
    pub network_bytes: u64,
    /// Compressed chunk bytes received, excluding manifests and disk reads.
    pub content_bytes: u64,
    pub current_file: String,
    /// A message key while the Transfer runs, then its outcome.
    pub message: String,
}

impl TransferProgress {
    pub fn new(game: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self {
            game: game.into(),
            state: TransferState::Preparing,
            completed_bytes: 0,
            total_bytes: 0,
            network_bytes: 0,
            content_bytes: 0,
            current_file: String::new(),
            message: "backend.transfer.preparing".into(),
        }
    }

    /// Shows one engine snapshot as the Transfer's progress. While files are
    /// inspected, inspection bytes stand in for completed bytes. Clears the
    /// message: a storefront that labels the Transfer, or counts work done
    /// before this engine run, adjusts the fields afterwards.
    pub fn show(&mut self, snapshot: DownloadProgress) {
        self.state = snapshot.phase.into();
        self.completed_bytes = snapshot
            .verification_bytes
            .unwrap_or(snapshot.completed_bytes);
        self.total_bytes = snapshot.total_bytes;
        self.network_bytes = snapshot.network_bytes;
        self.content_bytes = snapshot.content_bytes;
        self.current_file = snapshot.current_file;
        self.message.clear();
    }
}

impl TransferStatus for TransferProgress {
    fn finish(&mut self, state: TransferState, error: Option<String>) {
        self.state = state;
        self.message = error.unwrap_or_else(|| {
            match state {
                TransferState::Complete if self.content_bytes == 0 => "backend.transfer.upToDate",
                TransferState::Complete => "backend.transfer.complete",
                _ => "backend.transfer.stopped",
            }
            .into()
        });
    }
}

/// What obelisk-core refused or failed around an installation. Each storefront
/// turns it into its own message vocabulary.
#[derive(Debug, Error)]
pub enum InstallFailure {
    #[error("the installation folder's parent must be an existing absolute folder")]
    ParentMissing,
    #[error("the installation folder name must be one plain path component: {0}")]
    UnsafeDirectory(String),
    #[error("the installation folder must not be a link: {0}")]
    DestinationIsLink(PathBuf),
    #[error("a file occupies the installation folder: {0}")]
    DestinationIsFile(PathBuf),
    #[error("the installation lock must be a regular unlinked file: {0}")]
    UnsafeLock(PathBuf),
    #[error("another Transfer holds the installation")]
    Locked,
    #[error("the Installation receipt must be a regular unlinked file: {0}")]
    UnsafeReceipt(PathBuf),
    #[error(transparent)]
    Io(#[from] io::Error),
}

/// A storefront's errors around an installation Transfer.
pub trait TransferError:
    From<InstallFailure> + From<Cancelled> + From<TransferBusy> + Display
{
    /// The content engine stopped because the Transfer was cancelled.
    fn is_cancellation(&self) -> bool;
}

/// Every file of an installation succeeded. Obelisk publishes `receipt` next.
pub struct InstalledFiles<R> {
    pub receipt: R,
    pub total_bytes: u64,
    pub network_bytes: u64,
    pub content_bytes: u64,
}

/// Where one installation Transfer writes: `directory` inside `parent`.
pub struct Destination<'a> {
    /// The folder the player chose. It must exist.
    pub parent: &'a Path,
    /// The storefront's dedicated folder name for this installation.
    pub directory: &'a str,
}

/// Runs one installation Transfer through `transfers`, which admits one at a
/// time. `prepare` resolves everything the storefront needs before any file of
/// the installation exists, and decides itself how to honor cancellation.
/// `install_files` writes every file under the installation lock. The old
/// Installation receipt is withdrawn before `install_files` starts, so a failed
/// or cancelled Transfer leaves no receipt behind.
pub async fn install<R, P, E, Prepare, Prepared, Files, Installed>(
    transfers: &Transfers<TransferProgress>,
    game: impl Into<String>,
    destination: Destination<'_>,
    prepare: Prepare,
    install_files: Files,
) -> Result<R, E>
where
    R: Serialize,
    E: TransferError,
    Prepare: FnOnce(PathBuf, CancelToken) -> Prepared,
    Prepared: Future<Output = Result<P, E>>,
    Files: FnOnce(P, PathBuf, TransferContext<TransferProgress>) -> Installed,
    Installed: Future<Output = Result<InstalledFiles<R>, E>>,
{
    transfers
        .run(TransferProgress::new(game), |transfer| async move {
            let result = run(destination, &transfer, prepare, install_files).await;
            if result.as_ref().is_err_and(E::is_cancellation) {
                // Publish the engine's cancellation as the Transfer's outcome.
                transfer.cancel_token().cancel();
            }
            result
        })
        .await
}

async fn run<R, P, E, Prepare, Prepared, Files, Installed>(
    destination: Destination<'_>,
    transfer: &TransferContext<TransferProgress>,
    prepare: Prepare,
    install_files: Files,
) -> Result<R, E>
where
    R: Serialize,
    E: TransferError,
    Prepare: FnOnce(PathBuf, CancelToken) -> Prepared,
    Prepared: Future<Output = Result<P, E>>,
    Files: FnOnce(P, PathBuf, TransferContext<TransferProgress>) -> Installed,
    Installed: Future<Output = Result<InstalledFiles<R>, E>>,
{
    let cancel = transfer.cancel_token().clone();
    let root = confine(destination)?;
    let prepared = prepare(root.clone(), cancel.clone()).await?;
    cancel.check()?;
    // Held across every file and the new receipt. Other sessions and
    // processes, including uninstall, must not interleave.
    let _lock = lock(&root)?;
    let receipt = receipt_path(&root)?;
    match fs::remove_file(&receipt) {
        Ok(()) => {}
        Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {}
        Err(error) => return Err(InstallFailure::Io(error).into()),
    }
    let installed = install_files(prepared, root.clone(), transfer.clone()).await?;
    cancel.check()?;
    write_receipt(&root, &installed.receipt)?;
    transfer.update(|progress| {
        progress.completed_bytes = installed.total_bytes;
        progress.total_bytes = installed.total_bytes;
        progress.network_bytes = installed.network_bytes;
        progress.content_bytes = installed.content_bytes;
        progress.current_file.clear();
        progress.message.clear();
    });
    Ok(installed.receipt)
}

/// Resolves the installation folder under its existing parent. Nothing is
/// created yet; a link or a file in the folder's place is refused.
fn confine(destination: Destination<'_>) -> Result<PathBuf, InstallFailure> {
    let Destination { parent, directory } = destination;
    if !parent.is_absolute() || !parent.is_dir() {
        return Err(InstallFailure::ParentMissing);
    }
    let mut components = Path::new(directory).components();
    let plain = matches!(components.next(), Some(Component::Normal(_)))
        && components.next().is_none()
        && !directory.contains(['/', '\\', '\0'])
        && !directory.eq_ignore_ascii_case(PARTIAL_DIRECTORY);
    if !plain {
        return Err(InstallFailure::UnsafeDirectory(directory.into()));
    }
    let root = parent.canonicalize()?.join(directory);
    check_folder(&root)?;
    Ok(root)
}

fn check_folder(root: &Path) -> Result<(), InstallFailure> {
    match fs::symlink_metadata(root) {
        Ok(metadata) if metadata.file_type().is_symlink() => {
            Err(InstallFailure::DestinationIsLink(root.to_owned()))
        }
        Ok(metadata) if !metadata.is_dir() => {
            Err(InstallFailure::DestinationIsFile(root.to_owned()))
        }
        Ok(_) => Ok(()),
        Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(()),
        Err(error) => Err(error.into()),
    }
}

/// Takes an installation's exclusive lock, creating its folder when missing.
/// Every Transfer, launch and uninstall of the installation shares this lock,
/// across Obelisk processes. The lock is released when the file is dropped.
pub fn lock(root: &Path) -> Result<File, InstallFailure> {
    check_folder(root)?;
    fs::create_dir_all(root)?;
    check_folder(root)?;
    let path = checked_file_path(root, Path::new(LOCK_FILE)).map_err(|error| match error {
        InstallError::Io(error) => InstallFailure::Io(error),
        _ => InstallFailure::UnsafeLock(root.join(LOCK_FILE)),
    })?;
    try_lock_file(&path)?.ok_or(InstallFailure::Locked)
}

fn receipt_path(root: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, InstallFailure> {
    checked_file_path(root, Path::new(RECEIPT_FILE)).map_err(|error| match error {
        InstallError::Io(error) => InstallFailure::Io(error),
        _ => InstallFailure::UnsafeReceipt(root.join(RECEIPT_FILE)),
    })
}

/// A completed installation, opened for launch under its installation lock.
/// No Transfer or uninstall of it can start until this is dropped.
pub struct Installation<R> {
    /// The canonical installation folder.
    pub root: PathBuf,
    /// Absent when no Transfer completed, or when the receipt is unreadable.
    pub receipt: Option<R>,
    _lock: File,
}

/// Opens an existing installation folder and reads its Installation receipt.
pub fn open<R: DeserializeOwned>(directory: &Path) -> Result<Installation<R>, InstallFailure> {
    if !directory.is_dir() {
        return Err(io::Error::from(io::ErrorKind::NotFound).into());
    }
    let lock = lock(directory)?;
    let root = directory.canonicalize()?;
    let receipt = receipt_in(&root)?;
    Ok(Installation {
        root,
        receipt,
        _lock: lock,
    })
}

/// Reads an installation folder's Installation receipt without its lock, as
/// the game it holds may be running. `None` while a Transfer has withdrawn
/// it, or when it is unreadable.
pub fn read_receipt<R: DeserializeOwned>(directory: &Path) -> Result<Option<R>, InstallFailure> {
    if !directory.is_dir() {
        return Err(io::Error::from(io::ErrorKind::NotFound).into());
    }
    receipt_in(&directory.canonicalize()?)
}

fn receipt_in<R: DeserializeOwned>(root: &Path) -> Result<Option<R>, InstallFailure> {
    Ok(read_file_bounded(&receipt_path(root)?, MAX_RECEIPT_BYTES)?
        .and_then(|bytes| serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).ok()))
}

/// Makes `receipt` the Installation receipt in `root`. Its path is checked
/// again right before the replacement, so a link substituted while files
/// were written is refused too.
fn write_receipt(root: &Path, receipt: &impl Serialize) -> Result<(), InstallFailure> {
    let bytes = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(receipt).map_err(io::Error::other)?;
    crate::write_atomic_with(&receipt_path(root)?, &bytes, || {
        receipt_path(root).map(drop)
    })
}

/// Why an installation was not removed.
#[derive(Debug, Error)]
pub enum RemovalFailure {
    #[error("not a dedicated installation folder: {0}")]
    Unsafe(PathBuf),
    #[error("a Transfer, launch or uninstall holds the installation")]
    Busy,
    #[error(transparent)]
    Io(#[from] io::Error),
}

/// Removes a storefront's dedicated installation folder under its
/// installation lock. The folder must be named `expected`, must not be or
/// contain any of `protected`, and no link may lead to it. Links inside it
/// are removed, never followed.
pub fn remove(directory: &Path, expected: &str, protected: &[&Path]) -> Result<(), RemovalFailure> {
    let refuse = || RemovalFailure::Unsafe(directory.to_owned());
    let resolved = dedicated(directory, expected, protected)?.ok_or_else(refuse)?;
    let _lock = lock(&resolved).map_err(|failure| match failure {
        InstallFailure::Locked => RemovalFailure::Busy,
        InstallFailure::Io(error) => RemovalFailure::Io(error),
        _ => refuse(),
    })?;
    Ok(fs::remove_dir_all(&resolved)?)
}

/// The canonical path of a storefront's dedicated installation folder: named
/// `expected`, neither being nor holding any of `protected`, and reached
/// through no link. `None` for any other folder.
fn dedicated(directory: &Path, expected: &str, protected: &[&Path]) -> io::Result<Option<PathBuf>> {
    if !directory.is_absolute()
        || expected.is_empty()
        || expected.contains('/')
        || directory
            .components()
            .any(|component| matches!(component, Component::ParentDir))
    {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    let candidate: PathBuf = directory
        .components()
        .filter(|component| !matches!(component, Component::CurDir))
        .collect();
    let named = |path: &Path| path.file_name().is_some_and(|name| name == expected);
    if !fs::symlink_metadata(&candidate)?.is_dir() || !named(&candidate) {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    let resolved = candidate.canonicalize()?;
    let safe = named(&resolved)
        && resolved.components().count() > 2
        && !protected.iter().any(|path| {
            path.canonicalize()
                .unwrap_or_else(|_| path.to_path_buf())
                .starts_with(&resolved)
        })
        // macOS spells its temporary folders both ways; any other link on
        // the way redirects the removal.
        && system_path(&candidate) == system_path(&resolved);
    Ok(safe.then_some(resolved))
}

/// Why an installation was not moved.
#[derive(Debug, Error)]
pub enum RelocationFailure {
    #[error("not a dedicated installation folder: {0}")]
    Unsafe(PathBuf),
    #[error("a folder is already where the installation goes: {0}")]
    Occupied(PathBuf),
    #[error("a Transfer, launch or uninstall holds the installation")]
    Busy,
    #[error("the move was cancelled")]
    Cancelled,
    #[error(transparent)]
    Io(#[from] io::Error),
}

/// Where an installation went.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Relocation {
    /// The canonical installation folder at its old place.
    pub origin: PathBuf,
    /// The canonical installation folder at its new place.
    pub directory: PathBuf,
    /// Whether the folder at its old place is gone. A copy to another disk
    /// that could not remove every original file still succeeded.
    pub original_removed: bool,
}

/// Moves a storefront's dedicated installation folder, named `expected` as
/// `remove` requires, into `parent`, an existing folder, under its
/// installation lock. On the same disk the folder only changes its place. To
/// another disk its files are copied into a hidden folder beside the
/// destination, which takes the installation's name once complete, then the
/// original goes; `progress` hears the bytes copied of the total as the copy
/// goes, and a cancellation removes the copy and keeps the original. Links
/// are copied as links. The Installation receipt the folder keeps then names
/// its new place.
pub fn relocate(
    directory: &Path,
    parent: &Path,
    expected: &str,
    protected: &[&Path],
    cancel: &CancelToken,
    mut progress: impl FnMut(u64, u64),
) -> Result<Relocation, RelocationFailure> {
    let refuse = || RelocationFailure::Unsafe(directory.to_owned());
    let resolved = dedicated(directory, expected, protected)?.ok_or_else(refuse)?;
    let parent = parent.canonicalize()?;
    if parent.starts_with(&resolved) || resolved.parent() == Some(parent.as_path()) {
        return Err(refuse());
    }
    let destination = parent.join(expected);
    match fs::symlink_metadata(&destination) {
        Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {}
        Ok(_) => return Err(RelocationFailure::Occupied(destination)),
        Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
    }
    let _lock = lock(&resolved).map_err(|failure| match failure {
        InstallFailure::Locked => RelocationFailure::Busy,
        InstallFailure::Io(error) => RelocationFailure::Io(error),
        _ => refuse(),
    })?;
    let original_removed = match fs::rename(&resolved, &destination) {
        Ok(()) => true,
        Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::CrossesDevices => {
            copy_across(&resolved, &destination, cancel, &mut progress)?
        }
        Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
    };
    rebase_receipt(&destination)?;
    Ok(Relocation {
        origin: resolved,
        directory: destination,
        original_removed,
    })
}

/// Copies the installation folder `from`, whose lock the caller holds, to
/// `to` on another disk through its staging folder, then removes `from`:
/// `false` when some original file stayed.
fn copy_across(
    from: &Path,
    to: &Path,
    cancel: &CancelToken,
    progress: &mut impl FnMut(u64, u64),
) -> Result<bool, RelocationFailure> {
    let (Some(parent), Some(name)) = (to.parent(), to.file_name()) else {
        return Err(RelocationFailure::Unsafe(to.to_owned()));
    };
    // A copy an earlier move left behind is only ever Obelisk's own.
    let staging = staging(parent, &name.to_string_lossy());
    match fs::symlink_metadata(&staging) {
        Ok(_) => fs::remove_dir_all(&staging)?,
        Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {}
        Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
    }
    let mut copy = Copy {
        cancel,
        buffer: vec![0; COPY_CHUNK],
        copied: 0,
        total: size(from)?,
        progress,
    };
    (copy.progress)(0, copy.total);
    let outcome = copy
        .folder(from, &staging, true)
        .and_then(|()| Ok(fs::rename(&staging, to)?));
    if let Err(failure) = outcome {
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&staging);
        return Err(failure);
    }
    Ok(fs::remove_dir_all(from).is_ok())
}

/// The hidden folder a move to another disk copies `expected` into, inside
/// the destination's `parent`.
fn staging(parent: &Path, expected: &str) -> PathBuf {
    parent.join(format!(".{expected}{STAGING_SUFFIX}"))
}

/// Whether `name` is one of the hidden folders a move to another disk
/// copies into.
pub fn is_staging(name: &str) -> bool {
    name.starts_with('.') && name.ends_with(STAGING_SUFFIX)
}

/// The bytes of every regular file in `folder`, links not followed.
fn size(folder: &Path) -> io::Result<u64> {
    let mut total = 0;
    for entry in fs::read_dir(folder)? {
        let entry = entry?;
        let kind = entry.file_type()?;
        if kind.is_dir() {
            total += size(&entry.path())?;
        } else if kind.is_file() {
            total += entry.metadata()?.len();
        }
    }
    Ok(total)
}

/// One copy of an installation folder to another disk.
struct Copy<'a, P: FnMut(u64, u64)> {
    cancel: &'a CancelToken,
    buffer: Vec<u8>,
    copied: u64,
    total: u64,
    /// Hears the bytes copied of the total after each run written.
    progress: &'a mut P,
}

impl<P: FnMut(u64, u64)> Copy<'_, P> {
    /// Copies `from` into the new folder `to`: folders, regular files with
    /// their permissions and times, and links as links. The installation
    /// lock stays behind.
    fn folder(&mut self, from: &Path, to: &Path, root: bool) -> Result<(), RelocationFailure> {
        fs::create_dir(to)?;
        for entry in fs::read_dir(from)? {
            let entry = entry?;
            let name = entry.file_name();
            if root && name == LOCK_FILE {
                continue;
            }
            let (source, target) = (entry.path(), to.join(&name));
            let kind = entry.file_type()?;
            if kind.is_symlink() {
                std::os::unix::fs::symlink(fs::read_link(&source)?, &target)?;
            } else if kind.is_dir() {
                self.folder(&source, &target, false)?;
            } else if kind.is_file() {
                self.file(&source, &target)?;
            }
            // Nothing else, such as a socket, belongs to an installation.
        }
        // Last, so a folder that only reads still takes its files. A disk
        // that keeps no permissions, such as exFAT, keeps what it can.
        let _ = fs::set_permissions(to, fs::metadata(from)?.permissions());
        Ok(())
    }

    fn file(&mut self, from: &Path, to: &Path) -> Result<(), RelocationFailure> {
        let mut source = File::open(from)?;
        let metadata = source.metadata()?;
        let mut target = File::create_new(to)?;
        loop {
            if self.cancel.is_cancelled() {
                return Err(RelocationFailure::Cancelled);
            }
            let read = match source.read(&mut self.buffer) {
                Ok(0) => break,
                Ok(read) => read,
                Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::Interrupted => continue,
                Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
            };
            target.write_all(&self.buffer[..read])?;
            self.copied += read as u64;
            (self.progress)(self.copied, self.total);
        }
        let _ = target.set_permissions(metadata.permissions());
        if let (Ok(accessed), Ok(modified)) = (metadata.accessed(), metadata.modified()) {
            let _ = target.set_times(
                FileTimes::new()
                    .set_accessed(accessed)
                    .set_modified(modified),
            );
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Makes the Installation receipt in `root` name `root` as its folder, as
/// after the folder moved.
fn rebase_receipt(root: &Path) -> Result<(), RelocationFailure> {
    let failure = |failure: InstallFailure| match failure {
        InstallFailure::Io(error) => RelocationFailure::Io(error),
        _ => RelocationFailure::Unsafe(root.join(RECEIPT_FILE)),
    };
    let Some(mut receipt) = receipt_in::<serde_json::Value>(root).map_err(failure)? else {
        return Ok(());
    };
    let Some(directory) = receipt.get_mut("directory") else {
        return Ok(());
    };
    let named = serde_json::Value::String(root.to_string_lossy().into_owned());
    if *directory == named {
        return Ok(());
    }
    *directory = named;
    write_receipt(root, &receipt).map_err(failure)
}

fn system_path(path: &Path) -> PathBuf {
    for alias in ["/var", "/tmp"] {
        if let Ok(rest) = path.strip_prefix(alias) {
            return Path::new("/private")
                .join(alias.trim_start_matches('/'))
                .join(rest);
        }
    }
    path.to_owned()
}
```

```rs
use super::*;
use crate::transfer::DownloadPhase;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
enum Failure {
    #[error("busy")]
    Busy,
    #[error("cancelled")]
    Cancelled,
    #[error("engine failed")]
    Engine,
    #[error("{0}")]
    Install(InstallFailure),
}

impl From<InstallFailure> for Failure {
    fn from(error: InstallFailure) -> Self {
        Self::Install(error)
    }
}
impl From<Cancelled> for Failure {
    fn from(_: Cancelled) -> Self {
        Self::Cancelled
    }
}
impl From<TransferBusy> for Failure {
    fn from(_: TransferBusy) -> Self {
        Self::Busy
    }
}
impl TransferError for Failure {
    fn is_cancellation(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Self::Cancelled)
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
struct Receipt {
    build: u32,
}

const NAME: &str = "store-7-macos";

fn files(build: u32) -> InstalledFiles<Receipt> {
    InstalledFiles {
        receipt: Receipt { build },
        total_bytes: 30,
        network_bytes: 12,
        content_bytes: 10,
    }
}

/// Installs through the real sequence with an engine that writes one file.
async fn install_build(
    transfers: &Transfers<TransferProgress>,
    parent: &Path,
    build: u32,
    engine: impl FnOnce(&Path) -> Result<(), Failure>,
) -> Result<Receipt, Failure> {
    install(
        transfers,
        "7",
        Destination {
            parent,
            directory: NAME,
        },
        |_, _| async { Ok::<_, Failure>(()) },
        |(), root, _| async move {
            engine(&root)?;
            Ok(files(build))
        },
    )
    .await
}

fn receipt_on_disk(root: &Path) -> Option<Receipt> {
    fs::read(root.join(RECEIPT_FILE))
        .ok()
        .map(|bytes| serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).unwrap())
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn the_receipt_is_published_after_every_file_with_the_final_progress() {
    let parent = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let transfers = Transfers::default();
    let root = parent.path().canonicalize().unwrap().join(NAME);
    let receipt = install_build(&transfers, parent.path(), 1, |root| {
        assert!(
            !root.join(RECEIPT_FILE).exists(),
            "no receipt while files change"
        );
        fs::write(root.join("game"), b"files").map_err(|_| Failure::Engine)
    })
    .await
    .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(receipt, Receipt { build: 1 });
    assert_eq!(receipt_on_disk(&root), Some(Receipt { build: 1 }));
    let progress = transfers.snapshot().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(progress.game, "7");
    assert_eq!(progress.state, TransferState::Complete);
    assert_eq!((progress.completed_bytes, progress.total_bytes), (30, 30));
    assert_eq!((progress.network_bytes, progress.content_bytes), (12, 10));
    assert_eq!(progress.message, "backend.transfer.complete");
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn preparation_runs_before_the_folder_or_its_lock_exists() {
    let parent = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let transfers = Transfers::default();
    let root = parent.path().canonicalize().unwrap().join(NAME);
    let seen = Arc::new(Mutex::new(None));
    let during = Arc::clone(&seen);
    install(
        &transfers,
        "7",
        Destination {
            parent: parent.path(),
            directory: NAME,
        },
        |prepared_root, _| async move {
            *during.lock().unwrap() = Some((prepared_root.clone(), prepared_root.exists()));
            Ok::<_, Failure>(())
        },
        |(), root, _| async move {
            assert!(
                matches!(lock(&root), Err(InstallFailure::Locked)),
                "files are written under the installation lock"
            );
            assert!(matches!(
                open::<Receipt>(&root),
                Err(InstallFailure::Locked)
            ));
            Ok(files(1))
        },
    )
    .await
    .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(*seen.lock().unwrap(), Some((root.clone(), false)));
    assert!(
        lock(&root).is_ok(),
        "the lock is released with the Transfer"
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn the_destination_is_confined_before_preparation() {
    let parent = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let transfers = Transfers::default();
    let attempt = |parent: PathBuf, directory: &'static str| {
        let transfers = &transfers;
        async move {
            install(
                transfers,
                "7",
                Destination {
                    parent: &parent,
                    directory,
                },
                |_, _| async { panic!("an unsafe destination is refused before preparation") },
                |(), _, _| async { Ok::<_, Failure>(files(1)) },
            )
            .await
            .map(|_: Receipt| ())
        }
    };
    let missing = parent.path().join("missing");
    assert!(matches!(
        attempt(missing, NAME).await,
        Err(Failure::Install(InstallFailure::ParentMissing))
    ));
    assert!(matches!(
        attempt(PathBuf::from("relative"), NAME).await,
        Err(Failure::Install(InstallFailure::ParentMissing))
    ));
    for directory in ["", ".", "..", "a/b", "a\\b", ".obelisk-content"] {
        assert!(
            matches!(
                attempt(parent.path().to_owned(), directory).await,
                Err(Failure::Install(InstallFailure::UnsafeDirectory(_)))
            ),
            "{directory:?}"
        );
    }
    fs::write(parent.path().join("file"), b"").unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(
        attempt(parent.path().to_owned(), "file").await,
        Err(Failure::Install(InstallFailure::DestinationIsFile(_)))
    ));
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        let outside = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(outside.path(), parent.path().join("link")).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            attempt(parent.path().to_owned(), "link").await,
            Err(Failure::Install(InstallFailure::DestinationIsLink(_)))
        ));
        assert_eq!(fs::read_dir(outside.path()).unwrap().count(), 0);
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_linked_lock_or_receipt_is_refused() {
    let parent = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let outside = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let target = outside.path().join("target");
    fs::write(&target, b"unchanged").unwrap();
    let root = parent.path().canonicalize().unwrap().join(NAME);
    fs::create_dir(&root).unwrap();
    std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&target, root.join(LOCK_FILE)).unwrap();
    let transfers = Transfers::default();
    assert!(matches!(
        install_build(&transfers, parent.path(), 1, |_| Ok(())).await,
        Err(Failure::Install(InstallFailure::UnsafeLock(_)))
    ));
    fs::remove_file(root.join(LOCK_FILE)).unwrap();
    fs::hard_link(&target, root.join(RECEIPT_FILE)).unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(
        install_build(&transfers, parent.path(), 1, |_| Ok(())).await,
        Err(Failure::Install(InstallFailure::UnsafeReceipt(_)))
    ));
    fs::remove_file(root.join(RECEIPT_FILE)).unwrap();
    // A link substituted while files are written is refused at publication.
    let substituted = target.clone();
    assert!(matches!(
        install_build(&transfers, parent.path(), 1, move |root| {
            std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&substituted, root.join(RECEIPT_FILE))
                .map_err(|_| Failure::Engine)
        })
        .await,
        Err(Failure::Install(InstallFailure::UnsafeReceipt(_)))
    ));
    assert_eq!(fs::read(&target).unwrap(), b"unchanged");
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn an_installation_opens_with_its_receipt_under_the_lock() {
    let parent = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let transfers = Transfers::default();
    let root = parent.path().canonicalize().unwrap().join(NAME);
    install_build(&transfers, parent.path(), 3, |_| Ok(()))
        .await
        .unwrap();

    let opened = open::<Receipt>(&parent.path().join(NAME)).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(opened.root, root);
    assert_eq!(opened.receipt, Some(Receipt { build: 3 }));
    assert!(matches!(lock(&root), Err(InstallFailure::Locked)));
    assert_eq!(
        read_receipt::<Receipt>(&root).unwrap(),
        Some(Receipt { build: 3 }),
        "a held installation's receipt still reads"
    );
    let busy = install_build(&transfers, parent.path(), 4, |_| Ok(())).await;
    assert!(matches!(
        busy,
        Err(Failure::Install(InstallFailure::Locked))
    ));
    assert_eq!(
        receipt_on_disk(&root),
        Some(Receipt { build: 3 }),
        "a refused Transfer withdraws nothing"
    );
    drop(opened);

    fs::write(root.join(RECEIPT_FILE), b"not json").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(open::<Receipt>(&root).unwrap().receipt, None);
    assert_eq!(read_receipt::<Receipt>(&root).unwrap(), None);
    assert!(matches!(
        open::<Receipt>(&parent.path().join("missing")),
        Err(InstallFailure::Io(_))
    ));
    assert!(matches!(
        read_receipt::<Receipt>(&parent.path().join("missing")),
        Err(InstallFailure::Io(_))
    ));
}

#[test]
fn show_uses_inspection_bytes_while_files_are_inspected_and_clears_the_message() {
    let mut progress = TransferProgress::new("7");
    let snapshot = DownloadProgress {
        phase: DownloadPhase::Verifying,
        completed_bytes: 10,
        verification_bytes: Some(40),
        total_bytes: 100,
        network_bytes: 3,
        content_bytes: 2,
        current_file: "Game/data.pak".into(),
        ..DownloadProgress::default()
    };
    progress.show(snapshot);
    assert_eq!(progress.state, TransferState::Verifying);
    assert_eq!((progress.completed_bytes, progress.total_bytes), (40, 100));
    assert_eq!((progress.network_bytes, progress.content_bytes), (3, 2));
    assert_eq!(progress.current_file, "Game/data.pak");
    assert_eq!(
        progress.message, "",
        "a storefront labels the Transfer itself"
    );

    progress.show(DownloadProgress {
        phase: DownloadPhase::Downloading,
        completed_bytes: 25,
        total_bytes: 100,
        ..DownloadProgress::default()
    });
    assert_eq!(progress.state, TransferState::Downloading);
    assert_eq!(
        progress.completed_bytes, 25,
        "repair reports completed bytes"
    );
    assert_eq!(progress.current_file, "");
    assert_eq!(progress.game, "7");
}

fn installed(parent: &Path, name: &str) -> PathBuf {
    let directory = parent.join(name);
    fs::create_dir_all(&directory).unwrap();
    fs::write(directory.join("game.bin"), b"installed content").unwrap();
    directory
}

#[test]
fn removal_deletes_only_the_dedicated_installation() {
    let parent = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let game = installed(parent.path(), "steam-620-macos");
    let sibling = installed(parent.path(), "steam-570-macos");
    remove(&game, "steam-620-macos", &[parent.path()]).unwrap();

    assert!(sibling.join("game.bin").exists());
}

#[test]
fn removal_refuses_other_names_protected_folders_and_short_paths() {
    let parent = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let game = installed(parent.path(), "Imported folder");
    for (directory, expected) in [
        (game.as_path(), "steam-620-macos"),
        (game.as_path(), ""),
        (game.as_path(), "a/b"),
        (Path::new("relative/steam-620-macos"), "steam-620-macos"),
    ] {
        assert!(
            matches!(
                remove(directory, expected, &[]),
                Err(RemovalFailure::Unsafe(_))
            ),
            "{directory:?} {expected:?}"
        );
    }
    let library = parent.path().join("library");
    fs::create_dir_all(library.join("inside")).unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(
        remove(&library, "library", &[&library.join("inside")]),
        Err(RemovalFailure::Unsafe(_))
    ));
    assert!(matches!(
        remove(Path::new("/"), "", &[]),
        Err(RemovalFailure::Unsafe(_))
    ));
    assert!(matches!(
        remove(Path::new("/tmp"), "tmp", &[]),
        Err(RemovalFailure::Unsafe(_))
    ));
    assert!(game.join("game.bin").exists());
    assert!(library.join("inside").exists());
}

#[test]
fn removal_accepts_both_spellings_of_the_system_temporary_folder() {
    let component = format!("ObeliskRemovalAliases-{}", std::process::id());
    let temporary = std::env::temp_dir();
    let temporary = temporary.to_string_lossy().trim_end_matches('/').to_owned();
    let private = if temporary.starts_with("/var/") {
        format!("/private{temporary}")
    } else {
        temporary.clone()
    };
    for parent in [
        "/tmp".to_owned(),
        "/private/tmp".to_owned(),
        temporary,
        private,
    ] {
        let root = Path::new(&parent).join(&component);
        let game = installed(&root, "steam-620-macos");
        remove(&game, "steam-620-macos", &[&root]).unwrap();
        assert!(!game.exists(), "{parent}");
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
    }
}

/// An installation with its receipt, a nested file and a link inside it.
fn complete(parent: &Path, name: &str) -> PathBuf {
    let game = installed(parent, name);
    fs::create_dir_all(game.join("Contents/MacOS")).unwrap();
    fs::write(game.join("Contents/MacOS/game"), b"binary").unwrap();
    std::os::unix::fs::symlink("Contents/MacOS/game", game.join("launcher")).unwrap();
    let receipt = serde_json::json!({ "appId": 620, "directory": game.to_string_lossy() });
    fs::write(game.join(RECEIPT_FILE), receipt.to_string()).unwrap();
    game
}

fn recorded_directory(game: &Path) -> String {
    let receipt: serde_json::Value =
        serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(game.join(RECEIPT_FILE)).unwrap()).unwrap();
    receipt["directory"].as_str().unwrap().to_owned()
}

#[test]
fn an_installation_moves_whole_and_its_receipt_names_its_new_place() {
    let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let root = root.path().canonicalize().unwrap();
    let game = complete(&root.join("internal"), "steam-620-macos");
    let external = root.join("external");
    fs::create_dir_all(&external).unwrap();
    let mut heard = Vec::new();
    let moved = relocate(
        &game,
        &external,
        "steam-620-macos",
        &[&root],
        &CancelToken::new(),
        |copied, total| heard.push((copied, total)),
    )
    .unwrap();
    let destination = external.join("steam-620-macos");
    assert_eq!(moved.directory, destination);
    assert!(moved.original_removed && !game.exists());
    assert!(heard.is_empty(), "the same disk only renames the folder");
    assert_eq!(fs::read(destination.join("launcher")).unwrap(), b"binary");
    assert_eq!(
        recorded_directory(&destination),
        destination.to_string_lossy()
    );
    assert!(lock(&destination).is_ok(), "no lock stays held");
}

#[test]
fn a_copy_to_another_disk_keeps_links_modes_and_times_and_reports_its_bytes() {
    use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
    let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let root = root.path().canonicalize().unwrap();
    let game = complete(&root.join("internal"), "steam-620-macos");
    let binary = game.join("Contents/MacOS/game");
    fs::set_permissions(&binary, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o755)).unwrap();
    let modified =
        std::time::SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH + std::time::Duration::from_secs(1_700_000_000);
    File::options()
        .write(true)
        .open(&binary)
        .unwrap()
        .set_modified(modified)
        .unwrap();
    let held = lock(&game).unwrap();
    let destination = root.join("external/steam-620-macos");
    fs::create_dir_all(destination.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
    let mut heard = Vec::new();
    let removed = copy_across(
        &game,
        &destination,
        &CancelToken::new(),
        &mut |copied, total| heard.push((copied, total)),
    )
    .unwrap();
    drop(held);
    assert!(removed && !game.exists());
    let link = destination.join("launcher");
    assert!(
        fs::symlink_metadata(&link)
            .unwrap()
            .file_type()
            .is_symlink()
    );
    assert_eq!(
        fs::read_link(&link).unwrap(),
        Path::new("Contents/MacOS/game")
    );
    let copied = fs::metadata(destination.join("Contents/MacOS/game")).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(copied.permissions().mode() & 0o777, 0o755);
    assert_eq!(copied.modified().unwrap(), modified);
    assert!(
        !destination.join(LOCK_FILE).exists(),
        "the lock stays behind"
    );
    assert_eq!(heard.first(), Some(&(0, heard[0].1)));
    let &(copied, total) = heard.last().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(copied, total);
    assert!(total > 0);
    assert!(heard.windows(2).all(|pair| pair[0].0 <= pair[1].0));
    assert!(!staging(destination.parent().unwrap(), "steam-620-macos").exists());
}

#[test]

        0
    );

#[test]
fn a_move_refuses_an_occupied_destination_and_any_other_folder() {
    let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let root = root.path().canonicalize().unwrap();
    let game = complete(&root.join("internal"), "steam-620-macos");
    let external = root.join("external");
    fs::create_dir_all(external.join("steam-620-macos")).unwrap();
    let cancel = CancelToken::new();
    assert!(matches!(
        relocate(&game, &external, "steam-620-macos", &[], &cancel, |_, _| {}),
        Err(RelocationFailure::Occupied(_))
    ));
    assert!(matches!(
        relocate(&game, &external, "steam-570-macos", &[], &cancel, |_, _| {}),
        Err(RelocationFailure::Unsafe(_))
    ));
    assert!(matches!(
        relocate(
            &game,
            &external,
            "steam-620-macos",
            &[&game],
            &cancel,
            |_, _| {}
        ),
        Err(RelocationFailure::Unsafe(_))
    ));
    assert!(matches!(
        relocate(
            &game,
            game.parent().unwrap(),
            "steam-620-macos",
            &[],
            &cancel,
            |_, _| {}
        ),
        Err(RelocationFailure::Unsafe(_))
    ));
    let held = lock(&game).unwrap();
    fs::remove_dir_all(external.join("steam-620-macos")).unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(
        relocate(&game, &external, "steam-620-macos", &[], &cancel, |_, _| {}),
        Err(RelocationFailure::Busy)
    ));
    drop(held);
    assert!(game.join("game.bin").exists());
}

#[test]
fn a_rebased_receipt_keeps_its_other_fields() {
    let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let root = root.path().canonicalize().unwrap();
    let game = complete(&root.join("internal"), "steam-620-macos");
    let moved = root.join("elsewhere/steam-620-macos");
    fs::create_dir_all(moved.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
    fs::rename(&game, &moved).unwrap();
    rebase_receipt(&moved).unwrap();
    let receipt: serde_json::Value =
        serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(moved.join(RECEIPT_FILE)).unwrap()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(receipt["directory"], moved.to_string_lossy().as_ref());
    assert_eq!(receipt["appId"], 620);
}
```

```rs
//! Validate storefront launch metadata without executing a process or a shell.
use std::path::{Component, Path, PathBuf};

use crate::Platform;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct LaunchTarget {
    pub executable: String,
    pub arguments: Vec<String>,
    pub working_directory: String,
    pub is_application_bundle: bool,
}

/// Storefront-neutral error suffix; callers supply their localization namespace.
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
#[error("{0}")]
pub struct LaunchError(&'static str);

impl LaunchError {
    pub fn key_suffix(&self) -> &'static str {
        self.0
    }
}

/// A canonical installation directory selected by the caller.
/// Validating it separately preserves storefront-specific configuration ordering.
pub struct LaunchDirectory(PathBuf);

impl LaunchDirectory {
    pub fn new(directory: &Path) -> Result<Self, LaunchError> {
        if !directory.is_absolute() || !directory.is_dir() {
            return Err(LaunchError("directoryMissing"));
        }
        directory
            .canonicalize()
            .map(Self)
            .map_err(|_| LaunchError("directoryUnreadable"))
    }

    pub fn resolve(
        &self,
        platform: Platform,
        executable: &str,
        launch_arguments: &str,
        working_directory: &str,
    ) -> Result<LaunchTarget, LaunchError> {
        let relative = relative_path(executable)?;
        if relative.as_os_str().is_empty() {
            return Err(LaunchError("executableMissing"));
        }
        let executable = confined_existing(&self.0, &relative)?;
        let extension = executable
            .extension()
            .and_then(|ext| ext.to_str())
            .unwrap_or("");
        if platform == Platform::Mac
            && ["exe", "com", "bat", "cmd"]
                .iter()
                .any(|ext| extension.eq_ignore_ascii_case(ext))
        {
            return Err(LaunchError("windowsExecutable"));
        }
        let bundle = if platform == Platform::Mac {
            application_bundle(&executable)?
        } else {
            None
        };
        if bundle.is_none() && !executable.is_file() {
            return Err(LaunchError("notExecutable"));
        }
        let working_directory = confined_existing(&self.0, &relative_path(working_directory)?)?;
        if !working_directory.is_dir() {
            return Err(LaunchError("invalidWorkingDirectory"));
        }
        let is_application_bundle = bundle.is_some();
        let executable = bundle.unwrap_or(executable);
        Ok(LaunchTarget {
            executable: path_string(&executable)?,
            arguments: parse_arguments(launch_arguments, platform)?,
            working_directory: path_string(&working_directory)?,
            is_application_bundle,
        })
    }
}

pub fn resolve(
    platform: Platform,
    directory: &Path,
    executable: &str,
    arguments: &str,
    working_directory: &str,
) -> Result<LaunchTarget, LaunchError> {
    LaunchDirectory::new(directory)?.resolve(platform, executable, arguments, working_directory)
}

fn relative_path(value: &str) -> Result<PathBuf, LaunchError> {
    // Storefront Windows metadata uses backslashes even when read on macOS.
    let normalized = value.replace('\\', "/");
    if normalized.contains(['\0', ':']) || normalized.starts_with('/') {
        return Err(LaunchError("invalidPath"));
    }
    let path = Path::new(&normalized);
    if path
        .components()
        .any(|part| !matches!(part, Component::Normal(_) | Component::CurDir))
    {
        return Err(LaunchError("pathOutsideGame"));
    }
    Ok(path.to_owned())
}

fn confined_existing(root: &Path, relative: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, LaunchError> {
    let path = root
        .join(relative)
        .canonicalize()
        .map_err(|_| LaunchError("fileMissing"))?;
    if !path.starts_with(root) {
        return Err(LaunchError("linkOutsideGame"));
    }
    Ok(path)
}

fn application_bundle(executable: &Path) -> Result<Option<PathBuf>, LaunchError> {
    if executable
        .extension()
        .is_some_and(|extension| extension.eq_ignore_ascii_case("app"))
    {
        if executable.is_dir() {
            return Ok(Some(executable.to_owned()));
        }
        return Err(LaunchError("invalidApplication"));
    }
    // An explicit executable within a bundle may differ from CFBundleExecutable.
    // Preserve the publisher's exact target instead of substituting the bundle.
    Ok(None)
}

fn path_string(path: &Path) -> Result<String, LaunchError> {
    path.to_str()
        .map(str::to_owned)
        .ok_or(LaunchError("invalidUtf8Path"))
}

/// Split publisher arguments with platform quoting rules and no shell expansion.
pub fn parse_arguments(source: &str, platform: Platform) -> Result<Vec<String>, LaunchError> {
    if source.contains('\0') || source.len() > 65_536 {
        return Err(LaunchError("invalidArguments"));
    }
    match platform {
        Platform::Windows => Ok(windows_arguments(source)),
        Platform::Mac => macos_arguments(source),
    }
}

fn windows_arguments(source: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    // Microsoft C runtime argv rules. Backslashes only escape double quotes;
    // no percent-variable expansion, wildcard expansion or command execution.
    let mut chars = source.chars().peekable();
    let mut output = Vec::new();
    while chars.peek().is_some() {
        while chars.peek().is_some_and(|c| matches!(c, ' ' | '\t')) {
            chars.next();
        }
        if chars.peek().is_none() {
            break;
        }
        let mut argument = String::new();
        let mut quoted = false;
        while chars.peek().is_some() {
            if !quoted && chars.peek().is_some_and(|c| matches!(c, ' ' | '\t')) {
                break;
            }
            let mut backslashes = 0;
            while chars.peek() == Some(&'\\') {
                chars.next();
                backslashes += 1;
            }
            if chars.peek() == Some(&'"') {
                argument.extend(std::iter::repeat_n('\\', backslashes / 2));
                chars.next();
                if backslashes % 2 == 1 {
                    argument.push('"');
                } else if quoted && chars.peek() == Some(&'"') {
                    argument.push('"');
                    chars.next();
                } else {
                    quoted = !quoted;
                }
            } else {
                argument.extend(std::iter::repeat_n('\\', backslashes));
                if !quoted && chars.peek().is_some_and(|c| matches!(c, ' ' | '\t')) {
                    break;
                }
                if let Some(character) = chars.next() {
                    argument.push(character);
                }
            }
        }
        output.push(argument);
    }
    output
}

fn macos_arguments(source: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, LaunchError> {
    let mut chars = source.chars().peekable();
    let mut output = Vec::new();
    let mut argument = String::new();
    let mut quote = None;
    let mut started = false;
    while let Some(character) = chars.next() {
        match (quote, character) {
            (None, character) if character.is_ascii_whitespace() => {
                if started {
                    output.push(std::mem::take(&mut argument));
                    started = false;
                }
            }
            (None, '\'' | '"') => {
                quote = Some(character);
                started = true;
            }
            (Some(current), character) if character == current => quote = None,
            (None | Some('"'), '\\') => {
                let escaped = chars.next().ok_or(LaunchError("incompleteEscape"))?;
                if escaped == '\n' {
                    continue;
                }
                if quote == Some('"') && !matches!(escaped, '$' | '`' | '"' | '\\') {
                    argument.push('\\');
                }
                argument.push(escaped);
                started = true;
            }
            _ => {
                argument.push(character);
                started = true;
            }
        }
    }
    if quote.is_some() {
        return Err(LaunchError("unclosedQuotes"));
    }
    if started {
        output.push(argument);
    }
    Ok(output)
}
```
