`crates/obelisk-core/src/library.rs`:

```rs
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::collections::HashSet;
use std::fs::{self, OpenOptions};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::Mutex;
use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};
use thiserror::Error;
use uuid::Uuid;

const SCHEMA_VERSION: u32 = 1;
const CATALOG_NAME: &str = "library.json";

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Error, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum CoreError {
    #[error("Invalid game: {reason}")]
    InvalidGame { reason: String },
    #[error("Cannot access the library: {reason}")]
    Storage { reason: String },
    #[error("The library cannot be read: {reason}")]
    CorruptLibrary { reason: String },
    #[error("Game not found: {id}")]
    NotFound { id: String },
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Deserialize, Serialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum GameKind {
    NativeMac,
    WindowsExecutable,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize, Serialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Game {
    pub id: String,
    pub title: String,
    pub path: String,
    pub added_at: u64,
    pub last_played_at: Option<u64>,
    pub kind: GameKind,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize, Serialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct Catalog {
    schema_version: u32,
    games: Vec<Game>,
}

impl Default for Catalog {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            schema_version: SCHEMA_VERSION,
            games: Vec::new(),
        }
    }
}

/// A small, synchronous catalog. Call from a background executor in a UI.
///
/// Each operation reloads validated data under an OS file lock. This avoids
/// stale overwrites across multiple instances and processes. A mutex also
/// serializes calls on the same instance. Replacing JSON is atomic; failed
/// mutations leave the previous catalog intact. Game files are never changed.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Library {
    storage_dir: PathBuf,
    operation: Mutex<()>,
}

impl Library {
    pub fn open(storage_dir: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<Self, CoreError> {
        fs::create_dir_all(storage_dir.as_ref()).map_err(storage_error)?;
        let storage_dir = fs::canonicalize(storage_dir.as_ref()).map_err(storage_error)?;
        let library = Self {
            storage_dir,
            operation: Mutex::new(()),
        };
        // Check existing data immediately; malformed data must not appear empty.
        library.with_catalog(|_| Ok(()))?;
        Ok(library)
    }

    pub fn games(&self) -> Result<Vec<Game>, CoreError> {
        self.with_catalog(|catalog| {
            let mut games = catalog.games;
            games.sort_by(|left, right| {
                right
                    .last_played_at
                    .unwrap_or(right.added_at)
                    .cmp(&left.last_played_at.unwrap_or(left.added_at))
                    .then_with(|| left.title.cmp(&right.title))
                    .then_with(|| left.id.cmp(&right.id))
            });
            Ok(games)
        })
    }

    pub fn add_local_game(&self, path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<Game, CoreError> {
        let canonical =
            fs::canonicalize(path.as_ref()).map_err(|error| CoreError::InvalidGame {
                reason: format!("The selected path is unavailable: {error}"),
            })?;
        let kind = game_kind(&canonical)?;
        let path = canonical
            .to_str()
            .ok_or_else(|| invalid_game("The selected path is not valid UTF-8."))?
            .to_owned();
        let title = canonical
            .file_stem()
            .and_then(|name| name.to_str())
            .filter(|name| !name.trim().is_empty())
            .ok_or_else(|| invalid_game("The selected game has no valid name."))?
            .to_owned();
        self.with_catalog(|mut catalog| {
            if let Some(existing) = catalog.games.iter().find(|game| game.path == path) {
                return Ok(existing.clone());
            }
            let game = Game {
                id: Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
                title,
                path,
                added_at: now()?,
                last_played_at: None,
                kind,
            };
            catalog.games.push(game.clone());
            self.save(&catalog)?;
            Ok(game)
        })
    }

    /// Removes only the catalog entry. Never deletes the original game.
    pub fn remove_game(&self, id: &str) -> Result<(), CoreError> {
        self.with_catalog(|mut catalog| {
            let index = catalog
                .games
                .iter()
                .position(|game| game.id == id)
                .ok_or_else(|| CoreError::NotFound { id: id.to_owned() })?;
            catalog.games.remove(index);
            self.save(&catalog)
        })
    }

    /// Records an acknowledged launch. Does not launch the game itself.
    pub fn record_launch(&self, id: &str) -> Result<(), CoreError> {
        self.with_catalog(|mut catalog| {
            let game = catalog
                .games
                .iter_mut()
                .find(|game| game.id == id)
                .ok_or_else(|| CoreError::NotFound { id: id.to_owned() })?;
            game.last_played_at = Some(now()?);
            self.save(&catalog)
        })
    }

    fn with_catalog<T>(
        &self,
        action: impl FnOnce(Catalog) -> Result<T, CoreError>,
    ) -> Result<T, CoreError> {
        let _operation = self.operation.lock().map_err(|_| CoreError::Storage {
            reason: "The library operation lock was poisoned.".to_owned(),
        })?;
        let lock = OpenOptions::new()
            .create(true)
            .truncate(false)
            .read(true)
            .write(true)
            .open(self.storage_dir.join("library.lock"))
            .map_err(storage_error)?;
        lock.lock().map_err(storage_error)?;
        // Dropping this file releases the OS lock even when reading/action fails.
        let catalog = self.load()?;
        action(catalog)
    }

    fn load(&self) -> Result<Catalog, CoreError> {
        let bytes = match fs::read(self.storage_dir.join(CATALOG_NAME)) {
            Ok(bytes) => bytes,
            Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
                return Ok(Catalog::default());
            }
            Err(error) => return Err(storage_error(error)),
        };
        let catalog: Catalog = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes)
            .map_err(|error| corrupt_library(format!("Invalid JSON or catalog fields: {error}")))?;
        validate_catalog(&catalog)?;
        Ok(catalog)
    }

    fn save(&self, catalog: &Catalog) -> Result<(), CoreError> {
        let mut bytes = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(catalog).map_err(storage_error)?;
        bytes.push(b'\n');
        crate::write_atomic(&self.storage_dir.join(CATALOG_NAME), &bytes).map_err(storage_error)
    }
}

fn game_kind(path: &Path) -> Result<GameKind, CoreError> {
    let extension = path.extension().and_then(|value| value.to_str());
    match extension {
        Some(value) if value.eq_ignore_ascii_case("app") && path.is_dir() => {
            Ok(GameKind::NativeMac)
        }
        Some(value) if value.eq_ignore_ascii_case("exe") && path.is_file() => {
            Ok(GameKind::WindowsExecutable)
        }
        _ => Err(invalid_game(
            "Select a macOS .app directory or a Windows .exe file.",
        )),
    }
}

fn validate_catalog(catalog: &Catalog) -> Result<(), CoreError> {
    if catalog.schema_version != SCHEMA_VERSION {
        return Err(corrupt_library(format!(
            "Unsupported schema version {} (expected {SCHEMA_VERSION}).",
            catalog.schema_version
        )));
    }
    let mut ids = HashSet::new();
    let mut paths = HashSet::new();
    for game in &catalog.games {
        if Uuid::parse_str(&game.id).is_err() || !ids.insert(&game.id) {
            return Err(corrupt_library("Invalid or duplicate game ID."));
        }
        let path = Path::new(&game.path);
        let extension = path.extension().and_then(|value| value.to_str());
        let expected_extension = match game.kind {
            GameKind::NativeMac => "app",
            GameKind::WindowsExecutable => "exe",
        };
        if !path.is_absolute()
            || !paths.insert(&game.path)
            || game.title.trim().is_empty()
            || !extension.is_some_and(|value| value.eq_ignore_ascii_case(expected_extension))
        {
            return Err(corrupt_library(
                "Invalid or duplicate game path, title, or kind.",
            ));
        }
        // Missing games remain in the catalog so users can remove them explicitly.
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn now() -> Result<u64, CoreError> {
    SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|duration| duration.as_secs())
        .map_err(storage_error)
}

fn invalid_game(reason: impl Into<String>) -> CoreError {
    CoreError::InvalidGame {
        reason: reason.into(),
    }
}

fn corrupt_library(reason: impl Into<String>) -> CoreError {
    CoreError::CorruptLibrary {
        reason: reason.into(),
    }
}

fn storage_error(error: impl std::fmt::Display) -> CoreError {
    CoreError::Storage {
        reason: error.to_string(),
    }
}
```

`crates/obelisk-core/src/library_cache.rs`:

```rs
//! The last library each storefront account loaded, in one JSON file beside
//! the catalog: `{"version": 1, "<storefront>": {"<account>": [games]}}`, each
//! game a JSON object named by its `id`. A library shows from it at once, then
//! updates from its storefront. Each game also keeps `lastLaunchedAt`, when
//! the account last launched it from Obelisk.
//!
//! The cache only spares the wait for a storefront: an unreadable file has no
//! library, the next change replaces it, and a failed write is retried by the
//! next change.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::{Map, Value};
use std::{
    collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap},
    fs,
    path::{Path, PathBuf},
    sync::{
        Arc, LazyLock, Mutex, Weak,
        atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering},
    },
    time::Duration,
};

use crate::date;

/// Its name in the library directory, beside the catalog's `library.json`.
pub const FILE_NAME: &str = "library-cache.json";
const VERSION: u64 = 1;
const LAUNCH: &str = "lastLaunchedAt";
/// How long a write waits for the changes that follow the first.
const WRITE_DELAY: Duration = Duration::from_millis(500);

/// One game as the cache keeps it.
pub type Entry = Map<String, Value>;

/// One game's last launch from Obelisk.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Launch {
    pub storefront: String,
    pub account: String,
    pub game: String,
    /// Seconds since the Unix epoch.
    pub at: u64,
}

/// The cache of one library directory. Every cache of a directory in this
/// process shares one document, so none overwrites another's changes. Changes
/// reach the file off the caller's thread.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct LibraryCache {
    shared: Arc<Shared>,
}

static OPEN: LazyLock<Mutex<HashMap<PathBuf, Weak<Shared>>>> = LazyLock::new(Default::default);

impl LibraryCache {
    pub fn open(directory: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Self {
        let file = directory.as_ref().join(FILE_NAME);
        let mut open = OPEN.lock().unwrap();
        if let Some(shared) = open.get(&file).and_then(Weak::upgrade) {
            return Self { shared };
        }
        open.retain(|_, shared| shared.strong_count() > 0);
        let shared = Arc::new(Shared {
            document: Mutex::new(Document::read(&file)),
            file: file.clone(),
            written: Mutex::new(0),
            scheduled: AtomicBool::new(false),
        });
        open.insert(file, Arc::downgrade(&shared));
        Self { shared }
    }

    /// The account's last library, each game as `read` reads it; empty when
    /// it has none.
    pub fn library<T>(
        &self,
        storefront: &str,
        account: &str,
        read: impl FnMut(&Entry) -> Option<T>,
    ) -> Vec<T> {
        let document = self.shared.document.lock().unwrap();
        document
            .libraries
            .get(storefront)
            .and_then(|libraries| libraries.get(account))
            .map_or_else(Vec::new, |entries| {
                entries.iter().filter_map(read).collect()
            })
    }

    /// Where a session signed in to `account` keeps the libraries it loads,
    /// until the account is forgotten.
    pub fn account(&self, storefront: &str, account: &str) -> AccountLibrary {
        let key = (storefront.to_owned(), account.to_owned());
        let forgotten = self.shared.document.lock().unwrap().forgotten(&key);
        AccountLibrary {
            cache: self.clone(),
            key,
            forgotten,
        }
    }

    /// Records that the account launched `game` from Obelisk, in the game's
    /// entry. A game whose library was never saved has no entry to keep it.
    pub fn record_launch(&self, storefront: &str, account: &str, game: &str, at: u64) {
        self.shared.change(|document| {
            let Some(entry) = document
                .libraries
                .get_mut(storefront)
                .and_then(|libraries| libraries.get_mut(account))
                .and_then(|entries| entries.iter_mut().find(|entry| id(entry) == Some(game)))
            else {
                return false;
            };
            entry.insert(LAUNCH.into(), Value::String(iso8601(at)));
            true
        });
    }

    /// Every game's last launch, for every storefront and account.
    pub fn launches(&self) -> Vec<Launch> {
        let document = self.shared.document.lock().unwrap();
        let mut launches = Vec::new();
        for (storefront, libraries) in &document.libraries {
            for (account, entries) in libraries {
                launches.extend(entries.iter().filter_map(|entry| {
                    Some(Launch {
                        storefront: storefront.clone(),
                        account: account.clone(),
                        game: id(entry)?.to_owned(),
                        at: launched_at(entry)?,
                    })
                }));
            }
        }
        launches
    }

    /// Removes the account's library and its launches, as signing it out
    /// does. A session bound to the account before can no longer write it.
    pub fn forget(&self, storefront: &str, account: &str) {
        self.shared.change(|document| {
            let key = (storefront.to_owned(), account.to_owned());
            *document.forgotten.entry(key).or_default() += 1;
            document
                .libraries
                .get_mut(storefront)
                .and_then(|libraries| libraries.remove(account))
                .is_some()
        });
    }

    /// Writes the last change now, on the caller's thread.
    pub fn flush(&self) {
        self.shared.write();
    }
}

/// One account's library, as the session signed in to it loads it.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct AccountLibrary {
    cache: LibraryCache,
    key: (String, String),
    /// How many times the account was forgotten when the session bound it.
    forgotten: u64,
}

impl AccountLibrary {
    /// Replaces the account's library with `games`. Each game keeps its last
    /// launch, and the fields `kept` that its previous entry had and `games`
    /// lacks, such as details another request loads.
    pub fn replace(&self, games: Vec<Entry>, kept: &[&str]) {
        self.change(|libraries, account| {
            let previous = libraries.get(account);
            let by_id: HashMap<&str, &Entry> = previous
                .into_iter()
                .flatten()
                .filter_map(|entry| Some((id(entry)?, entry)))
                .collect();
            let games: Vec<Entry> = games
                .into_iter()
                .map(|mut game| {
                    if let Some(old) = id(&game).and_then(|id| by_id.get(id)) {
                        for key in kept.iter().copied().chain([LAUNCH]) {
                            if !game.contains_key(key)
                                && let Some(value) = old.get(key)
                            {
                                game.insert(key.into(), value.clone());
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    game
                })
                .collect();
            // A library loaded again unchanged is not written again.
            if previous == Some(&games) {
                return false;
            }
            libraries.insert(account.to_owned(), games);
            true
        });
    }

    /// The account's library, each game as `read` reads it; empty when it has
    /// none.
    pub fn read<T>(&self, read: impl FnMut(&Entry) -> Option<T>) -> Vec<T> {
        let (storefront, account) = &self.key;
        self.cache.library(storefront, account, read)
    }

    /// Changes every game of the account's library, as a request that loaded
    /// more of each does; `change` tells whether it changed the game. An
    /// account with no library is left without one.
    pub fn update(&self, mut change: impl FnMut(&mut Entry) -> bool) {
        self.change(|libraries, account| {
            let Some(entries) = libraries.get_mut(account) else {
                return false;
            };
            entries
                .iter_mut()
                .fold(false, |changed, entry| change(entry) | changed)
        });
    }

    fn change(&self, change: impl FnOnce(&mut BTreeMap<String, Vec<Entry>>, &str) -> bool) {
        let (storefront, account) = &self.key;
        self.cache.shared.change(|document| {
            if document.forgotten(&self.key) != self.forgotten {
                return false;
            }
            change(
                document.libraries.entry(storefront.clone()).or_default(),
                account,
            )
        });
    }
}

struct Shared {
    file: PathBuf,
    document: Mutex<Document>,
    /// The document revision on disk, held while it is written.
    written: Mutex<u64>,
    /// A write waits for the changes that follow the first.
    scheduled: AtomicBool,
}

impl Shared {
    fn change(self: &Arc<Self>, change: impl FnOnce(&mut Document) -> bool) {
        let mut document = self.document.lock().unwrap();
        if !change(&mut document) {
            return;
        }
        document.revision += 1;
        drop(document);
        // Changes in quick succession, such as a library's batches of
        // platforms, share one write.
        if !self.scheduled.swap(true, Ordering::AcqRel) {
            let shared = self.clone();
            std::thread::spawn(move || {
                std::thread::sleep(WRITE_DELAY);
                shared.scheduled.store(false, Ordering::Release);
                shared.write();
            });
        }
    }

    /// Writes the document, unless a later write already did.
    fn write(&self) {
        let mut written = self.written.lock().unwrap();
        let (revision, bytes) = {
            let document = self.document.lock().unwrap();
            if document.revision <= *written {
                return;
            }
            (document.revision, document.bytes())
        };
        if let Some(directory) = self.file.parent() {
            let _ = fs::create_dir_all(directory);
        }
        if bytes.is_some_and(|bytes| crate::write_atomic(&self.file, &bytes).is_ok()) {
            *written = revision;
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Default)]
struct Document {
    /// Each storefront's libraries, by account.
    libraries: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, Vec<Entry>>>,
    revision: u64,
    /// How many times each storefront account was forgotten.
    forgotten: HashMap<(String, String), u64>,
}

/// The file: its version beside each storefront's libraries.
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct File<Libraries> {
    version: u64,
    #[serde(flatten)]
    libraries: Libraries,
}

impl Document {
    fn read(file: &Path) -> Self {
        let file = fs::read(file)
            .ok()
            .and_then(|bytes| serde_json::from_slice::<File<_>>(&bytes).ok())
            .filter(|file| file.version == VERSION);
        Self {
            libraries: file.map(|file| file.libraries).unwrap_or_default(),
            ..Self::default()
        }
    }

    fn bytes(&self) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
        serde_json::to_vec(&File {
            version: VERSION,
            libraries: &self.libraries,
        })
        .ok()
    }

    fn forgotten(&self, key: &(String, String)) -> u64 {
        self.forgotten.get(key).copied().unwrap_or(0)
    }
}

fn id(entry: &Entry) -> Option<&str> {
    entry.get("id")?.as_str()
}

/// When the account last launched the entry's game from Obelisk, in seconds
/// since the Unix epoch.
pub fn launched_at(entry: &Entry) -> Option<u64> {
    entry.get(LAUNCH)?.as_str().and_then(parse_iso8601)
}

/// `at` in UTC, as Swift's `ISO8601DateFormatter` writes a date.
fn iso8601(at: u64) -> String {
    let (days, seconds) = (at / 86_400, at % 86_400);
    let (year, month, day) = date::civil_from_days(days as i64);
    format!(
        "{year:04}-{month:02}-{day:02}T{:02}:{:02}:{:02}Z",
        seconds / 3600,
        seconds / 60 % 60,
        seconds % 60
    )
}

fn parse_iso8601(text: &str) -> Option<u64> {
    let bytes = text.as_bytes();
    let separators = [
        (4, b'-'),
        (7, b'-'),
        (10, b'T'),
        (13, b':'),
        (16, b':'),
        (19, b'Z'),
    ];
    if bytes.len() != 20 || separators.iter().any(|&(at, byte)| bytes[at] != byte) {
        return None;
    }
    let number = |start: usize, end: usize| text[start..end].parse::<u64>().ok();
    let (year, month, day) = (number(0, 4)?, number(5, 7)?, number(8, 10)?);
    let (hour, minute, second) = (number(11, 13)?, number(14, 16)?, number(17, 19)?);
    if year < 1970 || !(1..=12).contains(&month) || !(1..=31).contains(&day) {
        return None;
    }
    if hour > 23 || minute > 59 || second > 59 {
        return None;
    }
    let days = date::days_from_civil(year as i64, month as i64, day as i64) as u64;
    Some(days * 86_400 + hour * 3600 + minute * 60 + second)
}
```

```rs
use super::*;
use serde_json::json;
use tempfile::TempDir;

fn entry(value: Value) -> Entry {
    match value {
        Value::Object(entry) => entry,
        _ => panic!("an entry is an object"),
    }
}

fn names(entries: &[Entry]) -> Vec<&str> {
    entries
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|entry| entry["name"].as_str())
        .collect()
}

fn library(cache: &LibraryCache, storefront: &str, account: &str) -> Vec<Entry> {
    cache.library(storefront, account, |entry| Some(entry.clone()))
}

/// The file as a later Obelisk would read it, past every shared document.
fn on_disk(directory: &TempDir) -> Document {
    Document::read(&directory.path().join(FILE_NAME))
}

#[test]
fn every_storefront_and_account_keeps_its_own_library_in_one_compact_file() {
    let directory = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let cache = LibraryCache::open(directory.path());
    cache.account("steam", "7").replace(
        vec![entry(
            json!({"id": "620", "name": "Portal 2", "record": {"has_dlc": true}}),
        )],
        &[],
    );
    cache
        .account("steam", "8")
        .replace(vec![entry(json!({"id": "570", "name": "Dota 2"}))], &[]);
    cache.account("epic", "epic-a").replace(
        vec![entry(
            json!({"id": "space:rocket", "name": "Rocket League"}),
        )],
        &[],
    );
    cache.flush();

    let bytes = fs::read(directory.path().join(FILE_NAME)).unwrap();
    assert!(!bytes.contains(&b'\n'), "written compact");
    let file: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(file["version"], 1);
    assert_eq!(file["steam"]["7"][0]["record"]["has_dlc"], true);
    let reopened = on_disk(&directory);
    assert_eq!(
        names(&reopened.libraries["steam"]["8"]),
        ["Dota 2"],
        "saving one library keeps the others"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        names(&reopened.libraries["epic"]["epic-a"]),
        ["Rocket League"]
    );
    assert!(library(&cache, "steam", "9").is_empty());
}

#[test]
fn every_cache_of_a_directory_shares_one_document() {
    let directory = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let first = LibraryCache::open(directory.path());
    let second = LibraryCache::open(directory.path());
    first
        .account("steam", "7")
        .replace(vec![entry(json!({"id": "620", "name": "Portal 2"}))], &[]);
    second.record_launch("steam", "7", "620", 1_790_000_000);
    second.account("epic", "epic-a").replace(
        vec![entry(
            json!({"id": "space:rocket", "name": "Rocket League"}),
        )],
        &[],
    );
    first.flush();

    let reopened = on_disk(&directory);
    assert_eq!(
        reopened.libraries["steam"]["7"][0][LAUNCH], "2026-09-21T14:13:20Z",
        "neither cache overwrote the other's change"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        names(&reopened.libraries["epic"]["epic-a"]),
        ["Rocket League"]
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_reloaded_library_keeps_each_games_launch_and_the_details_another_request_loaded() {
    let directory = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let cache = LibraryCache::open(directory.path());
    let account = cache.account("steam", "7");
    account.replace(
        vec![
            entry(json!({"id": "620", "name": "Portal 2"})),
            entry(json!({"id": "570", "name": "Dota 2"})),
        ],
        &["platforms"],
    );
    account.update(|entry| entry.insert("platforms".into(), json!(["macos"])).is_none());
    cache.record_launch("steam", "7", "620", 1_790_000_000);

    account.replace(
        vec![
            entry(json!({"id": "620", "name": "Portal 2 renamed"})),
            entry(json!({"id": "400", "name": "Portal", "platforms": ["windows"]})),
        ],
        &["platforms"],
    );
    let library = library(&cache, "steam", "7");
    assert_eq!(
        names(&library),
        ["Portal 2 renamed", "Portal"],
        "Dota 2 left the library"
    );
    assert_eq!(library[0]["platforms"], json!(["macos"]));
    assert_eq!(library[0][LAUNCH], "2026-09-21T14:13:20Z");
    assert_eq!(
        library[1]["platforms"],
        json!(["windows"]),
        "a loaded field wins"
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_library_loaded_again_unchanged_is_not_written_again() {
    let directory = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let cache = LibraryCache::open(directory.path());
    let account = cache.account("steam", "7");
    let games = || vec![entry(json!({"id": "620", "name": "Portal 2"}))];
    account.replace(games(), &[]);
    account.update(|entry| entry.insert("platforms".into(), json!(["macos"])).is_none());
    cache.flush();
    fs::remove_file(directory.path().join(FILE_NAME)).unwrap();

    account.replace(games(), &["platforms"]);
    account.update(|_| false);
    cache.flush();
    assert!(!directory.path().join(FILE_NAME).exists());
}

#[test]
fn an_update_never_creates_a_library() {
    let directory = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let cache = LibraryCache::open(directory.path());
    cache
        .account("epic", "epic-a")
        .update(|entry| entry.insert("playtimeSeconds".into(), json!(60)).is_none());
    cache.record_launch("epic", "epic-a", "space:rocket", 1_790_000_000);
    cache.flush();
    assert!(library(&cache, "epic", "epic-a").is_empty());
    assert!(!directory.path().join(FILE_NAME).exists());
}

#[test]
fn forgetting_an_account_drops_its_library_and_launches_and_its_earlier_session_can_no_longer_write_it()
 {
    let directory = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let cache = LibraryCache::open(directory.path());
    let earlier = cache.account("steam", "7");
    earlier.replace(vec![entry(json!({"id": "620", "name": "Portal 2"}))], &[]);
    cache
        .account("steam", "8")
        .replace(vec![entry(json!({"id": "570", "name": "Dota 2"}))], &[]);
    cache.record_launch("steam", "7", "620", 1_790_000_000);

    cache.forget("steam", "7");
    earlier.replace(vec![entry(json!({"id": "620", "name": "Portal 2"}))], &[]);
    assert!(
        library(&cache, "steam", "7").is_empty(),
        "a signed-out session's late answer"
    );
    assert!(cache.launches().is_empty());
    assert_eq!(names(&library(&cache, "steam", "8")), ["Dota 2"]);

    cache
        .account("steam", "7")
        .replace(vec![entry(json!({"id": "620", "name": "Portal 2"}))], &[]);
    assert_eq!(
        names(&library(&cache, "steam", "7")),
        ["Portal 2"],
        "signing in again"
    );
}

#[test]
fn launches_read_back_as_swift_wrote_them() {
    let directory = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    fs::write(
        directory.path().join(FILE_NAME),

            "version": 1,
            "steam": {"7": [
                {"id": "620", "lastLaunchedAt": "2026-09-14T23:53:20Z"},
                {"id": "570", "lastLaunchedAt": "yesterday"},
                {"id": "400"},
            ]},
            "epic": {"epic-a": [{"id": "space:rocket", "lastLaunchedAt": "2000-02-29T00:00:00Z"}]},
        })
        .to_string(),
    )
    .unwrap();
    let mut launches = LibraryCache::open(directory.path()).launches();
    launches.sort_by_key(|launch| launch.at);
    assert_eq!(
        launches,
        [
            Launch {
                storefront: "epic".into(),
                account: "epic-a".into(),
                game: "space:rocket".into(),
                at: 951_782_400,
            },
            Launch {
                storefront: "steam".into(),
                account: "7".into(),
                game: "620".into(),
                at: 1_789_430_000,
            },
        ]
    );
}

#[test]
fn dates_are_iso_8601_in_utc() {
    for (at, text) in [
        (0, "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"),
        (951_782_400, "2000-02-29T00:00:00Z"),
        (1_790_000_000, "2026-09-21T14:13:20Z"),
        (4_102_444_799, "2099-12-31T23:59:59Z"),
    ] {
        assert_eq!(iso8601(at), text);
        assert_eq!(parse_iso8601(text), Some(at));
    }
    for text in [
        "2026-09-21T14:13:20",
        "2026-13-01T00:00:00Z",
        "2026-09-21T24:00:00Z",
        "1969-12-31T23:59:59Z",
        "2026-09-21 14:13:20Z",
    ] {
        assert_eq!(parse_iso8601(text), None, "{text}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn an_unreadable_file_has_no_library_and_the_next_change_replaces_it() {
    for content in ["not json", r#"{"version": 2, "steam": {"7": []}}"#] {
        let directory = TempDir::new().unwrap();
        fs::write(directory.path().join(FILE_NAME), content).unwrap();
        let cache = LibraryCache::open(directory.path());
        assert!(library(&cache, "steam", "7").is_empty(), "{content}");
        cache
            .account("steam", "7")
            .replace(vec![entry(json!({"id": "620", "name": "Portal 2"}))], &[]);
        cache.flush();
        assert_eq!(
            names(&on_disk(&directory).libraries["steam"]["7"]),
            ["Portal 2"]
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_cache_leaves_the_catalog_readable() {
    let directory = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let catalog = crate::Library::open(directory.path()).unwrap();
    let executable = directory.path().join("A game.exe");
    fs::write(&executable, [0x4d, 0x5a]).unwrap();
    let added = catalog.add_local_game(&executable).unwrap();

    let cache = LibraryCache::open(directory.path());
    cache
        .account("steam", "7")

    cache.flush();

    let games = crate::Library::open(directory.path())
        .unwrap()
        .games()
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        games.iter().map(|game| &game.id).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        [&added.id]
    );
}
```

`crates/obelisk-core/src/mac_build.rs`:

```rs
//! Whether a Mac build's game runs natively on Apple silicon, told from the
//! build's own files before it is installed. A storefront lists the files its
//! manifest names and reads the first bytes of the few asked for; nothing here
//! reaches the network or the disk. Obelisk installs a Mac build only when it
//! does: an Intel or 32-bit one goes through Wine as its Windows build.
use std::{
    collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap},
    future::Future,
};

/// How many bytes of a program tell its architectures: more than the header
/// of a universal binary of the most slices a launch accepts.
pub const PROGRAM_HEAD: u64 = 4096;
/// An Info.plist larger than this names no executable.
const MAX_INFO_PLIST: u64 = 1024 * 1024;
/// Links followed to reach one file.
const MAX_LINKS: usize = 8;
const CPU_TYPE_ARM64: u32 = 0x0100_000c;
/// A universal binary listing more slices is refused at launch.
const MAX_SLICES: u32 = 32;

enum Entry<F> {
    File {
        file: F,
        size: u64,
    },
    /// Its target, from the build's root.
    Link(String),
}

/// A build's files and links, by their path from the installation's root as
/// the storefront's manifest names them. Folders are those the paths go
/// through. Paths match whatever their case, as on the Mac's disk.
pub struct Listing<F> {
    entries: HashMap<String, (String, Entry<F>)>,
}

impl<F> Default for Listing<F> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            entries: HashMap::new(),
        }
    }
}

impl<F: Copy> Listing<F> {
    /// A file, which `read` names as `file`. A later entry of the same path
    /// replaces it.
    pub fn file(&mut self, path: &str, file: F, size: u64) {
        self.insert(path, Entry::File { file, size });
    }

    /// A link to `target`, a path from the build's root.
    pub fn link(&mut self, path: &str, target: &str) {
        self.insert(path, Entry::Link(normalized(target)));
    }

    fn insert(&mut self, path: &str, entry: Entry<F>) {
        let path = normalized(path);
        self.entries.insert(path.to_lowercase(), (path, entry));
    }

    /// The file at `path`, through links, and its size.
    pub fn find(&self, path: &str) -> Option<(F, u64)> {
        let mut path = normalized(path);
        for _ in 0..=MAX_LINKS {
            match &self.entries.get(&path.to_lowercase())?.1 {
                Entry::File { file, size } => return Some((*file, *size)),
                Entry::Link(target) => path = target.clone(),
            }
        }
        None
    }

    fn is_folder(&self, path: &str) -> bool {
        let prefix = format!("{}/", normalized(path).to_lowercase());
        self.entries.keys().any(|key| key.starts_with(&prefix))
    }

    /// The first file under `folder` named like one of `names`, whatever
    /// their case, as a launch finds a library there: each folder's entries
    /// in name order, its files before its subfolders, the last subfolder
    /// first. Links and hidden entries are passed over.
    fn first_named(&self, folder: &str, names: &[&str]) -> Option<(F, u64)> {
        let folder = normalized(folder);
        let prefix = match folder.as_str() {
            "" => String::new(),
            folder => format!("{}/", folder.to_lowercase()),
        };
        // Each folder's entries, by its lowercased path: name, then the file
        // it is, or None for a subfolder.
        let mut folders: HashMap<String, BTreeMap<String, Option<(F, u64)>>> = HashMap::new();
        for (key, (path, entry)) in &self.entries {
            if !key.starts_with(&prefix) {
                continue;
            }
            let parts: Vec<&str> = path[prefix.len()..].split('/').collect();
            let mut parent = folder.to_lowercase();
            for (index, part) in parts.iter().enumerate() {
                let last = index + 1 == parts.len();
                let child = match last {
                    true => match entry {
                        Entry::File { file, size } => Some((*file, *size)),
                        Entry::Link(_) => break,
                    },
                    false => None,
                };
                folders
                    .entry(parent.clone())
                    .or_default()
                    .entry((*part).to_owned())
                    .or_insert(child);
                parent = match parent.as_str() {
                    "" => part.to_lowercase(),
                    parent => format!("{parent}/{}", part.to_lowercase()),
                };
            }
        }
        let mut pending = vec![folder.to_lowercase()];
        while let Some(current) = pending.pop() {
            for (name, child) in folders.get(&current).into_iter().flatten() {
                if name.starts_with('.') {
                    continue;
                }
                match child {
                    None => pending.push(match current.as_str() {
                        "" => name.to_lowercase(),
                        current => format!("{current}/{}", name.to_lowercase()),
                    }),
                    Some(file) if names.iter().any(|wanted| name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(wanted)) => {
                        return Some(*file);
                    }
                    Some(_) => {}
                }
            }
        }
        None
    }
}

/// Whether the game a Mac build starts from `executable`, a path from the
/// installation's root, runs natively on Apple silicon: its program holds an
/// arm64 slice, and so does the first library named like one of `libraries`
/// in the folder a launch searches, which must hold one. An application
/// bundle starts the executable its Info.plist names. `read` gives a file's
/// first bytes, never more than its size.
pub async fn runs_natively<F: Copy, E, Read>(
    listing: &Listing<F>,
    executable: &str,
    libraries: &[&str],
    read: impl Fn(F, u64) -> Read,
) -> Result<bool, E>
where
    Read: Future<Output = Result<Vec<u8>, E>>,
{
    let executable = normalized(executable);
    let bundle = executable.to_lowercase().ends_with(".app");
    let (program, searched) = if bundle {
        if !listing.is_folder(&executable) {
            return Ok(false);
        }
        let Some((plist, size)) = listing.find(&format!("{executable}/Contents/Info.plist")) else {
            return Ok(false);
        };
        if size > MAX_INFO_PLIST {
            return Ok(false);
        }
        let Some(name) = bundle_executable(&read(plist, size).await?) else {
            return Ok(false);
        };
        (
            format!("{executable}/Contents/MacOS/{name}"),
            executable.clone(),
        )
    } else {
        let parent = executable
            .rsplit_once('/')
            .map_or("", |(parent, _)| parent)
            .to_owned();
        (executable, parent)
    };
    let Some(program) = listing.find(&program) else {
        return Ok(false);
    };
    if !has_arm64(&read_head(program, &read).await?) {
        return Ok(false);
    }
    if libraries.is_empty() {
        return Ok(true);
    }
    match listing.first_named(&searched, libraries) {
        Some(library) => Ok(has_arm64(&read_head(library, &read).await?)),
        None => Ok(false),
    }
}

fn read_head<F, Read>((file, size): (F, u64), read: impl Fn(F, u64) -> Read) -> Read {
    read(file, size.min(PROGRAM_HEAD))
}

/// Whether a program starting with `head` holds an arm64 slice: a 64-bit
/// Mach-O for arm64, or a universal binary listing one.
pub fn has_arm64(head: &[u8]) -> bool {
    let word = |offset: usize, little: bool| -> Option<u32> {
        let bytes = head.get(offset..offset.checked_add(4)?)?.try_into().ok()?;
        Some(match little {
            true => u32::from_le_bytes(bytes),
            false => u32::from_be_bytes(bytes),
        })
    };
    match head {
        [0xcf, 0xfa, 0xed, 0xfe, ..] => word(4, true) == Some(CPU_TYPE_ARM64),
        [0xfe, 0xed, 0xfa, 0xcf, ..] => word(4, false) == Some(CPU_TYPE_ARM64),
        [0xca, 0xfe, 0xba, magic @ (0xbe | 0xbf), ..]
        | [magic @ (0xbe | 0xbf), 0xba, 0xfe, 0xca, ..] => {
            let little = head[0] != 0xca;
            let entry = if *magic == 0xbf { 32 } else { 20 };
            // A Java class file starts the same way, with its version where
            // the slice count would be.
            word(4, little).is_some_and(|count| {
                (1..=MAX_SLICES).contains(&count)
                    && (0..count as usize)
                        .any(|index| word(8 + index * entry, little) == Some(CPU_TYPE_ARM64))
            })
        }
        _ => false,
    }
}

/// The executable an application bundle's Info.plist names, in XML or binary
/// form; none when it names no single file of `Contents/MacOS`.
pub fn bundle_executable(info_plist: &[u8]) -> Option<String> {
    const KEY: &str = "CFBundleExecutable";
    let name = match info_plist.starts_with(b"bplist00") {
        true => binary_string(info_plist, KEY),
        false => xml_string(info_plist, KEY),
    }?;
    (!name.is_empty() && name.len() <= 255 && !name.contains('/') && name != "." && name != "..")
        .then_some(name)
}

/// The string `key` names in an XML property list's dictionary.
fn xml_string(plist: &[u8], key: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let text = std::str::from_utf8(plist).ok()?;
    let marker = format!("<key>{key}</key>");
    let after = &text[text.find(&marker)? + marker.len()..];
    let value = after.trim_start().strip_prefix("<string>")?;
    unescape(&value[..value.find("</string>")?])
}

/// XML text with its entities replaced.
fn unescape(text: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let mut output = String::with_capacity(text.len());
    let mut rest = text;
    while let Some(start) = rest.find('&') {
        output.push_str(&rest[..start]);
        let end = start + rest[start..].find(';')?;
        let entity = &rest[start + 1..end];
        let character = match entity {
            "amp" => '&',
            "lt" => '<',
            "gt" => '>',
            "quot" => '"',
            "apos" => '\'',
            _ => {
                let code = entity.strip_prefix('#')?;
                let code = match code.strip_prefix(['x', 'X']) {
                    Some(hex) => u32::from_str_radix(hex, 16).ok()?,
                    None => code.parse().ok()?,
                };
                char::from_u32(code)?
            }
        };
        output.push(character);
        rest = &rest[end + 1..];
    }
    output.push_str(rest);
    Some(output)
}

/// The string `key` names in a binary property list's top dictionary.
fn binary_string(plist: &[u8], key: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let trailer = plist.get(plist.len().checked_sub(32)?..)?;
    let (offset_size, reference_size) = (usize::from(trailer[6]), usize::from(trailer[7]));
    if !(1..=8).contains(&offset_size) || !(1..=8).contains(&reference_size) {
        return None;
    }
    let objects = number(&trailer[8..16])?;
    let top = number(&trailer[16..24])?;
    let table = usize::try_from(number(&trailer[24..32])?).ok()?;
    let object = |index: u64| -> Option<usize> {
        if index >= objects {
            return None;
        }
        let at = table.checked_add(usize::try_from(index).ok()?.checked_mul(offset_size)?)?;
        usize::try_from(number(plist.get(at..at.checked_add(offset_size)?)?)?).ok()
    };
    let start = object(top)?;
    if plist.get(start)? >> 4 != 0xd {
        return None;
    }
    let (entries, references) = length(plist, start)?;
    let reference = |index: usize| -> Option<u64> {
        let at = references.checked_add(index.checked_mul(reference_size)?)?;
        number(plist.get(at..at.checked_add(reference_size)?)?)
    };
    (0..entries).find_map(|index| {
        let name = string(plist, object(reference(index)?)?)?;
        (name == key)
            .then(|| string(plist, object(reference(entries.checked_add(index)?)?)?))
            .flatten()
    })
}

/// The length an object's marker at `start` gives, and where its content
/// starts.
fn length(plist: &[u8], start: usize) -> Option<(usize, usize)> {
    let info = plist.get(start)? & 0xf;
    if info != 0xf {
        return Some((usize::from(info), start + 1));
    }
    let marker = *plist.get(start + 1)?;
    if marker >> 4 != 0x1 || marker & 0xf > 3 {
        return None;
    }
    let size = 1usize << (marker & 0xf);
    let value = number(plist.get(start + 2..start + 2 + size)?)?;
    Some((usize::try_from(value).ok()?, start + 2 + size))
}

/// An ASCII or UTF-16 string object.
fn string(plist: &[u8], start: usize) -> Option<String> {
    let (count, content) = length(plist, start)?;
    match plist.get(start)? >> 4 {
        0x5 => {
            let bytes = plist.get(content..content.checked_add(count)?)?;
            bytes
                .is_ascii()
                .then(|| String::from_utf8_lossy(bytes).into_owned())
        }
        0x6 => {
            let bytes = plist.get(content..content.checked_add(count.checked_mul(2)?)?)?;
            let units: Vec<u16> = bytes
                .as_chunks::<2>()
                .0
                .iter()
                .map(|unit| u16::from_be_bytes(*unit))
                .collect();
            String::from_utf16(&units).ok()
        }
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// A big-endian unsigned number of at most eight bytes.
fn number(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<u64> {
    (bytes.len() <= 8).then(|| {
        bytes
            .iter()
            .fold(0, |value, byte| value << 8 | u64::from(*byte))
    })
}

/// A path with forward slashes, without empty or `.` parts, its `..` parts
/// applied; a `..` past the root is dropped.
fn normalized(path: &str) -> String {
    let mut parts: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();
    for part in path.split(['/', '\\']) {
        match part {
            "" | "." => {}
            ".." => {
                parts.pop();
            }
            part => parts.push(part),
        }
    }
    parts.join("/")
}
```

```rs
use super::*;
use std::{cell::RefCell, convert::Infallible};

const ARM64: u32 = 0x0100_000c;
const X86_64: u32 = 0x0100_0007;
const I386: u32 = 7;

fn thin(cpu: u32) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut bytes = vec![0xcf, 0xfa, 0xed, 0xfe];
    bytes.extend(cpu.to_le_bytes());
    bytes.resize(64, 0);
    bytes
}

fn thin_32(cpu: u32) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut bytes = vec![0xce, 0xfa, 0xed, 0xfe];
    bytes.extend(cpu.to_le_bytes());
    bytes.resize(64, 0);
    bytes
}

fn universal(cpus: &[u32]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut bytes = vec![0xca, 0xfe, 0xba, 0xbe];
    bytes.extend((cpus.len() as u32).to_be_bytes());
    for cpu in cpus {
        bytes.extend(cpu.to_be_bytes());
        bytes.extend([0; 16]);
    }
    bytes
}

/// The plist `plutil -convert binary1` writes for CFBundleName "Café",

fn xml_plist(executable: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
    format!(
        "<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"UTF-8\"?>\n<plist version=\"1.0\">\n<dict>\n\
         \t<key>CFBundleName</key>\n\t<string>Game</string>\n\
         \t<key>CFBundleExecutable</key>\n\t<string>{executable}</string>\n</dict>\n</plist>\n"
    )
    .into_bytes()
}

#[test]
fn an_arm64_slice_is_found_in_thin_and_universal_programs_only() {
    assert!(has_arm64(&thin(ARM64)));
    assert!(has_arm64(&universal(&[X86_64, ARM64])));
    assert!(!has_arm64(&thin(X86_64)));
    assert!(!has_arm64(&thin_32(I386)));
    assert!(!has_arm64(&thin_32(ARM64)));
    assert!(!has_arm64(&universal(&[I386, X86_64])));
    // A Java class file: 0xcafebabe, then its version.
    assert!(!has_arm64(&[
        0xca, 0xfe, 0xba, 0xbe, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x34
    ]));
    assert!(!has_arm64(b"#!/bin/sh\n"));
    assert!(!has_arm64(&[]));
    // A slice table cut short names no arm64 slice beyond its end.
    assert!(!has_arm64(&universal(&[X86_64, ARM64])[..30]));
}

#[test]
fn a_universal_binary_of_64_bit_entries_or_either_byte_order_is_read() {
    let mut wide = vec![0xca, 0xfe, 0xba, 0xbf, 0, 0, 0, 2];
    for cpu in [X86_64, ARM64] {
        wide.extend(cpu.to_be_bytes());
        wide.extend([0; 28]);
    }
    assert!(has_arm64(&wide));
    let mut swapped = vec![0xbe, 0xba, 0xfe, 0xca];
    swapped.extend(1u32.to_le_bytes());
    swapped.extend(ARM64.to_le_bytes());
    swapped.extend([0; 16]);
    assert!(has_arm64(&swapped));
}

#[test]
fn the_bundle_executable_is_read_from_xml_and_binary_plists() {
    assert_eq!(
        bundle_executable(&xml_plist("Tom &amp; Jerry&#x21;")).as_deref(),
        Some("Tom & Jerry!")
    );
    assert_eq!(bundle_executable(BINARY_PLIST).as_deref(), Some("My Game"));
    for unsafe_name in ["", "..", "MacOS/Game", "Bad&unknown;"] {
        assert_eq!(bundle_executable(&xml_plist(unsafe_name)), None);
    }
    assert_eq!(bundle_executable(b"<plist><dict></dict></plist>"), None);
    assert_eq!(bundle_executable(&BINARY_PLIST[..100]), None);
}

/// A build listing whose files read from memory, recording what was read.
struct Build {
    listing: Listing<usize>,
    files: Vec<(String, Vec<u8>)>,
    reads: RefCell<Vec<(String, u64)>>,
}

impl Build {
    fn new(files: &[(&str, Vec<u8>)]) -> Self {
        let mut listing = Listing::default();
        for (index, (path, bytes)) in files.iter().enumerate() {
            listing.file(path, index, bytes.len() as u64);
        }
        Self {
            listing,
            files: files
                .iter()
                .map(|(path, bytes)| ((*path).to_owned(), bytes.clone()))
                .collect(),
            reads: RefCell::default(),
        }
    }

    async fn native(&self, executable: &str, libraries: &[&str]) -> bool {
        let read = |file: usize, bytes: u64| {
            let (path, content) = &self.files[file];
            self.reads.borrow_mut().push((path.clone(), bytes));
            std::future::ready(Ok::<_, Infallible>(content[..bytes as usize].to_vec()))
        };
        runs_natively(&self.listing, executable, libraries, read)
            .await
            .unwrap()
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_bundle_runs_natively_when_its_program_and_steam_library_hold_arm64() {
    let mut program = universal(&[X86_64, ARM64]);
    program.resize(10_000, 0);
    let build = Build::new(&[
        ("Game.app/Contents/Info.plist", xml_plist("Game")),
        ("Game.app/Contents/MacOS/Game", program),
        (
            "Game.app/Contents/Frameworks/libsteam_api.dylib",
            universal(&[X86_64, ARM64]),
        ),
    ]);
    assert!(build.native("game.APP", &["libsteam_api.dylib"]).await);
    // Only a program's head is read.
    assert!(
        build
            .reads
            .borrow()
            .contains(&("Game.app/Contents/MacOS/Game".into(), PROGRAM_HEAD))
    );
    assert!(build.native("Game.app", &[]).await);
}

#[tokio::test]

    ]);

    assert!(build.native("Game.app", &[]).await);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn links_lead_to_their_targets_and_a_cycle_to_nothing() {
    let mut build = Build::new(&[
        ("Game.app/Contents/Info.plist", xml_plist("Game")),
        ("Game.app/Contents/MacOS/Game-arm64", thin(ARM64)),
        (
            "Game.app/Contents/Frameworks/Steam.framework/Versions/A/libsteam_api.dylib",
            thin(ARM64),
        ),
    ]);
    build.listing.link(
        "Game.app/Contents/MacOS/Game",
        "Game.app/Contents/MacOS/Game-arm64",
    );
    build.listing.link(
        "Game.app/Contents/Frameworks/Steam.framework/Versions/Current",
        "Game.app/Contents/Frameworks/Steam.framework/Versions/A",
    );
    assert!(build.native("Game.app", &["libsteam_api.dylib"]).await);
    // A cycle never resolves.
    build.listing.link(
        "Loop.app/Contents/Info.plist",
        "Loop.app/Contents/Info.plist",
    );
    build.listing.file("Loop.app/Contents/MacOS/Loop", 0, 1);
    assert!(!build.native("Loop.app", &[]).await);
}

#[tokio::test]

    // subfolder is searched first.
    let build = Build::new(&[
        ("Game/Game", thin(ARM64)),
        ("Game/a/libsteam_api.dylib", thin(ARM64)),
        ("Game/b/libsteam_api.dylib", thin(X86_64)),
        ("Game/.hidden/libsteam_api.dylib", thin(ARM64)),
        ("Other/libsteam_api.dylib", thin(ARM64)),

    let build = Build::new(&[
        ("Game/Game", thin(ARM64)),

        ("Game/b/libsteam_api.dylib", thin(X86_64)),
```

```rs
//! each storefront calls it.

/// Which of a game's builds: the Mac build, which runs natively, or the
/// Windows build, which runs in Wine. It reads every spelling an Obelisk
/// record ever held, and is written only as a storefront spells it.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Deserialize)]
pub enum Platform {
    #[serde(rename = "macos", alias = "Mac")]
    Mac,
    #[serde(rename = "windows", alias = "Windows")]
    Windows,
}

/// How one storefront spells the two builds in its requests, receipts,
/// folder names and ids. Each kit declares its own.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct Spelling {
    mac: &'static str,
    windows: &'static str,
}

impl Spelling {
    pub const fn new(mac: &'static str, windows: &'static str) -> Self {
        Self { mac, windows }
    }

    /// `platform`, as this storefront spells it.
    pub const fn name(self, platform: Platform) -> &'static str {
        match platform {
            Platform::Mac => self.mac,
            Platform::Windows => self.windows,
        }
    }

    /// Writes `platform` as this storefront spells it, for a record's
    /// `serialize_with` helper.
    pub fn serialize<S: Serializer>(
        self,
        platform: Platform,
        serializer: S,
    ) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
        serializer.serialize_str(self.name(platform))
    }
}
```

`crates/obelisk-core/src/transfer.rs`:

```rs
//! Cancellation and progress vocabulary shared by storefront download engines.
mod body;
mod engine;
mod lifecycle;
mod window;
pub use body::{BodyError, BodySize, read_body};
pub use engine::{Chunks, Delivery, Interrupted, Pipeline, run_engine};
pub use lifecycle::{TransferBusy, TransferContext, TransferStatus, Transfers};
pub use window::Window;

use std::{
    future::Future,
    sync::{
        Arc, Mutex, PoisonError,
        atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicUsize, Ordering},
    },
};

use tokio::sync::Notify;

/// Cancels a download from any thread. Synchronous checks stay a cheap atomic
/// load; pending CDN requests are woken immediately instead of polling.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct CancelToken(Arc<CancelState>);

#[derive(Debug, Default)]
struct CancelState {
    cancelled: AtomicBool,
    notify: Notify,
    workers: AtomicUsize,
    workers_finished: Notify,
}

/// Returned by [`CancelToken::check`]; storefront errors convert it into their
/// own cancellation variant so `cancel.check()?` reads the same everywhere.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Cancelled;

impl CancelToken {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    pub fn cancel(&self) {
        self.0.cancelled.store(true, Ordering::Release);
        self.0.notify.notify_waiters();
    }

    pub fn is_cancelled(&self) -> bool {
        self.0.cancelled.load(Ordering::Acquire)
    }

    pub fn check(&self) -> Result<(), Cancelled> {
        if self.is_cancelled() {
            Err(Cancelled)
        } else {
            Ok(())
        }
    }

    /// Completes once cancelled, including when cancellation happened earlier.
    pub async fn cancelled(&self) {
        let notified = self.0.notify.notified();
        tokio::pin!(notified);
        // Register before re-reading the flag so a cancel between the two is not lost.
        notified.as_mut().enable();
        if self.is_cancelled() {
            return;
        }
        notified.await;
    }

    /// Runs `work` unless this token is cancelled first, including earlier.
    /// A cancellation drops `work` at once, so a CDN request or a retry pause
    /// stalled on the network ends without waiting for its timeout. When both
    /// are ready, the cancellation wins.
    pub async fn race<T>(&self, work: impl Future<Output = T>) -> Result<T, Cancelled> {
        tokio::select! {
            biased;
            () = self.cancelled() => Err(Cancelled),
            value = work => Ok(value),
        }
    }

    /// Registers work before it reaches the blocking pool. A dropped async
    /// caller cannot release its transfer slot while this work still runs.
    /// The worker must check this token at its normal cancellation points.
    pub fn spawn_blocking<F, R>(&self, work: F) -> tokio::task::JoinHandle<R>
    where
        F: FnOnce() -> R + Send + 'static,
        R: Send + 'static,
    {
        self.0.workers.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
        let worker = BlockingWorker(Arc::clone(&self.0));
        tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
            let _worker = worker;
            work()
        })
    }

    /// Cancels the token when the guard drops before it is disarmed. Dropping
    /// an async task does not stop its `spawn_blocking` work: the guard wakes
    /// its network wait and lets its next disk check stop before a new
    /// attempt can acquire the lock.
    pub fn cancel_on_drop(&self) -> CancelOnDrop {
        CancelOnDrop(Some(self.clone()))
    }

    fn workers_finished(&self) -> bool {
        self.0.workers.load(Ordering::Acquire) == 0
    }

    async fn wait_for_workers(&self) {
        loop {
            let notified = self.0.workers_finished.notified();
            tokio::pin!(notified);
            notified.as_mut().enable();
            if self.workers_finished() {
                return;
            }
            notified.await;
        }
    }
}

struct BlockingWorker(Arc<CancelState>);

impl Drop for BlockingWorker {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if self.0.workers.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::AcqRel) == 1 {
            self.0.workers_finished.notify_waiters();
        }
    }
}

/// Returned by [`CancelToken::cancel_on_drop`].
pub struct CancelOnDrop(Option<CancelToken>);

impl CancelOnDrop {
    /// The work finished: dropping the guard cancels nothing.
    pub fn disarm(mut self) {
        self.0 = None;
    }
}

impl Drop for CancelOnDrop {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if let Some(cancel) = &self.0 {
            cancel.cancel();
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum DownloadPhase {
    #[default]
    Preparing,
    Verifying,
    Downloading,
}

/// Cumulative counters for one engine invocation, published on every change.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct DownloadProgress {
    pub phase: DownloadPhase,
    /// Verified, installed or reusable uncompressed bytes.
    pub completed_bytes: u64,
    /// Inspection progress during the initial file scan, including bytes whose
    /// hash is still pending. Separate from reusable bytes; absent during repair.
    pub verification_bytes: Option<u64>,
    pub total_bytes: u64,
    /// Compressed bytes received during this invocation, including manifests.
    pub network_bytes: u64,
    /// Compressed chunk bytes received, excluding manifests and disk reads.
    pub content_bytes: u64,
    pub completed_files: u32,
    pub total_files: u32,
    pub current_file: String,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct DownloadSummary {
    pub downloaded_bytes: u64,
    pub content_bytes: u64,
    pub reused_bytes: u64,
    pub completed_files: u32,
    pub total_bytes: u64,
}

/// Lifecycle of one account-scoped transfer as presented to the host.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum TransferState {
    Preparing,
    Verifying,
    Downloading,
    /// The installation moves into the games folder.
    Moving,
    Complete,
    Cancelled,
    Failed,
}

impl From<DownloadPhase> for TransferState {
    fn from(phase: DownloadPhase) -> Self {
        match phase {
            DownloadPhase::Preparing => Self::Preparing,
            DownloadPhase::Verifying => Self::Verifying,
            DownloadPhase::Downloading => Self::Downloading,
        }
    }
}

/// Serializes progress so every snapshot handed to the caller is consistent and
/// monotonic, whether the change came from the network pump or the disk thread.
/// The callback runs inline under the lock, so a caller that cancels from within
/// it is observed before the next chunk is written.
pub struct Reporter {
    status: Mutex<DownloadProgress>,
    callback: Box<dyn Fn(DownloadProgress) + Send + Sync>,
}

impl Reporter {
    /// Publishes `initial` once so observers see the starting state immediately.
    pub fn new(
        initial: DownloadProgress,
        callback: impl Fn(DownloadProgress) + Send + Sync + 'static,
    ) -> Arc<Self> {
        let reporter = Arc::new(Self {
            status: Mutex::new(initial),
            callback: Box::new(callback),
        });
        reporter.update(|_| {});
        reporter
    }

    pub fn update(&self, change: impl FnOnce(&mut DownloadProgress)) {
        let mut status = self.status.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner);
        change(&mut status);
        (self.callback)(status.clone());
    }

    pub fn snapshot(&self) -> DownloadProgress {
        self.status
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
            .clone()
    }

    pub fn summary(&self, reused_bytes: u64) -> DownloadSummary {
        let status = self.snapshot();
        DownloadSummary {
            downloaded_bytes: status.network_bytes,
            content_bytes: status.content_bytes,
            reused_bytes,
            completed_files: status.completed_files,
            total_bytes: status.total_bytes,
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn check_reports_the_flag_and_cancellation_is_shared_by_every_clone() {
        let cancel = CancelToken::new();
        let clone = cancel.clone();
        assert!(cancel.check().is_ok());
        assert!(!clone.is_cancelled());
        clone.cancel();
        assert!(cancel.is_cancelled());
        assert!(matches!(cancel.check(), Err(Cancelled)));
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn waiting_on_a_token_cancelled_earlier_returns_instead_of_hanging() {
        let cancel = CancelToken::new();
        cancel.cancel();
        // `cancelled` registers before re-reading the flag, so a cancellation
        // that already happened cannot be missed by a later waiter.
        cancel.cancelled().await;
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_pending_waiter_wakes_on_a_cancellation_from_another_task() {
        let cancel = CancelToken::new();
        let waiter = cancel.clone();
        let woken = tokio::spawn(async move { waiter.cancelled().await });
        tokio::task::yield_now().await;
        cancel.cancel();
        woken.await.unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_reporter_publishes_its_initial_snapshot_once_before_new_returns() {
        let seen = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
        let sink = Arc::clone(&seen);
        let reporter = Reporter::new(
            DownloadProgress {
                total_files: 3,
                ..DownloadProgress::default()
            },
            move |snapshot| sink.lock().unwrap().push(snapshot.total_files),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            *seen.lock().unwrap(),
            [3],
            "observers see the starting state"
        );
        reporter.update(|status| status.completed_files = 1);
        assert_eq!(*seen.lock().unwrap(), [3, 3]);
        assert_eq!(reporter.snapshot().completed_files, 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_cancellation_from_inside_the_callback_is_visible_when_update_returns() {
        // The callback runs inline under the lock, so an engine that cancels
        // from within it is observed before the next chunk is written.
        let cancel = CancelToken::new();
        let inner = cancel.clone();
        let reporter = Reporter::new(DownloadProgress::default(), move |status| {
            if status.completed_bytes > 0 {
                inner.cancel();
            }
        });
        assert!(!cancel.is_cancelled());
        reporter.update(|status| status.completed_bytes = 1);
        assert!(cancel.is_cancelled());
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_summary_reports_network_bytes_as_downloaded_and_keeps_reused_separate() {
        let reporter = Reporter::new(DownloadProgress::default(), |_| {});
        reporter.update(|status| {
            status.network_bytes = 900;
            status.content_bytes = 800;
            status.completed_files = 4;
            status.total_bytes = 5_000;
        });
        let summary = reporter.summary(1_200);
        assert_eq!(summary.downloaded_bytes, 900);
        assert_eq!(summary.content_bytes, 800);
        assert_eq!(summary.reused_bytes, 1_200);
        assert_eq!(summary.completed_files, 4);
        assert_eq!(summary.total_bytes, 5_000);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn race_returns_cancelled_for_a_token_cancelled_earlier_or_while_work_is_pending() {
        let cancel = CancelToken::new();
        let pending = cancel.race(std::future::pending::<()>());
        let cancelling = async {
            tokio::task::yield_now().await;
            cancel.cancel();
        };
        let (raced, ()) = tokio::join!(pending, cancelling);
        assert_eq!(raced, Err(Cancelled));
        // Cancelled earlier, the cancellation wins even over finished work.
        assert_eq!(cancel.race(async { 1 }).await, Err(Cancelled));
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn race_returns_the_work_when_it_finishes_first() {
        let cancel = CancelToken::new();
        assert_eq!(cancel.race(async { 7 }).await, Ok(7));
        assert!(!cancel.is_cancelled());
    }
```

`crates/obelisk-core/src/transfer/body.rs`:

```rs
//! Bounded reading of a streamed response body, shared by every storefront's
//! chunk fetch so the bound, the byte counting and the cancellation stay in
//! one order.
use futures_util::{Stream, StreamExt};

use super::{CancelToken, Cancelled};

/// How long a response body may or must be.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum BodySize {
    /// Anything up to this many bytes.
    AtMost(u64),
    /// Exactly this many bytes, such as a chunk whose compressed size the
    /// manifest names.
    Exactly(u64),
}

/// Why a body was not read. Each storefront turns it into its own vocabulary.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum BodyError {
    /// The connection failed while the body streamed.
    Network,
    /// The advertised or streamed length broke the bound, or an exact body
    /// ended short.
    Size,
    Cancelled,
}

impl From<Cancelled> for BodyError {
    fn from(_: Cancelled) -> Self {
        Self::Cancelled
    }
}

/// Reads a streamed response body within `size`. An advertised length outside
/// it is refused before anything is read; the buffer is reserved only after
/// that check, for the advertised length or the exact size. Each part is
/// passed to `received` before it is checked, so network counters include a
/// refused body's bytes, and a cancellation from inside that callback is seen
/// before the part is kept. Returns `Cancelled` as soon as `cancel` fires,
/// even while a part is pending. `parts` is any byte stream, such as
/// `reqwest::Response::bytes_stream()`; transport errors are opaque.
pub async fn read_body<B: AsRef<[u8]>, X>(
    advertised: Option<u64>,
    parts: impl Stream<Item = Result<B, X>>,
    size: BodySize,
    cancel: &CancelToken,
    mut received: impl FnMut(u64),
) -> Result<Vec<u8>, BodyError> {
    let (bound, reserved) = match size {
        BodySize::AtMost(limit) if advertised.is_some_and(|length| length > limit) => {
            return Err(BodyError::Size);
        }
        BodySize::AtMost(limit) => (limit, advertised.unwrap_or(0)),
        BodySize::Exactly(length) if advertised.is_some_and(|other| other != length) => {
            return Err(BodyError::Size);
        }
        BodySize::Exactly(length) => (length, length),
    };
    let mut body = Vec::with_capacity(usize::try_from(reserved).map_err(|_| BodyError::Size)?);
    let read = async {
        tokio::pin!(parts);
        while let Some(part) = parts.next().await {
            let part = part.map_err(|_| BodyError::Network)?;
            let part = part.as_ref();
            let length = part.len() as u64;
            received(length);
            cancel.check()?;
            // The body never exceeds the bound, so the subtraction cannot wrap.
            if length > bound - body.len() as u64 {
                return Err(BodyError::Size);
            }
            body.extend_from_slice(part);
        }
        Ok(())
    };
    cancel.race(read).await??;
    if let BodySize::Exactly(length) = size
        && body.len() as u64 != length
    {
        return Err(BodyError::Size);
    }
    Ok(body)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use futures_util::stream;

    type Part = Result<&'static [u8], ()>;

    async fn read(
        advertised: Option<u64>,
        parts: Vec<Part>,
        size: BodySize,
    ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, BodyError> {
        read_body(
            advertised,
            stream::iter(parts),
            size,
            &CancelToken::new(),
            |_| {},
        )
        .await
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn at_most_refuses_an_advertised_excess_without_reading() {
        let mut counted = 0;
        let body = read_body(
            Some(5),
            stream::iter([Ok::<_, ()>(b"abcde".as_slice())]),
            BodySize::AtMost(4),
            &CancelToken::new(),
            |length| counted += length,
        )
        .await;
        assert_eq!(body, Err(BodyError::Size));
        assert_eq!(counted, 0, "nothing is read past a refused length");
        assert_eq!(
            read(Some(4), vec![Ok(b"ab"), Ok(b"cd")], BodySize::AtMost(4)).await,
            Ok(b"abcd".to_vec())
        );
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn at_most_refuses_a_streamed_excess() {
        assert_eq!(
            read(None, vec![Ok(b"abc"), Ok(b"de")], BodySize::AtMost(4)).await,
            Err(BodyError::Size)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            read(Some(2), vec![Ok(b"abc")], BodySize::AtMost(4)).await,
            Ok(b"abc".to_vec()),
            "an advertised length is a hint inside the bound"
        );
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn exactly_refuses_a_wrong_advertised_length() {
        assert_eq!(
            read(Some(3), vec![Ok(b"abcd")], BodySize::Exactly(4)).await,
            Err(BodyError::Size)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            read(Some(4), vec![Ok(b"abcd")], BodySize::Exactly(4)).await,
            Ok(b"abcd".to_vec())
        );
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn exactly_refuses_a_long_and_a_short_body() {
        assert_eq!(
            read(None, vec![Ok(b"abc"), Ok(b"de")], BodySize::Exactly(4)).await,
            Err(BodyError::Size)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            read(None, vec![Ok(b"abc")], BodySize::Exactly(4)).await,
            Err(BodyError::Size)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            read(None, vec![Ok(b"ab"), Ok(b"cd")], BodySize::Exactly(4)).await,
            Ok(b"abcd".to_vec())
        );
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn every_part_is_counted_before_the_bound_is_checked() {
        let mut counted = Vec::new();
        let body = read_body(
            None,
            stream::iter([Ok::<_, ()>(b"abc".as_slice()), Ok(b"def"), Ok(b"g")]),
            BodySize::AtMost(4),
            &CancelToken::new(),
            |length| counted.push(length),
        )
        .await;
        assert_eq!(body, Err(BodyError::Size));
        assert_eq!(
            counted,
            [3, 3],
            "the refused part reached the network counters"
        );
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_cancellation_from_the_received_callback_stops_before_the_part_is_kept() {
        let cancel = CancelToken::new();
        let mut counted = Vec::new();
        let body = read_body(
            None,
            stream::iter([Ok::<_, ()>(b"abc".as_slice()), Ok(b"def")]),
            BodySize::AtMost(16),
            &cancel,
            |length| {
                counted.push(length);
                cancel.cancel();
            },
        )
        .await;
        assert_eq!(body, Err(BodyError::Cancelled));
        assert_eq!(counted, [3], "no part is read after the cancellation");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn cancellation_returns_while_a_part_is_pending() {
        let cancel = CancelToken::new();
        let reading = read_body(
            Some(4),
            stream::pending::<Part>(),
            BodySize::AtMost(4),
            &cancel,
            |_| {},
        );
        let cancelling = async {
            tokio::task::yield_now().await;
            cancel.cancel();
        };
        let (body, ()) = tokio::join!(reading, cancelling);
        assert_eq!(body, Err(BodyError::Cancelled));
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_transport_error_is_network() {
        assert_eq!(
            read(None, vec![Ok(b"ab"), Err(())], BodySize::AtMost(4)).await,
            Err(BodyError::Network)
        );
    }
}
```
