`crates/obelisk-core/src/transfer/engine.rs`:

```rs
//! The chunk engine every storefront runs between the network and the disk.
//! It owns the queues between the two sides, the blocking worker's
//! registration and the cancellation that ties them together. A storefront
//! keeps its own assembly, resume strategy and mirror policy.
use std::future::Future;

use futures_util::{Stream, StreamExt, stream};
use tokio::sync::mpsc;

use super::{CancelToken, Cancelled};

/// The order fetched chunks reach [`Chunks::receive`].
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Delivery {
    /// Request order, for a disk side that writes and hashes sequentially.
    InOrder,
    /// As each chunk arrives, for a disk side that places chunks itself: a
    /// slow chunk then holds up nothing fetched after it.
    AsFetched,
}

/// How hard one engine pulls on the network.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct Pipeline {
    pub delivery: Delivery,
    /// Chunk fetches in flight at once. At least one.
    pub fetches: usize,
    /// Fetched chunks waiting for the disk side. Bounds decoded memory. At
    /// least one.
    pub queue: usize,
}

/// The disk worker ended without an outcome: it panicked, or the runtime shut
/// down under it. Each storefront turns it into its own vocabulary.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Interrupted;

/// The disk side's end of a running engine. Only [`run_engine`] makes one; it
/// lives on the blocking pool with the disk closure. Dropping it stops the
/// network side.
pub struct Chunks<C, T, E> {
    requests: mpsc::UnboundedSender<C>,
    results: mpsc::Receiver<Result<T, E>>,
    refused: bool,
}

impl<C, T, E> Chunks<C, T, E> {
    /// This end, with the network side's: the requests it takes up and the
    /// queue it delivers outcomes to.
    fn open(queue: usize) -> (Self, mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<C>, mpsc::Sender<Result<T, E>>) {
        let (requests, taken) = mpsc::unbounded_channel();
        let (deliveries, results) = mpsc::channel(queue);
        let chunks = Self {
            requests,
            results,
            refused: false,
        };
        (chunks, taken, deliveries)
    }

    /// A disk side's end with no engine behind it, for a test that plays the
    /// network side: it takes requests and queues outcomes itself, and closes
    /// its request receiver where the engine would stop.
    #[cfg(any(test, feature = "testing"))]
    pub fn detached(
        queue: usize,
    ) -> (Self, mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<C>, mpsc::Sender<Result<T, E>>) {
        Self::open(queue)
    }
}

impl<C, T, E: From<Cancelled>> Chunks<C, T, E> {
    /// Queues `chunk` for the network side. Requests are unbounded: the disk
    /// side bounds how far it plans ahead.
    ///
    /// `false` once the network side has stopped, after a chunk failed for
    /// good or the Transfer was cancelled. The request is then dropped and
    /// there is nothing to handle: the outcome that stopped the network side
    /// is already queued ahead of anything requested after it, so `receive`
    /// returns it no later than in this request's place. Every later request
    /// is refused too, without reaching the network side; see [`Self::refused`].
    pub fn request(&mut self, chunk: C) -> bool {
        self.refused = self.refused || self.requests.send(chunk).is_err();
        !self.refused
    }

    /// Whether a request was refused. A disk side stops planning more work
    /// then: the plan holding the refused request already reaches the outcome
    /// that stopped the network side. Seen only through a refusal, never
    /// earlier, so that a disk side never stops with nothing planned that
    /// would receive the outcome.
    pub fn refused(&self) -> bool {
        self.refused
    }

    /// Blocks for the next fetched chunk in the pipeline's delivery order. In
    /// its place comes the error that stopped the network side, or `Cancelled`.
    /// Also `Cancelled` when the engine's future was dropped, which cancels
    /// its token. Waits only for what this side requested: with nothing
    /// requested it blocks until the Transfer is cancelled. Call it from the
    /// disk closure only, never from async code.
    pub fn receive(&mut self) -> Result<T, E> {
        // The pump closes this queue only after the outcome that stopped it,
        // so a closed queue means the engine's future was dropped. The token
        // may not be cancelled yet at that point, so it is not consulted.
        self.results
            .blocking_recv()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| Err(Cancelled.into()))
    }
}

/// Runs one content engine and returns the disk side's outcome once both
/// sides have ended.
///
/// `disk` runs on the blocking pool, registered with `cancel`, so the Transfer
/// keeps its admission until the worker really stops. It must check `cancel`
/// at its usual points.
///
/// `fetch` runs on this task with at most `pipeline.fetches` chunks in flight.
/// It is called once per request, synchronously and in request order, when the
/// request is taken up and before its future is first polled. Work done in the
/// closure before it returns the future, such as numbering a mirror ticket,
/// keeps request order. It may borrow anything that outlives this call.
/// A fetch error ends the network side once it is delivered. So does a
/// cancellation, which is delivered as `Cancelled` so that a disk side blocked
/// in `receive` wakes, and it wins over a chunk that is ready. When `disk`
/// returns early, fetches still in flight are dropped, and no request it left
/// queued starts once the network side sees it gone.
///
/// Dropping the returned future cancels `cancel`: the disk worker keeps
/// running and stops at its next check. A disk worker that panics returns
/// `Interrupted`.
pub async fn run_engine<C, T, R, E, F>(
    pipeline: Pipeline,
    cancel: &CancelToken,
    disk: impl FnOnce(Chunks<C, T, E>) -> Result<R, E> + Send + 'static,
    fetch: impl Fn(C) -> F,
) -> Result<R, E>
where
    C: Send + 'static,
    T: Send + 'static,
    R: Send + 'static,
    E: From<Cancelled> + From<Interrupted> + Send + 'static,
    F: Future<Output = Result<T, E>>,
{
    // A zero window never pulls a request, leaving the disk side blocked for good.
    assert!(pipeline.fetches > 0 && pipeline.queue > 0);
    let (chunks, taken, deliveries) = Chunks::open(pipeline.queue);
    let guard = cancel.cancel_on_drop();
    let (outcome, ()) = tokio::join!(
        cancel.spawn_blocking(move || disk(chunks)),
        pump(taken, deliveries, pipeline, cancel, fetch),
    );
    guard.disarm();
    outcome.map_err(|_| E::from(Interrupted))?
}

/// Fetches requested chunks within the pipeline's window and delivers them in
/// its order. Stops as soon as the disk side goes away, a chunk fails for good,
/// or cancellation is requested.
async fn pump<C, T, E, F>(
    queue: mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<C>,
    deliveries: mpsc::Sender<Result<T, E>>,
    pipeline: Pipeline,
    cancel: &CancelToken,
    fetch: impl Fn(C) -> F,
) where
    F: Future<Output = Result<T, E>>,
    E: From<Cancelled>,
{
    let requested = queued(queue).map(fetch);
    let fetched = match pipeline.delivery {
        Delivery::InOrder => requested.buffered(pipeline.fetches).left_stream(),
        Delivery::AsFetched => requested.buffer_unordered(pipeline.fetches).right_stream(),
    };
    deliver(fetched, deliveries, cancel).await;
}

fn queued<C>(requests: mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<C>) -> impl Stream<Item = C> {
    stream::unfold(requests, |mut requests| async move {
        requests.recv().await.map(|chunk| (chunk, requests))
    })
}

async fn deliver<T, E: From<Cancelled>>(
    fetched: impl Stream<Item = Result<T, E>>,
    deliveries: mpsc::Sender<Result<T, E>>,
    cancel: &CancelToken,
) {
    tokio::pin!(fetched);
    loop {
        // Polling the stream refills the fetch window, so a gone disk side or
        // a cancellation must be seen first, or one more fetch would start.
        let next = tokio::select! {
            biased;
            () = deliveries.closed() => return,
            () = cancel.cancelled() => {
                let _ = deliveries.send(Err(Cancelled.into())).await;
                return;
            }
            result = fetched.next() => result,
        };
        let Some(result) = next else { return };
        let failed = result.is_err();
        if deliveries.send(result).await.is_err() || failed {
            return;
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::{
        sync::{
            Arc, Mutex,
            atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering},
            mpsc as std_mpsc,
        },
        time::{Duration, Instant},
    };
    use tokio::sync::Notify;

    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
    enum Failure {
        Cancelled,
        Interrupted,
        Chunk(usize),
    }

    impl From<Cancelled> for Failure {
        fn from(_: Cancelled) -> Self {
            Self::Cancelled
        }
    }

    impl From<Interrupted> for Failure {
        fn from(_: Interrupted) -> Self {
            Self::Interrupted
        }
    }

    type TestChunks = Chunks<usize, usize, Failure>;

    const WAIT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2);

    fn pipeline(delivery: Delivery, fetches: usize, queue: usize) -> Pipeline {
        Pipeline {
            delivery,
            fetches,
            queue,
        }
    }

    /// One gate per request, so a test decides exactly when each fetch finishes.
    fn gates(count: usize) -> Arc<Vec<Notify>> {
        Arc::new((0..count).map(|_| Notify::new()).collect())
    }

    /// Polls `done` from the disk side until it holds or the deadline passes.
    fn wait_until(done: impl Fn() -> bool) -> bool {
        let deadline = Instant::now() + WAIT;
        while !done() {
            if Instant::now() > deadline {
                return false;
            }
            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1));
        }
        true
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn chunks_reach_an_in_order_disk_side_in_request_order_however_they_finish() {
        let open = gates(3);
        let fetch_gates = Arc::clone(&open);
        let (finished, finishes) = std_mpsc::channel();
        let cancel = CancelToken::new();
        let disk = move |mut chunks: TestChunks| {
            for index in 0..3 {
                assert!(chunks.request(index));
            }
            // Finish backwards, each fetch only after the later one is done.
            for index in [2_usize, 1, 0] {
                open[index].notify_one();
                assert_eq!(finishes.recv_timeout(WAIT), Ok(index));
            }
            (0..3)
                .map(|_| chunks.receive())
                .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()
        };
        let order = run_engine(
            pipeline(Delivery::InOrder, 3, 3),
            &cancel,
            disk,
            |index: usize| {
                let (gates, finished) = (Arc::clone(&fetch_gates), finished.clone());
                async move {
                    gates[index].notified().await;
                    finished.send(index).unwrap();
                    Ok(index)
                }
            },
        )
        .await;
        assert_eq!(
            order,
            Ok(vec![0, 1, 2]),
            "the disk side writes in manifest order"
        );
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_slow_chunk_holds_up_nothing_after_it_when_delivered_as_fetched() {
        let slow = Arc::new(Notify::new());
        let release = Arc::clone(&slow);
        let cancel = CancelToken::new();
        let disk = move |mut chunks: TestChunks| {
            for index in 0..3 {
                assert!(chunks.request(index));
            }
            let mut early = [chunks.receive()?, chunks.receive()?];
            early.sort_unstable();
            // Chunk 0 finishes only once both chunks after it arrived.
            release.notify_one();
            Ok((early, chunks.receive()?))
        };
        let received = run_engine(
            pipeline(Delivery::AsFetched, 3, 3),
            &cancel,
            disk,
            |index: usize| {
                let slow = Arc::clone(&slow);
                async move {
                    if index == 0 {
                        slow.notified().await;
                    }
                    Ok(index)
                }
            },
        )
        .await;
        assert_eq!(received, Ok(([1, 2], 0)));
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn no_more_than_pipeline_fetches_are_in_flight() {
        const REQUESTS: usize = 6;
        let open = gates(REQUESTS);
        let fetch_gates = Arc::clone(&open);
        let started = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
        let active = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
        let peak = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
        let observed = Arc::clone(&started);
        let cancel = CancelToken::new();
        let disk = move |mut chunks: TestChunks| {
            for index in 0..REQUESTS {
                assert!(chunks.request(index));
            }
            let mut received = Vec::new();
            for index in 0..REQUESTS {
                // Hold each chunk until the next one is in flight too, so the
                // window is full whenever it can be.
                let in_flight = (index + 2).min(REQUESTS);
                assert!(wait_until(|| observed.load(Ordering::Acquire) >= in_flight));
                open[index].notify_one();
                received.push(chunks.receive()?);
            }
            Ok(received)
        };
        let counters = (Arc::clone(&started), Arc::clone(&active), Arc::clone(&peak));
        // A queue smaller than the window still completes.
        let received = run_engine(
            pipeline(Delivery::InOrder, 2, 1),
            &cancel,
            disk,
            |index: usize| {
                let gates = Arc::clone(&fetch_gates);
                let (started, active, peak) = (
                    Arc::clone(&counters.0),
                    Arc::clone(&counters.1),
                    Arc::clone(&counters.2),
                );
                async move {
                    let running = active.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel) + 1;
                    peak.fetch_max(running, Ordering::AcqRel);
                    started.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
                    gates[index].notified().await;
                    active.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
                    Ok(index)
                }
            },
        )
        .await;
        assert_eq!(received, Ok((0..REQUESTS).collect()));
        assert_eq!(peak.load(Ordering::Acquire), 2, "CDN requests stay bounded");
        assert_eq!(active.load(Ordering::Acquire), 0);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn fetch_is_called_in_request_order_before_its_future_runs() {
        const REQUESTS: usize = 6;
        let calls = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
        let cancel = CancelToken::new();
        let disk = |mut chunks: TestChunks| {
            for index in 0..REQUESTS {
                assert!(chunks.request(index));
            }
            let mut received = (0..REQUESTS)
                .map(|_| chunks.receive())
                .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
            received.sort_unstable();
            Ok(received)
        };
        let received = run_engine(
            pipeline(Delivery::AsFetched, 3, 3),
            &cancel,
            disk,
            |index: usize| {
                calls.lock().unwrap().push(index);
                let calls = Arc::clone(&calls);
                async move {
                    assert!(
                        calls.lock().unwrap().contains(&index),
                        "the closure ran before its future"
                    );
                    // Later requests finish sooner.
                    for _ in index..REQUESTS {
                        tokio::task::yield_now().await;
                    }
                    Ok(index)
                }
            },
        )
        .await;
        assert_eq!(received, Ok((0..REQUESTS).collect()));
        assert_eq!(
            *calls.lock().unwrap(),
            (0..REQUESTS).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            "mirror tickets are numbered in request order"
        );
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_cancellation_wakes_a_disk_side_blocked_in_receive() {
        let fetching = Notify::new();
        let cancel = CancelToken::new();
        let disk = |mut chunks: TestChunks| {
            assert!(chunks.request(0));
            chunks.receive()
        };
        // This fetch never finishes on its own: only the cancellation ends it.
        let engine = run_engine(
            pipeline(Delivery::InOrder, 1, 1),
            &cancel,
            disk,
            |_: usize| {
                fetching.notify_one();
                std::future::pending()
            },
        );
        let cancelling = async {
            fetching.notified().await;
            cancel.cancel();
        };
        let (outcome, ()) = tokio::join!(engine, cancelling);
        assert_eq!(outcome, Err(Failure::Cancelled));
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_failed_chunk_is_received_in_its_place_and_stops_fetching() {
        let started = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
        let cancel = CancelToken::new();
        let disk = |mut chunks: TestChunks| {
            for index in 0..4 {
                assert!(chunks.request(index));
            }
            Ok([chunks.receive(), chunks.receive()])
        };
        let received = run_engine(
            pipeline(Delivery::InOrder, 1, 4),
            &cancel,
            disk,
            |index: usize| {
                let started = Arc::clone(&started);
                async move {
                    started.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
                    if index == 1 {
                        return Err(Failure::Chunk(1));
                    }
                    Ok(index)
                }
            },
        )
        .await;
        assert_eq!(received, Ok([Ok(0), Err(Failure::Chunk(1))]));
        assert_eq!(
            started.load(Ordering::Acquire),
            2,
            "a chunk that fails for good stops the queue"
        );
    }

    async fn request_after_the_network_side_stopped(delivery: Delivery) {
        let cancel = CancelToken::new();
        let disk = move |mut chunks: TestChunks| {
            let first = if delivery == Delivery::InOrder {
                assert!(chunks.request(0));
                assert!(chunks.request(1));
                Some(chunks.receive())
            } else {
                assert!(chunks.request(1));
                None
            };
            let stopped = wait_until(|| chunks.requests.is_closed());
            let unrefused = !chunks.refused();
            // No retry: the first refused request is the one that matters.
            let accepted = chunks.request(10);
            Ok((
                first,
                stopped && unrefused,
                accepted,
                chunks.refused(),
                chunks.receive(),
            ))
        };
        let outcome = run_engine(
            pipeline(delivery, 2, 2),
            &cancel,
            disk,
            |index: usize| async move {
                match index {
                    0 => Ok(0),
                    1 => Err(Failure::Chunk(1)),
                    _ => std::future::pending().await,
                }
            },
        )
        .await;
        let expected_first = (delivery == Delivery::InOrder).then_some(Ok(0));
        assert_eq!(
            outcome,
            Ok((expected_first, true, false, true, Err(Failure::Chunk(1)))),
            "{delivery:?}: the request is dropped and the queued error still arrives"
        );
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_request_after_the_network_side_stopped_is_dropped_and_the_original_error_still_arrives()
     {
        request_after_the_network_side_stopped(Delivery::InOrder).await;
        request_after_the_network_side_stopped(Delivery::AsFetched).await;
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_disk_side_that_returns_early_stops_the_network_side() {
        let started = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
        let cancel = CancelToken::new();
        let disk = |mut chunks: TestChunks| {
            for index in 0..8 {
                assert!(chunks.request(index));
            }
            chunks.receive()?;
            Ok(7)
        };
        let outcome = run_engine(
            pipeline(Delivery::InOrder, 2, 1),
            &cancel,
            disk,
            |index: usize| {
                let started = Arc::clone(&started);
                async move {
                    started.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
                    Ok(index)
                }
            },
        )
        .await;
        assert_eq!(outcome, Ok(7));
        assert!(
            started.load(Ordering::Acquire) <= 3,
            "no chunk is fetched for a disk side that is already gone"
        );
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn no_fetch_starts_once_the_disk_side_is_gone() {
        let calls = AtomicUsize::new(0);
        let cancel = CancelToken::new();
        let hold = Arc::new(Notify::new());
        let (held, holding) = std_mpsc::channel();
        let (gone, going) = std_mpsc::channel();
        let disk = {
            let hold = Arc::clone(&hold);
            move |mut chunks: TestChunks| {
                assert!(chunks.request(0));
                assert_eq!(chunks.receive(), Ok(0));
                // The pump is idle with a free window. Queue more work and go
                // while its task cannot run, so it next wakes to both.
                hold.notify_one();
                holding.recv_timeout(WAIT).unwrap();
                for index in 1..8 {
                    assert!(chunks.request(index));
                }
                drop(chunks);
                gone.send(()).unwrap();
                Ok(7)
            }
        };
        let (outcome, ()) = tokio::join!(
            run_engine(
                pipeline(Delivery::InOrder, 2, 1),
                &cancel,
                disk,
                |index: usize| {
                    calls.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
                    async move { Ok(index) }
                },
            ),
            async {
                hold.notified().await;
                held.send(()).unwrap();
                // Blocks this task, and with it the pump, until the disk side
                // has dropped its end.
                going.recv_timeout(WAIT).unwrap();
            },
        );
        assert_eq!(outcome, Ok(7));
        assert_eq!(calls.load(Ordering::Acquire), 1);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_disk_side_with_nothing_to_request_returns_its_value() {
        let calls = AtomicUsize::new(0);
        let cancel = CancelToken::new();
        let outcome = run_engine(
            pipeline(Delivery::InOrder, 1, 1),
            &cancel,
            |_: TestChunks| Ok(5),
            |index: usize| {
                calls.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
                async move { Ok(index) }
            },
        )
        .await;
        assert_eq!(outcome, Ok(5));
        assert_eq!(calls.load(Ordering::Acquire), 0);
        assert!(!cancel.is_cancelled(), "a finished engine cancels nothing");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn dropping_the_engine_cancels_the_token_and_the_worker_reads_cancelled() {
        let cancel = CancelToken::new();
        let fetching = Arc::new(Notify::new());
        let (received, receipts) = std_mpsc::channel();
        let task = {
            let (cancel, fetching) = (cancel.clone(), Arc::clone(&fetching));
            tokio::spawn(async move {
                let disk = move |mut chunks: TestChunks| {
                    assert!(chunks.request(0));
                    received.send(chunks.receive()).unwrap();
                    Ok(())
                };
                run_engine(
                    pipeline(Delivery::InOrder, 1, 1),
                    &cancel,
                    disk,
                    move |_: usize| {
                        fetching.notify_one();
                        std::future::pending()
                    },
                )
                .await
            })
        };
        // The disk side requested its chunk and nothing will ever answer it.
        fetching.notified().await;
        task.abort();
        assert!(task.await.unwrap_err().is_cancelled());
        assert!(cancel.is_cancelled());
        assert_eq!(receipts.recv_timeout(WAIT), Ok(Err(Failure::Cancelled)));
        tokio::time::timeout(WAIT, cancel.wait_for_workers())
            .await
            .expect("the disk worker stops");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_panicking_disk_worker_returns_interrupted() {
        let cancel = CancelToken::new();
        let outcome = run_engine(
            pipeline(Delivery::InOrder, 1, 1),
            &cancel,
            |_: TestChunks| -> Result<(), Failure> { panic!("the disk worker failed") },
            |index: usize| async move { Ok(index) },
        )
        .await;
        assert_eq!(outcome, Err(Failure::Interrupted));
        assert!(!cancel.is_cancelled());
    }
}
```

`crates/obelisk-core/src/transfer/lifecycle.rs`:

```rs
//! One account's transfer admission, cancellation, progress and completion.
use std::{
    fmt::Display,
    future::Future,
    sync::{Arc, Mutex, PoisonError},
};

use super::{CancelToken, TransferState};

/// Storefronts retain their progress fields and terminal message vocabulary.
pub trait TransferStatus: Clone + Send + 'static {
    fn finish(&mut self, state: TransferState, error: Option<String>);
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct TransferBusy;

/// Admits one transfer at a time, including outstanding blocking work after
/// its caller disappears. Progress remains readable without an async lock.
pub struct Transfers<P> {
    state: Arc<Mutex<State<P>>>,
}

struct State<P> {
    progress: Option<P>,
    active: Option<Active>,
}

struct Active {
    cancel: CancelToken,
    terminal: Option<(TransferState, Option<String>)>,
}

impl<P> Default for Transfers<P> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            state: Arc::new(Mutex::new(State {
                progress: None,
                active: None,
            })),
        }
    }
}

impl<P: TransferStatus> Transfers<P> {
    pub fn snapshot(&self) -> Option<P> {
        let mut state = self.state.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner);
        state.reap();
        state.progress.clone()
    }

    pub fn cancel(&self) {
        let state = self.state.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner);
        if let Some(active) = &state.active {
            active.cancel.cancel();
        }
    }

    /// The operation and its progress callbacks share an attempt identity.
    /// Dropping this future cancels that attempt. Registered blocking work
    /// retains admission until it has really stopped, even after a drop.
    pub async fn run<T, E, F, Fut>(&self, initial: P, operation: F) -> Result<T, E>
    where
        E: From<TransferBusy> + Display,
        F: FnOnce(TransferContext<P>) -> Fut,
        Fut: Future<Output = Result<T, E>>,
    {
        let context = {
            let mut state = self.state.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner);
            state.reap();
            if state.active.is_some() {
                return Err(TransferBusy.into());
            }
            let cancel = CancelToken::new();
            state.active = Some(Active {
                cancel: cancel.clone(),
                terminal: None,
            });
            state.progress = Some(initial);
            TransferContext {
                state: Arc::clone(&self.state),
                cancel,
            }
        };
        let mut owner = Owner(Some(context.clone()));
        let result = operation(context.clone()).await;
        // Close publication before waiting for any outstanding work. Neither a
        // late callback nor explicit cancellation can rewrite this outcome.
        let terminal = match &result {
            Ok(_) => (TransferState::Complete, None),
            Err(error) => (
                if context.cancel.is_cancelled() {
                    TransferState::Cancelled
                } else {
                    TransferState::Failed
                },
                Some(error.to_string()),
            ),
        };
        context.finish(terminal);
        context.cancel.wait_for_workers().await;
        owner.0.take();
        // Terminal state is published together with releasing admission.
        self.snapshot();
        result
    }
}

impl<P: TransferStatus> State<P> {
    fn reap(&mut self) {
        let Some(active) = &mut self.active else {
            return;
        };
        if active.cancel.workers_finished()
            && let Some((phase, error)) = active.terminal.take()
        {
            if let Some(progress) = &mut self.progress {
                progress.finish(phase, error);
            }
            self.active = None;
        }
    }
}

/// Attempt-scoped progress publication. Keeping a callback alive does not hold
/// admission; callbacks from cancelled or older attempts are ignored.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct TransferContext<P> {
    state: Arc<Mutex<State<P>>>,
    cancel: CancelToken,
}

impl<P: TransferStatus> TransferContext<P> {
    pub fn cancel_token(&self) -> &CancelToken {
        &self.cancel
    }

    pub fn update(&self, update: impl FnOnce(&mut P)) {
        let mut state = self.state.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner);
        if state.active.as_ref().is_some_and(|active| {
            Arc::ptr_eq(&active.cancel.0, &self.cancel.0)
                && active.terminal.is_none()
                && !self.cancel.is_cancelled()
        }) && let Some(progress) = &mut state.progress
        {
            update(progress);
        }
    }

    fn finish(&self, terminal: (TransferState, Option<String>)) {
        let mut state = self.state.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner);
        if let Some(active) = &mut state.active
            && Arc::ptr_eq(&active.cancel.0, &self.cancel.0)
            && active.terminal.is_none()
        {
            active.terminal = Some(terminal);
        }
        state.reap();
    }
}

struct Owner<P: TransferStatus>(Option<TransferContext<P>>);

impl<P: TransferStatus> Drop for Owner<P> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if let Some(context) = &self.0 {
            context.cancel.cancel();
            context.finish((TransferState::Cancelled, None));
        }
    }
}
```

```rs
use super::*;
use std::{future::pending, time::Duration};
use tokio::{sync::oneshot, task::JoinHandle};

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
struct Progress {
    game: u32,
    phase: TransferState,
    bytes: u64,
    error: Option<String>,
}

impl Progress {
    fn new(game: u32) -> Self {
        Self {
            game,
            phase: TransferState::Preparing,
            bytes: 0,
            error: None,
        }
    }
}

impl TransferStatus for Progress {
    fn finish(&mut self, state: TransferState, error: Option<String>) {
        self.phase = state;
        self.error = error;
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
enum Failure {
    #[error("busy")]
    Busy,
    #[error("cancelled")]
    Cancelled,
    #[error("disk failure")]
    Disk,
}

impl From<TransferBusy> for Failure {
    fn from(_: TransferBusy) -> Self {
        Self::Busy
    }
}

async fn bounded<T>(future: impl Future<Output = T>) -> T {
    tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), future)
        .await
        .expect("transfer lifecycle did not settle")
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn abandoned_transfer_keeps_admission_until_disk_exit_and_rejects_old_progress() {
    let transfers = Arc::new(Transfers::default());
    let (release, blocked) = oneshot::channel();
    let (started, running) = oneshot::channel();
    let (expose, worker) = oneshot::channel();
    let owner = Arc::clone(&transfers);
    let task = tokio::spawn(async move {
        owner
            .run(Progress::new(1), |context| async move {
                let late = context.clone();
                let work = context.cancel_token().spawn_blocking(move || {
                    started.send(()).unwrap();
                    blocked.blocking_recv().unwrap();
                    assert!(late.cancel_token().is_cancelled());
                    late.update(|progress| progress.bytes = 999);
                });
                expose
                    .send((context, work))
                    .unwrap_or_else(|_| panic!("test receiver lost"));
                pending::<Result<(), Failure>>().await
            })
            .await
    });
    let (late, work) = bounded(worker).await.unwrap();
    bounded(running).await.unwrap();
    task.abort();
    assert!(bounded(task).await.unwrap_err().is_cancelled());
    assert!(late.cancel_token().is_cancelled());
    assert_eq!(
        transfers
            .run(Progress::new(2), |_| async { Ok::<_, Failure>(()) })
            .await,
        Err(Failure::Busy)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        transfers.snapshot().unwrap().phase,
        TransferState::Preparing
    );
    release.send(()).unwrap();
    bounded(work).await.unwrap();
    let cancelled = transfers.snapshot().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(cancelled.phase, TransferState::Cancelled);
    assert_eq!(cancelled.bytes, 0);
    transfers
        .run(Progress::new(2), |context| async move {
            late.update(|progress| {
                progress.game = 1;
                progress.bytes = 999;
            });
            context.update(|progress| progress.bytes = 42);
            Ok::<_, Failure>(())
        })
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let completed = transfers.snapshot().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(completed.game, 2);
    assert_eq!(completed.bytes, 42);
    assert_eq!(completed.phase, TransferState::Complete);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn explicit_cancellation_drains_workers_before_returning_or_admitting_next_transfer() {
    let transfers = Arc::new(Transfers::default());
    let (release, blocked) = oneshot::channel();
    let (expose, worker) = oneshot::channel::<JoinHandle<()>>();
    let (ending, ended) = oneshot::channel();
    let owner = Arc::clone(&transfers);
    let task = tokio::spawn(async move {
        owner
            .run(Progress::new(1), |context| async move {
                let work = context.cancel_token().spawn_blocking(move || {
                    blocked.blocking_recv().unwrap();
                });
                expose.send(work).unwrap();
                context.cancel_token().cancelled().await;
                context.update(|progress| progress.bytes = 999);
                ending.send(()).unwrap();
                Err::<(), _>(Failure::Cancelled)
            })
            .await
    });
    let work = bounded(worker).await.unwrap();
    transfers.cancel();
    bounded(ended).await.unwrap();
    assert!(!task.is_finished());
    assert_eq!(
        transfers
            .run(Progress::new(2), |_| async { Ok::<_, Failure>(()) })
            .await,
        Err(Failure::Busy)
    );
    release.send(()).unwrap();
    bounded(work).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(bounded(task).await.unwrap(), Err(Failure::Cancelled));
    let snapshot = transfers.snapshot().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(snapshot.phase, TransferState::Cancelled);
    assert_eq!(snapshot.bytes, 0);
    assert_eq!(snapshot.error.as_deref(), Some("cancelled"));
    transfers
        .run(Progress::new(2), |_| async { Ok::<_, Failure>(()) })
        .await
        .unwrap();
}

#[tokio::test]

#[tokio::test]
async fn abandonment_waits_for_every_worker_not_only_the_first_one() {
    let transfers = Arc::new(Transfers::default());
    let (first_release, first_wait) = oneshot::channel();
    let (last_release, last_wait) = oneshot::channel();
    let (expose, workers) = oneshot::channel();
    let owner = Arc::clone(&transfers);
    let task = tokio::spawn(async move {
        owner
            .run(Progress::new(1), |context| async move {
                let first = context.cancel_token().spawn_blocking(move || {
                    first_wait.blocking_recv().unwrap();
                });
                let last = context.cancel_token().spawn_blocking(move || {
                    last_wait.blocking_recv().unwrap();
                });
                expose.send((first, last)).unwrap();
                pending::<Result<(), Failure>>().await
            })
            .await
    });
    let (first, last) = bounded(workers).await.unwrap();
    task.abort();
    assert!(bounded(task).await.unwrap_err().is_cancelled());
    first_release.send(()).unwrap();
    bounded(first).await.unwrap();

        transfers
            .run(Progress::new(2), |_| async { Ok::<_, Failure>(()) })
            .await,
        Err(Failure::Busy)
    );
    last_release.send(()).unwrap();
    bounded(last).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        transfers.snapshot().unwrap().phase,
        TransferState::Cancelled
    );
    transfers
        .run(Progress::new(2), |_| async { Ok::<_, Failure>(()) })
        .await
        .unwrap();
}
```

`crates/obelisk-core/src/transfer/window.rs`:

```rs
use futures_util::{StreamExt, stream::FuturesUnordered};
use std::future::Future;

/// How many transfers of one storefront overlap, and how many bytes they may
/// hold at once.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct Window {
    pub width: usize,
    pub bytes: u64,
}

impl Window {
    /// Runs `transfer` on each unit, at most `width` at once and within
    /// `bytes`; a unit larger than `bytes` runs alone. Results reach `receive`
    /// as they complete, so a slow unit holds back nothing after it. `check`
    /// runs before each unit starts, before each result is received and once
    /// at the end. The first error stops the window, and dropping the future
    /// cancels every transfer in flight; no detached worker outlives it.
    pub async fn run<U, T, E, F: Future<Output = Result<T, E>>>(
        self,
        units: impl IntoIterator<Item = U>,
        size: impl Fn(&U) -> u64,
        check: impl Fn() -> Result<(), E>,
        transfer: impl Fn(U) -> F,
        mut receive: impl FnMut(T) -> Result<(), E>,
    ) -> Result<(), E> {
        let transfer = &transfer;
        let mut queued = units.into_iter().peekable();
        let mut pending = FuturesUnordered::new();
        let mut bytes = 0_u64;
        loop {
            // A large unit runs alone. Smaller ones overlap without holding
            // the whole set in memory.
            while let Some(unit) = queued.next_if(|unit| {
                pending.is_empty()
                    || pending.len() < self.width && bytes.saturating_add(size(unit)) <= self.bytes
            }) {
                check()?;
                let unit_size = size(&unit);
                bytes = bytes.saturating_add(unit_size);
                pending.push(async move { (unit_size, transfer(unit).await) });
            }
            let Some((unit_size, result)) = pending.next().await else {
                break;
            };
            let value = result?;
            bytes = bytes.saturating_sub(unit_size);
            check()?;
            receive(value)?;
        }
        check()
    }
}
```

```rs
use super::*;
use std::{
    cell::Cell,
    collections::BTreeSet,
    sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering},
    time::Duration,
};

const WINDOW: Window = Window {
    width: 4,
    bytes: 100,
};

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Failed {
    Check,
    Receive,
}

struct Active<'a>(&'a Cell<usize>);
impl<'a> Active<'a> {
    fn new(active: &'a Cell<usize>, peak: &Cell<usize>) -> Self {
        active.set(active.get() + 1);
        peak.set(peak.get().max(active.get()));
        Self(active)
    }
}
impl Drop for Active<'_> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.0.set(self.0.get() - 1);
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn runs_at_most_its_width_at_once_and_delivers_each_unit_once() {
    let active = Cell::new(0);
    let peak = Cell::new(0);
    let mut received = BTreeSet::new();
    WINDOW
        .run(
            0..WINDOW.width * 2 + 3,
            |_| 1,
            || Ok::<_, Failed>(()),
            |unit| {
                let (active, peak) = (&active, &peak);
                async move {
                    let _active = Active::new(active, peak);
                    tokio::task::yield_now().await;
                    Ok(unit)
                }
            },
            |unit| {
                assert!(received.insert(unit));
                Ok(())
            },
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(received.len(), WINDOW.width * 2 + 3);
    assert_eq!(peak.get(), WINDOW.width);
    assert_eq!(active.get(), 0);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn large_units_run_alone_and_dropping_cancels_every_transfer() {
    let active = Cell::new(0);
    let peak = Cell::new(0);
    let started = Cell::new(0);
    for size in [1, WINDOW.bytes + 1] {
        peak.set(0);
        started.set(0);
        let operation = WINDOW.run(
            0..WINDOW.width + 4,
            |_| size,
            || Ok::<_, Failed>(()),
            |_| {
                started.set(started.get() + 1);
                let (active, peak) = (&active, &peak);
                async move {
                    let _active = Active::new(active, peak);
                    std::future::pending::<()>().await;
                    Ok(())
                }
            },
            |()| panic!("a cancelled transfer must not deliver"),
        );
        assert!(
            tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_millis(10), operation)
                .await
                .is_err()
        );
        let expected = if size > WINDOW.bytes { 1 } else { WINDOW.width };
        assert_eq!(peak.get(), expected);
        assert_eq!(started.get(), expected);
        assert_eq!(active.get(), 0);
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn transfers_overlap_instead_of_waiting_for_each_other() {
    let active = AtomicUsize::new(0);
    let peak = AtomicUsize::new(0);
    let mut received = 0;
    WINDOW
        .run(
            0..WINDOW.width * 2,
            |_| 1,
            || Ok::<_, Failed>(()),
            |_| {
                let (active, peak) = (&active, &peak);
                async move {
                    let now = active.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst) + 1;
                    peak.fetch_max(now, Ordering::SeqCst);
                    tokio::task::yield_now().await;
                    active.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
                    Ok(())
                }
            },
            |()| {
                received += 1;
                Ok(())
            },
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(received, WINDOW.width * 2);
    assert_eq!(peak.load(Ordering::SeqCst), WINDOW.width);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_slow_unit_does_not_hold_back_the_units_after_it() {
    let started = Cell::new(0);
    let operation = WINDOW.run(
        0..WINDOW.width * 2,
        |_| 1,
        || Ok::<_, Failed>(()),
        |unit| {
            started.set(started.get() + 1);
            let started = &started;
            async move {
                // The first unit ends only once units past the first window
                // have started.
                while unit == 0 && started.get() <= WINDOW.width {
                    tokio::task::yield_now().await;
                }
                Ok(())
            }
        },
        |()| Ok(()),
    );
    tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(1), operation)
        .await
        .expect("the window refills while a unit is slow")
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(started.get(), WINDOW.width * 2);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn failed_checks_and_receivers_stop_refills() {
    let started = Cell::new(0);
    let allowed = Cell::new(false);
    let check = || {
        if allowed.get() {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(Failed::Check)
        }
    };
    let transfer = |_| {
        started.set(started.get() + 1);
        allowed.set(false);
        async { Ok(()) }
    };
    let result = WINDOW
        .run(
            0..WINDOW.width * 2,
            |_| 1,
            check,
            transfer,
            |()| panic!("a failed check must stop before receiving"),
        )
        .await;
    assert_eq!(result, Err(Failed::Check));
    assert_eq!(started.get(), 0);

    // A check that fails once transfers run stops before their results.
    allowed.set(true);
    let result = WINDOW
        .run(
            0..WINDOW.width * 2,
            |_| 1,
            check,
            transfer,
            |()| panic!("a failed check must stop before receiving"),
        )
        .await;
    assert_eq!(result, Err(Failed::Check));
    assert!((1..=WINDOW.width).contains(&started.get()));

    started.set(0);
    let result = WINDOW
        .run(
            0..WINDOW.width * 2,
            |_| 1,
            || Ok(()),
            |_| {
                started.set(started.get() + 1);
                async { Ok(()) }
            },
            |()| Err(Failed::Receive),
        )
        .await;
    assert_eq!(result, Err(Failed::Receive));
    // Nothing past the first window starts once the receiver failed.
    assert!(started.get() <= WINDOW.width);
}
```

`crates/obelisk-core/src/verification.rs`:

```rs
//! Bounded full-file verification shared by storefront installers.
//!
//! One call confines every manifest name under the installation root, reads the
//! file through its digest with at most four disk readers, serializes progress, and
//! joins every reader before returning to the caller's repair loop. Storefronts
//! describe their manifest entries and map one error; they do not repeat the
//! path checks or the hashing.
use std::{
    path::{Path, PathBuf},
    sync::{
        Mutex,
        atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicUsize, Ordering},
    },
    thread,
};

use crate::{
    install::{self, FileDigest, InstallError, Matched},
    transfer::{CancelToken, Cancelled, Reporter},
};

const MAX_WORKERS: usize = 4;

/// What the scheduler needs from one manifest entry: where it goes, how big it
/// must be and what it must hash to. Directory entries remain in the result
/// vector as `false` without being passed to a reader.
pub trait VerificationFile {
    /// The manifest name, confined under the installation root before any read.
    fn name(&self) -> &str;
    fn size(&self) -> u64;
    /// What the fully installed file hashes to.
    fn digest(&self) -> FileDigest<'_>;
    fn is_directory(&self) -> bool {
        false
    }
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum VerificationError {
    Cancelled,
    /// A manifest name escaped the installation root, or a read failed.
    Install(InstallError),
    /// A reader panicked, or a verified byte or file counter overflowed. The
    /// scheduler's own failure modes, opaque to callers.
    SchedulerFailed,
}

impl From<Cancelled> for VerificationError {
    fn from(_: Cancelled) -> Self {
        Self::Cancelled
    }
}

impl From<InstallError> for VerificationError {
    fn from(error: InstallError) -> Self {
        match error {
            InstallError::Cancelled => Self::Cancelled,
            other => Self::Install(other),
        }
    }
}

/// The outcome of one verification pass, in manifest order.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct Verified {
    /// One flag per manifest entry. Directory entries are always `false`.
    pub valid: Vec<bool>,
    /// One count per manifest entry: its leading digest parts that matched,
    /// such as the chunks of a GOG file a repair can keep.
    pub matched_parts: Vec<usize>,
    /// Bytes already on disk and verified whole: what this installation reuses.
    pub reused_bytes: u64,
}

pub fn worker_limit() -> usize {
    thread::available_parallelism()
        .map(usize::from)
        .unwrap_or(1)
        .min(MAX_WORKERS)
}

/// Verify every file of the installation at `root` with the host's available
/// parallelism, bounded to four disk readers. Every reader has stopped before
/// this returns, so the caller may begin repairing files immediately.
///
/// Inspection bytes, verified whole files and the current name are published
/// on `reporter` as they are counted. Whole-file validation stays separate from
/// inspection progress, so corrupt files never count as reusable. Updates run
/// inline under the reporter's lock; its callback must not reenter this verifier.
pub fn verify_files<T>(
    root: &Path,
    files: &[T],
    cancel: &CancelToken,
    reporter: &Reporter,
) -> Result<Verified, VerificationError>
where
    T: VerificationFile + Sync,
{
    verify_with_workers(root, files, cancel, reporter, worker_limit())
}

/// An explicit reader limit supports single-reader benchmarks and deterministic
/// overlap tests. Values are clamped to the production ceiling of four.
pub fn verify_with_workers<T>(
    root: &Path,
    files: &[T],
    cancel: &CancelToken,
    reporter: &Reporter,
    workers: usize,
) -> Result<Verified, VerificationError>
where
    T: VerificationFile + Sync,
{
    cancel.check()?;
    reporter.update(|status| status.verification_bytes = Some(0));
    let verified = schedule(
        files,
        cancel,
        |file| confined_path(root, file),
        |path, file: &T, cancel| {
            let mut inspected = 0_u64;
            let mut report = |bytes: u64| {
                // The file can change while it is read. Its contribution must
                // never exceed the size in the manifest.
                let bytes = bytes.min(file.size().saturating_sub(inspected));
                inspected += bytes;
                reporter.update(|status| {
                    status.verification_bytes =
                        Some(status.verification_bytes.unwrap_or(0).saturating_add(bytes));
                    status.current_file.replace_range(.., file.name());
                });
            };
            let matched = install::verify_file_with_progress(
                path,
                file.size(),
                file.digest(),
                cancel,
                &mut report,
            )?;
            // Missing and wrong-size files are inspected without being read.
            // Their full size still belongs to this pass's progress denominator.
            let remaining = file.size().saturating_sub(inspected);
            if remaining != 0 {
                reporter.update(|status| {
                    status.verification_bytes = Some(
                        status
                            .verification_bytes
                            .unwrap_or(0)
                            .saturating_add(remaining),
                    );
                    status.current_file.replace_range(.., file.name());
                });
            }
            Ok(matched)
        },
        |bytes, files, name| {
            reporter.update(|status| {
                status.completed_bytes = bytes;
                status.completed_files = files;
                status.current_file.replace_range(.., name);
            });
        },
        workers,
    )
    .map_err(|error| match error {
        ScheduleError::Cancelled => VerificationError::Cancelled,
        ScheduleError::File(error) => error.into(),
        ScheduleError::WorkerFailed
        | ScheduleError::InvalidTotalSize
        | ScheduleError::InvalidFileCount => VerificationError::SchedulerFailed,
    })?;
    // Repair uses validated bytes and may inspect partial chunks of its own.
    // Do not let the initial scan's numerator leak into that phase.
    reporter.update(|status| status.verification_bytes = None);
    Ok(verified)
}

/// Resolved before a file is reported, so an unsafe name never reaches a reader.
fn confined_path<T: VerificationFile>(root: &Path, file: &T) -> Result<PathBuf, InstallError> {
    install::checked_file_path(root, &install::safe_relative_path(file.name())?)
}

/// The scheduler's internal failures, before they are narrowed for callers.
#[derive(Debug)]
enum ScheduleError<E> {
    Cancelled,
    File(E),
    WorkerFailed,
    InvalidTotalSize,
    InvalidFileCount,
}

impl<E> From<Cancelled> for ScheduleError<E> {
    fn from(_: Cancelled) -> Self {
        Self::Cancelled
    }
}

struct CheckedFiles {
    valid: Vec<bool>,
    matched_parts: Vec<usize>,
    bytes: u64,
    files: u32,
}

/// The reader pool itself. `prepare` and `verify` stay injectable so this
/// module's own tests can drive panics, read failures and counter overflow
/// without a filesystem; they are an internal seam, not part of the interface.
fn schedule<T, P, E>(
    files: &[T],
    cancel: &CancelToken,
    prepare: impl Fn(&T) -> Result<P, E> + Sync,
    verify: impl Fn(&P, &T, &CancelToken) -> Result<Matched, E> + Sync,
    progress: impl Fn(u64, u32, &str) + Sync,
    workers: usize,
) -> Result<Verified, ScheduleError<E>>
where
    T: VerificationFile + Sync,
    E: Send,
{
    cancel.check()?;
    let jobs: Vec<_> = files
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .filter(|(_, file)| !file.is_directory())
        .collect();
    let state = Mutex::new(CheckedFiles {
        valid: vec![false; files.len()],
        matched_parts: vec![0; files.len()],
        bytes: 0,
        files: 0,
    });
    let next = AtomicUsize::new(0);
    let stopped = AtomicBool::new(false);
    let count = workers.clamp(1, MAX_WORKERS).min(jobs.len());
    thread::scope(|scope| {
        let mut handles = Vec::with_capacity(count);
        for _ in 0..count {
            handles.push(scope.spawn(|| {
                // A reader panic stops new work too; scoped threads are still
                // joined below before any caller can repair or replace a file.
                let result = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
                    loop {
                        cancel.check()?;
                        if stopped.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
                            return Ok(());
                        }
                        let job = next.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
                        let Some(&(index, file)) = jobs.get(job) else {
                            return Ok(());
                        };
                        let prepared = prepare(file).map_err(ScheduleError::File)?;
                        {
                            let checked = state.lock().map_err(|_| ScheduleError::WorkerFailed)?;
                            progress(checked.bytes, checked.files, file.name());
                        }
                        cancel.check()?;
                        let matched =
                            verify(&prepared, file, cancel).map_err(ScheduleError::File)?;
                        cancel.check()?;
                        let mut checked = state.lock().map_err(|_| ScheduleError::WorkerFailed)?;
                        checked.valid[index] = matched.whole;
                        checked.matched_parts[index] = matched.parts;
                        if matched.whole {
                            checked.bytes = checked
                                .bytes
                                .checked_add(file.size())
                                .ok_or(ScheduleError::InvalidTotalSize)?;
                            checked.files = checked
                                .files
                                .checked_add(1)
                                .ok_or(ScheduleError::InvalidFileCount)?;
                        }
                        progress(checked.bytes, checked.files, file.name());
                    }
                }))
                .unwrap_or(Err(ScheduleError::WorkerFailed));
                if result.is_err() {
                    stopped.store(true, Ordering::Release);
                }
                result
            }));
        }
        let mut error = None;
        for handle in handles {
            let result = handle.join().unwrap_or(Err(ScheduleError::WorkerFailed));
            if let Err(failure) = result {
                stopped.store(true, Ordering::Release);
                if error.is_none() {
                    error = Some(failure);
                }
            }
        }
        error.map_or(Ok(()), Err)
    })?;
    cancel.check()?;
    let checked = state
        .into_inner()
        .map_err(|_| ScheduleError::WorkerFailed)?;
    Ok(Verified {
        valid: checked.valid,
        matched_parts: checked.matched_parts,
        reused_bytes: checked.bytes,
    })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::transfer::DownloadProgress;
    use sha1::{Digest, Sha1};
    use std::{fs, sync::Arc, sync::Barrier};

    /// A reporter that keeps every snapshot it publishes, so the tests assert on
    /// what a caller actually observes rather than on a private callback.
    fn recording() -> (Arc<Reporter>, Arc<Mutex<Vec<DownloadProgress>>>) {
        let log = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
        let sink = Arc::clone(&log);
        let reporter = Reporter::new(DownloadProgress::default(), move |snapshot| {
            sink.lock().unwrap().push(snapshot);
        });
        (reporter, log)
    }

    /// Discards every snapshot.
    fn silent() -> Arc<Reporter> {
        Reporter::new(DownloadProgress::default(), |_| {})
    }

    /// A manifest entry described the way both storefronts describe theirs.
    struct Entry {
        name: String,
        size: u64,
        sha: Vec<u8>,
        directory: bool,
    }

    impl VerificationFile for Entry {
        fn name(&self) -> &str {
            &self.name
        }
        fn size(&self) -> u64 {
            self.size
        }
        fn digest(&self) -> FileDigest<'_> {
            FileDigest::Sha1(&self.sha)
        }
        fn is_directory(&self) -> bool {
            self.directory
        }
    }

    fn entry(name: &str, bytes: &[u8]) -> Entry {
        Entry {
            name: name.into(),
            size: bytes.len() as u64,
            sha: Sha1::digest(bytes).to_vec(),
            directory: false,
        }
    }

    /// Only the reader pool, so panics and counter overflow stay reachable.
    struct Sized(u64);
    impl VerificationFile for Sized {
        fn name(&self) -> &str {
            "fixture"
        }
        fn size(&self) -> u64 {
            self.0
        }
        fn digest(&self) -> FileDigest<'_> {
            FileDigest::Sha1(&[])
        }
    }

    struct Reader<'a>(&'a AtomicUsize);
    impl Drop for Reader<'_> {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            self.0.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn hashes_valid_corrupt_missing_and_directory_entries_under_the_root() {
        let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        fs::create_dir(root.path().join("folder")).unwrap();
        let bytes = vec![0x5a; 192 * 1024 + 17];
        fs::write(root.path().join("folder/valid"), &bytes).unwrap();
        fs::write(root.path().join("empty"), []).unwrap();
        let mut corrupt = bytes.clone();
        corrupt[128 * 1024] ^= 1;
        fs::write(root.path().join("corrupt"), corrupt).unwrap();
        fs::write(root.path().join("truncated"), &bytes[..100]).unwrap();
        let mut directory = entry("folder", &[]);
        directory.directory = true;
        let files = vec![
            directory,
            entry("folder/valid", &bytes),
            entry("empty", &[]),
            entry("corrupt", &bytes),
            entry("truncated", &bytes),
            entry("missing", &bytes),
        ];
        let (reporter, events) = recording();
        let valid = verify_files(root.path(), &files, &CancelToken::new(), &reporter).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(valid.valid, [false, true, true, false, false, false]);
        assert_eq!(
            valid.reused_bytes,
            bytes.len() as u64,
            "the reused total is the scheduler's own count, not a second fold"
        );
        let events = events.lock().unwrap();
        let scanned: Vec<_> = events
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|event| event.verification_bytes)
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(scanned.first(), Some(&0));
        assert_eq!(
            scanned.last(),
            Some(&(4 * bytes.len() as u64)),
            "corrupt, truncated and missing files advance inspection without becoming reusable"
        );
        assert!(
            scanned.windows(2).all(|pair| pair[0] <= pair[1]),
            "concurrent readers must publish monotonic inspection progress"
        );
        // Counters only ever move forward, whichever reader published them.
        assert!(events.windows(2).all(|pair| {
            pair[0].completed_bytes <= pair[1].completed_bytes
                && pair[0].completed_files <= pair[1].completed_files
        }));
        let last = events.last().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(last.verification_bytes, None, "the scan ends before repair");
        assert_eq!(
            (last.completed_bytes, last.completed_files),
            (bytes.len() as u64, 2)
        );
        assert!(
            events.iter().all(|event| event.current_file != "folder"),
            "a directory entry is never handed to a reader"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn large_file_reports_partial_inspection_before_becoming_reusable() {
        let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let bytes = vec![0x7b; 6 * 1024 * 1024 + 73];
        fs::write(root.path().join("large.pak"), &bytes).unwrap();
        let total_bytes = bytes.len() as u64;
        let cancel = CancelToken::new();
        let callback_cancel = cancel.clone();
        let events = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
        let sink = Arc::clone(&events);
        let reporter = Reporter::new(
            DownloadProgress {
                total_bytes,
                ..Default::default()
            },
            move |snapshot| {
                if snapshot
                    .verification_bytes
                    .is_some_and(|bytes| bytes > 0 && bytes < total_bytes)
                {
                    callback_cancel.cancel();
                }
                sink.lock().unwrap().push(snapshot);
            },
        );

        let result = verify_with_workers(
            root.path(),
            &[entry("large.pak", &bytes)],
            &cancel,
            &reporter,
            1,
        );

        assert!(
            matches!(result, Err(VerificationError::Cancelled)),
            "inspection progress must be published while the file is still being hashed"
        );
        let events = events.lock().unwrap();
        let partial = events
            .iter()
            .find(|event| {
                event
                    .verification_bytes
                    .is_some_and(|bytes| bytes > 0 && bytes < total_bytes)
            })
            .expect("a large file must publish progress before its hash is complete");
        assert_eq!(partial.current_file, "large.pak");
        assert_eq!((partial.completed_bytes, partial.completed_files), (0, 0));
        assert!(
            events
                .iter()
                .all(|event| { event.completed_bytes == 0 && event.completed_files == 0 }),
            "cancelled inspection must never count the unfinished file as reusable"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn unsafe_names_are_rejected_before_any_read() {
        let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let outside = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        fs::write(outside.path().join("secret"), b"unreadable").unwrap();
        #[cfg(unix)]
        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(outside.path(), root.path().join("link")).unwrap();
        let reporter = silent();
        for name in ["../outside", "/absolute", ".obelisk-content/lock"] {
            assert!(matches!(
                verify_files(
                    root.path(),
                    &[entry(name, b"x")],
                    &CancelToken::new(),
                    &reporter
                ),
                Err(VerificationError::Install(InstallError::UnsafePath(_)))
            ));
        }
        #[cfg(unix)]
        assert!(matches!(
            verify_files(
                root.path(),
                &[entry("link/secret", b"unreadable")],
                &CancelToken::new(),
                &reporter
            ),
            Err(VerificationError::Install(InstallError::UnsafePath(_)))
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn readers_overlap_up_to_the_four_reader_ceiling() {
        let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let count = worker_limit();
        assert!((1..=4).contains(&count));
        let bytes = vec![7_u8; 64 * 1024];
        let files: Vec<_> = (0..count)
            .map(|index| {
                let name = format!("file-{index}");
                fs::write(root.path().join(&name), &bytes).unwrap();
                entry(&name, &bytes)
            })
            .collect();
        // Every reader must be able to run at once, or this never completes.
        let overlap = Barrier::new(count);
        let active = AtomicUsize::new(0);
        let peak = AtomicUsize::new(0);
        let valid = schedule(
            &files,
            &CancelToken::new(),
            |file| confined_path(root.path(), file),
            |path, file: &Entry, cancel| {
                let running = active.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel) + 1;
                let _reader = Reader(&active);
                peak.fetch_max(running, Ordering::AcqRel);
                overlap.wait();
                install::verify_file_with_progress(path, file.size(), file.digest(), cancel, |_| {})
            },
            |_, _, _| {},
            count,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert!(valid.valid.iter().all(|valid| *valid));
        assert_eq!(peak.load(Ordering::Acquire), count);
        assert_eq!(active.load(Ordering::Acquire), 0);
        assert!(count <= MAX_WORKERS);
    }

    #[test]
    fn cancellation_joins_every_reader_and_skips_remaining_files() {
        let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let bytes = vec![3_u8; 1024];
        let files: Vec<_> = (0..8)
            .map(|index| {
                let name = format!("file-{index}");
                fs::write(root.path().join(&name), &bytes).unwrap();
                entry(&name, &bytes)
            })
            .collect();
        let cancel = CancelToken::new();
        let active = AtomicUsize::new(0);
        let started = AtomicUsize::new(0);
        let result = schedule(
            &files,
            &cancel,
            |file| confined_path(root.path(), file),
            |path, file: &Entry, inner: &CancelToken| {
                active.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
                let _reader = Reader(&active);
                started.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
                let matched = install::verify_file_with_progress(
                    path,
                    file.size(),
                    file.digest(),
                    inner,
                    |_| {},
                )?;
                // Cancelled once this file is read: the scheduler must stop
                // before handing the next one to a reader.
                cancel.cancel();
                Ok(matched)
            },
            |_, _, _| {},
            1,
        );
        assert!(matches!(result, Err(ScheduleError::Cancelled)));
        assert_eq!(active.load(Ordering::Acquire), 0, "every reader is joined");
        assert_eq!(
            started.load(Ordering::Acquire),
            1,
            "cancellation stops the remaining files"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn error_and_panic_join_every_reader_and_stop_pending_files() {
        for panic in [false, true] {
            let active = AtomicUsize::new(0);
            let started = AtomicUsize::new(0);
            let overlap = Barrier::new(4);
            let result = schedule(
                &[Sized(1), Sized(1), Sized(1), Sized(1), Sized(1), Sized(1)],
                &CancelToken::new(),
                |_| Ok(()),
                |_, _, _| {
                    active.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
                    let _reader = Reader(&active);
                    started.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
                    overlap.wait();
                    if panic {
                        panic!("fixture reader failed");
                    }
                    Err("fixture read failure")
                },
                |_, _, _| {},
                4,
            );
            if panic {
                assert!(matches!(result, Err(ScheduleError::WorkerFailed)));
            } else {
                assert!(matches!(
                    result,
                    Err(ScheduleError::File("fixture read failure"))
                ));
            }
            assert_eq!(active.load(Ordering::Acquire), 0);
            assert_eq!(started.load(Ordering::Acquire), 4);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn scheduler_failures_stay_opaque_to_callers() {
        let overflow = schedule(
            &[Sized(u64::MAX), Sized(1)],
            &CancelToken::new(),
            |_| Ok::<_, ()>(()),
            |_, _, _| {
                Ok(Matched {
                    whole: true,
                    parts: 1,
                })
            },
            |_, _, _| {},
            1,
        );
        assert!(matches!(overflow, Err(ScheduleError::InvalidTotalSize)));
        let panic = schedule(
            &[Sized(1)],
            &CancelToken::new(),
            |_| Ok::<_, ()>(()),
            |_, _, _| {
                Ok(Matched {
                    whole: true,
                    parts: 1,
                })
            },
            |_, _, _| panic!("fixture callback failed"),
            1,
        );
        assert!(matches!(panic, Err(ScheduleError::WorkerFailed)));
        // Both reach the caller as one variant, not as five.
        for error in [
            ScheduleError::<()>::WorkerFailed,
            ScheduleError::InvalidTotalSize,
            ScheduleError::InvalidFileCount,
        ] {
            let narrowed = match error {
                ScheduleError::Cancelled => VerificationError::Cancelled,
                ScheduleError::File(()) => VerificationError::SchedulerFailed,
                ScheduleError::WorkerFailed
                | ScheduleError::InvalidTotalSize
                | ScheduleError::InvalidFileCount => VerificationError::SchedulerFailed,
            };
            assert!(matches!(narrowed, VerificationError::SchedulerFailed));
        }
    }
}
```

`crates/obelisk-core/src/watch.rs`:

```rs
//! Revisioned snapshot observation shared by the friends and credential watches.
use tokio::sync::watch;

/// Waits until the observed value satisfies `is_ready`, checking the current
/// value before waiting so a change between the two cannot be missed.
/// `Err` carries the last value once every sender has been dropped.
pub async fn next_matching<T: Clone>(
    mut receiver: watch::Receiver<T>,
    is_ready: impl Fn(&T) -> bool,
) -> Result<T, T> {
    loop {
        let value = receiver.borrow_and_update().clone();
        if is_ready(&value) {
            return Ok(value);
        }
        if receiver.changed().await.is_err() {
            return Err(receiver.borrow().clone());
        }
    }
}

/// A revision that grows with each change, such as a credential rotation,
/// until it is stopped. Clones share one revision.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Revisions(watch::Sender<RevisionState>);

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
struct RevisionState {
    revision: u64,
    stopped: bool,
}

impl Revisions {
    /// Starts at revision 1.
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self(
            watch::channel(RevisionState {
                revision: 1,
                stopped: false,
            })
            .0,
        )
    }

    /// The revision now.
    pub fn current(&self) -> u64 {
        self.0.borrow().revision
    }

    /// The first revision other than `after`; `None` once stopped.
    pub async fn next(&self, after: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        next_matching(self.0.subscribe(), |state| {
            state.stopped || state.revision != after
        })
        .await
        .ok()
        .filter(|state| !state.stopped)
        .map(|state| state.revision)
    }

    /// Moves on to the next revision.
    pub fn advance(&self) {
        self.0
            .send_modify(|state| state.revision = state.revision.wrapping_add(1));
    }

    /// Ends every wait for a next revision, now and later.
    pub fn stop(&self) {
        self.0.send_modify(|state| state.stopped = true);
    }
}

impl Default for Revisions {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn returns_current_value_when_already_ready_and_last_value_on_close() {
        let (sender, _) = watch::channel(1_u64);
        assert_eq!(next_matching(sender.subscribe(), |v| *v >= 1).await, Ok(1));
        let waiting = tokio::spawn(next_matching(sender.subscribe(), |v| *v >= 2));
        sender.send_replace(2);
        assert_eq!(waiting.await.unwrap(), Ok(2));
        let closing = tokio::spawn(next_matching(sender.subscribe(), |v| *v >= 3));
        tokio::task::yield_now().await;
        drop(sender);
        assert_eq!(closing.await.unwrap(), Err(2));
    }
}
```

```rs
use obelisk_core::{CoreError, GameKind, Library};
use std::fs;
use std::sync::Arc;
use tempfile::TempDir;

fn game_file(root: &TempDir, name: &str) -> std::path::PathBuf {
    let path = root.path().join(name);
    fs::write(&path, b"fixture, not a runnable executable").unwrap();
    path
}

#[test]
fn imports_reload_and_remove_preserve_original_game() {
    let root = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let storage = root.path().join("catalog");
    let path = game_file(&root, "Example.exe");
    let library = Library::open(&storage).unwrap();
    let game = library.add_local_game(&path).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(game.title, "Example");
    assert_eq!(game.kind, GameKind::WindowsExecutable);
    assert_eq!(game.last_played_at, None);
    library.record_launch(&game.id).unwrap();
    drop(library);

    let reloaded = Library::open(&storage).unwrap();
    let games = reloaded.games().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(games.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(games[0].id, game.id);
    assert!(games[0].last_played_at.is_some());
    reloaded.remove_game(&game.id).unwrap();
    assert!(reloaded.games().unwrap().is_empty());
    assert_eq!(
        fs::read(path).unwrap(),
        b"fixture, not a runnable executable"
    );
}

#[test]

#[test]
fn corrupt_and_unsupported_catalogs_are_preserved() {
    let root = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let path = root.path().join("library.json");
    for content in [
        "broken json",
        r#"{"schema_version":999,"games":[]}"#,
        r#"{"schema_version":1,"games":[{"id":"bad"}]}"#,
    ] {
        fs::write(&path, content).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            Library::open(root.path()),
            Err(CoreError::CorruptLibrary { .. })
        ));
        assert_eq!(fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap(), content);
    }
}

#[test]
fn corruption_after_open_blocks_mutations_instead_of_overwriting() {
    let root = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let library = Library::open(root.path().join("catalog")).unwrap();
    let catalog = root.path().join("catalog/library.json");
    fs::write(&catalog, "broken json").unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(
        library.add_local_game(game_file(&root, "Example.exe")),
        Err(CoreError::CorruptLibrary { .. })
    ));
    assert_eq!(fs::read_to_string(catalog).unwrap(), "broken json");
}

#[test]
fn multiple_instances_merge_changes_and_threads_deduplicate() {
    let root = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let storage = root.path().join("catalog");
    let first = Arc::new(Library::open(&storage).unwrap());
    let second = Library::open(&storage).unwrap();
    let path = game_file(&root, "First.exe");
    std::thread::scope(|scope| {
        for _ in 0..8 {
            scope.spawn(|| first.add_local_game(&path).unwrap());
        }
    });
    second
        .add_local_game(game_file(&root, "Second.exe"))
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(first.games().unwrap().len(), 2);
    assert_eq!(second.games().unwrap().len(), 2);
}

#[test]
fn missing_ids_do_not_modify_the_catalog_or_original() {
    let root = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let storage = root.path().join("catalog");
    let original = game_file(&root, "Example.exe");
    let library = Library::open(&storage).unwrap();
    library.add_local_game(&original).unwrap();
    let before = fs::read(storage.join("library.json")).unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(
        library.remove_game("missing"),
        Err(CoreError::NotFound { .. })
    ));
    assert!(matches!(
        library.record_launch("missing"),
        Err(CoreError::NotFound { .. })
    ));
    assert_eq!(fs::read(storage.join("library.json")).unwrap(), before);
    assert!(original.exists());
}

#[test]
fn orders_by_activity_then_title_and_keeps_missing_games() {
    let root = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let storage = root.path().join("catalog");
    let library = Library::open(&storage).unwrap();
    let alpha = library
        .add_local_game(game_file(&root, "Alpha.exe"))
        .unwrap();
    let beta = library
        .add_local_game(game_file(&root, "Beta.exe"))
        .unwrap();
    let catalog_path = storage.join("library.json");
    let mut catalog: serde_json::Value =
        serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(&catalog_path).unwrap()).unwrap();
    for game in catalog["games"].as_array_mut().unwrap() {
        game["added_at"] = 1.into();
        game["last_played_at"] = if game["id"] == beta.id {
            2.into()
        } else {
            serde_json::Value::Null
        };
    }
    fs::write(&catalog_path, serde_json::to_vec(&catalog).unwrap()).unwrap();
    fs::remove_file(&alpha.path).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        library
            .games()
            .unwrap()
            .iter()
            .map(|g| g.id.clone())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        vec![beta.id, alpha.id]
    );
}

#[test]
fn failed_storage_access_does_not_delete_game() {
    let root = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let storage = root.path().join("catalog");
    let library = Library::open(&storage).unwrap();
    let game_path = game_file(&root, "Example.exe");
    let game = library.add_local_game(&game_path).unwrap();
    let preserved = root.path().join("preserved-catalog");
    fs::rename(&storage, &preserved).unwrap();
    fs::write(&storage, "storage path is now a file").unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(
        library.remove_game(&game.id),
        Err(CoreError::Storage { .. })
    ));
    assert!(game_path.exists());
    assert_eq!(Library::open(preserved).unwrap().games().unwrap().len(), 1);
}
```
