```rs
//! Launcher OAuth protocol, independently implemented from the endpoints
//! documented by Legendary's `legendary/api/egs.py`.
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use obelisk_core::transfer::{BodySize, CancelToken, read_body};
use reqwest::{StatusCode, Url};
use serde::Deserialize;

use crate::EpicError;

const CLIENT_ID: &str = "34a02cf8f4414e29b15921876da36f9a";
// Public launcher client credentials, not an account secret.
const CLIENT_SECRET: &str = "daafbccc737745039dffe53d94fc76cf";
const USER_AGENT: &str =
    "UELauncher/11.0.1-14907503+++Portal+Release-Live Windows/10.0.19041.1.256.64bit";

// Deliberately no Debug: callers store this record in the system Keychain.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct Credentials {
    pub account_id: String,
    pub display_name: String,
    pub refresh_token: String,
}

pub fn login_url() -> String {
    // Epic's launcher web flow redirects to localhost with an authorization
    // code. The native login window intercepts it before any localhost request.
    "https://www.epicgames.com/id/login?responseType=code".to_owned()
}

/// Accept the code itself, Epic's JSON response, or the final redirect URL.
/// This only extracts a code; it never opens a URL provided by the caller.
pub fn authorization_code(input: &str) -> Result<String, EpicError> {
    let input = input.trim();
    if input.len() > 32_768 {
        return Err(EpicError::InvalidCode);
    }
    let candidate = if input.starts_with('{') {
        let value: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(input).map_err(|_| EpicError::InvalidCode)?;
        value["authorizationCode"]
            .as_str()
            .ok_or(EpicError::InvalidCode)?
            .to_owned()
    } else if input.contains("://") {
        let url = Url::parse(input).map_err(|_| EpicError::InvalidCode)?;
        if url.scheme() != "https"
            || !matches!(url.host_str(), Some("epicgames.com" | "www.epicgames.com"))
            || !url.username().is_empty()
            || url.password().is_some()
        {
            return Err(EpicError::InvalidCode);
        }
        let codes: Vec<_> = url
            .query_pairs()
            .filter(|(name, _)| name == "code" || name == "authorizationCode")
            .collect();
        if codes.len() != 1 {
            return Err(EpicError::InvalidCode);
        }
        codes[0].1.to_string()
    } else {
        input.to_owned()
    };
    let candidate = candidate.trim();
    if candidate.is_empty()
        || candidate.len() > 2048
        || !candidate
            .bytes()
            .all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(byte, b'-' | b'_'))
    {
        return Err(EpicError::InvalidCode);
    }
    Ok(candidate.to_owned())
}

pub(crate) struct Session {
    pub credentials: Credentials,
    pub access_token: String,
    pub expires_at: Instant,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct TokenResponse {
    access_token: String,
    refresh_token: String,
    account_id: String,
    #[serde(rename = "displayName", default)]
    display_name: String,
    expires_in: u64,
}

#[derive(Clone)]
pub(crate) struct Api {
    pub http: reqwest::Client,
    pub account: String,
    pub store: String,
    pub library: String,
    pub launcher: String,
    pub catalog: String,
    pub ecommerce: String,
    pub friends: String,
    pub presence: String,
    pub connect: String,
    pub cloud: String,
}

impl Api {
    pub fn new() -> Result<Self, EpicError> {
        Ok(Self {
            // Redirects are not needed for these APIs and must never carry an
            // OAuth credential to a different endpoint.
            http: reqwest::Client::builder()
                .user_agent(USER_AGENT)
                .redirect(reqwest::redirect::Policy::none())
                .connect_timeout(Duration::from_secs(15))
                .timeout(Duration::from_secs(45))
                .build()
                .map_err(|_| EpicError::Network)?,
            store: "https://launcher.store.epicgames.com".into(),
            friends: "https://friends-public-service-prod.ol.epicgames.com".into(),
            presence: "https://api.epicgames.dev".into(),
            connect: "wss://connect.ol.epicgames.com/".into(),
            cloud: "https://datastorage-public-service-liveegs.live.use1a.on.epicgames.com".into(),
            account: "https://account-public-service-prod03.ol.epicgames.com".into(),
            library: "https://library-service.live.use1a.on.epicgames.com".into(),
            launcher: "https://launcher-public-service-prod06.ol.epicgames.com".into(),
            catalog: "https://catalog-public-service-prod06.ol.epicgames.com".into(),
            ecommerce: "https://ecommerceintegration-public-service-ecomprod02.ol.epicgames.com"
                .into(),
        })
    }

    pub async fn authorize(&self, code: &str) -> Result<Session, EpicError> {
        self.token("authorization_code", "code", code).await
    }

    pub async fn exchange(&self, code: &str, account: &str) -> Result<Session, EpicError> {
        if !valid_secret(code) || account.is_empty() {
            return Err(EpicError::InvalidCode);
        }
        let session = self.token("exchange_code", "exchange_code", code).await?;
        if session.credentials.account_id != account {
            let _ = self.revoke(&session.access_token).await;
            return Err(EpicError::Unauthorized);
        }
        Ok(session)
    }

    pub async fn refresh(&self, credentials: &Credentials) -> Result<Session, EpicError> {
        if !valid_secret(&credentials.refresh_token) || credentials.account_id.is_empty() {
            return Err(EpicError::Unauthorized);
        }
        let session = self
            .token("refresh_token", "refresh_token", &credentials.refresh_token)
            .await?;
        if session.credentials.account_id != credentials.account_id {
            let _ = self.revoke(&session.access_token).await;
            return Err(EpicError::Unauthorized);
        }
        Ok(session)
    }

    async fn token(&self, grant: &str, key: &str, secret: &str) -> Result<Session, EpicError> {
        let response = self
            .http
            .post(format!("{}/account/api/oauth/token", self.account))
            .basic_auth(CLIENT_ID, Some(CLIENT_SECRET))
            .form(&[("grant_type", grant), (key, secret), ("token_type", "eg1")])
            .send()
            .await
            .map_err(|_| EpicError::Network)?;
        let status = response.status();
        if matches!(status, StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST | StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED) {
            return Err(if grant == "authorization_code" {
                EpicError::InvalidCode
            } else {
                EpicError::Unauthorized
            });
        }
        check_status(status)?;
        let response: TokenResponse = bounded_json(response, 1024 * 1024).await?;
        if !valid_secret(&response.access_token)
            || !valid_secret(&response.refresh_token)
            || response.account_id.is_empty()
            || response.expires_in == 0
        {
            return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
        }
        let lifetime = Duration::from_secs(response.expires_in.saturating_sub(60).max(1));
        let expires_at = Instant::now()
            .checked_add(lifetime)
            .ok_or(EpicError::Protocol)?;
        Ok(Session {
            access_token: response.access_token,
            credentials: Credentials {
                account_id: response.account_id,
                display_name: response.display_name,
                refresh_token: response.refresh_token,
            },
            expires_at,
        })
    }

    pub async fn revoke(&self, access_token: &str) -> Result<(), EpicError> {
        let mut url = Url::parse(&format!(
            "{}/account/api/oauth/sessions/kill/",
            self.account
        ))
        .map_err(|_| EpicError::Protocol)?;
        url.path_segments_mut()
            .map_err(|_| EpicError::Protocol)?
            .pop_if_empty()
            .push(access_token);
        let status = self
            .http
            .delete(url)
            .bearer_auth(access_token)
            .send()
            .await
            .map_err(|_| EpicError::Network)?
            .status();
        if matches!(status, StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED | StatusCode::NOT_FOUND) {
            return Ok(());
        }
        check_status(status)
    }

    pub async fn ownership_token(
        &self,
        access_token: &str,
        account_id: &str,
        namespace: &str,
        catalog_item_id: &str,
    ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, EpicError> {
        let mut url = Url::parse(&self.ecommerce).map_err(|_| EpicError::Protocol)?;
        url.path_segments_mut()
            .map_err(|_| EpicError::Protocol)?
            .clear()
            .extend([
                "ecommerceintegration",
                "api",
                "public",
                "platforms",
                "EPIC",
                "identities",
                account_id,
                "ownershipToken",
            ]);
        let response = self
            .http
            .post(url)
            .bearer_auth(access_token)
            .form(&[("nsCatalogItemId", format!("{namespace}:{catalog_item_id}"))])
            .send()
            .await
            .map_err(|_| EpicError::Network)?;
        check_status(response.status())?;
        let token = bounded_bytes(response, 1024 * 1024).await?;
        if token.is_empty() {
            return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
        }
        Ok(token)
    }

    pub async fn get<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(
        &self,
        url: Url,
        access_token: &str,
    ) -> Result<T, EpicError> {
        let response = self
            .http
            .get(url)
            .bearer_auth(access_token)
            .send()
            .await
            .map_err(|_| EpicError::Network)?;
        check_status(response.status())?;
        bounded_json(response, 8 * 1024 * 1024).await
    }

    /// `get`, where a resource Epic does not have answers `None`.
    pub async fn get_optional<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(
        &self,
        url: Url,
        access_token: &str,
    ) -> Result<Option<T>, EpicError> {
        let response = self
            .http
            .get(url)
            .bearer_auth(access_token)
            .send()
            .await
            .map_err(|_| EpicError::Network)?;
        if response.status() == StatusCode::NOT_FOUND {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        check_status(response.status())?;
        bounded_json(response, 8 * 1024 * 1024).await.map(Some)
    }

    /// Same bounds and status mapping as `get`, for endpoints that take a JSON
    /// body and identify the launcher component making the request.
    pub async fn post_json<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(
        &self,
        url: String,
        access_token: &str,
        agent: &str,
        body: &impl serde::Serialize,
    ) -> Result<T, EpicError> {
        let response = self
            .http
            .post(url)
            .header(reqwest::header::USER_AGENT, agent)
            .bearer_auth(access_token)
            .json(body)
            .send()
            .await
            .map_err(|_| EpicError::Network)?;
        check_status(response.status())?;
        bounded_json(response, 8 * 1024 * 1024).await
    }
}

/// Only HTTPS locations without embedded credentials are handed to the host,
/// for avatars, catalog artwork and achievement icons alike.
pub(crate) fn safe_https_url(value: String) -> Option<String> {
    Url::parse(&value)
        .ok()
        .filter(|url| {
            url.scheme() == "https"
                && url.host_str().is_some()
                && url.username().is_empty()
                && url.password().is_none()
        })
        .map(|_| value)
}

/// Embedded credentials and fragments never belong on a URL this crate fetches.
/// Callers layer their own scheme, host and port rules on top of this.
pub(crate) fn credential_free(url: &Url) -> bool {
    url.host_str().is_some()
        && url.username().is_empty()
        && url.password().is_none()
        && url.fragment().is_none()
}

pub(crate) async fn bounded_json<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(
    response: reqwest::Response,
    limit: usize,
) -> Result<T, EpicError> {
    serde_json::from_slice(&bounded_bytes(response, limit).await?).map_err(|_| EpicError::Protocol)
}

pub(crate) async fn bounded_bytes(
    response: reqwest::Response,
    limit: usize,
) -> Result<Vec<u8>, EpicError> {
    Ok(read_body(
        response.content_length(),
        response.bytes_stream(),
        BodySize::AtMost(limit as u64),
        &CancelToken::new(),
        |_| {},
    )
    .await?)
}

fn valid_secret(value: &str) -> bool {
    !value.is_empty() && value.len() <= 16_384 && !value.chars().any(char::is_whitespace)
}

pub(crate) fn check_status(status: StatusCode) -> Result<(), EpicError> {
    if status.is_success() {
        Ok(())
    } else if status == StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED {
        Err(EpicError::Unauthorized)
    } else {
        // Do not expose response bodies or reqwest errors: they can contain
        // account credentials and the revocation URL itself contains a token.
        Err(EpicError::Service {
            message: match status {
                StatusCode::TOO_MANY_REQUESTS => "backend.epic.rate_limited".into(),
                StatusCode::FORBIDDEN => "backend.epic.forbidden".into(),
                _ => serde_json::json!({
                    "key": "backend.epic.http",
                    "args": [status.as_u16().to_string()]
                })
                .to_string(),
            },
        })
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn code_input_accepts_epic_formats_without_accepting_other_urls() {
        for input in [
            "  abc_123-XYZ \n",
            r#"{"authorizationCode":"abc_123-XYZ","sid":null}"#,
            "https://www.epicgames.com/id/api/redirect?code=abc_123-XYZ",
        ] {
            assert_eq!(authorization_code(input).unwrap(), "abc_123-XYZ");
        }
        for input in [
            "",
            "{broken",
            r#"{"authorizationCode":null}"#,
            "https://example.com/?code=secret",
            "some words",
            "https://www.epicgames.com/?code=one&code=two",
            "https://www.epicgames.com/id/login",
            "code\r\ninjection",
        ] {
            assert!(matches!(
                authorization_code(input),
                Err(EpicError::InvalidCode)
            ));
        }
        let login = Url::parse(&login_url()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(login.host_str(), Some("www.epicgames.com"));
        assert_eq!(login.path(), "/id/login");
        assert_eq!(login.query(), Some("responseType=code"));
    }
}
```

`crates/storefronts/epic-kit/src/client.rs`:

```rs
//! Account-scoped library requests. Token refresh is serialized, while library
//! reads release the session lock so disconnect can invalidate them promptly.
use std::{
    collections::{BTreeMap, HashSet},
    future::Future,
    sync::Arc,
    time::Instant,
};

use futures_util::{StreamExt, TryStreamExt, stream};
use obelisk_core::{
    platform::{Platform, Spelling},
    watch::Revisions,
};
use reqwest::Url;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serializer};
use tokio::sync::Mutex;

use crate::{
    EpicError,
    auth::{self, Api, Credentials, Session},
};

mod achievements;
mod cloud_api;
pub use achievements::Achievement;
mod download;
mod launch;
pub use download::{
    Installation, Prerequisite, TransferProgress, TransferState, installation_directory_name,
};
pub use launch::{InstalledLaunch, LaunchPlan, installed_catalog_item, installed_launch};

/// Epic's asset API labels for the two builds; also its receipts', folders'
/// and ids' spelling.
pub const PLATFORM: Spelling = Spelling::new("Mac", "Windows");

/// Writes a platform as Epic spells it.
pub fn write_platform<S: Serializer>(
    platform: &Platform,
    serializer: S,
) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
    PLATFORM.serialize(*platform, serializer)
}

const MAX_LIBRARY_PAGES: usize = 1000;
const MAX_LIBRARY_RECORDS: usize = 100_000;

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Game {
    pub app_name: String,
    pub namespace: String,
    pub catalog_item_id: String,
    pub title: String,
    pub description: String,
    pub image_url: Option<String>,
    pub header_image_url: Option<String>,
    pub developer: String,
    pub windows: bool,
    pub macos: bool,
    /// When the game joined the account's library, in seconds since the
    /// Unix epoch.
    pub added_at: Option<u64>,
    /// Everything Epic returned for the game: `catalogItems` by catalog item
    /// ID, `libraryRecords`, and `assets` by platform.
    pub metadata: serde_json::Value,
}

/// What a game's page adds to its library entry: the build it shows before
/// any download, and its size.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct GameDetails {
    /// The Mac build, unless a download found that its game does not run
    /// natively. Unknown when Epic could not tell.
    pub platform: Option<Platform>,
    /// Unknown when Epic serves no manifest of the build.
    pub installation_bytes: Option<u64>,
}

pub struct Client {
    downloads: download::Downloads,
    api: Api,
    session: Arc<Mutex<Option<Session>>>,
    credential_events: Revisions,
    social: crate::social::SocialService,
    installation_sizes: crate::details::InstallationSizes,
    /// Each Mac build's verdict, and the manifest the last native one read,
    /// for its download.
    build_choice: crate::details::BuildChoice,
}

impl Client {
    pub async fn sign_in(input: &str) -> Result<Self, EpicError> {
        let code = auth::authorization_code(input)?;
        let api = Api::new()?;
        let session = api.authorize(&code).await?;
        Ok(Self::from_session(api, session))
    }

    pub async fn restore(credentials: Credentials) -> Result<Self, EpicError> {
        let api = Api::new()?;
        let session = api.refresh(&credentials).await?;
        Ok(Self::from_session(api, session))
    }

    /// Creates an independent in-memory session for a detached supervisor.
    /// The exchange code is single-use and must never be persisted or logged.
    pub async fn from_exchange_code(code: &str, expected_account: &str) -> Result<Self, EpicError> {
        let api = Api::new()?;
        let session = api.exchange(code, expected_account).await?;
        Ok(Self::from_session(api, session))
    }

    pub async fn exchange_code(&self) -> Result<String, EpicError> {
        #[derive(Deserialize)]
        struct Exchange {
            code: String,
        }
        self.with_access_token(|token| async move {
            let url = endpoint(&self.api.account, &["account", "api", "oauth", "exchange"])?;
            let exchange: Exchange = self.api.get(url, &token).await?;
            if exchange.code.is_empty()
                || exchange.code.len() > 2048
                || !exchange
                    .code
                    .bytes()
                    .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(c, b'-' | b'_'))
            {
                return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
            }
            Ok(exchange.code)
        })
        .await
    }

    /// Opens Epic's site signed in as the account, then goes on to
    /// `redirect`, as launchers open Epic's store: the page spends a new
    /// exchange code. The address is a secret until it loads.
    pub async fn web_sign_in_url(&self, redirect: &str) -> Result<String, EpicError> {
        let redirect = Url::parse(redirect).map_err(|_| EpicError::Protocol)?;
        if redirect.scheme() != "https"
            || !auth::credential_free(&redirect)
            || !redirect
                .host_str()
                .is_some_and(|host| host == "epicgames.com" || host.ends_with(".epicgames.com"))
        {
            return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
        }
        let code = self.exchange_code().await?;
        let mut url =
            Url::parse("https://www.epicgames.com/id/exchange").map_err(|_| EpicError::Protocol)?;
        url.query_pairs_mut()
            .append_pair("exchangeCode", &code)
            .append_pair("redirectUrl", redirect.as_str());
        Ok(url.into())
    }

    pub async fn credentials(&self) -> Result<Credentials, EpicError> {
        self.session
            .lock()
            .await
            .as_ref()
            .map(|session| session.credentials.clone())
            .ok_or(EpicError::Unauthorized)
    }

    /// Refresh before a long read so the caller can persist a rotated token
    /// without waiting for catalog enrichment to finish.
    pub async fn prepare(&self) -> Result<Credentials, EpicError> {
        self.access_token(None).await?;
        self.credentials().await
    }

    pub async fn games(&self) -> Result<Vec<Game>, EpicError> {
        self.with_access_token(|token| async move { library(&self.api, &token).await })
            .await
    }

    /// The build the game's page shows before any download, and its size:
    /// the Mac build, unless a download found that its game does not run
    /// natively. Only `platform` reads the build's files.
    pub async fn game_details(
        &self,
        namespace: &str,
        catalog_item_id: &str,
        app_name: &str,
    ) -> Result<GameDetails, EpicError> {
        validate_identity(namespace, catalog_item_id, app_name)?;
        let shown = self
            .with_access_token(|token| async move {
                let shown = crate::details::shown_build(
                    &self.api,
                    &token,
                    namespace,
                    catalog_item_id,
                    app_name,
                    &self.build_choice,
                    &self.installation_sizes,
                )
                .await;
                // Re-raise so the funnel refreshes the token once; the funnel
                // also rejects the result if the session went away meanwhile.
                match shown {
                    Err(EpicError::Unauthorized) => Err(EpicError::Unauthorized),
                    shown => Ok(shown.ok()),
                }
            })
            .await?;
        Ok(match shown {
            Some((platform, size)) => GameDetails {
                platform: Some(platform),
                installation_bytes: size,
            },
            None => GameDetails::default(),
        })
    }

    /// The build a download of the game installs: the Mac build when its
    /// game runs natively on Apple silicon, else the Windows build.
    /// `cancel_download` stops it.
    pub async fn platform(
        &self,
        namespace: &str,
        catalog_item_id: &str,
        app_name: &str,
    ) -> Result<Platform, EpicError> {
        self.build_choice
            .pick(async |pick| {
                validate_identity(namespace, catalog_item_id, app_name)?;
                let pick = &pick;
                self.with_access_token(|token| async move {
                    let game = crate::details::LiveBuilds::new(
                        &self.api,
                        &token,
                        namespace,
                        catalog_item_id,
                        app_name,
                    );
                    pick.of(&game).await
                })
                .await
            })
            .await
    }

    /// Every game's playtime in seconds, by app name, in one request. A game
    /// the account never played has no entry.
    pub async fn playtimes(&self) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, u64>, EpicError> {
        let account_id = self.credentials().await?.account_id;
        let account_id = account_id.as_str();
        self.with_access_token(
            |token| async move { playtimes(&self.api, &token, account_id).await },
        )
        .await
    }

    pub(crate) fn from_session(api: Api, session: Session) -> Self {
        let social = crate::social::SocialService::new(session.credentials.account_id.clone());
        Self {
            downloads: download::Downloads::default(),
            api,
            session: Arc::new(Mutex::new(Some(session))),
            credential_events: Revisions::new(),
            social,
            installation_sizes: Default::default(),
            build_choice: Default::default(),
        }
    }

    async fn access_token(&self, rejected: Option<&str>) -> Result<String, EpicError> {
        self.social_auth().access_token(rejected).await
    }

    /// Runs `operation` with a current access token. When Epic rejects that
    /// token, it is refreshed once and the operation runs again. A result
    /// computed for a session the account discarded while the request was in
    /// flight is never returned: sign-out clears the session concurrently.
    pub(crate) async fn with_access_token<T, Fut>(
        &self,
        operation: impl Fn(String) -> Fut,
    ) -> Result<T, EpicError>
    where
        Fut: Future<Output = Result<T, EpicError>>,
    {
        let token = self.access_token(None).await?;
        let result = match operation(token.clone()).await {
            Err(EpicError::Unauthorized) => {
                let token = self.access_token(Some(&token)).await?;
                operation(token).await
            }
            result => result,
        };
        if self.session.lock().await.is_none() {
            return Err(EpicError::Unauthorized);
        }
        result
    }

    /// The catalog is presentation data. Check the current account's paginated
    /// library before asking a content or launch service about a game.
    pub(crate) async fn ensure_owned(
        &self,
        access_token: &str,
        namespace: &str,
        catalog_item_id: &str,
        app_name: &str,
    ) -> Result<(), EpicError> {
        let owned = library_items(&self.api, access_token).await?;
        if owned.iter().any(|item| {
            item.usable()
                && item.namespace == namespace
                && item.catalog_item_id == catalog_item_id
                && item.app_name == app_name
        }) {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(EpicError::Service {
                message: "backend.epic.game_not_owned".into(),
            })
        }
    }

    fn social_auth(&self) -> SocialAuth {
        SocialAuth {
            api: self.api.clone(),
            session: self.session.clone(),
            credential_events: self.credential_events.clone(),
        }
    }

    pub fn start_friends(&self) {
        self.social.start(self.social_auth(), false, None);
    }
    /// Advertise the native game owned by this client's detached supervisor.
    /// The activity ID is the catalog PresenceId or namespace, not the app name.
    /// Stop the connection when that process exits or its account is revoked.
    pub fn start_game_presence(&self, activity: crate::friends::Activity) -> Result<(), EpicError> {
        if !activity.publishable() {
            return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
        }
        self.social.start(self.social_auth(), true, Some(activity));
        Ok(())
    }
    pub fn reconnect_friends(&self) {
        self.social.start(self.social_auth(), true, None);
    }
    pub fn stop_friends(&self) {
        self.social.stop();
    }
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub(crate) fn friends(&self) -> crate::friends::Snapshot {
        self.social.snapshot()
    }
    pub async fn next_friends(&self, after_revision: u64) -> crate::friends::Snapshot {
        self.social.next(after_revision).await
    }

    /// The revision of the credentials now, which grows with each rotation.
    pub fn credentials_revision(&self) -> u64 {
        self.credential_events.current()
    }

    /// A separate watch reports refresh immediately, even if the next HTTP request fails.
    pub async fn next_credentials_revision(&self, after_revision: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        self.credential_events.next(after_revision).await
    }

    /// Synchronous cancellation crosses UniFFI even when a Swift task is suspended.
    /// This does not revoke OAuth or affect a running content transfer.
    pub fn shutdown_observers(&self) {
        self.social.stop();
        self.credential_events.stop();
    }

    pub async fn disconnect(&self) -> Result<(), EpicError> {
        self.shutdown_observers();
        self.cancel_download();
        let session = self.session.lock().await.take();
        if let Some(session) = session {
            self.api.revoke(&session.access_token).await?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Catalog identity strings are interpolated into service URLs and hashed into
/// cache and installation paths: reject empty, oversized or NUL-bearing values.
pub(crate) fn validate_identity(
    namespace: &str,
    catalog_item_id: &str,
    app_name: &str,
) -> Result<(), EpicError> {
    if [namespace, catalog_item_id, app_name]
        .iter()
        .any(|value| value.is_empty() || value.len() > 1024 || value.contains('\0'))
    {
        return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
    }
    Ok(())
}

#[derive(Clone)]
pub(crate) struct SocialAuth {
    pub(crate) api: Api,
    session: Arc<Mutex<Option<Session>>>,
    credential_events: Revisions,
}
impl SocialAuth {
    pub(crate) async fn access_token(&self, rejected: Option<&str>) -> Result<String, EpicError> {
        // The renewing task owns the refresh, not the caller awaiting it. Social
        // reconnection may cancel that caller after Epic has already rotated the token.
        // Dropping a JoinHandle detaches it; the bounded OAuth request still publishes
        // credentials, and concurrent consumers reuse the session under the same lock.
        let auth = self.clone();
        let rejected = rejected.map(str::to_owned);
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            let mut guard = auth.session.lock().await;
            let session = guard.as_mut().ok_or(EpicError::Unauthorized)?;
            if session.expires_at <= Instant::now()
                || rejected.as_deref() == Some(&session.access_token)
            {
                *session = auth.api.refresh(&session.credentials).await?;
                auth.credential_events.advance();
            }
            Ok(session.access_token.clone())
        })
        .await
        .map_err(|_| EpicError::Cancelled)?
    }

    pub(crate) async fn expires_at(&self) -> Result<Instant, EpicError> {
        self.session
            .lock()
            .await
            .as_ref()
            .map(|s| s.expires_at)
            .ok_or(EpicError::Unauthorized)
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
struct LibraryItem {
    #[serde(default)]
    app_name: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    namespace: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    catalog_item_id: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    sandbox_type: String,
    /// The record as Epic returned it.
    #[serde(skip)]
    raw: serde_json::Value,
}

impl LibraryItem {
    fn parse(raw: serde_json::Value) -> Result<Self, EpicError> {
        let mut item = Self::deserialize(&raw).map_err(|_| EpicError::Protocol)?;
        item.raw = raw;
        Ok(item)
    }

    fn usable(&self) -> bool {
        !self.app_name.is_empty()
            && self.app_name != "1"
            && !self.namespace.is_empty()
            && self.namespace != "ue"
            && !self.catalog_item_id.is_empty()
            && self.sandbox_type != "PRIVATE"
    }
    fn key(&self) -> (String, String, String) {
        (
            self.namespace.clone(),
            self.catalog_item_id.clone(),
            self.app_name.clone(),
        )
    }
}

async fn library(api: &Api, access_token: &str) -> Result<Vec<Game>, EpicError> {
    let (windows_label, mac_label) = (
        PLATFORM.name(Platform::Windows),
        PLATFORM.name(Platform::Mac),
    );
    let (owned, windows, macos) = tokio::try_join!(
        library_items(api, access_token),
        assets(api, access_token, windows_label),
        assets(api, access_token, mac_label),
    )?;
    let excluded: HashSet<_> = owned
        .iter()
        .filter(|item| !item.usable())
        .map(LibraryItem::key)
        .collect();
    let windows_keys: HashSet<_> = windows.iter().map(LibraryItem::key).collect();
    let macos_keys: HashSet<_> = macos.iter().map(LibraryItem::key).collect();
    let mut items = BTreeMap::new();
    // Every record Epic returned for each game, by where it came from.
    let mut sources: BTreeMap<(String, String), BTreeMap<&str, Vec<serde_json::Value>>> =
        BTreeMap::new();
    let tagged = (owned.into_iter().map(|item| ("library", item)))
        .chain(windows.into_iter().map(|item| (windows_label, item)))
        .chain(macos.into_iter().map(|item| (mac_label, item)));
    for (source, mut item) in tagged {
        if item.usable() && !excluded.contains(&item.key()) {
            let records = sources
                .entry((item.namespace.clone(), item.app_name.clone()))
                .or_default()
                .entry(source)
                .or_default();
            // `sources` keeps the record: nothing reads it from the item again.
            let raw = std::mem::take(&mut item.raw);
            if !records.contains(&raw) {
                records.push(raw);
            }
            items.insert(item.key(), item);
        }
    }
    let mut namespaces: BTreeMap<String, HashSet<String>> = BTreeMap::new();
    for item in items.values() {
        namespaces
            .entry(item.namespace.clone())
            .or_default()
            .insert(item.catalog_item_id.clone());
    }
    let mut requests = Vec::new();
    for (namespace, ids) in namespaces {
        let mut ids: Vec<_> = ids.into_iter().collect();
        ids.sort();
        for batch in ids.chunks(50) {
            requests.push((namespace.clone(), batch.to_vec()));
        }
    }
    let metadata: Vec<_> = stream::iter(requests)
        .map(|(namespace, ids)| async move {
            let mut url = endpoint(
                &api.catalog,
                &[
                    "catalog",
                    "api",
                    "shared",
                    "namespace",
                    &namespace,
                    "bulk",
                    "items",
                ],
            )?;
            {
                let mut query = url.query_pairs_mut();
                query
                    .append_pair("includeDLCDetails", "true")
                    .append_pair("includeMainGameDetails", "true")
                    .append_pair("country", "US")
                    .append_pair("locale", "en");
                for id in ids {
                    query.append_pair("id", &id);
                }
            }
            let result: BTreeMap<String, serde_json::Value> = api.get(url, access_token).await?;
            let result = result
                .into_iter()
                .map(|(id, raw)| {
                    let item = CatalogItem::deserialize(&raw).map_err(|_| EpicError::Protocol)?;
                    Ok((id, (item, raw)))
                })
                .collect::<Result<BTreeMap<_, _>, EpicError>>()?;
            Ok::<_, EpicError>((namespace, result))
        })
        .buffer_unordered(6)
        .try_collect()
        .await?;
    let metadata: BTreeMap<_, _> = metadata
        .into_iter()
        .flat_map(|(namespace, catalog)| {
            catalog
                .into_iter()
                .map(move |(id, item)| ((namespace.clone(), id), item))
        })
        .collect();

    let mut games: BTreeMap<(String, String), Game> = BTreeMap::new();
    for (key, item) in items {
        let entry = metadata.get(&(item.namespace.clone(), item.catalog_item_id.clone()));
        let details = entry.map(|(details, _)| details);
        if details.is_some_and(|details| {
            details.main_game_item.is_some()
                || details.categories.iter().any(|category| {
                    matches!(
                        category.path.as_str(),
                        "mods" | "assets" | "plugins" | "projects" | "asset-format"
                    ) || category.path.starts_with("asset-format/")
                })
        }) {
            continue;
        }
        let mut windows = windows_keys.contains(&key);
        let mut macos = macos_keys.contains(&key);
        if let Some(details) = details {
            for release in &details.release_info {
                if release.app_id.is_empty() || release.app_id == item.app_name {
                    windows |= release
                        .platform
                        .iter()
                        .any(|platform| matches!(platform.as_str(), "Windows" | "Win32"));
                    macos |= release
                        .platform
                        .iter()
                        .any(|platform| matches!(platform.as_str(), "Mac" | "MacOS"));
                }
            }
            // Do not list mobile-only entries as desktop games. An empty
            // platform list is unknown and keeps older third-party titles.
            if !windows
                && !macos
                && details
                    .release_info
                    .iter()
                    .any(|release| !release.platform.is_empty())
            {
                continue;
            }
        }
        let metadata = game_metadata(
            &item,
            entry.map(|(_, raw)| raw),
            sources.get(&(item.namespace.clone(), item.app_name.clone())),
        );
        let game = Game {
            title: details
                .map(|details| details.title.as_str())
                .filter(|title| !title.is_empty())
                .unwrap_or(&item.app_name)
                .to_owned(),
            description: details
                .map(|details| details.description.clone())
                .unwrap_or_default(),
            developer: details
                .map(|details| details.developer.clone())
                .unwrap_or_default(),
            image_url: details.and_then(catalog_image),
            header_image_url: details.and_then(catalog_header_image),
            added_at: added_at(&metadata),
            metadata,
            app_name: item.app_name,
            namespace: item.namespace,
            catalog_item_id: item.catalog_item_id,
            windows,
            macos,
        };
        let identity = (game.namespace.clone(), game.app_name.clone());
        if let Some(existing) = games.get_mut(&identity) {
            existing.windows |= game.windows;
            existing.macos |= game.macos;
            if existing.title == existing.app_name && game.title != game.app_name {
                existing.title = game.title;
                existing.catalog_item_id = game.catalog_item_id;
            }
            if existing.description.is_empty() {
                existing.description = game.description;
            }
            if existing.developer.is_empty() {
                existing.developer = game.developer;
            }
            if existing.image_url.is_none() {
                existing.image_url = game.image_url;
            }
            if existing.header_image_url.is_none() {
                existing.header_image_url = game.header_image_url;
            }
            existing.added_at = existing.added_at.into_iter().chain(game.added_at).min();
            // Each catalog item of the game, under its own ID.
            if let (Some(all), Some(added)) = (
                existing.metadata["catalogItems"].as_object_mut(),
                game.metadata["catalogItems"].as_object(),
            ) {
                for (id, raw) in added {
                    all.entry(id.clone()).or_insert_with(|| raw.clone());
                }
            }
        } else {
            games.insert(identity, game);
        }
    }
    let mut games: Vec<_> = games.into_values().collect();
    games.sort_by_cached_key(|game| (game.title.to_lowercase(), game.app_name.clone()));
    Ok(games)
}

/// Everything Epic returned for a game: its catalog item, its library records
/// and its assets by platform.
fn game_metadata(
    item: &LibraryItem,
    catalog: Option<&serde_json::Value>,
    sources: Option<&BTreeMap<&str, Vec<serde_json::Value>>>,
) -> serde_json::Value {
    let records = |source: &str| {
        sources
            .and_then(|sources| sources.get(source))
            .cloned()
            .unwrap_or_default()
    };
    let mut catalog_items = serde_json::Map::new();
    if let Some(catalog) = catalog {
        catalog_items.insert(item.catalog_item_id.clone(), catalog.clone());
    }
    serde_json::json!({
        "catalogItems": catalog_items,
        "libraryRecords": records("library"),
        "assets": { "Windows": records("Windows"), "Mac": records("Mac") },
    })
}

/// When a game joined the account's library: its oldest library record's
/// acquisition, in seconds since the Unix epoch.
fn added_at(metadata: &serde_json::Value) -> Option<u64> {
    metadata["libraryRecords"]
        .as_array()?
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|record| record["acquisitionDate"].as_str())
        .filter_map(obelisk_core::date::unix_seconds)
        .min()
}

fn catalog_image(item: &CatalogItem) -> Option<String> {
    catalog_image_by_kind(
        item,
        &[
            "DieselGameBoxTall",
            "OfferImageTall",
            "DieselStoreFrontTall",
            "Thumbnail",
            "DieselGameBox",
            "OfferImageWide",
        ],
    )
}

fn catalog_header_image(item: &CatalogItem) -> Option<String> {
    catalog_image_by_kind(
        item,
        &[
            "DieselStoreFrontWide",
            "OfferImageWide",
            "DieselGameBox",
            "productFeatured",
            "Thumbnail",
        ],
    )
}

fn catalog_image_by_kind(item: &CatalogItem, kinds: &[&str]) -> Option<String> {
    kinds
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|kind| {
            item.key_images
                .iter()
                .filter(move |image| image.kind == *kind)
        })
        .find_map(|image| auth::safe_https_url(image.url.clone()))
}

async fn library_items(api: &Api, access_token: &str) -> Result<Vec<LibraryItem>, EpicError> {
    let mut cursor: Option<String> = None;
    let mut cursors = HashSet::new();
    let mut records = Vec::new();
    for _ in 0..MAX_LIBRARY_PAGES {
        let mut url = endpoint(&api.library, &["library", "api", "public", "items"])?;
        url.query_pairs_mut().append_pair("includeMetadata", "true");
        if let Some(cursor) = &cursor {
            url.query_pairs_mut().append_pair("cursor", cursor);
        }
        let page: LibraryPage = api.get(url, access_token).await?;
        let page_records = page
            .records
            .into_iter()
            .map(LibraryItem::parse)
            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
        if page_records.iter().any(|item| {
            !item.app_name.is_empty()
                && (item.namespace.is_empty() || item.catalog_item_id.is_empty())
        }) {
            return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
        }
        records.extend(page_records);
        if records.len() > MAX_LIBRARY_RECORDS {
            return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
        }
        cursor = page
            .response_metadata
            .next_cursor
            .filter(|cursor| !cursor.is_empty());
        match &cursor {
            None => return Ok(records),
            Some(cursor) if cursor.len() > 8192 || !cursors.insert(cursor.clone()) => {
                return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    Err(EpicError::Protocol)
}

async fn assets(
    api: &Api,
    access_token: &str,
    platform: &str,
) -> Result<Vec<LibraryItem>, EpicError> {
    let mut url = endpoint(
        &api.launcher,
        &["launcher", "api", "public", "assets", platform],
    )?;
    url.query_pairs_mut().append_pair("label", "Live");
    let assets: Vec<serde_json::Value> = api.get(url, access_token).await?;
    assets.into_iter().map(LibraryItem::parse).collect()
}

fn endpoint(base: &str, segments: &[&str]) -> Result<Url, EpicError> {
    let mut url = Url::parse(base).map_err(|_| EpicError::Protocol)?;
    url.path_segments_mut()
        .map_err(|_| EpicError::Protocol)?
        .clear()
        .extend(segments.iter().copied());
    Ok(url)
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
struct PlaytimeItem {
    account_id: String,
    artifact_id: String,
    total_time: u64,
}

/// The account's playtime of every game it played, by app name.
async fn playtimes(
    api: &Api,
    access_token: &str,
    account_id: &str,
) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, u64>, EpicError> {
    let url = endpoint(
        &api.library,
        &[
            "library", "api", "public", "playtime", "account", account_id, "all",
        ],
    )?;
    let records: Vec<PlaytimeItem> = api.get(url, access_token).await?;
    Ok(records
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|record| record.account_id == account_id)
        .map(|record| (record.artifact_id, record.total_time))
        .collect())
}
```

```rs
    name: String,
    hidden: bool,
    unlocked_display_name: Option<String>,
    locked_display_name: Option<String>,
    unlocked_description: Option<String>,
    locked_description: Option<String>,
    unlocked_icon_link: Option<String>,
    locked_icon_link: Option<String>,
}
#[derive(Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
struct PlayerRecord {
    player_achievements: Vec<UnlockRecord>,
}
#[derive(Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
struct UnlockRecord {
    player_achievement: Unlock,
}
#[derive(Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
struct Unlock {
    sandbox_id: String,
    epic_account_id: String,
    achievement_name: String,
    unlocked: bool,
    unlock_date: Option<String>,
}

impl Client {
    pub async fn achievements(
        &self,
        namespace: &str,
        locale: &str,
    ) -> Result<Vec<Achievement>, EpicError> {
        let account = self.credentials().await?.account_id;
        let account = account.as_str();
        self.with_access_token(|token| async move {
            let response = query(
                &self.api,
                &token,
                DEFINITIONS,
                json!({"sandboxId":namespace,"locale":locale}),
            )
            .await?;
            let product = product(response, namespace)?;
            let Some(product) = product else {
                return Ok(Vec::new());
            };
            let response = query(
                &self.api,
                &token,
                PLAYER,
                json!({"sandboxId":namespace,"epicAccountId":account}),
            )
            .await?;
            combine(product, response, account)
        })
        .await
    }
}

async fn query(api: &Api, token: &str, query: &str, variables: Value) -> Result<Value, EpicError> {
    let value: Value = api
        .post_json(
            format!("{}/graphql", api.store),
            token,
            LAUNCHER_AGENT,
            &json!({"query":query,"variables":variables}),
        )
        .await?;
    // GraphQL can report denied or partial results with HTTP 200. Never show
    // these as zero unlocked achievements, nor log provider messages/tokens.
    if value
        .get("errors")
        .is_some_and(|errors| !errors.as_array().is_some_and(Vec::is_empty))
    {
        return Err(EpicError::Service {
            message: "backend.epic.achievements_unavailable".into(),
        });
    }
    Ok(value)
}

fn product(mut value: Value, namespace: &str) -> Result<Option<Product>, EpicError> {
    let record = value
        .pointer_mut("/data/Achievement/productAchievementsRecordBySandbox")
        .ok_or(EpicError::Protocol)?;
    // A game without achievements has a record whose fields are all null.
    if record.is_null() || record.get("achievements").is_some_and(Value::is_null) {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    let product: Product =
        serde_json::from_value(record.take()).map_err(|_| EpicError::Protocol)?;
    if product.sandbox_id != namespace || product.total_achievements != product.achievements.len() {
        return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
    }
    if product.achievements.is_empty() {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    Ok(Some(product))
}

fn combine(
    product: Product,
    mut value: Value,
    account: &str,
) -> Result<Vec<Achievement>, EpicError> {
    let records = value
        .pointer_mut("/data/PlayerAchievement/playerAchievementGameRecordsBySandbox/records")
        .ok_or(EpicError::Protocol)?;
    let records: Vec<PlayerRecord> =
        serde_json::from_value(records.take()).map_err(|_| EpicError::Protocol)?;
    // Same keyed join as the Steam side, which also hashes rather than orders.
    let mut unlocked = HashMap::new();
    for record in records {
        for record in record.player_achievements {
            let state = record.player_achievement;
            if state.sandbox_id != product.sandbox_id
                || state.epic_account_id != account
                || unlocked
                    .insert(state.achievement_name.clone(), state)
                    .is_some()
            {
                return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
            }
        }
    }
    let mut ids = HashSet::new();
    let mut result = Vec::new();
    for record in product.achievements {
        let definition = record.achievement;
        let id = definition.name;
        if id.is_empty() || !ids.insert(id.clone()) {
            return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
        }
        // Only an unlocked record carries a date, so drop the others here and
        // let the rest of the loop read `earned` off the remaining state.
        let state = unlocked.remove(&id).filter(|state| state.unlocked);
        let earned = state.is_some();
        let (name, description, icon) = if earned {
            (
                definition.unlocked_display_name,
                definition.unlocked_description,
                definition.unlocked_icon_link,
            )
        } else {
            (
                definition.locked_display_name,
                definition.locked_description,
                definition.locked_icon_link,
            )
        };
        // A hidden achievement the account has not earned exposes its identity
        // and nothing else, so its display text and icon are never resolved.
        let hidden = definition.hidden && !earned;
        let (name, description, icon_url) = if hidden {
            (String::new(), String::new(), String::new())
        } else {
            (
                name.filter(|name| !name.is_empty()).unwrap_or(id.clone()),
                description.unwrap_or_default(),
                icon.and_then(auth::safe_https_url).unwrap_or_default(),
            )
        };
        result.push(Achievement {
            id,
            name,
            description,
            icon_url,
            hidden,
            unlocked: earned,
            unlock_date: state.and_then(|state| state.unlock_date),
        });
    }
    if !unlocked.is_empty() {
        return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
    }
    result.sort_by(|a, b| {
        b.unlocked
            .cmp(&a.unlocked)
            .then_with(|| b.unlock_date.cmp(&a.unlock_date))
            .then_with(|| a.id.cmp(&b.id))
    });
    Ok(result)
}
```

`crates/storefronts/epic-kit/src/client/cloud_api.rs`:

```rs
//! Account-fenced EGS Cloud transport. Each metadata request refreshes OAuth
//! independently; a rejected token never replays a complete upload transaction.
use std::{
    collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet},
    time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH},
};

use obelisk_core::{
    Platform,
    install::hex,
    transfer::{CancelToken, Window},
};
use reqwest::Url;
use serde::Deserialize;
use sha1::{Digest, Sha1};

use super::{Client, endpoint, validate_identity};
use crate::{
    EpicError,
    auth::{bounded_bytes, check_status, credential_free},
    cloud::{CloudGame, CloudListing, CloudRules, codec, identity, relative_path},
    content,
    content_manifest::{Chunk, ChunkGuid},
};

const MAX_METADATA_BYTES: usize = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
const MAX_CHUNK_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024 * 1024 + 98;
// The service has been observed to truncate at 1000 entries. Until pagination is
// established, a full page is ambiguous and must never be treated as complete.
const INVENTORY_LIMIT: usize = 1000;
const LINK_BATCH: usize = 100;
// Chunks are 1 MiB, so a large save is hundreds of round trips. Signed-link
// transfers carry no Authorization and no ordering, so they overlap freely.
const TRANSFERS: Window = Window {
    width: 8,
    bytes: u64::MAX,
};

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
struct Entry {
    #[serde(default, deserialize_with = "nullable_metadata")]
    hash: String,
    #[serde(default, deserialize_with = "nullable_metadata")]
    last_modified: String,
    read_link: Option<String>,
    write_link: Option<String>,
}

// Link responses legitimately contain null revision metadata. Inventories still
// require both nonempty values in list(); other JSON scalar types remain invalid.
fn nullable_metadata<'de, D: serde::Deserializer<'de>>(
    deserializer: D,
) -> Result<String, D::Error> {
    Option::<String>::deserialize(deserializer).map(Option::unwrap_or_default)
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
struct Listing {
    #[serde(deserialize_with = "unique_entries")]
    files: BTreeMap<String, Entry>,
    #[serde(default)]
    next_cursor: Option<serde_json::Value>,
    #[serde(default)]
    has_more: bool,
}

fn unique_entries<'de, D: serde::Deserializer<'de>>(
    deserializer: D,
) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, Entry>, D::Error> {
    struct Entries;
    impl<'de> serde::de::Visitor<'de> for Entries {
        type Value = BTreeMap<String, Entry>;
        fn expecting(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
            f.write_str("unique cloud file paths")
        }
        fn visit_map<M: serde::de::MapAccess<'de>>(
            self,
            mut map: M,
        ) -> Result<Self::Value, M::Error> {
            let mut files = BTreeMap::new();
            while let Some((name, entry)) = map.next_entry::<String, Entry>()? {
                if files.len() >= INVENTORY_LIMIT || files.insert(name, entry).is_some() {
                    return Err(serde::de::Error::custom(
                        "duplicate or excessive cloud files",
                    ));
                }
            }
            Ok(files)
        }
    }
    deserializer.deserialize_map(Entries)
}

impl Client {
    pub async fn cloud_configuration(
        &self,
        namespace: &str,
        catalog_item_id: &str,
        app_name: &str,
        platform: Platform,
    ) -> Result<Option<CloudRules>, EpicError> {
        validate_identity(namespace, catalog_item_id, app_name)?;
        #[derive(Deserialize)]
        #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
        struct Catalog {
            #[serde(default)]
            custom_attributes: BTreeMap<String, serde_json::Value>,
        }
        self.with_access_token(|token| async move {
            self.ensure_owned(&token, namespace, catalog_item_id, app_name)
                .await?;
            let mut url = endpoint(
                &self.api.catalog,
                &[
                    "catalog",
                    "api",
                    "shared",
                    "namespace",
                    namespace,
                    "bulk",
                    "items",
                ],
            )?;
            url.query_pairs_mut()
                .append_pair("id", catalog_item_id)
                .append_pair("includeDLCDetails", "true")
                .append_pair("includeMainGameDetails", "true")
                .append_pair("country", "US")
                .append_pair("locale", "en");
            let mut catalog: BTreeMap<String, Catalog> = self.api.get(url, &token).await?;
            let item = catalog.remove(catalog_item_id).ok_or(EpicError::Protocol)?;
            CloudRules::from_attributes(&item.custom_attributes, platform)
        })
        .await
    }

    /// Lists the inventory and reads its latest manifest. An empty inventory
    /// and a valid empty manifest are supported; malformed or incomplete data
    /// is an error.
    pub async fn cloud_list(
        &self,
        game: CloudGame<'_>,
        cancel: &CancelToken,
    ) -> Result<CloudListing, EpicError> {
        let account = self.credentials().await?.account_id;
        let cloud = Cloud {
            client: self,
            game,
            account: &account,
            cancel,
        };
        cloud.authorize().await?;
        let inventory = cloud.list().await?;
        cloud.listing(&inventory).await
    }

    /// The inventory's revision now, for the account `listing` was read for.
    pub async fn cloud_revision(
        &self,
        game: CloudGame<'_>,
        listing: &CloudListing,
        cancel: &CancelToken,
    ) -> Result<String, EpicError> {
        let cloud = Cloud {
            client: self,
            game,
            account: &listing.account,
            cancel,
        };
        cloud.validate()?;
        let revision = cloud.revision(&cloud.list().await?);
        cloud.fence().await?;
        Ok(revision)
    }

    /// Reads `names` of `listing`'s generation: only the chunks they use, in
    /// one window across link batches, each file checked against its SHA-1.
    pub async fn cloud_fetch(
        &self,
        game: CloudGame<'_>,
        listing: &CloudListing,
        names: &BTreeSet<String>,
        cancel: &CancelToken,
    ) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, Vec<u8>>, EpicError> {
        let cloud = Cloud {
            client: self,
            game,
            account: &listing.account,
            cancel,
        };
        cloud.validate()?;
        cloud.fetch(listing, Some(names)).await
    }

    /// Optimistic publication: unchanged baseline, complete chunk upload,
    /// manifest last, full readback, then stable inventory. EGS exposes no proven
    /// atomic compare-and-swap: another client can still race between checks.
    /// Returns the complete listing that confirmed it.
    pub async fn cloud_upload(
        &self,
        game: CloudGame<'_>,
        rules: &CloudRules,
        files: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<u8>>,
        expected_revision: &str,
        cancel: &CancelToken,
    ) -> Result<CloudListing, EpicError> {
        let account = self.credentials().await?.account_id;
        let cloud = Cloud {
            client: self,
            game,
            account: &account,
            cancel,
        };
        cloud.authorize().await?;
        let before = cloud.list().await?;
        if cloud.revision(&before) != expected_revision {
            return Err(EpicError::CloudConflict);
        }
        let now = SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
            .map_err(|_| EpicError::Protocol)?
            .as_secs();
        let latest = before
            .keys()
            .map(|name| codec::manifest_time(name))
            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?
            .into_iter()
            .max()
            .unwrap_or(0);
        // Avoid reusing a second-resolution manifest name, without silently
        // accepting a remote clock far in the future.
        if latest > now.saturating_add(300) {
            return Err(EpicError::CloudConflict);
        }
        let seconds = now.max(latest.saturating_add(1));
        cancel.check()?;
        let mut package = codec::package(game, &account, rules, files, seconds, cancel)?;
        let chunks = std::mem::take(&mut package.chunks);
        let batches = Batch::split(chunks.keys().cloned().collect());
        TRANSFERS
            .run(
                chunks.into_iter().enumerate(),
                |(_, (_, chunk))| chunk.len() as u64,
                || cancel.check().map_err(EpicError::from),
                |(index, (name, chunk))| {
                    let batch = &batches[index / LINK_BATCH];
                    let cloud = &cloud;
                    async move {
                        let links = batch.links(cloud).await?;
                        let link = links
                            .get(&name)
                            .and_then(|entry| entry.write_link.as_deref())
                            .ok_or(EpicError::Protocol)?;
                        cloud.put(link, chunk).await
                    }
                },
                |()| Ok(()),
            )
            .await?;
        // Request the manifest link only after every chunk PUT succeeds.
        // Content integrity is established by the complete readback below.
        if cloud.revision(&cloud.list().await?) != expected_revision {
            return Err(EpicError::CloudConflict);
        }
        let links = cloud
            .links(std::slice::from_ref(&package.manifest_path))
            .await?;
        let link = links
            .get(&package.manifest_path)
            .and_then(|entry| entry.write_link.as_deref())
            .ok_or(EpicError::Protocol)?;
        cloud
            .put(link, std::mem::take(&mut package.manifest))
            .await?;
        let after = cloud.list().await?;
        if !after.contains_key(&package.manifest_path)
            || cloud.revision_excluding(&after, &package.manifest_path) != expected_revision
        {
            return Err(EpicError::CloudConflict);
        }
        if latest_manifest(&after)?.map(|(name, _)| name) != Some(package.manifest_path.as_str()) {
            return Err(EpicError::CloudConflict);
        }
        let listing = cloud.listing(&after).await?;
        if cloud.fetch(&listing, None).await? != *files {
            return Err(EpicError::Integrity);
        }
        if cloud.revision(&cloud.list().await?) != listing.revision() {
            return Err(EpicError::CloudConflict);
        }
        cloud.fence().await?;
        Ok(listing)
    }
}

struct Cloud<'a> {
    client: &'a Client,
    game: CloudGame<'a>,
    account: &'a str,
    cancel: &'a CancelToken,
}

impl Cloud<'_> {
    fn revision(&self, listing: &BTreeMap<String, Entry>) -> String {
        revision(listing, self.game.app_name, self.account)
    }

    /// The revision the listing would have without `skip`, without copying it.
    fn revision_excluding(&self, listing: &BTreeMap<String, Entry>, skip: &str) -> String {
        revision(
            listing.iter().filter(|(name, _)| name.as_str() != skip),
            self.game.app_name,
            self.account,
        )
    }

    fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), EpicError> {
        self.cancel.check()?;
        self.game.validate()?;
        identity(self.account)
    }

    async fn authorize(&self) -> Result<(), EpicError> {
        self.validate()?;
        self.fence().await?;
        self.cancel
            .race(self.client.with_access_token(|token| async move {
                self.client
                    .ensure_owned(
                        &token,
                        self.game.namespace,
                        self.game.catalog_item_id,
                        self.game.app_name,
                    )
                    .await
            }))
            .await??;
        self.fence().await
    }

    async fn fence(&self) -> Result<(), EpicError> {
        self.cancel.check()?;
        if self.client.credentials().await?.account_id != self.account {
            return Err(EpicError::Unauthorized);
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn url(&self, manifests: bool) -> Result<Url, EpicError> {
        let mut segments = vec![
            "api",
            "v1",
            "access",
            "egstore",
            "savesync",
            self.account,
            self.game.app_name,
        ];
        if manifests {
            segments.push("manifests");
        }
        segments.push("");
        endpoint(&self.client.api.cloud, &segments)
    }

    async fn metadata(
        &self,
        names: Option<&[String]>,
    ) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, Entry>, EpicError> {
        self.fence().await?;
        let listing = self
            .cancel
            .race(self.client.with_access_token(|token| async move {
                let url = self.url(names.is_none())?;
                let request = match names {
                    Some(names) => self
                        .client
                        .api
                        .http
                        .post(url)
                        .json(&serde_json::json!({"files": names})),
                    None => self.client.api.http.get(url),
                }
                .bearer_auth(token);
                let response = request.send().await.map_err(|_| EpicError::Network)?;
                check_status(response.status())?;
                let bytes = bounded_bytes(response, MAX_METADATA_BYTES).await?;
                serde_json::from_slice::<Listing>(&bytes).map_err(|_| EpicError::Protocol)
            }))
            .await??;
        self.fence().await?;
        if listing.has_more
            || listing.next_cursor.is_some()
            || listing.files.len() >= INVENTORY_LIMIT
        {
            return Err(EpicError::UnsupportedContent);
        }
        let prefix = format!("savesync/{}/{}/", self.account, self.game.app_name);
        let mut result = BTreeMap::new();
        for (name, entry) in listing.files {
            let relative = name.strip_prefix(&prefix).unwrap_or(&name);
            relative_path(relative)?;
            if entry.hash.len() > 1024 || entry.last_modified.len() > 128 {
                return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
            }
            if result.insert(relative.to_owned(), entry).is_some() {
                return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
            }
        }
        Ok(result)
    }

    async fn list(&self) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, Entry>, EpicError> {
        let files = self.metadata(None).await?;
        for (name, entry) in &files {
            codec::manifest_time(name)?;
            if entry.hash.is_empty() || entry.last_modified.is_empty() {
                return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
            }
        }
        Ok(files)
    }

    async fn links(&self, names: &[String]) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, Entry>, EpicError> {
        if names.is_empty() || names.len() > LINK_BATCH {
            return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
        }
        let result = self.metadata(Some(names)).await?;
        if result.keys().collect::<BTreeSet<_>>() != names.iter().collect() {
            return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
        }
        Ok(result)
    }

    async fn get(&self, link: &str, limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>, EpicError> {
        self.fence().await?;
        let url = signed_url(link)?;
        let bytes = self
            .cancel
            .race(async {
                // Api's client has no default Authorization and refuses redirects.
                let response = self
                    .client
                    .api
                    .http
                    .get(url)
                    .send()
                    .await
                    .map_err(|_| EpicError::Network)?;
                if !response.status().is_success() {
                    return Err(EpicError::Http(response.status().as_u16()));
                }
                bounded_bytes(response, limit).await
            })
            .await??;
        self.fence().await?;
        Ok(bytes)
    }

    async fn put(&self, link: &str, bytes: Vec<u8>) -> Result<(), EpicError> {
        self.fence().await?;
        let url = signed_url(link)?;
        self.cancel
            .race(async {
                let response = self
                    .client
                    .api
                    .http
                    .put(url)
                    .header(reqwest::header::CONTENT_TYPE, "application/octet-stream")
                    .body(bytes)
                    .send()
                    .await
                    .map_err(|_| EpicError::Network)?;
                if !response.status().is_success() {
                    return Err(EpicError::Http(response.status().as_u16()));
                }
                Ok(())
            })
            .await??;
        self.fence().await
    }

    /// The generation `inventory` names: its latest manifest, read and parsed.
    async fn listing(
        &self,
        inventory: &BTreeMap<String, Entry>,
    ) -> Result<CloudListing, EpicError> {
        let revision = self.revision(inventory);
        let Some((_, entry)) = latest_manifest(inventory)? else {
            return Ok(CloudListing::read(revision, self.account.into(), None));
        };
        let bytes = self
            .get(
                entry.read_link.as_deref().ok_or(EpicError::Protocol)?,
                codec::MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES,
            )
            .await?;
        let manifest = codec::parse(&bytes, self.game, self.account)?;
        Ok(CloudListing::read(
            revision,
            self.account.into(),
            Some(manifest),
        ))
    }

    /// Reads `names` of `listing`'s generation, or every file when `None`.
    /// Only the chunks those files use are downloaded; every chunk when `None`.
    async fn fetch(
        &self,
        listing: &CloudListing,
        names: Option<&BTreeSet<String>>,
    ) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, Vec<u8>>, EpicError> {
        if names.is_some_and(|names| names.iter().any(|name| !listing.lists(name))) {
            return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
        }
        let Some(manifest) = listing.manifest.clone() else {
            // Only an empty inventory has no manifest to read chunks from.
            return match listing.files().next() {
                None => Ok(BTreeMap::new()),
                Some(_) => Err(EpicError::Protocol),
            };
        };
        let used: Option<BTreeSet<ChunkGuid>> = names.map(|names| {
            manifest
                .files
                .iter()
                .filter(|file| names.contains(&file.filename))
                .flat_map(|file| file.parts.iter().map(|part| part.guid))
                .collect()
        });
        let chunks: Vec<(String, &Chunk)> = manifest
            .chunks
            .values()
            .filter(|chunk| used.as_ref().is_none_or(|used| used.contains(&chunk.guid)))
            .map(|chunk| (chunk.relative_path(manifest.feature_level), chunk))
            .collect();
        let batches = Batch::split(chunks.iter().map(|(name, _)| name.clone()).collect());
        let mut decoded = BTreeMap::<ChunkGuid, Vec<u8>>::new();
        TRANSFERS
            .run(
                chunks.iter().enumerate(),
                |(_, (_, chunk))| chunk.file_size,
                || self.cancel.check().map_err(EpicError::from),
                |(index, (name, chunk))| {
                    let batch = &batches[index / LINK_BATCH];
                    async move {
                        let links = batch.links(self).await?;
                        let link = links
                            .get(name)
                            .and_then(|entry| entry.read_link.as_deref())
                            .ok_or(EpicError::Protocol)?;
                        let bytes = self
                            .get(link, MAX_CHUNK_BYTES.min(chunk.file_size as usize))
                            .await?;
                        self.cancel.check()?;
                        let guid = chunk.guid;
                        let chunk = (*chunk).clone();
                        let bytes = self
                            .cancel
                            .spawn_blocking(move || content::decode_chunk(&bytes, &chunk))
                            .await
                            .map_err(|_| EpicError::Protocol)??;
                        Ok((guid, bytes))
                    }
                },
                |(guid, bytes)| {
                    decoded.insert(guid, bytes);
                    Ok(())
                },
            )
            .await?;
        let names = names.cloned();
        let cancel = self.cancel.clone();
        self.cancel
            .spawn_blocking(move || {
                codec::reconstruct(&manifest, &decoded, names.as_ref(), &cancel)
            })
            .await
            .map_err(|_| EpicError::Protocol)?
    }
}

/// One link request's worth of objects. Its signed links are requested by the
/// first transfer that needs them, so the window refills across batches.
struct Batch {
    names: Vec<String>,
    links: tokio::sync::OnceCell<BTreeMap<String, Entry>>,
}

impl Batch {
    fn split(names: Vec<String>) -> Vec<Self> {
        names
            .chunks(LINK_BATCH)
            .map(|names| Self {
                names: names.to_vec(),
                links: tokio::sync::OnceCell::new(),
            })
            .collect()
    }

    async fn links(&self, cloud: &Cloud<'_>) -> Result<&BTreeMap<String, Entry>, EpicError> {
        self.links
            .get_or_try_init(|| cloud.links(&self.names))
            .await
    }
}

fn latest_manifest(listing: &BTreeMap<String, Entry>) -> Result<Option<(&str, &Entry)>, EpicError> {
    let mut latest = None;
    for (name, entry) in listing {
        let time = codec::manifest_time(name)?;
        if latest.is_none_or(|(previous, _, _)| time > previous) {
            latest = Some((time, name.as_str(), entry));
        }
    }
    Ok(latest.map(|(_, name, entry)| (name, entry)))
}

fn revision<'a>(
    listing: impl IntoIterator<Item = (&'a String, &'a Entry)>,
    app: &str,
    account: &str,
) -> String {
    let mut hash = Sha1::new();
    for value in [app, account] {
        hash.update((value.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
        hash.update(value.as_bytes());
    }
    for (name, entry) in listing {
        for value in [
            name.as_str(),
            entry.hash.as_str(),
            entry.last_modified.as_str(),
        ] {
            hash.update((value.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
            hash.update(value.as_bytes());
        }
    }
    hex(&hash.finalize())
}

fn signed_url(link: &str) -> Result<Url, EpicError> {
    if link.len() > 32_768 {
        return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
    }
    let url = Url::parse(link).map_err(|_| EpicError::Protocol)?;
    let host = url.host_str().ok_or(EpicError::Protocol)?;
    let allowed = ["epicgames.com", "epicgames.dev", "amazonaws.com"]
        .iter()
        .any(|domain| host == *domain || host.ends_with(&format!(".{domain}")));
    #[cfg(test)]
    let allowed = allowed || url.scheme() == "http" && host == "127.0.0.1";
    #[cfg(not(test))]
    if url.scheme() != "https" {
        return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
    }
    if !allowed || !matches!(url.scheme(), "https" | "http") || !credential_free(&url) {
        return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
    }
    Ok(url)
}

mod tests;
```

```rs
use super::*;
use crate::auth::{Api, Credentials, Session};
use serde_json::{Value, json};
use std::{
    io::{Read, Write},
    net::{TcpListener, TcpStream},
    sync::{
        Arc, Mutex,
        atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering},
    },
    thread,

struct State {
    objects: BTreeMap<String, Vec<u8>>,
    requests: Vec<(String, String, bool)>,
    fail_chunk_put: bool,
    missing_link: bool,
    corrupt_chunk: bool,
    redirect_manifest: bool,
    inventory_error: bool,
    list_count: usize,
    mutate_on_list: Option<(usize, String, Vec<u8>)>,
    delay_blob_ms: u64,
    nullable_link_metadata: bool,
    invalid_link_hash: bool,
    null_listing_field: Option<&'static str>,
    /// An object whose read waits for the next link request, logged as
    /// `DONE` once answered.
    slow_object: Option<String>,
}

struct Mock {
    api: Api,
    state: Arc<Mutex<State>>,
    stop: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    handle: Option<thread::JoinHandle<()>>,
```
