`crates/storefronts/epic-kit/src/content.rs`:

```rs
//! Epic BuildPatch chunk delivery and atomic installation.
//!
//! The shared chunk engine and the blocking disk worker come from `obelisk_core`,
//! as do path confinement, locking, hashing and progress reporting.
//! Complete files and verified chunk caches survive cancellation and are reused.
mod verification;

use std::{
    collections::{HashMap, HashSet, VecDeque},
    fs::{self, File, OpenOptions},
    io::{Read, Seek, SeekFrom, Write},
    path::{Path, PathBuf},
    sync::Arc,
    time::Duration,
};

use obelisk_core::{
    install::{
        self, PARTIAL_DIRECTORY, apply_permissions, checked_file_path, ensure_directory, hex,
        safe_relative_path,
    },
    transfer::{
        self, BodyError, BodySize, CancelToken, Chunks, Delivery, DownloadPhase, DownloadProgress,
        DownloadSummary, Interrupted, Pipeline, Reporter,
    },
};
use reqwest::{Client, Url};
use sha1::{Digest, Sha1};

use crate::{
    EpicError,
    auth::credential_free,
    content_manifest::{Chunk, ChunkGuid, Manifest, ManifestFile},
};

const MAX_CHUNK_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024 * 1024;
const CHUNK_CONCURRENCY: usize = 16;
const FILE_PREFETCH: usize = 8;
const PIPELINE: Pipeline = Pipeline {
    delivery: Delivery::InOrder,
    fetches: CHUNK_CONCURRENCY,
    queue: CHUNK_CONCURRENCY,
};

#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct ContentClient {
    client: Client,
}

type ChunkResult = Result<Vec<u8>, EpicError>;

impl From<Interrupted> for EpicError {
    fn from(_: Interrupted) -> Self {
        Self::Protocol
    }
}

impl From<BodyError> for EpicError {
    fn from(error: BodyError) -> Self {
        match error {
            BodyError::Network => Self::Network,
            BodyError::Size => Self::Protocol,
            BodyError::Cancelled => Self::Cancelled,
        }
    }
}

impl ContentClient {
    pub fn new(client: Client) -> Self {
        Self { client }
    }

    pub async fn download(
        &self,
        manifest: Arc<Manifest>,
        base_urls: &[Url],
        destination: &Path,
        cancel: &CancelToken,
        progress: impl Fn(DownloadProgress) + Send + Sync + 'static,
    ) -> Result<DownloadSummary, EpicError> {
        cancel.check()?;
        validate_manifest(&manifest)?;
        check_base_urls(base_urls)?;
        let reporter = Reporter::new(
            DownloadProgress {
                phase: DownloadPhase::Verifying,
                total_bytes: manifest.files.iter().map(ManifestFile::size).sum(),
                total_files: u32::try_from(manifest.files.len())
                    .map_err(|_| EpicError::Protocol)?,
                ..Default::default()
            },
            progress,
        );
        let feature_level = manifest.feature_level;
        let disk = DiskInstall::engine_side(
            destination.to_owned(),
            manifest,
            cancel.clone(),
            Arc::clone(&reporter),
        );
        let reused_bytes = transfer::run_engine(PIPELINE, cancel, disk, |chunk| {
            self.fetch_chunk(feature_level, base_urls, chunk, cancel, &reporter)
        })
        .await?;
        Ok(reporter.summary(reused_bytes))
    }

    /// The first `bytes` of the manifest's `file`, from the chunks that hold
    /// them, without installing it.
    pub(crate) async fn read(
        &self,
        manifest: &Manifest,
        base_urls: &[Url],
        file: &ManifestFile,
        bytes: u64,
        cancel: &CancelToken,
    ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, EpicError> {
        check_base_urls(base_urls)?;
        let reporter = Reporter::new(DownloadProgress::default(), |_| {});
        let mut output = Vec::new();
        for part in &file.parts {
            if output.len() as u64 >= bytes {
                break;
            }
            let chunk = manifest
                .chunks
                .get(&part.guid)
                .ok_or(EpicError::Protocol)?
                .clone();
            let window = self
                .fetch_chunk(manifest.feature_level, base_urls, chunk, cancel, &reporter)
                .await?;
            let start = part.offset as usize;
            output.extend_from_slice(
                window
                    .get(start..start + part.size as usize)
                    .ok_or(EpicError::Protocol)?,
            );
        }
        output.truncate(usize::try_from(bytes).unwrap_or(usize::MAX));
        Ok(output)
    }

    async fn fetch_chunk(
        &self,
        feature_level: u32,
        base_urls: &[Url],
        chunk: Chunk,
        cancel: &CancelToken,
        reporter: &Reporter,
    ) -> ChunkResult {
        let mut failure = EpicError::Network;
        for base_url in base_urls {
            let mut url = base_url
                .join(&chunk.relative_path(feature_level))
                .map_err(|_| EpicError::Protocol)?;
            // Signed manifest query parameters apply to the manifest only.
            // Account authorization is never attached to CDN chunk requests.
            url.set_query(None);
            for attempt in 0..3 {
                cancel.check()?;
                reporter.update(|status| status.phase = DownloadPhase::Downloading);
                match self.fetch(&url, cancel, reporter).await {
                    Ok(bytes) => {
                        let expected = chunk.clone();
                        let received = cfg!(debug_assertions).then(|| bytes.clone());
                        match cancel
                            .spawn_blocking(move || decode_chunk(&bytes, &expected))
                            .await
                            .map_err(|_| EpicError::Protocol)?
                        {
                            Ok(bytes) => return Ok(bytes),
                            Err(error) => {
                                if let Some(received) = &received {
                                    crate::details::diagnostic::write_chunk(
                                        &url, &chunk, received, &error,
                                    );
                                }
                                if matches!(error, EpicError::UnsupportedContent) {
                                    return Err(error);
                                }
                                failure = error;
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    Err(EpicError::Cancelled) => return Err(EpicError::Cancelled),
                    Err(error @ EpicError::Http(401 | 403 | 404)) => {
                        // A rejected or absent chunk is final for this mirror,
                        // but another current delivery URL may still serve it.
                        failure = error;
                        break;
                    }
                    Err(error) => failure = error,
                }
                if attempt < 2 {
                    cancel
                        .race(tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(
                            250 * (attempt + 1),
                        )))
                        .await?;
                }
            }
        }
        Err(failure)
    }

    async fn fetch(&self, url: &Url, cancel: &CancelToken, reporter: &Reporter) -> ChunkResult {
        let response = cancel
            .race(
                self.client
                    .get(url.clone())
                    .timeout(Duration::from_secs(45))
                    .send(),
            )
            .await?
            .map_err(|_| EpicError::Network)?;
        if !response.status().is_success() {
            return Err(EpicError::Http(response.status().as_u16()));
        }
        // At most, never exactly `chunk.file_size`: that size is only an
        // estimate (see decode_chunk).
        Ok(transfer::read_body(
            response.content_length(),
            response.bytes_stream(),
            BodySize::AtMost((MAX_CHUNK_BYTES + 98) as u64),
            cancel,
            |count| {
                reporter.update(|status| {
                    status.network_bytes += count;
                    status.content_bytes += count;
                });
            },
        )
        .await?)
    }
}

struct DiskInstall {
    destination: PathBuf,
    manifest: Arc<Manifest>,
    cancel: CancelToken,
    reporter: Arc<Reporter>,
    chunks: Chunks<Chunk, Vec<u8>, EpicError>,
    prefetch: FilePrefetch,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum ChunkState {
    Cached,
    Pending,
    /// Written by this run; `verified` once read back and hashed.
    Stored {
        verified: bool,
    },
}

struct PlannedFile {
    index: usize,
    reused: HashSet<ChunkGuid>,
    // A previous file owns these queued chunks. Check their persisted bytes
    // when this file is reached, after the owner has consumed its responses.
    verify_after_delivery: HashSet<ChunkGuid>,
}

#[derive(Default)]
struct FilePrefetch {
    next_file: usize,
    files: VecDeque<PlannedFile>,
    chunks: HashMap<ChunkGuid, ChunkState>,
    pending: VecDeque<ChunkGuid>,
}

impl DiskInstall {
    /// The disk side of one engine run, from its start state.
    fn engine_side(
        destination: PathBuf,
        manifest: Arc<Manifest>,
        cancel: CancelToken,
        reporter: Arc<Reporter>,
    ) -> impl FnOnce(Chunks<Chunk, Vec<u8>, EpicError>) -> Result<u64, EpicError> + Send + 'static
    {
        move |chunks| {
            Self {
                destination,
                manifest,
                cancel,
                reporter,
                chunks,
                prefetch: FilePrefetch::default(),
            }
            .run()
        }
    }

    /// Returns the number of verified bytes reused from disk.
    fn run(mut self) -> Result<u64, EpicError> {
        self.cancel.check()?;
        fs::create_dir_all(&self.destination)?;
        let root = fs::canonicalize(&self.destination)?;
        let _lock = install::lock_engine(&root)?.ok_or(EpicError::AlreadyDownloading)?;
        let manifest = Arc::clone(&self.manifest);
        let partial_relative = PathBuf::from(PARTIAL_DIRECTORY)
            .join("epic")
            .join(manifest_key(&manifest));
        let partial_root = ensure_directory(&root, &partial_relative)?;
        let chunk_root = ensure_directory(&partial_root, Path::new("chunks"))?;
        let verified =
            verification::verify_files(&root, &manifest.files, &self.cancel, &self.reporter)?;
        let mut reused_bytes = verified.reused_bytes;
        let mut remaining_chunks = HashMap::new();
        for (file, valid) in manifest.files.iter().zip(&verified.valid) {
            if !valid {
                for part in &file.parts {
                    *remaining_chunks.entry(part.guid).or_insert(0_usize) += 1;
                }
            }
        }
        self.prefetch_files(&verified.valid, &chunk_root)?;
        // Parents are created and checked once per distinct directory; every
        // file's full path is still confined right before it is written.
        let mut ensured_parents: HashSet<PathBuf> = HashSet::new();
        for (index, (file, valid)) in manifest.files.iter().zip(&verified.valid).enumerate() {
            self.cancel.check()?;
            let relative = safe_relative_path(&file.filename)?;
            let parent = relative.parent().unwrap_or(Path::new(""));
            if !ensured_parents.contains(parent) {
                ensure_directory(&root, parent)?;
                ensured_parents.insert(parent.to_path_buf());
            }
            let target = checked_file_path(&root, &relative)?;
            if *valid {
                apply_permissions(&target, is_executable(file, &target)?)?;
                continue;
            }
            // The phase stays the network side's: chunks still arrive for
            // the files after this one.
            self.reporter
                .update(|status| status.current_file.clone_from(&file.filename));
            let plan = self.prefetch.files.pop_front().ok_or(EpicError::Protocol)?;
            if plan.index != index {
                return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
            }
            reused_bytes +=
                self.assemble(file, &plan, &partial_root, &chunk_root, &root, &relative)?;
            // A published file can be verified directly next time. Keep only
            // chunks that are still required by unfinished files.
            for part in &file.parts {
                let remaining = remaining_chunks
                    .get_mut(&part.guid)
                    .ok_or(EpicError::Protocol)?;
                *remaining -= 1;
                if *remaining == 0 {
                    let chunk = manifest.chunks.get(&part.guid).ok_or(EpicError::Protocol)?;
                    let path = checked_file_path(&chunk_root, Path::new(&chunk_key(chunk)))?;
                    fs::remove_file(path)?;
                    self.prefetch.chunks.remove(&part.guid);
                }
            }
            self.reporter.update(|status| status.completed_files += 1);
            self.prefetch_files(&verified.valid, &chunk_root)?;
        }
        self.cancel.check()?;
        // Keep caches on failure/cancellation only, avoiding a second permanent copy of the game.
        fs::remove_dir_all(partial_root)?;
        Ok(reused_bytes)
    }

    /// Keep the next few repair files queued while the current file is written
    /// and published. Requests remain in first-consumer order, including chunks
    /// shared across files, so InOrder delivery needs no reordering.
    fn prefetch_files(&mut self, valid: &[bool], chunk_root: &Path) -> Result<(), EpicError> {
        while self.prefetch.files.len() < FILE_PREFETCH
            && self.prefetch.next_file < self.manifest.files.len()
            && !self.chunks.refused()
        {
            self.cancel.check()?;
            let index = self.prefetch.next_file;
            self.prefetch.next_file += 1;
            if valid[index] {
                continue;
            }
            let mut plan = PlannedFile {
                index,
                reused: HashSet::new(),
                verify_after_delivery: HashSet::new(),
            };
            let mut seen = HashSet::new();
            for part in &self.manifest.files[index].parts {
                self.cancel.check()?;
                if !seen.insert(part.guid) {
                    continue;
                }
                match self.prefetch.chunks.get(&part.guid) {
                    Some(ChunkState::Pending) => {
                        plan.reused.insert(part.guid);
                        plan.verify_after_delivery.insert(part.guid);
                        continue;
                    }
                    // Verified on disk earlier in this run and not yet evicted;
                    // the entry is dropped with the file at every removal site.
                    Some(ChunkState::Cached | ChunkState::Stored { verified: true }) => {
                        plan.reused.insert(part.guid);
                        continue;
                    }
                    Some(ChunkState::Stored { verified: false }) | None => (),
                }
                let chunk = self
                    .manifest
                    .chunks
                    .get(&part.guid)
                    .ok_or(EpicError::Protocol)?;
                let path = checked_file_path(chunk_root, Path::new(&chunk_key(chunk)))?;
                if verify_file(
                    &path,
                    u64::from(chunk.window_size),
                    &chunk.sha1,
                    &self.cancel,
                )? {
                    self.prefetch
                        .chunks
                        .entry(part.guid)
                        .and_modify(|state| *state = ChunkState::Stored { verified: true })
                        .or_insert(ChunkState::Cached);
                    plan.reused.insert(part.guid);
                } else {
                    if !self.chunks.request(chunk.clone()) {
                        // The network side stopped and its outcome is queued
                        // ahead of this request. Keep this partial plan so
                        // assembly reaches it before any unsent chunk.
                        break;
                    }
                    self.prefetch.pending.push_back(part.guid);
                    self.prefetch.chunks.insert(part.guid, ChunkState::Pending);
                }
            }
            self.prefetch.files.push_back(plan);
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Reuses verified cached chunks, writes each fresh chunk to the cache and
    /// straight into the partial file from memory, hashes what was assembled
    /// and publishes the file atomically. Only chunks that were already on
    /// disk, or that an earlier part of this file fetched, are read back.
    fn assemble(
        &mut self,
        file: &ManifestFile,
        plan: &PlannedFile,
        partial_root: &Path,
        chunk_root: &Path,
        root: &Path,
        relative: &Path,
    ) -> Result<u64, EpicError> {
        let manifest = Arc::clone(&self.manifest);
        for guid in &plan.verify_after_delivery {
            self.cancel.check()?;
            match self.prefetch.chunks.get(guid) {
                Some(ChunkState::Stored { verified: true }) => continue,
                Some(ChunkState::Stored { verified: false }) => (),
                _ => return Err(EpicError::Protocol),
            }
            let chunk = manifest.chunks.get(guid).ok_or(EpicError::Protocol)?;
            let path = checked_file_path(chunk_root, Path::new(&chunk_key(chunk)))?;
            if !verify_file(
                &path,
                u64::from(chunk.window_size),
                &chunk.sha1,
                &self.cancel,
            )? {
                return Err(EpicError::Integrity);
            }
            self.prefetch
                .chunks
                .insert(*guid, ChunkState::Stored { verified: true });
        }
        let mut delivered = HashSet::new();
        let partial_name = format!("{}.part", hex(&Sha1::digest(file.filename.as_bytes())));
        let partial_path = checked_file_path(partial_root, Path::new(&partial_name))?;
        let mut partial = OpenOptions::new()
            .create(true)
            .truncate(true)
            .write(true)
            .open(&partial_path)?;
        let mut reused_bytes = 0;
        let mut hash = Sha1::new();
        let mut buffer = [0_u8; 64 * 1024];
        // The most recently fetched chunk stays in memory for the parts that
        // follow it; anything older is read back from the chunk cache.
        let mut current: Option<(ChunkGuid, Vec<u8>)> = None;
        for part in &file.parts {
            self.cancel.check()?;
            let chunk = manifest.chunks.get(&part.guid).ok_or(EpicError::Protocol)?;
            if !plan.reused.contains(&part.guid) && delivered.insert(part.guid) {
                if self.prefetch.pending.front() != Some(&part.guid) {
                    return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
                }
                let bytes = self.chunks.receive()?;
                self.cancel.check()?;
                // A cached chunk is checked by size and SHA-1 before reuse, so a
                // torn write after a crash only costs one more download.
                let path = checked_file_path(chunk_root, Path::new(&chunk_key(chunk)))?;
                fs::write(path, &bytes)?;
                self.prefetch.pending.pop_front();
                self.prefetch
                    .chunks
                    .insert(part.guid, ChunkState::Stored { verified: false });
                current = Some((part.guid, bytes));
            }
            let start = part.offset as usize;
            let end = start + part.size as usize;
            match &current {
                Some((guid, bytes)) if *guid == part.guid => {
                    let slice = bytes.get(start..end).ok_or(EpicError::Protocol)?;
                    partial.write_all(slice)?;
                    hash.update(slice);
                }
                _ => {
                    let path = checked_file_path(chunk_root, Path::new(&chunk_key(chunk)))?;
                    let mut source = File::open(path)?;
                    source.seek(SeekFrom::Start(u64::from(part.offset)))?;
                    let mut remaining = part.size as usize;
                    while remaining > 0 {
                        self.cancel.check()?;
                        let count = remaining.min(buffer.len());
                        source.read_exact(&mut buffer[..count])?;
                        partial.write_all(&buffer[..count])?;
                        hash.update(&buffer[..count]);
                        remaining -= count;
                    }
                }
            }
            if plan.reused.contains(&part.guid) {
                reused_bytes += u64::from(part.size);
            }
            self.reporter
                .update(|status| status.completed_bytes += u64::from(part.size));
        }
        self.cancel.check()?;
        if hash.finalize()[..] != file.hash {
            return Err(EpicError::Integrity);
        }
        partial.sync_all()?;
        drop(partial);
        apply_permissions(&partial_path, is_executable(file, &partial_path)?)?;
        self.cancel.check()?;
        let target = checked_file_path(root, relative)?;
        fs::rename(&partial_path, &target)?;
        File::open(target.parent().unwrap_or(root))?.sync_all()?;
        Ok(reused_bytes)
    }
}

/// Manifests flag only the launch executable of some builds: Prison Architect's
/// Paradox bootstrap runs an unflagged installer beside it. Programs are then
/// recognised by their header, a Mach-O binary or a script.
fn is_executable(file: &ManifestFile, path: &Path) -> std::io::Result<bool> {
    Ok(file.flags & 4 != 0 || install::starts_as_program(path)?)
}

fn manifest_key(manifest: &Manifest) -> String {
    let mut hash = Sha1::new();
    hash.update(manifest.app_name.as_bytes());
    hash.update([0]);
    hash.update(manifest.build_version.as_bytes());
    for file in &manifest.files {
        hash.update(file.filename.as_bytes());
        hash.update(file.hash);
    }
    hex(&hash.finalize())
}

fn chunk_key(chunk: &Chunk) -> String {
    let [a, b, c, d] = chunk.guid;
    format!(
        "{a:08x}{b:08x}{c:08x}{d:08x}-{}-{:016x}.chunk",
        hex(&chunk.sha1),
        chunk.hash
    )
}

pub(crate) fn validate_manifest(manifest: &Manifest) -> Result<(), EpicError> {
    let mut paths = HashSet::new();
    let mut total_size = 0_u64;
    for file in &manifest.files {
        let relative = safe_relative_path(&file.filename)?;
        if file
            .symlink_target
            .as_ref()
            .is_some_and(|target| !target.is_empty())
        {
            return Err(EpicError::UnsupportedContent);
        }
        if !paths.insert(relative.to_string_lossy().to_lowercase()) {
            return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
        }
        total_size = total_size
            .checked_add(file.size())
            .ok_or(EpicError::Protocol)?;
        for part in &file.parts {
            let chunk = manifest.chunks.get(&part.guid).ok_or(EpicError::Protocol)?;
            if chunk.guid != part.guid
                || chunk.window_size == 0
                || chunk.window_size as usize > MAX_CHUNK_BYTES
                || chunk.file_size > (MAX_CHUNK_BYTES + 98) as u64
                || chunk.sha1 == [0; 20]
                || part.size == 0
                || u64::from(part.offset) + u64::from(part.size) > u64::from(chunk.window_size)
            {
                return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
            }
        }
    }
    // Reject a file that is also the parent directory of another file.
    for file in &manifest.files {
        let path = safe_relative_path(&file.filename)?;
        for parent in path
            .ancestors()
            .skip(1)
            .filter(|path| !path.as_os_str().is_empty())
        {
            if paths.contains(&parent.to_string_lossy().to_lowercase()) {
                return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Chunks come from at most eight HTTPS delivery URLs, without credentials.
fn check_base_urls(base_urls: &[Url]) -> Result<(), EpicError> {
    if base_urls.is_empty() || base_urls.len() > 8 {
        return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
    }
    for base_url in base_urls {
        let secure = base_url.scheme() == "https";
        #[cfg(test)]
        let secure = secure
            || base_url.scheme() == "http"
                && base_url
                    .host_str()
                    .is_some_and(|host| matches!(host, "127.0.0.1" | "localhost" | "[::1]"));
        if !secure || !credential_free(base_url) {
            return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub(crate) fn decode_chunk(bytes: &[u8], chunk: &Chunk) -> ChunkResult {
    let u32_at = |offset: usize| -> Result<u32, EpicError> {
        bytes
            .get(offset..offset + 4)
            .and_then(|part| part.try_into().ok())
            .map(u32::from_le_bytes)
            .ok_or(EpicError::Protocol)
    };
    if u32_at(0)? != 0xB1FE3AA2 {
        return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
    }
    let version = u32_at(4)?;
    let header_size = u32_at(8)? as usize;
    let expected_header = match version {
        1 => 41,
        2 => 62,
        3 => 66,
        4 => 98,
        _ => return Err(EpicError::Protocol),
    };
    let compressed_size = u32_at(12)? as usize;
    // The manifest's chunk file size is only an estimate: older manifests
    // list sizes for an older header, such as Unrailed's, 4 bytes short of
    // the version 3 header the CDN serves. The decoded window's SHA-1 and
    // rolling hash, both from the manifest, prove the chunk.
    if header_size != expected_header || bytes.len() != header_size + compressed_size {
        return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
    }
    for (index, word) in chunk.guid.iter().enumerate() {
        if u32_at(16 + 4 * index)? != *word {
            return Err(EpicError::Integrity);
        }
    }
    let header_hash = u64::from_le_bytes(
        bytes
            .get(32..40)
            .ok_or(EpicError::Protocol)?
            .try_into()
            .map_err(|_| EpicError::Protocol)?,
    );
    let stored_as = *bytes.get(40).ok_or(EpicError::Protocol)?;
    if stored_as & !1 != 0 {
        // Encrypted BuildPatch chunks require separate entitlement secrets.
        return Err(EpicError::UnsupportedContent);
    }
    let hash_type = if version >= 2 { bytes[61] } else { 1 };
    if hash_type == 0
        || hash_type & !3 != 0
        || version >= 3 && u32_at(62)? != chunk.window_size
        || version >= 4 && bytes[66..82].iter().any(|byte| *byte != 0)
    {
        return Err(EpicError::Protocol);
    }
    let payload = &bytes[header_size..];
    let decoded = if stored_as & 1 != 0 {
        crate::content_manifest::inflate(payload, chunk.window_size as usize)
            .ok_or(EpicError::Integrity)?
    } else {
        payload.to_vec()
    };
    let sha: [u8; 20] = Sha1::digest(&decoded).into();
    if decoded.len() != chunk.window_size as usize
        || sha != chunk.sha1
        || hash_type & 2 != 0 && bytes[41..61] != sha
        || hash_type & 1 != 0 && header_hash != chunk.hash
        || rolling_hash(&decoded) != chunk.hash
    {
        return Err(EpicError::Integrity);
    }
    Ok(decoded)
}

/// BuildPatch's byte-table rolling hash, using the reflected CRC64 polynomial.
pub(crate) fn rolling_hash(bytes: &[u8]) -> u64 {
    const TABLE: [u64; 256] = {
        let mut table = [0; 256];
        let mut index = 0;
        while index < 256 {
            let mut value = index as u64;
            let mut bit = 0;
            while bit < 8 {
                value = (value >> 1)
                    ^ if value & 1 != 0 {
                        0xC96C5795D7870F42
                    } else {
                        0
                    };
                bit += 1;
            }
            table[index] = value;
            index += 1;
        }
        table
    };
    bytes.iter().fold(0, |hash, byte| {
        hash.rotate_left(1) ^ TABLE[usize::from(*byte)]
    })
}

fn verify_file(
    path: &Path,
    size: u64,
    expected: &[u8; 20],
    cancel: &CancelToken,
) -> Result<bool, EpicError> {
    Ok(install::verify_sha1_file(path, size, expected, cancel)?)
}
```

```rs
use std::{
    collections::HashMap,
    net::{TcpListener, TcpStream},
    sync::{
        Mutex,
        atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering},
    },
    thread,
};

use super::*;
use crate::content_manifest::ChunkPart;

mod prefetch;

struct RequestGate {
    path: String,
    requests: usize,
    opened: AtomicBool,
}

struct Server {
    base: Url,
    requests: Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>>,
    headers: Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>>,
    stop: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    thread: Option<thread::JoinHandle<()>>,
}

impl Server {
    fn new(responses: HashMap<String, Vec<u8>>, stalled: bool) -> Self {
        Self::with_gate(responses, stalled, None)
    }

    fn with_gate(
        responses: HashMap<String, Vec<u8>>,
        stalled: bool,
        gate: Option<Arc<RequestGate>>,
    ) -> Self {
        let listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").unwrap();
        let base = Url::parse(&format!("http://{}/", listener.local_addr().unwrap())).unwrap();
        listener.set_nonblocking(true).unwrap();
        let requests = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
        let headers = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
        let thread_headers = Arc::clone(&headers);
        let stop = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
        let thread_requests = Arc::clone(&requests);
        let thread_stop = Arc::clone(&stop);
        let responses = Arc::new(responses);
        let thread = thread::spawn(move || {
            let mut workers = Vec::new();
            while !thread_stop.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
                match listener.accept() {
                    Ok((socket, _)) => {
                        let requests = Arc::clone(&thread_requests);
                        let headers = Arc::clone(&thread_headers);
                        let stop = Arc::clone(&thread_stop);
                        let responses = Arc::clone(&responses);
                        let gate = gate.clone();
                        workers.push(thread::spawn(move || {
                            serve(socket, requests, headers, stop, responses, stalled, gate)
                        }));
                    }
                    Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => {
                        thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(5))
                    }
                    Err(error) => panic!("accept failed: {error}"),
                }
            }
            for worker in workers {
                worker.join().unwrap();
            }
        });
        Self {
            base,
            requests,
            headers,
            stop,
            thread: Some(thread),
        }
    }

    fn paths(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        self.requests.lock().unwrap().clone()
    }
}

impl Drop for Server {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.stop.store(true, Ordering::Release);
        self.thread.take().unwrap().join().unwrap();
    }
}

fn serve(
    mut socket: TcpStream,
    requests: Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>>,
    headers: Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>>,
    stop: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    responses: Arc<HashMap<String, Vec<u8>>>,
    stalled: bool,
    gate: Option<Arc<RequestGate>>,
) {
    // macOS accept inherits O_NONBLOCK. Wait for the HTTP request instead
    // of treating an early WouldBlock as a disconnected client.
    socket.set_nonblocking(false).unwrap();
    socket
        .set_write_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(2)))
        .unwrap();
    socket
        .set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(2)))
        .unwrap();
    let mut request = Vec::new();
    let mut buffer = [0; 1024];
    loop {
        let Ok(count) = socket.read(&mut buffer) else {
            return;
        };
        if count == 0 {
            return;
        }
        request.extend_from_slice(&buffer[..count]);
        if request.windows(4).any(|bytes| bytes == b"\r\n\r\n") {
            break;
        }
    }
    let request = String::from_utf8_lossy(&request);
    let path = request.split_whitespace().nth(1).unwrap().to_owned();
    requests.lock().unwrap().push(path.clone());
    headers.lock().unwrap().push(request.to_string());
    if let Some(gate) = gate
        && gate.path == path
    {
        let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(3);
        while requests.lock().unwrap().len() < gate.requests
            && !stop.load(Ordering::Acquire)
            && std::time::Instant::now() < deadline
        {
            thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(2));
        }
        gate.opened.store(
            requests.lock().unwrap().len() >= gate.requests,
            Ordering::Release,
        );
    }
    if stalled {
        while !stop.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
            thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(5));
        }
        return;
    }
    if let Some(body) = responses.get(path.split('?').next().unwrap()) {
        let _ = write!(
            socket,
            "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n",
            body.len()
        );
        let _ = socket.write_all(body);
    } else {
        let _ = socket
            .write_all(b"HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n");
    }
}

fn chunk(data: &[u8], index: u32, compressed: bool) -> (Chunk, Vec<u8>) {
    let guid = [1, 2, 3, index];
    let hash = rolling_hash(data);
    let sha1: [u8; 20] = Sha1::digest(data).into();
    let payload = if compressed {
        let mut encoder = flate2::write::ZlibEncoder::new(Vec::new(), flate2::Compression::fast());
        encoder.write_all(data).unwrap();
        encoder.finish().unwrap()
    } else {
        data.to_vec()
    };
    let mut wire = Vec::new();
    for value in [0xB1FE3AA2, 3, 66, payload.len() as u32] {
        wire.extend_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes());
    }
    for value in guid {
        wire.extend_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes());
    }
    wire.extend_from_slice(&hash.to_le_bytes());
    wire.push(u8::from(compressed));
    wire.extend_from_slice(&sha1);
    wire.push(3);
    wire.extend_from_slice(&(data.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
    wire.extend_from_slice(&payload);
    (
        Chunk {
            guid,
            hash,
            sha1,
            group: 7,
            window_size: data.len() as u32,
            file_size: wire.len() as u64,
        },
        wire,
    )
}

fn fixture() -> (Manifest, HashMap<String, Vec<u8>>, Vec<u8>) {
    let (first, first_wire) = chunk(b"--hello", 10, true);
    let (second, second_wire) = chunk(b" world--", 11, false);
    let output = b"hello world".to_vec();
    let files = vec![ManifestFile {
        filename: "Game.app/Contents/MacOS/Game".into(),
        symlink_target: None,
        hash: Sha1::digest(&output).into(),
        flags: 4,
        parts: vec![
            ChunkPart {
                guid: first.guid,
                offset: 2,
                size: 5,
            },
            ChunkPart {
                guid: second.guid,
                offset: 0,
                size: 6,
            },
        ],
    }];
    let responses = [
        (format!("/{}", first.relative_path(18)), first_wire),
        (format!("/{}", second.relative_path(18)), second_wire),
    ]
    .into();
    let manifest = Manifest {
        custom_fields: Default::default(),
        app_name: "test-game".into(),
        build_version: "1.0".into(),
        launch_executable: files[0].filename.clone(),
        launch_command: String::new(),
        files,
        chunks: [(first.guid, first), (second.guid, second)].into(),
        feature_level: 18,
        prerequisite: None,
    };
    (manifest, responses, output)
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn installs_verified_parts_and_reuses_complete_files_without_network() {
    let (manifest, responses, expected) = fixture();
    let server = Server::new(responses, false);
    let temporary = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let snapshots = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
    let captured = Arc::clone(&snapshots);
    let client = ContentClient::new(Client::new());
    let first = client
        .download(
            Arc::new(manifest.clone()),
            std::slice::from_ref(&server.base),
            temporary.path(),
            &CancelToken::new(),
            move |snapshot| captured.lock().unwrap().push(snapshot),
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let target = temporary.path().join(&manifest.files[0].filename);
    assert_eq!(fs::read(&target).unwrap(), expected);
    assert_eq!(first.total_bytes, 11);
    assert_eq!(first.completed_files, 1);
    assert_eq!(first.reused_bytes, 0);
    assert!(first.content_bytes > 0);
    assert_eq!(server.paths().len(), 2);
    {
        let snapshots = snapshots.lock().unwrap();
        assert!(
            snapshots
                .windows(2)
                .all(|pair| pair[0].completed_bytes <= pair[1].completed_bytes
                    && pair[0].network_bytes <= pair[1].network_bytes)
        );
        assert_eq!(snapshots.last().unwrap().completed_bytes, 11);
    }
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
        assert_eq!(
            fs::metadata(&target).unwrap().permissions().mode() & 0o777,
            0o755
        );
    }
    let second = client
        .download(
            Arc::new(manifest.clone()),
            std::slice::from_ref(&server.base),
            temporary.path(),
            &CancelToken::new(),
            |_| {},
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(second.reused_bytes, 11);
    assert_eq!(second.downloaded_bytes, 0);
    assert_eq!(server.paths().len(), 2);
    assert!(
        !temporary
            .path()
            .join(PARTIAL_DIRECTORY)
            .join("epic")
            .join(manifest_key(&manifest))
            .exists()
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn cancellation_keeps_existing_file_and_verified_chunks_for_resume() {
    let (manifest, responses, expected) = fixture();
    let server = Server::new(responses, false);
    let temporary = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let target = temporary.path().join(&manifest.files[0].filename);
    fs::create_dir_all(target.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
    fs::write(&target, b"previous installed game").unwrap();
    let cancel = CancelToken::new();
    let from_callback = cancel.clone();
    let client = ContentClient::new(Client::new());
    let result = client
        .download(
            Arc::new(manifest.clone()),
            std::slice::from_ref(&server.base),
            temporary.path(),
            &cancel,
            move |status| {
                if status.completed_bytes >= 5 {
                    from_callback.cancel();
                }
            },
        )
        .await;
    assert!(matches!(result, Err(EpicError::Cancelled)));
    assert_eq!(fs::read(&target).unwrap(), b"previous installed game");
    let first_path = format!(
        "/{}",
        manifest.chunks[&manifest.files[0].parts[0].guid].relative_path(18)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        server
            .paths()
            .iter()
            .filter(|path| **path == first_path)
            .count(),
        1
    );
    let resumed = client
        .download(
            Arc::new(manifest.clone()),
            std::slice::from_ref(&server.base),
            temporary.path(),
            &CancelToken::new(),
            |_| {},
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(fs::read(&target).unwrap(), expected);
    assert_eq!(resumed.reused_bytes, 5);
    assert_eq!(
        server
            .paths()
            .iter()
            .filter(|path| **path == first_path)
            .count(),
        1
    );
}

#[test]
fn chunk_checks_header_guid_hash_size_and_bounded_decompression() {
    let (expected, wire) = chunk(&vec![42; 1024], 10, true);
    assert_eq!(decode_chunk(&wire, &expected).unwrap(), vec![42; 1024]);
    for offset in [0, 8, 12, 16, 32, 41, 62] {
        let mut corrupted = wire.clone();
        corrupted[offset] ^= 1;
        assert!(
            decode_chunk(&corrupted, &expected).is_err(),
            "offset {offset}"
        );
    }
    for count in [0, 16, 40, 61, 65] {
        assert!(decode_chunk(&wire[..count], &expected).is_err());
    }
    let mut smaller = expected.clone();
    smaller.window_size = 8;
    assert!(decode_chunk(&wire, &smaller).is_err());
}

#[test]
fn rejects_conflicting_paths_and_unsupported_symlinks() {
    let (mut manifest, _, _) = fixture();
    let mut duplicate = manifest.files[0].clone();
    duplicate.filename = duplicate.filename.to_uppercase();
    manifest.files.push(duplicate);
    assert!(matches!(
        validate_manifest(&manifest),
        Err(EpicError::Protocol)
    ));
    manifest.files.pop();

#[test]
fn rolling_hash_matches_independent_known_vector() {
    // Fixed output computed with Legendary's Python get_hash implementation:
    // https://github.com/derrod/legendary/blob/master/legendary/utils/rolling_hash.py
    assert_eq!(rolling_hash(b"hello world"), 0xd92e71f59dd35ed9);

#[test]
fn accepts_legacy_and_plain_v4_headers_but_rejects_encryption() {
    let (mut expected, wire) = chunk(b"uncompressed bytes", 25, false);
    for (version, header_size) in [(1_u32, 41_usize), (2, 62), (4, 98)] {
        let mut variant = wire[..header_size.min(66)].to_vec();
        variant[4..8].copy_from_slice(&version.to_le_bytes());
        variant[8..12].copy_from_slice(&(header_size as u32).to_le_bytes());
        variant.resize(header_size, 0);
        variant.extend_from_slice(&wire[66..]);
        expected.file_size = variant.len() as u64;
        assert_eq!(
            decode_chunk(&variant, &expected).unwrap(),
            b"uncompressed bytes"
        );
        variant[40] = 2;
        assert!(matches!(
            decode_chunk(&variant, &expected),
            Err(EpicError::UnsupportedContent)
        ));
    }
}

#[test]
fn a_chunk_decodes_whatever_size_the_manifest_estimated_but_never_torn() {
    let (mut expected, wire) = chunk(b"uncompressed bytes", 25, false);
    // Older manifests list a version 2 header's size for a version 3 chunk.
    expected.file_size = wire.len() as u64 - 4;
    assert_eq!(
        decode_chunk(&wire, &expected).unwrap(),
        b"uncompressed bytes"
    );
    assert!(matches!(
        decode_chunk(&wire[..wire.len() - 1], &expected),
        Err(EpicError::Protocol)
    ));
    let mut longer = wire.clone();
    longer.push(0);
    assert!(matches!(
        decode_chunk(&longer, &expected),
        Err(EpicError::Protocol)
    ));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn dropping_download_cancels_disk_worker_and_releases_install_lock() {
    let (manifest, responses, _) = fixture();
    let server = Server::new(responses, true);
    let temporary = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let destination = temporary.path().to_owned();
    let cancel = CancelToken::new();
    let task_cancel = cancel.clone();
    let base = server.base.clone();
    let task = tokio::spawn(async move {
        ContentClient::new(Client::new())
            .download(
                Arc::new(manifest.clone()),
                std::slice::from_ref(&base),
                &destination,
                &task_cancel,
                |_| {},
            )
            .await
    });
    tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(2), async {
        while server.paths().is_empty() {
            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(5)).await;
        }
    })
    .await
    .unwrap();
    task.abort();
    assert!(task.await.unwrap_err().is_cancelled());
    assert!(cancel.is_cancelled());
    let lock = OpenOptions::new()
        .read(true)
        .write(true)
        .open(
            temporary
                .path()
                .join(PARTIAL_DIRECTORY)
                .join("install.lock"),
        )
        .unwrap();
    tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(2), async {
        while lock.try_lock().is_err() {
            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(5)).await;
        }
    })
    .await
    .unwrap();
}

#[tokio::test]

    let (mut manifest, responses, _) = fixture();

    second.filename = "second.txt".into();

    second.hash = Sha1::digest(b"hello").into();
    manifest.files.push(second);
    let server = Server::new(responses, false);
    let temporary = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();

        .download(
            Arc::new(manifest),
            std::slice::from_ref(&server.base),

        .iter()

            .iter()
            .all(|phase| *phase == DownloadPhase::Downloading)
    );

#[tokio::test]
async fn repairs_corrupt_files_using_another_mirror_without_manifest_credentials() {
    for corrupt_response in [false, true] {
        let (manifest, responses, expected) = fixture();
        let first_responses = if corrupt_response {
            responses
                .iter()
                .map(|(path, bytes)| {
                    let mut corrupted = bytes.clone();
                    *corrupted.last_mut().unwrap() ^= 0xff;
                    (path.clone(), corrupted)
                })
                .collect()
        } else {
            HashMap::new()
        }; // This mirror returns 404 for every chunk.
        let first = Server::new(first_responses, false);
        let second = Server::new(responses, false);
        let mut bases = vec![first.base.clone(), second.base.clone()];
        for base in &mut bases {
            base.set_query(Some("Signature=manifest-only"));
        }
        let temporary = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let target = temporary.path().join(&manifest.files[0].filename);
        fs::create_dir_all(target.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
        fs::write(&target, b"corrupt local game").unwrap();
        let summary = ContentClient::new(Client::new())
            .download(
                Arc::new(manifest.clone()),
                &bases,
                temporary.path(),
                &CancelToken::new(),
                |_| {},
            )
            .await
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(fs::read(&target).unwrap(), expected);
        assert_eq!(summary.completed_files, 1);
        assert_eq!(first.paths().len(), if corrupt_response { 6 } else { 2 });
        assert_eq!(second.paths().len(), 2);
        for server in [&first, &second] {
            assert!(server.paths().iter().all(|path| !path.contains('?')));
            assert!(
                server
                    .headers
                    .lock()
                    .unwrap()
                    .iter()
                    .all(|request| !request.to_ascii_lowercase().contains("authorization:"))
            );
        }
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn abandoned_account_transfer_keeps_disk_admission_until_worker_exits() {
    use crate::client::{TransferProgress, TransferState};
    use obelisk_core::transfer::Transfers;
    fn initial() -> TransferProgress {
        TransferProgress::new("test-game")
    }
    let (manifest, responses, expected) = fixture();
    let manifest = Arc::new(manifest);
    let server = Server::new(responses, false);
    let temporary = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let target = temporary.path().join(&manifest.files[0].filename);
    fs::create_dir_all(target.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
    fs::write(&target, b"original").unwrap();
    let transfers = Arc::new(Transfers::default());
    let owner = Arc::clone(&transfers);
    let destination = temporary.path().to_owned();
    let task_manifest = Arc::clone(&manifest);
    let filename = manifest.files[0].filename.clone();
    let base = server.base.clone();
    let (reached, waiting) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel();
    let (release, blocked) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();
    let gate = Mutex::new(Some((reached, blocked)));
    let task = tokio::spawn(async move {
        owner
            .run(initial(), |transfer| async move {
                let progress = transfer.clone();
                ContentClient::new(Client::new())
                    .download(
                        task_manifest,
                        &[base],
                        &destination,
                        transfer.cancel_token(),
                        move |snapshot| {
                            progress.update(|status| {
                                status.state = snapshot.phase.into();
                                status.completed_bytes = snapshot.completed_bytes;
                            });
                            // This report comes from the disk worker before it asks for chunks.
                            if snapshot.current_file == filename
                                && let Some((reached, blocked)) = gate.lock().unwrap().take()
                            {
                                reached.send(()).unwrap();
                                blocked.recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(5)).unwrap();
                            }
                        },
                    )
                    .await
            })
            .await
    });
    tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), waiting)
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .unwrap();
    task.abort();
    assert!(task.await.unwrap_err().is_cancelled());
    assert!(matches!(
        transfers
            .run(initial(), |_| async { Ok::<_, EpicError>(()) })
            .await,
        Err(EpicError::AlreadyDownloading)
    ));
    assert!(install::lock_engine(temporary.path()).unwrap().is_none());
    assert_eq!(fs::read(&target).unwrap(), b"original");
    release.send(()).unwrap();
    tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), async {
        while transfers.snapshot().unwrap().state != TransferState::Cancelled {
            tokio::task::yield_now().await;
        }
    })
    .await
    .unwrap();
    assert!(install::lock_engine(temporary.path()).unwrap().is_some());
    transfers
        .run(initial(), |transfer| async move {
            ContentClient::new(Client::new())
                .download(
                    manifest,
                    std::slice::from_ref(&server.base),
                    temporary.path(),
                    transfer.cancel_token(),
                    |_| {},
                )
                .await?;
            assert_eq!(fs::read(&target).unwrap(), expected);
            Ok::<_, EpicError>(())
        })
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(transfers.snapshot().unwrap().state, TransferState::Complete);
}

#[test]
fn unflagged_programs_are_recognised_by_their_header() {
    let temporary = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let file = |flags| ManifestFile {
        filename: "file".into(),
        symlink_target: None,
        hash: [0; 20],
        flags,
        parts: Vec::new(),
    };
    for (contents, executable) in [
        (&[0xcf, 0xfa, 0xed, 0xfe, 7, 0, 0, 1][..], true),
        (&[0xca, 0xfe, 0xba, 0xbe, 0, 0, 0, 2][..], true),
        (b"#!/bin/sh\n", true),
        (b"{\"gameId\": 1}", false),
        (b"#", false),
        (b"", false),
    ] {
        let path = temporary.path().join("file");
        fs::write(&path, contents).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(is_executable(&file(0), &path).unwrap(), executable);
        assert!(is_executable(&file(4), &path).unwrap());
    }
}
```

```rs
use super::*;

fn files_fixture(count: usize) -> (Manifest, HashMap<String, Vec<u8>>, Vec<Vec<u8>>) {
    let mut manifest = fixture().0;
    manifest.files.clear();
    manifest.chunks.clear();
    let mut responses = HashMap::new();
    let mut outputs = Vec::new();
    for index in 0..count {
        let bytes = format!("content of file {index:02}").into_bytes();
        let (chunk, wire) = chunk(&bytes, index as u32 + 100, true);
        manifest.files.push(ManifestFile {
            filename: format!("Game/file-{index:02}"),
            symlink_target: None,
            hash: Sha1::digest(&bytes).into(),
            flags: 0,
            parts: vec![ChunkPart {
                guid: chunk.guid,
                offset: 0,
                size: bytes.len() as u32,
            }],
        });
        responses.insert(format!("/{}", chunk.relative_path(18)), wire);
        manifest.chunks.insert(chunk.guid, chunk);
        outputs.push(bytes);
    }
    (manifest, responses, outputs)
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn later_files_download_before_the_first_response_and_window_keeps_advancing() {
    let (manifest, responses, outputs) = files_fixture(FILE_PREFETCH + 3);
    let first = &manifest.chunks[&manifest.files[0].parts[0].guid];
    // Each fixture file has one chunk. The blocked first response must leave
    // room for other files, up to the smaller file-window and network limits.
    let overlapping_files = manifest
        .files
        .len()
        .min(FILE_PREFETCH)
        .min(CHUNK_CONCURRENCY);
    assert!(
        overlapping_files > 1,
        "this test requires overlap across files"
    );
    let gate = Arc::new(RequestGate {
        path: format!("/{}", first.relative_path(18)),
        requests: overlapping_files,
        opened: AtomicBool::new(false),
    });
    let server = Server::with_gate(responses, false, Some(Arc::clone(&gate)));
    let temporary = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let summary = tokio::time::timeout(
        Duration::from_secs(8),
        ContentClient::new(Client::new()).download(
            Arc::new(manifest.clone()),
            std::slice::from_ref(&server.base),
            temporary.path(),
            &CancelToken::new(),
            |_| {},
        ),
    )
    .await
    .unwrap()
    .unwrap();
    assert!(
        gate.opened.load(Ordering::Acquire),
        "later files must be requested while file 0 is blocked"
    );
    assert_eq!(summary.completed_files as usize, outputs.len());
    assert_eq!(server.paths().len(), outputs.len());
    for (file, expected) in manifest.files.iter().zip(outputs) {
        assert_eq!(
            fs::read(temporary.path().join(&file.filename)).unwrap(),
            expected
        );
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn shared_chunks_cross_the_window_and_survive_cancellation_with_cached_repairs() {
    let (mut manifest, responses, mut outputs) = files_fixture(FILE_PREFETCH + 3);
    let shared = manifest.files[0].parts[0].clone();
    manifest.files[0].parts.push(shared.clone());
    let original_shared = outputs[0].clone();
    outputs[0].extend_from_slice(&original_shared);
    manifest.files[0].hash = Sha1::digest(&outputs[0]).into();
    for index in [3, FILE_PREFETCH + 2] {
        manifest.files[index].parts.insert(0, shared.clone());
        outputs[index] = [original_shared.as_slice(), outputs[index].as_slice()].concat();
        manifest.files[index].hash = Sha1::digest(&outputs[index]).into();
    }
    let server = Server::new(responses, false);
    let temporary = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let cache = temporary
        .path()
        .join(PARTIAL_DIRECTORY)
        .join("epic")
        .join(manifest_key(&manifest))
        .join("chunks");
    fs::create_dir_all(&cache).unwrap();
    let cached = &manifest.chunks[&manifest.files[2].parts[0].guid];
    fs::write(cache.join(chunk_key(cached)), &outputs[2]).unwrap();
    let corrupt = &manifest.chunks[&manifest.files[4].parts[0].guid];
    fs::write(
        cache.join(chunk_key(corrupt)),
        vec![0; corrupt.window_size as usize],
    )
    .unwrap();
    fs::create_dir_all(temporary.path().join("Game")).unwrap();
    fs::write(
        temporary.path().join(&manifest.files[1].filename),
        &outputs[1],
    )
    .unwrap();
    let old_target = temporary.path().join(&manifest.files[3].filename);
    fs::write(&old_target, b"previous installed file").unwrap();
    let cancel = CancelToken::new();
    let stop = cancel.clone();
    let client = ContentClient::new(Client::new());
    let result = client
        .download(
            Arc::new(manifest.clone()),
            std::slice::from_ref(&server.base),
            temporary.path(),
            &cancel,
            move |progress| {
                // One complete file was already present. Stop after publishing file 0.
                if progress.completed_files == 2 && progress.content_bytes > 0 {
                    stop.cancel();
                }
            },
        )
        .await;
    assert!(matches!(result, Err(EpicError::Cancelled)));
    assert_eq!(fs::read(&old_target).unwrap(), b"previous installed file");
    assert_eq!(
        fs::read(temporary.path().join(&manifest.files[0].filename)).unwrap(),
        outputs[0]
    );
    let shared_chunk = &manifest.chunks[&shared.guid];
    assert_eq!(
        fs::read(cache.join(chunk_key(shared_chunk))).unwrap(),
        original_shared
    );
    let summary = client
        .download(
            Arc::new(manifest.clone()),
            std::slice::from_ref(&server.base),
            temporary.path(),
            &CancelToken::new(),
            |_| {},
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(summary.completed_files as usize, outputs.len());
    assert_eq!(
        summary.reused_bytes,
        (original_shared.len() * 4 + outputs[1].len() + outputs[2].len()) as u64
    );
    for (file, expected) in manifest.files.iter().zip(outputs) {
        assert_eq!(
            fs::read(temporary.path().join(&file.filename)).unwrap(),
            expected
        );
    }
    let paths = server.paths();
    let shared_path = format!("/{}", shared_chunk.relative_path(18));
    assert_eq!(paths.iter().filter(|path| **path == shared_path).count(), 1);
    for index in [1, 2] {
        let chunk = &manifest.chunks[&manifest.files[index].parts[0].guid];
        assert!(!paths.contains(&format!("/{}", chunk.relative_path(18))));
    }
    assert!(!cache.exists());
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn prefetch_window_is_bounded_and_closed_requests_preserve_the_ordered_error() {
    let (manifest, _, outputs) = files_fixture(FILE_PREFETCH + 3);
    let manifest = Arc::new(manifest);
    let temporary = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    // This test plays the network side.
    let (chunks, mut requests, deliveries) = Chunks::detached(PIPELINE.queue);
    let disk = DiskInstall::engine_side(
        temporary.path().to_owned(),
        Arc::clone(&manifest),
        CancelToken::new(),
        Reporter::new(DownloadProgress::default(), |_| {}),
    );
    let disk = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || disk(chunks));
    for file in &manifest.files[..FILE_PREFETCH] {
        let chunk = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(2), requests.recv())
            .await
            .unwrap()
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(chunk.guid, file.parts[0].guid);
    }
    // The disk side waits for file 0's chunk before it plans another file.
    assert!(matches!(
        requests.try_recv(),
        Err(tokio::sync::mpsc::error::TryRecvError::Empty)
    ));
    // File 1's chunk fails for good: the network side stops after delivering
    // file 0's chunk and that error, so the refill after file 0 is refused.
    // It must not replace the ordered error with Protocol.
    drop(requests);
    deliveries.send(Ok(outputs[0].clone())).await.unwrap();
    deliveries.send(Err(EpicError::Http(404))).await.unwrap();
    drop(deliveries);
    let result = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(8), disk)
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(result, Err(EpicError::Http(404))));
    let root = temporary.path();
    assert_eq!(
        fs::read(root.join(&manifest.files[0].filename)).unwrap(),
        outputs[0]
    );
    assert!(!root.join(&manifest.files[1].filename).exists());
    assert!(
        root.join(PARTIAL_DIRECTORY)
            .join("epic")
            .join(manifest_key(&manifest))
            .is_dir()
    );
    assert!(install::lock_engine(root).unwrap().is_some());
}
```

`crates/storefronts/epic-kit/src/content/verification.rs`:

```rs
//! Epic manifest entries described for the same verification scheduler as Steam.
//!
//! Path confinement, the SHA-1 read, the reader bound and the join-before-repair
//! guarantee all live in `obelisk_core::verification`. Rust's orphan rule is why
//! the trait implementation stays in this crate.
use obelisk_core::{
    install::FileDigest,
    verification::{VerificationError, VerificationFile},
};

use crate::{EpicError, content_manifest::ManifestFile};

pub(super) use obelisk_core::verification::verify_files;

impl VerificationFile for ManifestFile {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        &self.filename
    }
    fn size(&self) -> u64 {
        ManifestFile::size(self)
    }
    fn digest(&self) -> FileDigest<'_> {
        FileDigest::Sha1(&self.hash)
    }
}

impl From<VerificationError> for EpicError {
    fn from(error: VerificationError) -> Self {
        match error {
            VerificationError::Cancelled => Self::Cancelled,
            VerificationError::Install(error) => error.into(),
            // A reader panic and a counter overflow are the scheduler's own
            // failures; the installation stopped either way.
            VerificationError::SchedulerFailed => Self::Protocol,
        }
    }
}
```
