```rs
//! Bounded reads and the status mapping every GOG request shares.
use std::{io::Read, time::Duration};

use obelisk_core::transfer::{BodyError, BodySize, CancelToken, read_body};
use reqwest::{RequestBuilder, Response, StatusCode, Url};

use crate::GogError;

/// GOG's services answer a desktop client; some refuse an empty agent.
pub(crate) const USER_AGENT: &str = "GOGGalaxyClient/2.0.80.21 (Windows_NT 10.0.19045) Obelisk";

pub(crate) fn client() -> Result<reqwest::Client, GogError> {
    // Redirects never carry the account's bearer token elsewhere.
    reqwest::Client::builder()
        .user_agent(USER_AGENT)
        .redirect(reqwest::redirect::Policy::none())
        .connect_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(15))
        .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(45))
        .build()
        .map_err(|_| GogError::Network)
}

pub(crate) async fn bounded_json<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(
    response: reqwest::Response,
    limit: usize,
) -> Result<T, GogError> {
    serde_json::from_slice(&bounded_bytes(response, limit).await?).map_err(|_| GogError::Protocol)
}

pub(crate) async fn bounded_bytes(
    response: reqwest::Response,
    limit: usize,
) -> Result<Vec<u8>, GogError> {
    read_body(
        response.content_length(),
        response.bytes_stream(),
        BodySize::AtMost(limit as u64),
        &CancelToken::new(),
        |_| {},
    )
    .await
    .map_err(|error| match error {
        // An oversized answer is malformed, unlike a chunk of the wrong size.
        BodyError::Size => GogError::Protocol,
        error => error.into(),
    })
}

/// A content-system document: zlib-compressed JSON, or plain JSON for the
/// few GOG serves uncompressed.
pub(crate) fn inflate_json<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(
    bytes: &[u8],
    limit: u64,
) -> Result<T, GogError> {
    let mut inflated = Vec::new();
    let decoded = flate2::read::ZlibDecoder::new(bytes)
        .take(limit + 1)
        .read_to_end(&mut inflated);
    let json = match decoded {
        Ok(_) if inflated.len() as u64 > limit => return Err(GogError::Protocol),
        Ok(_) => &inflated[..],
        Err(_) => bytes,
    };
    serde_json::from_slice(json).map_err(|_| GogError::Protocol)
}

/// Sends `request` and refuses any answer but a success.
pub(crate) async fn send(request: RequestBuilder) -> Result<Response, GogError> {
    let response = request.send().await.map_err(|_| GogError::Network)?;
    check_status(response.status())?;
    Ok(response)
}

/// Sends the request `request` builds, again after a lost connection, a
/// server error or a rate limit, up to `attempts` times, each `backoff`
/// longer apart; `None` when what it asks for does not exist.
pub(crate) async fn send_retrying(
    request: impl Fn() -> RequestBuilder,
    attempts: u32,
    backoff: Duration,
) -> Result<Option<Response>, GogError> {
    let mut failure = GogError::Network;
    for attempt in 0..attempts {
        if attempt > 0 {
            tokio::time::sleep(backoff * attempt).await;
        }
        let Ok(response) = request().send().await else {
            continue;
        };
        match response.status() {
            StatusCode::NOT_FOUND => return Ok(None),
            status if status.is_server_error() || status == StatusCode::TOO_MANY_REQUESTS => {
                failure = status_error(status);
            }
            status => {
                check_status(status)?;
                return Ok(Some(response));
            }
        }
    }
    Err(failure)
}

pub(crate) fn check_status(status: StatusCode) -> Result<(), GogError> {
    match status.is_success() {
        true => Ok(()),
        false => Err(status_error(status)),
    }
}

fn status_error(status: StatusCode) -> GogError {
    if status == StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED {
        return GogError::Unauthorized;
    }
    // Response bodies never reach the player: they may echo a token.
    GogError::Service {
        message: match status {
            StatusCode::TOO_MANY_REQUESTS => "backend.gog.rate_limited".into(),
            StatusCode::FORBIDDEN => "backend.gog.forbidden".into(),
            _ => serde_json::json!({
                "key": "backend.gog.http",
                "args": [status.as_u16().to_string()]
            })
            .to_string(),
        },
    }
}

/// Only HTTPS locations without embedded credentials reach the host.
pub(crate) fn safe_https_url(value: &str) -> Option<String> {
    // GOG spells many image locations without their scheme.
    let value = match value.strip_prefix("//") {
        Some(rest) => format!("https://{rest}"),
        None => value.to_owned(),
    };
    Url::parse(&value)
        .ok()
        .filter(|url| {
            url.scheme() == "https"
                && url.host_str().is_some()
                && url.username().is_empty()
                && url.password().is_none()
        })
        .map(|_| value)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::io::Write;

    #[test]
    fn content_documents_inflate_or_read_as_plain_json() {
        let mut encoder =
            flate2::write::ZlibEncoder::new(Vec::new(), flate2::Compression::default());
        encoder.write_all(br#"{"a":1}"#).unwrap();
        let compressed = encoder.finish().unwrap();
        let value: serde_json::Value = inflate_json(&compressed, 1024).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(value["a"], 1);
        let value: serde_json::Value = inflate_json(br#"{"a":2}"#, 1024).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(value["a"], 2);
        assert!(matches!(
            inflate_json::<serde_json::Value>(&compressed, 3),
            Err(GogError::Protocol)
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn images_gain_their_scheme_and_other_locations_are_refused() {
        assert_eq!(
            safe_https_url("//images.gog-statics.com/a.jpg").as_deref(),
            Some("https://images.gog-statics.com/a.jpg")
        );
        assert_eq!(safe_https_url("http://images.gog.com/a.jpg"), None);
        assert_eq!(safe_https_url("https://user:pw@images.gog.com/a.jpg"), None);
        assert_eq!(safe_https_url("not a url"), None);
    }
}
```

```rs
//! GOG account authentication, owned libraries and verified Galaxy content
//! downloads, independently implemented from the endpoints documented by
//! heroic-gogdl and Heroic's GOG store manager.

pub mod auth;
pub mod client;
mod content;
mod http;
mod library;
mod manifest;

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum GogError {
    #[error("backend.gog.network")]
    Network,
    #[error("backend.gog.unauthorized")]
    Unauthorized,
    #[error("backend.gog.invalid_code")]
    InvalidCode,
    #[error("backend.gog.invalid_response")]
    Protocol,
    #[error("backend.gog.cancelled")]
    Cancelled,
    #[error("backend.gog.storage")]
    Io(#[from] std::io::Error),
    #[error("backend.gog.download_in_progress")]
    AlreadyDownloading,
    #[error("backend.gog.unsafe_path")]
    UnsafePath(String),
    #[error("backend.gog.integrity")]
    Integrity,
    #[error("backend.gog.content_http")]
    Http(u16),
    /// GOG serves no build Obelisk can install for this platform.
    #[error("backend.gog.no_build")]
    NoBuild,
    #[error("{message}")]
    Service { message: String },
}

use obelisk_core::{
    build_choice::{NOT_NATIVE, Unavailable},
    install::InstallError,
    storefront::{StorefrontCapabilities, StorefrontDescriptor, StorefrontId},
    transfer::Cancelled,
};

impl From<Cancelled> for GogError {
    fn from(_: Cancelled) -> Self {
        Self::Cancelled
    }
}

impl From<Unavailable> for GogError {
    fn from(unavailable: Unavailable) -> Self {
        match unavailable {
            Unavailable::NoBuild => Self::NoBuild,
            Unavailable::NotNative => Self::Service {
                message: NOT_NATIVE.into(),
            },
        }
    }
}

impl From<InstallError> for GogError {
    fn from(error: InstallError) -> Self {
        match error {
            InstallError::Cancelled => Self::Cancelled,
            InstallError::UnsafePath(path) => Self::UnsafePath(path),
            InstallError::Io(error) => Self::Io(error),
        }
    }
}

pub fn descriptor() -> StorefrontDescriptor {
    StorefrontDescriptor {
        id: StorefrontId::Gog,
        display_name: "GOG",
        capabilities: StorefrontCapabilities {
            authentication: true,
            owned_library: true,
            downloads: true,
            local_import: false,
        },
    }
}
```

`crates/storefronts/gog-kit/src/library.rs`:

```rs
//! The account's games, as Heroic's `library.ts` reads them: the Galaxy
//! library names the products the account owns, gamesdb describes each one,
//! and `api.gog.com/products` the few gamesdb does not know.
use std::{collections::HashSet, time::Duration};

use futures_util::{StreamExt, TryStreamExt, stream};
use obelisk_core::Platform;
use reqwest::Url;
use serde::Deserialize;
use serde_json::Value;

use crate::{
    GogError,
    auth::Api,
    client::valid_product_id,
    http::{bounded_json, safe_https_url, send_retrying},
};

const MAX_LIBRARY_PAGES: usize = 1000;
/// Concurrent gamesdb requests while a library loads.
const DESCRIPTIONS: usize = 12;

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Game {
    pub product_id: String,
    pub title: String,
    /// The portrait cover.
    pub image_url: Option<String>,
    /// The wide artwork the hero and the game's page show.
    pub header_image_url: Option<String>,
    pub windows: bool,
    pub macos: bool,
    pub info: GameInfo,
    /// When the game joined the account's library, in seconds since the Unix
    /// epoch.
    pub added_at: Option<u64>,
    /// Everything GOG returned for the game: its Galaxy library record,
    /// `release`, and its gamesdb release or store product, `catalog`.
    pub metadata: Value,
}

/// What GOG tells of a game, for its page.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct GameInfo {
    /// In English: gamesdb has no other language.
    pub summary: String,
    pub developers: Vec<String>,
    pub publishers: Vec<String>,
    /// Seconds since the Unix epoch.
    pub release_date: Option<u64>,
    pub genres: Vec<String>,
    /// The critics' rating, out of 100.
    pub rating: Option<u32>,
    /// The languages the game speaks, such as `fr-FR`.
    pub languages: Vec<String>,
}

impl GameInfo {
    /// What a gamesdb release tells of its game.
    fn of_release(catalog: &Value) -> Self {
        let game = &catalog["game"];
        let names = |list: &Value| -> Vec<String> {
            list.as_array()
                .into_iter()
                .flatten()
                .filter_map(|item| match &item["name"] {
                    Value::String(name) => Some(name.clone()),
                    name => localized(name),
                })
                .filter(|name| !name.is_empty())
                .collect()
        };
        Self {
            summary: localized(&game["summary"])
                .or_else(|| localized(&catalog["summary"]))
                .unwrap_or_default(),
            developers: names(&game["developers"]),
            publishers: names(&game["publishers"]),
            release_date: [&catalog["first_release_date"], &game["first_release_date"]]
                .into_iter()
                .find_map(|date| date.as_str().and_then(obelisk_core::date::unix_seconds)),
            genres: names(&game["genres"]),
            rating: game["aggregated_rating"]
                .as_f64()
                .filter(|rating| *rating > 0.0 && *rating <= 100.0)
                .map(|rating| rating.round() as u32),
            languages: catalog["available_languages"]
                .as_array()
                .into_iter()
                .flatten()
                .filter_map(|language| language["code"].as_str().map(str::to_owned))
                .collect(),
        }
    }
}

/// What a game's page adds to its library entry: the build it shows before
/// any download, and its size.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct GameDetails {
    /// The Mac build, unless a download found that its game does not run
    /// natively. Unknown when GOG could not tell.
    pub platform: Option<Platform>,
    /// Unknown when GOG serves no build Obelisk installs.
    pub installation_bytes: Option<u64>,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct ReleasesPage {
    #[serde(default)]
    items: Vec<Value>,
    #[serde(default)]
    next_page_token: Option<String>,
}

/// One product of the account's Galaxy library.
struct Release {
    platform_id: String,
    external_id: String,
    certificate: Option<String>,
}

impl Release {
    /// The record's product, whose id Galaxy may spell as a number.
    fn of(record: &Value) -> Self {
        let text = |key: &str| match &record[key] {
            Value::String(text) => text.clone(),
            Value::Number(number) => number.to_string(),
            _ => String::new(),
        };
        Self {
            platform_id: text("platform_id"),
            external_id: text("external_id"),
            certificate: record["certificate"].as_str().map(str::to_owned),
        }
    }
}

/// The account's games, in the order Galaxy lists them.
pub(crate) async fn games(
    api: &Api,
    access_token: &str,
    user_id: &str,
) -> Result<Vec<Game>, GogError> {
    let releases = releases(api, access_token, user_id).await?;
    let descriptions =
        releases
            .into_iter()
            .enumerate()
            .map(|(index, (release, record))| async move {
                Ok::<_, GogError>((index, describe(api, access_token, release, record).await?))
            });
    // A slow product never holds back the others' requests.
    let mut described: Vec<(usize, Option<Game>)> = stream::iter(descriptions)
        .buffer_unordered(DESCRIPTIONS)
        .try_collect()
        .await?;
    described.sort_unstable_by_key(|(index, _)| *index);
    Ok(described.into_iter().filter_map(|(_, game)| game).collect())
}

/// Every GOG product of the account's Galaxy library, once each, with its
/// record as Galaxy returned it.
async fn releases(
    api: &Api,
    access_token: &str,
    user_id: &str,
) -> Result<Vec<(Release, Value)>, GogError> {
    let mut seen = HashSet::new();
    let mut releases = Vec::new();
    let mut token: Option<String> = None;
    for _ in 0..MAX_LIBRARY_PAGES {
        let mut url = endpoint(&api.library, &["users", user_id, "releases"])?;
        if let Some(token) = &token {
            url.query_pairs_mut().append_pair("page_token", token);
        }
        let page: ReleasesPage = api.get(url, access_token).await?;
        for mut record in page.items {
            let release = Release::of(&record);
            if release.platform_id != "gog"
                || !valid_product_id(&release.external_id)
                || !seen.insert(release.external_id.clone())
            {
                continue;
            }
            // The ownership certificate stays in memory: it reaches gamesdb
            // only.
            if let Some(record) = record.as_object_mut() {
                record.remove("certificate");
            }
            releases.push((release, record));
        }
        match page.next_page_token.filter(|next| !next.is_empty()) {
            Some(next) if Some(&next) != token.as_ref() => token = Some(next),
            _ => return Ok(releases),
        }
    }
    Err(GogError::Protocol)
}

/// The game a library record names, or `None` for a product the library does
/// not show, such as a DLC.
async fn describe(
    api: &Api,
    access_token: &str,
    release: Release,
    record: Value,
) -> Result<Option<Game>, GogError> {
    let id = &release.external_id;
    let added_at = added_at(&record);
    if let Some(catalog) = gamesdb(api, access_token, &release).await? {
        let kind = catalog["type"].as_str().unwrap_or_default();
        let visible = catalog["game"]["visible_in_library"].as_bool() != Some(false);
        if !matches!(kind, "game" | "mod") || !visible {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let systems: Vec<&str> = catalog["supported_operating_systems"]
            .as_array()
            .into_iter()
            .flatten()
            .filter_map(|system| system["slug"].as_str())
            .collect();
        return Ok(Some(Game {
            product_id: id.clone(),
            title: localized(&catalog["title"])
                .or_else(|| localized(&catalog["game"]["title"]))
                .unwrap_or_else(|| id.clone()),
            image_url: image(&catalog["game"]["vertical_cover"], "_glx_vertical_cover"),
            header_image_url: image(&catalog["game"]["background"], "")
                .or_else(|| image(&catalog["game"]["horizontal_artwork"], "")),
            windows: systems.contains(&"windows"),
            macos: systems.contains(&"osx"),
            info: GameInfo::of_release(&catalog),
            added_at,
            metadata: metadata(record, catalog),
        }));
    }
    // gamesdb does not know this product: the store tells what it is.
    let product = product(api, id).await?;
    if product["game_type"].as_str() != Some("game") {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    let compatibility = &product["content_system_compatibility"];
    Ok(Some(Game {
        product_id: id.clone(),
        title: product["title"].as_str().unwrap_or(id).to_owned(),
        image_url: None,
        header_image_url: product["images"]["background"]
            .as_str()
            .and_then(safe_https_url),
        windows: compatibility["windows"].as_bool() == Some(true),
        macos: compatibility["osx"].as_bool() == Some(true),
        info: GameInfo {
            release_date: product["release_date"]
                .as_str()
                .and_then(obelisk_core::date::unix_seconds),
            ..GameInfo::default()
        },
        added_at,
        metadata: metadata(record, product),
    }))
}

/// When a Galaxy library record says the account got its product: the
/// earlier of its creation and its ownership, in seconds since the Unix epoch.
fn added_at(record: &Value) -> Option<u64> {
    [&record["date_created"], &record["owned_since"]]
        .into_iter()
        .filter_map(Value::as_u64)
        .filter(|seconds| *seconds > 0)
        .min()
}

/// What the library cache keeps of a game beyond what it shows: its Galaxy
/// record and its catalog data.
fn metadata(record: Value, catalog: Value) -> Value {
    Value::Object(serde_json::Map::from_iter([
        ("release".into(), record),
        ("catalog".into(), catalog),
    ]))
}

/// The product's gamesdb release, `None` when gamesdb does not know it. A
/// failed request is tried again, as Heroic does.
async fn gamesdb(
    api: &Api,
    access_token: &str,
    release: &Release,
) -> Result<Option<Value>, GogError> {
    let url = endpoint(
        &api.gamesdb,
        &[
            "platforms",
            "gog",
            "external_releases",
            &release.external_id,
        ],
    )?;
    let request = || {
        let request = api.http.get(url.clone()).bearer_auth(access_token);
        match &release.certificate {
            Some(certificate) => request.header("X-GOG-Library-Cert", certificate),
            None => request,
        }
    };
    match send_retrying(request, 3, Duration::from_millis(500)).await? {
        Some(response) => bounded_json(response, 4 * 1024 * 1024).await.map(Some),
        None => Ok(None),
    }
}

/// The store's product, which describes every product, DLC included.
async fn product(api: &Api, id: &str) -> Result<Value, GogError> {
    let mut url = endpoint(&api.api, &["products", id])?;
    url.query_pairs_mut().append_pair("locale", "en-US");
    api.get_public(url).await
}

/// A gamesdb localized text: every language's, else English.
fn localized(value: &Value) -> Option<String> {
    ["*", "en-US"]
        .iter()
        .find_map(|key| value[key].as_str())
        .filter(|text| !text.is_empty())
        .map(str::to_owned)
}

/// A gamesdb image in `formatter`'s size, as JPEG.
fn image(value: &Value, formatter: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let format = value["url_format"].as_str()?;
    safe_https_url(
        &format
            .replace("{formatter}", formatter)
            .replace("{ext}", "jpg"),
    )
}

pub(crate) fn endpoint(base: &str, segments: &[&str]) -> Result<Url, GogError> {
    let mut url = Url::parse(base).map_err(|_| GogError::Protocol)?;
    url.path_segments_mut()
        .map_err(|_| GogError::Protocol)?
        .pop_if_empty()
        .extend(segments);
    Ok(url)
}
```

```rs
use super::*;
use serde_json::json;

#[test]
fn gamesdb_images_take_their_size_as_jpeg() {
    let cover =
        json!({"url_format": "https://images.gog.com/7fbb{formatter}.{ext}?namespace=gamesdb"});
    assert_eq!(
        image(&cover, "_glx_vertical_cover").as_deref(),
        Some("https://images.gog.com/7fbb_glx_vertical_cover.jpg?namespace=gamesdb")
    );
    assert_eq!(
        image(&cover, "").as_deref(),
        Some("https://images.gog.com/7fbb.jpg?namespace=gamesdb")
    );
    assert_eq!(image(&json!(null), ""), None);
    assert_eq!(
        image(
            &json!({"url_format": "http://images.gog.com/a{formatter}.{ext}"}),
            ""
        ),
        None
    );
}

#[test]
fn titles_prefer_every_languages_then_english() {
    assert_eq!(
        localized(&json!({"*": "The Witcher", "en-US": "The Witcher (EN)"})).as_deref(),
        Some("The Witcher")
    );
    assert_eq!(
        localized(&json!({"en-US": "Cyberpunk 2077"})).as_deref(),
        Some("Cyberpunk 2077")
    );
    assert_eq!(localized(&json!({"*": ""})), None);
}

#[test]
fn library_records_name_their_product_either_way() {
    let release =
        Release::of(&json!({"platform_id": "gog", "external_id": 1207658924, "certificate": "c"}));
    assert_eq!(release.external_id, "1207658924");
    assert_eq!(release.certificate.as_deref(), Some("c"));
    let release = Release::of(&json!({"platform_id": "steam", "external_id": "620"}));
    assert_eq!(
        (release.platform_id.as_str(), release.external_id.as_str()),
        ("steam", "620")
    );
}

#[test]
fn endpoints_escape_their_segments() {
    assert_eq!(
        endpoint(
            "https://galaxy-library.gog.com",
            &["users", "48628349957132247", "releases"]
        )
        .unwrap()
        .as_str(),
        "https://galaxy-library.gog.com/users/48628349957132247/releases"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        endpoint("https://api.gog.com", &["products", "../x"])
            .unwrap()
            .as_str(),
        "https://api.gog.com/products/..%2Fx"
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_gamesdb_release_tells_the_games_page() {
    let info = GameInfo::of_release(&json!({
        "summary": {"*": "Short."},
        "first_release_date": "2014-10-13T00:00:00+0000",
        "available_languages": [{"code": "en-US"}, {"code": "fr-FR"}],
        "game": {
            "summary": {"*": "The Evil Within embodies survival horror."},
            "first_release_date": "2014-10-14T00:00:00+0000",
            "developers": [{"name": "Tango Gameworks"}],
            "publishers": [{"name": "Bethesda Softworks"}],
            "genres": [{"name": {"*": "Adventure", "en-US": "Adventure"}}, {"name": {"*": "Shooter"}}],
            "aggregated_rating": 75.1176,
        },
    }));
    assert_eq!(
        info,
        GameInfo {
            summary: "The Evil Within embodies survival horror.".into(),
            developers: vec!["Tango Gameworks".into()],
            publishers: vec!["Bethesda Softworks".into()],
            release_date: Some(1_413_158_400),
            genres: vec!["Adventure".into(), "Shooter".into()],
            rating: Some(75),
            languages: vec!["en-US".into(), "fr-FR".into()],
        }
    );
    let unknown = GameInfo::of_release(&json!({"game": {"aggregated_rating": 0}}));
    assert_eq!(
        unknown,
        GameInfo::default(),
        "an unrated game has no rating"
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_game_joins_the_library_when_its_record_was_created_or_owned_first() {
    assert_eq!(
        added_at(&json!({"date_created": 1_590_000_000, "owned_since": 1_500_000_000})),
        Some(1_500_000_000)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        added_at(&json!({"date_created": 1_590_000_000, "owned_since": null})),
        Some(1_590_000_000)
    );
    assert_eq!(added_at(&json!({"date_created": 0})), None);
    assert_eq!(added_at(&json!({})), None);
}
```

`crates/storefronts/gog-kit/src/manifest.rs`:

```rs
//! GOG content system generation 2 documents: a build's manifest, which names
//! its depots and redistributables, the redistributables' repository, and each
//! depot's manifest, which names its files and their chunks. They arrive
//! zlib-compressed from the CDN.
use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet, hash_map::Entry};

use obelisk_core::install::safe_relative_path;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use crate::GogError;

/// Chunks are cut at 10 MiB, but a file's last one may reach twice that.
pub(crate) const MAX_CHUNK_BYTES: u64 = 32 * 1024 * 1024;
/// Where Galaxy keeps a product's support files, which only its installer
/// scripts read.
pub(crate) const SUPPORT_DIRECTORY: &str = "gog-support";

/// One build of a product, as `builds?generation=2` lists it.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize)]
pub(crate) struct Build {
    /// The build's identity, which its manifest records too.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub build_id: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub branch: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub generation: u32,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub version_name: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub link: String,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub(crate) struct Builds {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub items: Vec<Build>,
}

impl Builds {
    /// The newest build of the default branch, as Galaxy picks it: GOG lists
    /// the newest first, older generations among them.
    pub fn current(self) -> Option<Build> {
        self.items
            .into_iter()
            .find(|build| build.branch.is_none())
            .filter(|build| build.generation == 2)
    }
}

/// A build's manifest.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub(crate) struct BuildManifest {
    pub base_product_id: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub build_id: String,
    /// The folder Galaxy installs into. A Mac build may name its application
    /// bundle itself.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub install_directory: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub depots: Vec<Depot>,
    /// The redistributables the build needs, such as `MSVC2017`.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub dependencies: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub products: Vec<Product>,
    /// The build's installer scripts run in the Install Script Interpreter.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub script_interpreter: bool,
}

impl BuildManifest {
    /// Where the build's files go inside the installation folder: inside its
    /// bundle when the build names one, so the bundle keeps its `.app` name.
    pub fn content_root(&self) -> Result<String, GogError> {
        let directory = self.install_directory.replace('\\', "/");
        if !directory.to_ascii_lowercase().ends_with(".app") {
            return Ok(String::new());
        }
        safe_relative_path(&directory)?;
        if directory.contains('/') {
            return Err(GogError::Protocol);
        }
        Ok(directory)
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize, Serialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct Product {
    pub product_id: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub name: String,
    /// The installer a product without installer scripts runs, among its
    /// support files.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub temp_executable: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub temp_arguments: String,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub(crate) struct Depot {
    pub product_id: String,
    pub manifest: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub languages: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub size: u64,
}

impl Depot {
    /// Whether the depot belongs to an installation in `language`, such as
    /// `fr-FR`: a depot of every language, or of the language itself.
    pub fn speaks(&self, language: &str) -> bool {
        let base = |tag: &str| {
            tag.split(['-', '_'])
                .next()
                .unwrap_or(tag)
                .to_ascii_lowercase()
        };
        self.languages.iter().any(|tag| {
            tag == "*" || tag.eq_ignore_ascii_case(language) || base(tag) == base(language)
        })
    }

    pub fn universal(&self) -> bool {
        self.languages.iter().any(|tag| tag == "*")
    }
}

/// The depots an installation in `language` holds, of the products it owns:
/// GOG's own language, else English, as Galaxy falls back.
pub(crate) fn depots<'a>(
    manifest: &'a BuildManifest,
    products: &HashSet<&str>,
    language: &str,
) -> Vec<&'a Depot> {
    let owned: Vec<&Depot> = manifest
        .depots
        .iter()
        .filter(|depot| products.contains(depot.product_id.as_str()))
        .collect();
    let spoken = |language: &str| {
        owned
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .filter(|depot| depot.speaks(language))
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
    };
    let localized = spoken(language);
    if localized.iter().any(|depot| !depot.universal()) || language.eq_ignore_ascii_case("en-US") {
        return localized;
    }
    spoken("en-US")
}

/// The redistributables' repository, which every build's dependencies name.
#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub(crate) struct DependencyRepository {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub depots: Vec<DependencyDepot>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub(crate) struct DependencyDepot {
    pub dependency_id: String,
    pub manifest: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub executable: DependencyExecutable,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, Deserialize)]
pub(crate) struct DependencyExecutable {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub path: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub arguments: String,
}

impl DependencyDepot {
    /// The .NET Framework and XNA installers do not work in Wine: .NET games
    /// run on the Wine Mono Voile carries. Neither are Windows Installer
    /// packages run, nor installed.
    pub fn installs_in_wine(&self) -> bool {
        let id = self.dependency_id.to_ascii_lowercase();
        let framework = id.starts_with("dotnet")
            && !id.starts_with("dotnetcore")
            && !id.starts_with("dotnetdesktopruntime");
        !framework
            && !id.starts_with("xna")
            && !self.executable.path.to_ascii_lowercase().ends_with(".msi")
    }
}

/// A depot's manifest.
#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub(crate) struct DepotManifest {
    pub depot: DepotItems,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub(crate) struct DepotItems {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub items: Vec<Item>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "type")]
pub(crate) enum Item {
    DepotFile(File),
    DepotDirectory(Directory),
    DepotLink(Link),
    /// Kinds this client does not know are refused at validation.
    #[serde(other)]
    Unknown,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize)]
pub(crate) struct Directory {
    pub path: String,
}

/// A link, whose target GOG gives from the installation's root.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize)]
pub(crate) struct Link {
    pub path: String,
    pub target: String,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize)]
pub(crate) struct File {
    pub path: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub chunks: Vec<Chunk>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub flags: Vec<String>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub(crate) struct Chunk {
    pub md5: String,
    pub size: u64,
    pub compressed_md5: String,
    pub compressed_size: u64,
}

impl File {
    pub fn size(&self) -> u64 {
        self.chunks.iter().map(|chunk| chunk.size).sum()
    }
    pub fn executable(&self) -> bool {
        self.flags.iter().any(|flag| flag == "executable")
    }
    fn support(&self) -> bool {
        self.flags.iter().any(|flag| flag == "support")
    }
}

/// Where the content system keeps the document or chunk `hash` names: under
/// `ab/cd/abcdef…`. A manifest may already name that path.
pub(crate) fn galaxy_path(hash: &str) -> Result<String, GogError> {
    if hash.contains('/') {
        let parts: Vec<_> = hash.split('/').collect();
        let well_formed = parts.len() == 3
            && parts[0].len() == 2
            && parts[1].len() == 2
            && is_md5(parts[2])
            && parts[2].starts_with(&format!("{}{}", parts[0], parts[1]));
        return well_formed
            .then(|| hash.to_owned())
            .ok_or(GogError::Protocol);
    }
    if !is_md5(hash) {
        return Err(GogError::Protocol);
    }
    Ok(format!("{}/{}/{hash}", &hash[..2], &hash[2..4]))
}

pub(crate) fn is_md5(value: &str) -> bool {
    value.len() == 32 && value.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_hexdigit())
}

/// Which secure link serves a file's chunks.
pub(crate) const DEPENDENCIES: &str = "dependencies";

/// Every file an installation holds, in manifest order, with where its chunks
/// come from. Directories and links follow.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub(crate) struct Installed {
    pub files: Vec<InstalledFile>,
    pub directories: Vec<String>,
    pub links: Vec<Link>,
    /// Each file's place in `files`, by its lowercased path.
    positions: HashMap<String, usize>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub(crate) struct InstalledFile {
    /// The file's place in the installation folder.
    pub path: String,
    pub file: File,
    /// The product whose secure link serves its chunks, or `DEPENDENCIES`.
    pub source: String,
}

impl Installed {
    /// Adds a depot's items under `root`, a folder inside the installation;
    /// a later depot's file replaces an earlier one of the same path, as
    /// Galaxy installs them in order. `source` serves their chunks. A
    /// product's support files go to its own support folder.
    pub fn add(&mut self, root: &str, source: &str, items: Vec<Item>) -> Result<(), GogError> {
        let place = |path: &str| -> Result<String, GogError> {
            let path = normalized(path)?;
            Ok(match root {
                "" => path,
                root => format!("{root}/{path}"),
            })
        };
        for item in items {
            match item {
                Item::DepotFile(file) => {
                    let path = match file.support() {
                        // Only a product's files have support files.
                        true if source == DEPENDENCIES => continue,
                        true => format!("{SUPPORT_DIRECTORY}/{source}/{}", normalized(&file.path)?),
                        false => place(&file.path)?,
                    };
                    let installed = InstalledFile {
                        path,
                        file,
                        source: source.to_owned(),
                    };
                    match self.positions.entry(installed.path.to_lowercase()) {
                        Entry::Occupied(kept) => self.files[*kept.get()] = installed,
                        Entry::Vacant(place) => {
                            place.insert(self.files.len());
                            self.files.push(installed);
                        }
                    }
                }
                Item::DepotDirectory(directory) => self.directories.push(place(&directory.path)?),
                Item::DepotLink(link) => self.links.push(Link {
                    path: place(&link.path)?,
                    target: place(&link.target)?,
                }),
                Item::Unknown => return Err(GogError::Protocol),
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Refuses what no installation may hold: an unsafe or duplicate path, a
    /// file inside another file, a malformed chunk, or a link leaving the
    /// installation.
    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), GogError> {
        let mut paths = HashSet::new();
        for installed in &self.files {
            safe_relative_path(&installed.path)?;
            if !paths.insert(installed.path.to_lowercase()) {
                return Err(GogError::Protocol);
            }
            for chunk in &installed.file.chunks {
                if !is_md5(&chunk.md5)
                    || !is_md5(&chunk.compressed_md5)
                    || chunk.size == 0
                    || chunk.size > MAX_CHUNK_BYTES
                    || chunk.compressed_size == 0
                    || chunk.compressed_size > MAX_CHUNK_BYTES * 2
                {
                    return Err(GogError::Protocol);
                }
            }
        }
        // No file may sit inside another file, or behind a link.
        let links: HashSet<String> = self
            .links
            .iter()
            .map(|link| link.path.to_lowercase())
            .collect();
        for installed in &self.files {
            let path = safe_relative_path(&installed.path)?;
            for parent in path.ancestors().skip(1) {
                let parent = parent.to_string_lossy().to_lowercase();
                if !parent.is_empty() && (paths.contains(&parent) || links.contains(&parent)) {
                    return Err(GogError::Protocol);
                }
            }
        }
        for directory in &self.directories {
            safe_relative_path(directory)?;
        }
        for link in &self.links {
            safe_relative_path(&link.path)?;
            safe_relative_path(&link.target)
                .map_err(|_| GogError::UnsafePath(link.path.clone()))?;
            if paths.contains(&link.path.to_lowercase()) {
                return Err(GogError::UnsafePath(link.path.clone()));
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn total_bytes(&self) -> u64 {
        self.files
            .iter()
            .map(|installed| installed.file.size())
            .sum()
    }
}

/// A manifest path with forward slashes and no leading separator: GOG's
/// depots spell them either way, whatever their platform.
fn normalized(path: &str) -> Result<String, GogError> {
    let path = path.replace('\\', "/");
    let path = path.trim_start_matches('/');
    if path.is_empty() {
        return Err(GogError::Protocol);
    }
    Ok(path.to_owned())
}

/// The relative target a link at `path` needs to reach `target`, both from
/// the installation's root.
pub(crate) fn relative_target(path: &str, target: &str) -> String {
    let depth = path.split('/').count().saturating_sub(1);
    let mut relative = "../".repeat(depth);
    relative.push_str(target);
    relative
}
```

```rs
use super::*;
use serde_json::json;

fn build_manifest(value: serde_json::Value) -> BuildManifest {
    serde_json::from_value(value).unwrap()
}

/// The Witcher's Mac build manifest as GOG serves it, trimmed.
fn witcher() -> BuildManifest {
    build_manifest(json!({
        "version": 2,
        "baseProductId": "1207658924",
        "platform": "osx",
        "products": [{"name": "The Witcher: Enhanced Edition", "productId": "1207658924",
                      "temp_executable": "", "temp_arguments": ""}],
        "buildId": "57325240911024496",
        "installDirectory": "The Witcher Enhanced Edition",
        "depots": [
            {"manifest": "24b59fcf4a04b94f6cd03dbae1fe5f3f", "size": 15_104_925_994_u64,
             "compressedSize": 10_318_796_398_u64, "productId": "1207658924", "languages": ["en-US"]},
            {"manifest": "47554788d74dcc53009bfd8b171324e6", "size": 996, "compressedSize": 330,
             "productId": "1207658924", "languages": ["en-US"], "isGogDepot": true},
        ],
    }))

#[test]
fn the_current_build_is_the_newest_of_the_default_branch() {
    let builds: Builds = serde_json::from_value(json!({"items": [
        {"build_id": "3", "branch": "beta", "generation": 2, "version_name": "beta", "link": "https://a/3"},
        {"build_id": "2", "branch": null, "generation": 2, "version_name": "1.2", "link": "https://a/2"},
        {"build_id": "1", "branch": null, "generation": 2, "version_name": "1.1", "link": "https://a/1"},
    ]}))
    .unwrap();
    let current = builds.current().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(current.version_name, "1.2");
    assert_eq!(
        current.build_id, "2",
        "an installation compares its build to it"
    );
    let legacy: Builds = serde_json::from_value(json!({"items": [
        {"build_id": "1", "branch": null, "generation": 1, "legacy_build_id": 7, "link": "https://a/1"},
    ]}))
    .unwrap();
    assert!(
        legacy.current().is_none(),
        "a generation 1 build is not installed"
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_mac_build_that_names_its_bundle_installs_inside_it() {
    assert_eq!(witcher().content_root().unwrap(), "");
    let mut stardew = witcher();
    stardew.install_directory = "Stardew Valley.app".into();
    assert_eq!(stardew.content_root().unwrap(), "Stardew Valley.app");
    stardew.install_directory = "../Escape.app".into();
    assert!(stardew.content_root().is_err());
}

#[test]
fn depots_follow_the_language_then_english() {
    let manifest = build_manifest(json!({
        "baseProductId": "1",
        "depots": [
            {"manifest": "a", "productId": "1", "languages": ["*"], "size": 1},
            {"manifest": "en", "productId": "1", "languages": ["en-US"], "size": 10},
            {"manifest": "fr", "productId": "1", "languages": ["fr-FR"], "size": 100},
            {"manifest": "dlc", "productId": "2", "languages": ["*"], "size": 1000},
            {"manifest": "other", "productId": "3", "languages": ["*"], "size": 10000},
        ],
    }));
    let owned = HashSet::from(["1", "2"]);
    let names = |language: &str| -> Vec<&str> {
        depots(&manifest, &owned, language)
            .iter()
            .map(|depot| depot.manifest.as_str())
            .collect()
    };
    assert_eq!(names("fr-FR"), ["a", "fr", "dlc"]);
    assert_eq!(
        names("fr"),
        ["a", "fr", "dlc"],
        "a bare language matches its region"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        names("de-DE"),
        ["a", "en", "dlc"],
        "English stands in for a missing language"
    );
    assert_eq!(names("en-US"), ["a", "en", "dlc"]);
}

#[test]
fn galaxy_paths_split_the_hash() {
    assert_eq!(
        galaxy_path("24b59fcf4a04b94f6cd03dbae1fe5f3f").unwrap(),
        "24/b5/24b59fcf4a04b94f6cd03dbae1fe5f3f"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        galaxy_path("24/b5/24b59fcf4a04b94f6cd03dbae1fe5f3f").unwrap(),
        "24/b5/24b59fcf4a04b94f6cd03dbae1fe5f3f"
    );
    for hash in [
        "",
        "../b5/24b59fcf4a04b94f6cd03dbae1fe5f3f",
        "zz",
        "aa/bb/24b59fcf4a04b94f6cd03dbae1fe5f3f",
    ] {
        assert!(galaxy_path(hash).is_err(), "{hash}");
    }
}

fn chunk(md5: &str) -> serde_json::Value {
    json!({"md5": md5, "size": 4, "compressedMd5": md5, "compressedSize": 12})
}

fn items(value: serde_json::Value) -> Vec<Item> {
    serde_json::from_value::<DepotManifest>(json!({"depot": {"items": value}, "version": 2}))
        .unwrap()
        .depot
        .items
}

#[test]
fn files_land_under_the_content_root_and_support_files_apart() {
    let md5 = "efd1e52118fbc32baf1a429b0b80fcad";
    let mut installed = Installed::default();
    installed
        .add(
            "Game.app",
            "1",
            items(json!([
                {"type": "DepotFile", "path": "Contents\\MacOS\\Game", "chunks": [chunk(md5)], "flags": ["executable"]},
                {"type": "DepotFile", "path": "setup.exe", "chunks": [chunk(md5)], "flags": ["support"]},
                {"type": "DepotDirectory", "path": "Contents/Resources"},
                {"type": "DepotLink", "path": "Contents/Frameworks/X.framework/X",
                 "target": "Contents/Frameworks/X.framework/Versions/A/X"},
            ])),
        )
        .unwrap();
    installed
        .add(
            "Game.app",
            DEPENDENCIES,
            items(json!([
                {"type": "DepotFile", "path": "__redist/ISI/scriptinterpreter.exe", "chunks": [chunk(md5)]},
                {"type": "DepotFile", "path": "ignored.txt", "chunks": [chunk(md5)], "flags": ["support"]},
            ])),
        )
        .unwrap();
    let paths: Vec<_> = installed
        .files
        .iter()
        .map(|file| file.path.as_str())
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(
        paths,
        [
            "Game.app/Contents/MacOS/Game",
            "gog-support/1/setup.exe",
            "Game.app/__redist/ISI/scriptinterpreter.exe",
        ]
    );
    assert_eq!(installed.files[2].source, DEPENDENCIES);
    assert_eq!(installed.directories, ["Game.app/Contents/Resources"]);
    assert_eq!(
        installed.links[0].target,
        "Game.app/Contents/Frameworks/X.framework/Versions/A/X"
    );
    installed.validate().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(installed.total_bytes(), 12);
}

#[test]
fn a_later_depot_replaces_a_file_of_the_same_path() {
    let mut installed = Installed::default();

        .add(

        .add(

}

#[test]
fn validation_refuses_what_no_installation_may_hold() {
    let md5 = "efd1e52118fbc32baf1a429b0b80fcad";
    let refused = [
        json!([{"type": "DepotFile", "path": "../escape", "chunks": []}]),
        json!([{"type": "DepotFile", "path": ".obelisk-install.json", "chunks": []}]),
        json!([{"type": "DepotFile", "path": "a", "chunks": []},
               {"type": "DepotFile", "path": "a/b", "chunks": []}]),
        json!([{"type": "DepotFile", "path": "a", "chunks": [{"md5": "x", "size": 1, "compressedMd5": md5, "compressedSize": 1}]}]),
        json!([{"type": "DepotFile", "path": "a", "chunks": [{"md5": md5, "size": 0, "compressedMd5": md5, "compressedSize": 1}]}]),
        json!([{"type": "DepotLink", "path": "link", "target": "../../outside"}]),
        json!([{"type": "DepotLink", "path": "Versions/Current", "target": "Versions/A"},
               {"type": "DepotFile", "path": "Versions/Current/X", "chunks": []}]),
    ];
    for value in refused {
        let mut installed = Installed::default();
        let added = installed.add("", "1", items(value.clone()));
        assert!(added.is_err() || installed.validate().is_err(), "{value}");
    }
    let mut unknown = Installed::default();
    assert!(
        unknown
            .add("", "1", items(json!([{"type": "DepotPatch", "path": "a"}])))
            .is_err()
    );
}
```

`crates/storefronts/steam-kit/examples/inspect_autocloud_metadata.rs`:

```rs
//! Parse a read-only Obelisk metadata report without accessing actual save paths.
use std::{fs, path::Path};
use steam_kit::cloud::{AutoCloudPaths, CloudListing};
fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let path = std::env::args_os()
        .nth(1)
        .ok_or("metadata report required")?;
    let report: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(path)?)?;
    for app in report["apps"].as_array().ok_or("apps missing")? {
        let mac = app["os_list"]
            .as_array()
            .is_some_and(|v| v.iter().any(|os| os == "macos"));
        if !mac {
            continue;
        }
        let metadata = serde_json::from_value(app["ufs"].clone())?;
        let listing: Option<CloudListing> = serde_json::from_value(app["listing"].clone())?;
        // Fixture roots exercise parsing only. No filesystem scan. Existing
        // names use the manifest's authenticated identity for substitutions.
        let result = AutoCloudPaths::mac(
            &metadata,
            listing.as_ref().map_or(0x011000010000002a, |l| l.steam_id),
            Path::new("/Users/fixture"),
            Path::new("/Games/fixture"),
        );
        let status = match result {
            Err(error) => error.to_string(),
            Ok(paths) => {
                let mut mapped = 0;
                let mut failed = 0;
                for file in listing.into_iter().flat_map(|l| l.files) {
                    match paths.existing_file(&file) {
                        Ok(Some(_)) => mapped += 1,
                        Ok(None) => (),
                        Err(_) => failed += 1,
                    }
                }
                format!("parsed; mapped={mapped}; unmapped={failed}")
            }
        };
        println!("{} {}: {}", app["app_id"], app["name"], status);
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

`crates/storefronts/steam-kit/examples/inspect_cloud_saves.rs`:

```rs
//! Read-only local-discovery validation against an authenticated Cloud backup.
//! Stop the game before invoking this diagnostic. No save or Cloud data changes.
use sha1::{Digest, Sha1};
use std::{
    fs,
    io::{Read, Write},
    os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt,
    path::Path,
};
use steam_kit::cloud::{AutoCloudPaths, CloudListing, CloudMetadata};

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let args: Vec<_> = std::env::args_os().collect();
    if args.len() != 5 {
        return Err("usage: inspect_cloud_saves BACKUP_MANIFEST HOME INSTALL REPORT".into());
    }
    let backup: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(&args[1])?)?;
    let listing: CloudListing = serde_json::from_value(backup["listing"].clone())?;
    let metadata: CloudMetadata = serde_json::from_value(backup["ufs"].clone())?;
    if backup["operation"] != "read_only_cloud_backup"
        || backup["steam_id"].as_u64() != Some(listing.steam_id)
        || backup["app_id"].as_u64() != Some(u64::from(listing.app_id))
    {
        return Err("backup identity mismatch".into());
    }
    let paths = AutoCloudPaths::mac(
        &metadata,
        listing.steam_id,
        Path::new(&args[2]),
        Path::new(&args[3]),
    )?;
    let selected = paths.local_files(&listing.files)?;
    let mut entries = Vec::new();
    let mut matching = 0;
    for file in &selected {
        let (size, digest) = match fs::File::open(&file.path) {
            Ok(input) => {
                let mut bytes = Vec::new();
                input.take(256 * 1024 * 1024 + 1).read_to_end(&mut bytes)?;
                if bytes.len() > 256 * 1024 * 1024 {
                    return Err("save exceeds validation bound".into());
                }
                (
                    Some(bytes.len()),
                    Some(
                        Sha1::digest(&bytes)
                            .iter()
                            .map(|byte| format!("{byte:02x}"))
                            .collect::<String>(),
                    ),
                )
            }
            Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => (None, None),
            Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
        };
        let matches = listing.files.iter().any(|remote| {
            remote.name == file.name
                && Some(remote.size as usize) == size
                && Some(&remote.sha1) == digest.as_ref()
                && remote.platforms == file.platforms
        });
        matching += usize::from(matches);
        entries.push(serde_json::json!({"name":file.name, "path":file.path, "bytes":size, "sha1":digest, "platforms":file.platforms, "matches_remote":matches}));
    }
    let report = serde_json::json!({"operation":"read_only_local_cloud_discovery", "selected":entries, "selected_count":selected.len(), "matches_remote_count":matching});
    let mut output = fs::File::create_new(&args[4])?;
    output.set_permissions(fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o600))?;
    output.write_all(serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report)?.as_bytes())?;
    output.sync_all()?;
    println!(
        "{} files selected; {} match the verified remote backup",
        selected.len(),
        matching
    );
    Ok(())
}
```

`crates/storefronts/steam-kit/src/artwork.rs`:

```rs
//! A game's library artwork as its PICS app info names it, picked as Steam's
//! library asset cache picks it. Newer games publish their images only under a
//! hashed folder, such as `480bd879…/library_600x900.jpg`, and a game whose
//! artwork changed keeps its old images at the plain names: only PICS names
//! the current ones.
use serde_json::Value;

/// Each image's path under the game's store assets, in one language.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct LibraryArtwork {
    /// The portrait capsule, 300 × 450.
    pub cover: Option<String>,
    /// The wide hero, 1920 × 620.
    pub hero: Option<String>,
    pub logo: Option<String>,
    /// The library header, or the store's when the game has no library one.
    pub header: Option<String>,
    /// The app whose artwork stands in for the game's missing images, such
    /// as Rust's for its staging branch.
    pub parent: Option<u32>,
}

/// The artwork `pics`, a game's whole PICS app info, names in `language`, or
/// in English where it has none in it. Steam keeps each image at its standard
/// size, never the `image2x` one.
pub fn library_artwork(pics: &Value, language: &str) -> LibraryArtwork {
    let common = &pics["common"];
    let localized = |images: &Value| {
        [language, "english"]
            .into_iter()
            .find_map(|language| images[language].as_str().filter(|path| valid(path)))
            .map(String::from)
    };
    let image = |asset: &str| localized(&common["library_assets_full"][asset]["image"]);
    LibraryArtwork {
        cover: image("library_capsule"),
        hero: image("library_hero"),
        logo: image("library_logo"),
        header: image("library_header").or_else(|| localized(&common["header_image"])),
        parent: positive(&common["parent"]).and_then(|parent| u32::try_from(parent).ok()),
    }
}

/// A number of a game's PICS app info, which PICS mostly writes as text;
/// none when absent or 0.
fn positive(value: &Value) -> Option<u64> {
    match value {
        Value::String(text) => text.parse().ok(),
        value => value.as_u64(),
    }
    .filter(|value| *value > 0)
}

/// A file name, or one in a single folder, that stays under the game's assets.
fn valid(path: &str) -> bool {
    path.matches('/').count() <= 1
        && path.split('/').all(|part| {
            !part.is_empty()
                && !part.starts_with('.')
                && part
                    .bytes()
                    .all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b"._-".contains(&byte))
        })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use serde_json::json;

    #[test]
    fn names_the_hashed_images_in_the_language_or_in_english() {
        let pics = json!({ "common": {
            "header_image": { "english": "31bac6/header.jpg" },
            "library_assets_full": {
                "library_capsule": {
                    "image": { "english": "480bd8/library_600x900.jpg", "french": "9f0e1d/library_600x900_french.jpg" },
                    "image2x": { "english": "480bd8/library_600x900_2x.jpg" }
                },
                "library_hero": {
                    "image": { "english": "d75184/library_hero.jpg" },
                    "image2x": { "english": "d75184/library_hero_2x.jpg" }
                },
                "library_logo": { "image": { "english": "logo.png" } },
                "library_header": { "image": { "english": "31bac6/library_header.jpg" } }
            }
        }});
        assert_eq!(
            library_artwork(&pics, "french"),
            LibraryArtwork {
                cover: Some("9f0e1d/library_600x900_french.jpg".into()),
                hero: Some("d75184/library_hero.jpg".into()),
                logo: Some("logo.png".into()),
                header: Some("31bac6/library_header.jpg".into()),
                parent: None,
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(
            library_artwork(&pics, "german").cover.as_deref(),
            Some("480bd8/library_600x900.jpg")
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_game_without_a_library_header_has_its_store_one() {
        let pics = json!({ "common": { "header_image": { "english": "31bac6/header.jpg" } } });
        assert_eq!(

            Some("31bac6/header.jpg")
        );
    }

        assert_eq!(
            library_artwork(&pics, "english"),

                parent: Some(252_490),
                ..LibraryArtwork::default()
            }
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn names_nothing_a_game_does_not_publish() {
        assert_eq!(
            library_artwork(&json!({}), "english"),
            LibraryArtwork::default()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn ignores_a_path_that_would_leave_the_assets() {
        for path in [
            "../440/header.jpg",
            "a/b/header.jpg",
            "/header.jpg",
            "",
            "a/",
            "x?y.jpg",
            "https://evil/x.jpg",
        ] {
            let pics = json!({ "common": { "header_image": { "english": path } } });
            assert_eq!(library_artwork(&pics, "english").header, None, "{path}");
        }
    }
}
```

`crates/storefronts/steam-kit/src/auth.rs`:

```rs
//! Steam client authentication through Valve's HTTPS Authentication service.
//!
//! Passwords are RSA-encrypted for Steam and are never retained in a session.
//! Session IDs, QR challenges, and tokens are deliberately not `Debug`.
//! Persist refresh tokens in the host's secure credential store, never a library JSON.

mod wire;

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;

use std::time::Duration;

use base64::{Engine as _, engine::general_purpose};
use obelisk_core::transfer::BodyError;
use prost::Message;
use reqwest::{Client, Method};
use rsa::{
    BigUint, Pkcs1v15Encrypt, RsaPublicKey,
    rand_core::{OsRng, RngCore},
    traits::PublicKeyParts,
};
use thiserror::Error;

const AUTH_API: &str = "https://api.steampowered.com/IAuthenticationService";
const MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES: usize = 1_048_576;
const MAX_TOKEN_BYTES: usize = 32_768;
/// Steam's sites that read its login cookie.
const WEB_DOMAINS: [&str; 4] = [
    "store.steampowered.com",
    "steamcommunity.com",
    "help.steampowered.com",
    "checkout.steampowered.com",
];

#[derive(Debug, Error, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum AuthError {
    #[error("backend.steam.auth.invalidCredentialsInput")]
    InvalidCredentialsInput,
    #[error("backend.steam.auth.credentialsRejected")]
    CredentialsRejected,
    #[error("backend.steam.auth.guardRejected")]
    GuardRejected,
    #[error("backend.steam.auth.unsupportedConfirmation")]
    UnsupportedConfirmation,
    #[error("backend.steam.auth.expired")]
    Expired,
    #[error("backend.steam.auth.rateLimited")]
    RateLimited,
    #[error("backend.steam.auth.agreementRequired")]
    AgreementRequired,
    #[error("backend.steam.auth.network")]
    Network,
    #[error("{}", crate::message::format("backend.steam.auth.http", &[.status.to_string()]))]
    Http { status: u16 },
    #[error("{}", crate::message::format("backend.steam.auth.steam", &[.result.to_string()]))]
    Steam { result: i32 },
    #[error("backend.steam.auth.protocol")]
    Protocol,
}

/// Steam's offered methods. Only code methods accept `submit_guard`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum GuardType {
    None,
    EmailCode,
    DeviceCode,
    DeviceConfirmation,
    EmailConfirmation,
    MachineToken,
    Unknown,
}

impl GuardType {
    fn from_wire(value: i32) -> Self {
        match value {
            1 => Self::None,
            2 => Self::EmailCode,
            3 => Self::DeviceCode,
            4 => Self::DeviceConfirmation,
            5 => Self::EmailConfirmation,
            6 => Self::MachineToken,
            _ => Self::Unknown,
        }
    }

    fn code_value(self) -> Result<i32, AuthError> {
        match self {
            Self::EmailCode => Ok(2),
            Self::DeviceCode => Ok(3),
            _ => Err(AuthError::UnsupportedConfirmation),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct GuardConfirmation {
    pub kind: GuardType,
    /// Steam's masked email destination, if supplied. Present as text only.
    pub message: String,
}

/// One in-progress authorization request. Dropping it cancels local polling.
pub struct AuthSession {
    client_id: u64,
    request_id: Vec<u8>,
    steam_id: Option<u64>,
    challenge_url: Option<String>,
    confirmations: Vec<GuardConfirmation>,
    interval: Duration,
    had_remote_interaction: bool,
    completed: bool,
}

impl AuthSession {
    pub fn challenge_url(&self) -> Option<&str> {
        self.challenge_url.as_deref()
    }

    pub fn allowed_confirmations(&self) -> &[GuardConfirmation] {
        &self.confirmations
    }

    /// Wait at least this long between calls to `poll`.
    pub fn polling_interval(&self) -> Duration {
        self.interval
    }

    pub fn had_remote_interaction(&self) -> bool {
        self.had_remote_interaction
    }
}

/// Secrets returned only after Steam approves the session.
/// The Connection Manager must still validate the refresh token at logon.
pub struct AuthTokens {
    pub account_name: String,
    pub steam_id: u64,
    pub refresh_token: String,
}

impl AuthTokens {
    /// Restore a saved token for CM logon. This parses its routing identity; it
    /// does not verify the JWT signature or prove that Steam will accept it.
    pub fn restore(account_name: String, refresh_token: String) -> Result<Self, AuthError> {
        if account_name.is_empty() || account_name.len() > 256 {
            return Err(AuthError::Protocol);
        }
        let steam_id = steam_id_from_refresh_token(&refresh_token)?;
        Ok(Self {
            account_name,
            steam_id,
            refresh_token,
        })
    }
}

/// Reads the routing SteamID from a token, without claiming JWT verification.
pub fn steam_id_from_refresh_token(token: &str) -> Result<u64, AuthError> {
    if token.len() > MAX_TOKEN_BYTES {
        return Err(AuthError::Protocol);
    }
    let mut components = token.split('.');
    let header = components.next().ok_or(AuthError::Protocol)?;
    let payload = components.next().ok_or(AuthError::Protocol)?;
    let signature = components.next().ok_or(AuthError::Protocol)?;
    if header.is_empty() || signature.is_empty() || components.next().is_some() {
        return Err(AuthError::Protocol);
    }
    let payload = general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
        .decode(payload)
        .map_err(|_| AuthError::Protocol)?;
    let claims: serde_json::Value =
        serde_json::from_slice(&payload).map_err(|_| AuthError::Protocol)?;
    let steam_id = claims
        .get("sub")
        .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)
        .and_then(|value| value.parse::<u64>().ok())
        .filter(|value| valid_individual_steam_id(*value))
        .ok_or(AuthError::Protocol)?;
    Ok(steam_id)
}

/// Cookies that sign Steam's sites in with a web access token, as Valve's
/// client signs its own browser in, and as SteamKit's `webLogOn` does. Ask
/// the token over the account's CM session (`Client::web_cookies`): Steam
/// refuses a client refresh token sent to its Web API for one, and revoked
/// the session the one time Obelisk tried.
pub fn web_cookies(steam_id: u64, access_token: &str) -> Vec<WebCookie> {
    let login = format!("{steam_id}%7C%7C{access_token}");
    let session = random_hex::<12>();
    let client_session = random_hex::<8>();
    WEB_DOMAINS
        .into_iter()
        .flat_map(|domain| {
            [
                WebCookie {
                    domain,
                    name: "steamLoginSecure",
                    value: login.clone(),
                    http_only: true,
                },
                WebCookie {
                    domain,
                    name: "sessionid",
                    value: session.clone(),
                    http_only: false,
                },
                WebCookie {
                    domain,
                    name: "clientsessionid",
                    value: client_session.clone(),
                    http_only: false,
                },
            ]
        })
        .collect()
}

fn random_hex<const BYTES: usize>() -> String {
    let mut bytes = [0u8; BYTES];
    OsRng.fill_bytes(&mut bytes);
    crate::content::hex(&bytes)
}

/// A cookie that signs Steam's sites in. Its value is a secret: no `Debug`.
pub struct WebCookie {
    pub domain: &'static str,
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub value: String,
    /// Steam's pages read `sessionid` from script; the login stays out of reach.
    pub http_only: bool,
}

fn valid_individual_steam_id(value: u64) -> bool {
    value >> 56 == 1 && (value >> 52) & 0xf == 1 && value as u32 != 0
}

pub struct AuthClient {
    http: Client,
    endpoint: String,
}

impl AuthClient {
    /// Supply a HTTPS client with TLS certificate validation and redirects disabled.
    pub fn new(http: Client) -> Self {
        Self {
            http,
            endpoint: AUTH_API.into(),
        }
    }

    pub async fn begin_qr(&self) -> Result<AuthSession, AuthError> {
        let response: wire::BeginQrResponse = self
            .call(
                Method::POST,
                "BeginAuthSessionViaQR",
                &wire::BeginQrRequest {
                    device: Some(device_details()),
                    website: "Client".into(),
                },
                false,
            )
            .await?;
        let challenge_url = validate_challenge_url(response.challenge_url)?;
        make_session(
            response.client_id,
            response.request_id,
            None,
            Some(challenge_url),
            response.confirmations,
            response.interval,
        )
    }

    pub async fn begin_credentials(
        &self,
        account_name: &str,
        password: &str,
    ) -> Result<AuthSession, AuthError> {
        let account_name = account_name.trim();
        let password = steam_password(password);
        if account_name.is_empty() || account_name.len() > 256 || password.is_empty() {
            return Err(AuthError::InvalidCredentialsInput);
        }
        let key: wire::PasswordKeyResponse = self
            .call(
                Method::GET,
                "GetPasswordRSAPublicKey",
                &wire::PasswordKeyRequest {
                    account_name: account_name.into(),
                },
                false,
            )
            .await?;
        let encrypted_password = encrypt_password(&password, &key)?;
        let response: wire::BeginCredentialsResponse = self
            .call(
                Method::POST,
                "BeginAuthSessionViaCredentials",
                &wire::BeginCredentialsRequest {
                    account_name: account_name.into(),
                    encrypted_password,
                    encryption_timestamp: key.timestamp,
                    remember_login: true,
                    persistence: 1,
                    website: "Client".into(),
                    device: Some(device_details()),
                },
                false,
            )
            .await?;
        require_no_agreement(&response.agreement_url)?;
        if !valid_individual_steam_id(response.steam_id) {
            return Err(AuthError::Protocol);
        }
        make_session(
            response.client_id,
            response.request_id,
            Some(response.steam_id),
            None,
            response.confirmations,
            response.interval,
        )
    }

    pub async fn submit_guard(
        &self,
        session: &AuthSession,
        code: &str,
        kind: GuardType,
    ) -> Result<(), AuthError> {
        if session.completed {
            return Err(AuthError::Expired);
        }
        let kind_value = kind.code_value()?;
        if !session.confirmations.iter().any(|value| value.kind == kind) {
            return Err(AuthError::UnsupportedConfirmation);
        }
        let steam_id = session.steam_id.ok_or(AuthError::UnsupportedConfirmation)?;
        let code = code.trim();
        if code.len() != 5 || !code.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_alphanumeric()) {
            return Err(AuthError::GuardRejected);
        }
        let response: wire::GuardResponse = self
            .call(
                Method::POST,
                "UpdateAuthSessionWithSteamGuardCode",
                &wire::GuardRequest {
                    client_id: session.client_id,
                    steam_id,
                    code: code.to_ascii_uppercase(),
                    kind: kind_value,
                },
                true,
            )
            .await?;
        require_no_agreement(&response.agreement_url)
    }

    pub async fn poll(&self, session: &mut AuthSession) -> Result<Option<AuthTokens>, AuthError> {
        if session.completed {
            return Err(AuthError::Expired);
        }
        let response: wire::PollResponse = self
            .call(
                Method::POST,
                "PollAuthSessionStatus",
                &wire::PollRequest {
                    client_id: session.client_id,
                    request_id: session.request_id.clone(),
                },
                false,
            )
            .await?;
        apply_poll_response(session, response)
    }

    async fn call<Request, Response>(
        &self,
        method: Method,
        operation: &'static str,
        input: &Request,
        accept_duplicate: bool,
    ) -> Result<Response, AuthError>
    where
        Request: Message,
        Response: Message + Default,
    {
        let fields = [
            ("format", "protobuf_raw".to_owned()),
            (
                "input_protobuf_encoded",
                general_purpose::STANDARD.encode(input.encode_to_vec()),
            ),
        ];
        let request = self
            .http
            .request(method.clone(), format!("{}/{operation}/v1/", self.endpoint))
            .timeout(Duration::from_secs(30));
        let request = if method == Method::GET {
            request.query(&fields)
        } else {
            request.form(&fields)
        };
        // Do not attach reqwest errors: GET URLs include the encoded account name.
        let response = request.send().await.map_err(|_| AuthError::Network)?;
        if response.status().as_u16() == 429 {
            return Err(AuthError::RateLimited);
        }
        let result = response
            .headers()
            .get("x-eresult")
            .and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok())
            .and_then(|value| value.parse::<i32>().ok());
        if let Some(result) = result {
            check_result(result, accept_duplicate)?;
        }
        if !response.status().is_success() {
            return Err(AuthError::Http {
                status: response.status().as_u16(),
            });
        }
        if result.is_none() {
            return Err(AuthError::Protocol);
        }
        let body = crate::client::read_bounded(response, MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES)
            .await
            .map_err(|error| match error {
                BodyError::Size => AuthError::Protocol,
                BodyError::Network | BodyError::Cancelled => AuthError::Network,
            })?;
        Response::decode(body.as_slice()).map_err(|_| AuthError::Protocol)
    }
}

fn device_details() -> wire::DeviceDetails {
    wire::DeviceDetails {
        name: "Obelisk on macOS".into(),
        platform: 1,   // SteamClient: produces a token usable for CM logon.
        os_type: -102, // MacOSUnknown: avoids claiming an obsolete macOS version.
    }
}

/// The password as Steam's own client sends it: its ASCII characters, cut to
/// 64. A longer password only ever worked there by its first 64.
fn steam_password(password: &str) -> String {
    password.chars().filter(char::is_ascii).take(64).collect()
}

fn encrypt_password(
    password: &str,
    response: &wire::PasswordKeyResponse,
) -> Result<String, AuthError> {
    if response.timestamp == 0
        || !(512..=1024).contains(&response.modulus.len())
        || response.exponent.len() > 8
    {
        return Err(AuthError::Protocol);
    }
    let modulus =
        BigUint::parse_bytes(response.modulus.as_bytes(), 16).ok_or(AuthError::Protocol)?;
    let exponent =
        BigUint::parse_bytes(response.exponent.as_bytes(), 16).ok_or(AuthError::Protocol)?;
    let key = RsaPublicKey::new(modulus, exponent).map_err(|_| AuthError::Protocol)?;
    if !(2048..=4096).contains(&key.n().bits()) {
        return Err(AuthError::Protocol);
    }
    if password.len() > key.size().saturating_sub(11) {
        return Err(AuthError::InvalidCredentialsInput);
    }
    let encrypted = key
        .encrypt(&mut OsRng, Pkcs1v15Encrypt, password.as_bytes())
        .map_err(|_| AuthError::Protocol)?;
    Ok(general_purpose::STANDARD.encode(encrypted))
}

fn make_session(
    client_id: u64,
    request_id: Vec<u8>,
    steam_id: Option<u64>,
    challenge_url: Option<String>,
    confirmations: Vec<wire::Confirmation>,
    interval: f32,
) -> Result<AuthSession, AuthError> {
    if client_id == 0
        || request_id.is_empty()
        || request_id.len() > 4096
        || !interval.is_finite()
        || interval <= 0.0
        || interval > 300.0
        || confirmations.is_empty()
        || confirmations.len() > 32
    {
        return Err(AuthError::Protocol);
    }
    let confirmations: Vec<_> = confirmations
        .into_iter()
        .map(|confirmation| GuardConfirmation {
            kind: GuardType::from_wire(confirmation.kind),
            message: confirmation.message.chars().take(256).collect(),
        })
        .collect();
    if !confirmations.iter().any(|value| {
        matches!(
            value.kind,
            GuardType::None
                | GuardType::EmailCode
                | GuardType::DeviceCode
                | GuardType::DeviceConfirmation
                | GuardType::EmailConfirmation
        )
    }) {
        return Err(AuthError::UnsupportedConfirmation);
    }
    Ok(AuthSession {
        client_id,
        request_id,
        steam_id,
        challenge_url,
        confirmations,
        interval: Duration::from_secs_f32(interval.max(1.0)),
        had_remote_interaction: false,
        completed: false,
    })
}

fn validate_challenge_url(value: String) -> Result<String, AuthError> {
    if value.len() > 4096 {
        return Err(AuthError::Protocol);
    }
    let url = reqwest::Url::parse(&value).map_err(|_| AuthError::Protocol)?;
    if url.scheme() != "https"
        || url.host_str() != Some("s.team")
        || !url.path().starts_with("/q/")
        || !url.username().is_empty()
        || url.password().is_some()
        || url.port().is_some()
    {
        return Err(AuthError::Protocol);
    }
    Ok(value)
}

fn require_no_agreement(agreement_url: &str) -> Result<(), AuthError> {
    if agreement_url.is_empty() {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(AuthError::AgreementRequired)
    }
}

fn check_result(result: i32, accept_duplicate: bool) -> Result<(), AuthError> {
    match result {
        1 => Ok(()),
        29 if accept_duplicate => Ok(()),
        5 => Err(AuthError::CredentialsRejected),
        65 | 88 => Err(AuthError::GuardRejected),
        9 | 27 => Err(AuthError::Expired),
        84 | 87 => Err(AuthError::RateLimited),
        _ => Err(AuthError::Steam { result }),
    }
}

fn apply_poll_response(
    session: &mut AuthSession,
    response: wire::PollResponse,
) -> Result<Option<AuthTokens>, AuthError> {
    require_no_agreement(&response.agreement_url)?;
    if response.new_client_id != 0 {
        session.client_id = response.new_client_id;
    }
    if !response.new_challenge_url.is_empty() {
        session.challenge_url = Some(validate_challenge_url(response.new_challenge_url)?);
    }
    session.had_remote_interaction |= response.had_remote_interaction;
    if response.refresh_token.is_empty() {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    let steam_id = steam_id_from_refresh_token(&response.refresh_token)?;
    if session
        .steam_id
        .is_some_and(|expected| expected != steam_id)
        || response.account_name.is_empty()
        || response.account_name.len() > 256
    {
        return Err(AuthError::Protocol);
    }
    session.completed = true;
    session.request_id.fill(0);
    session.challenge_url = None;
    Ok(Some(AuthTokens {
        account_name: response.account_name,
        steam_id,
        refresh_token: response.refresh_token,
    }))
}
```
