```rs
#[tokio::test]
async fn typing_is_throttled_per_friend() {
    let (client, mut server) = session().await;
    let client = Arc::new(client);
    let typing = |friend| {
        let client = Arc::clone(&client);
        tokio::spawn(async move { client.send_typing(friend).await })
    };
    for friend in [FRIEND, FRIEND + 1] {
        let sending = typing(friend);
        let request = server.request(SERVICE_REQUEST).await;
        let body = proto::SendMessageRequest::decode(&request.body[..]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            (body.steamid, body.chat_entry_type, body.message.as_str()),
            (friend, 2, "")
        );
        server
            .reply(
                &request,
                SERVICE_RESPONSE,
                &proto::SendMessageResponse::default(),
            )
            .await;
        sending.await.unwrap().unwrap();
    }
    // Within the interval, typing again tells the friend nothing new.
    typing(FRIEND).await.unwrap().unwrap();
    assert!(server.quiet().await);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn history_pages_backwards_oldest_first() {
    let (client, mut server) = session().await;
    let loading =
        tokio::spawn(async move { client.recent_messages(FRIEND, Some((100, 2)), 500).await });
    let request = server.request(SERVICE_REQUEST).await;
    assert_eq!(
        request.header.target_name.as_deref(),
        Some("FriendMessages.GetRecentMessages#1")
    );
    // steamid1 1 = self, steamid2 2 = friend, count 3 = 50, bbcode_format 6,
    // time_last 8, ordinal_last 9.
    let mut expected = fixed64(0x09, ACCOUNT);
    expected.extend(fixed64(0x11, FRIEND));
    expected.extend_from_slice(&[0x18, 50, 0x30, 0x01, 0x40, 100, 0x48, 0x02]);
    assert_eq!(&request.body[..], expected);
    let message = |accountid: u64, timestamp, ordinal| proto::FriendMessage {
        accountid: accountid as u32,
        timestamp,
        message: format!("{timestamp}.{ordinal}"),
        ordinal,
    };
    server
        .reply(
            &request,
            SERVICE_RESPONSE,
            &proto::RecentMessagesResponse {
                // Newest first, repeating the boundary.
                messages: vec![
                    message(ACCOUNT, 100, 2),
                    message(FRIEND, 100, 1),
                    message(ACCOUNT, 90, 0),
                ],
                more_available: true,
            },
        )
        .await;
    let history = loading.await.unwrap().unwrap();
    assert!(history.more_available);
    assert_eq!(
        history.messages,
        vec![
            HistoryMessage {
                from_me: true,
                timestamp: 90,
                ordinal: 0,
                message: "90.0".into()
            },
            HistoryMessage {
                from_me: false,
                timestamp: 100,
                ordinal: 1,
                message: "100.1".into()
            },
        ]
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn invitations_reach_the_invite_stream_from_every_channel() {
    const LOBBY: u64 = 109_775_244_421_126_053;
    let (client, mut server) = session().await;
    let client = Arc::new(client);
    let waiting = tokio::spawn({
        let client = Arc::clone(&client);
        async move { client.next_invites(1).await }
    });
    server
        .send(
            crate::invites::CHAT_INVITE,
            proto::Header::default(),
            &crate::invites::fixture::lobby_invite(FRIEND, LOBBY, 3_527_290),
        )
        .await;
    let invites = waiting.await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(invites.invites.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(invites.invites[0].app_id, 3_527_290);
    // Steam's chat copy of the same invitation adds nothing.
    server
        .send(
            146,
            proto::Header {
                target_name: Some(crate::chat::INCOMING_MESSAGE.into()),
                ..Default::default()
            },
            &crate::chat::fixture::incoming_message(
                FRIEND,
                1,
                &format!("[lobbyinvite appid=\"3527290\" lobbyid=\"{LOBBY}\"][/lobbyinvite]"),
                1_700_000_000,
                5,
                false,
            ),
        )
        .await;
    let waiting = tokio::spawn({
        let client = Arc::clone(&client);
        let revision = invites.revision;
        async move { client.next_invites(revision).await }
    });
    // A connect invitation names its game in the header only.
    server
        .send(
            crate::invites::INVITE_TO_GAME,
            proto::Header {
                routing_appid: Some(620),
                ..Default::default()
            },
            &crate::invites::fixture::connect_invite(FRIEND + 1, "+connect 10.0.0.1"),
        )
        .await;
    let invites = waiting.await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(invites.invites.len(), 2);
    assert_eq!(invites.invites[0].friend, FRIEND + 1);
    assert_eq!(invites.invites[0].app_id, 620);
}

/// Invites the friend into app 620. The caller keeps the session alive, since
/// dropping it would abort the worker before the invitation is written.
fn invite(client: &Arc<Client>) -> tokio::task::JoinHandle<Result<GameInviteKind, String>> {
    let client = Arc::clone(client);
    tokio::spawn(async move {
        client
            .invite_to_game(FRIEND, 620)
            .await
            .map_err(|error| error.to_string())
    })
}

/// The account's own game, as Steam pushes it: an invitation never asks,
/// since asking makes the game drop out for every friend.
async fn push_own_game(client: &Client, server: &mut test_server::TestServer, persona: Vec<u8>) {
    server
        .send(PERSONA_STATE, proto::Header::default(), &persona)
        .await;
    client.next_own_game(1).await;
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_reported_invitation_is_refused_for_another_game_or_target() {
    let (client, mut server) = session().await;
    const LOBBY: u64 = 109_775_244_421_126_053;
    let refused = |app_id, invite| {
        let client = &client;
        async move {
            client
                .invite_into_game(FRIEND, app_id, &invite)
                .await
                .unwrap_err()
                .to_string()
        }
    };
    let unavailable = "backend.steam.invite.unavailable";
    assert_eq!(
        refused(0, own_game::GameInvite::Lobby { lobby_id: LOBBY }).await,
        unavailable
    );
    assert_eq!(refused(620, own_game::GameInvite::None).await, unavailable);
    // An account is no lobby.
    assert_eq!(
        refused(620, own_game::GameInvite::Lobby { lobby_id: FRIEND }).await,
        unavailable
    );
    assert_eq!(
        refused(
            620,
            own_game::GameInvite::Connect {
                connect: "x".repeat(256)
            }
        )
        .await,
        unavailable
    );
    // The persona shows the account in another game.
    server
        .send(
            PERSONA_STATE,
            proto::Header::default(),
            &own_persona(730, 0, None),
        )
        .await;
    let game = client.next_own_game(1).await;
    assert_eq!(game.app_id, 730);
    assert_eq!(
        refused(620, own_game::GameInvite::Lobby { lobby_id: LOBBY }).await,
        unavailable
    );
    // To a stranger's account type, nothing leaves.
    assert_eq!(
        client
            .invite_into_game(
                0x0170_0001_0000_0001,
                730,
                &own_game::GameInvite::Lobby { lobby_id: LOBBY }
            )
            .await
            .unwrap_err()
            .to_string(),
        "backend.steam.chat.invalidRecipient"
    );
    assert!(server.quiet().await);
}
```

`crates/storefronts/steam-kit/src/cm/test_server.rs`:

```rs
//! A local Steam CM for tests: the real connection worker over a local
//! WebSocket, with the test answering as Steam.
use super::*;

pub(crate) struct TestServer(tokio_tungstenite::WebSocketStream<tokio::net::TcpStream>);

/// A connection for `steam_id`, already logged on when `logged_on`.
pub(crate) async fn connection(steam_id: u64, logged_on: bool) -> (SteamConnection, TestServer) {
    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").await.unwrap();
    let endpoint = format!("ws://{}", listener.local_addr().unwrap());
    let (client, server) = tokio::join!(tokio_tungstenite::connect_async(endpoint), async {
        let (stream, _) = listener.accept().await.unwrap();
        tokio_tungstenite::accept_async(stream).await.unwrap()
    });
    let mut connection = SteamConnection::start(client.unwrap().0, steam_id, logged_on);
    connection.session_id = 1;
    (connection, TestServer(server))
}

impl TestServer {
    /// The next message Obelisk sent, which must be of `kind`.
    pub(super) async fn request(&mut self, kind: u32) -> Packet {
        let packet = timeout(Duration::from_secs(1), self.next())
            .await
            .expect("Obelisk sent nothing");
        assert_eq!(packet.kind, kind);
        packet
    }

    async fn next(&mut self) -> Packet {
        loop {
            let frame = self
                .0
                .next()
                .await
                .expect("Obelisk closed the connection")
                .unwrap();
            let WsMessage::Binary(bytes) = frame else {
                continue;
            };
            let mut packets = Vec::new();
            decode_packets(bytes, 0, &mut { MAX_PACKET }, &mut packets).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(packets.len(), 1);
            let packet = packets.remove(0);
            if packet.kind != HEARTBEAT {
                return packet;
            }
        }
    }

    /// Answers `request` as Steam does, addressing its job.
    pub(super) async fn reply(&mut self, request: &Packet, kind: u32, body: &impl Message) {
        self.send(
            kind,
            proto::Header {
                job_target: request.header.job_source,
                result: Some(1),
                ..Default::default()
            },
            &body.encode_to_vec(),
        )
        .await;
    }

    pub(super) async fn send(&mut self, kind: u32, header: proto::Header, body: &[u8]) {
        self.0
            .send(WsMessage::Binary(encode_body(kind, &header, body).into()))
            .await
            .unwrap();
    }

    /// Obelisk sends nothing for a moment.
    pub(super) async fn quiet(&mut self) -> bool {
        timeout(Duration::from_millis(100), self.next())
            .await
            .is_err()
    }
}

```

`crates/storefronts/steam-kit/src/content.rs`:

```rs
//! Steam depot delivery: manifests, authenticated CDN chunks, verification and installation.
//!
//! The caller obtains entitlements, depot keys and request codes through Steam's CM.
//! Protocol references and format limits are recorded in docs/steam-content-notes.md.
//! Path confinement, locking, hashing and progress reporting come from `obelisk_core`.

mod format;
mod manifest_cache;
mod mirrors;
mod verification;

pub use manifest_cache::CachedManifest;

use std::{
    collections::{HashMap, HashSet},
    fs::{self, File, OpenOptions},
    io::{Read, Seek, SeekFrom, Write},
    path::{Path, PathBuf},
    sync::Arc,
    time::Duration,
};

use futures_util::future::BoxFuture;
use obelisk_core::{
    install::{
        self, InstallError, PARTIAL_DIRECTORY, apply_permissions, checked_file_path,
        ensure_directory, reject_link_or_special_file, safe_relative_path,
    },
    mac_build::Listing,
    transfer::{
        self, BodyError, BodySize, Cancelled, Chunks, Delivery, DownloadPhase, DownloadProgress,
        DownloadSummary, Interrupted, Pipeline, Reporter,
    },
};
use reqwest::{Client, Url};
use sha1::{Digest, Sha1};
#[cfg(test)]
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use thiserror::Error;

use crate::cm::ContentServer;
use format::{Chunk, Manifest, ManifestFile, decode_chunk, parse_manifest, unpack_zip};
use mirrors::{Mirrors, Ticket};

/// Shared with CM avatar hashes.
pub(crate) use obelisk_core::install::hex;
pub use obelisk_core::transfer::CancelToken;

const MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES: usize = 128 * 1024 * 1024;
const MAX_CHUNK_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024 * 1024;
/// Chunk requests in flight per depot, across every server. One CDN
/// connection carries about a megabyte per second, so a fast link needs many.
/// Chunks are typically 1 MiB, so this also bounds the memory decoded chunks
/// hold.
const CHUNK_REQUESTS: usize = 64;
/// Chunks requested ahead of the writer: enough that requests in flight never
/// wait for it to prepare files.
const QUEUED_CHUNKS: usize = 2 * CHUNK_REQUESTS;
/// Decoded chunks waiting for the disk writer.
const WRITE_QUEUE: usize = 16;
/// Files prepared ahead of the writer, each holding its partial file open:
/// requests queue without opening partial files for the whole depot.
const PREPARED_FILES: usize = 32;
/// Chunks reach the writer as they arrive: it places each one itself.
const PIPELINE: Pipeline = Pipeline {
    delivery: Delivery::AsFetched,
    fetches: CHUNK_REQUESTS,
    queue: WRITE_QUEUE,
};

/// No Debug implementation: depot keys are credentials.
pub struct DepotDownload<'a> {
    pub depot_id: u32,
    pub manifest_id: u64,
    pub request_code: u64,
    pub depot_key: [u8; 32],
    /// The CDN servers allowed to serve the depot, in Steam's order of
    /// preference. HTTPS is always used.
    pub servers: Vec<ContentServer>,
    /// Grants the tokens servers may require; without it, a refusal is final.
    pub authorization: Option<&'a dyn CdnAuthorization>,
    pub destination: PathBuf,
    /// Already validated snapshot of the current manifest, if available locally.
    pub cached_manifest: Option<CachedManifest>,
}

/// Where a depot's files come from, to read a few of them before it is
/// installed. No Debug implementation: depot keys are credentials.
pub struct DepotSource<'a> {
    pub depot_id: u32,
    pub manifest_id: u64,
    pub request_code: u64,
    pub depot_key: [u8; 32],
    pub servers: &'a [ContentServer],
    pub authorization: Option<&'a dyn CdnAuthorization>,
}

/// A depot's files as its checked manifest lists them, whose bytes come from
/// its servers without being installed.
pub struct DepotFiles<'a> {
    content: &'a ContentClient,
    mirrors: Mirrors<'a>,
    depot_id: u32,
    depot_key: [u8; 32],
    manifest: Arc<Manifest>,
    archive: Vec<u8>,
}

/// Grants the CDN authorization a server may require before serving a depot.
pub trait CdnAuthorization: Sync {
    /// A token for `host`, or `None` when Steam grants none.
    fn token<'a>(&'a self, host: &'a str) -> BoxFuture<'a, Option<String>>;
}

/// One installed depot.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct DepotInstallation {
    pub summary: DownloadSummary,
    /// The installation paths of the install scripts its manifest flags.
    pub install_scripts: Vec<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Error)]
pub enum ContentError {
    #[error("backend.steam.content.cancelled")]
    Cancelled,
    #[error("backend.steam.content.network")]
    Network,
    #[error("{}", crate::message::format("backend.steam.content.http", &[.0.to_string()]))]
    Http(u16),
    #[error("{}", crate::message::format("backend.steam.content.invalid", std::slice::from_ref(.0)))]
    InvalidData(String),
    #[error("{}", crate::message::format("backend.steam.content.unsafePath", std::slice::from_ref(.0)))]
    UnsafePath(String),
    #[error("{}", crate::message::format("backend.steam.content.unsupportedSymlink", std::slice::from_ref(.0)))]
    UnsupportedSymlink(String),
    #[error("backend.steam.content.locked")]
    AlreadyDownloading,
    #[error("{}", crate::message::format("backend.steam.content.io", &[.0.to_string()]))]
    Io(#[from] std::io::Error),
}

impl From<Cancelled> for ContentError {
    fn from(_: Cancelled) -> Self {
        Self::Cancelled
    }
}

impl From<Interrupted> for ContentError {
    fn from(_: Interrupted) -> Self {
        invalid("backend.steam.content.diskInstallationInterrupted")
    }
}

impl From<BodyError> for ContentError {
    fn from(error: BodyError) -> Self {
        match error {
            BodyError::Network => Self::Network,
            BodyError::Size => invalid("backend.steam.content.cdnResponseTooLarge"),
            BodyError::Cancelled => Self::Cancelled,
        }
    }
}

impl From<InstallError> for ContentError {
    fn from(error: InstallError) -> Self {
        match error {
            InstallError::Cancelled => Self::Cancelled,
            InstallError::UnsafePath(path) => Self::UnsafePath(path),
            InstallError::Io(error) => Self::Io(error),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct ContentClient {
    client: Client,
    /// Local servers standing in for CDN hosts; any other host is unreachable.
    #[cfg(test)]
    test_endpoints: HashMap<String, Url>,
}

impl ContentClient {
    pub fn new(client: Client) -> Self {
        Self {
            client,
            #[cfg(test)]
            test_endpoints: HashMap::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Reads and validates the cache without issuing a CDN or authentication request.
    pub async fn cached_manifest(
        &self,
        destination: &Path,
        depot_id: u32,
        manifest_id: u64,
        key: &[u8; 32],
    ) -> Result<Option<CachedManifest>, ContentError> {
        let destination = destination.to_owned();
        let key = *key;
        tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
            manifest_cache::load(&destination, depot_id, manifest_id, &key)
        })
        .await
        .map_err(|_| invalid("backend.steam.content.manifestReadInterrupted"))?
    }

    /// Fetches and checks a depot's manifest, to read some of its files.
    pub async fn depot_files<'a>(
        &'a self,
        source: DepotSource<'a>,
        cancel: &CancelToken,
    ) -> Result<DepotFiles<'a>, ContentError> {
        let mirrors = Mirrors::new(source.servers, source.authorization)?;
        let path = manifest_path(source.depot_id, source.manifest_id, source.request_code);
        let (zipped, _) = mirrors
            .fetch(&path, None, 0, cancel, |url| {
                self.fetch(url, MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES, cancel, |_| {})
            })
            .await?;
        let key = source.depot_key;
        let (manifest, archive) = cancel
            .spawn_blocking(move || {
                let manifest = parse_manifest(&unpack_zip(&zipped, MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES)?, &key)?;
                validate_manifest_files(&manifest.files)?;
                Ok::<_, ContentError>((manifest, zipped))
            })
            .await
            .map_err(|_| invalid("backend.steam.content.manifestParseInterrupted"))??;
        if manifest.depot_id != source.depot_id || manifest.manifest_id != source.manifest_id {
            return Err(invalid("backend.steam.content.manifestDepotMismatch"));
        }
        Ok(DepotFiles {
            content: self,
            mirrors,
            depot_id: source.depot_id,
            depot_key: key,
            manifest: Arc::new(manifest),
            archive,
        })
    }

    /// Opt-in protocol smoke test: validates the smallest real file (up to 8 MiB)
    /// without installing a depot or writing any game files.
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub(crate) async fn verify_live_sample(
        &self,
        plan: &DepotDownload<'_>,
    ) -> Result<(u64, u32), ContentError> {
        let cancel = CancelToken::new();
        let mirrors = Mirrors::new(&plan.servers, plan.authorization)?;
        let path = format!(
            "depot/{}/manifest/{}/5/{}",
            plan.depot_id, plan.manifest_id, plan.request_code
        );
        let (zipped, _) = mirrors
            .fetch(&path, None, 0, &cancel, |url| {
                self.fetch(url, MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES, &cancel, |_| {})
            })
            .await?;
        let bytes = unpack_zip(&zipped, MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES)?;
        let manifest = parse_manifest(&bytes, &plan.depot_key)?;
        if manifest.depot_id != plan.depot_id || manifest.manifest_id != plan.manifest_id {
            return Err(invalid("backend.steam.content.manifestDepotMismatch"));
        }
        let file = manifest
            .files
            .iter()
            .filter(|file| {
                !file.is_directory()
                    && !file.is_link()
                    && file.size > 0
                    && file.size <= 8 * 1024 * 1024
            })
            .min_by_key(|file| file.size)
            .ok_or_else(|| invalid("backend.steam.content.noSampleFile"))?;
        validate_manifest_files(std::slice::from_ref(file))?;
        let mut hasher = Sha1::new();
        let mut size = 0_u64;
        for chunk in &file.chunks {
            let path = format!("depot/{}/chunk/{}", plan.depot_id, hex(&chunk.sha));
            let (mut encrypted, _) = mirrors
                .fetch(&path, None, 0, &cancel, |url| {
                    self.fetch(url, MAX_CHUNK_BYTES, &cancel, |_| {})
                })
                .await?;
            let plaintext = decode_chunk(&mut encrypted, chunk, &plan.depot_key)?;
            size += plaintext.len() as u64;
            hasher.update(plaintext);
        }
        if size != file.size || hasher.finalize()[..] != file.sha {
            return Err(invalid("backend.steam.content.sampleHashMismatch"));
        }
        Ok((size, file.chunks.len() as u32))
    }

    /// Installs one authorized depot, its chunks spread over every server the
    /// plan names. Network work stays on the async runtime while every disk
    /// operation runs on the blocking pool, so a multi-GB depot does not pin a
    /// runtime worker. Existing complete files and verified partial chunks are
    /// reused on the next invocation. File replacement is atomic; an incomplete
    /// file never replaces an installed file.
    pub async fn download_depot(
        &self,
        plan: &DepotDownload<'_>,
        cancel: &CancelToken,
        progress: impl Fn(DownloadProgress) + Send + Sync + 'static,
    ) -> Result<DepotInstallation, ContentError> {
        cancel.check()?;
        let mirrors = Mirrors::new(&plan.servers, plan.authorization)?;
        let reporter = Reporter::new(
            DownloadProgress {
                current_file: "backend.steam.content.fetchingManifest".into(),
                ..Default::default()
            },
            progress,
        );
        let cached = match &plan.cached_manifest {
            Some(cached) => Some(cached.clone()),
            None => {
                self.cached_manifest(
                    &plan.destination,
                    plan.depot_id,
                    plan.manifest_id,
                    &plan.depot_key,
                )
                .await?
            }
        };
        cancel.check()?;
        // A cached manifest was validated when it was loaded; only a fresh
        // download must be checked in full before any installation file exists.
        let (manifest, archive) = if let Some(cached) = cached {
            (cached.manifest, cached.archive)
        } else {
            let manifest_path = manifest_path(plan.depot_id, plan.manifest_id, plan.request_code);
            let reporter = &reporter;
            // Every chunk waits on the manifest: it is raced like the oldest chunk.
            let ticket = mirrors.ticket();
            let (zipped, _) = mirrors
                .fetch(&manifest_path, Some(&ticket), 0, cancel, |url| {
                    self.fetch(url, MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES, cancel, |received| {
                        reporter.update(|status| status.network_bytes += received);
                    })
                })
                .await?;
            let key = plan.depot_key;
            let manifest = cancel
                .spawn_blocking(move || {
                    let manifest_bytes = unpack_zip(&zipped, MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES)?;
                    let manifest = parse_manifest(&manifest_bytes, &key)?;
                    validate_manifest_files(&manifest.files)?;
                    Ok::<_, ContentError>((manifest, zipped))
                })
                .await
                .map_err(|_| invalid("backend.steam.content.manifestParseInterrupted"))?;
            let (manifest, zipped) = manifest?;
            (Arc::new(manifest), Some(zipped))
        };
        if manifest.depot_id != plan.depot_id || manifest.manifest_id != plan.manifest_id {
            return Err(invalid("backend.steam.content.manifestDepotMismatch"));
        }
        // A link holds no content, whatever size its entry gives.
        let total_bytes = manifest
            .files
            .iter()
            .filter(|file| !file.is_link())
            .map(|file| file.size)
            .sum();
        let total_files = u32::try_from(
            manifest
                .files
                .iter()
                .filter(|file| !file.is_directory() && !file.is_link())
                .count(),
        )
        .map_err(|_| invalid("backend.steam.content.tooManyFiles"))?;
        reporter.update(|status| {
            status.total_bytes = total_bytes;
            status.total_files = total_files;
            status.phase = DownloadPhase::Verifying;
            status.current_file.clear();
        });
        let install_scripts = manifest
            .files
            .iter()
            .filter(|file| {
                !file.is_directory()
                    && !file.is_link()
                    && file.flags & crate::install_script::FLAG != 0
            })
            .map(|file| file.name.clone())
            .collect();

        let disk = DiskInstall::engine_side(
            plan.destination.clone(),
            plan.depot_id,
            plan.manifest_id,
            archive,
            manifest,
            cancel.clone(),
            Arc::clone(&reporter),
        );
        let reused_bytes =
            transfer::run_engine(PIPELINE, cancel, disk, |(place, chunk): ChunkRequest| {
                // Requests are created in manifest order and taken up in that order.
                let ticket = mirrors.ticket();
                let fetched = self.fetch_chunk(&mirrors, ticket, plan, chunk, cancel, &reporter);
                async move { fetched.await.map(|bytes| (place, bytes)) }
            })
            .await?;
        Ok(DepotInstallation {
            summary: reporter.summary(reused_bytes),
            install_scripts,
        })
    }

    /// Fetches one chunk through the depot's servers and decodes it. Chunk
    /// bytes count once, from the response that answered; a corrupt response
    /// moves the chunk to another server. Decryption and decompression run on
    /// the blocking pool.
    async fn fetch_chunk(
        &self,
        mirrors: &Mirrors<'_>,
        ticket: Ticket<'_>,
        plan: &DepotDownload<'_>,
        chunk: Chunk,
        cancel: &CancelToken,
        reporter: &Reporter,
    ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ContentError> {
        let path = format!("depot/{}/chunk/{}", plan.depot_id, hex(&chunk.sha));
        let key = plan.depot_key;
        let chunk = &chunk;
        reporter.update(|status| status.phase = DownloadPhase::Downloading);
        let (bytes, received) = mirrors
            .fetch(
                &path,
                Some(&ticket),
                u64::from(chunk.compressed_size),
                cancel,
                |url| async move {
                    let (mut encrypted, received) = self
                        .fetch(url, MAX_CHUNK_BYTES, cancel, |received| {
                            reporter.update(|status| status.network_bytes += received);
                        })
                        .await?;
                    let expected = chunk.clone();
                    let decoded = cancel
                        .spawn_blocking(move || decode_chunk(&mut encrypted, &expected, &key))
                        .await
                        .map_err(|_| {
                            invalid("backend.steam.content.chunkDecryptionInterrupted")
                        })??;
                    Ok((decoded, received))
                },
            )
            .await?;
        reporter.update(|status| status.content_bytes += received);
        Ok(bytes)
    }

    /// Returns the response body with its size, which measures the server.
    async fn fetch(
        &self,
        url: Url,
        limit: usize,
        cancel: &CancelToken,
        on_bytes: impl FnMut(u64),
    ) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, u64), ContentError> {
        #[cfg(test)]
        let url = if self.test_endpoints.is_empty() {
            url
        } else {
            let Some(endpoint) = url
                .host_str()
                .and_then(|host| self.test_endpoints.get(host))
            else {
                return Err(ContentError::Network);
            };
            let mut local = endpoint.join(url.path()).expect("test URL");
            local.set_query(url.query());
            local
        };
        let response = cancel
            .race(self.client.get(url).timeout(Duration::from_secs(45)).send())
            .await?
            .map_err(|_| ContentError::Network)?;
        if !response.status().is_success() {
            return Err(ContentError::Http(response.status().as_u16()));
        }
        let bytes = transfer::read_body(
            response.content_length(),
            response.bytes_stream(),
            BodySize::AtMost(limit as u64),
            cancel,
            on_bytes,
        )
        .await?;
        let size = bytes.len() as u64;
        Ok((bytes, size))
    }
}

impl DepotFiles<'_> {
    /// The checked manifest, for the installation of the depot to start from
    /// instead of fetching it again.
    pub fn into_manifest(self) -> ((u32, u64), CachedManifest) {
        let identity = (self.depot_id, self.manifest.manifest_id);
        let manifest = CachedManifest {
            manifest: self.manifest,
            archive: Some(self.archive),
        };
        (identity, manifest)
    }

    /// Adds the depot's files and links to `listing`, each file named by
    /// `depot` and its place in the manifest. Steam keeps a link's target
    /// from the link's own folder.
    pub fn list(&self, listing: &mut Listing<(usize, usize)>, depot: usize) {
        for (index, file) in self.manifest.files.iter().enumerate() {
            if file.is_link() {
                let folder = file.name.rsplit_once('/').map_or("", |(folder, _)| folder);
                listing.link(&file.name, &format!("{folder}/{}", file.link_target));
            } else if !file.is_directory() {
                listing.file(&file.name, (depot, index), file.size);
            }
        }
    }

    /// The first `bytes` of the manifest's file `index`, from the chunks that
    /// hold them.
    pub async fn read(
        &self,
        index: usize,
        bytes: u64,
        cancel: &CancelToken,
    ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ContentError> {
        let file = self
            .manifest
            .files
            .get(index)
            .ok_or_else(|| invalid("backend.steam.content.noSampleFile"))?;
        let mut output = Vec::new();
        for chunk in &file.chunks {
            if output.len() as u64 >= bytes {
                break;
            }
            let path = format!("depot/{}/chunk/{}", self.depot_id, hex(&chunk.sha));
            let key = self.depot_key;
            let (plaintext, _) = self
                .mirrors
                .fetch(
                    &path,
                    None,
                    u64::from(chunk.compressed_size),
                    cancel,
                    |url| async move {
                        let (mut encrypted, received) = self
                            .content
                            .fetch(url, MAX_CHUNK_BYTES, cancel, |_| {})
                            .await?;
                        let expected = chunk.clone();
                        let decoded = cancel
                            .spawn_blocking(move || decode_chunk(&mut encrypted, &expected, &key))
                            .await
                            .map_err(|_| {
                                invalid("backend.steam.content.chunkDecryptionInterrupted")
                            })??;
                        Ok((decoded, received))
                    },
                )
                .await?;
            output.extend(plaintext);
        }
        output.truncate(usize::try_from(bytes).unwrap_or(usize::MAX));
        Ok(output)
    }
}

/// The CDN path of a depot's manifest; a request code of 0 is left out.
fn manifest_path(depot_id: u32, manifest_id: u64, request_code: u64) -> String {
    match request_code {
        0 => format!("depot/{depot_id}/manifest/{manifest_id}/5"),
        code => format!("depot/{depot_id}/manifest/{manifest_id}/5/{code}"),
    }
}

/// Where a chunk belongs: its file's index in the manifest and its own index
/// in that file.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct ChunkPlace {
    file: usize,
    chunk: usize,
}

type ChunkRequest = (ChunkPlace, Chunk);
/// The writer's end of the depot's engine.
type DepotChunks = Chunks<ChunkRequest, (ChunkPlace, Vec<u8>), ContentError>;

/// Everything that touches the disk for one depot, on a blocking thread: the
/// destination lock, manifest cache, verification, assembly and atomic publication.
struct DiskInstall {
    destination: PathBuf,
    depot_id: u32,
    manifest_id: u64,
    archive: Option<Vec<u8>>,
    manifest: Arc<Manifest>,
    cancel: CancelToken,
    reporter: Arc<Reporter>,
    chunks: DepotChunks,
}

/// A file being assembled in its partial file. Its chunks arrive in any
/// order and each is written in place; the file is hashed in order as far as
/// its chunks are present, so a chunk arriving late holds up only its file.
struct PreparedFile<'a> {
    file: &'a ManifestFile,
    relative: PathBuf,
    target: PathBuf,
    partial_path: PathBuf,
    partial: File,
    /// Chunks in the partial file: verified from an earlier run, or written.
    present: Vec<bool>,
    /// Chunks requested and not written yet.
    missing: usize,
    hasher: Sha1,
    /// Chunks hashed so far, from the start of the file.
    hashed: usize,
    /// Holds a chunk read back from the partial file.
    buffer: Vec<u8>,
    reused_bytes: u64,
}

impl PreparedFile<'_> {
    /// Writes a chunk in place, then hashes on as far as the file is present.
    fn write(&mut self, index: usize, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), ContentError> {
        let chunk = self
            .file
            .chunks
            .get(index)
            .filter(|_| !self.present[index])
            .ok_or_else(|| invalid("backend.steam.content.chunkDownloadInterrupted"))?;
        self.partial.seek(SeekFrom::Start(chunk.offset))?;
        self.partial.write_all(bytes)?;
        self.present[index] = true;
        self.missing -= 1;
        self.hash_present(index, bytes)
    }

    /// Hashes the chunks present from where hashing stopped. The chunk just
    /// written is hashed from memory; one that arrived early is read back.
    fn hash_present(&mut self, written: usize, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), ContentError> {
        while self.present.get(self.hashed) == Some(&true) {
            if self.hashed == written {
                self.hasher.update(bytes);
            } else {
                let chunk = &self.file.chunks[self.hashed];
                self.buffer.resize(chunk.original_size as usize, 0);
                self.partial.seek(SeekFrom::Start(chunk.offset))?;
                self.partial.read_exact(&mut self.buffer)?;
                self.hasher.update(&self.buffer);
            }
            self.hashed += 1;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl DiskInstall {
    /// The writer for one depot's engine, ready to run on its blocking thread.
    fn engine_side(
        destination: PathBuf,
        depot_id: u32,
        manifest_id: u64,
        archive: Option<Vec<u8>>,
        manifest: Arc<Manifest>,
        cancel: CancelToken,
        reporter: Arc<Reporter>,
    ) -> impl FnOnce(DepotChunks) -> Result<u64, ContentError> + Send + 'static {
        move |chunks| {
            Self {
                destination,
                depot_id,
                manifest_id,
                archive,
                manifest,
                cancel,
                reporter,
                chunks,
            }
            .run()
        }
    }

    /// Returns the number of verified bytes reused from disk.
    fn run(mut self) -> Result<u64, ContentError> {
        self.cancel.check()?;
        fs::create_dir_all(&self.destination)?;
        let root = fs::canonicalize(&self.destination)?;
        // A per-destination lock also prevents conflicting depots from being installed together.
        let _lock = install::lock_engine(&root)?.ok_or(ContentError::AlreadyDownloading)?;
        if let Some(archive) = self.archive.take() {
            self.cancel.check()?;
            manifest_cache::store(&root, self.depot_id, self.manifest_id, &archive)?;
        }
        let partial_relative = PathBuf::from(PARTIAL_DIRECTORY)
            .join(self.depot_id.to_string())
            .join(self.manifest_id.to_string());
        let partial_root = ensure_directory(&root, &partial_relative)?;
        let manifest = Arc::clone(&self.manifest);
        // Readers finish before the repair loop can replace any game files.
        // Reusable bytes include only valid whole files; inspection progress is
        // reported separately while a large file is still being hashed.
        let verified =
            verification::verify_files(&root, &manifest.files, &self.cancel, &self.reporter)?;
        let mut reused_bytes = verified.reused_bytes;

        // Directory entries are synced once per run of files sharing a parent
        // rather than after every rename; a lost rename is repaired next run
        // from the partial file that is still on disk.
        let mut pending_directory: Option<PathBuf> = None;
        // Parents are created and checked once per distinct directory; every
        // file's full path is still confined right before it is written.
        let mut ensured_parents: HashSet<PathBuf> = HashSet::new();
        let mut remaining = manifest.files.iter().enumerate();
        // Files being assembled, by manifest index.
        let mut assembling = HashMap::new();
        // Chunks requested for them and not written yet.
        let mut queued = 0;
        loop {
            // Requests follow manifest order. Files are prepared until enough
            // of their chunks are queued; valid files and directories do not
            // count. After a refused request, the file that held it is
            // assembling and receives the outcome: preparing more is wasted.
            while assembling.len() < PREPARED_FILES
                && queued < QUEUED_CHUNKS
                && !self.chunks.refused()
            {
                let Some((index, file)) = remaining.next() else {
                    break;
                };
                self.cancel.check()?;
                if file.is_link() {
                    continue;
                }
                let relative = safe_relative_path(&file.name)?;
                if file.is_directory() {
                    ensure_directory(&root, &relative)?;
                    ensured_parents.insert(relative);
                    continue;
                }
                let parent = relative.parent().unwrap_or(Path::new(""));
                if !ensured_parents.contains(parent) {
                    ensure_directory(&root, parent)?;
                    ensured_parents.insert(parent.to_path_buf());
                }
                let target = checked_file_path(&root, &relative)?;
                if verified.valid[index] {
                    apply_permissions(&target, is_executable(file, &target)?)?;
                    continue;
                }
                let prepared = self.prepare(&partial_root, index, file, relative, target)?;
                if prepared.missing == 0 {
                    reused_bytes += self.publish(prepared, &root, &mut pending_directory)?;
                } else {
                    queued += prepared.missing;
                    assembling.insert(index, prepared);
                }
            }
            if assembling.is_empty() {
                break;
            }
            self.cancel.check()?;
            let (place, bytes) = self.chunks.receive()?;
            let file: &mut PreparedFile<'_> = assembling
                .get_mut(&place.file)
                .ok_or_else(|| invalid("backend.steam.content.chunkDownloadInterrupted"))?;
            file.write(place.chunk, &bytes)?;
            queued -= 1;
            let size = bytes.len() as u64;
            self.reporter
                .update(|status| status.completed_bytes += size);
            if file.missing == 0
                && let Some(file) = assembling.remove(&place.file)
            {
                reused_bytes += self.publish(file, &root, &mut pending_directory)?;
            }
        }
        // Links come once every file is in place. Validation kept every file
        // and folder from sitting behind one.
        for file in manifest.files.iter().filter(|file| file.is_link()) {
            self.cancel.check()?;
            install::place_link(
                &root,
                &safe_relative_path(&file.name)?,
                Path::new(&file.link_target),
            )?;
        }
        if let Some(directory) = pending_directory {
            File::open(directory)?.sync_all()?;
        }
        Ok(reused_bytes)
    }

    /// Inspect the partial file once and request only its missing chunks. Keep
    /// its open handle until its last chunk is written.
    fn prepare<'a>(
        &mut self,
        partial_root: &Path,
        index: usize,
        file: &'a ManifestFile,
        relative: PathBuf,
        target: PathBuf,
    ) -> Result<PreparedFile<'a>, ContentError> {
        let partial_name = format!("{}.part", hex(&Sha1::digest(file.name.as_bytes())));
        let partial_path = partial_root.join(partial_name);
        reject_link_or_special_file(&partial_path)?;
        let mut partial = OpenOptions::new()
            .create(true)
            .truncate(false)
            .read(true)
            .write(true)
            .open(&partial_path)?;
        let existing = partial.metadata()?.len();
        partial.set_len(file.size)?;
        let mut present = vec![false; file.chunks.len()];
        let mut buffer = Vec::new();
        // The present chunks at the start of the file are hashed as they are
        // verified, rather than read again.
        let mut hasher = Sha1::new();
        let mut hashed = 0;
        for (index, chunk) in file.chunks.iter().enumerate() {
            self.cancel.check()?;
            if chunk.offset + u64::from(chunk.original_size) > existing {
                continue;
            }
            buffer.clear();
            buffer.resize(chunk.original_size as usize, 0);
            partial.seek(SeekFrom::Start(chunk.offset))?;
            partial.read_exact(&mut buffer)?;
            present[index] = format::verify_chunk(&buffer, chunk).is_ok();
            if present[index] && index == hashed {
                hasher.update(&buffer);
                hashed += 1;
            }
        }
        let reused_bytes = file
            .chunks
            .iter()
            .zip(&present)
            .filter(|(_, present)| **present)
            .map(|(chunk, _)| u64::from(chunk.original_size))
            .sum();
        self.reporter
            .update(|status| status.completed_bytes += reused_bytes);
        for (chunk_index, chunk) in file.chunks.iter().enumerate() {
            if present[chunk_index] {
                continue;
            }
            self.cancel.check()?;
            let place = ChunkPlace {
                file: index,
                chunk: chunk_index,
            };
            if !self.chunks.request((place, chunk.clone())) {
                // The writer receives the outcome that stopped the network side.
                break;
            }
        }
        Ok(PreparedFile {
            file,
            relative,
            target,
            partial_path,
            partial,
            missing: present.iter().filter(|present| !**present).count(),
            present,
            hasher,
            hashed,
            buffer,
            reused_bytes,
        })
    }

    /// Checks a fully assembled file's hash and publishes it atomically.
    /// Returns the bytes it reused from an earlier run.
    fn publish(
        &mut self,
        prepared: PreparedFile<'_>,
        root: &Path,
        pending_directory: &mut Option<PathBuf>,
    ) -> Result<u64, ContentError> {
        let PreparedFile {
            file,
            relative,
            target,
            partial_path,
            partial,
            present,
            hasher,
            hashed,
            reused_bytes,
            ..
        } = prepared;
        self.cancel.check()?;
        // Only a file this pass actually repairs is reported: verification
        // finished earlier, and traversing a valid file is one chmod. The
        // phase stays the network side's: chunks still arrive for other files.
        self.reporter
            .update(|status| status.current_file.clone_from(&file.name));
        partial.sync_all()?;
        drop(partial);
        if hashed != present.len() || hasher.finalize()[..] != file.sha {
            return Err(invalid("backend.steam.content.assembledHashMismatch"));
        }
        apply_permissions(&partial_path, is_executable(file, &partial_path)?)?;
        // Re-check parents before publishing; never follow existing symlinks under root.
        checked_file_path(root, &relative)?;
        let directory = target.parent().unwrap_or(root).to_path_buf();
        fs::rename(&partial_path, target)?;
        if pending_directory.as_ref() != Some(&directory)
            && let Some(previous) = pending_directory.replace(directory)
        {
            File::open(previous)?.sync_all()?;
        }
        self.reporter.update(|status| status.completed_files += 1);
        Ok(reused_bytes)
    }
}

fn invalid(reason: &str) -> ContentError {
    ContentError::InvalidData(reason.into())
}

/// Some depots flag only the launch executable: OpenFront's Electron helpers
/// come unflagged. Programs are then recognised by their header, a Mach-O
/// binary or a script.
fn is_executable(file: &ManifestFile, path: &Path) -> std::io::Result<bool> {
    Ok(file.flags & 32 != 0 || install::starts_as_program(path)?)
}

fn validate_manifest_files(files: &[ManifestFile]) -> Result<(), ContentError> {
    let mut paths = HashSet::new();
    let mut total_size = 0_u64;
    for file in files {
        let path = safe_relative_path(&file.name)?;
        if !paths.insert(path.to_string_lossy().to_lowercase()) {
            return Err(invalid("backend.steam.content.conflictingPaths"));
        }
        if file.is_link() {
            if !link_stays_inside(&path, &file.link_target) {
                return Err(ContentError::UnsupportedSymlink(file.name.clone()));
            }
            continue;
        }
        if file.is_directory() {
            if file.size != 0 || !file.chunks.is_empty() {
                return Err(invalid("backend.steam.content.directoryContainsData"));
            }
            continue;
        }
        if file.sha.len() != 20 {
            return Err(invalid("backend.steam.content.invalidFileChecksum"));
        }
        total_size = total_size
            .checked_add(file.size)
            .ok_or_else(|| invalid("backend.steam.content.invalidDepotSize"))?;
        let mut offset = 0_u64;
        for chunk in &file.chunks {
            if chunk.sha.len() != 20
                || chunk.original_size == 0
                || chunk.original_size as usize > MAX_CHUNK_BYTES
                || chunk.compressed_size as usize > MAX_CHUNK_BYTES
                || chunk.offset != offset
            {
                return Err(invalid("backend.steam.content.invalidChunkLayout"));
            }
            offset = offset
                .checked_add(u64::from(chunk.original_size))
                .ok_or_else(|| invalid("backend.steam.content.invalidChunkSize"))?;
        }
        if offset != file.size {
            return Err(invalid("backend.steam.content.missingChunks"));
        }
    }
    // Nothing sits inside a file, or behind a link.
    let files_only: HashSet<_> = files
        .iter()
        .filter(|file| !file.is_directory())
        .map(|file| {
            safe_relative_path(&file.name).map(|path| path.to_string_lossy().to_lowercase())
        })
        .collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;
    for file in files {
        let path = safe_relative_path(&file.name)?;
        if path
            .ancestors()
            .skip(1)
            .any(|parent| files_only.contains(&parent.to_string_lossy().to_lowercase()))
        {
            return Err(invalid("backend.steam.content.fileUsedAsDirectory"));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Whether the link at `path` leads inside the installation. Steam keeps a
/// target as the link holds it, from the link's own folder. Only a target
/// that climbs first, then descends, is followed: past a step that may be
/// another link, `..` could leave the installation.
fn link_stays_inside(path: &Path, target: &str) -> bool {
    if target.is_empty() || target.starts_with('/') {
        return false;
    }
    let mut destination: Vec<_> = path
        .parent()
        .into_iter()
        .flat_map(Path::iter)
        .filter_map(|part| part.to_str())
        .collect();
    let mut descending = false;
    for part in target.split('/') {
        match part {
            "" | "." => {}
            ".." if !descending => {
                if destination.pop().is_none() {
                    return false;
                }
            }
            ".." => return false,
            part => {
                descending = true;
                destination.push(part);
            }
        }
    }
    destination.is_empty() || safe_relative_path(&destination.join("/")).is_ok()
}
```

`crates/storefronts/steam-kit/src/content/format.rs`:

```rs
use std::io::{Read, Write};

use aes::{
    Aes256,
    cipher::{BlockCipherDecrypt, BlockModeDecrypt, KeyInit, KeyIvInit, block_padding::Pkcs7},
};
use base64::{Engine, engine::general_purpose::STANDARD};
use prost::Message;
use sha1::{Digest, Sha1};

use super::{ContentError, MAX_CHUNK_BYTES, invalid};

const PAYLOAD_MAGIC: u32 = 0x71f6_17d0;
const METADATA_MAGIC: u32 = 0x1f48_12be;
const SIGNATURE_MAGIC: u32 = 0x1b81_b817;
const END_MAGIC: u32 = 0x32c4_15ab;

pub(super) struct Manifest {
    pub depot_id: u32,
    pub manifest_id: u64,
    pub files: Vec<ManifestFile>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Message)]
pub(super) struct ManifestFile {
    #[prost(string, tag = "1")]
    pub name: String,
    #[prost(uint64, tag = "2")]
    pub size: u64,
    #[prost(uint32, tag = "3")]
    pub flags: u32,
    #[prost(bytes = "vec", tag = "4")]
    pub name_sha: Vec<u8>,
    #[prost(bytes = "vec", tag = "5")]
    pub sha: Vec<u8>,
    #[prost(message, repeated, tag = "6")]
    pub chunks: Vec<Chunk>,
    #[prost(string, tag = "7")]
    pub link_target: String,
}

impl ManifestFile {
    /// A link to a folder may carry the folder flag too: it stays a link.
    pub fn is_directory(&self) -> bool {
        self.flags & 64 != 0 && !self.is_link()
    }

    /// A symbolic link, such as a macOS framework's `Versions/Current`.
    pub fn is_link(&self) -> bool {
        self.flags & 512 != 0 || !self.link_target.is_empty()
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Message)]
pub(super) struct Chunk {
    #[prost(bytes = "vec", tag = "1")]
    pub sha: Vec<u8>,
    #[prost(fixed32, tag = "2")]
    pub adler: u32,
    #[prost(uint64, tag = "3")]
    pub offset: u64,
    #[prost(uint32, tag = "4")]
    pub original_size: u32,
    #[prost(uint32, tag = "5")]
    pub compressed_size: u32,
}

#[derive(Message)]
struct Payload {
    #[prost(message, repeated, tag = "1")]
    files: Vec<ManifestFile>,
}

#[derive(Message)]
struct Metadata {
    #[prost(uint32, tag = "1")]
    depot_id: u32,
    #[prost(uint64, tag = "2")]
    manifest_id: u64,
    #[prost(bool, tag = "4")]
    encrypted_names: bool,
    #[prost(uint32, tag = "8")]
    encrypted_crc: u32,
    #[prost(uint32, tag = "9")]
    clear_crc: u32,
}

pub(super) fn parse_manifest(data: &[u8], key: &[u8; 32]) -> Result<Manifest, ContentError> {
    let mut cursor = 0_usize;
    let mut payload: Option<&[u8]> = None;
    let mut metadata = None;
    let mut signature_seen = false;
    loop {
        let magic = u32_at(data, cursor)?;
        cursor += 4;
        if magic == END_MAGIC {
            if cursor != data.len() {
                return Err(invalid("backend.steam.format.trailingManifestData"));
            }
            break;
        }
        let length = u32_at(data, cursor)? as usize;
        cursor += 4;
        let section = slice(data, cursor, length)?;
        cursor += length;
        match magic {
            PAYLOAD_MAGIC if payload.is_none() => payload = Some(section),
            METADATA_MAGIC if metadata.is_none() => {
                metadata = Some(
                    Metadata::decode(section)
                        .map_err(|_| invalid("backend.steam.format.invalidProtobufMetadata"))?,
                );
            }
            SIGNATURE_MAGIC if !signature_seen => signature_seen = true,
            _ => return Err(invalid("backend.steam.format.invalidManifestSection")),
        }
    }
    let payload = payload.ok_or_else(|| invalid("backend.steam.format.inventoryMissing"))?;
    let metadata = metadata.ok_or_else(|| invalid("backend.steam.format.metadataMissing"))?;
    if !signature_seen {
        return Err(invalid("backend.steam.format.signatureMissing"));
    }
    let expected_crc = if metadata.encrypted_names {
        metadata.encrypted_crc
    } else {
        metadata.clear_crc
    };
    if expected_crc != 0 {
        let mut hasher = crc32fast::Hasher::new();
        hasher.update(&(payload.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
        hasher.update(payload);
        if hasher.finalize() != expected_crc {
            return Err(invalid("backend.steam.format.invalidManifestCrc"));
        }
    }
    let mut payload = Payload::decode(payload)
        .map_err(|_| invalid("backend.steam.format.invalidProtobufInventory"))?;
    for file in &mut payload.files {
        if metadata.encrypted_names {
            file.name = decrypt_name(&file.name, key)?;
            if !file.link_target.is_empty() {
                file.link_target = decrypt_name(&file.link_target, key)?;
            }
        }
        file.name = file.name.replace('\\', "/");
        file.chunks.sort_by_key(|chunk| chunk.offset);
        // Steam lists an empty file with a zero SHA-1, not the SHA-1 of no
        // bytes that every check here computes.
        if !file.is_directory() && file.size == 0 && file.sha == [0; 20] {
            file.sha = Sha1::digest([]).to_vec();
        }
    }
    Ok(Manifest {
        depot_id: metadata.depot_id,
        manifest_id: metadata.manifest_id,
        files: payload.files,
    })
}

fn decrypt_name(name: &str, key: &[u8; 32]) -> Result<String, ContentError> {
    // Valve's older manifests insert line breaks into base64-encoded names.
    let encoded: Vec<u8> = name
        .bytes()
        .filter(|byte| !byte.is_ascii_whitespace())
        .collect();
    let mut encrypted = STANDARD
        .decode(encoded)
        .map_err(|_| invalid("backend.steam.format.invalidEncryptedFileName"))?;
    let bytes = decrypt(&mut encrypted, key)?;
    // Steam's encrypted filename representation includes a UTF-8 NUL terminator.
    let bytes = bytes.strip_suffix(&[0]).unwrap_or(bytes);
    String::from_utf8(bytes.to_vec())
        .map_err(|_| invalid("backend.steam.format.invalidUtf8FileName"))
}

/// Decrypts in place and returns the plaintext, which lies within `data`.
fn decrypt<'a>(data: &'a mut [u8], key: &[u8; 32]) -> Result<&'a [u8], ContentError> {
    if data.len() < 32 || !data.len().is_multiple_of(16) {
        return Err(invalid("backend.steam.format.invalidAesBlockSize"));
    }
    let aes = Aes256::new(key.into());
    let mut iv = aes::cipher::Block::<Aes256>::default();
    iv.copy_from_slice(&data[..16]);
    aes.decrypt_block(&mut iv);
    cbc::Decryptor::<Aes256>::new(key.into(), &iv)
        .decrypt_padded::<Pkcs7>(&mut data[16..])
        .map_err(|_| invalid("backend.steam.format.decryptionFailed"))
}

pub(super) fn decode_chunk(
    encrypted: &mut [u8],
    expected: &Chunk,
    key: &[u8; 32],
) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ContentError> {
    if encrypted.len() > MAX_CHUNK_BYTES || expected.original_size as usize > MAX_CHUNK_BYTES {
        return Err(invalid("backend.steam.format.chunkTooLarge"));
    }
    if expected.compressed_size != 0 && encrypted.len() != expected.compressed_size as usize {
        return Err(invalid("backend.steam.format.invalidCdnChunkSize"));
    }
    let compressed = decrypt(encrypted, key)?;
    let output = if compressed.starts_with(b"VZa") {
        unpack_vzip(compressed, expected.original_size as usize)?
    } else if compressed.starts_with(b"VSZa") {
        unpack_vzstd(compressed, expected.original_size as usize)?
    } else if compressed.starts_with(b"PK\x03\x04") {
        unpack_zip(compressed, expected.original_size as usize)?
    } else {
        return Err(invalid("backend.steam.format.unknownCompression"));
    };
    verify_chunk(&output, expected)?;
    Ok(output)
}

pub(super) fn verify_chunk(bytes: &[u8], expected: &Chunk) -> Result<(), ContentError> {
    if bytes.len() != expected.original_size as usize
        || steam_adler(bytes) != expected.adler
        || Sha1::digest(bytes)[..] != expected.sha
    {
        return Err(invalid("backend.steam.format.invalidChunkChecksum"));
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Steam uses Adler-32 with seed zero, unlike the usual zlib seed of one.
pub(super) fn steam_adler(bytes: &[u8]) -> u32 {
    let (mut a, mut b) = (0_u32, 0_u32);
    for block in bytes.chunks(5552) {
        for &byte in block {
            a += u32::from(byte);
            b += a;
        }
        a %= 65521;
        b %= 65521;
    }
    (b << 16) | a
}

/// A ZIP reader for the one-entry containers Steam serves. It deliberately rejects
/// multi-volume, ZIP64, encrypted and unsupported compression variants.
pub(super) fn unpack_zip(data: &[u8], limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ContentError> {
    let first = data.len().saturating_sub(65535 + 22);
    let end = (first..data.len().saturating_sub(21))
        .rev()
        .find(|&position| data.get(position..position + 4) == Some(b"PK\x05\x06"))
        .ok_or_else(|| invalid("backend.steam.format.zipDirectoryMissing"))?;
    if u16_at(data, end + 4)? != 0
        || u16_at(data, end + 6)? != 0
        || u16_at(data, end + 8)? != 1
        || u16_at(data, end + 10)? != 1
        || end + 22 + usize::from(u16_at(data, end + 20)?) != data.len()
    {
        return Err(invalid("backend.steam.format.zipFileCount"));
    }
    let central_length = u32_at(data, end + 12)? as usize;
    let central = u32_at(data, end + 16)? as usize;
    if central.checked_add(central_length) != Some(end) || slice(data, central, 4)? != b"PK\x01\x02"
    {
        return Err(invalid("backend.steam.format.invalidZipDirectory"));
    }
    let flags = u16_at(data, central + 8)?;
    let method = u16_at(data, central + 10)?;
    let crc = u32_at(data, central + 16)?;
    let compressed_size = u32_at(data, central + 20)? as usize;
    let original_size = u32_at(data, central + 24)? as usize;
    let central_name_len = usize::from(u16_at(data, central + 28)?);
    let central_extra_len = usize::from(u16_at(data, central + 30)?);
    let central_comment_len = usize::from(u16_at(data, central + 32)?);
    let local = u32_at(data, central + 42)? as usize;
    if flags & 1 != 0
        || original_size > limit
        || compressed_size > data.len()
        || central_length != 46 + central_name_len + central_extra_len + central_comment_len
        || slice(data, local, 4)? != b"PK\x03\x04"
        || u16_at(data, local + 6)? != flags
        || u16_at(data, local + 8)? != method
    {
        return Err(invalid("backend.steam.format.invalidZipHeader"));
    }
    let local_name_len = usize::from(u16_at(data, local + 26)?);
    let local_extra_len = usize::from(u16_at(data, local + 28)?);
    let payload_start = local + 30 + local_name_len + local_extra_len;
    if payload_start
        .checked_add(compressed_size)
        .is_none_or(|end| end > central)
    {
        return Err(invalid("backend.steam.format.invalidZipSizes"));
    }
    let compressed = slice(data, payload_start, compressed_size)?;
    let output = match method {
        0 => compressed.to_vec(),
        8 => read_limited(flate2::read::DeflateDecoder::new(compressed), original_size)?,
        _ => return Err(invalid("backend.steam.format.unsupportedZipCompression")),
    };
    if output.len() != original_size || crc32fast::hash(&output) != crc {
        return Err(invalid("backend.steam.format.invalidZipChecksum"));
    }
    Ok(output)
}

fn unpack_vzip(data: &[u8], expected: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ContentError> {
    if data.len() < 22 || !data.ends_with(b"zv") {
        return Err(invalid("backend.steam.format.invalidVzipEnvelope"));
    }
    let footer = data.len() - 10;
    let crc = u32_at(data, footer)?;
    let original_size = u32_at(data, footer + 4)? as usize;
    let dictionary_size = u32_at(data, 8)? as usize;
    if original_size != expected || dictionary_size > MAX_CHUNK_BYTES {
        return Err(invalid("backend.steam.format.invalidVzipDictionary"));
    }
    // Adapt Valve's envelope into an LZMA-alone header, keeping the original LZMA stream.
    let mut header = [0_u8; 13];
    header[..5].copy_from_slice(&data[7..12]);
    header[5..].copy_from_slice(&(original_size as u64).to_le_bytes());
    let mut lzma = (&header[..]).chain(&data[12..footer]);
    let options = lzma_rs::decompress::Options {
        memlimit: Some(MAX_CHUNK_BYTES),
        ..Default::default()
    };
    let mut output = LimitedWriter {
        bytes: Vec::with_capacity(expected),
        limit: expected,
    };
    lzma_rs::lzma_decompress_with_options(&mut lzma, &mut output, &options)
        .map_err(|_| invalid("backend.steam.format.lzmaFailed"))?;
    if output.bytes.len() != expected || crc32fast::hash(&output.bytes) != crc {
        return Err(invalid("backend.steam.format.invalidVzipChecksum"));
    }
    Ok(output.bytes)
}

fn unpack_vzstd(data: &[u8], expected: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ContentError> {
    if data.len() < 23 || !data.ends_with(b"zsv") {
        return Err(invalid("backend.steam.format.invalidVzstdEnvelope"));
    }
    let footer = data.len() - 15;
    let crc = u32_at(data, footer)?;
    let original_size = u32_at(data, footer + 4)? as usize;
    if original_size != expected || u32_at(data, 4)? != crc {
        return Err(invalid("backend.steam.format.invalidVzstdChecksum"));
    }
    let decoder = ruzstd::decoding::StreamingDecoder::new_with_max_window_size(
        &data[8..footer],
        MAX_CHUNK_BYTES as u64,
    )
    .map_err(|_| invalid("backend.steam.format.invalidZstandardHeader"))?;
    let output = read_limited(decoder, expected)?;
    if output.len() != expected || crc32fast::hash(&output) != crc {
        return Err(invalid("backend.steam.format.invalidZstandardChecksum"));
    }
    Ok(output)
}

fn read_limited(reader: impl Read, limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ContentError> {
    let mut output = Vec::with_capacity(limit);
    reader
        .take(limit as u64 + 1)
        .read_to_end(&mut output)
        .map_err(|_| invalid("backend.steam.format.invalidCompressedData"))?;
    if output.len() > limit {
        return Err(invalid("backend.steam.format.decompressedDataTooLarge"));
    }
    Ok(output)
}

struct LimitedWriter {
    bytes: Vec<u8>,
    limit: usize,
}
impl Write for LimitedWriter {
    fn write(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<usize> {
        if self.bytes.len().saturating_add(bytes.len()) > self.limit {
            return Err(std::io::Error::other(
                "backend.steam.format.lzmaOutputTooLarge",
            ));
        }
        self.bytes.extend_from_slice(bytes);
        Ok(bytes.len())
    }
    fn flush(&mut self) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }
}

fn slice(data: &[u8], offset: usize, size: usize) -> Result<&[u8], ContentError> {
    let end = offset
        .checked_add(size)
        .ok_or_else(|| invalid("backend.steam.format.invalidBlockSize"))?;
    data.get(offset..end)
        .ok_or_else(|| invalid("backend.steam.format.truncatedBlock"))
}
fn u16_at(data: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Result<u16, ContentError> {
    let bytes: [u8; 2] = slice(data, offset, 2)?
        .try_into()
        .map_err(|_| invalid("backend.steam.format.truncatedInteger"))?;
    Ok(u16::from_le_bytes(bytes))
}
fn u32_at(data: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Result<u32, ContentError> {
    let bytes: [u8; 4] = slice(data, offset, 4)?
        .try_into()
        .map_err(|_| invalid("backend.steam.format.truncatedInteger"))?;
    Ok(u32::from_le_bytes(bytes))
}
```

```rs
//! Immutable, validated manifests keyed by depot and manifest identity.
//! Only the original CDN archive is persisted; depot keys and decrypted names
//! remain in memory. Local game files are still verified in full on every run.

use std::{
    path::{Path, PathBuf},
    sync::Arc,
};

use obelisk_core::install::{self, PARTIAL_DIRECTORY};

use super::{
    ContentError, MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES,
    format::{Manifest, parse_manifest, unpack_zip},
    invalid, validate_manifest_files,
};

/// An opaque snapshot validated with this depot's key. Keeping it in memory
/// avoids a race between probing a cache file and opening it for installation.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct CachedManifest {
    pub(super) manifest: Arc<Manifest>,
    /// The CDN's archive of a manifest fetched before the installation,
    /// which the installation keeps in its cache; none for one read from it.
    pub(super) archive: Option<Vec<u8>>,
}

pub(super) fn load(
    destination: &Path,
    depot_id: u32,
    manifest_id: u64,
    key: &[u8; 32],
) -> Result<Option<CachedManifest>, ContentError> {
    let relative = relative_path(depot_id, manifest_id);
    let Some(archive) = install::read_cached_file(destination, &relative, MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES)?
    else {
        return Ok(None);
    };
    // The cache is only an optimization. Corrupt, mismatched or stale-format
    // archives fall back to an authorized CDN request, never to trusted metadata.
    let validated = (|| {
        let bytes = unpack_zip(&archive, MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES)?;
        let manifest = parse_manifest(&bytes, key)?;
        if manifest.depot_id != depot_id || manifest.manifest_id != manifest_id {
            return Err(invalid("backend.steam.cache.manifestDepotMismatch"));
        }
        validate_manifest_files(&manifest.files)?;
        Ok(CachedManifest {
            manifest: Arc::new(manifest),
            archive: None,
        })
    })();
    match validated {
        Ok(manifest) => Ok(Some(manifest)),
        Err(
            ContentError::InvalidData(_)
            | ContentError::UnsafePath(_)
            | ContentError::UnsupportedSymlink(_),
        ) => Ok(None),
        Err(error) => Err(error),
    }
}

/// Called only after the caller validated the downloaded archive and created
/// the installation root. Never serializes a decrypted Manifest back to disk.
pub(super) fn store(
    destination: &Path,
    depot_id: u32,
    manifest_id: u64,
    archive: &[u8],
) -> Result<(), ContentError> {
    if archive.len() > MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES {
        return Err(invalid("backend.steam.cache.manifestTooLarge"));
    }
    install::write_cached_file(destination, &relative_path(depot_id, manifest_id), archive)?;
    Ok(())
}

fn relative_path(depot_id: u32, manifest_id: u64) -> PathBuf {
    PathBuf::from(PARTIAL_DIRECTORY)
        .join("manifests")
        .join(depot_id.to_string())
        .join(format!("{manifest_id}.zip"))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use aes::cipher::{
        BlockCipherEncrypt, BlockModeEncrypt, KeyInit, KeyIvInit, block_padding::Pkcs7,
    };
    use base64::{Engine, engine::general_purpose::STANDARD};
    use prost::Message;
    use std::fs::{self, File};

    const KEY: [u8; 32] = [0x42; 32];

    #[derive(Message)]
    struct Payload {
        #[prost(message, repeated, tag = "1")]
        files: Vec<super::super::format::ManifestFile>,
    }
    #[derive(Message)]
    struct Metadata {
        #[prost(uint32, tag = "1")]
        depot: u32,
        #[prost(uint64, tag = "2")]
        manifest: u64,
        #[prost(bool, tag = "4")]
        encrypted_names: bool,
    }

    fn archive(depot: u32, manifest: u64, filename: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
        let iv = [0x12; 16];
        let mut name = filename.as_bytes().to_vec();
        name.push(0);
        let name_len = name.len();
        name.resize(name_len + 16, 0);
        let name = cbc::Encryptor::<aes::Aes256>::new((&KEY).into(), (&iv).into())
            .encrypt_padded::<Pkcs7>(&mut name, name_len)
            .unwrap();
        let mut encrypted_iv = aes::cipher::Block::<aes::Aes256>::default();
        encrypted_iv.copy_from_slice(&iv);
        aes::Aes256::new((&KEY).into()).encrypt_block(&mut encrypted_iv);
        let mut encrypted_name = encrypted_iv.to_vec();
        encrypted_name.extend_from_slice(name);
        let file = super::super::format::ManifestFile {
            name: STANDARD.encode(encrypted_name),
            sha: vec![
                0xda, 0x39, 0xa3, 0xee, 0x5e, 0x6b, 0x4b, 0x0d, 0x32, 0x55, 0xbf, 0xef, 0x95, 0x60,
                0x18, 0x90, 0xaf, 0xd8, 0x07, 0x09,
            ],
            ..Default::default()
        };
        let payload = Payload { files: vec![file] }.encode_to_vec();
        let metadata = Metadata {
            depot,
            manifest,
            encrypted_names: true,
        }
        .encode_to_vec();
        let mut data = Vec::new();
        for (magic, bytes) in [
            (0x71f6_17d0_u32, payload),
            (0x1f48_12be, metadata),
            (0x1b81_b817, Vec::new()),
        ] {
            data.extend_from_slice(&magic.to_le_bytes());
            data.extend_from_slice(&(bytes.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
            data.extend_from_slice(&bytes);
        }
        data.extend_from_slice(&0x32c4_15ab_u32.to_le_bytes());
        stored_zip(&data)
    }

    fn stored_zip(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        let crc = crc32fast::hash(data);
        let mut zip = Vec::new();
        zip.extend_from_slice(b"PK\x03\x04");
        for value in [20_u16, 0, 0, 0, 0] {
            zip.extend_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes());
        }
        for value in [crc, data.len() as u32, data.len() as u32] {
            zip.extend_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes());
        }
        zip.extend_from_slice(&[1, 0, 0, 0, b'm']);
        zip.extend_from_slice(data);
        let central = zip.len() as u32;
        zip.extend_from_slice(b"PK\x01\x02");
        for value in [20_u16, 20, 0, 0, 0, 0] {
            zip.extend_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes());
        }
        for value in [crc, data.len() as u32, data.len() as u32] {
            zip.extend_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes());
        }
        for value in [1_u16, 0, 0, 0, 0] {
            zip.extend_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes());
        }
        zip.extend_from_slice(&[0; 8]);
        zip.push(b'm');
        let central_len = zip.len() as u32 - central;
        zip.extend_from_slice(b"PK\x05\x06");
        for value in [0_u16, 0, 1, 1] {
            zip.extend_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes());
        }
        zip.extend_from_slice(&central_len.to_le_bytes());
        zip.extend_from_slice(&central.to_le_bytes());
        zip.extend_from_slice(&0_u16.to_le_bytes());
        zip
    }

    #[test]
    fn caches_original_encrypted_archive_and_returns_validated_snapshot() {
        let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let bytes = archive(42, 99, "game.exe");
        store(directory.path(), 42, 99, &bytes).unwrap();
        let cached = load(directory.path(), 42, 99, &KEY).unwrap().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(cached.manifest.files[0].name, "game.exe");
        assert_eq!(
            fs::read(directory.path().join(relative_path(42, 99))).unwrap(),
            bytes
        );
        assert!(
            !bytes
                .windows(b"game.exe".len())
                .any(|window| window == b"game.exe")
        );
        assert!(load(directory.path(), 42, 100, &KEY).unwrap().is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn malformed_mismatched_or_unsafe_cached_manifests_are_misses() {
        let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let valid = archive(42, 99, "game.exe");
        let mut bad_crc = valid.clone();
        bad_crc[40] ^= 1;
        for bytes in [
            vec![1, 2, 3],
            bad_crc,
            valid[..valid.len() / 2].to_vec(),
            archive(42, 100, "game.exe"),
            archive(43, 99, "game.exe"),
            archive(42, 99, "../escape"),
        ] {
            store(directory.path(), 42, 99, &bytes).unwrap();
            assert!(load(directory.path(), 42, 99, &KEY).unwrap().is_none());
        }
        store(directory.path(), 42, 99, &valid).unwrap();
        assert!(load(directory.path(), 42, 99, &[0; 32]).unwrap().is_none());
        let file = File::options()
            .write(true)
            .open(directory.path().join(relative_path(42, 99)))
            .unwrap();
        file.set_len(MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES as u64 + 1).unwrap();
        assert!(load(directory.path(), 42, 99, &KEY).unwrap().is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn cache_miss_does_not_create_installation_and_snapshot_survives_disk_changes() {
        let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let absent = directory.path().join("absent");
        assert!(load(&absent, 42, 99, &KEY).unwrap().is_none());
        assert!(!absent.exists());
        store(directory.path(), 42, 99, &archive(42, 99, "game.exe")).unwrap();
        let snapshot = load(directory.path(), 42, 99, &KEY).unwrap().unwrap();
        fs::write(
            directory.path().join(relative_path(42, 99)),
            b"corrupted after load",
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(snapshot.manifest.files[0].name, "game.exe");
        assert!(load(directory.path(), 42, 99, &KEY).unwrap().is_none());
    }

    #[cfg(unix)]
    #[test]
    fn symlink_cache_locations_are_rejected_for_load_and_store() {
        let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let outside = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(outside.path(), directory.path().join(PARTIAL_DIRECTORY))
            .unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            load(directory.path(), 42, 99, &KEY),

        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            store(directory.path(), 42, 99, &archive(42, 99, "game.exe")),
            Err(ContentError::UnsafePath(_))
        ));
        assert!(fs::read_dir(outside.path()).unwrap().next().is_none());
    }

    #[cfg(unix)]
    #[test]
    fn cache_file_symlinks_and_hardlinks_cannot_redirect_atomic_replacement() {
        for symlink in [false, true] {
            let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
            let outside = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
            let archive = archive(42, 99, "game.exe");
            let external_file = outside.path().join("outside.zip");
            fs::write(&external_file, &archive).unwrap();
            let relative = relative_path(42, 99);
            fs::create_dir_all(directory.path().join(relative.parent().unwrap())).unwrap();
            let cache_path = directory.path().join(relative);
            if symlink {
                std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&external_file, &cache_path).unwrap();
            } else {
                fs::hard_link(&external_file, &cache_path).unwrap();
            }
            assert!(matches!(
                load(directory.path(), 42, 99, &KEY),
                Err(ContentError::UnsafePath(_))
            ));
            assert!(matches!(
                store(directory.path(), 42, 99, &archive),
                Err(ContentError::UnsafePath(_))
            ));
            assert_eq!(fs::read(external_file).unwrap(), archive);
        }
    }
```
